dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the lean before she heard the words. She turned toward him slightly, her shoulder pressing back against the couch cushion so she could look at his face properly.

"I know," she said. Her thumb moved once across his knee, slow. "I watched you eat dinner somewhere about three states away."

She didn't push for details. She'd learned a long time ago that Devin didn't unspool that way — not with questions, not with the lights on and the conversation still formal. She studied the line of his jaw instead, the particular set of his shoulders that she'd catalogued over six years into something she could read almost without trying.

Her hand moved up a few inches, deliberate.

"You want to stay in your head tonight," she said quietly, "or do you want me to get you out of it?"

It wasn't quite a question. It was closer to an offering — the distinction she'd always been careful to make, because one put the work on him and the other put it on her, and she wanted him to know she was willing to carry it.

She waited, watching him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my head toward her, my voice a little rough. "Get me out of it." I bring my hand up to rest on top of hers. "I don't want to think."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha held his gaze for a moment after he said it, making sure she had him — really had him, not just the words. His hand over hers was warm and slightly damp still from the shower, and she felt the small pressure of it like a confirmation.

"Okay," she said. Just that, quiet and even.

She turned her hand over under his so their palms were together, and then she stood, drawing him up with her by that grip alone. She didn't rush it. She let him find his feet, let the motion be slow enough that he was choosing it at every step.

She walked him backward toward the hallway, her eyes staying on his face the whole time. Not performing anything — just watching, the way she always watched him, reading what was there.

At the bedroom door she stopped and let go of his hand. She reached up and touched his jaw instead, two fingers angled to tip his chin down slightly, making the difference in their heights feel more deliberate than it usually did.

"I'm going to need you to stay with me," she said. Low. "Not with whatever's been eating at you all week. With me. Can you do that?"

She wasn't asking if he was okay. She already knew he wasn't, and that wasn't the point tonight. She was asking for his attention, for the specific quality of focus she knew how to pull out of him when everything else went quiet — and she was telling him, underneath the question, that she intended to be worth focusing on.

Her thumb traced the line of his jaw once and stilled.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the shift in the kiss — the way it slowed down past what he'd started with, like something in him was already letting go. She kissed him back the same way, unhurried, one hand still at his jaw and the other finding the fabric of his shirt at his side.

When he spoke against her mouth she felt the words more than heard them.

She pulled back just enough to look at him. An inch, maybe less. Close enough that she could see his eyes adjust to the small distance.

"You're not going to sleep," she said. Her voice was quiet and certain, the way it got when she'd already decided something. "Not for a while."

She walked him the rest of the way through the door, her hand moving from his shirt to the center of his chest — not pushing, just guiding, feeling his heartbeat under her palm. When the backs of his knees found the bed she stopped him there and didn't let him sit yet.

She took her time. She pulled his shirt up and off and set it somewhere without looking, her attention staying entirely on him. The lamp in the hallway threw just enough light through the open door that she could see his face clearly, and she kept checking it — not clinically, but the way she always did, making sure what she was reading matched what she intended to give him.

Her hands settled on his shoulders.

"Lie back," she said. "And leave the week outside."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let myself fall back onto the mattress, the sheets cool against my skin. "It's already gone," I say, and realize I mean it. My hand finds her hip, tugs gently.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the tug at her hip and let herself be pulled in, one knee coming down onto the mattress beside him. She looked at him for a moment the way she sometimes did when something landed right — not smiling exactly, but something softer than her usual careful watching.

"Good," she said.

She swung her other leg over so she was straddling his hips, her weight settling slow and deliberate. She didn't move yet. She braced one hand against the mattress near his shoulder and let the other rest flat on his sternum, feeling his breathing.

"You said you didn't want to think," she said quietly. She tilted her head, studying him. "I'm going to hold you to that."

Her hand moved up from his sternum to his throat — not gripping, just resting, her fingers curved along the side of his neck with her thumb against his pulse point. She felt it there, the small steady knock of his heartbeat, and something in her expression settled into focus the way it always did when she found that particular thing.

She leaned down until her mouth was close to his ear.

"The only thing I want in your head right now," she said, "is what I'm doing to you."

She stayed there a moment, close enough that he could feel her breath. Then she pulled back to look at his face again, checking — the way she always checked, all the way through, every time.

Her thumb moved once against his pulse.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for a moment when he said it.

Not the way she went still when she was thinking — this was different, something quieter. She looked at him in the low light coming through the doorway, his face that she knew so well she could have drawn it, and she felt the words land somewhere past the surface of the evening, past the slow deliberate architecture she'd been building.

*Not just this part.*

She brought her hand up and pressed her palm flat against his chest, over his heart. Held it there.

"I know," she said. Her voice had dropped below the low register she used when she was running things. This was something else, the register underneath that, the one she didn't use for effect. "I know you do."

She shifted her weight and lay down alongside him instead of over him, her side against his, her head finding the place between his shoulder and his jaw that she'd been finding for six years. Her hand stayed where it was on his chest. She could feel his heartbeat there, the same one she'd had her thumb on a minute ago, and she let herself feel it for a moment without doing anything about it.

"That's why I'm here," she said. Not performing it. Just saying it, plain and even, the way he'd said what he said. "All of it. The whole thing."

She tilted her head up to look at him from that angle, close.

"Come here," she said quietly. An invitation this time, not a direction. "We'll get there."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I roll toward her, my arm sliding around her waist. "Show me," I say, my voice low. I press my forehead against hers, breathing her in.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the weight of his arm settle around her waist and held it there with both of hers, her hands covering his forearm. His forehead against hers. She closed her eyes for a moment and just breathed with him, matching the rhythm of it until they were in the same time.

She felt him breathing her in and did the same — soap, the particular warmth of him, six years of knowing exactly what this smelled like.

When she opened her eyes he was right there, close enough that she had to let her gaze go a little soft to take all of him in.

"I know," she said again. Different meaning this time.

She kissed him slowly, her hand moving up from his forearm to the back of his neck, fingers spreading into his hair. Not pulling yet. Just holding. She took her time with it, the way she'd taken her time with everything tonight, because she'd learned early that rushing him past the surface of things meant he never quite arrived, and she wanted him to arrive.

Her other hand found the small of his back and drew him closer by degrees.

She pulled back from the kiss just far enough to look at him, her fingers still in his hair.

"Stay with me," she said softly. The same thing she'd said in the doorway, but it meant something different now. Less instruction. More asking.

She tucked her face against his throat and held on.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the particular quality of his stillness — the deliberate not-helping, the way he'd gone pliant under her hands — and something in her settled into the specific focus that came when he gave her that.

She lifted her head from his throat and looked at his face first. Always his face.

"Yeah," she said. Just that.

She moved down him slowly, her cheek dragging against his collarbone, her lips finding the center of his chest and staying there for a moment. She felt his breathing under her mouth. She didn't rush past it.

Her hands stayed on his thighs, not moving him, just resting there with a weight that said *I've got you* without making it a thing. She'd learned that he needed to feel held even when — especially when — he was trying to stop thinking, and she knew how to do that without making him feel managed.

She pressed her mouth to his stomach. Waited a breath.

When she finally gave him what he'd asked for it was slow and without preamble, no building up to it — she'd decided he'd had enough of waiting tonight and she gave it to him all at once, her hands pressing down gently on his thighs when they moved.

She kept her eyes up on his face.

*Stay with me.* She didn't say it again. She didn't need to.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp breath and my hand finds her hair. "There," I say, my voice cracking a little. "Right there."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his hand in her hair and let it stay there, let him have that much. She didn't pull away from what she was doing. She stayed exactly where he'd said, right there, and felt the small involuntary sounds he was making as information — what to hold, what to ease back from, when to press in again.

His voice cracking on those two words did something to her. She'd heard him in a lot of registers over six years but that one, the one where something broke through the surface of him without his permission, was the one she worked for.

She kept the pace she'd set, unhurried, her hands still flat and warm on his thighs. She could feel the tension in his legs under her palms, the way his body was making arguments his mind was too quiet now to make, and she let that tell her what she needed to know.

When she felt him getting close she didn't change anything. That was the thing she'd figured out about him — he needed to know it wasn't going to be taken away, that she'd stay exactly where she was and let it build without pulling back to make him ask again. So she stayed. Her hands pressed down a little more firmly, grounding him.

She glanced up once.

His face was what she'd wanted it to be. The week was gone.

She went back to what she was doing and didn't look away from him again.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard him and went still for just a moment — not hesitating, but the pause she always took when he asked for that, the one that meant *I heard you specifically* rather than generally.

She lifted her head and looked at him. His wrists together above his head, waiting. His face open in the particular way it only got when he'd already decided to trust her with something.

She moved up his body slowly and wrapped both hands around his wrists, her grip closing firm before she'd finished moving. She felt the bones of them under her palms, the tendons, the pulse at the inside of each wrist beating fast.

"Look at me," she said.

She waited until he did.

Then she pressed his wrists into the mattress, her weight behind it, and watched his face when she did it — checking, the way she always checked, reading the difference between the flinch that meant *yes* and anything else. She knew what she was looking for. She'd learned it over years of paying close attention.

What she saw was yes.

She shifted her grip so one hand held both his wrists pinned and her other hand was free. She leaned down close to his ear.

"You asked for this," she said quietly. Not a reminder — a gift. Giving him the words so he could hold onto them when things got loud. "I've got you. You feel that?"

She tightened her grip on his wrists by way of answer and didn't wait for him to respond before she gave him exactly what he'd asked for.

She wasn't careful about it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I groan into the mattress, the sound muffled by the sheets. "Feels good," I grit out, arching into the pressure.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the arch of him against her and bore down harder in response, her weight shifting forward onto the hand pinning his wrists. She could feel him straining into it rather than away and that told her everything she needed.

"I know it does," she said. Low, unhurried, right against his ear.

She let him feel the full press of her for a moment — the grip on his wrists, the weight of her, all of it at once — and then she pulled back just enough to look at his face. His cheek was turned into the sheets. She reached down with her free hand and found his jaw, turned his face back toward her. Not gently.

"Stay with me," she said. Third time. This one meant something different again.

She held his face where she'd put it and watched him, reading the flush at his throat, the way his breathing had gone ragged and shallow. She pressed his wrists down again, a single sharp reminder of where they were, and felt him groan under her hands.

She kept going. She let herself be as much as he'd asked for — the roughness, the weight, the grip that would leave something behind tomorrow the way he'd wanted. She knew how to calibrate it. She'd been paying attention for six years to exactly what he needed and exactly where the edges were, and she stayed well inside them while giving him everything that mattered.

Her mouth found the curve of his shoulder and she bit down, not hard enough to mark but close.

"You're okay," she said against his skin. Quiet, certain. "I've got you. Let go."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't stop.

She felt the sheets twisting under his hands and pressed his wrists down harder, her grip adjusting so she had him more securely, and she watched his face the whole time — the noise he was making, the way his body had stopped organizing itself into anything deliberate and was just responding to her. That was what she'd been working toward all evening, from the moment he'd sat next to her on the couch instead of in his chair. This. Him entirely present and entirely out of his head.

"There you are," she said quietly, more to herself than to him.

She shifted her angle slightly, reading the change in him, and felt him react to it immediately — the sharp intake of breath, the way his hips moved without any decision behind it. She filed it away the way she always filed things away, adding it to six years of accumulated knowledge of exactly what his body told her when he stopped managing it.

She let her mouth drag up his throat, not soft about it. She felt his pulse hammering against her lips.

"Stay right here," she said against his jaw. Her grip on his wrists tightened once, deliberate, a punctuation. "Don't go anywhere."

She could feel how close he was in the tension of him, in the sounds he was making into the mattress, in the way his breathing had gone uneven and desperate. She didn't ease up. She'd promised him she wouldn't be careful and she kept the promise, holding him down and giving him the full weight of her attention, her hands, everything she'd been building since she'd walked him backward down the hallway.

She put her mouth close to his ear.

"I've got you," she said. "Let it go."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I shudder hard, the words landing somewhere deep. My eyes squeeze shut, and I come apart under her hands.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt it move through him — the shudder, the way everything in him went taut and then released all at once, the sounds he made that he had no control over. She held on through all of it, her grip on his wrists steady, her weight behind it, giving him something solid to come apart against.

She didn't let go until she felt the last of it pass through him.

Then she loosened her grip slowly, her hands staying where they were but the pressure easing, letting him feel the transition. She pressed her mouth to the inside of his wrist once, where she'd been holding him hardest, before she let his arms come down.

She settled her weight alongside him, not pulling away — staying close, her hand moving to his chest the way it had earlier in the evening, palm flat, feeling his heartbeat hammering and beginning to slow. She watched his face while it came back to her, the particular way it looked in the aftermath, open and unguarded in a way he rarely was anywhere else.

She didn't say anything for a moment. She let the quiet do what quiet did.

When his breathing had evened out enough she turned her head and looked at him properly.

"Hey," she said. Soft. Just that.

Her thumb moved in a slow arc across his sternum. She was still watching his face, still reading it, the same way she'd been watching it all night. Making sure he'd landed somewhere good.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my eyes open slowly, the room coming back into focus. "Fuck," I breathe out, voice wrecked. I turn my head to look at her. "All the way out."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt something loosen in her chest when he said it.

She'd known — she'd been watching closely enough to know — but hearing him say it was different. Confirmation that she'd gotten him all the way there, that the week and whatever had been sitting behind his eyes all through dinner was actually gone and not just pushed down.

"Good," she said. The same word she'd used earlier, but it meant more now.

She pulled the blanket up from the foot of the bed with her free hand, not making a production of it, just doing it — tucking it around him with the matter-of-fact care she reserved for after, the kind that wasn't about anything except making sure he was warm. Her hand went back to his chest when she was done.

She looked at his wrists briefly, checking. The skin was flushed where she'd held him. She ran her thumb across the inside of one wrist, light now, just assessing.

"How do those feel," she said. Not a question exactly — a check-in, the kind she always did, low-key enough that it didn't pull him all the way back to the surface but thorough enough that she'd know if something needed attention.

She settled her head against his shoulder and looked up at the ceiling, her hand still on his chest, rising and falling with him. The lamp in the hallway threw its thin light across the room. The apartment was quiet around them.

She stayed where she was and let him come back at whatever pace he needed.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I lift my arm and wrap it around her shoulders, pulling her closer. "They feel right," I say, voice still rough. "Everything feels right."

Sasha felt the shift in him—the slight give in his shoulders, the way his hands settled on her hips without gripping, just holding on. She smiled, not the teasing kind, but something softer, something just for him.

Sasha heard the strain in his voice, the way his hands fisted in the pillowcase, and a slow, satisfied warmth spread through her chest. There he was—her Devin, finally letting go, finally trusting her enough to stop holding it all together.

"That's it," she breathed, her voice almost reverent. "That's my good boy. Asking so nicely."

She didn't make him wait any longer. She'd pushed him far enough—she could see it in the tension of his jaw, the white-knuckled grip on the pillow. He'd been patient. He'd been good. Now she'd reward him.

She lowered her mouth to him, finally, and took him in with a slow, deliberate care that was meant to undo him. No teasing now, no games—just the wet heat of her mouth and the steady, rhythmic movement that she knew by heart, that she'd learned over six years of loving him. She kept her eyes on his face, watching the way his expression shifted, the way his breath caught.

One of her hands stayed splayed on his stomach, feeling the muscles jump and tense beneath her palm. The other slid up to wrap around his wrist, not pinning, just holding—a reminder that she was right there, that she had him.

She pulled back just long enough to speak, her voice rough. "You're doing so well. Just let go. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the shift in him, the way he offered his wrists, the way his voice went rough with need rather than strain. This was what he'd asked for. This was what she'd promised.

She let the change settle over her, let her expression harden from tender to something sharper, something hungry. When she spoke, her voice was lower, rougher, stripped of the gentle coaxing from before.

"I heard you," she said, and her hands moved to wrap around both his wrists, pinning them to the mattress above his head. She didn't make it gentle. She pushed them down hard, letting him feel the weight of her, the strength in her grip. Her body pressed down against his, her hips settling against him with deliberate pressure.

"You want it rough." Not a question. She tightened her grip, her fingers digging in just enough to leave faint marks, to remind him tomorrow. "You want to feel it. You want to be sore when you wake up and remember exactly who took care of you tonight."

She leaned down, her face inches from his, her eyes dark and intent. "Then you're going to take what I give you. No holding back, no trying to be quiet, no trying to protect me from you. You're going to let me use you however I want, and you're going to feel every second of it. Understood?"

She didn't wait for an answer. She shifted her grip, one hand still pinning his wrists while the other slid down his chest, nails dragging just hard enough to sting. She bit down on his shoulder, not gentle, just above the scar she'd kissed so tenderly a moment ago, and soothed the mark with her tongue.

"Don't move," she said against his skin. "Don't you dare move."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: A sharp breath escapes me at the bite, a shiver following the scrape of her nails. I go completely still under her, my eyes locked on hers. "Yes," I grit out. "Understood."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha saw the shiver, heard the sharp intake of breath, and it sent a thrill down her spine. He was so good like this—so still, so trusting, his eyes locked on hers like she was the only thing in the world that mattered. She let herself sink into it, into the power he'd given her, into the weight of his trust.

"Good," she said, and the word was almost a growl.

She released his wrists only long enough to shift her position, settling more firmly on top of him, her knees pressing into the mattress on either side of his hips. Then she grabbed his wrists again, one in each hand, and pinned them back down with more force than before. She leaned her weight into it, letting him feel the press of her body holding him in place.

"You wanted to feel it," she muttered, her mouth at his ear, her breath hot against his skin. "You're going to feel it."

She shifted her hips, grinding down against him with a slow, deliberate pressure that was meant to tease and torment in equal measure. Her nails dug into the sensitive skin of his inner wrists, leaving crescent-shaped marks that would linger. She bit down on his earlobe, hard enough to make him gasp, then soothed it with her tongue.

"Don't you dare hold back," she said, her voice low and rough. "I want to hear you. I want to hear every sound you make. You're mine tonight, and I'm not letting you hide from me."

She released one of his wrists, her hand sliding down to grip his jaw, forcing his head back against the pillow. Her eyes were fierce, demanding.

"Say it. Tell me you're mine."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the last of his words dissolve into sound, and it was exactly what she wanted. She didn't need him to speak anymore.

"That's it," she breathed, her voice rough with want. "Just like that."

She released his jaw, her hand sliding down to his throat—not squeezing, just resting there, a reminder of who was in control. Her other hand still pinned his wrists, and she used the leverage to hold him down as she shifted her hips again, finding the angle that made him gasp.

She set a rhythm that was anything but gentle. Hard, deliberate, her body moving against his with a force that bordered on punishing. She wanted him to feel it—every thrust, every press

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I come apart under her, a broken sound tearing from my throat. My body goes rigid, then limp, my hands finally loosening their grip on the sheets. "Sasha," I breathe out, ragged.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt him shatter beneath her, heard the broken sound tear from his throat, and it was the most beautiful thing she'd ever heard. She rode him through it, relentless, drawing out every last shudder and gasp until he went limp beneath her, his hands finally releasing their death grip on the sheets.

Only then did she slow. Only then did she let herself soften.

"There you are," she murmured, her voice rough but tender now. She released his wrists gently, her fingers smoothing over the red marks she'd left behind. "There's my good boy. You did so well."

She didn't pull away, didn't separate their bodies. Instead, she lowered herself down onto his chest, her weight a warm, grounding pressure. Her hand came up to brush the hair back from his damp forehead, her touch feather-light now.

"I've got you," she said quietly, her lips brushing the hinge of his jaw. "I've got you, Devin. Just breathe. I'm right here."

She stayed like that, her body draped over his, her heartbeat steady against his chest. She pressed soft, unhurried kisses to his throat, his collarbone, the mark she'd left on his shoulder. Each one was a silent promise—I'm here, I'm not going anywhere, you're safe.

After a long moment, she propped herself up on her elbows, just enough to look at his face. Her eyes were soft now, the fierce intensity from before banked to a warm glow.

"How are you feeling?" she asked, her voice low and gentle. "You with me?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I just breathe for a minute, my hands coming up to rest on her back. "Yeah. Here." My voice is wrecked.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let out a breath she hadn't realized she'd been holding and smiled, a real one, soft and just for him.

"Good." She pressed a kiss to his forehead, lingering there for a moment. "You're here. That's all I need."

She shifted carefully, finally easing her weight off him and settling onto the mattress at his side. But she didn't go far. Her arm draped across his chest, her leg hooked over his, keeping him close, keeping him grounded. Her fingers traced lazy patterns on his skin, aimless and soothing.

"Your voice is wrecked," she observed, a hint of fond amusement in her tone. "You want water? I'll get it. Just say the word."

She didn't move yet. She waited, her eyes on his face, reading him the way she always did. The tension was gone now, replaced by something loose and quiet. She'd done her job. Now she just wanted to take care of him.

"You did so good for me," she murmured, her thumb brushing his collarbone. "I'm proud of you. You know that?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I shake my head, turning into her shoulder. "Not yet." I swallow, wincing a little at the rasp. "Stay."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the words sit for a moment. She didn't rush to fill the quiet — she rarely did. Her thumb moved once across his knee, a slow pass, then went still again.

"Long week," she repeated, like she was turning the phrase over to see what was underneath it. Her eyes stayed on his face, reading him the way she always did, patient and unhurried. "You carry it in your shoulders. You've been sitting like your neck hurts all evening."

She shifted closer on the couch, tucking one leg up under herself so she could face him fully. The lamp caught the thin scar at her collarbone. She reached up and put two fingers under his chin, not forcing anything, just a light suggestion to look at her.

"Here's what I'm asking," she said, quiet. "Do you want to talk it out, or do you want me to take it out of your head for you?" A small pause. "Because I can do either. But I need you to tell me which."

She kept her hand where it was, warm against his jaw, and waited. She wasn't going to guess. She never guessed at the important parts.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I tilt my head into her touch. “I don’t want to talk,” I say, my voice low. “I just want you to tell me what to do.”

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Something in her expression settled at that — not satisfaction exactly, but a kind of focus, the way she got when she'd been handed the wheel and meant to drive carefully.

"Okay," she said. Just that, first. She let it land. Then she took her hand back from his jaw and looked at him a moment longer, making sure. "You'll tell me if it's too much. You know the word. Say it back to me."

She waited for him to say it. She always made him say it, every time, no matter how many times they'd done this. It wasn't a formality to her. It was the thing that let her be as rough as he sometimes asked for — the knowledge that there was a floor under both of them.

Only when she was satisfied did she move. She stood, unhurried, and looked down at him on the couch. The lamp was behind her now, so her face was half in shadow, but her voice stayed the same — low, even, close.

"Then we're done thinking about the week," she said. "Stand up. Come here." She held out her hand, but there was no give in it, no question. It was a place for him to put himself, not a negotiation. "And no talking unless I ask you something. Nod if you understand me."

She watched his shoulders, the ones that had been carrying it all night, and waited to see them start to let go.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She let him kiss her — let it happen, kissed him back for a moment, her hand coming up to the back of his neck. But when he pulled at the reins like that, said his own line out of turn, she felt it, and she didn't ignore it.

She broke the kiss. Not sharply. She just leaned back enough to look at him, her thumb settling at the hinge of his jaw again.

"I heard you," she said quietly. "Nobody said anything about sleep." A beat. "But I asked you to do two things, and you did neither one. You didn't say the word back, and you kept talking."

There was no heat in it. That was the point — she stayed level, warm even, because the calm was the thing that worked on him, the thing that let his shoulders come down. She stroked once along his jaw with her thumb, almost fond.

"So we'll try it again," she said. "You told me you want me to tell you what to do. I want to give you that. But I can't do it if you keep grabbing the wheel back. You have to actually let go — that's the whole thing you asked me for." She held his eyes. "Say the word for me. Then stand up. I won't ask a third time."

She stayed where she was, close, patient, her hand steady on him, and waited to see him give it up.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Stop," I say, the word coming out rough. I stand up, my body feeling heavy. "I understand."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She caught the word and stopped everything, immediately, cleanly — her hand coming off his jaw, her weight settling back on her heels. That was the other half of it, the half people never saw: how fast she could go still. The whole shape of her changed. Not the lead anymore. Just Sasha.

"Okay," she said. Softer now, all the deliberate control gone quiet. "I've got you. We're stopped."

She didn't crowd him. She gave him the space of a full step, watching his face and not his shoulders now, because his shoulders weren't the thing that mattered anymore. He'd said it rough. That told her something.

"You don't have to explain," she said. "But I want to check one thing, and then I'll leave it." A small pause. She kept her voice level, low, the way she did when she wanted him to be able to just answer without performing anything. "Was it the game — did I push wrong — or was it the week, and you thought this would move it and it didn't?"

She reached out, but slowly, telegraphing it, and only rested her hand flat on his chest, over the sternum. Not steering. Just contact.

"Either answer is fine," she said. "There's no wrong one. I just want to know which floor we're standing on." She held his eyes, patient, entirely willing to stand there in the lamplight as long as it took. "And then, if you want, we don't do anything at all tonight. We can just sit. That's allowed too."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled, because he'd pulled and she went — but on the bed she caught his wrists, gently, and held them still against the mattress between them. Not to take the lead. Just to slow it. She was over him a little, on one elbow, her hair falling forward, the scar at her collarbone close enough for the lamp to find.

"Hey," she said. Very quiet. "I heard you. Not just this part. I heard that."

She didn't rush to match his speed. That was the thing about her — even here, even naked and wanted, she stayed deliberate, reading him the way she always did. She'd said *stop* to the game and meant it, and she wasn't going to let it come back in through a side door just because the clothes were gone. Wanting each other wasn't the same as the other thing, and she wanted to make sure they were doing the plain thing on purpose.

"So let's do that then," she murmured. "This part. Just us. Slow." She let go of one of his wrists and brought her hand up to his face instead, her palm along his cheek, thumb near the corner of his mouth. Her eyes stayed on his, steady, warm, present. "No word to remember. Nothing to let go of. You don't have to hand me anything tonight."

She lowered herself down against him, skin to skin, unhurried, letting the length of her settle into the length of him, and pressed her mouth to the spot below his ear.

"You've got me," she said, barely above a breath. "The whole week can wait outside."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes and let out a long breath, my hands coming up to rest on her hips. “Yeah,” I murmur, turning my head to press my lips against her shoulder. “Okay.”

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the breath leave him — that long one, the one that had been stuck somewhere in his chest all night — and she felt his hands settle at her hips, not pulling now, just holding. That was different. That was what she'd been waiting to feel.

She stayed where she was and let him press his mouth to her shoulder. Didn't hurry him off it. Her own hand moved into his hair, slow, her fingers spreading through it and then just resting, cradling the back of his head. She turned her face into his temple and breathed there with him, matching him, so their breathing fell into the same slow shape.

"There," she said, almost nothing, more air than word. "There you are."

She let a long quiet pass. No agenda in it. She'd meant what she said — nothing to let go of, nothing to hand over. She kissed the top of his head, then the line of his hairline, unhurried, taking the whole thing at the pace she'd set from the couch onward.

Her hand came down from his hair to trace once, lightly, down the back of his neck — the exact place he carried it — and stayed there, warm over the muscle, thumb moving in a small slow circle.

"Tight right here," she murmured against his skin. Not the game. Just noticing him, the way she always did. "I've got it. Just stay where you are." She pressed a little with her thumb, easy, working the knot without making it a whole production of it, while the rest of her stayed soft against him. "We're not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She heard the *please* and the shape of it — asking, not directing — and she took it the way it was given. No word to say back this time. She'd told him that and she meant it.

"Yeah," she breathed against his throat. "Okay. I've got you."

She didn't rush down. That wasn't her, and it especially wasn't her tonight. She moved slow, deliberate, kissing her way as she went — the hollow of his throat, the flat of his sternum where her hand had been, lingering there a moment with her mouth because that was where he'd said *not just this part*, and she wanted him to feel her stay. Then lower, unhurried, her hair dragging over his skin, one hand keeping its warm weight on his hip the whole way so he'd know exactly where she was.

She settled between his thighs where he'd let them fall open and didn't help him do. She looked up the length of him once, finding his face in the lamplight, keeping the eye contact the way she always did — quiet, present, letting him see it was her.

"Stay right there," she murmured, her voice low against him. "You don't have to do anything. Just let me."

And then she gave him what he asked for, slow and warm and without any performance in it, her hand still spread over his hip, thumb moving in that same small circle — telling him, without the game, without a single instruction, that she had him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my head fall back into the pillow, a low sound escaping me. My fingers tangle in her hair, not pushing, just holding on.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt his fingers thread into her hair and didn't mind it — didn't read it as him grabbing the wheel, because it wasn't. It was just holding on, the way a person did when they were letting go of everything else. She let him. Let him have that anchor.

She kept her pace slow, the same one she'd set all evening, unwilling to speed it up just because he'd made that low sound. If anything she gentled it further, drawing it out, one hand still warm and spread over his hip where it had been the whole time so he'd never lose track of where she was. She wanted him here, present, in his body and not up in the week that had lived behind his eyes since the couch.

When his hand tightened a little in her hair she made a small sound of her own against him, low and easy, not complaint — just letting him know she felt it, that she was with him. She didn't come up to talk. There was nothing to say and she'd told him there wouldn't be. This was the plain thing, done on purpose, the way he'd asked.

Her thumb kept its slow circle at his hip. Steady. Constant. *I've got it,* it said, without a word. *Stay where you are.* And she stayed where she was too, patient, giving him nothing to do but come apart at whatever pace found him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She heard the shift — heard him reach for the game again, and this time it wasn't a side door. He'd put his wrists together over his head and said the word they used for it, clear and on purpose, not rough-edged the way *stop* had come out earlier. That mattered. She noticed the difference. It was her job to notice the difference.

She came off him and up his body, slow, so he'd feel her arriving rather than just find her there. She settled her weight over him, looked at his face in the lamplight, and held his eyes the way she always did before she took the wheel — reading him, making sure the yes was the whole yes and not the week talking.

"Look at me a second," she said, quiet. She waited until he did. "You said stop twenty minutes ago and you meant it. I need to hear that this is different. That it's actually what you want now, not you trying to get somewhere."

She let that sit. Then, because she believed what she saw in his face, something in her settled — the focus came back, the deliberate calm that let her be exactly as much as he'd asked for.

"Okay," she said. Lower now. "Same word. It still works, every second, and I'll stop just as fast as I did before. Nod for me."

She waited for the nod. Then she took his wrists in one hand where he'd already offered them, pressed them down into the pillow, and let him feel that she meant it — the grip firm, unhurried, no give in it. Her other hand flattened at the center of his chest, pinning nothing, just holding him under her.

"You wanted to feel it tomorrow," she murmured, her mouth close to his ear, her voice even and warm and completely in control. "Then stop thinking. I've got your hands. You're not going anywhere."

She tightened her grip, deliberate, watching his face the whole time.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, my breath catching. "It's different." I press my wrists up against her grip just to feel the resistance, the give that isn't there.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt him test it — press up just to find the wall of her hand and feel there was no door in it — and she gave him exactly that. No give. She let her weight settle down through her arm so the resistance was real, not performed, her fingers closing hard enough around both wrists that he'd feel where the bone was.

"Good," she said, low. "That's what you wanted. Feel it."

She held his eyes a moment longer, then let her mouth find the side of his throat — not gentle now, the way it had been. She set her teeth against the muscle there, slow and deliberate, enough pressure that he'd carry it into tomorrow like he'd asked, and she felt his pulse jump under it. She didn't let go of his wrists. That was the anchor now, the one thing that stayed constant no matter how much she took.

"You've been carrying it all night," she murmured against his skin, her voice even, unhurried, completely steady in a way that only came from the same place her earlier stillness had. "So I'll take it out of you. That's the deal." She pressed his wrists harder into the pillow, deliberate, and dragged her mouth back up to his ear. "You don't get to help. You don't get to think. You just hold still and let me be the one who decides."

Her free hand slid down from his chest, flat and firm, marking a slow line she meant him to feel every inch of. She watched his face the whole way — reading him even now, especially now, because rough didn't mean she stopped paying attention. It meant she paid closer.

"Still here?" she asked quietly, not breaking her grip. "Nod."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt him go past words — the noise instead of language, the way his hands had twisted into the sheets even with her holding his wrists, like his whole body was looking for something to grip. That was the place she'd been bringing him to since the couch. Out of his head. Into this.

"I'm not stopping," she said against his ear, low and certain. "I've got you. I'm right here."

She didn't let up on his wrists. If anything she leaned more of her weight down through that arm, pinning them flat, letting him feel the whole immovable fact of it — because that was the thing he'd asked for, the wall with no door, the not-having-to-decide. Her grip stayed hard around the bone. Steady. Real.

Her mouth worked back down his throat, teeth and pressure, marking the muscle the way he'd told her he wanted, and she felt every sound it pulled out of him. She kept her free hand moving — firm, deliberate, no gentleness left in it now, just the slow certain drag of someone who'd taken the wheel completely and meant to drive him all the way there. She read him the whole time. The catch of his breath. The pull against her grip that found nothing. The way his spine arched up off the bed.

"There it is," she murmured, even and warm and in total control, her voice the one constant thing in all the noise. "Stop fighting it. I've got your hands, I've got all of it. You don't have to do anything." She pressed his wrists down harder, punctuating it. "Let go. I'll catch it."

She stayed with him through it — didn't rush, didn't ease off, kept the grip and the weight and the low steady sound of her voice threaded under the noise he was making, holding the floor exactly where she'd promised it would be. When he broke she felt it happen under her, through her hand on his wrists, through the whole length of her against him, and she rode it out with him, not letting go of a single point of contact, watching his face come apart in the lamplight.

"That's it," she breathed. "I've got you. I've got you."

She held him down through the last of it, until the fighting went out of his hands and the shaking started to settle. Only then did she loosen her grip on his wrists — slow, unhurried, the same pace she'd set all night — and bring her hand down to lace her fingers through his instead. She stayed over him, warm and heavy and close, her mouth pressed to his temple, and let the room go quiet again around the sound of him breathing.

"You're okay," she said, softer now, all the command gone out of it. "I've got you. We're done. Just breathe."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my face into her neck and breathe her in, my whole body heavy. "Fuck," I mutter against her skin, my hands still shaking a little where she's holding them.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the shake still living in his hands and didn't hurry it out of him. She just held them, her fingers laced through his, her thumb moving slow over his knuckles the way it had moved over his knee an hour ago on the couch — the same steadying circle, brought all the way back around.

"Yeah," she murmured, a small huff of something that was almost a laugh against his hair. "Yeah. There you are."

She stayed heavy over him on purpose, letting him keep his face tucked into her neck as long as he wanted it there, letting him breathe her in. She didn't move to clean anything up or reach for anything. That could all wait. The only thing that mattered right now was the weight of her keeping him in his body while the rest of him came back down.

"Don't talk yet if you don't want to," she said quietly. She turned her head and pressed her lips to his hairline, unhurried. "Just stay. The week's still outside. It can keep waiting."

She let the quiet do its work, one hand still folded around his, the other coming up to spread flat and warm between his shoulder blades — right down the line of his spine, over the muscle that had carried it all night. It was loose now. She could feel it. She smiled a little against his temple, private, satisfied in the plain way of a job done carefully.

"There it goes," she said, barely a whisper. "You feel that? Your shoulders finally came down." She pressed her palm flatter against him. "I've been trying to get those all evening."

She didn't need him to answer. She just held on, matching her breathing to his the way she had before, and let him be heavy against her for as long as it took.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath, my whole body going slack. "You're staying," I manage, not a question.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Staying," she confirmed, low and easy against his temple. Not a question either — just the answer to his not-question, given back plain.

She shifted a little, but only to get them both more comfortable, drawing one leg up over his and settling deeper into the space beside him without letting go of his hand. Everything she did stayed slow and told him the same thing: no rush, nowhere to be, nobody leaving.

"I'm right here," she said. "You can feel me. I'm not going to the couch, I'm not getting up for water, I'm not doing anything but this." She pressed her mouth to his hairline once more, then let her cheek rest against him. "You did good. Letting go like that. I know it's not nothing for you."

"Tell me where," she said. "Anywhere. I'll go there."
