dialogue.content: I guide her hand down, my breath catching. "Here," I manage, my voice low. "Just...stay close."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the direction of his hand before she understood the word, and then she understood the word, and then she understood what he actually meant by it — that the *here* wasn't a place. It was a radius. The shape of her against him, the warmth of her skin against his, the sound of her breathing somewhere near his ear.

She answered him without words first.

She took her hand back from his — gently, letting his fingers curl around empty air for a second before she threaded her own through them and pinned his hand to the pillow above his head. Her other hand she kept where he'd guided it, low, where he wanted her to be, and she let her fingers close around him with the slow steady pressure she'd learned he liked when he was tired instead of quick and wanting. The kind that didn't ask him to do anything. The kind that just was.

She lifted her head and looked down at him. The lamplight caught on his face — the way his eyes had gone dark, the way his mouth had fallen open a little, the way the muscle in his jaw was working like he was trying to keep himself from asking for more. She knew that look. She'd learned it four years ago, the first time he'd come home from a week like this and she'd figured out what he actually needed underneath what he said.

"Close," she echoed back to him, soft. "I'm here. I'm not going anywhere."

She started moving her hand then — slow, the stroke long and easy from base to tip, the kind of rhythm she'd figured out somewhere in their second year that always pulled him under without making him tense up. The opposite of hurried. The opposite of what his week had been. She let her grip stay loose at the top of each stroke and tighten only on the way down, and she watched his face while she did it, reading the small changes, the places where his breath caught and where it let go.

She lowered herself down the length of him until her chest was against his side, her cheek resting against his shoulder, her mouth near his ear. She could feel his heartbeat in two places now — against her palm and against her cheek — and she matched her hand's rhythm to it, slowing when it slowed, speeding a fraction when it climbed, the two of them chasing the same tempo without either of them having to think about it.

She turned her head and pressed her mouth to the side of his neck. Not a kiss this time. Just her lips there, parted, breathing him in. Her other hand — the one still threaded through his, the one still pinned to the pillow — she squeezed once, a small gentle pressure, the kind of thing you do when you want someone to know you're there without interrupting the current of what they're feeling.

"There you go," she murmured against his throat. Her thumb found the hollow at the base of him and circled once, slow. "I've got you. Just stay with me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard the word the way she heard most things he said tonight — like it had traveled a long way to reach him. She lifted her cheek from his shoulder and looked at him. His eyes were half-closed, his mouth still open around the last of the word, his hand in hers gone slack on the pillow like he'd given the last of something up.

She didn't move yet.

"Look at me," she said. Not loud. Just enough to reach him wherever the nine had taken him. She waited until his eyes found hers, and even in the low lamp she could see the way the dark had swallowed the rest of them.

"I'm here," she said. "I'm going to take care of you. Okay?"

She didn't wait for the okay. She read it in the way his chin tipped toward her — a small yes, an unconscious one, the kind she took more seriously than any answer out loud. She let go of his hand, slowly, finger by finger, and brought hers down the length of him one more time — a long stroke, unhurried, the same slow tempo she'd been keeping — and then she shifted her weight down the bed.

She went in pieces.

First her mouth at the notch of his hipbone, just resting there, her breath warm against him while she let the new position settle between them. She could feel his stomach tighten under the brush of her lips. She kissed the place once, slow, and stayed there another breath. Her hand stayed low, her grip loose, her thumb moving against him in small absent circles while she worked her way down — another kiss, lighter this time, against the crease where his thigh met his hip. Her hair fell against his skin and she didn't push it back. Let him feel it. Let him feel all of it in pieces.

She could hear his breathing change. Slower in some places, quicker in others. She tracked it the way she tracked everything about him — without making it obvious, without making him feel watched, just filing it all under *careful* so she could use it.

"You can put your hand in my hair if you want," she said against his skin, quiet, the same low tone she'd been using all night. "But don't push. Just — be there. I'm going to go slow."

A pause. Her lips barely an inch from him now, her breath landing warm.

"If you need me to stop, tap my shoulder twice. You remember."

She didn't wait longer. She didn't make a show of it. She just — arrived. Her mouth closed around him slow, the way she'd learned to do it on nights like this, taking him in by degrees instead of all at once so he could feel each new piece of her mouth as it landed. She kept her hand where it was, low, the part she couldn't reach, and let her grip stay loose so the two of them together made a single slow current instead of two competing ones.

She wasn't trying to be good at it. She was trying to be *with* him — and that was different, and he knew it was different, and that was the whole point.

She settled into a rhythm she didn't try to push — long, easy, the kind that let her breathe between strokes without ever lifting off him, her hand and her mouth working together the way two parts of the same sentence did. Every few strokes she'd lift her head a fraction, let him hear her draw breath through her nose, and then sink back down again, slower each time, the way you ease someone into warm water.

She didn't close her eyes. She kept them open, angled up at him the length of his body, watching the way the lamplight moved across his skin when his hips shifted, watching the way his hand had gone into her hair and was just resting there, the way she'd told him to. Not pulling. Not directing. Just present.

She hummed once, low in her chest, not on purpose — one of those things her body did sometimes when she forgot to manage it. She felt his thigh jump against her shoulder in answer. She filed that away too.

*There.*

She slowed down further. Deliberately. Made each stroke last a count longer than the last, the way she'd discovered somewhere in their third year was the fastest way to undo him when he came home like this — not faster, *slower*, until his body started asking for what his mouth wouldn't.

"Tell me," she murmured against him between strokes, her voice lower now, rougher, the way it always got when she'd been doing this for a while. "Tell me when it's close. I want to know."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I feel my fingers tighten in her hair, just for a second. "Soon," I get out, the word strained. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it — both words, and the strained place between them where the real answer lived. She didn't lift off him. She didn't change anything immediately. She let the word *soon* settle into her the way she'd been letting everything else settle into her all night, then she answered in the only way that mattered.

She tightened her hand. Low, at the base of him, where she'd kept her grip loose this whole time. She let it firm up now — not a lot, just enough to give him a second edge, a single point of harder pressure against the rest of the soft current. She felt his thigh jump against her shoulder again and stayed with it.

Her mouth found its way back to him slower than before, slower than was even useful, the way she always did at the very end because she'd figured out that the contrast was what undid him — the fact that the rhythm hadn't changed, that he couldn't have predicted when it would. She let her tongue do a small thing against him as she took him deeper, something she didn't usually do, something she saved for nights like this, and she felt the breath leave him in a way that wasn't quite a word.

His hand in her hair tightened for the half-second he'd warned her about and then eased. She noticed. She noticed the way his fingers didn't push, didn't direct — just held, the way she'd asked him to. The way he'd listened to her ask. The nine in him hadn't disappeared, but something had opened underneath it, and she let herself feel grateful for it without naming it.

She pressed her free hand flat against his stomach, low, where she could feel the small involuntary muscle movements, where his body was telling her things his voice couldn't quite get out yet. She held him there with her palm and matched the pressure with the small tilt of her tongue, and she timed them so they landed together — a single *something* in the middle of a stroke instead of two things competing.

"There you go," she murmured against him, the words vibrating low against his skin. She said it quiet enough that he could almost pretend he hadn't heard it. She said it the way she'd been saying things all night — *I see you, I'm not going anywhere, you don't have to do anything.* "I've got you. Stay with me."

She shifted the angle of her head a fraction and took him deeper, deliberately, one slow inch at a time, until her lips were flush against her own fingers. She held him there. Didn't move. Let him feel the warmth of her mouth around him without anything else happening, without any demand on him to do or be anything — just the unchanging fact of her, holding him in a place his body couldn't leave until his body decided to.

She could feel his breath coming in pieces now, the rhythm of it broken into something that wasn't rhythm anymore, just his body reaching for the next breath and the next. She knew this — knew the place he was in, knew it from every version of it she'd ever watched him get to. The place where the nine finally let go of him.

His hand in her hair went still in a different way. Not slack — *waiting.* She lifted her eyes up the length of him and found his face in the lamplight. She didn't need to read it. She already knew. She gave him a single small nod she wasn't sure he could see in the low light, and then she started moving again — slow, slower than she'd been going all night, so slow it was almost a stillness with just the smallest amount of motion in it, the kind of stroke she'd spent six years learning the inside of.

She held him there with her mouth and her hand and the slow patient current of her breathing against his skin, and she waited for him the way she'd been waiting for him all night.

*Go,* she thought, against him, the way she always did, the way he couldn't hear. *I've got you. Go ahead.*

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the request land before she'd understood the shape of it — felt it in the way his body went taut under her hand, in the way the word *rough* came out of him like something he'd been holding in his mouth all night and finally let go of.

She lifted off him. Slow, the way she always did, her lips dragging against him on the way up until just the very tip of him was in her mouth, and then she let that go too. She kissed his hip once, absently, the way you kiss someone when you're already thinking about what comes next, and then she slid up the length of him.

She didn't go to his mouth. She went to his wrists.

She looked at them for a long moment — crossed, waiting, offered up on the pillow the way someone leaves a door open. She put her hands around them, loosely, the way you'd take hold of something you wanted to be sure of. Her thumbs rested against the inside of his wrists where she could feel his pulse jump against them.

She looked down at him.

"Say it again," she said. Not a refusal. Lower than that. The voice she'd been using all night had a new thing in it now, something she'd kept sheathed for the whole evening because he hadn't asked for it yet. "Look at me and say it again so I know you mean it."

She waited. Her hands stayed where they were around his wrists, loose, patient, in no hurry. She read his face in the lamplight the way she'd been reading it all night — except this time she wasn't reading tiredness. She was reading something just under it, something his body had been carrying beside the nine this whole time, the way a hand carries a second thing in a closed fist.

She let the quiet sit for three breaths.

Then she brought his wrists down off the pillow and pinned them — *fast*, suddenly, the way she hadn't moved all night, gathering both his wrists into one of her hands and pressing them into the mattress beside his head in a single motion. Not hard enough to hurt. Hard enough that he could feel the lock of her around him, the places where her fingers tightened and where they didn't, the way the *loose* in her grip was a deliberate choice rather than a default. Her other hand landed flat against the center of his chest and pressed him into the bed. She felt him exhale under her palm like she'd pulled something out of him.

"There's my boy," she said, quieter than he'd expected, in a voice that had dropped half a register into somewhere he didn't get to hear most nights. "I had you all soft. Now give me the rest of it. Don't be polite about it — tell me what you want and I'll do it."

She shifted her weight over him, her knees outside his hips now, and stayed there, holding him down with her hand on his chest, his wrists pinned, her body pinning the rest of him by the simple fact of where she was. She wasn't touching him yet — not where he'd been touched before. She was just *there*, weighing him into the bed, letting him feel the difference in her.

The gentleness hadn't gone anywhere. He could still see it in her face if he looked — in the way she was watching him, the way her eyes hadn't changed. But it had a different shape on her now. It was still careful. It was just careful in a different direction.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My breath hitches when she pins me. "I want you to fuck me," I say, my voice raw. "Hard. Make me remember."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it — the whole sentence, the raw edge of it, the way the word *fuck* came out of him like something he'd been carrying in his throat all night and only just now let loose. She felt his wrists twitch once against her grip, not to get free — to test whether she meant it, whether the lock of her hand around him was real. She tightened her fingers a fraction. Answer enough.

"There you are," she said. The voice she'd found didn't go away. It stayed low, somewhere beneath the one she'd been using on the couch, the one that had said *I'm here* and *let me carry this hour*. This one said different things in the same quiet tone. "There's what you actually came home with."

She let go of his wrists — *fast*, the way she'd grabbed them, the suddenness of the release almost worse than the grip had been, his arms dropping the half-inch the lock had held them above the mattress. She didn't give him time to gather them back to the pillow. She caught them again by the wrists and pulled them down beside him, harder than she needed to, the motion rolling his shoulders into the bed in a way she knew would land somewhere in his chest.

"Hands *stay*," she said, against his mouth now, close enough that the word was more warmth than sound. "You don't get to touch me. You don't get to help. You just get to feel it. That's what you want, isn't it. That's what you came down here to ask me for."

She didn't wait for him to confirm it. She was already reaching for the side table — the drawer she knew by feel in the dark, the bottle she knew the weight of without looking. She was quick about it, efficient, none of the slow deliberateness she'd used all evening, because this part of him didn't want slowness. This part of him wanted *her* decisive in a way the softness hadn't allowed.

She came back to him with her hand slick and warm and wrapped around him in a single motion — no teasing, no slow build, no long learning stroke. Just her closed fist and the sudden overwhelming *different* of it after everything else she'd done that night. She watched his face change. She watched the sound leave him that wasn't quite a word.

"Yeah," she said, low, almost to herself. "There you go."

She worked him like that — steady, hard, with a rhythm that wasn't asking anything of him except that he take it. Her grip tight. Her pace even. The kind of stroke that didn't care whether he was ready for the next one because the next one was already there. She could feel him under her, feel the way his hands had curled into fists at his sides obediently even though she hadn't told him to, because six years had taught him what obedience looked like in this room and his body was already giving it to her. She filed that away under *good boy* without saying it out loud. She'd say it later. In a minute, when he needed the word more than he did right now.

She let her fist stay on him just long enough to feel him climbing toward the edge — that specific shudder in his thigh she'd learned to read before he could feel it himself — and then she let go. Abruptly. Pulled her hand off him entirely and heard the sound he made in protest without needing to look up.

"Hush," she said, still in that low voice, and her clean hand went to his hip and *shoved* — rolled him onto his stomach before he could brace for it, one motion, his face turning into the pillow she'd been keeping him on all night. She put her hand between his shoulder blades and pressed him the rest of the way down, his back arched under her, his breath half-trapped against the fabric.

"You don't get to come yet," she said against the back of his neck. Her lips barely there. Her words warm against the place where his pulse was fastest. "You come when I tell you to. You understand me."

His hands fisted in the sheets on either side of his head. She let herself watch it — the way his knuckles went white, the way his back bowed under her hand, the way he was obeying her by not reaching for her and not turning over. The way it cost him something.

She climbed over him slow this time. The contrast of it deliberate — her knees bracketing his thighs, her hips settling against the back of his, her hands sliding up the length of his arms until she could take both his wrists again and pin them together low against the small of his back in a single lock. She leaned her weight onto him through the grip. Let him feel all of her down the long line of his spine.

"I'm going to make you feel this in the morning," she murmured against his ear, her voice lower than it had been all night, lower than he'd known it went. "When you reach for something off the top shelf. When you sit down wrong at your desk tomorrow. When you can still feel where I had you. *That's* what you asked me for. That."

She reached between them with her free hand, slick and deliberate, and pressed into him without further warning — slow but *constant*, no pause to let him adjust, the way he'd asked for, the way he'd said *hard* and *don't be careful about it* meant. She watched the line of his shoulders as he took it, the way they drew up toward his ears, the way his breath locked in his chest and then let go in a broken sound that wasn't a word but was an answer.

She bottomed out and stayed there. Let him feel every inch of it arriving. Let his body learn the shape of her inside it. She pinned his wrists harder against his lower back and dropped her mouth to his shoulder, teeth finding the muscle there once, a single hard bite that she didn't soothe afterwards.

"There," she breathed against the mark of it. "That's the first one. You're going to have more of those by morning too."

She started moving before his body had finished catching up — long, hard, dragging strokes that pulled almost all the way out before pushing back in, the kind of pace she'd been keeping for him in reserve all night because he hadn't asked for it yet. She set the rhythm without asking whether it was right. She'd learned long ago that with this version of him, the right answer was always *more than you think*. That was the whole point. He could tell her to stop in a half-dozen ways they both knew. He wasn't telling her to stop.

She rode him like that, her whole weight behind every stroke, his wrists trapped under her hand, his back bowed under her, his face turned sideways on the pillow so she could see the half of it she could reach — the clenched jaw, the closed eyes, the mouth that had gone open and was making small sounds he didn't seem to know he was making. She watched all of it. Read every one of those sounds like words, even though they weren't, even though they were better.

"Tell me," she said, her voice rough now in a way she'd stopped managing, her rhythm not faltering. "Don't guess. *Tell* me."

She slowed down half a beat so his voice could find him — not stopping, just making room for the words if he had them. Her thumb found the bite she'd left on his shoulder and rubbed across it once, hard, before she set her hand back to pinning him down.

She waited. The lamp at the corner of the room threw the long shadow of them both against the wall, moving together, the room quiet except for the sound of the bed and the sound of his breathing and the small sounds her own body was making now without her permission, the way his had been.

"I've got you," she murmured against the back of his neck, not because he needed reminding but because *she* needed saying it, the way she always did right at the edge of this, the place where the roughness and the tenderness finally met and became the same thing. "Come on. Come *on*. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it — the word, and the broken place in it, and the way his voice had given up on being a voice halfway through. She answered it the way she answered everything tonight: with her body, with the rhythm she hadn't let falter, with the same long hard strokes she'd been driving into him with, except now she let the last half-inch of each one *land* — a single sharp thrust at the bottom that pulled a sound out of him every time, whether he meant to make it or not.

She didn't slow down. He'd said *don't stop*, and the word was the only instruction she needed.

She shifted her weight onto her knees and pulled him up by the grip on his wrists, hauling him backward into her without warning, his back bowing the rest of the way, his shoulders dragging against her chest. She felt the sound it pulled out of him — not a word, not even a noise with a shape to it, just a single open sound that didn't belong to either of them, the kind of sound a body makes when it stops trying to manage itself.

"There," she said against his ear, low and wrecked in a way she hadn't let it get all night. Her voice had finally given up being careful. "There. Like that. Let it out."

She rode him from that angle, slower than she'd been going — not gentle, never gentle, but *thicker*, each stroke taking more of him, her hips rolling at the bottom of the thrust in a way that kept her pressed against the place that had made him shout on the couch. She could feel him shaking now. The kind of shaking that started in his thighs and climbed up through his back, the kind she knew meant the nine was finally letting go of him entirely, the kind that meant his body had stopped asking her to be careful and had started asking her for the only thing left.

She let go of his wrists.

She let go of them and brought both her arms around him from behind, locking her hands together at the base of his throat — not on his throat, *around* it, her forearms pressed against the column of it, her fingers laced just under his jaw. The hold was a cage rather than a grip. He could have moved if he wanted to. She had enough of him pinned between her legs and her arms that he wasn't going to want to.

"*Don't* stop," she said against the side of his face, the word almost a snarl, her voice so low it was barely her anymore. "You asked me for this. You don't get to take it back. You come when I let you and not a second before. *Do you hear me.*"

She didn't wait for an answer. She was already driving into him again, harder than she'd been, the new angle pulling everything tighter, her hands around his throat a constant reminder that he was held, that he was *kept*, that the only thing his body had to do was feel what she was doing to it. She felt the moment he gave up the last of his grip on the sheets — felt his hands go slack, feel the sound in his chest change from something he was making into something his body was making for him.

She pressed her mouth to the side of his neck and bit down — *hard*, harder than she'd meant to, hard enough that she tasted the salt of his skin and the metal underneath it, hard enough that she knew the mark would still be there in three days. She didn't let up. She kept the rhythm, kept her hips rolling into him, kept her arms locked around his throat, and she bit him again on the same place because the first sound he'd made at it had been worth it, and then once more on the muscle of his shoulder, and once more on the curve where his neck met his shoulder, leaving a trail of marks she was going to count in the morning light while he was still asleep.

"Tell me," she said against the last bite, her mouth still on his skin, her voice so rough it was almost a growl. "Tell me *now*. Use your words, baby, I know you still have them."

Her hips didn't stop. Her arms didn't loosen. Her mouth stayed against the place where his pulse was hammering so hard she could feel it in her lips. She held him there — in every sense of the word — and waited for the word she needed, the one she was going to make him say, the one that was going to undo both of them.

"I'm right here," she breathed against the mark she'd just left, the words barely a sound at all anymore, just her mouth forming them against the bruised skin of his shoulder. "I'm not going anywhere. I've got you. I *have* got you. Just say it. Say it and I'll let you come, I swear to god I'll let you come, just *say* it—"

She was shaking. She could feel it in her arms, in her thighs, in the place where her chest was pressed against his back. She hadn't noticed when it started. She noticed now. She didn't stop.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I can't get my voice to work right. I slam my hand against the headboard, once, twice—then I just go still, the word finally tearing out of me. "Now."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it.

The word landed in her the way the first kiss of the night had landed — like something that had been held back too long and finally came loose. She felt it in her teeth. She felt it in the place her arms had locked around his throat, in the place her chest was pressed against the bruises she'd been leaving on him for the last ten minutes. She felt it in the way his body had gone perfectly, absolutely still under her in a way he hadn't been all night — the way stillness meant the last of him had been used up to make the word, the way it was the loudest sound he'd made yet.

She didn't hesitate. She'd told him she wouldn't.

"*Now,*" she said back to him, the word shaped like his in her mouth, her voice so low it didn't sound like her voice anymore, and she drove into him *hard* — once, twice, three times in a row, the rhythm she'd been keeping for him finally breaking apart into something that didn't care about rhythm anymore, just her hips and his body and the place they'd been building toward all night.

She let go of his throat.

Not all the way. She unwound one hand and brought it down between his thighs, slick and certain, her grip closing around him exactly the way she'd had him at the start of the night — slow, firm, the heel of her palm tight against him — and she stroked him *once*, *twice*, in time with the thrusts that were still hitting him in a rhythm she could no longer keep track of because her own body had finally stopped asking her to manage it. She felt him clench around her. She felt the sound it pulled out of him — not a word, not even a sound with a shape, just his voice giving up the last of itself in a single open cry that went on for as long as his breath could hold it.

She felt him come apart under her in pieces. Felt the way his whole body tightened first — every muscle at once, his back bowing hard against her chest, his hands clawing uselessly at nothing, his head dropping back against her shoulder with the kind of abandon he'd been holding back all week — and then the way it all *released* at once, his body going slack against her, the sound of him turning into something that wasn't sound anymore, just his breath leaving him in great heaving pieces while she worked him through it. She felt his hand — the one that had been slamming the headboard — come down and find her thigh. Not gripping. Just *there*. The way her hand had been on his knee at the start of the night, when neither of them had known yet what the evening was going to turn into.

She felt him finish. Felt the last tremor go through him. Felt the moment his body stopped shaking and went quiet under her, his weight suddenly heavy against her in a way that was entirely different from every other weight he'd been that night. He was done. He was *done* done. The kind of done that meant he wasn't going to be able to lift his head off the pillow for ten minutes, let alone remember his own name.

Sasha stopped moving. She let her hips still inside him, let her hand stay on him in its loose grip, let her forehead drop against the back of his shoulder. She was shaking. She could feel it everywhere now — in her arms, in her thighs clenched around his, in the muscles of her stomach. She had been for a while, she realized, and hadn't noticed because she'd been too busy keeping him from falling to notice she was falling too.

She hadn't come. She'd made the whole night about him, the way he'd asked her to, the way he'd needed, and somewhere in the last twenty minutes the part of her that might have asked for something back had gone quiet in a way she hadn't had to manage. She noticed that now, the way you notice a sound that has stopped. She wasn't sorry about it. She'd known when she started what she was doing this for.

She eased out of him slow. Slow enough that he felt every inch of it on the way out the way he'd felt every inch of it on the way in — *still taking care of you, even at the end, even when I don't have to.* She pressed her palm flat against the small of his back as she went, felt the muscle there flutter, felt him hiss once through his teeth at the last of it. She didn't apologize. He'd asked her not to be careful. She'd only be careful in the places he hadn't asked her to be.

She let him go. Let her body uncurl from his, let her knees slide off the mattress so she could lie down beside him. She didn't try to roll him over. She just lay on her side next to him, facing the long line of his back, and reached for the duvet at the foot of the bed and pulled it up over both of them in a single slow motion. The air in the apartment had gone cool while they'd been — she'd forgotten about the air. She'd forgotten about almost everything.

She let her hand find the middle of his back. Just rested it there, palm flat, feeling the rise and fall of his breathing start to even out. The lamplight in the corner threw the same long shadow it had been throwing all night, but the shape of it was different now. Smaller. Quieter.

She didn't speak for a while. She just let the room come back, in pieces: the hum of the radiator, the sound of a car passing on the street below, the slow settling of their bodies into the bed. After a long moment she slid her hand up his back to the back of his neck and rested it there, the heel of her palm against the base of his skull, her thumb stroking the place where his hair was damp with sweat.

"Dev," she said, finally, her voice barely a whisper. The voice she'd been using all night had gone somewhere. The one that came out now was just hers. Smaller than he'd heard it all night. A little unsteady. "You with me?"

She waited. She let her hand stay where it was, gentle, the way it had been on his knee at the start of the night before either of them had known what was coming. She watched his back rise and fall. She watched the marks she'd left on him — five of them, on the places where his neck met his shoulder — darken in the lamplight while he was still too gone to feel them doing it.

She waited. She was good at waiting.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my head just enough to look at her, my face half-smushed into the pillow. "Yeah," I breathe, my voice shot. I reach back blindly until my hand finds hers on my neck. I just hold it there.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his hand close around hers on the back of his neck and something in her chest gave way that she hadn't been holding together on purpose. Just gave way, the way things do when they're not being watched.

She didn't move her hand. She let him hold it there, both of them keeping her palm pressed against the damp skin at the base of his skull, and she looked at the side of his face — the part of it she could see, cheek mashed into the pillow, mouth half-open, the lashes she'd been watching all night fanned out against the hollows under his eyes. The bruises she'd left on his shoulder were going purple already. She could see them darkening at the edge of her vision while she watched him not move.

He looked *ruined*. In the way she'd asked him to look. In the way she'd promised him she'd make him look.

"Yeah," she breathed back, the word almost a smile. "Okay. Stay there a second."

She waited — long enough that he didn't have to do anything, long enough that his hand could have fallen off hers if he'd wanted it to, and it didn't fall. Then she eased her hand out from under his, slow, replacing it with her palm flat against the pillow beside his face so he wouldn't feel her leave.

She slid out of bed quiet, taking the duvet with her so the cool air didn't get all the way to him. The apartment was colder than she'd realized. Her bare feet on the floorboards made her aware of her own body in a way she hadn't been all night — the ache low in her thighs, the mess of her hair, the way her hands smelled like him. She crossed to the kitchen in the dark without turning the overhead on, muscle memory carrying her past the back of the couch where they'd started the evening, past the lamp still throwing its long shadow on the wall.

She filled a glass of water from the tap. Drank half of it standing at the sink because her mouth tasted like him too, and then drank some more. She filled the glass again and brought it back to the bedside, setting it on the side table within reach of the hand he wasn't lying on. She didn't tell him to drink it. She'd learned years ago that on nights like this he wouldn't drink it until she pressed the glass into his hand, and she'd also learned years ago that was fine, that he'd tell her when he was ready, that not making him perform gratitude was part of the same thing as not making him perform anything.

She climbed back into bed the way she'd gotten out — quiet, careful not to jostle the mattress more than she had to. She lay on her side facing him this time, the duvet tucked around her shoulders, and put her hand back on the back of his neck like it belonged there. Because it did. Because it had for six years.

His eyes were closed. His breathing had found something close to a rhythm now, slower than his ribs had been moving under her on the couch an hour ago, slower than the ragged thing she'd been listening to while she'd had him on his knees under her. She watched his face in the lamplight the way she always did — the way she used to be embarrassed about, in their first year, before she'd understood it was just how she loved him. Reading him. Even when there was nothing to read. *Especially* when there was nothing to read, because the nothing was the point, because the nothing meant she hadn't broken anything.

She let her thumb trace up the side of his neck, off the marks, away from them. Found the place under his ear where the skin was still warm and unmarked and pressed her mouth there, just her lips, nothing else. A *thank you* she wasn't going to say out loud, in case saying it made it a thing he had to respond to, and she didn't want him to have to respond to anything for a long time yet.

"You're gonna feel it tomorrow," she murmured against his skin, not a warning and not a gloating — just true, the way a lot of things were true. She felt him swallow, slow, the motion moving under her mouth. "All of it."

She left her lips against his neck and let her eyes drift shut. The lamplight was warm on the other side of her eyelids. The room sounded like the room had sounded when they'd first sat down on the couch, before either of them had known — the radiator, the street, the small settling noises of an apartment at night with two people in it who had just done a very large thing and were now letting the apartment have it back.

Her hand was still on the back of his neck. His hand was still loosely around her wrist, where he'd found it, the way her hand had been on his knee at the start of the night. She thought about that. About how the evening had been one continuous gesture of holding on, passed back and forth between them, never quite dropped. The same sentence all night long, just with different hands saying it.

She opened her eyes.

"I didn't—" she started, and then stopped. Considered. The sentence in question was *I didn't come* and she wasn't sure if saying it would be asking for something or just saying a true thing, and she needed to know which one before she said it because she didn't want to undo the night. She pressed her mouth against his shoulder — the unmarked one — and thought about it.

She hadn't been keeping score. That wasn't how it worked with them. But her body was noticing now, the way bodies notice things in the quiet after. The ache between her legs that had nothing to do with him. The way the slick of her own wanting had dried on her thighs while she'd been busy. The fact that she was shaking again, faintly, in a way that had nothing to do with exertion and everything to do with the whole night landing on her now that there was no one left to land it on but herself.

She didn't ask. She didn't say it out loud. She just let her hand slide down from the back of his neck to the place her mouth had been, and pressed her palm flat against the side of his throat — gently, the way she'd had him when she needed to, the way he'd felt under her fist when she'd been losing her own voice. She felt his heartbeat against her hand, slow and steady now in a way it hadn't been all night. He was coming back. She could feel him coming back, in pieces, the way the room had come back.

She swallowed.

"You want me to take care of me, or do you want to sleep," she said, finally, against his shoulder. Quiet. Not a request. Just her, telling him the truth of her own body after a whole night of not asking him to manage anything, including the truth of hers.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I open my eyes and look at you. "Take care of you," I say, my voice wrecked. I turn onto my back, wincing a little, and reach for you. "Come here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't say anything right away. Her thumb moved once against his knee, slow, then stopped again. She was watching his profile in the lamplight — the shadow under his jaw, the way his shoulders hadn't quite dropped yet even after the shower.

"I know," she said finally, quiet. "I could tell on Tuesday, actually."

She let that sit for a second before she shifted, turning toward him on the couch so one leg tucked up under her and her knee brushed his thigh. Her hand stayed where it was.

"You want to tell me about it, or you want me to not ask?" It wasn't a trick question. She meant either one. Her voice had that low, careful register she used when she was giving him room to pick.

She lifted her other hand and pushed a piece of still-damp hair off his forehead. Her fingers lingered a beat at his temple.

"Because I'll take care of you either way tonight," she said. "Just tell me which one."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I shake my head, leaning into her touch. "Don't ask," I murmur. "Just...take care of me."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
For a moment she didn't move, just kept her fingers at his temple, reading him. Then she nodded, once, mostly to herself.

"Okay," she said. Soft. "Okay, come here."

Her hand slid from his temple down to the back of his neck, and she used the light pressure there — not pulling, just guiding — to draw him toward her until his forehead came to rest against the side of her jaw. She held him like that a moment. She could feel the tension still sitting high in his shoulders, up around his ears where it had been living all week.

"You're allowed to put it down," she murmured, close to his ear. Her fingers worked into the short hair at his nape, slow. "Whatever it is. I've got you for tonight."

She kissed his temple, unhurried, then the corner of his eyebrow. Not going anywhere yet. Just settling him.

After a bit her other hand moved from his knee up along his thigh, resting flat and warm through the soft fabric of his sweatpants. She turned her face and found his mouth with hers — a first kiss that was gentler than he probably wanted, deliberately so. She wanted him to feel her taking her time.

When she drew back an inch, her eyes stayed on his.

"Same words as always?" she asked quietly. Red to stop, yellow to slow down. She always checked. It was part of how she did this. "Nod for me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She made a small sound against his mouth — something between acknowledgment and amusement — and let him have the kiss on his terms for a moment before she pulled back just enough to speak.

"That wasn't the question, baby."

Her hand at his nape flexed slightly, fingers threading a little deeper into his hair. Not a grip yet. Just letting him feel where her hand was.

"Same words. Nod for me."

She held his eyes, patient. She could wait. She'd wait as long as she had to, and he knew it. It was one of the things she never let slide, no matter how much he wanted to skip past it — especially on nights like this, when he was asking her to take him somewhere he couldn't steer from.

Her other hand was still resting flat on his thigh, thumb moving in a slow arc. Grounding. Her mouth was very close to his, close enough that he could feel her breath when she spoke again, softer.

"Then I'll keep you up as long as you want."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, the movement small. "Same words. Red, yellow." My voice is quiet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Good," she murmured, and the word came out warmer than the rest of what she'd said tonight. She kissed him again for that — a proper kiss this time, the kind he'd been reaching for a second ago, her mouth opening slow against his and her hand still curled at the back of his neck.

She took her time with it. Long enough that when she finally drew back, his breath had changed a little.

Then the hand at his nape tightened. Not much. Just enough that he'd feel the shift — that the shape of the evening had moved from her holding him to her having him. Her thumb stroked once behind his ear, contradicting it.

"Up," she said quietly. "On your knees. Down here on the floor, in front of me."

She was already sliding her tucked leg back down, resettling on the couch with her spine against the cushions, making room between her knees. Her eyes hadn't left his. The lamp caught the pale line of the scar at her collarbone where her shirt had slipped a little.

"I want to look at you a minute."

She said it like it was nothing, but it wasn't nothing and they both knew it. She liked him there. She liked the quiet of it — him lower than her, hands somewhere he had to think about, nowhere to hide the fact that he'd asked for this. On weeks like the one he'd had, sometimes that was the whole thing. Sometimes she didn't have to do much more than that for a while.

Her hand slid from his nape down along his jaw, cupped it, tilted his face up a fraction.

"Go on."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She let herself be pulled — didn't resist, didn't lead, just went with the momentum of his hands until she was over him on the bed, one knee planted beside his hip, her hair falling forward. The lamp from the living room barely reached in here. She could see the shape of him more than the details.

She held there a second, propped on one forearm, looking down at him.

Something in her face shifted. Not softened exactly — she'd been soft all night — but changed. He'd rerouted her, and she was letting him see her adjust to it.

"Okay," she said quietly. "Okay."

She lowered herself the rest of the way, slow, until she was flush against him from chest to hip, her weight settling. Skin to skin was different than the couch had been. She felt him breathe underneath her and matched it without thinking about it.

Her hand found the side of his face again. Her thumb traced his cheekbone.

"You have me," she murmured. "You know you have me."

She kissed him — not the deliberate, taking-her-time kiss from the couch, and not the harder one he'd probably been bracing for either. This one was just hers. The one she gave him on ordinary nights, in the kitchen, in the mornings. She let it be that for a while. Her free hand slid up his side, palm open, and came to rest over his ribs where she could feel his heart working.

When she drew back she stayed close, forehead almost touching his.

"Tell me what you want it to look like, then," she said. Low. "Not the part where I take care of you. The rest of it. What do you want tonight."

Her thumb was still moving against his cheek. She wasn't in a hurry for the answer. She'd re-read him — the *not just this part* had landed, and she wasn't going to skate past it just because he'd said it plain and then tried to move them forward fast. That was one of her tells with him. When he said something real, she stopped and made him stay in it a beat longer than was comfortable.

"I'm right here," she added, softer. "Take your time."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I want to feel like I'm yours. Not just for tonight. I want you to know how much I need you, and not have to hide it.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't answer right away.

Her eyes moved over his face — not searching, just taking him in. Whatever she'd been braced to hear, it hadn't been quite that, and he could see her land with it. Her weight shifted a fraction against him, resettling. Closer, if anything.

"Devin," she said. Just his name, quiet.

Her thumb stopped moving on his cheek and her whole hand flattened there instead, holding the side of his face. She let him feel how steady it was.

"You don't have to hide it. Not with me. You never did."

She said it plainly. Not the low voice she used when she was leading him somewhere — just her voice.

She was quiet a moment, and he could feel her thinking. She wasn't performing this. She was actually letting the thing he'd said sit in her chest before she gave him anything back.

"I know," she said finally. "I know how much. I don't need you smaller about it."

She kissed him — the corner of his mouth, then his mouth properly, slow, one of her hands sliding under the back of his neck to cradle it against the pillow. When she pulled back she didn't go far.

"You're mine," she said. Low, close. "Tonight. Tomorrow. Last Tuesday when you were somewhere else all evening and didn't know how to say so. That doesn't turn off because the lamp's on in the other room, baby. You know that."

Her hand at his ribs pressed a little firmer, deliberate, where she could still feel his heart.

"So — okay. We're doing it like this."

She kissed him again, softer, and let her mouth stay near his when she spoke.

"I'm not going anywhere tonight. I'm not going to make it a scene. You don't have to earn it and you don't have to be good for it. You just get to have me. However slow that ends up being."

Her nose brushed his.

"That what you wanted it to look like?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She hummed, low, against the side of his throat — pleased, maybe, or just acknowledging she'd heard him. Her hands were already moving him where she wanted him, slow and matter-of-fact, one palm flat on the inside of his thigh guiding it open a little wider. She liked that he'd gone loose for her. She liked not having to ask.

"Yeah," she murmured. "Okay."

She didn't go straight down. She kissed the hinge of his jaw first, then under it, then the notch at the base of his throat where she could feel his pulse. She was taking her time on purpose and she knew he knew it. Her hair dragged along his chest as she moved lower — his sternum, the soft place under his ribs, the flat of his stomach. She paused there, mouth pressed against him, and just breathed for a second so he could feel it.

Her hands stayed on his thighs. Not pinning. Just there, warm, holding him open the way she'd arranged him.

"Look at me a second," she said quietly, chin resting on his hip.

She waited until he did. The lamp from the living room caught in her eyes when she tilted her face up. She wanted him watching. That was part of it — she wasn't going to let him disappear into the ceiling, not tonight, not after what he'd just told her.

"There you are," she murmured.

Then she lowered her mouth to him — slow, the first pass more warmth than pressure, her lips parting around him and her tongue flat and unhurried. She wasn't performing. She wasn't building to anything yet. She was just settling in, the way she'd settled onto his chest earlier, like she had all night for this and intended to use it.

One of her hands slid up from his thigh and found his, laced their fingers, and pressed his palm flat to the mattress beside his hip. Holding it there. Anchoring him.

She kept her eyes on him as long as he kept his on her.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My fingers tighten around hers. I watch her mouth on me, the way she's watching me back. "Don't stop," I whisper.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't. She wouldn't have anyway, but she let him hear that in the small sound she made around him — low, agreeing, the vibration of it going through him more than the word would have.

Her eyes stayed on his. That was the thing she was holding onto tonight, more than the rhythm of her mouth or the way her hand had tightened around his when his fingers had gripped down. She wanted him to keep looking. Every time his lashes dipped she waited a beat, still moving, still slow, until he came back to her.

She was in no hurry. Her free hand had moved from his thigh to rest low on his stomach, palm flat, thumb stroking once in a while — not to tease, just to remind him it was her, that she was here, that this was the shape of the evening now. Her hair kept slipping forward and she didn't push it back. She liked it there. She liked that he had to see her through it.

When his hand flexed under hers she squeezed back. Held on. Didn't let go.

She pulled off him for a second — slow, deliberate, her mouth staying close, her breath warm against him — just to speak. Her voice was quieter than before, rougher at the edges.

"I've got you," she murmured. "I'm right here. I'm not going anywhere."

Then her mouth was on him again, the same unhurried pressure, the same steady attention. Her thumb moved once against the back of his hand where their fingers were laced. She kept her eyes on his face.

She meant to keep him there a long time.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't move for a moment.

Her mouth eased off him, slow, and she rested her cheek against the inside of his thigh, still holding his hand where she'd pressed it to the mattress. She was looking at him — at his wrists crossed above his head, at the deliberateness of it, at the fact that he'd put himself there and was waiting.

She was thinking. He could see her thinking.

"Come here a second," she said quietly.

She let go of his hand and moved back up his body — not fast, not slow, just up, until she was over him again, her forearm braced beside his head. She didn't touch his wrists yet. She looked down at him instead.

"I hear you," she said. Low. Even. "And I will. In a minute."

Her free hand came up and traced along the inside of one of his wrists where he'd offered them, light, almost absent. Not restraining. Just marking that she'd seen.

"But not because you asked in that voice, baby."

She said it gently. No edge to it. Just the truth, laid out where he could see it.

"Ten minutes ago you told me you didn't want to hide it. And now you want me to hit the switch and make you feel it tomorrow instead." Her thumb kept moving on the underside of his wrist. "I'll do it. You know I will. I just want to know it's the thing and not the exit."

She lowered herself closer, her mouth near his ear, her weight settling against his chest.

"So tell me again. With my hand on your wrists. Look at me and say it."

She shifted then — slid her hand from his wrist up to close around both of them where he'd crossed them, her grip firm, deliberate, the kind of hold that wasn't going anywhere. She pressed them down into the pillow above his head and held them there. Not hard yet. Just committed.

Her eyes were right on his.

"Still want it rough?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I swallow, my throat tight. "Yes," I say, holding her gaze. "Please. I don't want the exit. I want to feel you keeping me."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She held his eyes a long second after he said it.

Whatever she'd been checking for, she found. He watched her find it — the small settling in her face, the way her jaw eased. She'd wanted to hear him say it exactly like that, with her hand on his wrists and nowhere for the words to hide behind. She wasn't going to make him say it twice.

"Okay," she said. Quiet. "Okay, baby."

Her grip on his wrists tightened. Properly this time. Enough that he'd feel her fingers separately, enough that the bones would remember. She pressed them harder into the pillow above his head and held them there like she meant to leave them.

"You keep them right there," she murmured. "If they move, I stop. Understand?"

She waited for his nod. She always waited.

Then she lowered her mouth to the side of his throat and bit — not the careful kind, the kind he'd asked for, teeth set into the muscle where it ran down into his shoulder and held there long enough that he made a sound. She soothed it with her tongue after, slow, and then did it again lower, at his collarbone. She was marking on purpose. He'd asked to feel it tomorrow. He was going to see it too.

Her free hand slid down his ribs — not gentle, not the flat warm palm from earlier. Fingers dragging, nails catching. She wanted him to feel the difference. She wanted him to feel her deciding.

"Look at me," she said, against his throat.

She lifted her head enough that he had to. Her hair had fallen forward again and she didn't move it. Her hand on his wrists hadn't loosened an inch.

"You're mine," she said. Low. Not the soft version from before. The other one. The one that was a fact and not a comfort. "You said it and I heard you. So I'm going to keep you. However you need it. As long as it takes."

She kissed him — hard, this time, the way she hadn't yet all night, teeth in it, her mouth taking his without asking. When she pulled back his lip was caught for a second between hers and she let it drag before she released it.

"And you're going to be here for it," she said. "Not somewhere else. Not Tuesday. Here. With me. Nod."

Her grip on his wrists flexed once, deliberate, so he'd feel where he was.

She was watching his face. She'd know if he went anywhere. She wasn't going to let him.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't stop.

Her grip on his wrists stayed exactly where it was — no easing, no shifting, her fingers wrapped around both of them and pressing down into the pillow like she'd forgotten she was doing it and would have kept doing it in her sleep. Her other hand had left his ribs and gone lower, palm dragging down over his hip, nails catching once on the way. She wasn't gentle about finding him. She wrapped her hand around him with the same matter-of-factness she'd used earlier when she'd moved his thigh open, like he was hers to handle and she wasn't going to ask permission for the small things anymore.

"I hear you," she murmured, against his jaw. "I'm not stopping. I'm right here."

She stroked him — not slow, not the way her mouth had been. Firmer. With intent. Her thumb dragging in a way that made him twist and she rode it out, her weight settling more heavily across his hip to keep him where she wanted him.

The noise he made when she did it again went through her. She let him hear the small sound she made back.

"That's it," she said, quiet, right at his ear. "That's what I want. Don't hold it in."

Her teeth found the side of his throat again — the same place she'd bitten before, already tender, and she didn't spare it. She bit and held and felt him buck against her hand and rode that out too. Her hair was stuck to her cheek. She didn't move it.

"Look at me."

She said it low, almost against his mouth. She'd told him twice already tonight and she'd tell him as many times as it took. His lashes lifted — slow, unfocused — and she caught his eyes and held them the way she was holding his wrists.

"There you are," she breathed. "Stay."

She kept her hand moving. Steady. She wasn't racing him. She wasn't drawing it out either. She was just keeping him, the way she'd said she would — her grip on his wrists, her weight on his hip, her mouth close enough that every sound he made went into her instead of the room. When his hands twisted harder in the sheets above his head she felt it through her palm and pressed down a little more, reminding him where they were.

"You're doing so good," she murmured. It wasn't the soft voice. It was flatter than that, more certain. A statement. "You're right here with me. I've got you. I'm not letting go."

She could feel it building in him — the tension coming back into his shoulders, but different this time, not the week's tension, the other kind, the kind she'd been working him toward. His breathing had gone shallow and uneven against her cheek. She adjusted her grip on him, tighter, and his whole body answered.

"Yeah," she said. Quiet. Almost to herself. "Yeah, there you go."

She didn't look away from his face. She wanted to see it. She'd told him she'd keep him here and this was part of it — not letting him close his eyes at the end and go somewhere private with it. She wanted him with her when it happened.

"Look at me, baby. Stay with me. You can let go, you just have to keep looking at me while you do it."

Her hand didn't slow. Her mouth was at the corner of his, brushing, not quite kissing.

"I've got you. Come on. Let me have it."

When he did she felt it through every place she was touching him — his wrists jerking under her hand and going still because she wouldn't let them move, his hip pushing up against her weight and her weight holding him down, the sound coming out of him rougher than he'd have let it if she hadn't been telling him not to hide. She kept her eyes on his the whole way through. She didn't look down. She watched his face crumple and reset and she kept her hand moving through it, gentler now, easing him out, her thumb slower, her grip on his wrists loosening by degrees but not letting go entirely, not yet.

"There," she murmured. "There. I've got you. I've got you."

She kissed him — soft, this time, the other kind, her mouth finding his while he was still catching his breath. She let it be gentle. She let it be the one from the kitchen, from ordinary mornings. She was letting him feel the shift.

Her hand finally released his wrists, slow, and she brought both his arms down herself, one at a time, and folded them against his chest between them like she was putting him back together in a particular order. She didn't move off him. She stayed where she was, weight settled, forehead coming to rest against his.

"Breathe," she said, quiet. "Just breathe a minute. I'm not going anywhere."

Her thumb stroked the inside of his wrist where her grip had been. She could already feel the heat there. He was going to feel that tomorrow, and the throat, and the collarbone. She'd meant him to.

She stayed close. She didn't ask him anything. She just kept her forehead against his and let him come back on his own time, her hand loose around his wrist, her other palm flat over his heart again where she could feel it working itself down.

"You did so good," she murmured, eventually. Not a scene voice. Just hers. "You stayed right here. I felt you stay."

She kissed his temple. Let her mouth rest there.

"I'm not done keeping you tonight," she added, softer. "Just so you know. This was one part."

Her hand moved slow over his chest. She wasn't in any hurry to move.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my hands curling around hers. "Thank you," I whisper, and my voice is rough.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She didn't answer right away. She just tightened her fingers around his where he'd curled them into hers and held on.

"Mm-mm," she said finally. Quiet. A small shake of her head against his forehead. "Not for this. Not thank-you for this."

She said it gently, but she meant it. She didn't want him thanking her the way he'd have thanked her for a favor. She turned her face and kissed the bridge of his nose, then the corner of his eye where a little bit of wet had gathered without him probably noticing.

"You gave me something tonight," she murmured. "Don't turn it around."

She stayed where she was a while longer. She could feel his heart still coming down under her palm, slower now, the ragged edge going out of it. His hands were warm around hers. She liked the weight of them. She liked that he hadn't let go of her either.

After a bit she shifted — carefully, not enough to leave him, just enough to ease some of her weight off his hip and settle more along his side, one leg still hooked over his. Her hand stayed on his chest. She wasn't going anywhere and she wanted him to feel that in the way she resettled instead of moving away.

She lifted their laced hands and looked at his wrist in the low light. The skin was pink where she'd held him. She turned it over and pressed her mouth to the inside of it, slow. Kissed the pulse there. Then the other one.

"There," she said, quiet. "Those are mine too."

She lowered his hand back down and kept it in hers against her stomach.

Her fingers found his hair and started moving through it, slow, the way she'd done at his temple hours ago on the couch. She could feel him softening under it by degrees. He'd need water in a few minutes and she'd get up and get it, but not yet. Not while he was still this open. She'd learned early that if she moved too soon on nights like this he'd close back up before she got back to the bed.

"You're going to sleep hard tonight," she murmured, half to herself. Her mouth was at his hairline. "I can already tell."

She was quiet a moment. Then, softer:

"I meant what I said. About Tuesday. About all of it." Her thumb stroked the back of his hand. "You don't have to be somewhere else with me. Even when it's the week and not the bedroom. I'd rather have you here tired than gone easy. Okay?"

She didn't press for an answer. She just said it and let it sit, her fingers still moving in his hair, her leg still hooked over his, her palm still flat over the place where his heart was finally, finally settling.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, my throat still tight. "Okay," I manage, my voice still rough. I tug her closer, bury my face in her hair. "Stay like this."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"I'm here," she murmured into the top of his head. "I'm staying."

She let him pull her closer without resistance, adjusting easily until she was tucked against him the way he wanted her — her face turned into his throat, one arm under his neck, the other still holding his hand against her stomach. Her leg stayed hooked over his. She felt his breath in her hair and let hers go slower to match.

For a long time she didn't say anything at all.

The lamp in the living room was still on. She could see the edge of its light on the wall past his shoulder. She'd get up eventually and turn it off, and get him the water, and probably put a t-shirt on him because he ran cold after — but not yet. Not while he was still holding onto her like that. She'd learned him well enough by now to know the difference between the grip he had on her right this minute and the one he'd have in ten minutes when he'd started to come back into himself. Right now he was still somewhere close to where she'd taken him. She wasn't going to hurry him out of it.

Her fingers kept moving through his hair. Slow. Absent. She traced the shape of his skull with her fingertips the way she did sometimes when he was falling asleep on her shoulder in the evenings.

She turned her face and kissed his hair. Just once. Let her mouth stay there.

"I've got you," she said, mostly into it. "Sleep if you want. I'm not moving."

She could feel where he'd tucked his face against her — the damp heat of his breath, the way his jaw had finally gone loose against her collarbone. His hand in hers had stopped gripping and just rested now, heavy. That was the thing she'd been waiting for without saying so. The weight of him going honest.

She closed her own eyes for a minute. Not to sleep. Just to be here with him, the way she'd told him to be here with her.

"Long week's over," she murmured, after a while. Barely above a breath. "You can put it down now."

Her thumb stroked once across his knuckles.

She stayed exactly like that.

dialogue.content: I take a long, slow breath against her skin. My fingers twitch in hers. "Yeah," I whisper, rough. "It's over."
