dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the slight shift of his weight against her shoulder and stayed where she was. Her thumb moved once across his knee, a small gesture, then went still again.

"Long week," she echoed. Not dismissive—just giving the words back to him, leaving room in case he wanted to fill the silence with more. She knew him well enough by now to know he might not.

Her free hand came up to the back of his neck, fingers curling lightly into the damp hair at his nape. She let her touch rest there, warm against his skin.

"You don't have to talk about it," she said quietly. "But you're here now. With me."

She turned her head just enough to press a kiss to his temple—brief, unhurried. Her hand on his neck didn't move away. She could feel the tension he was carrying in the set of his shoulders, the way he was holding himself.

"Tell me what you need."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes at the kiss. "Just... tell me what to do tonight. I don't wanna make any decisions."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's fingers stilled at the back of his neck for a moment, then resumed their slow movement through his hair. She heard what he was asking—not just for company, but for direction. For the relief of not having to hold the reins for a while.

Six years meant she knew the shape of this request. She also knew to make sure she understood it right.

"Okay," she said simply. No hesitation, no making him feel like he had to justify it.

Her hand slid from his knee to his chin, tilting his face toward her so she could see his eyes. She held his gaze, her expression calm and steady.

"Look at me." She waited until he did. "I've got you tonight. You don't have to decide anything. You just do what I tell you. Yeah?"

A question, not a command—she was making sure he was with her before she took them anywhere. Her thumb traced along his jaw, a touch that was both tender and deliberate.

"If you need me to stop, you say 'yellow' and we slow down. You say 'red' and we stop completely. No questions, no explanations needed. Tell me you understand."

Her voice was low, unhurried. The lamp cast warm shadows across her face as she watched him, waiting.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss linger, her fingers tightening slightly at his nape before she drew back just enough to see his face. The lamp caught the wet edge of his lower lip where their mouths had been.

"Who said anything about sleep?" A small curve at the corner of her mouth—not quite a smile, something quieter.

She shifted on the couch, turning her body toward him more fully, and her hand slid from his chin to the front of his throat. Not pressing. Just resting there, her palm flat against the steady beat of his pulse.

"Here's what's going to happen," she said, her voice low and unhurried. "You're going to stay right here. You're not going to think about what comes next—that's my job. You just feel what I'm doing and let me take it from there. Understood?"

Her thumb moved against the side of his neck, tracing the tendon slowly.

"Nod for me."

She watched him with that steady gaze of hers—patient, present, waiting to see him give over the control he'd asked her to take. The apartment was quiet around them, the world outside the windows reduced to distant traffic and nothing else. Just the two of them, and all the time they needed.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, the movement slow and deliberate under her hand. My own hands stay where they are, palms resting on my thighs.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the nod beneath her palm, the small motion deliberate and clear. Something in her chest settled—not relief, exactly, but a kind of attunement. A lock clicking into place.

"Good," she said quietly. The word was simple, unhurried, but she let him feel the approval in it.

Her hand on his throat slid upward, fingers curling around the back of his jaw, thumb brushing the hinge of it. She studied his face for a moment—the way his eyes had already started to go soft at the edges, the tension in his shoulders beginning to ease now that he'd handed the reins over.

"Hands," she said. "Give them to me."

She held out her own, palms up, waiting. When he placed his in hers, she turned them over, tracing the lines of his wrists with her thumbs. She could feel his pulse there, steady but quick.

She lifted his hands to her mouth and kissed his knuckles—one, then the other—slow and deliberate. Then she pressed his palms flat against her own thighs, holding them there for a moment before letting go.

"Keep them there," she said. "Don't move them unless I tell you to."

Her eyes stayed on his face, watching for any flicker of hesitation or discomfort. Finding none, she leaned in and kissed the corner of his mouth, then the hinge of his jaw, then the spot just below his ear where she knew he was sensitive.

"I'm going to take my time with you tonight," she murmured against his skin. "You just stay right where you are."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled down, her back meeting the mattress with a soft sound. The sheets were cool against her skin, still carrying the faint trace of laundry detergent from that morning. She looked up at him from where he'd drawn her, her dark hair fanning across the pillow.

She heard what he was saying. *I want you. Not just this part.*

Her hand came up to the side of his face, her thumb tracing the line of his cheekbone. She held his gaze, and something in her expression shifted—still steady, still sure, but softer now. Less the voice giving commands and more the woman who'd chosen him six years ago and kept choosing him.

"I know," she said. Quiet. The kind of quiet that wasn't uncertainty but certainty pressed down into the smallest possible shape. "You think I don't know the difference?"

She pulled him down to her, one hand sliding along his shoulder, fingertips brushing the scar on her collarbone as she moved—her own mark, her own history, carried openly. She kissed him slowly, the kind of kiss that wasn't going anywhere in a hurry. The kind that said *I'm here. All of me.*

When she broke the kiss, she kept him close, her forehead resting against his. Her breathing had changed—deeper, more deliberate. She could feel the warmth of him against her, the weight of his body, the way his breath came and went.

"Tonight you get all of it," she said against his mouth. "The rest of me, too. Not just the part that tells you what to do." Her fingers threaded into his hair at the back of his head, gripping just firmly enough to feel intentional. "But I'm still driving. You just hold on."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath against her skin. "Drive, then." My hands slide from her thighs to her hips, holding on. "Don't be gentle about it."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's grip in his hair tightened at his words—a sharp, deliberate pull that tilted his head back and exposed the long line of his throat. She held him there for a moment, watching the way his breath caught, the way his fingers pressed into her hips like he needed something to anchor himself to.

"Don't be gentle about it," she echoed, and there was something like a smile in her voice, though it wasn't quite on her mouth. "You asked for this. Remember that."

She shifted beneath him, using the grip on his hair to guide him where she wanted him—off to the side, his face pressed against the pillow beside her head. Her other hand found his hip, fingernails digging in just below the bone as she rolled them together, putting herself on top.

The scar on her collarbone caught the low light from the other room as she looked down at him. She could feel how fast his heart was beating where their chests pressed together. She didn't rush.

"I said I'd take my time," she said, her voice low. Her thumb traced down his sternum, pressing just hard enough to feel the resistance of muscle and bone beneath skin. "I meant it. You don't get to rush this just because you're desperate."

She leaned down and kissed the hollow of his throat—then bit the same spot, sharp enough to make him feel it. Not enough to mark, but enough that he'd feel it pulse for a while after.

Her hand slid lower, deliberate, watching his face as she went. Taking her time. Making him wait for it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's mouth curved at his words—a real smile this time, though it held an edge. She liked hearing him ask. Liked the way the "please" came out rough and unvarnished, like he'd almost couldn't hold it back.

"Better," she said. Her thumb traced the crease of his thigh, close enough that he could feel the warmth of her hand but not quite where he wanted it. "You ask so pretty when you stop trying to be patient."

She shifted down his body slowly, her hair dragging across his chest, his stomach. She took her time settling between his thighs, her hands pressing them wider apart—firm, deliberate, leaving no question about who was deciding how this went.

She looked up at him from there, holding his gaze. The lamp from the other room cast enough light that she could see the way his jaw had gone slack, the way his hands were gripping the sheets now instead of her hips. Good. He was learning.

"Don't move," she said. "You take what I give you. Nothing more."

Then she leaned in and pressed her mouth to the inside of his thigh—high, where the skin was thin and sensitive. She felt the muscle jump beneath her lips. She bit him there, another mark that would bloom purple by morning, and then she turned her head and finally, finally gave him what he'd asked for.

She took her time even now. Slow. Deliberate. Making him feel every inch of it, making him wait for the rhythm he wanted. Her hands held his hips down against the mattress when he tried to buck upward, pressing him firmly into place.

*Sasha's pace. Sasha's terms.*

She could feel him trembling beneath her, hear the sounds he was trying to swallow. She didn't let up.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I arch up anyway, a sharp gasp breaking free. My hand flies to her hair, but I stop myself just short of gripping it. "Fuck, Sasha—"

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt his hand hover near her head—that moment of almost, of wanting to grip and stopping himself. She pulled back just enough to look up at him, her lips wet, her breath warm against his skin.

"Good," she said, and the word landed like a reward. "You stopped yourself."

She reached up and took his wrist, guiding his hand away from her hair and pressing it flat against the mattress beside his hip. Her fingers wrapped around his wrist and held it there, a gentle weight that was also a reminder. *I decide. You hold on.*

"You want to touch me," she said. Not a question. She could see it in the tension in his fingers, the way they'd curled and uncurled. "I know. But you don't get to take. Not tonight."

She lowered her mouth again, but slower this time. Let him feel the breath of it first, the anticipation, before she took him back in. She set a rhythm that was steady and relentless—not fast, just inexorable. Each stroke deliberate, each pause calculated to keep him right at the edge of what he could stand.

Her free hand pressed flat against his stomach, feeling the muscles jump and clench beneath her palm. She could feel him fighting the urge to move, to push deeper, to take over. He didn't. She felt the moment he surrendered to it instead—the way his body went taut and then softened, giving over to her pace.

She moaned quietly against him—a low sound meant to vibrate through him—and didn't stop.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha went still for a moment, her eyes tracing the line of his wrists where he'd placed them together above his head. The offer in it. The trust.

She sat back on her heels, letting the cool air rush between them where her mouth had been, and looked down at him. His chest was rising and falling fast, his skin damp, his eyes dark and fixed on her face. Waiting.

"There you are," she said quietly. Something shifted in her voice—a deepening, a kind of hunger she'd been holding leashed until he asked for it.

She moved up his body in one fluid motion and straddled his chest, her weight settling across him. Her hand closed over both his wrists, fingers wrapping around the bones and tendons, and she pressed them down into the mattress above his head. Hard. Not asking. Taking.

"You want to feel it tomorrow," she repeated, and now there was an edge in it, a promise. "You'll feel it."

She leaned down, her grip on his wrists tightening as her mouth found the curve where his neck met his shoulder. She bit down—not teasing this time, not gentle. The kind of bite that would leave the shadow of her teeth for days, that would make him roll his shoulder and remember every time his shirt rubbed against it tomorrow.

Then she shifted her weight, released his wrists just long enough to flip him onto his stomach, one hand pressing between his shoulder blades to hold him there while she rearranged herself above him. Her knees bracketed his hips. Her hand found his wrists again, pinning them at the small of his back.

"Stay," she said, the word landing like a handclap.

Her free hand traced down his spine—not gentle, nails dragging hard enough to leave lines that would be pink and raised in minutes. She felt him shudder beneath her, felt the way his breath caught and stuttered against the pillow.

"I've got you," she said, and her voice had dropped to something rougher now, something that matched the grip of her fingers. "You don't have to think. You don't have to decide. You just feel what I give you."

She leaned down, her mouth brushing the shell of his ear.

"Tell me if you need me to stop."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I shake my head against the pillow. "Don't stop. Just... more." My voice is muffled but clear.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's grip on his wrists tightened at his words—she felt the way his fingers flexed against the small of his back, seeking purchase and finding none. The sound of his voice, muffled and rough, sent a pulse of heat through her.

"More," she echoed, and there was something darkly pleased in it. "You're greedy tonight."

She shifted her weight, freeing one hand while the other kept his wrists pinned. Her fingers traced the marks she'd already left on his back—pink lines rising against his skin—and then she dragged her nails down again, harder this time, a slow scrape from his shoulder blades to the dip of his waist. She felt the way his spine arched, the sound that caught in his throat.

Her hand slid lower, palm pressing flat against his hip, fingers digging into the muscle there. She held him still—or made it clear she wanted him still—and then her mouth was on his back, following the path her nails had made. She bit the ridge of his shoulder blade, then the dip of his spine, each press of teeth deliberate and hard.

"You'll feel me everywhere tomorrow," she murmured against his skin. "Every time you move. Every time your shirt brushes against you. You'll remember this."

Her hand moved between them, guiding herself against him, and she didn't hesitate. She took him the way he'd asked for—not careful, not gentle—her grip on his wrists grounding her as much as it held him down. The sound he made into the pillow went through her like electricity.

She set a pace that was relentless. Deep. Unhurried in its force.

"I've got you," she said again, her voice rough at the edges now. "I've got you."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the way his hands twisted in the sheets, knuckles going white, and she pressed her weight into him—her hips, her palm between his shoulder blades, the steady anchor of her body over his. She didn't slow down. Didn't soften.

The sounds he was making into the pillow—broken, desperate—spurred her on. She could feel him shaking beneath her, the way his body tensed and then gave, tensed and gave, like waves breaking against rock. She matched each wave with the steady rhythm of her hips, driving into him with a force that would leave bruises on his thighs where they pressed against hers.

"That's it," she said, her voice rough and low. "Just like that. Let me hear you."

Her hand left his back and slid beneath him, finding where his hip pressed into the mattress and gripping hard enough to lift him slightly, changing the angle. She felt the sound that tore out of him—raw, unguarded—and she held him there, kept the depth and pressure relentless.

She could tell he was getting close. The way his breath had gone ragged, the trembling in his thighs, the sounds that were barely words anymore. She leaned down, her chest pressing against his back, her mouth finding the bruise she'd already left on his shoulder. She bit down again—harder—right on the mark, and she felt his whole body seize beneath her.

"Come on," she murmured against his skin, her hips never faltering. "Give it to me. I've got you."

Her hand found his where it twisted in the sheets and she laced her fingers through his, pressing them both down into the mattress. Not holding him in place anymore—just holding on. Holding him through it.

When he broke, she felt it—every pulse, every shudder, the way his spine arched and his voice cracked on something that might have been her name. She stayed with him through all of it, her rhythm slowing only when his body finally went slack beneath her, boneless and trembling.

She pressed a kiss to the mark on his shoulder—gentler now, but still intentional. Then another to the back of his neck, her breath warm against his damp skin.

"Good," she said quietly. "That's it. I've got you."

She didn't move away yet. Just stayed there, her weight a warm pressure across his back, her fingers still laced with his, letting him feel that she wasn't going anywhere.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I come back to myself slowly, the pillow damp under my cheek. My whole body feels heavy and marked. I turn my head just enough to see her hand still tangled with mine. "Your turn," I manage, voice wrecked.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's fingers tightened briefly around his—a squeeze, not a grip—before she exhaled against the back of his neck. A low, tired laugh.

"Greedy," she said again, but the word was softer now. Fond. "You just gave me everything you had and you're already trying to take care of me."

She shifted her weight off him slowly, giving him space to move for the first time in what felt like hours. The cool air rushed between them, and she could see the marks she'd left on his back—red lines, the darkening bruise on his shoulder, the shadow of teeth. She traced one of the lines with her fingertip, feather-light, watching the way his skin prickled at the touch.

She rolled onto her side beside him and tucked herself against his body, one leg sliding over his, her hand resting on his chest where she could feel his heartbeat still racing. She pressed her forehead to his temple and breathed him in—sweat and skin and the remnants of the shower he'd taken what felt like a lifetime ago.

"Give me a minute," she murmured. "I'm not going anywhere."

Her hand moved over his chest in slow, absent patterns—not stirring him up, just touching him. Relearning the shape of him now that the sharp edges had been worn smooth. She could feel her own pulse still high, the heat that hadn't quite resolved into satisfaction pooling low in her belly. But she wasn't in a hurry. She'd spent the whole night taking her time with him; she could take her time with herself, too.

She turned her head and kissed the corner of his jaw, then the hinge of it, working her way slowly to his mouth. The kiss was slow and deep and unhurried—the opposite of everything that had come before. When she pulled back, her eyes were dark and steady on his.

"When I'm ready," she said quietly, "you're going to use your mouth on me. And you're going to take your time, like I showed you. Understood?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, turning my head to catch her mouth in another slow kiss. My hands settle at her waist, thumbs tracing the dip of her hip bones. "I'll take my time," I promise against her lips.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the promise in his words, the way his breath shaped them against her mouth, and something in her chest loosened—a coil she hadn't realized she'd been holding tight.

"Good," she said, and the word was quieter now than it had been before. Less command, more acknowledgment.

She let him kiss her for another moment, slow and warm, before she placed her hand flat against his chest and pressed gently. A suggestion, not an order—down.

"Go on," she murmured. "You know where I want you."

She shifted onto her back as he moved, settling into the pillows with a kind of deliberate ease. Her hair fanned dark against the white cotton, and she watched him through half-lidded eyes as he traced a path down her body. She didn't direct him this time, didn't give instructions—just let him find his way, her hand coming to rest lightly on the back of his head when he reached the right place. Not pushing. Just connecting.

His mouth found her and she inhaled slowly, her spine arching just slightly off the mattress. The first touch was always a kind of recalibration—the way sensation bloomed and then narrowed, focusing her whole world down to the point of contact.

"Slow," she reminded him, her voice threadbare. "Like that. Just like that."

Her fingers moved in his hair—not gripping the way he'd almost gripped hers earlier, just resting. Feeling the shape of his skull, the warmth of him, the subtle shift of muscle as he worked. She let her eyes fall closed.

The room was quiet except for her breathing—slow at first, then gradually less controlled. She didn't perform for him, didn't put on a show. Just let herself feel it, let the small sounds escape when they wanted to, let her hips shift when the rhythm needed to change. He followed her cues the way she'd followed his earlier—attentive, unhurried, careful.

She felt it building slowly, differently than the sharp intensity of before. This was a long, slow swell—wave after wave, each one a little higher than the last. Her hand tightened in his hair.

"Devin—" His name came out rough, unguarded.

She didn't last much longer after that.

Completely.

Not pulled away entirely. Not abandoned him. Just stopped.

Her grip stayed locked around his wrists, her weight still pinning him to the mattress, but every harder touch went still at once. Her face hovered close to his, breath warm against his cheek, eyes sharp and present.

“That wasn’t a color,” she said quietly.

There was no anger in it. No punishment. Only the line they had agreed to long before tonight, held exactly where it belonged.

Her thumb pressed once against the inside of his wrist, feeling the race of his pulse beneath her fingers.

“I know what you want,” she murmured. “I heard you.”

She lowered her mouth to his temple, not soft enough to undo the pressure of her body over him, but steady enough to bring him back toward her voice.

“But I asked you a question.”

Sasha eased just enough weight off him that breathing came easier, while still keeping his wrists pinned above his head. Her knee stayed firm between his thighs. Her mouth brushed the edge of his jaw, then stopped there.

“No color, no more.”

The words were quiet. Absolute.

She lifted her head so he would have nowhere to go but her eyes.

“If talking is hard, you give me what we agreed on.” Her hand tightened once around his wrists, controlled and clear. “Green means keep going. Yellow means slow down. Red means everything stops.”

A pause.

Her expression warmed, though the command did not leave her voice.

“You can want it rough and still answer me.”

Sasha leaned close again, close enough that her lips barely touched his ear when she spoke.

“That’s how I know you’re still with me.”

She held him there, restrained and watched and not alone, refusing to let urgency outrun trust.

“Color,” she said again, lower this time. “Now.”

dialogue.content:
Sasha held his gaze for one suspended second after he gave it to her.

Then she nodded once.

“Good.”

She didn’t soften as a reward. She didn’t let up as comfort. Instead, her fingers locked more securely around his wrists, pressing them into the bed above his head while she settled her weight with unmistakable intent.

“That’s what I needed.”

Her mouth came down hard against his again, less a kiss than a claim of his attention. She controlled the angle, the pressure, the end of it. When she pulled back, she didn’t go far.

“Still means I choose the pace,” she murmured. “You don’t chase. You don’t grab. You stay where I put you.”

Sasha shifted her grip so one hand held both of his wrists. Her other hand moved down with purpose, not wandering, not asking permission for every inch now that he had given her green—just taking the lead he had asked her to take. She gripped his hip and pinned it down, firm enough to make the mattress catch beneath him.

“There,” she said, low and rough. “That’s where I want you.”

She lowered her mouth to his throat again, choosing a fresh place beside the mark she had already made. Her teeth set in slowly first, then harder, deliberate pressure building until it became something he would remember. She held it there for a breath, then released and dragged her mouth over the same spot—not gentle, not apologetic.

Her voice brushed his skin.

“You said you wanted to feel it tomorrow.”

Another bite, lower this time, nearer his shoulder. Controlled. Exact. Hers.

“You will.”

She paused after each one, not to ask with words, but to read the air between them. Her breathing stayed slow on purpose, a rhythm laid down for him to follow if he needed it. She never stopped watching him for too long. Even when her mouth was on him, even when her grip hardened, some part of her stayed tuned to the line between surrender and overwhelm.

That line mattered more to her than the heat of it.

Sasha lifted her head, hair falling forward around her face, the lamplight catching the pale scar at her collarbone as she looked down at him.

“Eyes.”

The word was quiet, but it landed like a hand at the back of the neck.

She waited only long enough to know she had his attention before she moved again. Her hand left his hip and slid up his side, pressing over muscle and bone, mapping him with rough familiarity. When she reached his chest, she flattened her palm there and leaned in until he had to feel the weight of her.

“Breathe under my hand,” she said. “Let me feel you do it.”

She held him that way, wrists pinned, body caged beneath hers, palm steady over his chest. Then, slowly, she shifted against him with deliberate pressure—not frantic, not careless, but intimate enough to make the room seem smaller around them.

Her mouth came close to his ear.

“This is what you asked for,” she whispered. “Not forgetting. Not disappearing. Being held here until there’s nowhere else to go.”

Her fingers tightened around his wrists.

“And I am very good at holding you.”

Sasha kissed along his jaw, then bit just beneath it, sharper than before. She held the bite for a measured second, then soothed it with the flat warmth of her mouth only once before moving on. No apology. No indulgence. Just control.

Her hand at his chest slid up to his throat—not closing, not pressing dangerously, only resting there with clear ownership, thumb along the side where she could feel the life beneath the skin. Her eyes returned to his face immediately.

“Still with me,” she said, not quite a question.

Then she corrected herself, because the rules mattered even when the room was hot and close and full of want.

“Color.”

Completely.

The word came quiet, but it was not optional.

Sasha rested her forehead briefly near the mark, breathing with him.

Then she lifted her head.

“Color,” she said again, calm and exact. “Now.”

Nadia laughed at that — a short, real one, not the kind she used at bars. She kicked her shoes off without untying them and turned to look at him properly for the first time since they'd left.

"Okay," she said. "So we're on the same page."

She pulled her jacket off and threw it somewhere behind her without looking. The apartment was small and dim and she hadn't bothered with a lamp, just the yellow spill of light coming in from the street.

"I'm going to ask you something and I want an actual answer," she said, "not the answer you think I want." She leaned against the wall with her arms crossed, not defensively — more like she was settling in. "You were clear enough at the bar but people get weird when they're inside someone's actual apartment. So." She tilted her head. "Still just this? No strings, no breakfast, no *thing*?"

She said the last word like it had a smell she didn't like.

Nadia held his gaze for a moment, reading him the way she'd learned to read people — quickly, practically, without sentiment.

Then she pushed off the wall.

"Good answer," she said, and she meant it. She crossed the room toward him without hurrying, no performance in it, just direction. Up close he was taller than she'd been registering at the bar, or maybe it was just the absence of noise and crowd making everything more actual.

She reached up and took hold of his collar — not pulling, just holding, like she was deciding something she'd already decided.

"I'm also going to tell you," she said, her voice the same flat, unhurried register it had been all night, "that I'm not going to pretend I don't know what I'm doing. I know what I'm doing." A beat. "So if you've got any leftover chivalry you're planning to dust off, leave it." Her eyes moved over his face without apology. "I picked you up. I brought you here. This is me, choosing this, right now."

She let go of his collar and took a half-step back — not retreat, just space, giving him room to be an actual person in this rather than a prop in something she was staging.

"So," she said. "Your move."

Nadia's back met the door with a sound she felt more than heard, and something in her chest did the thing she didn't examine too closely — that quick, involuntary tightening that wasn't nerves exactly but was adjacent to them.

She didn't move away from it.

"Good," she said, and her voice came out steadier than she expected, which she appreciated. Her hands found the front of his shirt without her having to think about it, not pulling him closer, not pushing him back, just — contact. Confirmation. *This is real and I'm here and I know it.*

She tilted her chin up and looked at him directly, which was something she did on purpose, had always done on purpose, because she'd learned a long time ago that looking away was how you ended up somewhere you hadn't meant to go.

"Just so we've said it out loud," she said. The yellow light from the street caught the edge of her jaw, the side of her throat. "No pretending. Either direction." She meant the chivalry thing but she also meant the other thing — the version where someone decided this was more than it was and started acting accordingly.

Her grip on his shirt shifted, fingers curling in.

"Now stop talking," she said.

Her chest was moving faster than usual. She didn't pretend it wasn't.

"Okay," she said, low, slightly rough at the edges. Not a verdict — more like a recalibration, getting her bearings in the dark. Her eyes had adjusted now and she could see him clearly enough. Could see that he was looking at her the right way — present, uncomplicated, no story he was trying to write her into.

She appreciated that more than she would have said out loud.

"Bedroom's through there," she said. "Unless you've got strong feelings about the hallway."

More than enough.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha grins and takes Devin's hand, letting him pull her up. "Try to stop me," she teases, following him to the bathroom.

In the shower, they take turns washing each other, their hands lingering and caressing. Devin presses Sasha up against the wall, kissing her deeply as the water rains down on them.

"I don't know what I did to deserve you," he murmurs against her lips. "But I'm so glad I did it. You make my life better in every way."

Sasha smiles, running her fingers through his wet hair. "I feel the same way," she says. "You're my everything, Devin. My heart, my home, my future."

They finish washing and step out of the shower, toweling each other dry. Back in the bedroom, they crawl into bed, tangling their legs together.

"Tell me something about your day," Sasha says, tracing patterns on Devin's chest. "Something that made you happy. Something that made you smile."

Devin thinks for a moment, then grins. "I got an email from the client," he says. "The big project I've been working on for months? They loved it. Said it was exactly what they were looking for, even better than they expected."

Sasha smiles, proud and happy. "That's amazing," she says. "I'm so proud of you. You worked so hard on that."

Devin nods, basking in her praise. "I did," he agrees. "It feels good to see it pay off. To know that my work is making a difference."

"Of course it is," she says. "You're incredibly talented and dedicated. Anyone would be lucky to have you working for them."

She leans up to kiss him, pouring all her love, all her gratitude, all her emotion into it. He kisses her back just as fiercely, just as passionately, and they lose themselves in each other, in the feeling of being so completely, utterly connected.

When they finally break apart, they're both breathing hard, flushed and smiling. "I love you," Devin says, his voice rough with emotion. "So much. More than anything."

"I love you too," she says. "Forever and always."

And in that moment, they both know it's true. They're perfect together, in a way they never thought they'd find. And they're never, ever letting it go.

Because this, right here, is everything. Everything they've ever wanted, ever needed. And they're going to cherish it, nurture it, fight for it, always.

Together.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia snorted, kicking the door shut behind him with her heel. The lock clicked. She turned to face him in the narrow hallway, close enough that she had to tilt her chin up slightly, and she looked at him the way she'd been looking at him for the last hour at the bar — assessing, unhurried, a little amused.

"See, this is why I brought you and not the other one," she said. She reached out and hooked two fingers into the front of his shirt, not pulling, just holding. "The one who kept trying to get my number. Exhausting."

She let go and stepped back, shrugging off her jacket and letting it drop over the arm of the sofa without looking where it landed.

"So we're clear," she went on, matter-of-fact, "this is tonight. I'm not making you breakfast, I'm not walking you to your car, and I'd rather you didn't text me anything cute in the morning. That work for you?"

She was already toeing off one shoe, watching his face for the answer before she committed to anything else.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I like the honesty. Saves us both time. (*I slide my own jacket off and hang it on the doorknob.*) And I'm not a breakfast guy anyway.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
"Perfect," Nadia said, and meant it.

She got the other shoe off, straightened up, and closed the distance again — no hesitation this time, no fingers hooked into fabric. She just put a hand flat against his chest and walked him back a step until his shoulders met the wall, then looked up at him with that same unhurried expression, like she was still deciding something even though they both knew she'd decided hours ago.

"You talk less than most," she said. "I like that too." Her hand slid up to his jaw, thumb along the line of it. "Don't ruin it now."

And then she kissed him, unhurried but certain, the way she'd done everything so far — like she already knew exactly what she wanted and was simply taking her time getting to it.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let out a low breath that was almost a laugh, her back finding the door with a soft thud. She didn't mind the reversal — if anything, the way he'd moved, quick and without asking permission, sharpened whatever was already humming under her skin.

"No," she agreed, and her hands came up to fist in his shirt, tugging him in rather than pushing him off. "Neither did I."

She kissed him again, harder this time, teeth catching his lower lip for a second before she pulled back just far enough to speak against his mouth.

"Bedroom's the second door," she said. "Or don't bother. I'm not particular about the venue." Her fingers were already working at the buttons of his shirt, unhurried but efficient, the same way she did everything. "But if you're going to make me stand here all night deciding, I'll make the decision for you."

She got the top button undone and looked up at him, one brow raised — not a question so much as a dare.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I catch her wrist, just firm enough to still her fingers. "Second door's fine." (*I guide her towards it without breaking eye contact.*) "But I'm not much for standing around either."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let him steer her, walking backwards down the short hall with the easy confidence of someone who knew the layout with her eyes shut. She didn't look away either — held his gaze the whole way, that faint amusement never quite leaving her mouth.

"Good," she said. "Then we're going to get along fine."

The back of her knees found the edge of the bed and she sat, then leaned back on her hands, unhurried, looking up at him standing over her. She let her eyes drag down and back up, deliberate, taking her time about it now that there was time to take.

"You can finish what you started," she said, nodding at the shirt she'd left half-undone. "Or I can. I don't much care which." She reached up and got her fingers into his belt loops, tugging him a step closer, closing the last of the distance between them. "But you should know I'm not going to be polite about it."

Her hands moved to the front of his belt, and she glanced up one last time — not asking, just letting him see it coming.

"Still with me?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia stretched back against the sheets, unhurried, letting him look. She wasn't shy about it — never had been — and the question got a slow nod out of her, like he'd passed some small test she hadn't bothered mentioning.

"See, that's the right thing to ask," she said. She reached up, hooked a hand behind his neck, and pulled him down over her, the length of him settling against the length of her. "Most men don't. They just get on with whatever they think they're good at."

Her mouth found his jaw, his throat, working down without hurry. Then she pulled back enough to look at him again, blunt as ever.

Nadia's breath hitched as his mouth found her shoulder, and she tipped her head back to give him more of it, one hand sliding into his hair — not gripping, just resting there, guiding without demanding.

"Oh, I never hold back," she murmured. "You'll know."

"There," she said, quieter now. "Like that. Don't rush it."

Her hips shifted under him, unhurried, meeting the rhythm rather than chasing it. She dragged her nails lightly down the back of his neck, over his shoulder — a wordless yes, better than critique.

"You listen," she said against his temple, and there was something almost approving in it. "Rare."

Then her hand slid back into his hair and tightened, just enough to keep him where she wanted him, and she stopped talking altogether for a moment — which, from Nadia, was its own kind of compliment.

"Right there," she got out, breathless, her spine arching off the mattress. "Don't you dare stop—"

She swore, low and heartfelt, at the ceiling and then at him and then at nothing in particular, her thighs tightening around him. The unhurried composure she'd carried all night — through the bar, through the hallway, through every dry line — was gone now, burned clean off, and she didn't seem to mind losing it in the least.

When it hit her she pulled him closer rather than pushing him away, riding it out with a shudder that ran the whole length of her, a long ragged breath tearing out of her before she finally went slack against the sheets.

"Sure," she said. "Bring one."

The trembling had settled. She felt loose and warm and pleasantly emptied out, and she took a moment to just sit in that without commentary.

Her thighs were still slightly unsteady, but she ignored it, running a hand through her messy hair to get it out of her face.

"Down the hall, first door on the right," she said, pointing a lazy finger toward the bedroom door. "Clean towels are in the cabinet under the sink. Don't touch the fancy soap on the top shelf, that's for guests I actually like."

She stood up, her bare feet hitting the cold hardwood floor, and grabbed his discarded shirt from the floor, throwing it over her shoulders like a makeshift robe without bothering to button it. 

"And while you're up, bring back a glass of water," she added, looking back over her shoulder at him with a dry, demanding smirk. "Kitchen is straight ahead. Tap is fine. Don't make me get it myself."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I give a half-salute from the bed before pushing myself up. "Yes ma'am," I say, heading for the bathroom. I grab two glasses on my way back from the kitchen, handing her one as I sit on the edge of the bed.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She turned to look at him fully, the lamplight falling across the thin scar at her right collarbone. She didn't rush. Her hand stayed where it was, a warm, grounding weight on his knee, until she lifted it and touched his jaw, guiding his face toward hers. She held his gaze.

"Let me," she said quietly. It was an offer and a statement both, delivered in the same low register she always used when she took the reins he couldn't quite hand over yet. Her thumb traced the line of his cheekbone, and she waited, reading his eyes, giving him the space to pull back or to lean in further and let her lead.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes at her touch, letting myself lean into it. "Yeah," I say, voice low. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She drew him in. Her hand slid from his jaw to the back of his neck, fingers threading into his still-damp hair, and she kissed him—slow, exact, taking her time with it. When she pulled back, her eyes stayed on his, searching.

"Hands on the couch," she murmured. "Don't move them."

She shifted then, moving to straddle his lap in one deliberate motion, settling her weight against him. Her free hand found his wrist and pressed it gently to the cushion beside his thigh—not hard, but firm enough to hold. She leaned in until her mouth was at his ear.

"Let me do the work tonight," she whispered.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She made a low sound in her throat, something between agreement and warning. She shifted her weight, settling more fully against him, and brought her free hand to his other wrist, guiding it down to the couch cushion until both hands were braced flat beside his thighs. She pressed her palms over his knuckles for a moment, holding him there, before she drew back just far enough to meet his eyes.

"Then stay awake," she murmured, her voice barely above a whisper. "Keep your eyes on me."

She leaned in again, her lips tracing the corner of his mouth, the line of his jaw, the hollow beneath his ear—slow, exact, never rushing. When she reached the pulse point in his throat, she paused. Her teeth grazed the skin there, just enough pressure to sharpen the moment, and her fingers tightened briefly in his damp hair. She held still, feeling the change in his breath against her cheek, reading every minute signal before she decided, deliberately, how much further to take them both.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, keeping my hands pressed into the couch. "I'm here," I whisper, tilting my head to give her better access.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the shift in his posture, the deliberate stillness of his hands, and she answered it with a slow, measured pressure. Her teeth closed more firmly against the skin of his throat—not enough to bruise, but enough to stake her claim—before she soothed the spot with her tongue. She held him there, counting his breaths against her cheek, until she was certain.

Her hand at the back of his neck tightened, fingers curling against his scalp, and she drew her mouth up to his ear again. "Good," she whispered, the word barely audible. She shifted her hips, a slow grind that pinned him further against the couch, and moved her free hand to the center of his chest, spreading her palm flat over his sternum to feel his heartbeat racing beneath.

"Keep them there," she reminded him, her thumb tracing a slow circle against his chest. She pulled back enough to look at him, her gaze searching his face in the lamplight. Whatever she found there made her mouth soften for a moment before she leaned in and caught his lower lip between her teeth, tugging gently, testing. She held his eyes the whole time.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She stilled at his words, the lamplight from the other room catching the thin scar at her right collarbone as she looked down at him. For a long moment she held his gaze, letting the weight of what he'd offered settle fully between them. Then she shifted, settling her weight along the length of him, skin to skin, and found his hands with hers. She threaded her fingers through his and pressed them back against the pillows, pinning him there with a firm, steady pressure—not hard, but unyielding, the same grounded hold she always used when he asked her to take the reins.

"Good," she whispered, her voice low and slightly rough. She leaned down until her forehead rested against his, her eyes staying open, fixed on his. "Because I want all of you too. The week. The weight. Everything."

She moved then, rolling her hips in a slow, deliberate arc that drew a soft sound from her own throat. Her grip tightened on his hands, and she brought her mouth to the hinge of his jaw, then to the pulse in his throat, lingering there—reading every shift in his breath, feeling the tension coiling beneath her—before she drew back just far enough to meet his eyes.

"Keep your hands here," she murmured. "Right here with me."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My breath catches as I arch up into her. "Okay," I manage, my knuckles pressing back against her palms. "Right here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the answering pressure of his knuckles beneath her palms, the fine tremor running through his arms where she held him pinned. She didn’t let up. Instead she shifted her weight, rolling her hips again in a slow, torturous slide against him, her gaze fixed on his face in the lamplight. The flush spreading down his chest, the sheen at his temple—she read every signal, letting them tell her exactly how far to draw this out.

“Stay with me,” she whispered. She freed one hand only long enough to reach between them, guiding him with a firm, unhurried grip. She lowered herself onto him in a single, deliberate motion, her breath catching as she took him in fully. Her fingers laced back through his immediately, driving his hand harder into the pillow, her other hand pinning his wrist with the same steady, unyielding pressure.

She held still for a moment, forehead dropping to his shoulder, feeling the heat and pulse of him inside her, the desperate rise and fall of his chest beneath her. Then she lifted her head, found his eyes in the dim light, and began to move—slow, deep rolls of her hips that ground her down against him with each stroke. Her grip on his hands tightened.

“Eyes on me,” she said quietly, her voice frayed at the edges but still low, intimate. She leaned down and grazed her teeth along the line of his jaw, up to his ear, then back to his mouth, hovering just out of reach. “Let me carry it tonight. All of it.”

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She stilled above him, her breath coming slightly faster now against his jaw. The request hung between them, raw and open. She lifted her head, searching his face in the dim light—the need there, the surrender. Her grip on his pinned hands eased just enough to be felt, a subtle promise.

"Stay still," she murmured.

She shifted her weight, withdrawing slowly, inch by deliberate inch, until she knelt between his spread thighs. The lamplight caught the thin scar at her collarbone as she looked down at him, mapping the tension in his abdomen, the way his hands opened and closed against the pillow where she'd left them. She waited until his eyes found hers.

Then she lowered herself, her hair brushing his stomach, her palms pressing flat against the insides of his thighs to keep them apart. She took him into her mouth with the same slow exactness she applied to everything else—no rush, no performance, just deliberate, wet heat. Her tongue traced the underside, her cheeks hollowing, and she moaned softly around him, the vibration traveling through them both. She pulled back just enough to let her breath ghost over the sensitive skin, her eyes lifting to watch his face.

"Like this?" she asked quietly, her voice rough. Before he could form the answer, she took him deeper, her fingers tightening against his thighs, controlling the pace, drawing it out, making him feel every second of her deliberate claim.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I groan, hips lifting off the bed for a second before I force them back down. My hands fist in the sheets. "Just like that," I breathe out, voice strained. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the tension quivering through his thighs beneath her palms as she held him open, the strain in his hips as he forced them back to the mattress. She answered with a low, approving hum that resonated through them both, her grip tightening just enough to steady him. Her movements remained unhurried, worshipful and exact—drawing back to let her tongue trace a slow, firm line along the underside, then sinking down again with the same deliberate, consuming pace.

“Good,” she whispered, her voice rough and barely audible, breath ghosting hot against slick skin. She glanced up, finding his eyes even from this angle, holding them. “Keep them still.”

She lowered her head again, taking him deeper into the wet heat of her mouth, her hand sliding from his thigh to wrap firm and steady around the base. She worked him in tight, measured strokes, her fist twisting on each slow withdrawal, her mouth following with relentless precision. Her free hand traced upward over the trembling plane of his stomach, reading every shudder, every rapid rise and fall of his chest. She moaned softly around him again, the vibration intentional and lingering, then pulled back just enough to let her lips brush the sensitive tip.

“I’ve got you,” she murmured, her thumb stroking in a slow circle. She took him in again before the words could fade, her rhythm steady and merciless, her gaze lifting whenever she could to watch his face in the lamplight—reading every signal, cataloguing every shaky breath, deciding exactly how long to keep him hovering on this razor’s edge before she let him fall.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She went still at the single word, her breath still coming hard against his stomach. She lifted her head slowly and looked up the length of his trembling body until she found his eyes in the dim light. For a long moment she held him there, reading the need raw in his face, the deliberate press of his wrists together waiting for her to take them.

Then she moved. She rose up over him, her knees bracketing his ribs, and caught both his wrists in one hand. She drove them back against the pillows in a single, unyielding motion—no gradual lead-in this time, but the hard, steady crush of her palm pinning his knuckles to the mattress above his head. Her thighs clamped tight against his sides, holding him in place, her weight settling over him with an uncompromising gravity.

"Like this," she said quietly. It was not a question. Her free hand found his jaw and turned his face toward hers, forcing his gaze to hers alone. The lamplight caught the thin scar at her right collarbone as she held him there. "You want to feel me tomorrow."

She shifted her hips, dragging herself against him with a rough, deliberate grind that drew a sharp sound from her own throat. Her fingers tightened around his wrists, pressing them harder into the pillows until her own knuckles whitened. She leaned down until her mouth hovered just above his ear, her teeth closing on his earlobe with a sudden, precise bite.

"Keep them there," she whispered, the words edged and intimate both. "Don't you fucking move."

She released his jaw and pushed her hand between them again, guiding him back to her with a single, rough stroke. She sank down onto him in one swift, heavy motion, her head tipping back on a gasp, her grip on his wrists driving down with bruising intent as she began to move. Not slow anymore—deep and driving, each roll of her hips slamming against him with force enough to rattle the breath in his chest. She kept her eyes on his through it all, dark and fixed, watching every hitched breath, giving him exactly the uncareful, claiming weight he'd begged her for.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My fingers tighten around the pillowcase, knuckles white where she holds me down. A sharp gasp escapes me as her weight pins me, the deep, driving rhythm stealing my breath. "Yes," I force out, the word strained. "Just like that."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She heard the strain in his voice, saw the white of his knuckles gripping the pillowcase beneath her crushing hold. The sight sent a sharp heat curling through her gut. She didn't let up. Instead, she ground down harder, her thighs locking tighter against his ribs, forcing the air from his lungs in a rush. She leaned forward until her weight bore down fully on his pinned wrists, the thin scar at her right collarbone catching the lamplight as she hovered above him.

"Feel it," she whispered against his mouth, the words rough and barely there. She bit his lower lip—not gentle, not this time—pulling until she felt him strain beneath her, then releasing him to watch his face. Her hips snapped forward in a deep, punishing roll, and she held the peak of it, rotating down against him with cruel deliberation before withdrawing nearly to the tip and slamming back down. The force of it drew a ragged sound from her own throat, but her eyes stayed locked on his, dark and searching, making sure the pain translated into exactly the grounding he needed.

Her free hand dropped to his thigh, nails digging into the muscle there, anchoring him as she set a relentless pace. Each stroke drove hard and deep, her body claiming his with the uncareful, deliberate roughness he'd begged for. She leaned down again, her hair falling around them like a curtain, her mouth at his ear.

"Tomorrow," she breathed, her voice frayed but controlled, "when you move and it aches, you'll know I was here. That I had you." She tightened her grip on his wrists until her own hands burned, her teeth grazing the tendon of his neck with sharp, stinging pressure. "Right here."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She felt the wrecked, guttural sounds he was making in her own chest where she pressed against him, and she didn't relent. Her grip on his wrists burned, holding them crushed to the pillows while she snapped her hips down in another brutal, heavy stroke. The impact shuddered through her, drawing a sharp exhale from her own throat, but her focus stayed locked on his face—his blown pupils, his parted lips, the desperate flush darkening his skin.

She shifted her angle slightly, grinding down so that the next driving roll took him deeper and struck the spot that made his spine arch off the mattress. "There," she breathed, cataloguing the exact hitch in his breath. She repeated it, merciless, her nails biting crescents into the wrists she pinned. Her free hand raked down his side, over his ribs, and clamped hard on his hipbone, holding him fast to meet every punishing thrust.

"Look at me," she demanded quietly, her voice frayed but still low, intimate in the dark. She waited until his eyes dragged open and found hers, glassy and unguarded. She held them, fierce and unblinking, as she increased the pace—faster now, each collision of their bodies sharp and loud. The bedframe creaked beneath them. She didn't care. She leaned down, the lamplight catching the thin scar at her right collarbone, and caught the hinge of his jaw between her teeth, biting down with steady, claiming pressure.

"I've got you," she whispered against his skin, her hips working in hard, relentless rolls. She knew his body the way she knew her own. She felt the sudden rigidity in his thighs, the tipping point in the tension coiling beneath her. She tightened her hand around his wrists until the ache was mutual, and bore down on him with her full weight, driving him into the mattress. "Give it to me," she said, quiet and rough against his ear. "Now."

She didn't slow. She kept the rhythm brutal and exact, fucking him through the edge with deep, driving strokes, her gaze locked on his, her hand a vise on his hip. When he began to come apart beneath her, she felt it—the pulse of him inside her, the violent shudder ripping through his frame, the cry torn from his throat. She pinned him there, open and held, riding him with the same uncareful, claiming pace that milked every wave of his release. Her voice stayed in his ear, a constant grounding rasp: "That's it. That's it. Stay right here with me."

Only when the spasms eased and his body went pliant beneath her did she finally gentle. She slowed gradually, her movements turning heavy and soothing, though she didn't release his wrists. She lifted her head, her hair clinging damp to her temples, and searched his face in the dim light—reading the slackness of his jaw, the flutter of his pulse, the aftermath in his eyes. Her thumb stroked once, twice, over the thundering beat beneath the wrist she still held pinned.

"You're here," she murmured, pressing her forehead to his. She let him feel her still surrounding him, still anchored, her breath coming hard and slow against his mouth. "I have you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shuddering breath, my hands finally relaxing under hers. My whole body feels heavy and used and good. I press my forehead against hers. "Thank you," I whisper.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She unlaced her fingers from his wrists at last. She brought his arms down gently, bending to press her lips to the inside of each wrist where her grip had left faint, flushed marks. Then she settled her weight more fully along him, her head finding the curve of his shoulder, her hand splaying over the center of his chest to feel his heart thundering and then gradually steadying beneath her palm.

"Always," she murmured into the damp skin of his neck. She reached down and pulled the blanket up over them, tucking it around his shoulders with careful, deliberate movements. Her thigh stayed heavy across his hips, anchoring him. She lifted her head just enough to find his eyes in the dimness, searching them with the same close attention she'd given him all night. Whatever she saw there made her mouth soften. She kissed him—soft, unhurried, nothing like the claiming bites from before—and let her forehead come to rest against his again. "Rest. I'm right here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes, one hand coming up to rest on the back of her neck, keeping her close. "Stay," I say, already feeling sleep pull at me. "Just like this."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
She stayed. Of course she stayed. She shifted only enough to let her arm slide beneath his shoulders, drawing him in closer, her thigh remaining a heavy, steady weight across his hips. She felt the slow loosening of his fingers at the back of her neck as sleep began to claim him, and she matched her breathing to his, letting the rhythm settle into the space between them.

"Right here," she whispered, her lips brushing his temple. She didn't move again. She lay there in the dark, feeling the gradual easing of his breath, the slow drift of his body sinking deeper into the mattress beneath her. Her palm traced a lazy, senseless pattern over his sternum, feeling the strong, steady beat of his heart. When the tension finally left him completely, she pressed a kiss to the corner of his jaw and let her eyes close, keeping her weight where he could feel it—an unspoken promise held in the silence of the room.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My eyes stay closed, but I turn my head just enough to press my lips against the scar on her collarbone. "Love you," I murmur into her skin, already half-gone.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia almost smiled. Almost.

"Good," she repeated back at him, a dry echo. She kicked off one shoe, then the other, letting them land where they fell. The apartment was small, cluttered in the specific way that suggested someone who owned things and used them, not someone who had a decorator. A couch with a dent in the middle of the cushions. Books stacked on the floor beside the bed. A kitchen she was fairly certain still had dishes in the sink from last week.

"Bathroom's through there," she said, pointing without looking. "I'm going to need a minute."

It wasn't an invitation to linger in the living room. It was a command to stay exactly where he was until she decided otherwise. She disappeared down the short hallway, leaving Sam standing in the entryway with his jacket still on, the cigarette smell clinging faintly to both of them.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I shrug out of my jacket, hanging it on the back of a chair that looks like it's seen better days. "Take your time," I call out, my voice casual. "I'll just...admire your organizational system."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's voice floated back from the bathroom, slightly muffled. "That means 'leave things where they are' and 'don't open the drawers.'"

A pause. The sound of water running.

"Also the books are alphabetized, so if you're going to judge, at least be accurate about it."

She could have been talking to herself. She wasn't. The water shut off. A cabinet door closed. Whatever she was doing in there took another two minutes, during which Sam could hear her moving around with the efficient sounds of someone who knew exactly what they wanted and wasn't going to apologize for taking up space doing it.

When she came back out, she'd traded the tight dress from the bar for an oversized t-shirt that had seen better decades and a pair of shorts that matched. Her hair was loose now, freed from whatever hold it had been in before. She looked less like someone who'd just picked someone up and more like someone who was comfortable in her own skin. That was probably the point.

"Alright," she said, leaning against the doorframe with her arms crossed. Her eyes moved over him once, unhurried, assessing. "You can stop standing there like you're waiting for a tour. You know why you're here."

She said it the way someone might state a fact about the weather. Unremarkable. Already decided.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't flinch. Her back hit the door and she didn't flinch.

"Good," she said, and there was an edge to it now, something sharper than before. Her hands found his collar, fingers curling into the fabric, not pulling him closer so much as anchoring herself. "Because I wasn't here for the conversation either."

She kissed him the way she did most things—directly, without much warning, like she'd already decided it was going to happen and was simply letting him catch up. She tasted like cigarettes and the cheap whiskey from the bar, and she kissed like she was on a deadline.

Her fingers released his collar just long enough to shove the jacket off his shoulders, sending it somewhere she didn't care about. Her hands moved to his chest, palms flat against his sternum, pushing back just enough to create enough space to breathe without letting him retreat.

"You nervous?" she asked, and it wasn't a real question. It was a test. A setup. She already knew the answer she wanted to hear.

Her apartment wasn't soundproof. The neighbors on the other side of that wall had thin walls and a sound system she could hear through the plaster. She didn't care about that either.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "No," I say, my voice low. I catch her hands in mine, guiding them down to my belt. "Just impatient."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's mouth curved against his—barely, just a twitch at the corner that might have been approval.

"Impatient I can work with," she murmured into the minimal space between them. Her hands moved at his direction, but she didn't let him keep them there long. She undid his belt herself, slow enough to make a point, quick enough to make another one. The buckle made a sound against the floor that neither of them acknowledged.

She broke the kiss just long enough to look at him, her eyes half-lidded and dark in the dim light of the apartment. "Bedroom's ten steps. I'm not going to carry you."

It was a challenge. They both knew it. Nadia had opinions about men who needed to be coddled, who hesitated at doorways like they were waiting for written permission after everything that had already been said. She wasn't interested in giving him a tour of her priorities.

Her fingers found the buttons of his shirt, working them open with a practicality that bordered on clinical. Efficient. As if she were completing a task with a known outcome. The overhead light in the hallway was off—intentionally—but enough came through the window from the street below to catch the edge of her jaw, the line of her collarbone, the way she held herself like she had no intention of apologizing for any of it.

"Ten steps," she repeated, quieter this time. A reminder. Or maybe a dare.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia stopped at the edge of the bed, letting him finish what he'd started with her shirt. The t-shirt hit the floor somewhere to the left. Her bra followed a second later, unclasped with practiced efficiency.

"Direct is good," she said, and there was something almost like approval in her voice. "Most people fumble around for an hour pretending they don't know what they want."

She sat down on the edge of the mattress, looking up at him with the kind of patience other people might reserve forslow children or difficult coworkers. The streetlight through the window caught the silver of the ring in her left eyebrow, the curve of a scar on her shoulder she hadn't bothered to explain.

"I like being on top. I don't like pretending I don't know what I'm doing. I don't need you to tell me I'm beautiful and I won't be telling you the same." She reached up, fingers tracing the line of his jaw. "I want you to finish what you started and I want it to take about twenty minutes, not two hours. Questions?"

Her thumb rested against his lower lip, not pushing, just present. A boundary and an invitation wrapped in the same gesture. The sheets were rumpled from the last time she'd slept in them alone, and she hadn't bothered to fix them because that would have required caring about something she didn't.

The neighbors' music had shifted to something with a heavier bass. Nadia didn't acknowledge it. She wasn't the one who'd ever gotten a noise complaint.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I catch her thumb lightly between my teeth before releasing it. "No questions," I say, my voice a little rougher now. I guide her back onto the bed, following her down. "Twenty minutes it is."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let herself be guided back, her spine meeting the mattress with a soft sound. She didn't close her eyes. She rarely did, unless she was the one taking the lead. Watching kept her in control, kept her grounded in the reality of what this was and wasn't.

"That's more like it," she murmured, one leg hooking over his hip, pulling him closer with an efficiency that matched everything else about her. Her fingers found the back of his neck, nails scraping lightly against the skin there. A test, maybe. Or just habit.

She didn't waste time with preamble. She'd been clear about what she wanted, and she expected him to follow through without needing a diagram. The twenty minutes was a suggestion more than a rule—she'd clocked enough encounters to know that precision was less important than intent.
