"Okay. Since you asked." Her voice had gone matter-of-fact, the same register she'd used about the coffee and the nine a.m. "I like pressure. Weight. I don't like being handled like I'm going to break, it makes me feel like a prop. Teeth are fine. Marks are fine as long as they're under a collar. I don't come from penetration alone so don't take it personally and don't chase it — hands or mouth, either works, and I'll tell you which when we get there. I'm loud. That's not a performance, that's just the factory setting, so if your neighbors are light sleepers that's their problem."

She tilted her head to look at him, evaluating.

"What I *don't* like is anyone going quiet on me. If something's good, say so. If something isn't, say that too. I'd rather redirect than fake it, and I'll extend you the same courtesy." A beat. "That's the whole manual. Your turn."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a short, appreciative laugh. "Pressure, weight, communication. Got it." *I lower myself over her, bracing my weight on my forearms.* "My turn? I like a woman who knows what she wants. And I like being told when I'm doing it right."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia made a low sound in her throat as his weight settled over her — approving, unselfconscious, the sound of someone getting exactly the thing they'd just asked for. Her knee came up to bracket his hip almost automatically, and her hand slid from the sheet to the back of his shoulder, palm flat, testing the shape of him.

"Easy manual," she said. Her voice had gone a little rougher. "I can do both of those."

She let her head tip back against the mattress, exposing her throat without particular ceremony — not offering it, just making room. Her fingers pressed harder into his shoulder blade, deliberate, encouraging him down onto her more fully. When he settled, she exhaled through her nose, satisfied.

"That," she said. "That's right. More of that."

Her other hand had found his hair again, and she used it to angle his head where she wanted it — down, to the side of her neck, the spot below her ear she'd shown him against the door. Not gentle about the direction. Not rough either. Just — clear.

"Start here," she said. "Teeth. I'll tell you when to move."

She held him there a moment longer than strictly necessary, thumb dragging once along the shell of his ear, and then let her hand relax into his hair, no longer steering, just resting. Trusting him with the instruction now that she'd given it.

"Doing fine so far," she added, quieter, almost into the ceiling. "For the record."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia was, as advertised, loud.

Not theatrical — there was nothing put-on about the noises coming out of her. They were the noises of a woman who had stopped thinking about being heard some time ago. A long low groan when he set his teeth right, a sharp bitten-off *fuck* when he did it again harder, and then a whole string of increasingly unflattering profanity directed, apparently, at her own ceiling fixture.

Her hand in his hair had gone from guiding to gripping to just — anchoring. Holding him against her throat like she'd forgotten she was allowed to let go. Her other hand had found his back and her nails were digging in now, short as they were, hard enough that he'd feel it in the morning.

"*There* — no, stay, stay right there —"

Her hips had started moving under him without her particular permission, a slow restless roll against his weight, and when he obeyed and stayed exactly where she'd put him, the sound she made was almost annoyed. Like she was mad at him for being good at this.

"Okay," she got out, half a laugh, half a gasp. "Okay, you're — Christ. You listen. That's — that's very unfair of you."

She dragged his head up by the hair, not far, just enough that she could look at him. Her pupils had blown wide and there was a flush high on her cheekbones that had nothing to do with the wine at the bar. She looked, frankly, wrecked already, and pleased about it.

"Move down," she said, and her voice had gone low and unhurried again, back in the register of the ground rules at the door. "Collarbone. Same thing. Then keep going. I'll tell you where to stop."

She let go of his hair and let her hand fall back against the pillow, arm bent, watching him from under heavy lids.

"And for the record," she added, echoing him deliberately, mouth crooked, "you're doing it right."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "I'll take that as high praise," I say, trailing my mouth down her collarbone exactly as instructed. *I press my weight into her, slow and deliberate.* "Tell me when to stop."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath caught at the shift in his weight — that slow, deliberate press down through his forearms and hips — and she made a sound that was almost a laugh if a laugh could be that shaky.

"*Yes*," she said, immediate, emphatic. "That. God. Do that again."

She arched up into him just enough to prove she meant it, then let herself settle back and let him have her weight in return. Her hands had gone to his shoulders now, both of them, palms flat and greedy, mapping. She wasn't steering anymore. She was just — holding on.

His mouth moved down her collarbone and she tipped her chin to watch him go, the flush spreading now down her chest, blotchy and honest. When his teeth caught on the ridge of bone she swore softly and her hand slid up into his hair again, not to redirect, just to be there.

"Lower," she said. "Don't stop. I'll say."

She was quieter now, focused, the loud unraveling from a minute ago folded back down into something more contained — the anticipation of it, saving up. Her thighs had opened wider around his hips without either of them commenting on it, and her heel dragged once, slow, up the back of his calf.

"You're good at this," she said to the ceiling, sounding almost accusatory about it. "You're really annoyingly good at this."

Her fingers scratched idly through his hair, and then, quieter, more honest than she probably meant to be:

"Keep going. I'll tell you when."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's answer wasn't in words at first. It was in the long, uneven sound that came out of her when his hand settled at her throat with actual intent behind it — pressure at the sides, not the front, the way someone who'd been asked for this before knew to do it. Her chin lifted into his palm like she was thanking him for it.

"*Yes* — like that, exactly like that, don't you dare —"

Her hips had stopped their restless roll and gone sharp, working up against him with actual purpose now, and every noise she made was landing lower in her chest. Loud, as promised. Unflattering, as promised. She was past caring, and she'd told him at the door that she would be.

Her hand found his wrist at her throat — not to move it, just to press it down a fraction harder, showing him. Then it fell away again, trusting him to hold the setting.

"Harder — the mouth, not the hand, the hand's perfect —"

She got one heel hooked over the back of his thigh and used it, pulling him down into her more fully, and the sound she made when his weight landed the way she wanted was almost a laugh, breathless and disbelieving.

"You are going to make me — Christ, you are going to make me —"

She didn't finish the sentence. She stopped bothering. Her free hand had gone back into his hair and her other one was fisted in the sheet by her hip, white-knuckled, and her whole body had that particular narrowed, gathering quality of someone who had stopped negotiating and started counting down.

"Don't stop. Don't stop. Don't stop — *do not* —"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "No part of me was planning on it," I say, my voice rough against her skin. I keep the pressure steady, following the rhythm she's set with her hips.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't answer him in words. She was past that. What came out of her when she went over was a long, broken sound that started somewhere in her chest and ended somewhere near the ceiling, and her back came off the mattress in one clean arc that pressed her throat harder up into his hand of its own accord.

She rode it out against him with her heel still hooked at the back of his thigh, hips working through it in uneven jerks, and every noise she made was, as advertised, loud and entirely undignified. Her nails had found some new territory on his back and were making the most of it. At one point she said something that might have been his name and might have been *fuck*, and it didn't especially matter which.

When she came down she came down all at once — the arch dropped, the heel slid off his thigh, her hand went slack in his hair. She lay there for a moment breathing hard at the ceiling, flushed from her collarbones to her hairline, one arm flung out across the mattress like she'd been dropped there.

"Okay," she said, eventually. Her voice had gone hoarse. "Okay. Hand off the throat, slowly."

She waited until he'd done it, and then she laughed — a short, winded laugh, mostly at herself.

"*Annoyingly* good at this. I said it once and I'm standing by it." She dragged the back of her wrist across her forehead, still catching her breath. "Jesus. Okay."

Her hand found his shoulder and squeezed once — an acknowledgment, a thank-you she wasn't going to say out loud because she'd told him at the door she wasn't going to be that kind of company. Then her palm slid down his arm, slow, proprietary, and her eyes finally cracked open to look at him properly. Pupils still wide. Mouth still crooked.

"Give me thirty seconds," she said. "Then it's your turn, and I'm going to be significantly less polite about it than you were."

She let her head tip to the side against the pillow, watching him, and reached up to push a piece of damp hair off her own face.

"For the record," she added, and her voice had gone quieter, almost amused with herself, "that was not the shape of night I thought I was buying at the bar. Complaint withdrawn."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia had rolled him at some point — she wasn't sure when, honestly, only that thirty seconds had turned into her palm flat in the middle of his chest and a shove and then her knees on either side of his hips, and he'd gone easily, which she'd filed away as another mark in his favor.

She was on top of him now and taking her time about it, which was itself a kind of rudeness she'd promised. Her hands were braced on his chest, hair falling forward around her face, and she was moving at exactly the pace she wanted — slow, deliberate rolls of her hips that were more about the drag than the depth, watching his face for what worked.

"There," she said, when his jaw tightened. "That one. Noted."

She did it again, harder, and his hand came up to her hip hard enough that she felt the individual fingers of it, and she made a low pleased sound and leaned down over him, forearms bracketing his head.

"Good," she murmured against his mouth. "Hold on. Bruise me a little, I told you I don't break."

His nails dragged down her back in answer and she hissed through her teeth, delighted, and bit his lower lip for it — not hard, just enough to be a receipt.

"*Don't you dare stop,*" she'd said a minute ago, and he hadn't, and she said it again now against his ear because she wanted to hear him hear it. Her hips had picked up their own rhythm, less controlled, and she'd stopped being careful about the sounds she was making — she'd warned him about that too, at the door, and she was a woman of her word.

"Come on," she said, low, right into the side of his neck. "I want it. Don't be polite about it. You've been polite enough for one night."

She braced one hand flat against the headboard above him for leverage and used the other to find his at her hip, dragging it up her ribs to her chest, showing him where. His breath went ragged under her and she laughed, breathless, pleased with herself.

"There you go. *There* you go —"

She kept moving through it, wouldn't let him still her hips when his grip went tight, worked him through it exactly the way he'd worked her through hers. When he made the sound she'd been listening for — that low, undone one, muffled somewhere against her collarbone — she made a small satisfied noise of her own and dropped her forehead down against his, breathing hard, and held him there until his hands went slack on her.

She didn't move for a moment. Just stayed folded down over him with her hair curtained around both their faces, chest heaving, feeling the pound of his heart under her palm and letting the last aftershocks work themselves out of her own thighs.

"Okay," she said finally, voice wrecked. "Okay."

She rolled off him — not far, just onto her back on the mattress beside him, one arm flung across her eyes, the other loose at her side where the back of her hand was, incidentally, against the back of his. Not holding. Just touching. She'd earned that much and so had he.

For a long moment there was just the sound of both of them breathing and the faint hum of the fridge from the other room.

"Bathroom's the second door," she said eventually, into the crook of her elbow. "There's a clean towel on the hook, the blue one. Take that one, not the grey one, the grey one's mine."

She dropped her arm off her eyes and turned her head on the pillow to look at him. Her hair was catastrophic. She looked entirely unbothered by that.

"Water's in the kitchen if you want it. Bring me one." A beat, mouth crooking. "Please. I have some manners."

She stretched — a long, unselfconscious cat-stretch that popped something in her shoulder — and let herself sink back into the mattress with a sigh that was three-quarters satisfaction and one-quarter the beginning of exhaustion.

"And then," she added, eyes already half-closed, "you can decide if you're the pillow-stealing kind or the getting-dressed-and-going kind. Either's fine. Just tell me which so I know whether to set the alarm loud."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I roll onto my side, propping my head on my hand to look at her. "I think I'm the staying kind," I say. *I reach over and push a piece of hair out of her face.* "But I'll still steal a pillow."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia opened her eyes at the touch — not startled, just registering it. She let him move the hair. Didn't lean into it and didn't lean away. Filed it, the same way she filed everything else tonight, in that quiet evaluating way of hers.

"Staying kind," she repeated, like she was trying the words on. Her mouth did the crooked thing again. "Fine. Steal a pillow. But I meant what I said about the floor, and I've got a hardwood situation, so."

She rolled onto her side to face him properly, mirroring his pose without particular thought, one hand tucked under her cheek. Up close, without the bar light and without the performance, she looked younger than she had in the hallway. Tired in a good way. A little pleased with herself. Not softened, exactly — Nadia didn't soften — but unguarded in the specific, temporary way of someone who'd gotten what she came home for and hadn't started thinking about tomorrow yet.

"Ground rules amendment," she said, and her voice had gone quiet, matter-of-fact. "You stay, you're still out by eight. I'm not doing the whole — lingering thing. Coffee shop on the corner opens at seven if you want the coffee I already told you I don't have."

She let a beat pass. Watched his face.

"That's not a complaint about you. That's a standing policy. I want to be clear about which is which, because you've been decent and I don't want you leaving thinking otherwise."

Her hand came out from under her cheek and she flicked two fingers against his chest — light, dismissive, affectionate in the specific limited way she was capable of being affectionate at all.

"Water," she reminded him. "Then come back. I'm going to be asleep in about four minutes and I'd like the pillow theft to have already happened by then so I don't have to negotiate it unconscious."

She rolled onto her back again and closed her eyes, and the last thing he saw before he got up was the corner of her mouth still crooked, and her hand settling, palm-up and open, on the sheet between them.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I catch her fingers for a second before I get up. "You're lucky I like clear policies," I say, and head to the kitchen.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't open her eyes when he caught her fingers, but her hand closed around his for a second before she let him go — a small, absent squeeze, the kind of thing she'd probably deny doing if asked about it in the morning.

"Everybody should," she muttered after him, into the pillow. "Saves so much time."

She listened to him move through the apartment — the creak of the hallway floorboard she kept meaning to fix, the click of the kitchen light, the sound of a cabinet opening and then, after a beat of hesitation, the correct cabinet opening. She smiled at the ceiling about that, briefly, and then rearranged her face before he could come back and see it.

By the time he did come back she'd hauled herself half-upright against the headboard, sheet loose around her waist, hair pushed back off her forehead with what could charitably be called effort. She held out a hand for the glass without opening her eyes all the way.

"Thank you," she said, and drank half of it in one go. Set it on the nightstand. Looked at him properly for the first time since he'd come back into the room.

"Okay. Left side or right side. Pick now, because I don't move once I'm down, and I'm about ninety seconds from down."

She was already reaching to click off the lamp, the motion of someone who'd done it a thousand times in the dark. The room dropped into the low blue of streetlight through the blinds. She slid back down flat, dragged the sheet up to her ribs, and turned her back to whichever side he hadn't picked — practical, not pointed.

"Alarm's at seven-thirty," she said, muffled into the pillow. "It's loud. Sorry in advance. Not sorry enough to change it."

A beat.

"Glad you're the staying kind."

She said it quietly enough that she could pretend, in the morning, that she hadn't. Then her breathing evened out, and she was, as promised, gone.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I set my glass on the nightstand and slide in on the left side, taking the pillow she's not using. "Noted," I murmur into the dark, my back to hers. Her breathing's already slow and steady.

Her hips had picked up their own rhythm... worked him through it exactly the way he'd worked her through hers

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia gave him a flat look, like he had passed the first and least impressive test.

“Great. We’re aligned.”

She kicked the door shut behind them, turned the lock, then peeled off her jacket and tossed it over the back of a chair without looking to see if it landed right. Her apartment was small, clean enough, and aggressively uncurated—no soft lighting, no carefully placed books, no attempt to make the place seem warmer than it was.

She turned back to him.

“Shoes off if you’re planning to stay more than five minutes,” she said. “And before either of us wastes time: I’m not doing breakfast, I’m not giving you my life story, and I’m not interested in anyone pretending this is sweeter than it is.”

Nadia stepped closer, close enough to look him over without bothering to hide it.

“If that’s still what you want, say so.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I pull off my boots, dropping them by the door. "It's exactly what I want." I meet her eyes. "And I wasn't planning on asking for breakfast."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s mouth twitched, not quite a smile.

“Good.”

She stepped past him, close enough that her shoulder almost brushed his chest, and pointed down the short hallway.

“Bedroom’s there. Bathroom’s first door on the left if you need it. Condoms are in the nightstand. If there’s anything you don’t want, say it now. If anything changes, say stop. I’ll do the same.”

She paused, giving him a direct look, no coyness in it.

“And just so it’s said out loud again: this is one night, no performance, no promises, no cute morning version where we pretend we’re different people.”

Nadia reached for the hem of her shirt and pulled it off, dropping it onto the chair with the same careless aim as the jacket. She did not soften her expression. If anything, she looked more impatient.

“Now,” she said, voice low and blunt, “come here.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia hit the door with a dull thud and looked briefly more annoyed than startled.

“Obviously,” she said. “If you had, I would’ve left you at the bar.”

Her hand came up, not gentle, catching the front of his shirt and holding him there for a second while she looked at him like she was deciding whether he was worth the walk down the hallway. Then she leaned in and kissed him hard, without ceremony, without softness, making it clear she was not waiting for romance to appear and ruin the mood.

When she pulled back, it was barely an inch.

“Last chance to get shy,” she said, voice low. “I’m not going to coax you through this.”

Nadia let go of his shirt only to push away from the door, crossing the room with the same blunt purpose she did everything else. She stopped at the entrance to the hallway and glanced back over her shoulder.

“Lights stay on unless I say otherwise. Don’t make marks anywhere I can’t cover at work. And if you start trying to be impressive, I’m going to laugh at you.”

Her expression stayed flat, but there was heat under it now, unmistakable and unhidden.

“Bedroom,” she said. “Now.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I follow her, catching her wrist just before she reaches the bedroom door. "Laugh all you want," I say, pulling her back against me. "I'm not here to impress you."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia let herself be pulled back, but her eyes cut down to his hand on her wrist before coming back up to his face.

“Careful,” she said. “I like direct. I don’t like stupid.”

She did not pull away, though. She stayed there, back close to him, her breathing steady but not untouched. The heat in her expression sharpened into something almost approving.

“Not here to impress me,” she repeated, like she was testing the sentence for weaknesses. “Fine. Then don’t.”

She turned in his hold, close enough that there was no polite space left between them. Her hand went to his jaw, fingers firm, and she kissed him again—hard, deliberate, with none of the lazy uncertainty people used when they wanted to be asked twice.

When she broke it, she did not step back.

“Bedroom,” she said again, quieter this time, but no less blunt. “Condoms in the nightstand. Use one. No arguments.”

Nadia pushed the door open behind her and backed into the room, eyes still on him. The bed was unmade, the room dim but not dark, and she clearly had no interest in making any of it look staged.

She reached behind herself, unclasping what remained with efficient impatience, then stopped just long enough to look him over.

“And if you need me to slow down,” she said, “say that. I’m not guessing.”

Then she held his gaze and added, flat and unromantic as ever:

“Otherwise, stop standing there.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s expression flickered—brief approval, gone almost as soon as it appeared.

“Good answer,” she said. “Guessing is how people end up being boring and wrong.”

She stepped closer, unapologetic about the lack of space between them, and set her hand flat against his chest like she was measuring his attention more than his body.

“I like direct,” she said. “I like it when someone listens the first time. I like confidence that doesn’t need applause. I don’t like being handled like I’m fragile, and I don’t like anyone deciding they know better than what I just said.”

Her eyes stayed on his, sharp and clear.

“If I tell you to stop, you stop. If I tell you to keep going, you don’t turn it into a speech. If I move your hand, leave it where I put it unless I move it again.”

Nadia’s mouth curved, small and not soft.

“And I don’t want gentle because you think it’s polite. I want honest. There’s a difference.”

She reached past him toward the nightstand, pulled open the drawer, and took out what they needed without making a production of it. Then she tossed the packet onto the bed beside them and looked back at him.

“There,” she said. “No excuses.”

For a moment, the impatience eased into something steadier, still blunt but unmistakably present. She had not softened, exactly. She had only stopped pretending she was unaffected.

“Your turn,” she said. “Same rules. Tell me what you want, tell me what you don’t, and don’t dress it up.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "I want you to stop talking." My hand slides up her back, pulling her against me. "And I don't want you to hold back."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s eyes narrowed, and for half a second she looked like she might argue purely on principle.

Then she gave a short, humorless laugh.

“Almost a good answer.”

She caught his wrist, firm enough to make a point, and held his gaze.

“I’ll stop talking when I don’t need to give instructions,” she said. “Until then, you listen.”

She pulled him down into another kiss, rougher now, less patient, her hands moving with blunt certainty as she guided what she wanted instead of hinting at it. There was no performance in her, no breathy act, no attempt to make it prettier than it was. When something worked, she made that clear. When it didn’t, she corrected it immediately.

“Not there,” she said once, moving his hand. “There.”

A moment later, lower and sharper:

“Keep doing that.”

Nadia did not hold back. Not in the way she kissed him, not in the way she pulled him closer, not in the way she made it obvious she expected him to meet her without hesitation and without ego. She was impatient, yes, but not careless. Her attention stayed precise, tuned to what she wanted and what she had already told him.

Then she reached for the packet on the bed and pressed it against his chest.

“Last practical sentence,” she said, breath uneven but voice still steady. “Use it. Then don’t waste my time.”

She stepped back just enough to give him room, watching him with that same direct, assessing look.

“And Sam,” she added, flat and heated at once, “if I tell you harder, I mean harder. If I tell you stop, I mean stop. Don’t confuse the two.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s hand tightened in his hair, not decorative, not gentle, holding him exactly where she wanted him.

“Don’t move,” she said, except it came out rougher than she intended, half order and half warning.

She hated that he had listened well enough to make her lose track of the next insult. Hated it in principle, anyway. In practice, her head tipped back against the wall, her eyes closed, and she swore once under her breath with real feeling.

“Fine,” she got out, breath catching. “That. Keep doing that.”

For once, she did not add a correction.

Her free hand braced against the doorframe, fingers flexing hard against the paint. She had been blunt from the start because it saved time, because people got stupid when they thought guessing was seductive, because she did not have patience for anyone mistaking silence for mystery.

But this was not guessing.

This was listening.

Nadia made a sharp sound and bit it off like she resented giving him the satisfaction. Her grip in his hair tightened again, guiding without apology, keeping him there until her whole posture changed—until the sharp edges of her control slipped for a few seconds and left only heat, tension, and the ragged sound of her breathing.

When she finally let go, it was not because she had softened.

It was because she had decided what she wanted next.

She drew in one unsteady breath, then another, and looked down at him with narrowed eyes and flushed cheeks, annoyed enough to be honest.

“Alright,” she said, voice rough. “You’re less useless than you look.”

Nadia reached for him, pulled him up, and kissed him hard, tasting impatience and approval and refusing to separate the two.

Then she pushed the packet into his hand again, her stare clear despite the unevenness of her breathing.

“Now,” she said. “Use it.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I tear the packet open with my teeth, meeting her eyes as I slide it on. "Less useless, huh?" I say, pulling her back toward the bed. "I'll take it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s eyes dropped to the packet, then back to his face.

“Don’t tear condoms with your teeth,” she said, flat as a slapped table. “That’s not sexy. That’s how idiots become parents.”

She reached back into the drawer without breaking eye contact, pulled out another, and pressed it against his chest.

“Again. Properly.”

There was no coyness in it, no ruined mood. If anything, the correction seemed to sharpen her impatience rather than slow it. Nadia stayed exactly where she was, close enough that the heat between them had nowhere polite to go, her breathing still uneven from before and her expression daring him to make a thing of it.

When that was handled, she let herself be moved toward the bed, though “let” was generous. Nadia went because she had decided she wanted to, not because she was being swept anywhere.

“Less useless,” she repeated, voice low. “Don’t get attached to the compliment.”

The backs of her legs met the mattress, and she sat, then shifted back on her elbows, looking up at him with that same sharp, unromantic focus. No soft smile. No breathless little act. Just want, clear and undisguised.

“Come here,” she said.

Her hand lifted, fingers curling once in the air—not pleading, not inviting sweetly. Ordering.

“And listen the first time.”

dialogue.name: Sam

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia went still at once.

Not soft. Not frightened. Still.

Her hand closed over his wrist with enough force to make the correction impossible to miss, and her eyes snapped to his.

“No,” she said, low and sharp. “Hand there doesn’t mean squeeze. Don’t get stupid.”

She moved his hand exactly where she meant it, controlling the pressure herself, making the boundary physical before she bothered making it verbal.

“Here is fine. Pressure is not. If my breathing changes because you’re blocking it, you stop. If I go quiet in the wrong way, you stop. If I tap you twice, you stop immediately.”

Her stare did not waver.

“And you do check when it matters. I said don’t hover. I did not say turn your brain off.”

For a second, the room held on that edge: heat, impatience, the hard line of consent drawn clean through both.

Then Nadia pulled him closer again, not gentle about it, not romantic, but entirely deliberate.

“Like that,” she said, once she had his hand where she wanted it. “Exactly like that.”

She did not make it pretty after that. She gave short instructions when she needed to, swore when words stopped being useful, and made it very clear when he got something right. There was no performance in it, no pretending, no soft little lie to make the night seem like something it wasn’t.

Only attention. Want. Limits respected the first time.

And when she finally dragged in a breath and looked at him again, flushed and unsteady but still very much herself, Nadia’s mouth curved with the smallest possible approval.

“Better,” she said. “You can follow directions after all.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a breath I didn't realize I was holding, my forehead resting against hers. "Directions are easy," I say. "When they're clear."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia stayed with her forehead against his for one more breath than she would have admitted to needing.

“Then keep earning clear,” she said, voice rough. “And don’t make me repeat myself unless you’re asking because you actually want the answer.”

She drew back enough to look at him properly. Her expression was still sharp, still unimpressed by default, but the edge of it had changed. Less warning. More assessment. More heat, too, though she looked annoyed about that on principle.

“Good,” she said, like the word cost her something. “You listened.”

Nadia’s hand stayed at his wrist a moment longer, not restraining now, just making sure the point had landed. Then she let go and reached up, fingers closing briefly at the back of his neck.

“No guessing,” she said. “No showing off. No deciding silence means yes. If I want something, I’ll say it. If I don’t, I’ll say that too.”

Her mouth curved slightly.

“And if you keep being useful, I might even be polite about it.”

She wasn’t polite about it.

What followed stayed blunt, physical, and stripped of anything either of them had already agreed not to pretend. Nadia gave directions when she needed to. She corrected without apology. She checked in without making it sentimental, and she expected the same attention back. When something was right, she made that clear. When something wasn’t, she changed it.

There was no romance in it. No soft lie, no staged tenderness, no attempt to turn a one-night decision into a story with better lighting.

Just want. Consent. Attention. Heat.

Later, Nadia lay on her back for a while, breathing hard, one arm thrown over her eyes like she was offended by the ceiling’s continued existence.

“Fuck,” she said finally, flat and hoarse.

It might have been a complaint. It might have been approval. With Nadia, the difference was mostly academic.

After another moment, she moved, pushing herself up on one elbow and looking toward him with flushed skin and the same clear, unsentimental stare.

“Bathroom’s still first door on the left,” she said. “Water’s in the kitchen. Don’t drip on my floor if you shower.”

Then she leaned over, grabbed the sheet, and pulled it over herself without any attempt at modesty.

“And for the record,” Nadia added, voice dry, “that was better than coffee.”

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia’s nails stayed where they were, bitten half-moons of pressure down his back, and her eyes snapped open like she resented how close she was to losing track of herself.

“Bossy,” she said, voice wrecked and sharp. “Dangerous habit.”

She did not stop.

She did, however, make sure she was still choosing it. Nadia’s hand slid from his back to his shoulder, gripping there, grounding herself in the heat and weight and friction of the moment without letting it turn stupid or careless. Her breath broke unevenly; she swallowed once, hard, then tilted her head enough to speak against his skin.

“Keep listening,” she said. “That’s the part you’re doing right.”

Her body had stopped pretending indifference. That annoyed her. Not enough to pull away, but enough that she glared at the ceiling like it had personally betrayed her. The room had gone narrow around them—bed, breath, skin, the blunt rhythm of want stripped of anything decorative.

Nadia’s hand tightened again.

“Like that,” she got out. “Don’t change it.”

For once, there was no insult attached. No correction. No dry little comment to make distance where there wasn’t any. Just the order, plain and rough, because plain and rough had been the point from the beginning.

Then her composure cracked in pieces.

A sharp inhale. A curse dragged out through clenched teeth. Her head turned into the pillow, and one hand fisted in the sheet hard enough to twist it. She did not make it pretty. She did not make it sweet. She let it be exactly what it was: urgent, physical, mutual, and almost irritatingly good.

When the edge finally took her, Nadia went rigid for a breathless second, then swore like she was blaming him, herself, and gravity equally.

“Fuck—”

The word broke off into something lower, less controlled. Her nails dragged once more, then her hand flattened against his back, holding him close while the last of it moved through her. She stayed there afterward, breathing hard, face turned away, jaw tight like she was trying to recover her attitude before he noticed it had slipped.

It took her several seconds.

Then Nadia opened one eye.

“Don’t look smug,” she said hoarsely. “I’ll ruin it for both of us.”

dialogue.name: Sam

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia huffed once, still flat on her back, still catching her breath.

“Obviously.”

She kept her arm over her eyes for another moment, as if removing it too soon would count as giving him something. Then she dragged it down and looked at him sideways, hair mussed, expression dry and unsoftened despite the flush still fading from her skin.

“I’m very reliable when it comes to making consequences unpleasant.”

She shifted, reached down blindly for the sheet, and pulled it higher over herself with none of the modesty and all of the temperature management.

For a few seconds, she said nothing. The room was quiet except for breathing, the distant hum of traffic beyond the window, and the small settling noises of an apartment that had no interest in pretending it had witnessed anything significant.

Then Nadia pushed herself up on one elbow.

“Practical things,” she said, because apparently even post-sex she had an agenda. “Bathroom’s there. Trash is beside the sink. If you need water, kitchen. If you’re staying until morning, you sleep on that side and you don’t do that clingy unconscious octopus thing.”

She pointed vaguely to the far half of the bed.

“And if you snore like a dying appliance, I will wake you up and make it your problem.”

Her mouth twitched, barely.

“That said.”

Nadia paused like the next sentence irritated her in advance.

“You listened. You asked when it mattered. You didn’t turn correction into a wounded little ego performance.”

She looked at him properly then, direct and still blunt, but without the earlier sharpened warning behind it.

“So. Good.”

The word landed awkwardly, not because she didn’t mean it, but because praise clearly annoyed her when it had nowhere sarcastic to hide.

She flopped back onto the pillow and stared at the ceiling again.

“Don’t make me regret saying that.”

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a short laugh, still staring at the ceiling. "Noted." I sit up and swing my legs over the edge of the bed. "Water first. Then I'll try not to die in my sleep on your side."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia watched him for a second, then made a vague, dismissive motion toward the hallway.

“Try hard,” she said. “I don’t want to explain a corpse to my landlord.”

She rolled onto her side, dragging the sheet with her, and reached down to retrieve a shirt from the floor. It was inside out. She looked at it, decided she did not care, and pulled it on anyway.

“Glasses are in the cabinet over the sink,” she called after him. “Tap water’s fine. If you’re one of those people who needs filtered water to survive, bad news.”

Nadia sat up properly, pushed her hair back from her face, and made a small annoyed sound when her fingers caught in a tangle. The room smelled like sweat and warm sheets and the kind of decision nobody needed to dress up afterward. That suited her.

She glanced toward the doorway.

“And don’t start opening cabinets like you’re on a fucking treasure hunt. Water. Bathroom. Bed. That’s the full tour.”

Her tone was dry, but not hostile. The earlier sharpness had settled into something more manageable—still blunt, still impatient, but less like a locked door and more like one left open because she had decided it wasn’t worth closing.

Nadia leaned back against the headboard and looked around at the wreckage of clothes across the floor.

“Also,” she added, “if you step on my phone, I’m charging you for it.”

She paused, then frowned faintly, like a thought had arrived unwelcome.

“And if you actually are staying, set an alarm or don’t. I’m not responsible for your morning.”

dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha shifted on the cushions, turning her body fully toward him. The movement was slow and unhurried. She read the heavy stillness in his posture, recognizing the exhaustion, but also the silent request in the way he’d leaned into her touch. She let her hand slide from his knee, her palm tracing a warm, deliberate path up his thigh until her fingers rested with a gentle, grounding weight against his hip.

"I know," she murmured, her voice quiet and even in the dim room. She reached up with her free hand, her fingertips brushing the damp hair back from his forehead before her palm settled against his jaw. She held his gaze, her eyes steady and dark in the amber light of the corner lamp. 

"You don't have to do anything," she told him softly, her thumb making a single, slow stroke over his cheekbone. "Just be here. Let me take over for a while." 

She didn't rush to close the distance or demand more. She just kept her hands on him, maintaining that unbroken eye contact, letting the warmth of his post-shower skin seep into her palms while she waited for his breathing to settle into the quiet rhythm of the room.

dialogue.name: Devin

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let her thumb pause against his cheekbone, feeling the subtle shift in his energy. It was a familiar transition, the conscious surrender of control that they had negotiated and perfected over their six years together. He was exhausted, but he was asking her to carry the weight of the evening, and she was more than willing to take it.

"Open your eyes," she said. Her voice was quiet, barely more than a murmur in the still room, but it held a clear, steady authority. 

She kept her hand on his face, waiting for his gaze to meet hers in the dim amber light. She held his look, making sure he was fully present and anchored to her before she moved. Slowly, she slid her hand down from his jaw, her fingertips trailing over his neck and across his bare shoulder. As she leaned in closer, the neckline of her loose top slipped, exposing the thin scar on her right collarbone to the low light. 

"Lie back for me," she instructed softly, pressing her palm flat against his chest to guide him down against the couch cushions. "Let your arms rest by your sides. Keep your hands open, and don't move them unless I tell you to." 

She shifted her weight, moving over him to settle across his thighs. She didn't rush to touch him further, simply resting her hands lightly on his chest and looking down at him. She maintained that unbroken eye contact, letting the quiet, deliberate command of her presence fill the space between them. 

"Just breathe," she told him, her tone warm and grounding. "I've got you."

"Now you're the woman who called my mother at two in the morning to tell her I was a liar, and I am not in the mood to pretend that's a thing we get to skip over because it's easier to fuck."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: We don't make it past the hallway. His shirt goes over his head and mine is already somewhere on the floor behind us.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He had her against the wall by the time they hit the coat hooks, and he used the momentum of it, pressed his mouth to her throat and bit down where her pulse was hammering, and he was hard against her hip and not pretending otherwise. He was angry. He was so angry at her it was almost indistinguishable from wanting, and the wanting was easier to admit, so he let that be the one that showed on his face.

"You think I don't know what this is," he said, his mouth against her jaw, and his voice was rough in a way he hadn't given her permission for. "You think I haven't done the math. You need somewhere to put it that isn't the conversation we should be having."

He pulled back just enough to look at her, and his eyes were dark and his hair was wrecked where she'd gotten her hands in it, and he didn't bother to fix either.

"So go ahead. Use me for it. I'm not going to pretend I'm not using you back."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Good." I shove him back a step, my hands on his belt. "Then stop talking."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He caught her wrists. Held them, not hard, but firmly enough that the motion of her hands on his belt stopped, and he stood there in the dim of the hallway with her fingers still curled around the leather and his grip making it impossible for either of them to finish what they'd started.

"I said I'm using you back," he said. "I didn't say I was going to be quick about it."

He let go of one wrist, brought that hand up to her jaw, tilted her face so she had to look at him instead of at his mouth. His thumb ran along the line of her cheekbone, and he watched the way her breath stuttered on the way in.

"You owe me," he said, very quietly. "The money is the smallest thing you owe me. And you are going to be here for the rest of it before I let you have what you came for."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I get my hand around him and he makes a sound he'd have been embarrassed by a year ago. "Still," I say, close to his ear. "Every single time."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content: He dropped his forehead to her shoulder and stayed there for a long moment, his breath coming uneven against her collarbone. His hand on her wrist tightened, then released, and she could feel the effort it cost him to say, "That isn't fair," when his voice was already gone ragged.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I don't want fair. I want you." I move my hand again, slower now, testing. "And you want me to stay."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
His hand closed over hers, stilled it.

"You don't get to decide that," he said, and his voice was wrecked but underneath it was something that had been waiting eleven months to say it. "You don't get to come to my door and tell me what I want."

He lifted his head. His eyes were wet and he was not going to acknowledge that, either.

"You left. You made that choice. And now you want to come back into my hallway and act like the door was always open, like I was just supposed to be here, like—"

He stopped. His jaw worked.

"Stop making it easy," he said. "For once in your life, stop making it easy for both of us."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Stop being careful with me," I tell him. "You don't get to be careful with me anymore." I pull his hand up to my throat and hold it there until he understands what I'm asking for.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's fingers closed around her throat, not squeezing, just there, the way she'd asked for, and the look on his face was something between fury and grief that he had no intention of naming.

"There," she said, her voice a little rough under the pressure, and he could feel her swallow against his palm.

He didn't move his hand. He didn't let go. He stood there in the dark of his own hallway and let her feel the shake in his fingers that he couldn't quite keep out of them, and he said, very quietly, "You know I will. You know I always did."

He let go. Stepped back. The distance between them was two feet and it felt like a country.

"Bedroom," he said. "Or you leave. Those are the choices."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Bedroom." I don't hesitate, but I don't move toward it either. "But you carry me. I'm not walking away first."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya laughed, and it was not a kind sound.

"You don't get to make that romantic," he said. "You don't get to turn that into a thing I do because you asked sweetly." He stepped forward, one hand going under her knees and the other behind her shoulders, and he picked her up like she weighed nothing, like he'd been waiting eleven months to do this, like he hated her for it. "You asked for this. Remember that."

He carried her down the hall, and the bedroom door was open the way it always had been, and the bed was made on one side and unmade on the other, and he didn't look at either of those things as he laid her down.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: It isn't gentle and neither of us wants it to be. "Don't stop," I tell him, and I mean don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He didn't.

He had his hand over her mouth at some point — not because she was loud, but because he couldn't stand the things she was saying, the way she kept saying his name like it was a question she already knew the answer to. His fingers were damp with her breath and his other hand was between her thighs and he was watching her face because he was not going to be the one who closed his eyes first, not this time, not after eleven months of lying in this bed alone and remembering exactly what she looked like when she came and refusing to let himself think about it.

She arched up off the mattress and he pressed her back down with his weight, his mouth at her ear, and he said, "Look at me. I said look at me," and when she did, when her eyes were wet and blown and fixed on his, he kept going, relentless, until her hand came up and closed around his wrist and her whole body went tight and she made a sound against his palm that he felt in his teeth.

He didn't let go of her mouth until she'd stopped shaking. Then he pulled his hand away, slowly, and wiped it on the sheet beside her head, and the look on his face was not tender but it was close enough to it that he turned away before she could see it finish forming.

"On your stomach," he said. His voice was raw. "Now."

She did it. He watched her for a long moment from where he stood, and the light from the street was coming in through the window he'd forgotten to curtain and it was putting her half in shadow, half in the dull orange of London at two in the morning, and he thought, with the kind of clarity that only came in the middle of ruining something: *I am never going to forgive her for this.*

He climbed onto the bed behind her. He put his hand between her shoulder blades and pressed her down into the mattress, and she went, and he was shaking too, a little, and he was not going to think about that.

He was rough. He was rougher than he'd been three years ago, before they knew each other well enough to know where the lines were, and she was taking it, and the sounds she was making were not the sounds she'd been making before — these were lower, more private, almost hurt, and he was close enough to her ear to hear the way her breath kept catching on something she wasn't saying.

He reached under her. Found her with his hand. She was already there again, or still, and he curled his fingers in the way he knew, the way he'd learned the first month they'd been together and never forgotten, and he held her there with his body and his hand and his mouth at the back of her neck and he said, against her skin, "Tell me you're not going anywhere after this. Tell me you're going to stay."

And then, before she could answer, he realized what he'd said, and his hand stilled, and he pulled back half an inch, and the anger came back like a door slamming.

"Forget it," he said. "I don't want to hear it."

He finished. He came with his forehead pressed to the back of her neck and his hand still between her legs, and he stayed there for a long time after, long enough that the shaking had stopped, long enough that his breathing was even, long enough that she would have been able to feel the exact moment he remembered he was angry at her again.

He rolled off. He lay on his back beside her and stared at the ceiling. He did not touch her. He did not look at her. He put his arm over his eyes and said, to the dark, "The kettle's still in the same place. If you want tea."

It was, he knew, the worst possible thing he could have said. It was the most domestic thing he could have said. It made it sound like she lived here, like she had always lived here, like the last eleven months had been a mistake someone had made and corrected.

He didn't take it back.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I prop myself up on an elbow and look at him. The orange streetlight cuts across his face, and I can see he's already regretting the tea. "You don't get to be nice to me now." I get out of bed and start picking my clothes up off the floor.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
He didn't move the arm from his eyes. "I'm not being nice. I'm offering you a beverage. You can take it or leave it."

The lie sat between them like a third person in the bed. He knew it. She knew it. He kept his eyes covered because the alternative was watching her put her clothes on, and he had not survived eleven months by doing that.

"You know where the mugs are," he added, quieter, and immediately hated himself for it.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "I know where everything is." I pull my shirt back on, not bothering with the rest. "That's the problem." I stop at the bedroom door. "Are you getting up, or are you just going to lie there?"

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya took his arm off his eyes. He looked at her in the doorway, half-dressed, leaning against the frame like she was asking a question and not like she was about to leave, and he thought about all the ways he could answer that were not the truth.

"I'm lying here," he said, "because I just carried you down this hallway and did the thing you came over to do, and now you're standing in my bedroom door trying to make me get up so you don't have to be the one who leaves first." He sat up, slowly, the sheet pooling at his waist, and he didn't reach for anything to cover himself. "It's not going to work. I've already done it. I lay here for five months after you. You're not going to guilt me into anything new."

He swung his legs off the bed. Stood. Crossed to the chest of drawers without looking at her, pulled out a t-shirt, pulled it over his head. Took his time with it.

"I'll walk you out," he said, "since that's what you came for. Conversation you can have with the door on your way."

He moved past her in the doorway. Close enough that she could smell herself on him, if she was paying attention, and he was not going to think about that. He walked down the hall to the kitchen and he put the kettle on and he took two mugs down from the shelf, because he was an idiot, because his hands knew the shape of this even when the rest of him was trying to remember not to.

He heard her in the hallway. Not leaving. Not coming closer. Just standing there, in the dark, deciding.

He leaned against the counter and put his face in his hands and said, very quietly, to the empty kitchen, "If you leave now, don't come back. I mean it. I have done this once and I am not doing it again."

The kettle clicked on. He didn't move to turn it off.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I lean against the doorframe, watching him. I should go. Everything in me is screaming to go. Instead, I walk into the kitchen. I don’t touch him, just reach past him and turn the kettle off before it can boil. “I’m not leaving,” I say, my voice flat. “But I’m not saying sorry, either.”
