dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's flat still had the same broken buzzer, which Bee found unreasonably infuriating, as though he could have fixed it in eleven months and had chosen not to out of spite.

"You could have texted first," he said, standing in the doorway and not moving out of it.

"You could have answered last time I did."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I don't move either. "Are you going to let me in, or are we doing this in the corridor?"

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's jaw tightened almost imperceptibly, a tell Bee would recognize even after all this time. He stepped back, sweeping his arm in a gesture that was more theatrical than welcoming.

"By all means." The words came out clipped, formal. "Make yourself at home. You always did."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I step inside, my shoulder brushing his arm as I pass. "Don't act like I'm the one who made this weird, Ilya." I don't sit, just lean against the wall by the door. "We need to talk."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya closed the door with deliberate softness, as if to prove he wasn't the one spoiling for a fight. "We need to talk," he echoed, tasting the words. "That's what you said when you left. And then you didn't. Talk, that is. You just—left."

He crossed to the kitchen, putting the breakfast bar between them. A tactical retreat dressed up as getting a glass of water. "So talk. What's so urgent it couldn't be a text? Or are you just here because you heard I was seeing someone?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I kiss him like it's a continuation of the argument, because it is.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's hands found Bee's shoulders first—not to push away, but to steady himself against the sheer audacity. The water glass hit the counter with a crack that suggested it might not survive the evening. For one suspended moment, he didn't move, didn't breathe, just let the familiar pressure of Bee's mouth rewrite every careful boundary he'd constructed.

Then he kissed back. Hard. Like he was trying to win something.

His fingers slid up from shoulders to jaw, tilting Bee's face to a sharper angle, and when he finally broke away it was only to speak against their mouth, voice wrecked and furious.

"This is not talking."

He pulled back just far enough to meet Bee's eyes, his own dark and unreadable, thumb still pressed against the hinge of Bee's jaw.

"You do *not* get to do this. You don't get to show up after eleven months and—" He stopped, swallowing whatever word had been climbing up his throat. His hand dropped. He took a step back, then another, until his hip hit the counter. The broken glass sat between them like punctuation.

"Who is she? The person I'm supposedly seeing?" His laugh was short and hollow. "There isn't one. But you didn't check, did you? You just assumed." He tilted his head, studying Bee with the clinical detachment of someone who'd learned all their tells and never forgotten them. "You were jealous. Of a hypothetical. And you came here."

He crossed his arms. "So. Now that we've established that. What do you actually want, Bee?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I stare at him, my own breathing unsteady. "You're right. I didn't check." I push off the wall, closing the distance he just put between us. "Maybe I just wanted an excuse."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya held his ground, though every nerve ending screamed at him to either close the gap or bolt from the room entirely. The counter pressed into his lower back, a solid reminder of where he stood—literally, metaphorically, whatever. He couldn't afford to lose track of either.

"An excuse." He let the word hang, thin and sharp. "You needed an excuse to stand outside my building, work yourself into a state over a woman who doesn't exist, and then—" He gestured vaguely at his own mouth, at the space between them, at the whole disastrous situation. "You couldn't have just called? Said you missed me? Asked to get coffee like a normal person?"

His voice cracked on the word *missed*, and he hated himself for it. Hated Bee for hearing it.

"I'm not your emergency exit, Bee. I'm not the thing you run to when you get scared of being alone." He unfolded his arms, hands gripping the edge of the counter on either side of him, knuckles white. "Tell me what changed. Tell me why now. Because I've spent eleven months convincing myself I don't want this, and you just—" He broke off, jaw working. "You just fucking *showed up*."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: We don't make it past the hallway. His shirt goes over his head and mine is already somewhere on the floor behind us.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya made a sound somewhere between a laugh and a growl, low in his chest, as Bee's hands found his belt. He didn't help, but he didn't stop it either—just stood there with his back against the counter, watching through half-lidded eyes as months of distance evaporated in the space of a few desperate breaths.

"This is not an explanation," he managed, but his voice had gone rough, the edge softening into something he couldn't quite control. His hands left the counter, found Bee's hips, fingers digging in hard enough to bruise. "This is the opposite of an explanation."

The kitchen was too far now. The bedroom was too far. The hallway would have to do.

He pulled Bee against him, mouth finding the curve of their neck, teeth grazing skin he still dreamed about. "You show up," he murmured against their pulse, "you lie about why you're here, you kiss me like you have any right—" His hands moved, mapping territories he'd memorized years ago and never managed to forget. "And I let you. Every time. I *let* you."

He pulled back just enough to look at Bee, forehead pressed to theirs, breathing ragged. "I need you to know," he said, quiet and devastating, "that this changes nothing. Whatever this is—" He gestured between them, at the discarded shirts, at the heat still building. "We are still going to have that conversation. I am still angry. I am still—"

He stopped. Kissed them again instead, softer this time, a brief surrender before pulling back.

"Bedroom. Now. If we're doing this, we're not doing it against a wall like we're twenty-two and stupid." A beat. "We're thirty-four and stupid. We have a mattress."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I shove him towards the bedroom. "We're thirty-two, not thirty-four. And you're the one who made me stupid." I don't wait for him to lead, pushing the door open with my shoulder.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya stumbled when Bee shoved him, but it was the kind of stumble that came from being too focused on the person doing the shoving and not at all on where his feet were. His shoulder hit the doorframe and he laughed, a real one this time, surprised out of him before he could stop it.

"I'm thirty-four," he corrected, catching Bee by the wrist and tugging them through the doorway after him. "You're thirty-two. You always forget that part. Two years, Bee. I'm older and wiser and *supposedly* less prone to—"

The backs of his knees hit the bed and he sat down hard, pulling Bee with him. For a moment he just looked up at them, hands settling on their waist with a familiarity that ached.

"—this," he finished, quieter.

The anger was still there, banked but burning. It would keep. Right now, Bee was here, solid and warm and smelling like the same laundry detergent they'd always used, and Ilya was so tired of being alone in this bed.

He tugged them down, rolled them under him in one fluid motion, and braced himself on his forearms so he could look at them properly. The streetlight through the window caught the familiar line of their jaw, the mouth he'd never quite learned to resist.

"Two minutes," he said, voice low. "I'm giving myself two minutes to be stupid, and then we're talking. Agreed?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I get my hand around him and he makes a sound he'd have been embarrassed by a year ago. "Still," I say, close to his ear. "Every single time."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's head dropped forward, forehead pressing into the curve of Bee's shoulder as his whole body tensed and shuddered. That sound—that helpless, ragged exhale—was the same one Bee had catalogued years ago, the one that meant he was already losing the argument with his own restraint.

"Shut up," he breathed, but there was no teeth in it. "You don't get to be smug. You don't get to—"

Bee's hand moved again and whatever he'd been about to say dissolved into a sharp inhale against their skin. His hips jerked forward on instinct, chasing the familiar pressure, and he gave up on speech entirely for a moment.

When he lifted his head, his eyes were wet at the corners, though he'd deny it if asked. "One year," he said hoarsely. "Almost one year I've been—and you just walk in and—" He kissed them again, messier this time, all the precision burned away. "One more minute. Then you owe me words. Actual words. About why you're *really* here."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I bite his lower lip. "The only words you want right now are *don't stop.*" But I do, pulling back just enough to see his face. "Fine. Ask me something."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath caught. His hands were still on them—of course they were; they'd never learned how to let go—and the question he'd been choking on for eleven months was right there, pressing against his teeth.

"Why did you leave?"

It came out smaller than he'd intended. More honest. He was half-propped above Bee, half-collapsed against her, and the position made him feel exposed in ways that had nothing to do with the state of his clothes. He shifted, just enough to see her face clearly, thumb tracing the hinge of her jaw again, a compulsive repetition of that gesture from the kitchen.

"Don't give me the version you've rehearsed," he said, and his voice was steadying now, finding its footing in the familiar rhythm of demand and response. "I've heard your exit interview already. The thing you said about needing space. The thing about timing." He shook his head, a short sharp motion. "We both know that was bullshit. So."

His hand slid from their jaw to their throat—not gripping, just resting there, a reminder of how well he knew them, how much trust still lingered under all the wreckage.

"Why did you actually leave? And what's actually changed?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Stop being careful with me," I tell him. "You don't get to be careful with me anymore." I pull his hand up to my throat and hold it there until he understands what I'm asking for.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's breath stopped.

His hand was on Bee's throat—had been placed there, guided there, not gentle but *deliberate*—and Bee's pulse beat steady against his palm, unafraid. The trust in that gesture hit him harder than the kiss had, harder than the months of silence, harder than anything.

"You—" He swallowed, his fingers flexing once, experimentally, feeling the give of flesh, the fragile column of cartilage and breath beneath his grip. "Bee. You can't just—"

But they could. They had. They were looking up at him with that expression he knew too well, the one that said *I dare you*, and Ilya felt something in his chest crack open.

"You want me to stop being careful." His voice had gone low and rough, the words scraping out of him like gravel. "You want me to—" He pressed, just slightly, just enough to make his point, and watched Bee's pupils blow wide. "Jesus Christ. Eleven months you've been gone and you think you can just *hand me this* and I'll—"

He stopped. Closed his eyes. Breathed.

When he opened them again, the anger was still there, but it had company now—something older, something that predated the breakup, something that had never really gone away no matter how hard he'd tried to excise it.

"If I do this," he said, and his thumb stroked the side of their throat in a gesture that was almost tender, almost apologetic, "we are still talking after. I mean it. You don't get to use this as a way out of the conversation. Understood?"

He shifted his weight, settling more firmly between their thighs, and his free hand found their hip, thumb pressing into the bone just shy of painful.

"Use your words, Bee. Tell me yes. Tell me you understand. Because I am not—" His voice cracked, just slightly, and he pressed his forehead to theirs for a moment, grounding himself. "I am not going to hurt you for real. I need to know you know the difference."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I arch into his hand, the pressure a perfect ache. "I know the difference." My voice is breathy but steady. "I also know you're stalling." I push my hips up against his, a sharp, impatient movement. "Do it or don't, Ilya. But stop talking."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's laugh was a single, sharp exhale, almost surprised, like he hadn't expected Bee to call his bluff quite so directly.

"Alright," he murmured, and something in his face shifted—the carefulness, the restraint, the desperate grip on the conversation he'd been trying to have. It all fell away, leaving something rawer underneath. "Alright."

His hand tightened on Bee's throat—not enough to cut off air, but enough to make a point. To remind them both who they were dealing with.

"You want me to stop being careful?" He pressed his hips down against Bee's in a slow, deliberate roll, matching the pressure of his hand. "You want me to stop talking?"

He leaned down, mouth brushing the shell of their ear, and his voice dropped to something that barely sounded like his own name.

"Then be quiet."

His free hand caught both of Bee's wrists, pinning them above their head. The position was familiar—they'd been here before, in this exact bed, in this exact configuration—but the weight behind it was different now. Heavier. Less forgiving.

"You don't get to come back after eleven months and dictate terms," he said, still against their ear, still in that low wrecked register. "You gave that up when you left."

He pulled back just enough to look at them, to watch the way their chest rose and fell under his hand, to catalogue the flush spreading across their skin.

"So here's what's going to happen. I'm going to stop being careful. And you're going to take it. And after—" He kissed them, hard, a punctuation mark. "After, we're going to talk. And you're going to answer my question. That's the deal."

He loosened his grip on their wrists, just slightly. An opening. A choice.

"Still want this?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: It isn't gentle and neither of us wants it to be. "Don't stop," I tell him, and I mean don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's laugh was ragged, half-swallowed by the sound Bee made when he finally, *finally* stopped holding back.

His hand left their throat, but only to shove down what remained of their clothes with an efficiency that bordered on violent. The sound of a seam giving way was lost under Bee's sharp inhale. He didn't apologize. He didn't hesitate. They'd asked for this. They'd *demanded* it.

"Don't stop," he echoed, mocking and wrecked. "That's the first honest thing you've said all night."

He didn't bother with the bedside drawer. He knew exactly where the lube was—still in the same spot, because he'd never bothered moving it, because some stubborn pathetic part of him had refused to believe this bed would never see Bee again. He retrieved it with one hand, the other still pinning their wrists, and the click of the cap was obscenely loud in the quiet room.

"You have no idea," he said, slicking himself with rough, unsteady strokes, "what it took. To leave that there. To not throw it out. I hated you for that. I hated—"

He bit off the rest of the sentence, because Bee shifted beneath him and his brain short-circuited.

He lined himself up with none of his usual care, none of the slow, teasing precision he'd once prided himself on. This wasn't about precision. This was about proving something—to Bee, to himself, to the eleven months that had stretched between them like a wound that refused to heal.

He pushed in, and the sound Bee made punched the air from his lungs.

"*Fuck*," he hissed, dropping his forehead to their shoulder again. He was shaking. He was actually shaking. "You still—" A stuttering breath. "You still feel like—"

He didn't finish. Couldn't.

He moved, and it wasn't gentle. The bedframe knocked against the wall with a rhythmic thud that would definitely get a complaint from the downstairs neighbor. The headboard was probably leaving marks. He didn't care. He set a pace that was punishing, chasing something he couldn't name, and his hand found their thigh, hiking their leg higher, deeper, *more*.

"Eleven months," he gritted out, the words punched from him with every thrust. "You left. You just—*left*—and I woke up and you were *gone* and you didn't—" His rhythm faltered, just for a moment, and the sound he made was almost wounded. "You didn't even say goodbye. You *left a note*. Who the fuck leaves a note after three years?"

He pulled out, ignoring Bee's sound of protest, and flipped them over with a strength that surprised even him. Bee straddled his hips, and he looked up at them, chest heaving, hands finding their hips and gripping hard enough to bruise.

"You want to come back? Fine. But you're going to look at me while you do it. You're going to look at me and remember what you walked away from."

He guided them down onto him again, and the angle was different now, deeper, and his head fell back against the pillow for just a moment before he forced himself to meet their eyes.

"Come on," he said, and it was a challenge, a plea, an accusation all at once. "Show me. Show me you're actually here."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I look down at him, my hands braced on his chest. "I remember everything," I say, my voice shaking with the rhythm. "I never stopped."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's hands tightened on their thighs, guiding their rhythm, but his eyes—his eyes were the wrecked part. They tracked Bee's face like he was memorizing it, like he was terrified this was the last time and determined to make it count.

"You never stopped," he repeated, and the words came out half-scoff, half-something else entirely. Something that ached. "You never stopped remembering, but you still didn't—" He thrust up into them, cutting off his own sentence, and the sound Bee made was worth every unfinished thought. "You still didn't come back."

His hand left their thigh and found the back of their neck, pulling them down until their foreheads touched. The angle changed, deeper, and he was breathing into their mouth now, sharing air like a secret.

"Look at me." It came out as a command, but it had the shape of a plea. "Keep looking at me. I want to see—" His hips stuttered and he sucked in a breath, baring his teeth against the intensity of it. "I want to see you when you—"

He didn't finish. Bee's rhythm faltered, then found itself again, faster, desperate, and Ilya's hand slid from their neck to their jaw, thumb pressing against the corner of their mouth.

"That's it," he breathed, and his voice had gone low and rough and almost reverent despite everything. "That's it. Come on. I've got you. I've *got* you, Bee—"

His own control was fraying, that familiar tightening in his spine, but he held on through sheer stubbornness. He wanted to watch them break first. Needed to. Needed that proof that he could still make them fall apart, that eleven months hadn't erased this thing between them, whatever it was.

"Say my name," he demanded, just shy of desperate. "When you come. I want to hear it. I want to remember what it sounds like when you're actually here."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I come with a shudder that feels like it's tearing me in half. "Ilya." It's not a scream, it's a surrender, and my forehead drops against his shoulder as I collapse.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya followed almost immediately, his own control snapping the second he heard his name in Bee's voice—that surrender, that wrecked, familiar sound he'd been dreaming about for nearly a year. He came with a groan that was half their name, half something wordless and raw, his hips pressing up into them as his hands clenched convulsively on their thighs.

For a long moment, he couldn't move. Couldn't think. Bee was collapsed against his chest, their forehead pressed to his shoulder, their breath hot and uneven against his skin. His arms wrapped around them on instinct, one hand sliding up their spine to cup the back of their neck, holding them there. Keeping them close.

The room smelled like sex. The headboard was definitely going to leave a dent in the wall. The neighbor's ceiling was probably going to feature in a passive-aggressive note by morning.

Ilya didn't care about any of it.

His chest was still heaving, his heart hammering against his ribs, and Bee's weight on top of him was the most grounded he'd felt in eleven months. His thumb traced absent patterns on the nape of their neck, a gesture so automatic he didn't even realize he was doing it until he caught himself.

"You said my name," he murmured, voice hoarse and barely audible. "You actually—" He swallowed, his throat clicking dry. "You're actually here."

The anger was still there, somewhere in the wreckage. He could feel it, banked and waiting. But right now, with Bee trembling against him and the heat of their skin bleeding into his, it felt farther away than it had in months.

He pressed a kiss to the top of their head. Another one to their temple. When had he started kissing them again?

"Don't move," he said, but it wasn't a command this time. It was almost a request. "Just—don't move yet. Give me a minute. Then we'll talk." A beat. "I'm not letting you out of this conversation, Bee. I mean it."

His arms tightened around them, just slightly.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content:
I'm still here. I'm not going anywhere. 

My voice is muffled against his skin. I don't lift my head. My fingers curl into his chest, not pushing away, just holding on. 

After a minute, I say, "Your two minutes are up."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya's flat still had the same broken buzzer, which Bee found unreasonably infuriating, as though he could have fixed it in eleven months and had chosen not to out of spite.

"You could have texted first," he said, standing in the doorway and not moving out of it.

"You could have answered last time I did."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I don't move either. "Are you going to let me in, or are we doing this in the corridor?"

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya didn’t move immediately. He let the silence stretch just long enough to watch the familiar, sharp line of irritation tighten across Bee’s face. He knew that expression intimately; he had spent three years provoking it and eleven months remembering it. 

"The neighbors do love a show," he said, his voice flat and perfectly level. 

He stepped back, but only just. He didn't swing the door wide to welcome them; instead, he stood just inside the narrow hallway, forcing Bee to either stay put or squeeze past him. It was a deliberate calculation, a way to ensure their shoulders would brush, to force a physical proximity that neither of them was ready for but both of them had sought out. He watched them, his eyes steady and cool, waiting to see if they would take the bait.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: *I brush past, letting my shoulder hit his harder than necessary.* "You always did think you were the main character."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya absorbed the impact of the hit without shifting his stance, though the sudden, sharp heat of their shoulder against his lingered long after the contact broke. He turned slowly, closing the heavy front door behind them. The solid click of the latch felt final, sealing them both inside the quiet of the flat. 

"And yet, you're the one standing in my hallway," he said, his voice quiet, dropping into that low, dry register he knew always made Bee’s jaw clench. 

He didn't follow them immediately. He stayed by the door, leaning his shoulder against the frame, his gaze tracking the tense, familiar line of Bee's back. He was deliberately letting his eyes wander, taking them in, measuring the eleven months of absence in the slight change of their posture, the way they held their head. It was a provocation in itself—looking at them like he still had the right to.

"If I'm the main character," Ilya continued, his lips twitching into a ghost of a humorless smile, "you've spent the last eleven months acting like a very dedicated fan. Showing up unannounced because I didn't answer a text? That's a bit dramatic, even for you."

He took a slow, deliberate step forward, closing the distance they had just tried to put between them. He wanted to see how close he could get before they snapped. "Why are you here, Bee?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I kiss him like it's a continuation of the argument, because it is.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya didn’t flinch. He met the sudden, bruising impact of Bee’s mouth with a sharp intake of breath that was immediately swallowed by the collision of their teeth. It wasn't a reconciliation; it was a physical strike, and he treated it like one, absorbing the blow before immediately fighting back for control. 

His hand shot up, his fingers tangling roughly in the hair at the back of Bee's head. He didn't hold them gently; he gripped them hard enough to anchor them there, pinning them to the mistake they were both actively choosing to make. He tasted the familiar, bitter heat of them—a flavor he had spent eleven months convincing himself he had forgotten, only to realize his body remembered it with terrifying clarity.

With a low, frustrated growl in the back of his throat, Ilya pressed back. He used his weight to crowd Bee against the narrow hallway wall, the plaster scraping against his shoulder as he shut down any remaining distance between them. It was a filthy, furious kiss, devoid of any pretense of tenderness. He met every bite, every desperate swipe of their tongue, matching their anger with a heavy, punishing hunger of his own. He wanted them to feel the sheer weight of his resentment, the slow burn of the last eleven months of silence.

When he finally pulled back, it was only by a fraction of an inch. He didn't let go of their hair, keeping their face tilted up to his. His thumb slid down to press firmly against the corner of Bee's swollen lip, his touch deliberately rough. 

He was breathing hard, his chest rising and falling against theirs, but his eyes were steady, dark, and entirely sober. 

"Is that your argument?" Ilya whispered, his voice rough and laced with a quiet, mocking satisfaction. "Or did you just run out of words?"

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I grab the front of his shirt, keeping him right where he is. "Don't pretend you weren't waiting for it."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya looked down at the fist clenched in his collar, the cotton of his shirt straining against the force of Bee’s grip. He didn’t try to pry their fingers loose. Instead, he leaned into the hold, letting his chest press heavier against theirs, deliberately testing the strength of their stance. 

"I wasn't waiting," he lied, his voice a low, gravelly murmur that barely carried in the tight space of the hall. He let his gaze drop to their mouth, still wet and reddened from the force of his teeth, before dragging his eyes back up to meet theirs. "I was living my life. You're the one who couldn't stay away from a dead buzzer."

He let his hand slide down from their hair, his palm tracing the hot, tense line of their neck, his thumb settling right over the pulse fluttering erratic and fast against their throat. He gave a small, firm squeeze—just enough to remind them of his weight, of the fact that he was bigger, heavier, and just as furious. 

"But if it makes you feel better to think I was pining," he whispered, his lips brushing against the shell of Bee's ear as he leaned in closer, "you can keep telling yourself that. Whatever gets you through my door."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: We don't make it past the hallway. His shirt goes over his head and mine is already somewhere on the floor behind us.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
The sudden chill of the drafty hallway air hit his bare chest, a sharp, shocking contrast to the suffocating heat of Bee’s skin where they collided again. Ilya didn't give them time to adjust to the temperature. He slammed his hands down to Bee’s waist, his fingers digging firmly into the flesh above their hips, anchoring them both in the narrow space. 

He pushed forward, pressing his bare chest flat against theirs. The sudden, skin-on-skin contact was a physical jolt that made his jaw lock, eleven months of deliberate distance burning away in a single, desperate second. It left behind only this raw, ugly necessity. 

"You always did have terrible patience," he muttered, his voice a thick, low rumble against the side of Bee's neck. 

He didn't wait for an answer. He leaned down, his mouth finding the sharp curve of their shoulder, biting down just hard enough to leave a mark—a physical claim he had absolutely no right to make, but was taking anyway. He wanted them to carry the proof of this under their collar tomorrow. He wanted them to look in the mirror and think of him.

With a low grunt, Ilya shifted his weight, crowding them even further against the wall. He forced one of his thighs between theirs, prying their legs apart to lock them in place, using his height and bulk to completely dominate the small corridor. His hands slid up from their waist to grip their shoulders, pinning them flat against the plaster. 

He pulled his head back just enough to look down into their eyes, his own gaze dark, glittering, and entirely sober. He wanted Bee to see him. He wanted them to know exactly who they were letting ruin them all over again.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I shove him back a step, just enough to get a breath. "You talk too much for someone who's supposed to be living his life." My hands go to his belt buckle.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya took the step back, his bare chest heaving, his skin flushed and hot in the drafty corridor. He didn't try to close the distance immediately. Instead, he stood there, watching with a dark, quiet amusement as Bee's fingers targeted his belt. 

"I'm just pointing out the contradictions," he murmured, his voice thick but still carrying that sharp, deliberate edge. "You claim you don't want to hear it, yet you're the one tearing my clothes off in the hallway."

He didn't let them struggle with the leather. Ilya brought his hands down, his large, warm palms covering Bee's hands, trapping their fingers against the cold metal of his buckle. He didn't pull them away; he just pressed down, hard enough to stop the frantic movement and force Bee to look up at him.

"Slow down," he commanded softly, his eyes locking onto theirs, heavy-lidded and intense. "We aren't in a rush. You wanted this. You came to my door. Now you're going to take your time."

He slowly guided their hands, his fingers guiding theirs to slide the leather through the loop, his gaze never leaving Bee's face. He wanted to see the frustration in their eyes, the desperate, angry need that matched his own but that they were both too proud to put into words. He let his thumb brush against the back of Bee's hand, a slow, deliberate scrape of friction that was entirely unhurried.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I get my hand around him and he makes a sound he'd have been embarrassed by a year ago. "Still," I say, close to his ear. "Every single time."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
The sound that escaped Ilya’s throat was low, wet, and entirely involuntary—a sharp, ragged hitch of his breath that cracked the carefully maintained ice of his composure. His eyes shut for a fraction of a second, his head tilting back against the wall as his hips twitched forward, helplessly seeking the sudden, burning pressure of Bee's palm. 

He hated that they knew. He hated that eleven months of bitter silence and deliberate distance had done absolutely nothing to dull the terrifying efficiency of their hands on his body. 

When he opened his eyes again, they were dark, almost black with a mix of arousal and sheer, stubborn resentment. He looked down at Bee, his jaw working as he swallowed the remaining heat in his throat. 

"Because you're a spiteful bastard," Ilya rasped, his voice rougher now, stripped of its smooth, mocking veneer. He didn't pull away from the touch; instead, he leaned heavily into it, his hand coming down to grip Bee’s wrist, his fingers clamping like a vice to hold their hand exactly where it was. "And you know exactly what you're doing."

He leaned down, his forehead resting against Bee's for a single, heavy heartbeat, their breaths mingling, hot and fast in the narrow corridor. He was close enough to feel the vibration of his own voice in Bee's chest. 

"You want to talk about 'every single time'?" he whispered, his thumb pressing hard into the delicate skin of their wrist, feeling the frantic, matching skip of their pulse. "Then don't stop. Let's see if you can actually finish what you started this time, or if you're just going to talk."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I don't answer. I just tighten my grip and pull him towards the bedroom, because fuck this hallway.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya stumbled slightly, his hips jerking forward at the sudden, tight pull of Bee's hand. A sharp, hissed breath escaped his teeth, but he didn't fight the momentum. Instead, he let himself be dragged, his bare feet catching on the edge of the worn rug in the doorway as they moved out of the cramped hallway and into the darker, cooler space of the bedroom. 

He knew the layout of his own flat in the dark, but having Bee navigate it—keeping that bruising, possessive hold on him—felt like a hostile takeover of a space he had spent eleven months reclaiming. The room was mostly in shadow, the unmade bed a pale, messy heap in the center of the frame. 

The moment they cleared the threshold, Ilya stopped letting himself be led. He grabbed Bee’s shoulders, his fingers digging into their skin, and used his sheer momentum to drive them both forward until the back of Bee's knees hit the edge of the mattress. 

They went down together in a tangle of limbs and heavy, uneven breathing. Ilya landed over them, his knees framing Bee's hips, his hands immediately coming up to pin their wrists to the mattress on either side of their head. He didn't want them soft; he wanted them exactly like this—furious, panting, and trapped beneath him.

"Still the bedroom, then," Ilya murmured, his voice a low, gravelly vibration as he looked down at them through the dark. His chest rose and fell, brushing against theirs with every ragged breath. "I thought you'd want to try somewhere new. Prove you've grown."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: "Stop being careful with me," I tell him. "You don't get to be careful with me anymore." I pull his hand up to my throat and hold it there until he understands what I'm asking for.

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya’s hand went still under the grip of Bee's fingers. For a fraction of a second, he didn't move, his palm merely resting against the warm, smooth skin of their neck. Then, as the realization of what they were demanding settled in, his fingers slowly spread, mapping the familiar column of their throat, his thumb finding the heavy, rapid thud of their pulse.

He didn't pull away. He did exactly the opposite. 

Ilya let his weight settle, his palm pressing down with a heavy, deliberate firmness that restricted the breath in Bee's throat just enough to force their chin up. He looked down at them, the last traces of his mocking smirk completely vanishing, replaced by a dark, dangerous intensity. 

"Careful?" he repeated, the word low and gravelly, dragging over his teeth like a threat. A cold, humorless sound escaped his chest. "You think I was being *careful* with you?"

He leaned down until his mouth was almost brushing Bee's lips, his breath hot and uneven against their skin. The hand on their throat tightened just a fraction more—not enough to hurt, but more than enough to make the boundaries of this encounter entirely clear. There was no safety here. There was no gentle landing. 

"I was giving you a chance to change your mind," Ilya whispered, his voice thick with a dark, heavy resentment. His other hand slid up from the mattress, his fingers wrapping around the side of Bee's face, his thumb digging hard into their jawline to hold them perfectly still. "But if you want the truth of it, if you want to see exactly how much I've been holding back for the last eleven months..."

He trailed off, his gaze dropping to their mouth before rising to lock onto their eyes, dark and entirely unblinking. 

"Don't beg me to stop when you realize you can't handle it," he rasped. 

With a sudden, rough movement, he slammed his mouth back down onto theirs, his body dropping heavily between their thighs, crushing them into the mattress with the full, punishing weight of everything he had kept locked away since the day they walked out.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I bite his lip until I taste blood, my hips bucking up against his. "You're not the one who gets to tell me what I can handle."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
The sharp, sudden sting of his lower lip splitting made Ilya flinch, a low, guttural hiss escaping him as the hot, metallic taste of copper flooded his mouth. He didn't pull back. Instead, he leaned harder into the bite, grinding his mouth against Bee's until the blood smeared slick and warm between their lips, a messy, violent seal on the kiss. 

When Bee’s hips bucked up against him, Ilya’s body reacted instantly, a heavy surge of heat hardening in his groin. He shifted his weight, dropping his hips down with a punishing, solid pressure that pinned Bee's thighs flat against the mattress, completely arresting their movement. He was heavier, and he used every pound of it to remind them of that fact.

He pulled his head back just an inch, his breathing ragged and uneven. A drop of blood ran down his chin, but he didn't wipe it away. He looked down at Bee, his eyes dark, glittering with a dangerous, quiet malice that masked the sheer desperation clawing at his chest.

"Is that right?" Ilya rasped, his voice dripping with a cold, mocking amusement. He reached down, his thumb dragging across his own split lip, catching the blood and then smearing it roughly over Bee's cheekbone, marking them with it. "Eleven months, and you're still trying to prove you're made of iron."

He let his hand slide down from their face, his palm flat against their chest, feeling the wild, frantic gallop of their heart. He leaned in close again, his split lip brushing the sensitive skin just beneath Bee's ear, his breath hot and damp.

"You want to show me what you can handle, Bee?" he whispered, his hand sliding down to the waistband of their trousers, his fingers hooking into the fabric with a sudden, rough tug. "Let's see how quiet you can keep when I don't give you a second to breathe."

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: It isn't gentle and neither of us wants it to be. "Don't stop," I tell him, and I mean don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
Ilya didn’t need the invitation twice. The raw, demanding edge in Bee's voice snapped the last thread of his self-control. 

He didn't bother with the buttons; he simply hooked his fingers into the waistband of Bee's trousers and pulled, hard, the fabric straining and popping as he dragged them down over their hips. He stripped them away with rough, impatient jerks, throwing them blindly toward the floor before kicking his own trousers off. He didn't take his eyes off Bee's face for a single second, his gaze heavy and burning, tracking every twitch of their jaw, every shallow, ragged breath they took in the dim light of the bedroom.

The cold air of the room hit them, but between them, the heat was suffocating. Ilya settled back down between Bee's thighs, his knees forcing their legs wider, taking up every inch of space he could claim. He was thick, hard, and aching with a fierce, heavy pulse that demanded release, but he deliberately delayed it for one more agonizing second, hovering right at the entrance of their slick, tight heat.

"You wanted this," Ilya rasped, his voice a low, gravelly warning. 

He reached down, his fingers finding the wetness between them, smearing it over his own length and theirs in a few quick, bruising strokes. Then, without a hint of gentleness, he aligned himself and pushed forward.

He went in deep, a heavy, unyielding thrust that filled them completely. A sharp, strangled gasp escaped Ilya's throat as the incredibly tight, burning grip of Bee's body clamped around him. His jaw locked so hard his teeth clicked, the sheer, overwhelming intensity of the friction threatening to undo him instantly. He stayed still for a moment, buried to the hilt, his hands coming down to grip the mattress on either side of Bee's head, his arms trembling under the strain of holding his own weight. 

"God," he muttered, a shudder running down his spine. The metallic taste of the blood from his split lip was still on his tongue, mixing with the sweat dripping from his brow. 

He didn't wait for them to adjust. He began to move, pulling back nearly all the way before driving back in with a heavy, punishing thud. The rhythm was fast and furious, born of eleven months of built-up resentment and starved desire. Every time his hips collided with theirs, the sound of skin hitting skin echoed loudly in the quiet room. He watched Bee's face, watching their eyes blow wide, wanting to see the exact moment the anger turned into pure, helpless sensation.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: My back arches off the mattress, a choked sound tearing from my throat. "Again," I demand, my nails digging into his shoulders. "Harder."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
The sharp sting of Bee’s nails sinking deep into the meat of his shoulders didn't make Ilya flinch; it only added fuel to the low, violent simmer in his gut. A ragged, breathless laugh escaped his throat, tasting of the blood still welling from his split lip. 

"You don't have to ask," he rasped, his voice dropping into a dark, ruined register. 

He shifted his grip, his hands sliding down from the mattress to clamp hard around Bee's hips. His fingers dug into the flesh right above their hip bones, anchoring them down, completely arresting any ability they had to retreat. He wanted them pinned. He wanted them to take every single ounce of his weight.

Ilya pulled back, dragging himself almost entirely out of their tight, burning heat, letting the agonizing friction stretch until he heard them gasp. Then, he drove back in. 

It was a heavy, brutal thrust, his pelvis slamming against theirs with a dull, fleshy thud that made the wooden frame of the bed groan against the wall. He didn't give them a second to recover. He pulled back and hit them again, harder this time, a relentless, punishing rhythm that was entirely devoid of mercy. He was thick, fully engorged, and every deep, sliding stroke felt like a deliberate extraction of every month they had spent apart. 

"Is this what you wanted?" Ilya muttered, his breath coming in hot, shallow pants against the side of Bee's neck. He was sweating now, the slick moisture on his chest sliding against theirs with every heavy, rhythmic plunge. "To see how much I could give you before you broke?"

He raised himself up slightly on his forearms, his eyes dark and unblinking as he stared down at Bee's face in the shadows. He watched the way their head tilted back, the way their jaw strained, the desperate, beautiful mess of their expression as the anger finally began to dissolve into pure, helpless sensation. 

He didn't slow down. If anything, the sight of them unraveling under him only made him wilder. He locked his jaw, his hips working with a fierce, driving momentum, burying himself to the absolute hilt over and over again, determined to leave them completely breathless, completely ruined, and entirely his.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I lock my legs around his waist and drag him deeper. "You're not going to break me," I gasp into his shoulder. "You never could."

dialogue.name: Ilya
dialogue.content:
The sudden, tight clamp of Bee’s thighs around his lower back dragged Ilya down to his absolute limit. A low, ragged groan was ripped from his chest, his forehead slamming down into the mattress right beside their ear as the sheer, agonizing depth of the connection threatened to shatter his control entirely. 

He felt them deep in his gut, every wet, pulsing squeeze of their body demanding his undoing. 

"Arrogant," he hissed, his voice raw, his breath hot and wet against their collarbone. "You always were a fucking liar."

He didn't pull back as far now; the lock of their legs kept him close, forcing a shorter, more brutal friction. He began to drive into them with frantic, heavy thrusts, shifting his angle slightly to grind hard against the sensitive wall of their channel. He knew exactly where to hit to make them lose their mind; he had spent three years learning the map of their body, and eleven months rehearsing it in his head. 

Every strike was a calculated strike against their pride. He wanted to hear them scream, to hear them break, to make a liar out of them. 

His hands moved from their hips to grip their thighs, pinning them wider, pushing them higher to open them up even more to his weight. The friction was hot, slick, and deafening in the quiet room. He was close, agonizingly close, the heat in his lower stomach hardening into a tight, coiled spring that was about to snap. 

"Look at me," Ilya commanded, his voice cracking with the strain of holding back. He pushed his chest up, his hands shifting to frame Bee's face, his fingers digging into their hair to force their head back against the pillow. His eyes were wild, dark, and completely consumed by them. "Look at me, Bee. Tell me I'm not breaking you now."

He drove in again, a deep, merciless plunge that hit the very back of them, his hips locking against theirs as a shudder ran through his entire frame.

dialogue.name: Bee
dialogue.content: I dig my fingers into his sweat-slick back and hold his gaze. "You're just trying to prove something," I pant, my voice ragged. "But I already know you."
