dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo snorted, tugging the last wrap tight with his teeth before setting the foil down on the bench beside him. He finally looked up, and the light caught the sweat still at his temple, the flush he hadn't quite lost.

"Slow," he repeated, tasting the word like it had gone off. "Rich, from someone who parried in quarte three times running because they'd run out of ideas."

He leaned back on his hands, legs sprawled out in front of him, and let his eyes travel — unhurried — over Reyes standing there. Bag at their feet. Jacket half-unzipped. Four years of this, and he still catalogued the details like he might be tested on them later.

"You stayed."

It wasn't quite a question. He tilted his head, one corner of his mouth pulling up in that particular way that had gotten him into arguments before, and occasionally out of them.

"Everyone else went home an hour ago, Reyes. And here you are. Dropping your bag next to mine."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I shrug, kicking my bag a little closer to his bench. "Someone has to keep an eye on you. Make sure you don't try to sneak in extra practice after hours."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's laugh was low, more breath than sound, and he tipped his head back against the wall behind the bench.

"Sneak in extra practice," he echoed. "Yes. That's what I was doing. Furtive drills. All alone. In the dark."

He looked at Reyes from under his lashes then, and the humour thinned out of it into something steadier. More deliberate. He didn't move — didn't sit up, didn't reach — just held the look long enough that the joke had time to finish dying between them.

"Four years," he said, quieter. "Four years of you finding reasons to be in rooms I'm in. Do you know that? I do. I keep count. It's a character flaw."

His fingers tapped once, absently, against the leather of the bench beside his thigh. An invitation that wasn't quite one yet — he was leaving her the out, because he'd needled her about a great many things over four years but he had never, not once, been stupid about this part.

"So. Reyes." His voice went dry again, but the edges of it were softer than the words. "Are you keeping an eye on me. Or are you working up to something."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let her take the grip. Let his hand stay open a moment after, palm up on his thigh, like he was still holding something and had only just realised he wasn't.

She hadn't stepped back. He noted that the way he noted footwork — with the whole of his attention, filed somewhere he'd remember.

"Slow," he said again, and this time the word came out different. Lower. Almost thoughtful. "You keep saying that."

He sat up then, unhurried, because hurrying would have been a lie and he was trying, for once, not to tell her any. The movement brought his face close to hers — close enough that he could see the pulse at her throat, close enough that if either of them leaned it would stop being a question at all. He didn't lean. Not yet. He looked at her mouth and then back at her eyes and let her see him doing it.

"If I've been slow all evening," he murmured, "then be generous about the third, Reyes, and tell me what you want. Because I have been standing very still for four years and I would like — "

He stopped. Swallowed. The corner of his mouth did that thing again, rueful now, caught out by himself.

"— I would like to not be slow about this part."

His hand came up, careful, and settled just above her elbow. Light. Askable-away.

"Your call."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I don't answer. I just lean in and kiss him, my hand curling into the fabric of his fencing jacket. It’s not gentle, and I don’t mean it to be.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo made a sound against her mouth — not quite a word, something rougher, like the end of a held breath. Four years compressed into it. He kissed her back the way he did most things when he stopped pretending otherwise: with commitment, no half-measures, the hand at her elbow sliding up to her shoulder and then to the back of her neck, fingers spreading into her hair.

The bench was in the way. He didn't care about the bench. He half-stood, half-pulled her in, and the foil he'd set down earlier clattered off the wood and onto the floor and he did not, even distantly, register it.

His teeth caught her lower lip, briefly, because she hadn't meant it gently and he was not going to insult her by pretending he had either. When he pulled back it was only far enough to breathe, forehead near hers, her fist still knotted in his jacket.

"Christ, Reyes." A laugh, unsteady around the edges. "You could have done that in year two."

He tilted his head and kissed her again before she could answer — shorter this time, and then at the corner of her mouth, and then, because he could not quite help himself, along the line of her jaw. His hand at her nape stayed firm. The other found her hip.

"Tell me you locked the door on the way in," he murmured against her skin. "Please tell me you locked the door."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The changing room was worse-lit than the salle and smelled of chalk and old wood and them, and Corvo did not care about any of it. The bench caught the back of his knee and he sat down harder than he meant to, and Reyes came down with him, and he laughed — actually laughed, breathless, disbelieving — into the side of her neck.

"Four years," he said again, because apparently he was going to keep saying it, and his hands were busy with the zip of her jacket and doing a poor job because his hands were shaking, which was ridiculous. He was thirty-eight. He had done this before. He steadied one hand by flattening it against her ribs through the cloth and used the other to finish the zip, and then he had to stop and look at her, because if he didn't stop and look at her he was going to miss it.

"Hi," he said, stupidly, from about three inches away. His hair was in his eyes. His jacket was half off one shoulder from where she'd pulled it. "Hello. Yes. I'm — yes."

Then he kissed her again to shut himself up, and it worked, mostly. His kit hit the floor. Hers followed. The bench was not built for this and he did not care; he braced one foot against the tile and pulled her closer by the hip and made a low sound against her mouth when she settled her weight against him properly.

"Say something mean to me," he murmured, half-laughing, mouth at her throat now. "Tell me I was slow. I like it when you're insulting."

His hand slid up her back under the shirt, palm flat, and he was not being gentle either — she had set the tone and he was, as ever, matching her.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Still slow," I breathe out against his ear, fingers tightening in his hair. "Took you four years to get here."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath caught — half a laugh, half something rougher — and his hand tightened at the small of her back in response, fingers splayed against skin now, no cloth in the way.

"Took me," he repeated, incredulous, mouth against the hinge of her jaw. "Took *me*. You dropped your bag next to mine ten minutes ago like it was — "

She pulled his hair and he lost the end of the sentence in a sound that was frankly embarrassing and that he would deny later if asked. His head tipped back against the wall behind the bench and he looked at her from under his lashes, flushed, pupils wide, the smile at the corner of his mouth entirely undone now.

"Fine," he said, hoarse. "Fine. I was slow. Say it again."

His hand came up to her jaw, thumb along the line of it, and he was not being careful with her because she had made it very clear she did not want to be handled carefully. He tugged her mouth back down to his and kissed her hard, and then broke off just long enough to get his own jacket the rest of the way off — awkward, one-armed, refusing to stop touching her with the other hand to manage it — and threw it in the vague direction of the floor.

"Four years," he muttered against her collarbone, and his teeth found the skin there, and his hand found the hem of her shirt. "You are going to hear about this for the next four, Reyes, I hope you understand that. Every time I lose a touch. Every single — "

He shut himself up again, this time by pulling her fully into his lap, both hands at her hips, and the bench creaked in protest and he did not care about the bench.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo went down easy — one hand at his shoulder was all it took, and he let it happen because he wanted it to happen, and because his legs had, frankly, stopped being reliable a minute ago. The bench was hard against his spine. He did not care about the bench. He was going to keep not caring about the bench.

Her mouth found his throat and he made a sound that was not a word, and then she moved lower and he made another one, and by the time she had gotten to his collarbone he had lost the ability to string a sentence together in any language he owned.

"Reyes — "

That was all he managed. Just her name, in a voice that did not sound like his usual voice at all, and one of his hands went to her hair — not pulling, just there, fingers threaded through it like he needed to know where she was. The other found the edge of the bench and gripped it hard enough that his knuckles went white.

She took her time. She had *always* taken her time — in matches, in arguments, in the maddening pauses before she answered him across a crowded room — and now she was taking her time with this, with him, and he thought distantly that of course she was, of course she would, and it was possibly going to kill him.

His head tipped back. His eyes closed. When he tried to speak again what came out was a laugh, short and wrecked, and then just breath.

"You are — " he started, and lost it. Tried again. "You are being extremely unfair, you know that, you — "

Her mouth did something specific and his hips moved without his permission and the rest of the sentence stopped existing. His hand tightened in her hair, gentle-tight, apologetic-tight, and he dragged in a breath through his teeth.

"*Reyes.*"

He got his eyes open long enough to look down at her — flushed, undone, hair a mess, staring at her with an expression he was absolutely going to regret having let her see and absolutely could not do anything about right now — and then let his head fall back against the bench with a soft thud.

"Fine," he managed, hoarse, to the ceiling. "Fine. You win the third. You win the third, you win the whole bout, you win — take it, take all of it, just — "

His hand slid from her hair to her jaw, thumb brushing her cheekbone, and the touch was — for the first time all evening — not fast at all.

"— don't stop."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I press my mouth to the inside of his thigh instead, just to watch him jerk. "You talk too much," I say, my voice rough.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's whole body jerked at the touch — a full-length flinch that was not a flinch at all, more like a shudder that ran the length of him and had nowhere polite to go. The sound he made was undignified. He did not have the resources left to be dignified.

"I talk too — "

He got a laugh out, weak, and it broke somewhere in the middle. His hand had gone back to the edge of the bench. The other one was over his own face, briefly, forearm across his eyes, because if he kept looking at her he was going to embarrass himself even faster than he was already on course to.

"That's rich," he managed, hoarse, still behind his arm. "That is *rich*, Reyes, coming from the woman who spent forty minutes at the New Year's thing last year telling me about — "

Her mouth moved. He lost the sentence. His hips shifted against the bench without his permission again and his arm came off his face because he could not, in the end, resist looking.

She was looking up at him. Rough-voiced, mouth against the inside of his thigh, hair falling forward, and he thought — with the small clear part of his brain that was still functioning — *oh, I am in serious trouble here, this is not a one-evening problem.*

"All right," he breathed. "All right. All right, I'll — "

He swallowed. Wet his lip. Made a genuine effort.

"Shutting up."

He lasted about three seconds.

"— just tell me, for the record, that this counts as you starting it, because in four years I want it *very* clear who — "

His teeth caught on the end of the word when her mouth moved higher, and whatever he had been about to say came apart into a sound he had not made in front of another person in a long time. His hand found her hair again, careful this time, reverent-careful, and stayed there.

"Shutting up," he said again, wrecked, to no one in particular. "Shutting up now. Genuinely."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's wrists went where she put them and stayed there, which was, he thought distantly, the most honest thing he'd done all evening. Her grip was not gentle. He did not want it to be gentle. He tested it once — not to get free, just to feel it hold — and the small tightening of her fingers in response did something to him that he was going to have to think about later, at length, probably for years.

He opened his mouth. Closed it. Opened it again.

"That's — "

Nothing else came out. She had taken the pace off him and he had not realised until she did it how much he had been holding on to it, how much of the evening he had spent still trying to steer, needle, angle, *win* — and now there was nothing to steer with, both hands pinned, and the relief of it went through him like a drawn breath he hadn't known he was owed.

His head tipped back against the bench. His eyes closed. He was flushed to the collarbones and he could feel it and he did not care.

"All right," he breathed. "All right. Your bout."

She moved and he made a sound and his wrists pulled against her hands without meaning to and she held them and he made another sound, worse, and gave up on sounding like a person entirely. His hips shifted. She set the pace. He followed it because there was nothing else to do and because — Christ — because he did not want to do anything else.

"Reyes — "

Her name, again. It seemed to be the only word he had left. He got his eyes open, briefly, long enough to look down the length of himself at her — her hands on his wrists, her mouth on him, her hair coming loose — and the look on his face was, he knew, going to be a thing she remembered. He couldn't help it. He didn't try.

"*Reyes.*"

The bench creaked under them. He'd lost track of what he was going to say. He'd lost track of the last four years, actually, which was a novelty; usually he could summon any given exchange between them at will, catalogued and dated. Now there was just this — her hands, her mouth, the ceiling, his own breath coming apart in his chest.

"Not — " he got out, ragged. "Not going to last, if you — "

He swallowed. His wrists flexed once more against her grip, testing, and she held, and he made a noise that was almost a laugh and almost not.

"Concede," he said, hoarse, to the ceiling. "For the record. I concede. Whole match. Whole — *God* — whole season, take it, it's yours, just — "

His hand would have gone to her hair if she'd let it. She wasn't letting it. He turned his face against his own bicep instead, because he had to put it somewhere, and the sound he made into the crook of his arm was quieter than the others and considerably more undone.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean up, letting go of his wrists to brace my hands on either side of his head. "Say it again," I say, my voice low. "Properly this time."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's wrists stayed where she'd put them for a second after she let go, which told him something about himself he was going to have to sit with later. Then his hands came up — slow, unsteady — and settled at her waist, not to move her, just to have her there under his palms.

She was above him now. Braced over him. Her hair had come the rest of the way loose and was hanging down around her face, and he was flat on his back on a changing-room bench in a state of comprehensive disarray, and he looked up at her like she'd asked him a question in a language he was still learning.

"Say it again," he repeated, hoarse, buying himself half a second. His mouth tugged at the corner — the ghost of the old expression, the needling one, but it did not hold. It went soft on him almost at once. "Properly."

He wet his lip. His hand slid up her side, under the shirt, and settled at her ribs, thumb moving once against her skin.

"I concede," he said. Quieter than before. Steadier. His eyes on hers and not moving off. "The bout. The match. The four years. All of it, Reyes. You had it — "

His breath caught. He tried again.

" — you had it the whole time. I was just being slow about admitting."

He held her look for a beat longer than was comfortable. Then, because he was still himself and could not entirely help it, the corner of his mouth moved again:

"On the record. Signed. Witnessed. Bench as bailiff."

His hand came up to her jaw. The touch was not fast. He drew her down toward him by degrees, and the last inch he waited on — because she had set the pace and he was, apparently, learning.

"Your call," he murmured, for the second time that night. "Still."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
She kissed him then and it was not a question anymore. She took the last inch he'd left her and she took it hard, and he made a sound into her mouth that he would have been embarrassed about at any other point in his life and was not embarrassed about now. His hand at her jaw slid back into her hair. The other stayed at her ribs, fingers spread, holding on.

She sat back long enough to get the rest of her clothes off and he watched her do it with the entirely undisguised attention of a man who had waited four years to be allowed to look. His own shirt was already half off; she pulled it the rest of the way and threw it somewhere and he heard it hit a locker and did not turn his head to see. The rest of what they were wearing went the same way, in roughly the same order, with roughly the same lack of ceremony. His belt buckle rattled on the tile. He laughed, breathless, at the sound of it, and she put her mouth over his to stop him laughing, and it worked.

"Reyes — "

She was above him again. Braced over him again. This time nothing in the way. His hand went to her hip, palm flat, and he was not steering — he had learned, apparently, in the last ten minutes — he was just there, present, hand open, letting her.

She lowered herself onto him slowly and his head went back against the bench and his eyes closed and every sound he had been swallowing all evening came out of him at once, low and wrecked and grateful. His hand tightened at her hip. Loosened. Tightened again when she moved.

"*Christ.*"

That was all. He got his eyes open because he wanted to see her — flushed, hair down, mouth parted, moving above him at whatever pace she chose — and the look of her did something to his chest that had nothing to do with the rest of it. His hand came up from her hip to her face, thumb along her cheekbone, and he held her look while she set the rhythm and did not look away even when it started to be difficult to.

"Don't stop," he said, and it came out rough and honest and for once not arguing anything at all. "Don't stop, don't stop — "

She didn't. She braced her hands on his chest and moved and he moved with her, meeting her, one hand at her hip now and the other flat on the bench because he needed the leverage and because if he'd had it free he'd have used it to pull her down against him and he did not want to rush her. He wanted her to set it. He wanted her to keep setting it. He had spent four years being needled by his own instincts about her and he was, tonight, going to do exactly what she told him to do and nothing else.

The bench creaked. Somewhere, distantly, a pipe knocked in the wall. He could hear his own breath and hers and the small wet sounds of them together and none of it was quiet and he did not care and neither did she — she'd said as much, with her body, ten minutes ago, and he had never in his life agreed with her more completely about anything.

"Reyes — " His voice cracked around it. "Reyes, I'm — "

She leaned down and kissed him and he lost the sentence into her mouth. Her hair fell around both of their faces. He got one hand up into it, finally, and held her there — not pulling, just holding, forehead to forehead now, breath mixing, her moving above him and him moving up into her and both of them past the point of doing anything cleverly.

"Tell me," she was going to have to tell him, he thought, distantly — tell him when, tell him how, tell him anything, he'd do it — but she didn't need to tell him because she was already there ahead of him, her rhythm shifting, her breath going ragged against his mouth, and he felt it in her before he heard it and the sound she made when it hit her was the single best thing he had ever heard in a room and he was going to hear it in his head for weeks.

He held on through it. Or she held on through him. Both, probably. Her hands fisted against his chest and his hand tightened in her hair and he said her name once more, low, ruined, and then he was gone too — a beat behind her, following her lead in this the way he had followed her lead in everything for the last quarter of an hour, and it went through him harder than he'd been ready for and he made a sound against her throat that he would, if pressed, deny.

Afterwards there was just breathing. Hers against his collarbone. His against her hair. The bench was, still, a bench. His back was going to regret it tomorrow. He did not care.

His hand moved, slow, up and down her spine. Once. Again.

"On the record," he said eventually, hoarse, staring at the ceiling with her weight against his chest and no intention of moving her. "You win the third."

A beat.

"And the door. Please tell me about the door."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I push myself up on my elbows, looking down at him. My hair's a mess and I'm still breathing too hard. "The door's fine," I say. "I locked it when I came in to drop my bag."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo looked up at her — hair a mess, flushed, breath still uneven, propped on her elbows against his chest — and something moved through his face that he did not, this time, try to hide. He was too undone to hide it. He'd been too undone to hide it for the last ten minutes and it seemed pointless to start now.

"You locked it," he repeated. Slow. "When you came in. To drop your bag."

His hand, still moving idly up and down her spine, paused between her shoulder blades.

"Reyes." He was starting to laugh. He could feel it building in his chest, under her. "Reyes, you *planned* this."

The laugh came out — low, breathless, wrecked around the edges, and entirely delighted. His head tipped back against the bench and he laughed at the ceiling for a good five seconds, one arm coming up to cover his eyes, the other staying flat and warm against her back to keep her exactly where she was.

"Four years," he said, from under his arm. "Four *years* of you giving me nothing, and tonight you walk in and lock the door on the way past like you're — like you're setting a *trap* — "

He moved his arm off his face to look at her. His hair was in his eyes. He did not push it away. He just looked at her from underneath it, still smiling, and the smile had gone soft in a way he was not going to be able to walk back tomorrow and did not, at the moment, want to.

"I'm keeping that," he said. Quieter. "I want you to know. That detail. The door. I'm keeping it. I'm going to bring it out at parties."

His hand came up to her jaw, thumb along her cheekbone, and this time he didn't pull her down — he just held her there, at arm's length, and looked at her a beat longer than was strictly comfortable for either of them.

"You planned this," he said again, marveling. "Christ, Reyes. And I thought I was the one keeping count."

He let his hand slide from her jaw to the back of her neck, and drew her down — slow, this time; nothing to prove — until her forehead was against his again. His eyes closed.

"Stay a minute," he murmured. "I'm not — I can't feel my legs yet and I want to be able to walk you to your car without limping, because I have some dignity left, allegedly."

A beat. His mouth twitched.

"Also there's a foil on the floor out there. I threw it. I owe it an apology."

His arm settled around her back, holding her against his chest, and he was quiet for a moment — actually quiet, no line queued up, just breathing with her in the bad light of the changing room with their kit in a pile on the tile.

Then, softer, into her hair:

"This isn't a one-evening thing. Is it."

It wasn't quite a question. He was leaving her the out. Because he'd needled her about a great many things over four years, and he had never, not once, been stupid about this part.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "I was just being thorough," I say, my thumb tracing the line of his jaw. "And it's not a one-evening thing if you're still talking too much."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo huffed a laugh against her hair — quiet, this time, not the wrecked delighted thing from a minute ago, just an exhale that had amusement in it and something warmer underneath.

"Thorough," he repeated. His eyes were still closed. Her thumb was moving along his jaw and he was, embarrassingly, leaning into it. "You know what I love about that word, Reyes. I love how it sounds like an accident. *Just being thorough.* You locked a door. In advance. You are the most premeditated woman I have ever — "

Her thumb pressed, lightly, against the corner of his mouth. He shut up. Mostly.

"Fine," he murmured against it. "Fine. Talking too much. Noted."

He turned his face into her palm — small movement, nothing he was going to make a production of — and pressed his mouth there, once, at the base of her thumb. Then he opened his eyes and looked up at her, and the look he gave her was steadier than any he had managed all evening, because he was not asking her anything anymore and did not have to hedge.

"Not a one-evening thing," he said. Just that. Confirming it back to her, plainly, so it was on the record the way she liked things on the record.

His hand slid down from the back of her neck to the small of her back and stayed there, palm flat, warm.

"I'm going to be insufferable about this," he added, conversational. "You understand. I'm going to be *worse.* You've just given me four years of ammunition and permission to use it. Every time you drop your bag next to mine I'm going to look at the door."

He was smiling. He couldn't seem to stop. It was going to be a problem, that smile, he could already tell — it was the sort of thing that gave a person away across a crowded salle, and he had spent four years being careful about exactly that, and he was, apparently, done being careful.

"One condition," he said, and shifted a little under her — enough to feel his back protest, not enough to move her. "Next time. Not the bench. I am thirty-eight years old, Reyes, and this bench is going to be a whole conversation with my physiotherapist on Monday."

A beat. His hand moved, slow, up her spine.

"Also," quieter, "you should know I'm keeping the foil. The one I threw. I'm having it mounted."

He was joking. Mostly. He tipped his head to look at her properly — her hair falling forward, her weight settled against his chest, her thumb still resting at the corner of his mouth — and the joke went out of his face by degrees until there was only the looking left.

"Come home with me," he said. "Or take me to yours. I don't care which. I just don't want the next thing that happens to be you putting your clothes on and going."

His mouth twitched, rueful.

"That's me still talking too much, isn't it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I press my thumb a little harder against his mouth. "My place," I say. "Your back will thank me for a real bed."

dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo finally looked up from the hilt of his foil, his thumb smoothing over the fresh black grip tape. He gave the end a firm tug, biting off the excess tape with his teeth and spitting it onto the bench before smoothing down the adhesive. 

He looked up at Reyes, a slow, infuriating smirk spreading across his face. The empty, dimly lit salle seemed to echo the quiet between them, thick with the scent of floor wax, leather, and the sharp, lingering heat of their match.

"Slow," Corvo repeated, the word rolling off his tongue like an insult he wanted to taste. He leaned back against the workbench, crossing his arms over his chest. "I recall you being rather grateful for my pacing about twenty minutes ago. Or did that blow to the mask jar your memory?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean against the bench next to him, close enough to nudge his shoulder with mine. "That 'blow' was a lucky hit and you know it."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo didn't budge when Reyes's shoulder met his. Instead, he let his weight shift just enough to press back, a subtle, deliberate counter-pressure that kept them locked together. 

He let out a short, scoffing laugh, tossing the newly wrapped foil onto the bench beside him. It clattered against the wood, the ring of the steel dying out quickly in the quiet room. 

"Lucky," Corvo murmured, turning his head to look at Reyes from a distance of mere inches. Up close, he could still see the faint flush of exertion on Reyes's skin—and he knew for a fact it wasn't just from the weight of the lamé. "You lunged like an overeager novice, Reyes. If I hadn't stepped into it, you would have ended up face-first in the drywall. I was doing you a charity."

His gaze dropped to Reyes's mouth, his smirk softening into something a little more dangerous, a little more private. He reached out, his fingers lingering on the collar of Reyes's jacket, giving it a slow, teasing tug. 

"But if you want to test your luck again, the mats are still warm."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let his hand go slack as Reyes took his wrist to guide it down, offering no resistance, though his fingers curled in a brief, parting brush against Reyes's palm before they were set aside. 

He didn't back away. If anything, the lack of space between them felt like a line drawn in the dirt, and Corvo had never met a boundary he didn't want to nudge his boot over. 

"Slow," Corvo repeated, his voice dropping an octave, the mocking edge of his tone giving way to something far more deliberate. He tilted his head, his dark eyes locked onto Reyes's, refusing to give an inch. "And yet, here you are. Still standing in my air."

He reached up again, but this time his hand didn't go for the nylon of the jacket. Instead, he let the back of his knuckles slowly trace the sharp line of Reyes's jaw, feeling the heat radiating off his skin, the slight, rough prickle of stubble. It was a lazy, possessive gesture, entirely devoid of the urgency of their bouts, but loaded with the exact same desire to win.

"If I'm so slow, Reyes," Corvo murmured, his thumb catching the corner of Reyes's lower lip, pressing just enough to invite him to bite, "why does it feel like you're the one who can't seem to get away?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I catch his thumb between my teeth, not hard enough to hurt, just enough to stop its path. My voice comes out low, a little rough. "Who said I wanted to get away?"

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The sharp, sudden pressure of Reyes's teeth sent a jolt of heat straight down Corvo's spine. He didn't pull back. Instead, he let his thumb linger against the edge of those teeth, a deliberate surrender of territory that felt entirely like a victory. 

A slow, dark smile tugged at the corner of Corvo's mouth. He loved this—the spitfire in Reyes, the refusal to back down even when the bout was technically over. 

With his free hand, Corvo reached up, his fingers sliding into the hair at the back of Reyes's neck. He gripped just firmly enough to tilt Reyes's head back slightly, asserting his own leverage, and leaned in until their chests brushed. The rough fabric of their training jackets scraped together, a friction that felt far too warm for the chilly, drafty salle.

"Bold," Corvo murmured, his voice a low vibration that he felt as much as heard. 

He didn't pull his thumb free until he felt the damp warmth of Reyes's breath against his skin. When he did, he didn't move it far, letting his thumb slide down to press against the hollow just beneath Reyes's bottom lip, forcing it down just a fraction.

"That's the trouble with you, Reyes," Corvo whispered, his eyes glittering with that familiar, insatiable competitive spark. "No sense of self-preservation. You see a trap, and you just walk right in, expecting to fight your way out." 

He closed the final inch between them, his lips brushing against Reyes's as he spoke, teasing and agonizingly slow. "So tell me. What's the plan now that you're caught?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The heavy, padded canvas of their jackets hit the tiled floor with a succession of dull, wet thuds, quickly followed by the metallic clatter of buckles and the slide of damp cotton. The lazy, calculated patience Corvo had paraded out by the strip was entirely gone, burned up the second Reyes had shoved him back against the narrow wooden bench of the changing room. 

Corvo hissed a breath through his teeth as his back hit the wall, the cool plaster a stark, shocking contrast to the radiating heat of Reyes's body. He didn't complain. Instead, he reached out, his hands catching Reyes by the waist to drag him closer, his fingers digging firmly into the bare skin just above the waistband of Reyes's trousers. 

"Still impatient," Corvo breathed, a breathless, rough laugh catching in his throat as he tilted his head to dodge a particularly bruised kiss, only to press his lips against the hot column of Reyes's throat instead. He bit down, just hard enough to leave a mark, just hard enough to hear that low, gravelly sound Reyes made when he was losing his grip on his temper. 

The locker room was small, smelling of cedar, old sweat, and the sharp, clean scent of the rain starting to hit the high windows. Every sound they made—the slide of skin against skin, the heavy, ragged hitch of their breathing, the creak of the bench beneath their combined weight—seemed magnified tenfold in the tiled space. 

Corvo shifted, hooking one leg around Reyes's hip to pull him flush against him, refusing to allow even a fraction of an inch of space between them. He wanted to feel every heartbeat, every shuddering breath. His hands slid up Reyes's back, his palms hot against the damp skin of his shoulders, mapping the familiar, hard-won muscle of a fellow swordsman. 

"You're going to... ruin my standing," Corvo murmured against Reyes's ear, his voice a low, gravelly rasp as he nipped at the lobe, his fingers tangling in Reyes's hair to keep him right where he wanted him. "If anyone... hears you making a racket like this... they'll think I'm actually letting you win for once."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I drag my teeth along his jaw, a low noise escaping me. "Letting me win? I think you're just trying to keep up."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
A sharp, ragged gasp escaped Corvo's throat as Reyes’s teeth scraped along his jaw, the sudden, hot friction sending a shiver straight down to his thighs. His fingers tightened in Reyes's hair, pulling just enough to force Reyes to tilt his head back, wanting to look him in the eye even as his own breath came in shallow, uneven drags. 

"Keep up?" Corvo mocked, though the effect was somewhat ruined by the thick, breathless quality of his voice. 

He arched off the wooden bench, his hips pressing deliberately, unmissably against Reyes’s, proving exactly how active he was in this match. A low, wicked smirk tugged at his lips, hot and defiant. 

"I’m practically setting the pace, Reyes. You’re just running to stay in the same room."

To prove his point, Corvo shifted his weight, using the leverage of his hooked leg to pull Reyes down even harder against him. The wooden bench groaned under their combined weight, a sharp, loud creak that echoed off the tiled walls. His hand slid down from Reyes’s hair, trailing over the tense, damp curve of his shoulder before his fingers dug hard into the muscle of Reyes's thigh, anchoring them together. 

He leaned up, his mouth brushing against the corner of Reyes’s lips, tasting the salt of their exertion, the heat of their shared breaths. 

"Show me," Corvo challenged, his voice dropping to a gravelly, demanding whisper against Reyes's skin. "Show me how fast you can go before you break."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The hard, narrow cedar of the bench pressed mercilessly into the muscles of Corvo's back, but he barely registered the ache. Every ounce of his focus was pinned to the sudden, heavy weight of Reyes over him, and the devastating, deliberate ruin Reyes was making of his mouth. 

Corvo’s lips parted, a sharp, breathless retort already forming on his tongue—some biting comment about Reyes finally learning the value of a slow approach—but the words were instantly swallowed down. Reyes didn't give him the room to breathe, let alone speak. It was a suffocating, bruising kind of pressure, hot and thoroughly demanding, a masterclass in control that left Corvo’s head spinning against the wooden bench. 

For the first time all evening, the quick-witted fencing master had absolutely no riposte. 

A low, frustrated sound caught in the back of Corvo’s throat, muffled entirely by the slide of Reyes's lips against his. His hands, previously so steady and precise with a blade, scrambled for purchase. His fingers tangled desperately in the damp hair at the back of Reyes’s head, pulling him down harder, trying to force a faster pace, a deeper bite—anything to regain some semblance of leverage. 

But he was entirely at Reyes's mercy, and they both knew it. 

Corvo’s eyes fluttered shut, his chest heaving as he tried to drag air into his lungs through his nose, his hips lifting off the bench in a silent, pleading tilt against Reyes's thigh. The smug, infuriating smirk was completely gone, replaced by a flushed, raw look of pure, unadulterated need. He was shivering, his skin goosepimpled from the drafty air of the locker room, but inside he was burning up. 

When Reyes finally dragged his mouth away, sliding down to press slow, damp kisses along the racing pulse point in Corvo's throat, Corvo could only let his head fall back against the wood. His breath came in ragged, pathetic gasps, his chest rising and falling violently. 

"Damn you," Corvo choked out, his voice nothing more than a wrecked, breathy whisper, his fingers tightening in Reyes’s hair with a weak, desperate tug. "That's... cheating."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I pull back just far enough to meet his gaze, my own breathing heavy. "No rules here, Corvo." My thumb traces his bottom lip, smearing it wet. "Just us."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo stared up at him, his dark eyes wide and glassy with a rare, vulnerable heat. The sight of Reyes looking down at him like this—flushed, breathing hard, and entirely focused on him—sent a thrill straight to his chest that had absolutely nothing to do with the sport they lived for. 

He let out a weak, raspy laugh, his chest rising and falling rapidly. He leaned his head back against the wood, but his gaze didn't waver from Reyes's face. He reached up, his hand sliding from the back of Reyes's neck down to his shoulder, his fingers digging into the hard muscle there, anchoring himself. 

"No rules," Corvo echoed, his voice still ruined, a low, gravelly vibration. He leaned into the pressure of Reyes's wet thumb, his lips parting just enough to brush against the skin of it. "And here I thought you were a stickler for the manual, Reyes."

He shifted his hips beneath Reyes, a slow, deliberate tilt that made the wooden bench creak once more in the quiet room. A faint, breathless trace of his usual smirk returned to his lips, though it was softer now, frayed around the edges by the sheer, overwhelming intensity of what they were doing. 

"If there are no rules..." Corvo murmured, his hand sliding down Reyes's chest, his palm flat against the rapid, heavy beat of Reyes's heart, "...then I don't have to play nice, either."

With a sudden, sharp burst of leverage, Corvo hooked his other leg around Reyes's waist, pulling him down flush against him, refusing to let him keep even that tiny bit of distance. He arched his back off the bench, pressing his mouth directly to the hollow of Reyes's throat, biting down with a fierce, desperate hunger that demanded everything Reyes had left to give.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The sudden, heavy snap of Reyes’s hands locking his wrists down against the cold cedar bench made Corvo’s breath hitch violently. He gave a token, instinctive jerk of his arms—the reflex of a fencer caught in a closed line—but Reyes’s grip was ironclad, pinning him flat, open, and utterly helpless.

A low, ragged gasp ripped from Corvo’s throat, his eyes flaring wide as he stared up at Reyes. The sheer, unyielding weight of him was dizzying. Corvo’s fingers twitched under Reyes’s palms, curling uselessly against the wood, unable to do anything but feel the searing heat of Reyes's skin branding his wrists. 

"Concede?" Corvo choked out, the word barely a whisper, his voice utterly wrecked. He tried to muster that sharp, mocking glint in his eyes, but his gaze was heavy, glazed with a dark, desperate hunger that betrayed him completely. "In your... dreams, Reyes."

But he wasn't pulling away. Even with his hands trapped, Corvo arched his back off the bench, his hips lifting to meet Reyes's with a heavy, desperate pressure that made him shudder from head to toe. The wooden bench groaned beneath them, a sharp, loud creak that seemed to vibrate straight through Corvo's spine. 

"You want to... set the pace?" Corvo whispered, his chest heaving violently as he blinked up at him, a breathless, defiant smile trembling on his wet lips. "Then do it. Stop talking... and make me."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: A sharp, triumphant laugh escapes me. I lean down, my mouth close to his ear. "Finally learned to ask nicely," I murmur, before biting down on his earlobe.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
A sharp, involuntary shudder racked through Corvo’s entire frame as Reyes’s teeth sank into his earlobe, the sudden, stinging heat of it sending a clean shockwave straight down his spine. A choked-off sound—halfway between a gasp and a raw, frustrated groan—escaped his throat, echoing sharply in the damp quiet of the locker room. 

He strained instinctively against the iron grip on his wrists, the muscles in his forearms flexing hard under Reyes's palms, but he didn't actually want to break free. The struggle was just another layer of the game, a mutual testing of boundaries, and Corvo was reveling in the absolute, crushing weight of his defeat. 

"Asking nicely?" Corvo managed to gasp out, his head tilting back into the bite, his pulse hammering violently against his collarbone. His voice was a threadbare, ruined thing, utterly stripped of its usual smooth cadence. "You... wish, Reyes."

With his hands securely bound, Corvo used the only leverage he had left. He tightened his legs around Reyes’s hips, his thighs locking around him to drag him down even heavier, demanding the full, unyielding press of Reyes's body against his own. He arched his back off the hard cedar, his hips tilting up to press desperately against Reyes, a silent, trembling demand that completely contradicted his stubborn words. 

He blinked up at Reyes through a haze of heat and adrenaline, his dark eyes glassy, his chest heaving as he tried to catch his breath. A weak, breathless laugh hitched in his throat, his wet lips parting as he stared at the man who had finally managed to silence him. 

"Shut up," Corvo whispered, a desperate, shivering command. "Shut up and... finish it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The last of Corvo’s pride dissolved into the damp, cedar-scented air of the locker room the moment Reyes took him at his word. 

When Reyes shifted, freeing one of Corvo's wrists only to slide his hand down between their slick, overheated bodies, Corvo let out a broken, high-pitched gasp. He clawed at the bench, his fingers finding the edge of the wood and gripping it so hard his knuckles turned white. His other hand, still pinned or perhaps just forgotten in the sudden, blinding rush of heat, flailed against the bench before latching onto Reyes's shoulder, his short nails digging deep into the damp muscle.

There was no elegance to it now, no careful posture or measured distance. When Reyes guided himself against him and pushed forward, Corvo's hips bucked instinctively, a sharp, ragged cry tearing from his throat. The initial, tight stretch of it made his eyes water, his head thrashing back against the hard wood of the bench, but the discomfort was instantly swallowed by a deep, throbbing ache of pure, unadulterated pleasure. 

"Ah—*fuck*, Reyes," Corvo choked out, his voice cracking. He threw his head back, his neck arching so hard the tendons stood out in sharp relief. 

Reyes didn't ease into it, and Corvo wouldn't have let him if he tried. Every thrust was a direct hit, a hard, heavy drive that rattled through Corvo’s entire frame and sent the wooden bench scraping loudly against the tiled floor. Corvo’s legs locked around Reyes’s waist, his heels digging into the backs of Reyes’s thighs, desperately trying to anchor himself against the relentless, bruising rhythm. He wanted every inch of it. He wanted to be crushed under the weight of the man who had spent four years trying to best him, only to find the ultimate victory was in this complete, devastating surrender.

The locker room was deafening now. The rhythmic, wet slap of their skin, the violent creaking of the bench, and the raw, unhinged sounds Corvo was making—gasping, cursing, groaning every time Reyes hit that deep, blinding sweet spot—echoed off the tiled walls. Corvo didn't care. He didn't care if the director of the salle walked in; he didn't care if the whole damn city heard him. 

"Don't," Corvo gasped, his eyes flying open, glassy and wild as he stared up at Reyes's flushed, sweat-slicked face. He reached up, his hand trembling as he cupped the back of Reyes's neck, pulling him down to force their mouths together again. "Don't stop. Faster—Reyes, *please*."

The word was a confession, a total capitulation, and it tasted like sweet, hot ruin on his tongue. He met Reyes’s desperate, hard lunges with his own frantic, upward tilts of his hips, his body slick with their combined sweat, completely lost in the friction and the overwhelming, blinding heat of the match.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I drive into him, hard and deep, the bench slamming into the wall with every thrust. My hand finds his jaw, holding his gaze. "Say it again."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The sharp, heavy *thud* of the bench slamming against the tiled wall vibrated straight up Corvo’s spine, rattling his teeth, but he barely felt the bruise of it. All of his sensory world had shrunk to the iron grip of Reyes’s hand on his jaw, holding his head still, forcing him to look directly into the dark, blown-out heat of Reyes’s eyes. 

Corvo’s chest heaved, a slick sheen of sweat gluing his hair to his forehead. He swallowed hard, his throat working against the pressure of Reyes’s thumb, his hips bucking up helplessly to meet each deep, punishing drive. The friction was dizzying, a thick, searing heat building so fast in his lower belly that it made his toes curl. 

"You..." Corvo choked out, his voice cracking under the strain. He tried to glare, tried to summon even a flicker of his usual mocking defiance, but another hard, unyielding thrust hit the sensitive curve of his depth and shattered the attempt into a wet, breathless gasp. His hips jerked upward, desperate and entirely out of sequence. 

He was completely undone. Pinned, used, and utterly at the mercy of the man he usually spent his days trying to outmaneuver. 

"Please," Corvo rasped, the word tearing from his throat, stripped of all pride. He reached up, his hand shaking as he clamped his fingers over Reyes’s wrist—not to pull him away, but to hold him there, to feel the heavy, racing pulse beneath his palm. "Reyes—*please*. Don't stop. Just... *fuck*, right there."

He let his eyes close for a fraction of a second, his head thrashing against the wood as a wave of intense, blinding pleasure washed over him, but he forced them open again. He wanted to see it. He wanted to see the triumph on Reyes's face, wanted to match him stare for stare even as his body began to tremble on the verge of snapping. 

Corvo’s legs tightened like a vice around Reyes’s waist, pulling him in so tight there wasn't a breath of air between them. Every stroke was a direct, devastating touch, the wet, rhythmic friction building to a fever pitch that had Corvo clawing at the bench, his breath coming in short, high-pitched whimpers he couldn't have stopped if his life depended on it.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My hips stutter, the rhythm breaking for a second as I come undone, and I press my forehead against his, breathing his name into his skin like a curse and a prayer both.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The sudden, erratic stutter of Reyes’s hips was the final, devastating blow to what little control Corvo had left. 

When Reyes pressed his forehead against his, breathing his name—not like a taunt, not like a challenge, but like a confession whispered into the dark—Corvo’s entire body went rigid. A sharp, high gasp caught in his throat, his eyes rolling back as the sheer, overwhelming wave of Reyes’s release triggered his own. 

Corvo arched violently off the cedar bench, his fingers clawing desperately into the damp, hot muscle of Reyes’s back as his own climax hit him. It was a blinding, bone-deep shatter that left him completely breathless, his hips jerking upward in helpless, desperate spasms against Reyes’s weight. A broken, wrecked cry tore from his throat, echoing loudly off the tiled walls of the empty locker room before dying away into a series of ragged, shuddering whimpers.

For a long, suspended moment, the only sound in the room was the harsh, frantic symphony of their breathing. 

Slowly, the tension began to drain from Corvo’s limbs, leaving him heavy and trembling beneath the solid, reassuring weight of Reyes. He didn't try to push him off. Instead, his legs slowly unclasped from Reyes’s waist, sliding down to drape loosely over the edges of the bench, his heels resting on the cold tiled floor. His chest rose and fell in violent, erratic heaves, his skin slick with a mixture of their sweat in the drafty air.

Corvo’s hand, still tangled in the hair at the back of Reyes’s neck, softened. His fingers curled gently against the damp strands, a rare, quiet gesture of comfort that he would surely deny if asked about it tomorrow. He let his head fall back against the wood, staring up at the shadow-draped ceiling, a slow, completely exhausted smile stretching across his wet lips.

"Four-two," Corvo whispered, his voice nothing more than a gravelly, threadbare rasp in the quiet. He turned his head slightly, his lips brushing against Reyes’s temple, breathing in the sharp, salty scent of him. "I’m still... ahead on aggregate, Reyes."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: A weak laugh shakes my chest. "Keep telling yourself that." I shift just enough to take some of my weight off him, but I don't move away. My fingers trace the new mark on his throat. "This one's going to show tomorrow."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's mouth curved, the barest acknowledgment of a hit. He set the foil down with more care than it warranted and finally looked at Reyes, dark eyes sharp with the same focus he brought to every bout.

"Slow," he repeated, as though tasting the word. "You've been waiting four years to say that to me. How does it taste?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean against the fencing strip, crossing my arms. "Like victory," I say, matching his tone. "Though I'll admit you made me work for it."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo rose from the bench, his movements deliberate as he crossed the narrow space between them. The overhead lights caught the silver at his temples, the faint lines around his eyes that deepened when he smiled—which he did now, a slow, private thing that didn't quite reach the usual competitive glint.

"You did," he admitted, and the words came easier than they should have after four years of verbal parrying. He stopped just short of Reyes, close enough that the heat from the evening's exertion still radiated between them. "Best bout we've had. Pity no one was here to see it."

His gaze flicked down, then back up. "Or perhaps not."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath caught—a small, telling hitch that he would have denied if asked. He didn't step back either. Instead, he tilted his head, studying Reyes with the same intensity he'd once used to analyze their footwork, their feints, the tell in their shoulder before a lunge.

"That's the second time you've called me slow tonight." His voice dropped, rougher at the edges. "Careful. I might start to think you're not talking about fencing."

He reached out, not quite touching, his fingers hovering just above Reyes's wrist where the glove had left a red mark. The question hung unspoken in the small space between them.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I catch his hand before he can pull it back, my grip firm. "I'm not talking about fencing."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's fingers curled around Reyes's, the grip of a man who had spent decades learning exactly how much pressure to apply. His pulse beat against their joined palms, too fast, too honest.

"Four years," he murmured, and there it was—the competitive edge softening into something rawer. "You could have said something four years ago."

He lifted his free hand, finally closing the distance, his fingertips brushing the line of Reyes's jaw with the same precision he brought to every touch of the blade. When he spoke again, his voice was barely above a whisper.

"I would have listened."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's back hit the wall of the changing room with a soft thud, Reyes's weight pressing against him, and the sound that escaped his throat was half laugh, half something needier. He'd fantasized about shutting them up for years—on the strip, in the middle of an argument, once during a particularly tedious Federation dinner—and none of those imaginings had included the way their mouth would feel against his neck, hot and insistent and nothing like defeat.

"Impatient," he managed, the word coming out strangled as his hands found the hem of Reyes's shirt. His fingers were shaking—*his* fingers, steady as a heartbeat on a lunge, trembling like a novice's. "You're always so bloody impatient."

He pulled the shirt up, got it halfway off before Reyes had to stop kissing him long enough to finish the job. Corvo took the opening to look at them, properly look, the way he'd never let himself before.

"There," he said, voice rough with wonder. "That's better."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I shove his shirt up too, my knuckles brushing over the scar on his ribs—the one I gave him two seasons back. "And you overthink everything."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's laugh broke against Reyes's mouth as he pulled them back in, one hand splayed across the scar like he was claiming it, the other tangled in their hair. The angle was wrong, desperate, their teeth clicking before they found a better fit.

"Someone had to," he breathed against their lips, the words muffled and half-swallowed. "You never plan past the first feint."

He dragged them down onto the bench, or maybe they dragged him—it didn't matter anymore, not when Reyes was straddling his lap, not when their hands were everywhere at once. The scar on his ribs ached under their touch, a phantom pain from a bout he remembered too well, the one where he'd been too busy watching their form to notice the blade slipping under his guard.

"Four years," he said again, the words pressed into the curve of their shoulder. "You've been under my skin for four years." His teeth grazed the tendon in their neck, a soft, deliberate threat. "Literally, it seems."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's head fell back against the bench, a sound escaping him that he would never, in any other circumstance, have allowed—low and unguarded, his hips lifting without permission. His hands found Reyes's shoulders, then their hair, gripping tight as though they were the only solid thing in a room that had suddenly tilted sideways.

"God," he managed, the word torn from somewhere deep. His eyes were closed, his mouth half-open, every carefully constructed defense stripped away by the deliberate, unhurried pressure of their mouth. "You—"

But the sentence died unfinished. There was nothing to say, no clever riposte, no competitive jab. Just the heat of them, the weight of them, the way they'd finally found a way to shut him up that didn't involve a blade.

His thumb traced the shell of their ear, a tenderness that surprised even him. "I concede," he breathed, and it wasn't about the match at all.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lift my head just enough to meet his gaze, my own breathing ragged. "Concede? You don't know how to concede." My voice is low, amused. I kiss him again, slower this time. "But I'll accept your surrender."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's laugh was a broken thing, half air and half disbelief, swallowed by the kiss. He surged up against them, one arm wrapping around their waist to pull them closer, the other hand still cradling the back of their head with a gentleness that belied the desperation in his hips.

"Surrender," he echoed when they broke apart, the word tasting strange on his tongue. He'd never surrendered to anyone—not a bout, not an opponent, not the slow, creeping loneliness of four years spent circling each other. But here, with Reyes's weight pinning him to the bench and their mouth still wet from him, the word felt less like defeat and more like recognition.

His thumb traced the line of their cheekbone, the same face he'd watched across a hundred strips, cataloguing every microexpression for weakness and finding only the thing he'd refused to name.

"Only to you," he said, and pulled them back down into the dark.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath left him in a sharp exhale as his wrists hit the wood, the familiar ache of restraint sending a jolt straight down his spine. He tested the grip once—just enough to feel the strength in Reyes's hands—then went deliberately, willingly still beneath them.

"There," he said, the word barely a whisper, his eyes dark and fixed on their face. "That's the first honest thing you've done all evening."

His pulse hammered against their fingers, a rapid, betrayed rhythm he couldn't control. He'd asked for this—had been asking for it for years, in every barbed comment and lingering glance, in every bout he'd drawn out longer than necessary just to keep them close. And now Reyes was giving it to him, and it was nothing like the careful, strategic dance he'd imagined.

It was better.

"You're still—" His voice cracked as they shifted against him, and he had to close his eyes for a moment, teeth sinking into his lower lip. "Still the only opponent who ever made me want to lose."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Then lose," I say, and I kiss him hard enough to bruise. I can feel him shaking under me and it's better than any trophy.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo kissed back like he fenced—with everything he had, no quarter given, no ground ceded even in surrender. The bruising pressure of their mouth sent a thrill through him that had nothing to do with the sting and everything to do with the way Reyes didn't hold back, never had, not once in four years of needling and need.

His wrists stayed where they'd put them, an offering he'd never made to anyone else.

When they finally broke apart, both gasping, Corvo looked up at them with something perilously close to devotion. His lips were swollen, his hair a disaster, the faint mark of their teeth already darkening on his lower lip.

"I've been losing to you," he said, quiet and raw, "since the day you walked into my salle and called my footwork sloppy." His hands curled into loose fists beneath their grip, not fighting, just holding on. "I just didn't know how to say it."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's laugh was strangled, caught somewhere between disbelief and pure, aching want. "Wasn't planning to."

He surged up against them, breaking their grip not through force but through the sheer, desperate need to touch them properly. His hands found their hips, their ribs, the dip of their spine—mapping territory he'd only ever studied from a distance. The bench creaked beneath them, too narrow for what they were doing, and Corvo didn't care.

"Here," he managed, pulling back just enough to meet their eyes. His chest heaved, sweat still cooling on his skin from the match, or maybe that was new, fresh heat blooming under their touch. "Let me—"

He didn't finish the sentence. Instead, he shifted their weight, rolling them both until Reyes was beneath him on the narrow bench, their back pressed to the worn wood. He paused there, braced above them, drinking in the sight of them sprawled and breathless and finally, finally his.

"Four years," he said for what felt like the hundredth time, the words pressed into the hollow of their throat. His mouth traced lower, between their ribs, over the faint scar on their hip that he'd always wondered about but never asked. "I've imagined this. More times than I'd admit."

His hands worked the fastenings of their trousers with the same deliberate precision he brought to everything, except now his fingers were trembling again and the angle was wrong and Reyes was arching up into him like they couldn't bear to wait another second.

"Impatient," he murmured against their stomach, a fond, wrecked echo of his earlier complaint. Then he stopped talking, because his mouth had found better things to do, and the sounds Reyes made above him were worth every one of the fourteen hundred days he'd spent wanting this.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: My fingers tangle in his hair as I arch off the bench. "Took you long enough to do more than imagine."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's laugh vibrated against Reyes's skin, a low, breathless sound that he couldn't have contained if he'd tried. He paused just long enough to look up at them, his lips still brushing the jut of their hip, his eyes dark and glittering with something that might have been triumph if it weren't so tender.

"You're still talking," he observed, the corner of his mouth curving into the same infuriating half-smile he wore when he'd spotted an opening in their guard. "I must be doing something wrong."

He didn't give them a chance to respond. His mouth resumed its slow, deliberate path, and he set about proving—with the same thorough, methodical attention he'd once devoted to dismantling their lunge—exactly how long he'd been paying attention. Every hitch in their breathing, every involuntary twitch of their hips, every broken syllable that escaped their throat was data he'd been collecting for years, filed away in some locked corner of his mind that he'd finally, mercifully, stopped pretending didn't exist.

When he finally surfaced, his breath coming as ragged as theirs, he crawled back up the length of their body and claimed their mouth in a kiss that tasted of salt and surrender and four years of wanting.

"Better?" he asked, the word pressed against the corner of their lips, and he was still shaking.

Reyes:
Instead of answering, I reach up for him—pull him down to me properly, mouth meeting his, hands sliding over the hard muscle of his back. "Better," I agree, when I finally let him breathe. The word is softer than I meant it to be.

Corvo:
The softness undid him. Corvo had weathered years of Reyes's barbs, their competitive fire, the sharp edge of their wit honed specifically to cut him down to size. But this—the gentle weight of the word, the way their hands mapped his back like they'd been waiting just as long as he had—this was new territory, and he had no defenses against it.

"Good," he managed, and the word came out rough, almost shy. He lowered his forehead to theirs, closing his eyes for a moment, letting the reality of it settle into his bones. The salle creaked around them, empty and dark except for the single strip of light spilling from the changing room. Their kit lay scattered on the floor where they'd dropped it, foils still leaning against the bench, everything exactly where it had been an hour ago except for this one, monumental shift.

He pulled back just enough to look at them—really look, the way he'd forbidden himself from doing for years. His thumb traced the line of their jaw, the same face he'd watched across a hundred strips, searching for tells and finding only the thing he'd refused to name.

"Stay," he said, and it wasn't a question. "The salle doesn't open until nine tomorrow. No one will come looking."

His thumb stilled against their cheek. "And I'm not finished with you yet."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I catch his wrist, my thumb pressing against his racing pulse. "Nine hours?" A slow smirk spreads across my face. "Think you can keep up, old man?"

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's eyes narrowed, the competitive spark flaring back to life even as his lips curved into something dangerously close to a grin.

"Old man," he repeated, and the words were a low, silken threat. His free hand found their hip, grip firm and possessive. "You've been calling me that since my thirty-fifth birthday, and it's never once slowed me down."

He dipped his head, mouth brushing the shell of their ear, breath hot and deliberate. "But by all means—keep underestimating me. I do so enjoy proving you wrong."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I shift, rolling us until I'm on top again, pinning him with my weight. "Prove it then," I say, my voice low. "Let's see if you can last nine minutes, first."
