dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s fingers tightened around the linen, the knot on the grip suddenly more interesting than it had any right to be. He let out a breath, that familiar grin—the one that always preceded trouble—sliding into place as he finally glanced over his shoulder.

“Slow, you say?” He turned, leaning one hip against the battered bench. “Bold, considering you spent the last bout backpedaling like the floor was on fire.” His eyes flicked to Reyes’s bag, then up, assessing as always. “Should I chalk it up to nerves, or were you just hoping I’d tire myself out before you got serious?”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean against the bench next to him, close enough to be challenging. "I was waiting for you to run out of witty commentary. Figured it would tire you out faster than the footwork."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo laughed, low and genuine—one of those rare sounds that slipped out when he wasn’t thinking too hard about winning. He tossed the half-wrapped grip aside, letting the linen unravel, no longer bothering with the pretense of busy hands.

“Well, that’s your first mistake, Reyes,” he said, angling his body to face them fully, the line between challenge and something rougher blurring at the edges. “I’ve been running my mouth since I picked up a foil. If you’re waiting for me to wear out, you’ll be waiting a long time.”

His gaze dropped for half a second, tracking the distance—close, now, closer than it ever was in the heat of a match. “But if you’re looking to tire me out another way—” He let the implication hang there, a smirk ghosting across his lips, and nudged Reyes’s knee with his own, just enough to make the challenge clear. “You’re going to have to work for it.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s hands stilled, empty now, and he let Reyes take the space he’d always guarded with words and ironclad distance. The discarded grip thudded dully on the bench, unremarkable, utterly ignored. For once, Corvo didn’t need to fill the silence with retorts or jabs; the nearness spoke for itself, something taut and electric threading between them.

He studied Reyes, eyes narrowed just a little, searching for any hint of retreat—finding none. That sent a thrill through him, sharper than any touch or point scored. “Maybe I just needed the right motivation,” he replied, voice softer, roughened at the edges. His hand found Reyes’s wrist, fingers curling around it as if to anchor himself in this sudden, precarious shift between rivalry and something else entirely.

He leaned in, just enough that their breath mingled, not quite closing the gap. “Careful,” Corvo murmured, his grin crooked, all challenge, all invitation. “If you keep pushing, you might find out what happens when I stop holding back.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I don't pull my wrist away. "Holding back?" I repeat, my voice low. "You've been trying to impress me all night."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s thumb brushed slow circles against the inside of Reyes’s wrist, a touch as deliberate as any parry. He liked the way those words sounded—an accusation, a dare, a confession half-buried in the rasp of Reyes’s voice.

He tilted his head, close enough now that the world outside the salle felt very far away. “Trying?” he echoed, a faint scoff threading through the word. “You think that was my best?” His grin sharpened, all teeth, all mischief. “I only show off for people who might actually keep up.”

He let the silence stretch, the tension between them spinning out, delicious and dangerous. His other hand rose, slow enough to be stopped, fingers brushing the line of Reyes’s jaw—testing, not asking. “Tell me,” Corvo said, voice low, intent, “did I manage it?” And in that moment, he wasn’t fencing anymore, but the risk felt the same: exhilarating, knife-edged, worth every second.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo hit the bench first, spine pressed to the old, splintery wood, Reyes’s weight pinning him there. For once, he didn’t care about the ache in his shoulders or the way the room echoed with half-stifled laughter and the sharp catch of breath. The clatter of kit on tile, the metallic tang of sweat and adrenaline—these belonged to both of them now, the last remnants of rivalry crumbling under the urgency of touch.

His hands were everywhere, greedy and unrepentant—callused palms skating along Reyes’s hips, tracing the line of their ribs, memorizing the heat and tension beneath skin. He yanked Reyes closer, the move rough, unpracticed, all impatience. “So,” he muttered, mouth brushing the shell of Reyes’s ear, his voice gone ragged, “do I finally have your full attention, or are you still keeping score?”

His teeth found the edge of Reyes’s jaw, biting down just enough to sting—a mark, a warning, a promise. Corvo had always loved a close match, but this—this was better than any bout. Here, pressed between cold tile and a rival who’d finally stopped running, he had no intention of letting up. Not until Reyes begged for a rematch.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I laugh, low and breathless against his mouth. "Who said I was keeping score?" I catch his hands, pin them to the bench above his head. "Now you have mine."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s wrists pinned overhead, he arched into the restraint with a kind of feral delight, his grin flashing wicked and unrepentant. There was no point fighting it—not when Reyes’s grip was sure and the shift in their balance sent a jolt of want straight through him. He tested the hold anyway, twisting just enough to prove he could, to remind them both that submission was a choice, and right now, he was choosing it.

“Well,” he managed, voice rough with laughter and something sharper, “about time.” His breath fanned hot against Reyes’s cheek, close enough that every word vibrated through both of them. “I was starting to think you’d never get around to it.”

He craned his neck, mouth brushing the corner of Reyes’s lips—a taunt, a challenge, just out of reach. “So what’ll it be, then?” Corvo’s eyes glittered, daring. “You going to show me what I’ve been missing, or are you just planning to admire the view?” His pulse hammered under Reyes’s palm, wild and unguarded; he’d never surrendered anything on the strip, but here, he gave in gladly—if only to see how far Reyes might go before either of them called halt.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s laugh guttered out, choked off by the press of Reyes’s mouth against skin—throat, collarbone, the hollow where breath snagged and stuttered. For a heartbeat, he stilled, all sharp edges dissolving under the slow, relentless attention, the world narrowing to the heat of lips and tongue dragging over old bruises and new nerves alike. His hands twisted in the air, useless, searching for purchase where Reyes’s grip held him fast.

He tried for a retort, something clever, but it scattered to nothing when Reyes’s teeth grazed his chest, and what came out instead was a shuddering curse, half-muffled against the back of his own arm. There was no defense for this—not for the way Reyes took his time, as if every inch of Corvo’s skin needed mapping, claiming, undoing.

He bucked, just a little, hips lifting off the bench, a plea and a warning tangled together. “You always this thorough?” he managed, words fractured by a gasp, his head tipping back, baring his throat without a second thought. “Or is this just for me?” The question was barely a whisper, raw and open, hunger and surrender bleeding through every syllable. If Reyes wanted him undone, they’d succeeded—and Corvo, for once, was in no hurry for the round to end.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I release his wrists, my own hands settling on his hips to hold him there. "Just for you," I say against his skin. "Consider it a victory lap."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s hands dropped the instant Reyes let go, but instead of seizing control, he slid them into Reyes’s hair and held tight, anchoring himself against the onslaught of sensation and the raw, unguarded honesty in Reyes’s words. Victory lap. The phrase twisted something deep in him, sharp and sweet—a reward, a taunt, a promise fulfilled after years of circling, dodging, never quite closing the distance.

He let out a shuddering breath, fingers flexing against Reyes’s scalp, his hips pinned hard enough that struggling was pointless—not that he wanted to. “You always did have a flair for the dramatic,” he rasped, voice thick, roughened by want. “Suppose you earned it.”

But there was no real bite to the words, not now, not with Reyes’s mouth working him open and his body betraying every bit of composure he’d ever claimed to have. He let himself feel everything: the scrape of stubble, the press of strong hands, the surety of being wanted—of being known, at last, without armor or defense.

Corvo dragged Reyes up, just far enough to claim their mouth in a bruising, hungry kiss—messy, grateful, a challenge and an answer all at once. “Don’t stop,” he murmured against their lips, his voice gone ragged with need and something dangerously close to surrender. “I want you to finish what you started.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo gave in to the grip on his wrists without resistance this time, a breathless sound somewhere between a laugh and a moan spilling from his lips as Reyes flattened him to the bench, entirely at their mercy. The sudden, unrelenting control sent a jolt through him—exactly what he’d been daring Reyes to take all along.

He arched under the weight, the old wood creaking beneath him, every muscle tensed and straining for more. Each time he tried to move, Reyes’s hold kept him pinned, and Corvo found he liked the edge of frustration, the helplessness that was anything but defeat. His eyes found Reyes’s—hungry, wild, full of that bright, reckless light he only ever showed on the strip, when the match was close and the outcome uncertain.

His words came in broken pieces now, the bravado stripped raw. “You want me to concede?” he managed, breath catching as Reyes’s mouth found another sensitive spot, as skilled with this kind of pressure as with a blade. “You’ll have to take it from me—earn it.” He twisted his wrists experimentally, grinning when Reyes tightened their grip, pressing him down harder.

Corvo shuddered, surrendering to the rhythm Reyes set, letting himself be undone one deliberate touch at a time. No counters, no defense, just the rush of being claimed and the thrill of knowing he’d finally met his match—here, on the bench, with nothing left between them but skin and sweat and the sharp, bright promise of victory shared.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lean down, my mouth brushing his ear. "I've been earning it for years," I say, and let my teeth scrape his jaw. "You just didn't notice."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s laugh was softer now, pitched low and intimate, the kind that only surfaced when all his usual armor had been stripped away. Reyes’s words landed sharp as any touch, sending a fresh shiver through him. He turned his head to bare more of his throat, letting Reyes’s teeth find the edge of his jaw, exposing himself in a way he never would have risked before—on the strip or off it.

“Maybe I was distracted,” he said, voice frayed at the edges, every word pressed between panting breaths. “Hard to focus with you always pushing me—never quite close enough.” His wrists strained in Reyes’s grip, testing, not to break free but to feel the strength holding him fast, to let the years of back-and-forth rivalry bleed into something honest and vulnerable.

He rolled his hips up, dragging Reyes closer, his mouth brushing the shell of Reyes’s ear in turn. “If this is what I’ve been missing,” Corvo murmured, his voice shaking with laughter and need, “consider me thoroughly convinced.” There was no more pretense, no defense left; he yielded to every touch, every demand, letting Reyes see him—truly see him—for the first time.

“Go on, then,” he whispered, his grin a challenge and a plea, “show me how you finish a match you’ve already won.”

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s world narrowed to the crush of Reyes’s body, the ruthless surety of their hands pinning his wrists, the heat and scrape of their mouth marking a trail down his throat and chest. Each sound he made was ragged, unguarded, echoing off tile and echoing back, proof they were both far beyond caring who might hear them now. He pulled against Reyes’s grip, not to break free, but to feel the restraint, to let the helplessness burn through him—sweet, sharp, exhilarating.

Reyes’s mouth found its way lower, tongue flicking over sweat-slick skin, teeth leaving a constellation of bruises along Corvo’s ribs. He writhed under the attention, a low, rough moan torn from his lips as Reyes’s hands spread him open, holding him exactly where they wanted. The years of rivalry, of keeping distance, crumbled with every shuddering exhale. Here, Corvo was utterly exposed: hips pinned, wrists trapped, mouth open and hungry, desperate to meet every movement, every demand.

When Reyes closed a hand around him, Corvo’s breath hitched, his hips jerking helplessly up into the touch. Reyes set the pace, merciless and precise, never giving Corvo quite enough, never letting him dictate the rhythm. He groaned, bucking, his words dissolving into curses and pleas—“Fuck, yes, just like that—don’t you dare stop—” His body trembled with the effort to hold back, to draw it out, but Reyes’s mouth and hands were relentless, coaxing him closer and closer to the edge.

He looked up, meeting Reyes’s gaze, his eyes wild and unguarded, his mouth slack with pleasure. “Come here,” he rasped, dragging Reyes down for a kiss, teeth clashing, mouths wet and desperate, his legs wrapping around their hips to keep them close, to drag them flush against him. He ground up, greedy and shameless, lost in the grind and slide of skin on skin, in the heat building between them.

Reyes didn’t let up, their hand working him with infuriating control, their mouth finding every sensitive spot, their body heavy and inescapable. Corvo broke first, pleasure wracking him, his whole body tensed and shuddering as he cried out—louder than he meant to, louder than he’d ever allow on the strip. He spilled across Reyes’s hand and his own belly, breath coming in sharp, ragged bursts. Still pinned, still trembling, he bit back a laugh, pulling Reyes down for another kiss, messy and grateful.

“Your point,” he managed, voice barely more than a wrecked whisper, his hands finally slipping free to tangle in Reyes’s hair and pull them close, unwilling to let the moment end just yet. “But don’t think I won’t demand a rematch.” He nipped at Reyes’s lower lip, triumphant in defeat, wanting nothing more than to lose to them again.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I lick my palm clean, slow, watching him the whole time. "You can demand all you want," I say, voice rough. "I'll still win."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo’s gaze tracked Reyes’s tongue, a flush blooming high on his cheeks that had nothing to do with exertion and everything to do with the way Reyes watched him—hungry, unrepentant, victorious. He let his head fall back against the bench, chest heaving, a laugh spilling loose and ragged from his throat. “Cocky,” he said, his voice hoarse with aftershocks and something deeper, rougher than rivalry.

He reached for Reyes, hauling them down until their bodies pressed flush, one hand fisted in the back of Reyes’s shirt, the other skating up the hard line of their jaw. He kissed them—slow this time, savoring, tasting himself on Reyes’s lips, claiming a share of that victory as his own. When he finally let up, he stayed close, breath mingling, foreheads touching.

“You’re not wrong,” Corvo admitted, thumb stroking the angle of Reyes’s cheekbone. “But don’t think that means I won’t give you hell for it.” He slid a leg over Reyes’s hip, rolling his body with lazy intent, pinning Reyes in turn, though the threat was all in his eyes, not his grip.

His mouth found the line of Reyes’s throat, biting a mark in a place no collar would quite hide. “Next round’s mine,” he murmured, lips brushing skin, voice full of promise and warning both. “And I don’t plan on letting you off the bench until I’ve evened the score.” 

He grinned, teeth bright against the bruise, and settled atop Reyes, content—for now—to savor his loss, already plotting his return to the fray.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I wrap an arm around his waist, holding him there against me. "Next round's not for hours yet," I say, my voice still low. "Stop planning and catch your breath."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo huffed out a laugh, the sound all gravel and satisfaction, and let himself be gathered in, sprawling heavy and boneless across Reyes’s chest. The world outside the changing room felt impossibly distant—there was only the heat of skin, the solid press of Reyes’s arm anchoring him, and the faint, metallic scent of sweat and victory hanging in the air.

He nuzzled closer, mouth brushing the hollow of Reyes’s throat, letting himself be held, just for a moment. “You always did know how to shut me up,” he drawled, though the usual edge was gone, replaced by something softer—content, almost tender. His fingers traced idle patterns along Reyes’s ribs, exploring the curve of muscle, the rhythm of their breathing, as if still learning the terrain of this long-overdue truce.

“No more planning,” he promised, voice dropping low, intimate, reserved for this hush between matches. “Just enjoying the win. Or the loss.” He smirked, biting lightly at Reyes’s collarbone, savoring the taste and the ease between them. “Call it what you like—it’s the best bout I’ve had in years.”

He let his weight settle, eyes half-lidded, a lazy grin playing on his lips. “I’m not going anywhere,” Corvo murmured, the words a promise and a challenge both. “So you’d better hope you’re ready for overtime, Reyes. I don’t intend to stay quiet for long.”

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I press my mouth to his temple, a real kiss, not just a taunt. "I've been ready for overtime since the first time you tried to trip me in the salle."
