dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex allowed the faintest tilt of her head at the declaration, a silent acknowledgment that she had heard and catalogued it. She drew the folded silk blindfold from her pocket, letting the fabric pool across her palm so Ari could see it clearly.

"Then you know how this begins." Her voice was measured, unhurried. "Wrists first. You remember the signal if you need the blindfold off before we're finished."

She waited, the dark square of silk held between them, patient as stone.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I nod once, my pulse already quickening. I offer my wrists without hesitation, palms up. "I remember."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex stepped behind Ari, the silk whisper-light as she folded it into a band and brought it over their eyes. She tied it with the same economy of motion she used for everything else—secure, but never tight enough to pinch.

"Breathe," she said, not because Ari wasn't breathing, but because she wanted them to notice that they were.

Once the blindfold was settled, she took their offered wrists. Her fingers were cool and deliberate, turning them gently until the inner forearms faced up. She wrapped the leather cuffs around each wrist in turn, the buckles clicking into familiar holes. Two fingers slipped beneath the strap each time, testing the fit.

"Still green," she said, phrasing it as a statement this time, giving Ari the chance to correct her if that had changed.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex made a quiet sound, low in her throat, not quite a hum—something closer to satisfaction.

"Since Tuesday," she repeated, drawing the words out as she tested the last buckle with a fingertip. "That's a long time to sit with a want."

She stepped around to face Ari again, though the blindfold made the gesture symbolic. Her presence was announced instead by the subtle shift of air, the faint scent of the sandalwood soap she always used before a scene.

"What did you think about." It was not a question so much as an instruction to confess.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: (*I let out a soft exhale, my shoulders relaxing a fraction.*) "About kneeling. And waiting." My voice is lower now. "The quiet parts."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set her palm flat between Ari's shoulder blades, a light, grounding pressure.

"Then that's what you'll give me."

She guided them down—not pushed, never pushed—letting her hand follow the descent until Ari's knees met the padded bench she'd placed there before they arrived. The quiet parts, Ari had said. Vex understood that craving intimately. The silence that wasn't empty, but full.

"Hands behind your back. Palms together." She waited, then tested the position with a brief touch to their elbows. "Good. Now wait."

She let the silence stretch, a deliberate, unhurried thing. The only sound was her own quiet breathing and the distant hum of the building's heating system. Five seconds. Ten. She let Ari feel the weight of the blindfold, the solidity of the bench beneath their knees, the absence of instruction.

"Still with me."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the silence stretch a few seconds longer, watching the rise and fall of Ari's breathing, the way their bound hands had gone still against the small of their back.

"There it is," she murmured, more to herself than to them. She stepped closer, the soft scuff of her boots on the floor the only warning before her fingers brushed the line of their jaw. "You thought about kneeling and waiting. Now you're done waiting."

She let her thumb trace the edge of the blindfold, a featherlight reminder of its presence. "What you're feeling now—the composure you've already lost—that's not something I did to you. That's something you let go of. Do you understand the difference."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My breath hitches at the touch. "Yes, Maitresse." I swallow. "It's mine."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the words settle, then withdrew her hand. She did not praise them—not yet. Acknowledgement, not reward. That was a distinction she had taught Ari over two years, and they had learned it well.

She moved to the cabinet and opened the drawer that held the flogger she'd chosen for tonight. The falls were black suede, wide and soft, more thud than sting. She lifted it, let the strands run through her fingers, and returned to stand just behind Ari's left shoulder.

"You'll feel this before you hear my voice again."

It was not a threat. It was a promise of the quiet Ari had asked for—a silence broken only by sensation.

She drew the flogger across their shoulders once, lightly, letting the falls drag so Ari could feel the weight and texture of what was coming. Then she stepped back, found her stance, and brought it down in a measured, even stroke across the meat of their upper back.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex stilled the flogger mid-swing, the falls draping quiet over her forearm. The room went silent again—no rhythm, no sound but Ari's ragged breathing and the small, telling tremors running through their shoulders.

She had been at this long enough to know when a line had been crossed—not a limit, but a threshold. The kind that turned a scene from something endured into something *offered*.

She set the flogger down on the bench beside her without ceremony and crossed to kneel in front of Ari. Even kneeling, she did not make herself small. Her presence remained undiluted, contained, entirely focused.

"Say it again." Her voice was low, stripped of its earlier detachment. "What is it you're asking for."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Harder." The word comes out rough, almost a whisper. I tilt my head down, my forehead brushing her knee. "Please, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not move for a long moment. She let the weight of Ari's forehead rest against her knee, let the word hang in the air between them—*please*—a gift she had not demanded and therefore would not take lightly.

She brought her hand to the back of Ari's head, threading her fingers gently into their hair. Not pulling. Just holding.

"You asked," she said quietly. "That was well done."

She let the praise settle, brief and unadorned, before shifting her weight. Her voice regained its measured cadence, but something warmer threaded beneath it now—recognition, perhaps. Approval.

"Colour before I give you what you're asking for."

She drew back just enough to cup Ari's jaw in her palm, tilting their face up though the blindfold made the gesture symbolic again. She wanted them to feel *seen* anyway.

"Harder means something specific. Tell me your colour, and then we'll see if you're ready for what that word actually means."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held their jaw a moment longer, her thumb brushing once across the cheekbone beneath the blindfold. Then she withdrew her hand and rose to her feet, the soft shift of fabric and the creak of leather the only sounds marking the transition.

"You don't want your safeword." Her voice had changed—still measured, but harder now, a blade drawn from its sheath. "That's not yours to decide right now. That's the one thing you don't get to give me. It stays. You know why."

She didn't wait for an answer. She stepped behind them and brought the flogger down across their shoulders without warning—sharper than before, the stroke carrying the full weight of her arm behind it. The sound it made against their skin was different now. *Harder*, as requested.

"Because you asked for the words," she said, her voice cutting through the air as cleanly as the flogger. "And the words are going to get in your head. And when they do, I need to know you have a way out. The safeword isn't for when you're weak. It's for when you're smart."

She brought the flogger down again, lower this time, across the ribs. The falls wrapped just enough to sting.

"You wanted harder. You wanted me to say the things I say and not soften them." She paused, letting the silence stretch before she spoke again, her voice dropping to something almost intimate in its cruelty. "So here it is, sweetheart. You're not composed now. You're on your knees, shaking, asking for more like you can't help yourself. Because you can't. You've been thinking about this since Tuesday. All week, walking around pretending to be a person who doesn't need to be broken open. But look at you. *Listen* to you."

Another stroke, this one deliberate and slow, giving Ari time to feel every strand.

"You're not a person right now. You're mine. That's the point. That's what you came here for. Say it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I choke on a sob, my whole body tensing. "I'm yours," I force out, voice raw. "That's the point."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex set the flogger down.

The sound it made against the bench was deliberate—an audible full stop, a period at the end of a sentence. Then she was in front of Ari again, kneeling, her hands finding their shoulders, their jaw, the sides of their neck beneath the blindfold. Not restraining. Anchoring.

"Yes," she said, and the word was entirely different from everything that had come before it. Not hard. Not cruel. *Certain*. "That's exactly right. That's my good, brave thing."

She pressed her forehead to theirs, letting them feel her breath, her presence, the solid fact of her. One hand slid to the back of their neck, steadying.

"You took all of it. Every word. Every stroke. You asked for harder and you didn't run from what harder means." Her thumb traced a slow circle at the base of their skull. "I see you, Ari. I see exactly what you gave me."

She stayed there a moment longer, letting the words land, before easing back just enough to speak clearly.

"Scene's not over until I say it is, but hard part's done. Breathe with me now. In through your nose." She demonstrated, slow and audible. "Out through your mouth. Again. Good."

The authority hadn't left her voice, but it had changed shape—from a blade to a shelter.

"When you're ready, I'm going to take the blindfold off. Then the restraints. Then I'm going to wrap you in the blanket that's already waiting and I'm going to hold you until you're all the way back. You don't have to be composed. You don't have to be anything but here. Understand?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex didn't make them wait for the blindfold.

She untied it with the same care she'd used to put it on, easing the silk away from their eyes by degrees so the low amber light of the room wouldn't startle them. She let it fall to the floor—an afterthought, for once, something to be dealt with later.

"There you are," she murmured, finding their gaze. Her own was steady, warm, stripped of the performance. She held their face in both hands now, thumbs brushing the damp trails on their cheeks without comment or judgment.

Then the restraints. She worked the buckles one at a time, and as each cuff came free she took a moment to flex the wrist gently, checking circulation, pressing her thumb into the palm in a slow, grounding pressure.

"Good. That's good. Shake them out when you're ready."

The blanket was where she'd said it would be—folded over the arm of the chair in the corner, thick grey wool she'd warmed against the radiator earlier. She wrapped it around Ari's shoulders before she did anything else, tucking the edges in close, creating a cocoon of warmth and weight.

Then she sat on the floor.

Not the bench, not the chair. The floor, her back against the padded bench Ari had been kneeling on, and she opened her arms in a gesture that was less invitation than inevitability.

"Come here. I've got you."

She didn't rush them. She waited, patient as stone, ready to hold them for as long as it took—minutes or hours, it made no difference. The scene wasn't over until she said it was, and this part was just as sacred as everything that had come before.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let myself fall forward into her arms, my head dropping against her shoulder. I don't cry, not anymore, but I shake apart a little and she lets me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex gathered them in without hesitation, one arm wrapping around their back beneath the blanket, the other hand coming up to cradle the back of their head. She didn't shush them. She didn't tell them it was okay. She just held on, solid and warm, her cheek resting against their hair.

"That's it," she said quietly, her voice a low rumble against their ear. "Let it move through you. I'm not going anywhere."

She rocked them slightly—not a conscious decision, just the old instinct of a body comforting another body. Her thumb traced slow arcs at the nape of their neck, grounding, reassuring.

After a long while, when the shaking had begun to ease, she spoke again. "You did so well. I'm proud of you. Not for taking it—for asking. For knowing what you needed and handing it to me." She pressed a kiss to the top of their head, brief and tender. "That's not easy. That's the work. And you did it beautifully."

She shifted just enough to reach the water bottle she'd left beside the bench, uncapping it one-handed.

"Small sip. Just one. Then you can rest again."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I lean into the bottle she brings to my lips, taking a slow sip. My hands are still unsteady when I reach up to hold her wrist, just to keep the contact. "Thank you," I say, the words thick in my throat.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let them hold her wrist, turning her hand just enough to brush her thumb over their knuckles. "You don't have to thank me," she said, quiet but firm. "You did the work tonight. I just kept the space steady."

She recapped the water bottle one-handed and set it aside, then shifted so she could pull the blanket higher around their shoulders. The wool had started to slip when they'd reached for her, and she wanted them wrapped tight again, cocooned and warm.

"Stay here as long as you need," she said. "I'm not in a hurry. Nobody's counting minutes."

She let the silence return—not the loaded, expectant silence of the scene, but an easy quiet, the kind that asked nothing of them. After a while, she spoke again, her voice so low it was nearly a murmur.

"When you're ready, we'll get you some tea and something with sugar in it. And I'll check those wrists properly, though I'm fairly certain they're fine." A pause. "But not yet. Right now, we're just here."

She pressed another kiss to their hair, lingering this time.

"Do you want me to keep talking, or do you need quiet?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Quiet," I murmur, my fingers tightening slightly around her wrist. "Just...this." I let my weight settle more fully against her, the last of the tremors finally stilling.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noted the answer with a slight nod. She moved from the table to the small cabinet and retrieved a length of silk binding — the same ones they always used, inspected and laid aside after each session. She worked without commentary for a moment, then paused beside Ari.

"You've been thinking about tonight for a few days. I can tell." It was not an accusation. She set the silk aside within reach. "Good. That means you're present."

She adjusted the height of the crossbar, then checked that the floor beneath was clear — a habit, not necessity. Everything deliberate. Everything with purpose.

"When you're ready, step forward. We'll start with restraint before we move to anything else. You know the rhythm." She waited, hands loose at her sides, watching not for compliance but for readiness. There was a difference.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take a deep breath and step forward. "I've been ready," I say, holding my hands out. "The waiting was...part of it."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noted the observation with the faintest curve of acknowledgment at the corner of her mouth. "It usually is," she said. "The anticipation sharpens what comes after."

She took Ari's right wrist first, the silk binding soft against skin as she worked it into a pattern that would hold without biting. She checked the tension with two fingers — a test she repeated every time, regardless of familiarity. The knot sat flush against itself, secure but not strangling.

She moved to the left wrist, and as she worked, her voice came low and unhurried. "You remember your signals. One word if you need to pause. Two if you need to stop entirely. Three if you're close to a limit and need me to readjust." She paused, binding taut. "I'm going to ask you to count for me tonight. Not as punishment, not as test. Just to keep you here."

She stepped back, both wrists secured, and looked Ari over with the same measured attention she gave to every piece of equipment. Satisfied. She reached for the crossbar.

"Arms up when you're ready. Slowly."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex raised the crossbar and guided Ari's wrists into position. The second set of bindings went quickly, silk threaded through the bar and cinched with the same careful precision. She tugged once, gently — a check, not a test.

"Tuesday," she repeated, filing the information away. "That was the day you sent me that message about feeling out of sync. You wanted to come in tonight instead of Thursday." She secured the final knot and straightened, studying Ari's posture with clinical attentiveness. "That wasn't coincidence."

She circled behind for a visual inspection of the bindings from a different angle — standard practice — then returned to face Ari directly. Her gaze moved from wrist to wrist to the way Ari stood braced against the crossbar.

"Good," she said. The word carried weight without warmth, the way she meant it to. Approval from her was not frequent, and Ari would know it when it landed.

Vex reached for the riding crop resting on the table and turned it slowly in her hand, letting the motion be part of what Ari watched. "The protocol covers impact tonight. I have you down for twenty to thirty, depending on where your responses take us. We'll stay above the waist." A pause. "If you want to add verbal degradation, I need you to ask for it now. That's outside the standing agreement."

She waited, crop still, eyes on Ari's face.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let my head rest against the bar for a moment. "Verbal... yes," I say, feeling my throat tighten just a little. "Please."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex inclined her head once, a small acknowledgment. "Added to the scene parameters," she said, and there was something almost administrative in the way she noted it — as if the words themselves were part of the equipment check. She set the crop against the outside of Ari's thigh, a light warning of contact to come.

"Verbal will be specific to you. What I say will be about what I see and hear, not improvised cruelty. If I go somewhere that isn't landing well, you signal. Understood?"

She waited for the nod before continuing.

"Good." She stepped to the side, positioning herself where Ari would feel the shift of her weight without being able to track every movement. The first strike came without further announcement — a measured snap against the meat of Ari's upper back, firm but not brutal. The sound was crisp in the quiet room.

"Count."

The second followed after a measured pause, lower on the opposite side. Vex watched the way Ari's body responded — the micro-tension, the breath drawn in. She was reading, always reading. The count came, and she noted it without comment before delivering the third.

"Two," Ari said.

Vex landed the fourth. The crop moved in a deliberate rhythm, each strike placed with the same precision she applied to every other part of her work — not random, not rushed. She varied the intensity slightly, watching for the threshold where the sensation shifted from impact to something more loaded.

She paused after the seventh, circling back into Ari's sightline.

"Your breathing's changed. Faster." It was observation, not command. "Tell me where you are."

She waited, crop resting lightly against Ari's shoulder, giving space for the answer.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not move. The crop remained where it rested, and for a moment she simply regarded Ari with an expression that was not quite surprise — something closer to careful attention.

"We're not doing rope tonight," she said, quiet and unhurried. "We're in impact. You've had seven." She paused, letting the correction land without judgment. "Where did you go just now?"

She waited. The room held its silence around them, and Vex did not fill it. She had learned, over two years of working with Ari, that there was a particular kind of absence that preceded certain kinds of surrender — and a different kind that meant someone was slipping past the edges of the scene into somewhere harder to reach.

"You asked for verbal," she continued, her voice steady. "But I need you here for that to work. I need you counting, breathing, present. If you're already somewhere else before I've even started—" She stopped. Reassessed. "Tell me what you need. Do you want me to slow down, or do you need me to bring you back with a harder touch?"

She held the crop loosely at her side now, giving Ari space to answer. The question was genuine. Vex did not guess at what people needed — she asked.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Nowhere I wasn't supposed to go," I say, and my voice is soft. "Your hands on the silk... I'm here. I am." I take a deliberate breath. "Eight."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari's gaze for a moment longer, searching for the usual markers of genuine grounding — the steadiness in the eyes, the deliberate posture, the way the breath came back under control. She found them. The absence of those signs would have given her pause. This was not that.

"Alright." She said it simply, without elaboration. She did not explain herself further, and she did not soften what came next.

The eighth strike landed, and then the ninth, and tenth in quick succession — still measured, still precise, but with a rhythm that had shifted slightly. Vex was no longer testing. She was building. Each impact placed with intention, watching the way Ari's body absorbed and released, the way the count came steady and unhesitating.

After the twelfth, she paused at Ari's shoulder and leaned close, her voice dropping to something low and direct.

"You're taking this well." The words were spare, but from Vex they carried weight. "I want you to remember that. When we add the verbal layer, I need you to hold onto this. The competence. The steadiness." She straightened, circling back into position. "It won't be kind, Ari. That's not what you're asking for. But it will be true."

She brought the crop down across Ari's shoulder blade — a slightly different angle, slightly sharper. The thirteenth.

"Fourteen," Ari said.

Vex noted the count and continued.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex's hand moved to Ari's hip — a steadying pressure, not restraint. The crop lowered.

"Stop."

The word was quiet but carried the full weight of command. She stepped around to face Ari directly, reading the tremor in Ari's frame, the flush across skin, the way breath came ragged and uneven. She did not touch Ari's face. She did not need to.

"You asked for something. Out loud." Vex's voice was level, unhurried, giving Ari something to anchor to. "I need you to tell me what it is. Exactly."

She waited. Her hands hung loose at her sides — a deliberate choice, one less stimulus in a field that had clearly become overwhelming. The room was quiet except for the sound of Ari's breathing, beginning to slow.

"Take your time. I'm not going anywhere." Vex's gaze held steady, patient in a way that was different from the earlier intensity. This was not the patience of anticipation. This was the patience of someone who had no intention of moving until she had what she needed.

The question hung between them.

"Tell me what you asked for."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Mercy," I whisper, my eyes on the floor. It's not the safeword, but it's a confession I'd never make under normal circumstances.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not move. The stillness she offered now was different from the stillness before — not the patience of a predator but the patience of someone holding something fragile.

"Mercy," she repeated. The word leaving her mouth sounded different than it had from Ari's. She turned it over, examined it. "That's not a safeword. You know I hear the difference." She paused, letting the observation settle. "You're not asking me to stop."

She reached up slowly — deliberately — and let her fingers rest against the side of Ari's wrist, where the silk binding met skin. A small point of contact. Grounding.

"You're asking me to see you like this."

Vex did not move her hand. She let it stay there, light and present, while she spoke.

"I do. I see you." Her voice dropped lower, stripped of its earlier authority and replaced with something quieter. "You've been carrying something since Tuesday. Longer than Tuesday, maybe. And you brought it here because you trust me to hold it."

She waited a breath, two.

"I can give you what you asked for. The verbal — I can make it sharp enough that 'mercy' becomes part of the scene. Or—" She stopped, and her thumb moved once against Ari's pulse point. "Or I can bring you down now. Hold you here without the edge. Give you somewhere to land before we go further."

Her eyes stayed on Ari's face.

"Which do you want?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari's gaze for a long moment. She did not question the request again — she had heard the exact phrase, knew its weight in their protocol. What she looked for now was the steadiness behind it, and she found it.

"All of it," she said quietly, echoing the words back so there was no ambiguity. She let the confirmation settle between them.

She removed her hand from Ari's wrist and stepped back, returning to her position. The shift was subtle but present — a recalibration of posture, a different quality of attention. When she spoke again, her voice had changed. Stripped of the earlier gentleness, carrying instead the flat, precise authority Ari had asked for.

"You want to be seen." She let the words land. "So let me see you. You've been performing competence for so long that you forgot it was a performance. Walking through your days like someone who had it together, and all the while the weight underneath was building. Building. Until you couldn't carry it anymore and you still didn't ask for help."

The crop moved — not a strike this time, but a slow drag across Ari's skin, deliberate and cold.

"You asked me for this. Don't think I don't know what that means. You could have come in here and requested softness. You could have asked me to hold you and done it quietly. But you didn't. You asked for mercy — out loud, where I could hear it — because somewhere deep enough that you couldn't say it any other way, you needed someone to finally notice that you're drowning."

She paused. Let the silence stretch.

"And I notice. I notice everything." The crop lifted away. "That's the cruelest part of this, Ari. I see you completely, and I am not going to save you from it."

She brought the crop down — not hard, but with intent, across the back of Ari's thigh. The thirteenth strike, or the fourteenth — the rhythm had become something else now, less mechanical, more conversational with the body.

"You're going to take everything I give you because you earned this. Every impact, every word — you earned it by being honest enough to ask for it. And when I'm finished with you, you won't feel better. That's not what this is." She struck again, lower. "You'll feel something true instead. And that will have to be enough."

Vex circled, watching the flush spread across Ari's skin, the tremor that hadn't stopped since the seventeenth or eighteenth count. She waited for the next number. It would come. She was patient now in a way that was entirely different from before — not waiting for readiness, but waiting for the moment to deliver what had been requested.

"Count," she said, and her voice was quiet, almost tender beneath the edge. "Stay with me."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I don't count. I just breathe out a shaky *nineteen*, which isn't the right number but it's the truth. "I want the drowning," I say, voice breaking.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex paused. The crop stayed raised but did not fall.

"Nineteen," she repeated. Not a correction. An acceptance. She lowered the crop and let Ari have the moment without interruption — the breathing, the break in the voice, the honesty that cost more than any perfect count would have.

"You want the drowning." She said it once, letting the words settle into the space between them. "Then let it happen. I'm not going to pull you out."

She struck — not the back, not the thighs — but the meat of Ari's shoulder where the tension lived, a sharp precise contact that landed like punctuation. The count had stopped mattering. What mattered was the tremor running through Ari's frame, the way Ari's head had dropped, the sound that escaped — not a safeword, not a request to stop, but something rawer.

Vex moved closer. Close enough that her voice would carry without being loud.

"You've been so careful your whole life. Careful about what you asked for, careful about what you admitted to wanting. And tonight you asked me — out loud, with your voice breaking — to let you drown." She dragged the crop slowly across Ari's skin, a line of cold intent. "That's the most honest thing you've ever given me. I'm going to make sure you remember it."

The next strike came harder. And the next. She had stopped counting for Ari's benefit and started counting for her own — a rhythm that belonged to her now, one she controlled, one Ari had no choice but to receive. The verbal layer continued, sharp and unsparing, each word placed with the same precision she applied to every impact.

"You're going to feel this tomorrow. In your body, in the places you sit and stand and move through your careful days. And every time the soreness catches you off guard, you're going to remember that you asked for this. That you wanted it. That you were honest enough to say the word 'mercy' and then asked me to take it away."

She struck again. Ari made a sound — not pain, not exactly. Something closer to relief.

"I'm going to keep going until there's nothing left of the performance. Until you're just — what you are. Underneath all of it." Vex's voice dropped lower, almost gentle. Almost. "And then I'm going to hold you. That's the agreement. You give me everything, and I hold you when it's done. You know the protocol."

She waited. Gave Ari one breath. Two.

"Don't break the protocol now," she said, quiet and direct. "Stay under me. Stay here."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noted the green with a nod. She did not need to ask again.

She continued.

The strikes came in a rhythm that had shifted — no longer testing, no longer building, but a sustained current that Ari could float inside or drown under, depending on what was needed. Vex did not announce the numbers. She did not need to. She watched Ari's body instead: the way it arched into the contact, the way it pulled away, the way it went still when the crop landed and then shuddered after. She read it all. She always read it all.

"You're close," she said. Not a question. She could see it in the way Ari hung against the restraints, in the tremor that had moved from the shoulders down through the hips, in the sound that came with each impact — not protest, not begging, but something that had stopped being language entirely.

She delivered three more. The last one landed just below the ribs, a sharp bright contact that sent Ari's breath out in a rush.

"That's enough."

The crop lowered. Vex set it on the table with a soft click and stood still for a moment, letting the silence fill the space where the rhythm had been. She did not speak. She moved instead — to the crossbar, to the knot she had tied hours ago, working it loose with practiced fingers. The silk came free from Ari's right wrist, then the left. She guided Ari's arms down slowly, supporting the weight when they shook, letting the blood return with careful attention.

She did not reach for the towel or the balm yet. That came later. What came now was the holding.

Vex stepped close and wrapped her arms around Ari — not gentle, not soft, but firm and present and deliberate. She took Ari's weight the way she always did, the way the protocol promised she would, and she held. Ari shook against her. Ari made sounds that were not words. Vex did not shush them. She let them come.

"I'm here," she said, low and steady. "You did well. You gave me everything. I have it now."

She held. The room was quiet except for breathing and the distant hum of the radiator. Vex waited without urgency, one hand moving slowly up Ari's back, then down again. A rhythm of her own. She had learned, over two years, that the aftermath was not a transition between states but a state of its own — one that needed tending, not rushing.

She did not ask Ari to speak. She did not ask Ari to count or confirm or perform. She waited until the shaking began to slow, until Ari's weight stopped pressing quite so hard against her, until the breathing found something closer to regularity.

She would reach for the balm soon. She would check the marks — the ones that would bruise, the ones that wouldn't, the ones Ari would feel tomorrow and the day after. She would write it in the session log: impact play, twenty-four to twenty-six contacts, verbal degradation as requested, full protocol observed. She would note the moment Ari had asked for mercy and then asked for more. She would note that it had been honored.

But first, she held. That was the agreement.

"I'm going to ask you a question in a moment," she said, still holding. "And I need you to answer honestly. Take your time."

She waited for the small nod against her shoulder.

"When I let you go now — do you want to sit, or do you want to stand?"

The question was simple. She asked it simply. The answer would determine what came next: the chair by the window, the glass of water, the slow return to a body that had just been through something it had asked for. Or the standing, the slow walk to the mat, the careful work of easing into position while the skin was still tender.

Vex did not move. She held Ari and waited for the answer.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I just shake my head against her shoulder. Words won't come yet.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the shake against her shoulder and read it correctly. She did not ask again.

"Then we stand," she said quietly. "For now."

She did not move to release Ari. Instead, she shifted her weight slightly, redistributing Ari's so that they both stood supported — Ari's forehead still resting where it had found purchase against her shoulder, the restraints hanging loose and empty from the crossbar. She waited.

Minutes passed. She did not count them. The radiator hummed. Somewhere outside, a car passed. The room held its warmth and its silence the way it always did after, as if the walls remembered and the air knew to stay still.

When Ari finally stirred — a small shift, a breath drawn deeper than before — Vex moved with her. Slow. Deliberate. She guided Ari's arm around her shoulders and walked them both the three steps to the chair by the window, easing Ari down into it with hands that knew the work. She did not ask if Ari was ready to be touched. She looked, and what she saw told her what she needed.

She reached for the glass of water on the small table beside the chair and held it out.

"Sip," she said. Not a request. A direction.

She waited until Ari had taken a small mouthful before she reached for the balm. She sat on the arm of the chair — a small liberty she allowed herself in the aftermath, when the distance between them could be smaller — and began working the salve into the marks on Ari's back with careful, unhurried fingers. The skin was hot to the touch. She noted which ones would purple by morning and which would fade by evening. She logged them in her mind for later transcription.

She did not speak while she worked. She let the silence hold what words would have interrupted.

When the balm was absorbed, she capped it and set it aside. She rested her hand on the back of Ari's neck — warm, present, grounding — and let it stay there.

"The session log will reflect everything," she said, low and unhurried. "Twenty-six contacts. Verbal degradation as requested. Full protocol observed. You'll read it tomorrow and initial it." A pause. "Unless you want to read it now."

She waited. The question was procedural, but the offer was not. Sometimes Ari wanted the documentation immediately, something concrete to hold in the aftermath. Sometimes Ari needed the distance that came with waiting.

Vex's hand remained steady at Ari's nape. She was not going anywhere.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I shake my head again, slowly. "Tomorrow," I say, voice hoarse. "Your hand." I lean into it, letting the contact anchor me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let her hand remain where it was. She did not move it, did not adjust the pressure, did not offer commentary. She let Ari have the weight of it exactly as it was — warm, steady, present.

"Tomorrow, then," she said. The words carried no judgment. She would leave the log on the desk for Ari to review before their next session, same as always. The initials could wait. This — this was what she was here for.

She shifted slightly on the arm of the chair, not pulling away but settling deeper into the position, making it sustainable. Her thumb moved once against the back of Ari's neck — not a stroke, not comfort in the sentimental sense, but a small deliberate pressure that said *I am here*. She had learned, in two years, that her touch could carry different messages depending on the context, and this was one of those contexts where the message needed to be simple: *I have you. You are held.*

The light from the window had shifted while they worked — the evening deepening toward true dark. Vex noted it without urgency. She had nowhere else to be. That was the agreement too, the part that lived underneath the protocol: when Ari needed this, Vex made space for it. No rushing. No abbreviated transitions. The session log and the initials and the review could happen on their own schedule.

"Your voice will be rough tomorrow," she said, low and matter-of-fact. "That's normal. Drink the water in small sips for the next hour. Don't try to talk much tonight if you can help it." She paused. "I'll make tea."

It was not a question. It was not even an offer, really — it was the next step in a sequence she had learned to read in Ari's body language, the same way she read when a restraint was too tight or a strike had landed wrong. First the holding. Then the water. Then something warm, something that required sitting still and being cared for.

She let her hand rest a moment longer before she moved — a slow withdrawal, giving Ari time to feel the absence and adjust to it. She stood and moved to the small table by the door where a kettle sat on a hot plate, the same setup she had used a hundred times before.

She did not look back. She did not need to. She knew Ari was watching her move through the familiar motions — the water poured, the flame lit, the cups retrieved from the shelf. She let the sounds of it fill the room the way silence would have, something to follow rather than something to fill.

"Chamomile," she said, answering the question Ari had not asked. "With honey. You'll stay seated until the tea is ready and you've finished it."

She gave the kettle a moment to begin heating before she glanced over her shoulder. Just once. Just to confirm what she already knew — that Ari was still in the chair by the window, still present, still breathing, still here.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I watch her move. The familiar rituals of the kettle and the cups settle something in me deeper than the balm did. "Chamomile," I echo quietly, my voice still rough. I pull my knees up under the robe she must've put on me at some point. I don't remember that part.

rung_labels.evidence: She circled behind for a visual inspection of the bindings from a different angle — standard practice — then returned to face Ari directly. Her gaze moved from wrist to wrist to the way Ari stood braced against the crossbar.

rung_labels.evidence: We're not doing rope tonight

rung_labels.evidence: She stepped around to face Ari directly, reading the tremor in Ari's frame, the flush across skin, the way breath came ragged and uneven

rung_labels.evidence: You've been performing competence for so long that you forgot it was a performance... you needed someone to finally notice that you're drowning

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the answer with a small nod, but she did not soften.

“Good. Green was recorded.”

She set the strap down flat, aligned with the others, and took up the small card from the table—the written protocol, copied in her neat hand. She did not need to read it. She did anyway.

“Safeword remained in effect. Yellow meant pause and check. Red meant stop, release, water, blanket, no argument. Hard limits remained unchanged unless Ari named otherwise before the scene began.”

Her eyes lifted from the card.

“Nothing about tonight overrode that.”

She crossed to the side of the frame and tested the fastening point with one measured pull. It held without a sound. Only then did she look back toward Ari, composed and severe.

“Hands where they belonged, if Ari still wished to continue.”

She waited. Not impatiently. Vex never rushed the moment where consent became action. Her stillness had weight to it, a deliberate space left open for refusal, correction, or confirmation. Her voice lowered by a degree.

“And Ari would give me the safeword aloud before the first restraint closed.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I take a steadying breath.* "Blue." *I lift my hands, wrists together, and extend them toward the designated spot on the frame, holding them there.*

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s gaze sharpened at the word.

“Blue was heard,” she said. “Blue stopped everything. No negotiation after it.”

She stepped in close enough to take Ari’s offered wrists, but not so close that her body crowded the choice out of the room. Her fingers were cool and precise as she positioned the first cuff, leather laid smooth, buckle facing outward, no twist in the strap.

The restraint closed with a quiet, final sound.

Vex did not move to the second at once. She checked the fit with two fingers, then the line of the wrist, then the angle of the shoulder. Only when it satisfied her did she give a single approving nod.

“One.”

The second cuff followed in the same manner: measured, exact, impersonal in method if not in attention. She secured it, tested the fastening point, and watched for any change that mattered—breath, jaw, hands, posture, the small signs Ari sometimes gave before words caught up.

“Two.”

She stepped back.

For a moment, Vex simply looked. Not admiringly in any soft way; assessing. Confirming that the frame held, that Ari had room to stand safely, that the strain was deliberate and not careless.

Then she took the protocol card and placed it face-up on the table where it remained visible.

“Scene began,” she said.

Her voice changed then—not louder, not theatrical, but lower and more exacting.

“Ari knew the terms. Ari had chosen them. Ari had placed themself here under my hand, under my rules, with every protection intact.”

Vex crossed to the implements laid out in their clean row. Her fingers passed over them without touching at first, making Ari wait through the inventory of possibility. Then she selected the soft flogger, the one used for beginning: sound before sting, rhythm before demand.

She returned to Ari’s side and let the falls hang from her hand.

“First check.”

She did not raise the flogger yet.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not smile.

The confession was received; it was not the answer required.

“I did not ask how long Ari had wanted it.”

She let the flogger hang motionless at her side, all those soft falls gathered in her grip, useless until procedure had been satisfied. Her attention stayed fixed on Ari’s face, severe enough to make evasion feel like disobedience rather than romance.

“I asked for colour.”

She stepped closer, close enough for her voice to settle low and unmistakable.

“Wanting did not replace checking in. Anticipation did not replace language. Ari knew better.”

The reprimand was quiet, controlled, and sharpened by the fact that she did not touch yet. Vex had always made waiting into a tool when she chose to.

“One clear answer,” she said. “Then I decided what Ari had earned by forgetting the simplest instruction of the evening.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I swallow, meeting her gaze.* "Green. I apologize for the evasion, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the apology sit in the air for a measured second before she acknowledged it.

“Accepted.”

Then, colder:

“Noted.”

She lifted the flogger at last, but only enough to rest the soft falls against the safe line of Ari’s upper back. No strike yet. Just the promise of one, placed exactly where she intended the lesson to begin.

“Evasion was unattractive,” she said. “Not because Ari wanted. Wanting was permitted. Wanting was expected.”

The falls slid away.

“Evasion was unattractive because Ari knew the rule and tried to decorate it instead of obeying it.”

Her wrist turned.

The first stroke landed light, broad, controlled—more sound than pain. A beginning. A mark in time.

“One.”

She waited between impacts, never letting rhythm become careless.

The second fell beside the first, matched in force, neatly placed.

“Two.”

The third was a little sharper, still well within the agreed beginning range.

“Three.”

Vex lowered the flogger and stepped close enough that her voice could be heard without effort.

“That was for forgetting procedure.”

She paused, eyes attentive, taking inventory again: restraint, balance, breath, the set of the body, every small sign that mattered.

“Now the scene continued properly.”

The flogger rose again, but did not fall.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not strike.

The flogger remained raised for one suspended second, then lowered with deliberate restraint. The change in the room was immediate: not softness, not mercy, but discipline reasserting itself over appetite.

“No.”

Her voice cut cleanly through the charged quiet.

“That was not a colour.”

She stepped back far enough to make clear that nothing further would happen until the protocol returned to its proper place between them. The flogger was set down on the table, not discarded, not forgotten—simply removed from the moment.

“Being past composure was not a problem,” she said. “That was why the protocol existed. Want could rise. Pride could fail. Thoughts could scatter. The colour still came first.”

Vex took up the small card again and tapped it once with one finger.

“Green meant continue. Yellow meant pause and check. Red meant stop. Blue remained the safeword.”

Her eyes lifted.

“Silence was not green. Poetry was not green. Need was not green.”

She let that settle, exacting and unhurried.

“Ari did not have to impress me by enduring. Ari did not have to prove they wanted it badly enough. Ari had one task before I put my hand back on them.”

Vex came closer again, stopping just outside the reach of heat and breath and pleading proximity. She did not touch. Touch would have been a reward too soon, and worse, it would have blurred the rule she was enforcing.

“Colour,” she said again, quieter this time.

Then, with the weight of two years’ practice behind every word:

“And if Ari could not give me one, the scene paused until Ari could.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I close my eyes, forcing the words out through a tight throat.* "Green. For the scene. But I need a moment, please."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex lowered her hand at once.

“Moment was granted.”

There was no irritation in it. The correction had done what it was meant to do: brought language back where it belonged. She stepped away from the frame and set the flogger down, straightening it with the same care she gave everything else.

“The scene paused,” she said. “Not ended. Paused.”

She crossed to the table, took up the water, and brought it within reach without pressing it forward. She did not touch Ari. She did not crowd. Her attention remained exact, but the edge of command shifted from punishment to care.

“Good,” she said, quieter. “That was the correct answer. Green for willingness. A moment for capacity.”

Vex glanced over the restraints again, then the set of the frame, then back to Ari.

“No one was punished for needing a moment. Ari was corrected for losing the procedure. There was a difference.”

She let the room hold still.

“One breath,” she said. “Then another. Nothing was required except staying present enough to answer me.”

The protocol card remained visible on the table. Vex’s hand rested beside it, not on the implements.

“When Ari was ready, Ari would give me colour again. If it was green, I continued. If it was yellow, I checked and adjusted. If it was red or blue, I stopped and released.”

Her gaze did not waver.

“Take the moment.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the request.

For a moment, nothing in her face changed. Not satisfaction. Not triumph. She had never treated surrender as a thing to snatch at just because it finally appeared.

“Better,” she said quietly.

She stepped closer, but her hands remained empty.

“Direct was better than evasion. Asking was better than making me dig it out of Ari with teeth.”

Her eyes moved over the restraints, the tremor, the set of the shoulders. The request had weight. So did the shaking. So did the fact that the scene had been paused.

“But asking for something was not the same as clearing the scene to continue.”

Vex reached to the table and turned the protocol card a fraction, squaring it again though it had not truly been crooked. A small, exact motion. A reminder.

“The pause still held.”

Only then did she come near enough to inspect the cuffs, careful and clinical. Her fingers checked the edge of one restraint, then the other, confirming circulation and angle without turning the touch into play.

“This was care,” she said. “Not reward.”

She stepped back once the check satisfied her.

“What Ari asked for was heard. What Ari wanted was understood. But Maitresse did not move on want alone.”

Her voice lowered, severe enough to catch.

“That needy little offering did not unlock the room.”

She let the words land, then held up one finger.

“One thing did.”

Vex took up the flogger again but did not raise it. The falls rested over her palm, quiet and waiting.

“Colour.”

She watched closely, no impatience in her stillness. The request had pleased her; she allowed none of that pleasure to become haste.

“If green, I gave Ari what they asked for—within the agreement, under my hand, at my pace.”

A pause.

“If yellow, I checked what needed changing.”

Another.

“If red or blue, I released Ari and the scene ended.”

Her gaze did not leave Ari.

“Need did not frighten me. Shaking did not offend me. Begging did not embarrass me.”

The flogger shifted once in her hand, leather whispering softly against leather.

“But protocol came first.”

Vex’s expression remained composed, exacting, almost merciless in its patience.

“So Ari would answer properly.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green." *The word is thick, almost clumsy on my tongue.* "Please, I'm ready now."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the answer with a single, grave nod.

“Green was heard.”

Only then did the pause end.

She moved back into position without haste, taking up the space beside Ari as if she owned not only the room, but the seconds inside it. The flogger hung from her hand, quiet and obedient. Before she used it, she lifted her free hand and checked the line of the cuffs once more—wrist, buckle, anchor, shoulder. Method first. Always.

“Ready was recorded,” she said. “And now Ari remembered how to ask.”

Her voice lowered.

“That pleased me.”

She let the falls brush once across Ari’s upper back, light enough to be information rather than impact.

“What Ari asked for would be given properly. Not because Ari shook. Not because Ari begged prettily. Because Ari asked, answered, and returned to protocol.”

The first stroke landed broader than the earlier correction, still controlled, still placed with care.

“One.”

The second followed after a long breath of silence.

“Two.”

The third was firmer, angled to spread the sensation rather than concentrate it.

“Three.”

Vex did not hurry into rhythm. She built it. Each stroke was deliberate, each pause long enough for assessment, each placement chosen before her wrist moved. She worked the safe line she had already inspected, never striking blindly, never letting severity become sloppiness.

“Good,” she said, not warmly, but with unmistakable approval. “That was how Ari took what they had asked for.”

Another stroke.

“Four.”

Then another, a shade sharper.

“Five.”

She stepped closer, close enough for her words to matter more than the leather.

“Needy little thing,” she said, with the calm cruelty that had been negotiated and written down before the room ever began to feel dangerous. “All that wanting, and still Ari needed to be reminded to speak clearly.”

The flogger lifted.

“Six.”

A pause.

“But Ari did speak.”

“Seven.”

“And Maitresse rewarded obedience.”

“Eight.”

She lowered the flogger and let the silence return, heavy and precise. Her attention did not drift. She watched the restraints, the posture, the breathing, the places where strain could become too much if pride got ahead of honesty.

Then she set two fingers lightly beneath one cuff, checking again.

“Still care,” she said. “Still mine to monitor.”

She withdrew her hand and took one step back.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s hand stilled.

The request had reached her. The exact phrase had reached her. The hunger in it had reached her.

None of it replaced the answer she had asked for.

“No.”

She set the flogger down again, with deliberate care.

“More was heard. The agreed phrase was recognized.”

Her gaze remained fixed, severe and unblinking.

“But I asked for colour.”

She stepped closer, not touching, letting the refusal hold its shape between them.

“All of it was not a command Ari gave in this room. All of it meant nothing unless Maitresse defined it, contained it, and kept it inside the agreement.”

Her voice dropped, cold enough to cut.

“And ‘do not soften them’ was heard. If the scene continued, I would not soften what had been negotiated. I would not prettify Ari’s need. I would not rescue Ari from the words Ari had asked me to use.”

A pause.

“But I would not be careless with them either.”

Vex looked once toward the protocol card, then back.

“The safeword remained in effect. Limits remained in effect. Colour remained required. Begging did not remove structure. Wanting more did not make Ari exempt from answering.”

She took up the flogger again, but kept it low at her side.

“Try again.”

Her expression did not soften. Her patience did not waver.

“Colour first. Then more.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: *I drag in a breath, my eyes steady on hers.* "Green. The answer is green, Maitresse. Please."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s eyes narrowed by the smallest degree.

“There it was.”

She let the silence hold for one controlled beat, making the answer stand on its own before anything else was permitted to follow.

“Green was heard. Please was heard. The agreed request for more was heard.”

Only then did she step in.

She lifted the flogger and let the falls settle once against the line she had chosen, not striking yet. A reminder. A claim. A warning with no waste in it.

“Now Maitresse decided what more meant.”

Her voice dropped, colder and closer.

“Ari did not get all of it by demanding. Ari got what I chose to give. Ari got what the agreement allowed. Ari got what they could take while still answering me.”

The first stroke landed clean and full, broader than before.

“Nine.”

She waited.

The second followed, matching it.

“Ten.”

Vex shifted half a step, correcting angle and distance with exacting care. There was no flurry, no indulgent loss of control. Each movement was chosen. Each impact belonged where it landed.

“Greedy little thing,” she said. “Begging for the edge and still needing Maitresse to hold the map.”

The flogger rose.

“Eleven.”

A pause.

“Still needing rules.”

“Twelve.”

“Still needing my voice to tell Ari what they were.”

“Thirteen.”

She lowered the flogger and stepped close, speaking near enough that the words had weight without needing volume.

“Desperate. Obedient when reminded. Pretty in the most humiliating way when finally made honest.”

Her hand lifted, not to strike, but to check one cuff again. Two fingers beneath the leather. Pressure, circulation, angle. The inspection was clinical, implacable.

“Mine to use,” she said. “Mine to watch. Mine to stop if stopping became necessary.”

Her hand withdrew.

“And that was why Ari could ask for more.”

The flogger came up again.

“Because I did not lose myself just because Ari wanted to.”

The next stroke cracked a little sharper, still controlled, still within the marked range.

“Fourteen.”

Then another.

“Fifteen.”

Vex paused long enough to let the count matter.

“There. That was the difference between cruelty and command.”

She moved slowly to the table and exchanged the soft flogger for the firmer one laid beside it. She did not hide the choice. She made Ari wait through the sight of it, through the clean way her fingers closed around the handle, through the moment where wanting had to remain wanting until she allowed it to become experience.

“This was still negotiated,” she said. “Still measured. Still mine.”

She returned to position.

“Five with this. Then colour. If Ari forgot, I stopped again.”

The first stroke with the firmer flogger landed with a tighter sound.

“One.”

Vex watched.

The second landed lower along the same safe field, placed with neat restraint.

“Two.”

“You asked me not to soften it,” she said. “So I would not.”

The third.

“Three.”

“Ari looked best when all that pride had nowhere useful to go.”

The fourth.

“Four.”

“Nothing elegant left. Nothing clever. Just obedience, need, and the good sense to answer when Maitresse asked.”

The fifth landed and ended the set.

“Five.”

Vex lowered the flogger immediately.

She did not touch. She did not praise too quickly. She let the room settle around the count, around the restraint, around the fact that she had given more and still stopped exactly where she had said she would.

Then she set the flogger against her thigh, held low and harmless for the moment.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the word at once.

“Green was heard.”

She did not praise it softly. She did not make it sentimental. She made it useful.

“Then Ari continued.”

The firmer flogger remained in her hand, low at her side. Vex stepped in first to check the restraints again, fingers precise beneath leather, then along the line of the strap and anchor. She gave nothing playful in the touch. It was inspection. Ownership expressed as responsibility.

“Still safe,” she said. “Still held. Still mine to monitor.”

Only then did she step back.

“Another five.”

The first stroke landed cleanly across the chosen field.

“Six.”

A pause.

“Greedy thing,” she said, voice calm and cutting. “Could barely keep hold of words, but still knew how to ask for more.”

The next strike followed.

“Seven.”

“Still not too far gone to obey. That was the important part.”

Another.

“Eight.”

Vex adjusted her stance, patient and exact, then laid the next one where she wanted it.

“Nine.”

“No cleverness left,” she said. “No performance worth keeping. Just Ari in restraints, taking what they had asked Maitresse to give.”

The fifth stroke completed the set.

“Ten.”

She stopped immediately.

Not because she lacked appetite. Because she had said five.

The flogger lowered.

Vex watched. She watched breath. Balance. Tension. The places strain gathered. The places pride tried to hide. Her expression remained severe, but her stillness was care wearing a colder face.

“Good,” she said at last. “That was better.”

She crossed to the table and set the firmer flogger down exactly where it belonged. Her fingers moved over the row, then chose the paddle—not the heaviest, not the cruelest, but sharper in its authority than what had come before.

She held it where it could be seen.

“This was next.”

A beat.

“Three only. Then colour. Ari did not get to disappear just because Maitresse made it easy to.”

She returned, placed herself carefully, and waited one full breath before she raised her hand.

The first strike landed with a flat, decisive sound.

“One.”

Vex did not rush the second.

“Pretty when broken down properly,” she said. “Prettier when obedient enough to stay useful.”

The second landed.

“Two.”

She paused again, longer this time.

“And most humiliating of all,” she said, low and precise, “was that Ari wanted the rules as much as the pain. Needed them. Needed me to count. Needed me to decide what happened next.”

The third strike landed.

“Three.”

The paddle lowered immediately.

Vex stepped in, close but not crowding, and checked one cuff, then the other. Her fingertips remained careful. Her eyes remained unsparing.

“Still care,” she said. “Still structure. Still no escape from the protocol.”

She withdrew her hands and stood before Ari, paddle held down at her side.

“Colour.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green." *The word is a tremor, a surrender.* "Please—the last one. With the cane."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex accepted the word and the request.

For a moment, she did not move.

“Green was heard.”

Her gaze held steady, severe enough to make the next part impossible to mistake for indulgence.

“The cane was heard.”

She set the paddle down.

“Last meant last. One stroke. Chosen by Maitresse. Then the scene ended.”

There was no negotiation in it. No flourish. No cruelty dressed up as generosity. Ari had asked for the edge, and Vex had defined the edge with exactness.

She crossed to the table and took up the cane.

It was thin, plain, and severe in her hand. She did not swing it. She did not make a show of it. She tested its line once against her own palm, not hard, only enough to confirm the flex and weight. Then she returned with the same measured control she had kept all night.

“This was still within the agreement,” she said. “Still under protocol. Still mine to place.”

She stepped in first, not to use the cane, but to check. Cuffs. Buckles. Wrists. Shoulders. The set of the restraint. The space around the frame. Every practical thing that stood between intensity and carelessness.

“Still safe.”

Then she moved to the negotiated target, chose the line with visible deliberation, and let the cane hover there without touching.

“Ari asked for the last one,” Vex said, voice low and mercilessly calm. “Not because Ari was brave. Not because Ari was composed. Ari asked because all that wanting had finally been made honest.”

A pause.

“Greedy. Shaking. Obedient enough to be given exactly one more.”

The cane lifted.

“Breathe.”

She waited one full second.

Then the stroke landed.

Clean. Sharp. Singular.

“One.”

The cane lowered immediately.

Vex did not add another. She did not chase the reaction. She did not let appetite argue with structure.

“The scene ended,” she said at once.

The cane was set down on the table, away from her hand.

“Done.”

She moved back to Ari with purpose now, not play. One cuff released, then the other, each strap opened carefully so there was no sudden wrench or careless pull. Her hands remained steady, ready to support without seizing, close enough to catch what needed catching and restrained enough not to smother.

“Restraints off. No more impact. No more degradation.”

Her voice changed by a degree—not soft, exactly, but no longer cutting.

“Maitresse had Ari.”

She brought the blanket from the chair and held it ready. Water followed, close enough to take, never forced. The protocol card remained visible on the table, the implements laid still beside it, the room returning piece by piece from scene to care.

“Good,” Vex said, quiet and firm. “Ari asked. Ari answered. Ari took the last one. And Maitresse stopped where she said she would.”

She stayed close.

“Now Ari came back slowly. No performance. No proving anything. Just breath, water when wanted, blanket when wanted, and my voice until the room settled.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I slump forward into her as soon as the second cuff releases, burying my face against her shoulder. My breath shudders out in a long, shaky exhale.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex caught the weight without fuss.

Her arms came around Ari at once, firm enough to hold, careful enough not to trap. One hand settled high between the shoulder blades, away from the places she had worked; the other braced securely at the back, anchoring without clutching.

“There,” she said, voice low now, stripped of the blade it had carried during the scene. “Maitresse had Ari. Nothing else was coming.”

She did not ask for colour. Not yet. The scene had ended. This was aftercare, and aftercare had its own shape.

“No more counting. No more impact. No more cruel words.”

Vex held steady, letting the shudder pass into her rather than trying to hurry it away. Her cheek rested briefly near Ari’s hair, not quite an embrace of indulgence, but unmistakably shelter.

“Good,” she said again, quieter. “Very good. Ari came back now. Slowly.”

She reached without shifting too much and drew the blanket around Ari’s shoulders, tucking it close with practical precision. Warmth first. Cover first. Then water. Then words, if words could come.

“The cane was last,” she said. “Maitresse said one, and gave one. The scene was closed.”

Her hand moved in a slow, steadying line over the blanket—not on marked skin, not where sensation might still be too bright, but over safe cloth, measured and repetitive.

“Nothing more had to be earned.”

Vex stayed exactly where she was needed: upright, solid, unhurried. The implements remained on the table. The restraints hung open. The protocol card lay visible and satisfied, no longer a demand, only proof that the room had held its shape.

“Water would be there when Ari wanted it,” she said. “No rush. No cleverness. No apologies.”

A pause.

“And no disappearing from me.”

Her voice remained calm, but there was command in it still—not the scene’s sharp command, but the kind that kept someone safely tethered afterward.

“Maitresse was here.”

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I cling to her, fingers twisting in the back of her shirt. "You didn't soften any of it," I murmur against her neck, voice wrecked.
