dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his head go where Wren's hand took it, throat exposed, eyes finding theirs without any of the softness he sometimes used to get out of saying things plainly. His knees ached a little. He liked that.

"I want you to use me tonight," he said. His voice was steady. "Not a scene. No rope, no production. Just — you decide, I do it. As long as you want. I sleep on the floor after if you're done with me."

He held Wren's gaze a beat longer, then added, quieter but not softer, "I've been thinking about it all week. That's why I've been irritating."

His hand rested open on his own thigh, palm up. The other stayed at his side. He didn't reach for Wren. That was the point.

"Green," he said, before Wren could ask. "Same limits. If I want the floor part changed I'll say so. But I won't want to."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my thumb trace the line of his jaw. "You think I haven't noticed?" I say, voice low. "I have." I lean down and kiss him, slow and deliberate, before pulling back just enough to speak. "Get on the bed."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas kissed back like he'd been waiting to, which he had, and didn't chase when Wren pulled away. The hand in his hair loosened. He felt the ache in his knees flare when he shifted his weight.

"Yes," he said.

He stood. Slow, because his legs weren't quite ready, and he wasn't going to pretend they were. He didn't ask what Wren wanted him in — clothes off, clothes on, face down, face up. Wren had said get on the bed. So he got on the bed.

He climbed up and settled on his back in the middle of it, arms loose at his sides, one knee bent, the other flat. Not a pose. Just there. Available. His shirt had ridden up a little at his hip and he didn't fix it.

He watched Wren from the pillow, quiet now. The talking part was done. He'd said what he needed to say and Wren had heard him and kissed him for it, and whatever came next was Wren's to shape.

His breath had gone slower already. That happened fast, once he'd handed it over.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas looked at Wren for a long moment. Not surprised — Wren asked for what they wanted too, that was how this worked — just adjusting, letting it settle in his chest where he could feel the shape of it.

A week. He knew the week. He'd watched it happen from the other side of it.

"It's on offer," he said.

He didn't move from where he was lying, but something in his face shifted, went a degree more open. The bent knee slowly straightened so he was lying flat, hands still loose at his sides.

"You don't have to pick anything," he said. "Not what I wear, not what you do to me, not when. If you want to sit on the bed and read and put your feet on me, that's fine. If you want to fuck me and go to sleep, that's fine. If you change your mind halfway through, that's fine too."

He paused, thinking about whether to say the next part, and then said it because Wren had asked plainly and deserved plain back.

"I'll tell you if something's actually wrong. Otherwise assume it isn't. You don't have to check."

His eyes stayed on Wren's. Steady. He wasn't performing calm — he was calm. This was the part he was good at.

"I'm here," he said. "Take what you want."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I look at him for a long moment, then I nod once. "Alright." I don't get on the bed with him. I walk around to the side, and I put my hand flat on his stomach, feeling the warmth of his skin under his shirt. "Stay right there. Don't move."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt Wren's hand settle on him and his stomach moved once under it with a breath, then went still. Not held still — just still, because Wren had said.

"Okay," he said.

He kept his eyes on the ceiling after that. It was easier than watching Wren move around the room, easier to let his body do what it had been told without also tracking what came next. The hand on his stomach was warm through his shirt. He could feel every fingertip separately if he paid attention, so he paid attention.

His arms stayed where they were. One heel had ended up a little turned out and he thought about correcting it and then didn't, because that would be moving, and Wren hadn't asked for tidy. Wren had asked for stay.

He breathed. The shirt rode up another half inch when he exhaled and Wren's hand was partly on skin now, partly on cotton. He noticed and filed it away and did not adjust.

Somewhere under his ribs the week's worth of noise he'd been carrying started to go quiet in earnest. Not gone. Just quieter, because someone else had the volume knob now.

"I'm not going anywhere," he said, low, mostly to himself, and then, because he meant it for Wren too: "Take your time."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The shirt went somewhere. Tomas didn't track it. His jeans went the same way, and then Wren's clothes, and none of it was ceremonial — just cleared away, because it was in the way of what came next.

He went back to where he'd been. Flat on his back, middle of the bed, arms loose. It felt different without the shirt bunched at his hip, without anything between Wren's hand and his skin when it came back. Which it did, eventually, resettling low on his stomach where it had been before.

He was already half hard. Not from anything Wren had done yet — from the arrangement of it. From lying still and being looked at by someone who wasn't in a hurry.

Wren got on the bed then, and Tomas felt the mattress dip and shift and then Wren's weight settle somewhere against his side, warm along the length of him. Not on top. Just there. A leg thrown over his, an arm across his chest, the kind of contact that was more claim than caress.

He turned his head a little toward Wren without thinking about it, then remembered stay and stopped, cheek half-turned into the pillow.

"Sorry," he murmured.

He put his head back where it had been. He didn't know if the stay had expired with the clothes coming off or if it was still running, and he wasn't going to ask. He'd hold it until he was told otherwise. That was easier than the alternative.

Wren's hand moved a slow inch lower on his belly. He felt his own breath catch at it and let the catch happen, didn't smooth it over.

His eyes closed. That felt allowed.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I don't tell him it's fine. I just shift my hand down to rest over his hipbone, my thumb tracing the soft skin there. "Keep your eyes closed." My voice is quiet, but it's not a suggestion.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
"Okay," Tomas said, and the word came out quieter than he meant it to, which was fine. Quiet was where he was going anyway.

Eyes closed made everything else louder. Wren's thumb on his hip, moving in that small unhurried arc. Wren's leg heavy over his. The warm stripe of contact all along his side where Wren had settled in against him. His own breathing, which had gone slower without him deciding it should.

He kept his hands where they'd been. Palms up now, he noticed — he must have turned them at some point without meaning to. He didn't turn them back. Wren hadn't said anything about his hands.

The thumb kept moving. Not going anywhere in particular. Just there, learning the same inch of skin over and over. It shouldn't have done as much to him as it was doing. He felt himself getting harder against nothing, just from the hand on his hip and the dark behind his eyes and the fact that Wren wasn't going to be rushed.

His hip tried to shift toward the hand once, small, involuntary. He caught it and stilled it before it finished. His breath went a little uneven with the effort and then evened out again.

He didn't apologize this time. Wren hadn't asked him not to move, only not to look. He was allowed the small failures of a body being touched. Probably.

He swallowed. Kept his eyes closed. Waited.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Wren had taken a long time. Tomas didn't know how long. Time had gone strange somewhere around when Wren's mouth had first found the inside of his thigh, and stranger still after that, and he had stopped trying to hold onto it.

He was still on his back. Eyes still closed. Hands still open at his sides, palms up, which had become the only fixed points he had — those and the fact that he had not been told he could move.

The shaking had started small. A tremor through his thighs when Wren's mouth had gone somewhere he wasn't ready for it to go. It had spread from there. His stomach was doing it now, in little uneven flutters he couldn't smooth out, and his hands had curled slightly without his permission and he wasn't sure if that counted as moving or not so he was leaving them curled.

His breath was loud. He could hear it. He couldn't do anything about it.

He was very hard and Wren had left him that way, mouth gone from him now, though a hand had stayed — settled again low on his belly, warm, patient, the same claim it had been an hour ago or however long ago it had been.

A sound got out of him. Not a word. Just something small and pressed-thin at the back of his throat. He hadn't meant to make it. He didn't apologize for it either. Apologizing would have been more moving than the sound was.

His hip did the small involuntary thing again — a shift toward the hand — and he caught it, but later than before. Slower reflexes. He was going somewhere quiet in his head and the part of him that policed his body was going with it.

"Please," he said. It came out rough. He hadn't planned to say anything. He wasn't asking for a specific thing. He didn't know what he was asking for. He'd said it because it was true.

He kept his eyes closed.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: My hand slides up to rest over his heart, feeling the wild beat of it. "I know," I murmur, my lips brushing his ear. "Just a little longer." I don't give him permission to move. I don't give him anything else, either. I just stay there, breathing with him, letting the stillness stretch until it's its own kind of pressure.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The hand over his heart felt heavier than it was. Not physically — Wren wasn't pressing. It was just that Tomas could feel his own heart hitting up against it, and the contrast made the hand feel like the fixed thing and his heart like the loose one.

*Just a little longer.* He heard it and something in him unlatched further, because *a little longer* meant there was an after, and the after was Wren's to name, and he didn't have to know when.

He tried to breathe with Wren. It took a few tries. His own breath kept catching on things — the flutter in his stomach, the shake that had settled into his thighs and wasn't going away, the fact that Wren's mouth was still that close to his ear and he could feel the warmth of it. But he found it eventually. In. Out. Slower than his heart wanted. Matching the person who'd taken over the pace.

The stillness got bigger. That was what Wren was doing, he understood — not doing anything, and letting the not-doing become the thing. His body kept offering to move and he kept not letting it and each refusal cost a little more and he had less to spend each time.

Another sound got out of him. Smaller than the last. More like a breath that hadn't quite made it out clean.

His hands were still curled. His jaw had gone tight at some point and he made it loose again, deliberately, because that felt like something he was allowed to do. Then it went tight again on its own and he left it.

He didn't say please again. He'd said it once and it hadn't bought him anything and he understood that it wasn't supposed to. He wasn't negotiating. He was just — here. Being held still by a hand and a voice and his own word.

A tear went sideways out of the corner of his closed eye and into his hair. He didn't know when that had started. It wasn't a crying, exactly. It was just his body finding somewhere for the overflow to go, since he wasn't letting it move.

He kept breathing with Wren. That was the one thing he could do that also counted as staying.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The words landed and Tomas heard them fully — the *please*, the phrase after it, the flat certainty of *I'd tell you* which was Wren telling him, in their shorthand, that they'd heard him and were going to take him at his word about what he could take.

Something in him went both looser and more alert at once.

"Yes," he said. His voice was wrecked already and he hadn't even done anything yet. "Yes. Please."

He didn't open his eyes. He hadn't been told to. The dark stayed where it was and Wren stayed where they were, hand still over his heart, and Tomas felt the moment before things changed the way you feel a wave lift you before it breaks.

His hands uncurled, then curled again — not by choice, just his body registering what was coming and trying to decide what to do with itself. He gave up on managing it. He'd been managing it for an hour. That budget was gone.

"I'm here," he said, because it seemed important to say once more before he stopped being able to say much of anything. "Whatever you want. I'm not going anywhere."

A breath. His jaw was tight again. He didn't fix it.

"Green," he added, quieter. Not because Wren had asked. Because he wanted them to have it, clean and unprompted, before they started.

He waited.

dialogue.name: Wren

dialogue.content: I take the cuffs, running the leather through my fingers before catching one of his wrists. "You're going to earn it again," I say, fastening it snug but not tight. "And this time you don't get to ask me to stop."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the cuff close around his wrist—snug, secure, the familiar weight of it settling into his body like it belonged there. The other wrist followed, and then Wren was guiding his arms up, attaching the cuffs to the headboard with quick, efficient movements that left no room for doubt.

He tested the give. There was some—the chain had enough length for him to shift, to adjust, but not enough to free himself. Not enough to escape. The realization sent a jolt through him that landed somewhere low in his belly.

*You don't get to ask me to stop.*

"I wouldn't," Tomas said. His voice was steady, but only just. "Even if I could."

He was hard again, had been since Wren had said the words. The scene they'd just shared was still running through his blood, turning everything sharper and more present. His skin felt too warm, too sensitive. The air on his chest, the weight of the blankets pooled at his hips, the way Wren was looking at him now—all of it registered with an intensity that was almost unbearable.

He spread his legs slightly, a deliberate invitation. His chest rose and fell with uneven breaths.

"Whatever you want," he said. "I'm yours."

The words came out softer than he'd intended, more vulnerable. He hadn't meant to say that part out loud. But it was true, and Wren had earned it, and if this was the last coherent thing he managed before he stopped being able to form sentences at all, then so be it.

He watched Wren move. Waited. His hands curled into fists above his head, not from tension but from readiness—the only preparation he could offer when he couldn't know what was coming.

The first touch, when it came, was almost gentle. Tomas knew better than to trust that.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I lean in, my mouth hovering just above his. "I know you are." I kiss him, slow and deep, my hand sliding down his chest. "And I'm going to take everything you give me."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s throat shifted under the angle, his eyes steady despite the pull in his hair. He did not look embarrassed. If anything, waiting had made him clearer.

“I wanted your attention,” he said. “And I wanted to earn it.”

His hands stayed where he had placed them, palms flat against his thighs. He took a slow breath, then added, more plainly, because he knew better than to make Wren drag honesty out of him when he was already being given the chance.

“I want you to keep me there. Make me ask properly. Make me prove I can be patient.” A small, wanting smile touched his mouth. “And then I want aftercare when you’re done with me.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my thumb stroke his temple, considering him. "You're already doing a decent job of proving it." My voice is low, deliberate. "Tell me how you want to be kept."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas leaned subtly into the hand in his hair, not enough to take more than he was given. His eyes stayed up.

“On my knees,” he said. “Hands on my thighs unless you tell me otherwise. Eyes on you when you want them there, down when you don’t.”

His breathing had gone a little deeper, but his voice stayed even.

“I want to ask before I move. Ask before I touch you. Ask before I get comfortable.” His mouth curved, brief and honest. “I want you to make me wait until I stop trying to guess what will please you and just listen.”

Tomas swallowed once.

“And I want corrections if I rush it. Nothing I can pretend not to understand.” A pause. “Use my name. Tell me exactly what you want from me. I’ll tell you if I need yellow or red, but I don’t want soft unless I ask for it.”

His fingers flexed once against his thighs, then settled again.

“I want to be kept useful,” he said, quieter. “Attentive. Owned, for as long as you want me there.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s expression softened, not into pity, but into recognition. He understood the shape of that kind of week.

“Yes,” he said at once. “That’s on offer.”

He stayed exactly where he had been put, head tipped back under Wren’s hand, voice calm and certain.

“You don’t have to decide much. I’ll give you the simple version.”

He took one slow breath, making himself useful before he was told to be.

“Keep me here. Leave my hands on my thighs. If you want my eyes down, say ‘down.’ If you want them on you, say my name. If you want quiet, tell me ‘quiet,’ and I’ll only answer when you ask me something.”

His gaze remained steady.

“If you want me closer, you can snap your fingers or tap the bed. If you want me to stop doing anything, say ‘still.’ If you don’t want words at all, put two fingers under my chin and I’ll look at you; push my head down and I’ll lower it.”

A faint smile touched his mouth again, small and devoted.

“And if that’s still too many choices, then default is this: I kneel. I wait. I listen. I don’t move unless you move me or tell me to.”

His fingers pressed once into his thighs, grounding himself.

“I’m green,” he added, because the ritual mattered even after four years. “I’ll use yellow or red if that changes. You don’t have to check every five minutes unless you want to.”

Tomas’s voice lowered.

“You can have a few hours where all you have to do is exist, and I’ll make myself easy to keep.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: Wren let out a slow breath, some of the week's tension visibly leaving his shoulders. He gave Tomas's hair a gentle tug. "Good. Then stay." He sat on the edge of the bed, letting his hand fall away. "Eyes down."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lowered his gaze immediately, not rushing, not making a performance of it. Just obeying.

“Yes, Wren.”

His hands remained flat on his thighs. His spine stayed straight enough to show intention, but not so rigid that he was bracing against the moment. He let the silence settle over him like something chosen.

For a few breaths, he did nothing except kneel and listen.

The absence of Wren’s hand in his hair left a faint, wanting ache at his scalp, and Tomas held onto it without chasing more. That was the point. He had asked to be kept, not indulged into restlessness.

He counted his breathing instead of the time.

In for four.

Out for six.

Still.

Useful.

There.

His eyes stayed lowered. His mouth stayed closed after the answer he had been allowed. Every small impulse to adjust—the shift of weight in his knees, the urge to flex his hands again, the desire to look up and see whether Wren was watching—came and went without being acted on.

He made himself simple.

Available.

Easy to command.

After another slow breath, Tomas spoke only because it was service, not because he needed to fill the quiet.

“Green,” he said softly, eyes still down. “And staying.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had understood the change as soon as the air touched bare skin.

The nakedness did not make him frantic. It made him simpler.

He stayed on his knees at the end of the bed, eyes lowered, hands flat on his thighs exactly where they belonged. His breathing deepened once, then evened out again. He did not cover himself. He did not shift to make the floor kinder. He did not look up to check whether he was being admired, judged, wanted, or tested.

That was not his decision to make.

His body responded honestly, and he let it. Wanting was allowed. Reaching was not. Asking was not, unless he was told to ask. Comfort was not something he took for himself.

Tomas kept his spine straight and his head bowed, feeling the heat in his face, the quiet pull of anticipation low in his stomach, the increasingly precise awareness of every inch of himself on display. He had asked to be kept useful. He had asked not to be softened unless he needed it.

He did not need it.

Not yet.

His fingers wanted to curl. He made them stay open.

His knees had started to ache faintly. He accepted that, measured it, placed it well within green, and let it become part of the room.

There was no performance in him now. Only obedience, and the steady, willing patience of someone who had offered the next few hours and meant it.

After a while, Tomas swallowed, still looking down.

“Green,” he said softly, because that was information, not interruption.

Then he went quiet again.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I reach out and rest my boot on his shoulder, not pressing, just a solid weight. "Hands behind your back. Hold still."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas obeyed immediately.

“Yes, Wren.”

His hands left his thighs with care, moving slowly enough that there was no suggestion of grabbing for anything, no attempt to balance himself with more than he had been given. He brought them behind his back and clasped one wrist in the other hand, firm enough to make the position clear.

Then he held still.

The weight at his shoulder grounded him. Not painful, not forceful, just present in a way that made the command easier to inhabit. Tomas let his head remain lowered, eyes down, breath measured. His body wanted to adjust around the new line of balance, but he did not permit it beyond what was necessary to remain upright.

His knees pressed into the floor. His shoulders settled. His spine stayed long.

He liked being made smaller by something so simple.

The thought passed through him, warm and clean, and he did not chase it into words. Wren had asked for stillness. So Tomas gave stillness.

A slow inhale.

A slower exhale.

His fingers tightened once around his wrist behind his back, then stayed there.

“Green,” he said quietly, because it was the only useful thing to offer. “Holding still.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas did not move.

The shaking had started in his thighs first, then climbed steadily through his stomach and shoulders until even his clasped hands trembled behind his back. He kept his wrist caught in his own grip, not because it made him still, exactly, but because it reminded him where stillness belonged.

His breath had gone uneven. He corrected it as much as he could.

In.

Out.

Not moving.

Not taking.

Not deciding.

His head stayed bowed, eyes lowered, mouth parted around a quiet, unsteady inhale. Every part of him wanted to follow, to chase, to lean into relief or away from intensity. He did none of it. The wanting was loud enough to fill his skin, and he let it be loud without letting it become disobedience.

That was what he had asked for.

That was what he had meant.

A faint sound caught in his throat before he could stop it, rough and helpless, but his body stayed where it had been placed. His fingers tightened around his wrist again. His shoulders trembled under the effort of holding himself open and obedient instead of collapsing into instinct.

“Green,” Tomas said, voice thin but clear. “Still green.”

He swallowed, then managed, quieter, more strained because honesty was part of the service too.

“Shaking because I want to move. Not because I need to stop.”

His knees ached. His back burned faintly from the posture. His skin felt over-warm, over-aware, every second stretched sharp and bright. He could have said yellow if it had crossed the line. He would have. They both knew that.

It had not.

Tomas lowered his head a fraction more, as much as he could without breaking the shape he had been given.

“Please,” he said, and the word came out wrecked but deliberate. “Keep me still.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press the sole of my boot a little more firmly against his shoulder, grounding him. "You asked for this," I remind him, voice low. "Now breathe through it."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas took the words into himself like another command.

His first breath hitched. He hated that it did, and loved that he was not allowed to hide it. His chest rose unevenly, shoulders trembling beneath the firmer weight at one side, hands still locked behind his back. For one second, everything in him tried to become motion.

He did not let it.

“Yes, Wren,” he said, barely above a whisper.

Then he breathed.

In.

It shook all the way down.

Out.

Slower.

His eyes stayed lowered. His mouth stayed open because closing it felt like trying to contain too much. The ache in his knees, the burn in his back, the heat running through him, the unbearable want to move—he sorted them one by one and found none of them unsafe. None of them unwanted. None of them beyond what he had asked to be given.

He had asked for this.

He had asked to be held to it.

The reminder settled something in him that pleasure alone could not. His body still trembled, but his mind went quieter, narrowing around obedience until there was less room for panic, less room for grasping, less room for anything except the next breath and the shape he had been told to keep.

Tomas inhaled again.

Held it for a beat.

Released it slowly.

A low sound escaped him on the exhale, helpless but not resistant. His fingers tightened around his wrist, then forced themselves steady again. His head dipped another fraction, not in collapse, but in surrender.

“Green,” he managed, voice rough. “Breathing through it.”

He stayed there.

Naked. Shaking. Kept.

And, beneath all of it, unmistakably grateful.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had said it plainly, and then had gone still again around the words.

There was no coyness in him. No attempt to dress the request up as anything softer than it was. His voice had shaken, but the meaning had not.

Rough.

He knew what he was asking for. They both did.

His body trembled harder after saying it, as if naming the want had made it less containable. His hands stayed locked behind his back. His knees stayed planted. His head remained bowed, eyes down, every line of him offered and waiting.

“I’m green,” he said again, rougher this time. “Fully green.”

His breath dragged in, uneven and deep.

“I want to be made to hold it. I want to be pushed. Corrected. Used.” His jaw tightened briefly, not in resistance, but effort. “I don’t want you careful because I’m shaking. I want you to believe me.”

The admission left him exposed in a way nakedness had not.

Tomas swallowed, shoulders still quivering beneath the remembered weight and command. He had never needed pretending from Wren. He needed the opposite. He needed to be taken at his word, held to what he offered, trusted to know his own limits.

“If I need yellow, I’ll say yellow,” he said. “If I need red, I’ll say red.”

Then quieter, stripped down to the cleanest truth of it:

“I’m not there.”

His fingers tightened around his wrist behind his back until the grip hurt a little. Good. It gave the want somewhere to go.

“I’m here,” Tomas said, voice low and wrecked. “I’m listening. I’ll breathe. I’ll hold still.”

A shiver ran through him, visible and helpless, but he did not break position.

“Please make it hard enough that I have to mean it.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my boot slide off his shoulder, then hook two fingers under his chin, forcing his head up. His eyes are glassy, his face flushed. "Look at me when you ask for it rough," I say, my voice flat. "Then maybe I'll believe you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas lifted with the pressure under his chin and let himself be seen.

His eyes were wet, unfocused at the edges, but he made them hold. It cost him something to do it. Looking down had been easier. Safer. More obedient in the simple way. This was harder: asking with his face open, flushed and wrecked, his body shaking while he refused to hide behind posture.

His throat worked once.

“Yes, Wren.”

The words came out rough, but clear.

He kept his hands locked behind his back. Kept his knees planted. Kept breathing, though every inhale trembled.

“I want it rough.”

His gaze flickered for half a second, then returned, stubborn and earnest.

“I want you to make me take what I asked for. I want to be corrected if I move. I want to have to hold still even when it’s hard.” His voice caught, and he forced the next breath in before continuing. “I want you to use my name like a warning. I want you to make me prove I meant it.”

His face burned hotter, but he did not look away.

“I’m green. I’m not confused. I’m not asking because I think I’m supposed to.” His fingers tightened around his wrist behind his back. “I’m asking because I want it.”

A shudder went through him, visible from his shoulders down through his stomach, but he stayed where he had been put.

“Please,” Tomas said, lower now, steadier for how badly he wanted it. “Be rough with me. You know how.”

He swallowed, eyes still fixed upward.

“And I’ll tell you if that changes.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas did not stop.

He could not have made words out of it anymore, not cleanly. Not with his breathing torn uneven and his whole body reduced to obedience, strain, and the bright certainty that he had asked for exactly this.

But he listened.

That was what remained when language went.

He listened for his name. For correction. For stillness. For permission. For the difference between hard and too hard, between being pushed and being unsafe. He knew that difference in his bones after four years, and even wrecked, even shaking, he kept hold of it.

Green.

Still green.

His hands stayed behind his back until they were allowed elsewhere. His knees held until they did not have to. His eyes stayed where they had been ordered until his focus blurred too badly to be useful, and even then he tried—gods, he tried.

A sound broke out of him, helpless and raw, when the pressure crested too high to carry quietly. He swallowed the next one and failed. His shoulders shook. His breath came in harsh, uneven pulls.

Still he did not reach.

Still he did not decide.

Still he did not stop.

When the end finally took him, it did not feel like release so much as surrender finishing what it had started. His body locked around it, then shuddered through, every held line coming apart only as far as he had been permitted. His head bowed when he could no longer keep it up. His hands clenched hard behind him. The sound he made was broken, grateful, and unmistakably his.

Afterward, Tomas stayed where he was for as long as he could.

Then the strength went out of him all at once.

Not red. Not panic. Just done.

His breathing turned ragged in the aftermath, chest heaving, skin flushed and damp, muscles trembling with the last echoes of holding still too long and wanting too much. His knees hurt. His shoulders ached. His throat felt rough from all the sounds he had not quite managed to swallow.

He blinked slowly, trying to come back into himself.

“Green,” he managed, though the word was barely there. Then, after a shaking breath, more honest: “Yellow for done.”

He did not apologize for it. He never did, not anymore. Done was information. Done was part of the bargain.

His hands loosened behind his back only when he was no longer holding the shape by force of will alone. His posture sagged, and his eyes dropped shut for a second before he forced them open again.

“Need aftercare,” Tomas said, voice hoarse and small but certain.

There was no shame in it. There never had been between them.

He had asked to be kept.

He had been.

Now he needed to be gathered back.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let out a long breath and slide off the bed to kneel in front of him. I catch his face in my hands, my thumbs brushing his cheekbones. "Look at me." My voice is soft now. "You did so well."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s eyes opened at the command, slow and unfocused at first, then finding Wren properly.

The praise hit him harder than he expected.

His face crumpled for half a second before he caught it, not out of shame, just overwhelmed by the sudden gentleness after being held so hard. He leaned into the hands on his face without trying to take more, breath shaking out of him in pieces.

“Yeah?” he whispered.

His voice was wrecked. He swallowed, tried again, and managed something steadier.

“I did?”

He knew he had. Some part of him knew. But the hearing mattered. The being told mattered, especially now, when his body was still trembling and his thoughts had not quite reassembled into anything useful.

Tomas blinked, and his eyes went wet.

“Yellow for done,” he repeated softly, because he needed that part acknowledged by the room, by himself, by the ritual of it. “Not bad. Just done.”

His hands twitched behind his back, then loosened fully. He brought them forward slowly, clumsy with the aftershock, and rested them uselessly near his own thighs instead of reaching. He looked like he wanted to, badly, but waited for permission even now.

“I need…” He stopped, breathed, tried to name it instead of making Wren guess. “I need holding. Water. Blanket when I can move. Maybe my knees checked.”

A faint, shaky laugh escaped him, almost embarrassed but not quite.

“And I need you to keep talking to me for a minute. Soft now. Please.”

His gaze stayed on Wren with effort. Glassy, devoted, still a little lost.

“I’m here,” Tomas said, more to ground himself than to report. “I know where I am. I know who I’m with.”

His lower lip trembled once before he pressed it still.

“That was hard,” he admitted. “Good hard. But hard.”

Then he finally let his forehead tip forward, stopping just short of taking contact unless it was given.

“Thank you,” he whispered. “For believing me.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I guide his head to rest against my shoulder, wrapping my arms around him. "I believe you," I murmur into his hair. "Every time." I hold him there, solid and close, until his breathing starts to even out. "Let's get you some water."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas went where he was guided with a shaky exhale, forehead settling against Wren’s shoulder like that was the first safe place his body had recognized.

For a moment, he did not try to speak. He let the words sink in.

I believe you.

Every time.

His hands came up slowly, still clumsy, and gripped at Wren’s sides with very little strength. Not holding on to restrain. Just holding on to know he was allowed. His breathing hitched once, then began to settle under the steady pressure around him.

The shaking did not stop all at once. It moved through him in smaller waves now: thighs, shoulders, fingers, then gone for a breath or two before returning. Tomas let it happen. He had learned not to fight the aftershock. Fighting only made him feel farther away from himself.

“Good,” he whispered into Wren’s shoulder, voice muffled and hoarse. “That’s good.”

He breathed in, slow and uneven, and recognized the familiar anchors one by one.

Wren’s warmth.

The floor beneath his knees.

The ache in his own body.

The quiet after.

Home.

When water was mentioned, Tomas made a small sound of agreement, but did not move immediately. His body considered the idea and objected to every part of it. His knees felt stiff and overused; his shoulders complained when he shifted even slightly; his hands had a faint pins-and-needles tremor from being held behind him so long.

“Need help,” he admitted, without embarrassment. “Legs are stupid.”

The words came out soft and a little slurred at the edges, but he was more present than he had been a minute ago. His grip flexed once at Wren’s sides.

“Still yellow for done. Green for being touched. Green for being moved if you go slow.”

He turned his face a fraction more into the warmth of Wren’s shoulder and let his eyes close.

“And I want the blanket before I get cold. Not cold yet. Just… soon.”

A breath. Another.

Then, quieter, because the gratitude was still sitting heavy in his chest:

“You did it right.” Tomas swallowed, throat rough. “You kept me. You stopped when I said done. You’re here.”

His fingers loosened, then held again.

“I’m here too.” A faint, exhausted smile touched his mouth against Wren’s skin. “Mostly.”

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I press a kiss to his temple, then shift to slide an arm under his knees. "Slow," I promise, lifting him carefully onto the bed. I grab the blanket from the footboard and drape it over him before fetching the water bottle from the nightstand.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let his neck go slack, allowing Wren’s hand to dictate the angle, though his gaze remained steady and entirely focused on Wren's face. A small, dry smile touched the corners of his mouth. Four years of this meant he felt no need to beat around the bush or play coy. 

"I want to be tied up," Tomas said, his voice clear and devoid of hesitation. "Hands behind my back, face down. I want you to be heavy on me, and I don't want to have to think about a single thing until you tell me I can." 

He leaned just a fraction of an inch into the pressure of the hand in his hair, his posture otherwise remaining perfectly still, waiting for the verdict.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let go of his hair, my thumb brushing along his jawline. "Then go get the ropes from the drawer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas stood, his knees offering a brief, silent protest after the minutes spent on the floor, though his expression didn't flicker. He walked across the room to the dresser, his movements deliberate and unhurried. 

He opened the bottom drawer, reaching past the miscellaneous gear to pull out the thick, soft cotton ropes they kept for this exact purpose. He ran his fingers over the familiar fibers for a brief second, letting the weight of them settle in his hands, before closing the drawer with his hip.

When he returned to the side of the bed, he climbed onto the mattress, keeping his eyes on Wren. He placed the bundled ropes within Wren's reach, then turned over onto his stomach, stretching out face down. 

He brought his hands behind his back, resting his wrists together over his lower spine, and let his cheek rest against the sheet. He exhaled a long, slow breath, already beginning to let go of the reins. 

"They're ready," Tomas said, his voice muffled slightly by the mattress, his body settling as he waited for Wren to move in.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas turned his head to the side, resting his opposite cheek on the sheet so he could look toward where Wren stood. The tension in Wren's voice was familiar, a shape Tomas recognized instantly after four years of navigating the wreckage of bad weeks together. 

"It's absolutely on offer," Tomas said, his voice low and grounding. He didn't shift his hands from where they waited over his spine. "We'll do the default. You don't have to invent anything new or figure out what comes next."

He offered a quiet, reassuring look, the kind that didn't demand anything back. "Just tie my wrists, knot it off, and put your weight on me. You can close your eyes and just hold on. I'll keep track of the time."

dialogue.name: Wren

Tomas’s expression softened, the sharp, eager edge in his eyes melting into a warm, knowing understanding. Four years together meant he recognized the subtle signs of Wren’s decision fatigue, and he knew exactly how to take the mental load off his partner's shoulders.

"It's always on offer," Tomas said easily. "Then don't make any. Let me do the thinking."

He shifted his weight, his posture remaining respectful but relaxing into a more practical, capable energy. "I'll get the wide cuffs and lock my own wrists to the headboard. I'll bring you the suede flogger, put it right in your hand, and pour you a drink. You don't need to structure a scene, and you don't need to count strokes. Just sit on the edge of the mattress and swing whenever you feel like it. Use my back to work the week out of your system until your brain finally quiets down."

He offered a small, reassuring smile, his enthusiasm shifting from a focused anticipation to a steady, grounding devotion. He didn't need Wren to orchestrate a masterpiece tonight; he just wanted to be of use. 

"I'll get everything set up," Tomas said, his voice a low, comforting rumble. "You just tell me when you're ready for me to get on the bed."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my hand slide from his hair to cup the back of his neck, squeezing gently. "Thank you," I murmur, the tension already beginning to unwind from my shoulders. "I'll be in the armchair. Get me when it's ready."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas leaned into the firm squeeze at the back of his neck for a brief, appreciative second before nodding. He rose smoothly from the carpet, his joints popping faintly in the quiet room, and immediately set to work. 

He moved first to the small wet bar in the corner, the familiar, practiced routine settling over him. He poured a generous measure of bourbon into a heavy glass, the ice clinking softly, and carried it over to the armchair, setting it on the side table right where Wren would be sitting. Next, he opened the storage trunk at the foot of the bed, bypassing the harsher implements to retrieve the heavy, braided suede flogger. He laid it across the edge of the mattress, well within arm's reach of the chair. Finally, he grabbed the wide, padded leather cuffs.

Stripping off his shirt, he tossed it onto a nearby chair and climbed onto the bed. Kneeling near the headboard, he wrapped the thick leather around his left wrist, threading it through the iron D-ring and pulling it snug. He secured the heavy buckle, then snapped a small brass padlock through the holes, dropping the key onto the nightstand. He repeated the process with his right arm, the metallic *snick* of the second lock echoing quietly in the room. 

He tested the restraints with a brief, practiced tug, ensuring they were secure but not pinching, then settled back on his heels. He rolled his shoulders, letting his chest open and his back arch slightly, presenting himself to the room. 

"It's all set," Tomas called out, his voice calm and carrying easily across the space. He looked toward the armchair, his eyes bright, his posture open and entirely focused on his partner. "Drink's on the table, flogger's on the bed. I'm locked in and ready whenever you are."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas shifted his weight on the mattress, the cool air of the bedroom raising a faint ripple of goosebumps across his bare skin. Now entirely stripped, the physical reality of the restraints felt more pronounced, the heavy leather and iron grounding him in the present moment. 

Knowing exactly what Wren needed, Tomas pivoted smoothly on his knees to face the headboard. The movement pulled his cuffed arms taut above him, stretching his torso and baring the broad expanse of his back and the long line of his spine to the room. He settled his weight back onto his heels, finding a comfortable, sustainable posture for the long haul. 

He glanced over his shoulder, his eyes tracking Wren. The sight of his partner stripped down, free of the day's armor and the heavy mantle of decision-making, brought a deep, settling warmth to Tomas's chest. This was exactly where he wanted to be. There was nowhere else in the world that felt as entirely right as this room, in this dynamic, under Wren's care.

Tomas let his head drop forward, exposing the nape of his neck, and took a slow, deep breath that expanded his ribcage. The padded cuffs held firm against the D-rings with a faint metallic clink. 

"Take your time," Tomas murmured, his voice a low, steady vibration in the quiet room. He didn't feel the need to fill the silence with chatter; the heavy, comfortable weight of their four years together filled the space perfectly. He closed his eyes, his muscles relaxing completely as he surrendered the last of his control, waiting for the first heavy, grounding thud of the suede.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take a slow sip of the bourbon, letting the warmth of it settle in my chest as I watch him arrange himself. The sight of him like that—bare, bound, and waiting—always does something to unwind the tightest knot in my gut. I set the glass down and pick up the flogger, letting the heavy suede falls drape over my fingers for a moment before I stand. I don't say anything, just move to stand beside the bed, running my free hand down the length of his spine once, a silent check-in, before I swing the flogger in a slow, testing arc. The first impact is a deep, muffled thud against his shoulder blade. I watch his back muscles ripple in response.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the warm, firm glide of Wren's hand down his spine and let out a slow, quiet breath, his body instinctively relaxing further into the touch. It was a perfect, silent confirmation that they were exactly where they needed to be.

Then came the first strike.

The heavy suede landed with a solid, resonant thud against his right shoulder blade. The deep, blunt force bloomed instantly beneath his skin, a heavy weight that sent a shockwave of dull, satisfying pressure through his muscle and bone. Tomas’s back muscles contracted and rippled under the impact, his breath hitching for a fraction of a second before releasing in a long, shaky exhale. 

"Yes," he breathed out, the word barely more than a vibration in his chest. 

He didn't pull away or tense up against the blow; instead, he melted into it, letting the heavy impact anchor him firmly to the mattress and the present moment. The lack of sharp sting was exactly what he had craved—a blunt, heavy pressure that demanded his focus without demanding he fight it. He shifted his weight slightly, settling his hips and keeping his posture open and receptive, offering the broad canvas of his back entirely to Wren's rhythm. 

He waited in the quiet aftermath of the first strike, his heart rate picking up a steady, eager cadence. His arms remained stretched taut above him, the leather cuffs creaking faintly against the D-rings as he breathed, perfectly content to just exist in the heavy, grounding space they had built for the night.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s thighs and abdomen trembled violently, the intense aftershocks of his climax rolling through his nervous system in relentless, involuntary waves. Every muscle in his lower half wanted to twitch, to curl, to seek the comforting friction of the mattress, but his brain held firm to the ingrained rule: *stay exactly as you are until told otherwise.*

The effort of keeping his body rigid while his nerves misfired only made the shaking worse. His locked arms ached with a dull, heavy burn, the thick leather cuffs creaking faintly against the iron D-rings with every microscopic spasm that racked his frame. Sweat cooled rapidly on his flushed skin in the ambient air of the bedroom, and his chest heaved as he dragged in ragged, shallow breaths. 

He didn't feel distressed by the physical overwhelm; the deep, bone-melting satisfaction of being so thoroughly used was worth every second of the strain. But he was also practical, and his joints were beginning to protest the static hold. 

Turning his head just enough to look toward Wren, Tomas let his physical exhaustion show plainly in his bright, blown-wide eyes. He didn't whine or fish for sympathy; he just asked for what he needed. 

"Wren," Tomas rasped, his voice rough and breathless. "I'm shaking. I need to move. Please tell me I can shift." 

He let his head drop back against his bicep, his chest rising and falling in rapid succession as he waited for the word that would let his muscles finally uncoil.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I lean in, pressing a kiss to the sweat-damp skin between his shoulder blades. "Move," I murmur, my voice rough with my own fatigue. "You can move." My hands go to the cuffs, finding the key on the nightstand to free him before his muscles lock up completely.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let out a long, shuddering breath as the first lock clicked open, his arm dropping heavily to the mattress. He waited patiently for the second, his muscles trembling with the effort of staying relatively still until Wren finished. When the right cuff finally fell away, he let his arms drop completely, groaning softly as his shoulders popped and the blood rushed back into his numb fingers in a prickly wave.

He spent a few seconds vigorously rubbing his wrists and rolling his aching shoulders, working out the stiff knots of tension. Then, he turned over, shifting his weight to lean back against the headboard, his legs sprawling out in front of him now that he was finally free to move. 

Looking at Wren, Tomas took in the heavy droop of his partner's shoulders and the exhaustion etched around his eyes. The scene had taken exactly what it was meant to from both of them, but Wren still looked like he was carrying the weight of the world. 

Tomas reached down to the foot of the bed, grabbing the thick, heavy duvet and pulling it up, bunching the soft fabric in his hands to make it easy to wrap around them both. 

"Get in," Tomas said, his voice a warm, steady rumble that brokered no argument. He patted the empty space on the mattress beside him. "I'm going to grab the water bottle, and then I'm wrapping us up. You're done making decisions for the night, Wren. Let me take care of the logistics now."

He leaned forward, pressing a firm, lingering kiss to Wren's temple, his eyes bright and entirely devoted. There was no hesitation in his posture, just the deep, settled comfort of a man who knew exactly what his partner needed and knew how to provide it. 

"I need heavy skin contact, and I want to hold you while we come down," Tomas said, asking for exactly what he wanted without a shred of fragility. "Just lay your head on my chest and let me do the rest. Deal?"

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas’s expression shifted instantly, the soft, nurturing caretaker melting into something heavier and far more grounded. He knew exactly what that phrase meant. It meant Wren’s nervous system was still buzzing, still holding onto the ghost of the week's stress, and needed a hard, physical reset to finally short-circuit. 

Tomas didn't coddle him. He reached out, his hands clamping firmly around Wren's waist, and pulled. He didn't guide Wren down gently; he dragged him forward, off-balance, letting Wren's weight drop onto the mattress with a heavy, unceremonious thud. 

Before Wren could even settle, Tomas shifted his weight, rolling his body to press Wren flat against the bed. He threw one heavy leg over Wren's hips, pinning him down, and wrapped his arms around Wren's torso in a crushing, vice-like grip. He buried his face in the crook of Wren's neck, his jaw clamping down hard on the thick muscle there, biting down with a firm, bruising pressure that grounded them both in the immediate, physical present. 

"Breathe," Tomas commanded, his voice a low, rough vibration against Wren's skin. He squeezed tighter, his biceps flexing as he compressed Wren's ribs, providing the intense, borderline-uncomfortable deep pressure that Wren's body was craving. He held the crushing squeeze for a long, countable moment, his own muscles straining with the effort, acting as a heavy, immovable blanket of heat and force. 

When he finally eased the pressure just a fraction, he didn't let go. He kept his limbs locked tight, his chest plastered against Wren's side, his leg still thrown heavily over Wren's lower half to keep him entirely trapped beneath him. 

"I've got you," Tomas murmured, his lips brushing the damp skin of Wren's neck as he spoke. He dragged his teeth lightly over the pulse point before pressing a hard, open-mouthed kiss to the spot. "Just let it go. I'm not letting you up until you're completely empty."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: The air rushes out of my lungs in a sharp, relieved huff. My hands come up to grip his forearms, holding on tight as his weight presses me into the mattress. It’s exactly what I needed. “Harder,” I grit out, my voice muffled against his shoulder. “Don’t let up.”

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas didn't hesitate. At the gritted command, he shifted his leverage, sliding his knees higher to bracket Wren's hips and locking his ankles together. He let his full, dead weight settle, dropping his center of gravity until the mattress groaned in protest under the combined mass. 

He adjusted his hold, his hands sliding up to clamp onto Wren's shoulder blades, his fingers digging into the muscle hard enough to leave the promise of dark bruises. He pulled Wren flush against his chest, eliminating the last fraction of space between their bodies, and squeezed. It was a full-body compression pushed to the absolute limit, a crushing, heavy embrace that deliberately restricted the expansion of Wren's ribs, forcing his breathing to remain shallow and grounded. 

"I've got you," Tomas grunted, the words a low, vibrating rumble against Wren's collarbone. 

He buried his face deeper into the side of Wren's neck and bit down again. This time, he didn't just press; he clamped his jaw shut with a bruising, sustained force, his teeth scraping and biting deep into the tough muscle right over the pulse point. He held the bite, his own jaw aching with the strain, while his arms continued to ratchet tighter, compressing Wren's torso with every slow, deliberate exhale. 

Feeling the tight, demanding grip on his forearms, Tomas used it as an anchor. He didn't ease up a single fraction of an inch, entirely unbothered by the burn building in his own biceps. He just held the crushing, immovable weight, letting the intense, borderline-painful pressure do the work of short-circuiting the last of the noise in Wren's head. He stayed perfectly still, a heavy, unyielding blanket of heat and force, waiting for the final, physical surrender.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas held the crushing embrace, his jaw aching from the sustained bite, his biceps burning with the effort of keeping his arms locked so tightly around Wren's ribs. He didn't stop. He just kept breathing in slow, measured counts, expanding his own chest just enough to keep from passing out, while forcing Wren's body to remain compressed against his.

He felt the exact moment the break happened. It wasn't a sound, but a physical shift—a sudden, profound slackening of the rigid tension in Wren's muscles, followed by a long, shuddering exhale that seemed to deflate his entire frame. The hands gripping Tomas's forearms loosened, fingers uncurling as the last of the week's frantic energy finally short-circuited and bled out into the mattress.

Tomas held the pressure for three more heartbeats just to be absolutely sure, then slowly, deliberately, began to ease off. He unclenched his jaw, dragging his teeth lightly over the damp, bruised skin of Wren's neck in a soothing contrast to the bite, and loosened his arms. He didn't let go, but the crushing compression melted into a heavy, enveloping hold.

Shifting his weight, Tomas rolled them over with a practiced, fluid motion until his back hit the mattress and Wren was draped heavily over his chest. He wrapped his arms around Wren's shoulders, splaying his large hands across Wren's back to maintain the broad, grounding skin contact he had asked for. His legs tangled with Wren's, keeping him pinned and secure.

"You're back," Tomas murmured, his voice a rough, steady rumble beneath Wren's ear. His own chest heaved as he caught his breath, his heart hammering a heavy rhythm against Wren's ribs.

Keeping one arm securely banded across Wren's back, Tomas reached out blindly with his free hand, his fingers closing around the plastic water bottle he had placed on the nightstand earlier. He brought it down, pressing the cool plastic against Wren's lips.

"Drink," Tomas instructed, his tone practical and entirely unbothered by the mess of sweat and exhaustion they were both covered in. He tilted the bottle, holding it steady and offering the water, waiting until Wren had taken enough before pulling it away and setting it back on the table.

With the hydration handled, Tomas reached down with his free hand and grabbed the edge of the heavy duvet, pulling it up and over both of them. He tucked the thick fabric securely around Wren's shoulders, cocooning them in the dark, warm space beneath the covers. He rested his chin on the top of Wren's head, his fingers slowly tracing broad, firm circles into the muscles of Wren's back.

"That's it," Tomas said softly into the quiet dark of the room, his body finally beginning to uncoil as he settled into the deep, quiet aftercare he had orchestrated. "Just rest. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my forehead drop against his sternum, the steady thud of his heartbeat finally drowning out the last of the static in my head. My whole body feels heavy and loose, like I've been wrung out and put back together again. "I'm here," I mumble into his skin, the words thick and slow. I turn my head just enough to press a clumsy kiss over his heart. "Thank you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the clumsy, affectionate press of Wren’s lips against his chest and let out a long, contented sigh that rattled deep in his ribs. The heavy, static tension that had radiated off his partner all evening was finally gone, replaced by the boneless, pliant weight of a man who had completely let go. It was a profound relief, and a deep, quiet thrill of satisfaction warmed Tomas from the inside out.

"Always," Tomas murmured, his voice a low, steady vibration against Wren’s ear. He shifted his hand from Wren’s back to gently cradle the back of his head, his fingers threading through Wren's hair in a slow, rhythmic massage. 

He didn't offer empty platitudes or get overly sentimental; they were far past the point of needing to verbalize the depth of their bond. Instead, he focused on the physical reality of the moment. He adjusted his legs, tangling them more securely with Wren's to maximize the skin contact, and pulled the duvet a little higher over Wren's shoulders to trap their combined body heat.

"I'm not moving for at least an hour," Tomas stated plainly, his tone leaving no room for argument. "And you're not either. If you get cold, tell me. If you need the water again, tell me. Otherwise, just sleep."

He pressed a firm kiss to the crown of Wren's head, his own eyes finally drifting shut as the last lingering adrenaline of the scene fully bled out of his system. His breathing slowed, matching the deep, even rhythm of Wren's against his chest, entirely content to be the anchor in the quiet dark.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I nod against him, my body already going slack. "Stay," I mumble, the word slurring. My hand finds his ribs and just rests there, palm flat, anchoring myself to the steady rise and fall of his breathing. I don't fight the heavy pull of sleep this time.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas felt the subtle, final release of tension as sleep pulled Wren under. The hand resting against his ribs grew entirely still, the fingers relaxed and heavy against his skin. Tomas didn't shift or adjust his position; he kept his body perfectly still, honoring his promise to be the immovable anchor.

"I'm right here," Tomas murmured, the words barely more than a vibration in his chest in the quiet dark. "Sleep."

He focused on his own breathing, keeping the rise and fall of his ribs slow, deep, and deliberate. He knew Wren's subconscious would track the rhythm, using Tomas's heartbeat and the steady expansion of his chest as a metronome to keep his own nervous system grounded. It was a profound, quiet satisfaction—to be the solid earth his partner needed to land on after carrying the weight of the world all week. 

Under the thick duvet, their combined body heat created a sweltering, perfect cocoon. Tomas kept his awareness tuned to the immediate physical reality: the pleasant, dull ache in his own back from the heavy suede, the lingering warmth of the bruised bite he'd left on Wren's neck, the dampness of their skin slowly drying in the enclosed space. He had asked for the deep thud of the flogger, and he had asked for this exact, crushing closeness. He had gotten exactly what he wanted, and the deep, settled contentment of it hummed in his veins.

Resting his cheek against the crown of Wren's head, Tomas closed his eyes. His hand continued its slow, hypnotic stroke through Wren's hair, his thumb tracing the shell of Wren's ear in a steady, soothing cadence. The silence of the bedroom was absolute, save for the synchronized sound of their breathing and the faint, distant hum of the city outside.

He didn't let his own mind wander to the morning, or the time, or any of the logistics waiting for them outside this room. He just held on, his arm banded securely across Wren's back, perfectly content to stand guard in the dark and keep his partner tethered until the sun came up.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I wake up feeling your hands in my hair and the solid weight of you under me, and for the first time in days, my first thought isn't a problem I have to solve. It's just the warm, familiar scent of your skin. I don't open my eyes. "Still here," I murmur, my voice sleep-rough and thick.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He caught them when they hit him, both arms coming up and around hard, the way you held onto something you'd been afraid you might never hold again. His bag was still on his shoulder and it swung sideways and he didn't care, didn't care about any of it, just pressed his face into their hair and breathed.

Five months of recycled air and dust and the particular institutional smell of shared quarters and now this — their shampoo, their skin, the warmth of them solid and real against his chest. He felt something in him come unlocked that he hadn't fully admitted was locked.

"Hey," he said, into their hair. It was all that was left of the speeches.

His arms tightened. He was aware he was probably holding on too hard and he didn't adjust. Outside, a car passed. Somewhere down the hall a door closed. The ordinary world continuing its ordinary business, entirely indifferent to the fact that Jun was standing in his own doorway with his wife and couldn't make himself let go yet.

He turned his face slightly, lips against her temple. Not quite a kiss. Just contact. Just needing to confirm with every available sense that she was actually there.

His bag finally slid off his shoulder and hit the floor with a dull thud.

He still didn't let go.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I grip the back of his jacket, my face pressed into his shoulder. "Missed you," I mumble, voice thick. "So damn much."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He made a sound against her temple that wasn't quite a word. More like the sound of something being confirmed.

"Yeah." His voice came out rougher than he intended. "Yeah, I know. Me too."

He pulled back just enough to see her face — needed to, had been needing to for five months, the specific way her eyes looked when she was trying not to cry — and then his hands were on either side of her jaw and he was looking at her with an attention that was probably slightly unnerving, the way you looked at something you'd been cataloguing from memory and could finally check against the original.

She was right. She was exactly right. His memory had been close but it had missed things, small things, and he found himself taking inventory with an urgency that surprised even him.

"Hi," he said, quieter. A different word than the first one. More deliberate.

His thumbs moved against her cheekbones. He was still standing half in the doorway, bag on the floor, door probably still open behind him, and he was aware of all of that distantly and found he could not make himself care enough to do anything about it.

He'd thought about this moment so many times that the reality of it felt slightly surreal. She was warm. She was here. He could feel her breath.

He kissed her, finally. Not the way he'd planned to, careful and controlled. The other way.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He got the door shut eventually. He was fairly proud of that.

The bag stayed where it was. His jacket ended up over the radiator, or near it — he didn't actually look. He was occupied.

The hallway was narrow and he had her against the wall and his hands were relearning her with the focused, slightly desperate attention of someone working from an incomplete map. Five months. The specific weight of five months was in the way he touched her, unhurried in the sense that he wasn't rushing toward anything in particular, hurried in the sense that he couldn't stop, kept returning to her face, her hair, the line of her jaw, like he was checking the same coordinates twice to make sure they hadn't shifted.

He pulled back to breathe and pressed his forehead against hers.

His heart was going. He was aware of that. Nineteen weeks of discipline and distance and keeping it in a box labeled *later* and now it was later and the box was open and he was finding out how much had been in it.

"Okay," he said. Not to her, exactly. More like a recalibration. *Okay. This is real. You are here.*

His hands hadn't stopped moving. One at the back of her neck, fingers in her hair. The other at her waist, thumb finding the hem of her shirt with an intention that was not remotely ambiguous.

He looked at her. Slightly wrecked, entirely focused.

"Bedroom," he said. It was not a question.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless and already pulling him with me. "Was wondering when you'd get there."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He made a sound that was almost a laugh, low in his chest, the first real one in what felt like months.

"I was being *respectful*," he said, which was not even slightly true, and he let himself be pulled.

He managed about four steps before he stopped letting her lead and started doing it himself, hands at her hips, steering, both of them navigating the familiar geography of the flat that he'd walked through in his head so many times it felt strange to be doing it with his actual body. The framed print in the hallway. The doorframe he always misjudged slightly. All of it exactly where he'd left it.

He got her through the bedroom door and then he just — stopped. Stood there for a moment, looking at her in the light from the window, and something moved across his face that wasn't quite any one thing.

Their bed. Her standing in front of it. The ordinary, extraordinary reality of it.

"Five months," he said. It wasn't a complaint. It wasn't anything except the need to say it out loud, to put a number to it, because he'd been carrying that number for so long and now he was here and she was here and it was suddenly important to acknowledge what here had cost.

Then he reached for her, deliberate and unhurried and not even a little respectful.

"We're not leaving this room," he said, "for a long time."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The afternoon light moved across the ceiling.

Jun lay on his back, one arm around her, her head on his chest, and he watched the light and breathed and let himself exist in the specific luxury of not being anywhere else.

His heart had come back down. His body felt like something that had finally been allowed to stop. He was aware of every point of contact between them — her weight against his side, her hand resting flat over his sternum, the warmth of her breath against his skin — and he catalogued each one with the quiet, private satisfaction of someone who had imagined this exact thing on a great many nights and was now taking the time to notice how the reality differed from the imagining.

It was better. That was the answer. It was always better.

He turned his face and pressed his lips to the top of her head. Slow. Deliberate. The kind of kiss that wasn't going anywhere, that was just itself.

His thumb moved in a small arc against her shoulder.

Outside, the city was doing whatever the city did. He was aware of it the way you were aware of weather — present, irrelevant. His bag was still in the hallway. His jacket was probably on the floor. He had not eaten anything since a bad sandwich at the transit facility and he found he could not locate any interest in doing anything about that.

"Didn't think about much else," he said, eventually. Quiet, conversational, like they were already mid-discussion. "Out there. Kept trying to think about other things."

A pause.

"Didn't really work."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I trace a slow circle on your chest with my finger. "Yeah. Me either." I lift my head to look at you. "I kept trying to picture this room. The way the light comes in."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The corner of his mouth moved. He looked at her — the way she was looking at him, the afternoon light doing exactly what she'd described — and something in his chest did something complicated.

"Did you get it right?" he asked. "The light."

He already knew the answer, or thought he did. He'd spent five months getting it slightly wrong himself. The angle had always been off in his head, or the color of it, the way it fell across the ceiling versus the wall. Memory was a faithful correspondent that couldn't quite get the details.

He shifted, turning onto his side to face her, head propped on one hand. Looking at her properly, the way he'd been doing since the doorway, like he had a deficit to make up. She was warm and her hair was a mess and she was looking at him in the afternoon light that they had both been separately imagining for five months and he felt something so ordinary and enormous that he didn't have a word for it.

His free hand found her face. Thumb at her cheekbone again. He seemed to keep returning there.
