dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The hallway wall was cool against his shoulder blades at some point—he didn't remember when they'd shifted, only that Halle had pressed him there and he'd let them, grateful for the solid support because his knees felt less than reliable. His hands had mapped the familiar geography of Halle's back, their sides, the nape of their neck where the hair was softer. Relearning. Confirming.

His uniform jacket was halfway unbuttoned. He didn't remember doing that either.

"Bed," he managed between kisses, the word more grunt than speech. It wasn't a suggestion so much as a direction, except his body seemed uninterested in following it. Every time he thought about moving, Halle did something—tugged his lower lip, pressed closer, made a sound against his mouth—and he forgot again.

Five months. Five months of cold showers and colder sleeps and nothing, *nothing*, that felt like this.

His thumb found the strip of skin where Halle's shirt had ridden up. Just that small contact—warm, soft, *real*—made him groan into their mouth like he was dying.

"Seriously." He panted the word against their jaw, kissing a path to their ear. "Bed. Before I—" He didn't finish. Couldn't. His hand slid lower, palm flattening against the curve of their hip, and his brain whited out briefly.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh into your ear, breathless. "You're not moving." I nip your earlobe, then grab your hand. *"Come on."*

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun went. He'd have followed Halle anywhere right then—into fire, off a cliff, certainly the fifteen feet to their bedroom. His fingers threaded tight through theirs, and he let himself be pulled, let himself be led, because the alternative was standing in the hallway until his legs gave out.

The bedroom door was open. He didn't look at it. He looked at Halle—the line of their shoulders, the back of their neck, the way their hair fell. Details he'd tried to hold onto through static-garbled calls and frozen screens. Details that didn't do the real thing justice.

The back of his knees hit the mattress and he sat down hard, pulling Halle with him. His hands found their hips, steadying, anchoring, and he pressed his forehead against their stomach just to breathe for a second. Just to feel them standing between his knees, solid and present and *here*.

"Five months," he said against the fabric of their shirt, and it came out like an accusation, like a prayer, like something he couldn't contain. His fingers curled into the back of their waistband. "Five fucking months thinking about you. About this."

He tilted his head up to look at them, and his eyes were dark, desperate, honest in a way that satellite connections never allowed.

"I'm not going slow." It wasn't a question. "I can't. I *need*—"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Later, Jun wouldn't be able to recall the specific order of events—only sensation, only fragments. The rasp of fabric, the heat of skin finally against skin, the way his own breathing sounded jagged and foreign in his ears. The soft sound Halle made when he pulled them down onto the mattress with him. The way the sheets smelled like home, like *them*, like something he'd ached for in a narrow rack surrounded by the hum of the ship.

He wasn't gentle. He couldn't be. Five months of wanting had wound him tight as a spring, and every touch from Halle's hands unwound him further, left him shaking, desperate, saying their name like a litany against their throat, their shoulder, the soft inside of their wrist.

Afterwards—when his heart had slowed from its frantic hammering and his limbs felt heavy and loose in a way they hadn't in months—he pulled Halle against his chest. His arm locked around them. Possessive. Grateful. Still a little disbelieving.

"Don't move," he mumbled against their hair. His voice was wrecked. "Just—stay. Stay right here."

His thumb traced absent patterns on their shoulder. Outside, the city sounds filtered through the window—cars, voices, the ordinary noise of a world that had kept turning while he was gone. Inside, there was just this. Just them.

"I kept your voicemail," he said quietly, into the stillness. "The one from week eleven. When you said—" His voice caught. Swallowed. "Played it every night."

His arm tightened.

"I'm not doing that again. Five months. I'm not—I can't—"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I press my face into your neck, breathing you in. "Good. Because I'm not letting you go again." My voice is muffled against your skin. I hook a leg over yours, anchoring us together.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's breath caught—a sharp, involuntary thing that he couldn't have hidden even if he'd tried. His arm around Halle tightened, and he pressed his lips to the top of their head, not quite a kiss, just... contact. Just proof.

"You couldn't get rid of me if you tried," he said, and the words came out lighter than he expected, undercut with an exhaustion that was more emotional than physical. His free hand found theirs where it rested against his chest, lacing their fingers together, pressing their joined knuckles against his sternum like he could keep them there permanently.

He was quiet for a moment. The radiator clicked on—familiar, domestic, absurdly wonderful—and outside someone's car alarm went off and then cut off. Normal sounds. Home sounds.

"I used to count the days," he admitted, voice low. "Had this app. Little X marks on the calendar. Toward the end I was checking it every hour like some kind of—" He huffed a laugh against their hair. "Like it would make it go faster. It didn't."

His thumb traced the ridge of their knuckles. Back and forth. Soothing himself as much as them.

"I thought about what I'd say. When I got back." A pause. "Had whole speeches planned. Practiced them. And then you opened the door and I forgot every single word."

He shifted just enough to press his lips to their temple. Soft. Reverent.

"Still don't have any. Words, I mean." Another pause, longer this time. "Just—this. You. Us."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had spent five months imagining this—had constructed elaborate scenarios in the rack at 0200, had thought about it in the shower, had visualized it so many times the fantasy had worn smooth with handling. None of it compared to the reality.

Halle's hands on him weren't fantasy-neat. They were deliberate, slow, devastating in a way that made his breath stutter and his fingers twist in the sheets. Every point of contact flared hot, like his skin had been waiting—five months of dormancy, and now every nerve ending remembered exactly how to feel.

He couldn't stay quiet. He'd never been particularly good at it, but now—now it was like five months of silence poured out of him in fragments. Sounds he didn't quite recognize as his own. Halle's name, broken into syllables. Words that didn't quite form. A moan that he'd have been mortified about if he had any capacity for embarrassment left.

His hand found the back of Halle's head—not directing, just needing to touch, needing to feel them there. His back arched off the mattress without his permission, offering himself up, and he didn't even care how desperate he looked. How desperate he *was*.

"Please—" The word escaped him, rough and raw. "Please, I can't—"

He didn't know what he was asking for. More. Everything. Slower, faster. He didn't know. His thoughts had scattered like startled birds, leaving only sensation and the overwhelming, crushing *relief* of being touched by someone who knew him, who wanted him, who'd waited for him.

His eyes stung. He closed them tight.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I slow down, cupping your face. "Hey. Look at me." My thumb brushes your cheek. "You're here. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun opened his eyes.

Halle's face swam above him—soft, focused, real. The bedroom light caught the familiar angles of their features, and something in his chest cracked open a little wider. His breath was still unsteady, his pulse still racing, but the frantic edge had softened into something more tender. More terrifying.

"I know," he said, and his voice came out wrecked. Hoarser than he'd ever heard it. He turned his head just enough to press his lips to Halle's palm where it cradled his cheek—a kiss that was more gratitude than heat. "I know. I just—"

He stopped. Swallowed. His throat worked around words that wouldn't come, and his eyes were wet now, he could feel it, could feel the dampness gathering at the corners despite his best efforts.

"It's a lot," he managed finally. "Being back. Being—" His hand came up to cover Halle's on his face, holding it there. "You. All of you. All at once."

A laugh escaped him, watery and strange. He blinked, and a tear slipped free, tracking down toward his temple. He didn't wipe it away.

"I'm not sad," he said quickly, because they needed to know that. "I'm not—it's just. Five months. And now you're here and I can touch you and it's—" His voice cracked. "It's a lot."

He pulled in a shaky breath. Let it out slowly.

"Don't stop. Please. I just—" His thumb stroked over Halle's knuckles. "I just needed to see you. Needed to know you were really here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The words hit him like a match to dry kindling.

Something in Jun's expression shifted—the tenderness didn't vanish, exactly, but it got swallowed by something hungrier. Older. Five months of wanting crystallized into a single, sharp point of intent.

"Gentle," he repeated, and the word came out rough, almost mocking. His hand slid from Halle's cheek to the back of their neck, gripping—not cruel, but firm. Certain. "You want me to—"

He didn't finish the sentence. He showed them.

Jun pulled them down into a kiss that was nothing like the ones before. Those had been desperate, scattered, grateful. This one was *deliberate*. He bit at Halle's lower lip, then soothed it with his tongue, then bit again. His other hand found their hip, fingers digging in hard enough to leave marks—marks they'd see tomorrow, marks they'd feel every time they moved.

"Tomorrow," he echoed against their mouth, and there was a promise in it. A threat. Both. "You'll feel me tomorrow. Every time you sit down. Every time you—*fuck*—"

He flipped them. Or tried to—the motion was more clumsy than graceful, all urgency and no finesse, but he got Halle beneath him and that was what mattered. He planted his hands on either side of their head, breathing hard, and stared down at them like he was cataloging every detail for later.

"You don't know—" His voice was ragged. "—what you're asking for. Nineteen weeks. I've had nineteen weeks to think about this. About what I'd do when I got back."

His knee pressed between their thighs, parting them, and he leaned down to drag his teeth along the column of their throat.

"I'm going to ruin you." Not a question. Not a threat. Just fact, delivered against their pulse point like a secret.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I arch up against you, a sharp gasp turning into a low laugh. "Prove it." My hands slide down your back, nails digging in. "Don't hold back."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a sound—low, raw, almost feral—and that was the last coherent thing before instinct took over.

He didn't hold back. Couldn't have if he tried. Nineteen weeks of restraint shattered like glass, and every fantasy he'd constructed in the dark paled against the reality of Halle beneath him, around him, meeting him thrust for thrust with a ferocity that made his vision blur.

His hands left marks. He could feel himself doing it—gripping too hard, moving too fast—but Halle's nails were raking down his back and their voice was breaking on his name and every rough demand for *more, harder, don't stop* only fed the fire. He gave them everything. Took everything in return.

The headboard hit the wall. Neither of them cared.

He lost track of time—lost track of everything except the heat and the friction and the sounds Halle made when he found the angle that made them arch off the mattress. He did it again. Again. Watched them fall apart and felt something savage and satisfied curl in his chest at the sight.

"*Mine,*" he growled against their throat, and it wasn't a question. His hips snapped forward, punctuating the word. "You're—*fuck*—you're mine."

After, when the world stopped spinning and his arms stopped shaking enough to hold him up, Jun collapsed beside Halle rather than on them. His chest heaved. Sweat cooled on his skin. Every muscle in his back screamed from the scratches they'd left, and he felt them with a distant, satisfied awareness.

He reached out blindly, found Halle's hand, and held on like letting go would kill him.

"Ruin you," he mumbled into the pillow, voice wrecked. "Told you."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun heard them—heard himself—through the thin walls of the apartment and couldn't bring himself to care. Let the neighbors know. Let the whole building know. Five months of silence and self-restraint and now he couldn't stop the sounds spilling out of him any more than he could stop breathing.

"Don't stop," Halle said, and Jun laughed—breathless, disbelieving, *wrecked*—because stopping wasn't even on the table. Wasn't in the same universe as the table.

"Wasn't planning on it," he managed, and his voice was ruined, hoarse in a way it hadn't been since the last deployment, since the time before that.

He pulled Halle closer—impossible, necessary—and started again. Slower this time, but no less intense. Deliberate. Every thrust a statement. Every kiss a claim. He watched their face, watched the way their expression fractured when he found the right angle, the right rhythm. Cataloged every reaction like intelligence data, like something he could carry back to the cold rack and the hum of the ship.

But he wouldn't have to. That was the thing. He was *here*. They were here. And tomorrow he'd wake up next to them and the day after that and the day after that and—

His rhythm stuttered. Emotion surged up his throat like a tide, and he buried his face against Halle's neck to hide it, to muffle the sound that escaped, something between a groan and something else entirely.

"Missed you," he said again, the words muffled against their skin. "Missed you, missed you, *fuck*—"

His hips rolled, deep and grinding, and he felt Halle clench around him and his brain whited out again.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I drag my fingers through your hair, pulling just enough to make you look at me. "I'm not going anywhere." My voice is wrecked too. "*Never again.*"

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The words hit him somewhere vital—somewhere he'd been guarding without realizing it, somewhere that had calcified over nineteen weeks of distance and doubt and 0300 what-ifs.

Jun's breath hitched. His hips stilled, buried deep, and for a moment he just *looked* at them. Halle beneath him, wrecked and beautiful, their fingers in his hair, their voice broken on a promise that sounded like a vow.

"Never," he repeated, and it came out cracked. Fractured. His hand found their face again—couldn't stop touching it, couldn't stop needing that contact—and his thumb traced the line of their cheekbone like he was memorizing it. Again. Still.

"You don't—" He stopped. Swallowed. Started again. "You can't promise that. The deployments—"

But Halle's hand was in his hair and their eyes were on his and the words died in his throat because right now, in this moment, with their body warm around him and their breath mingling with his, *never* felt possible. Felt real.

He kissed them. Softer than before, but no less consuming—a kiss that said things he couldn't articulate, that pressed all the words he'd never been good at into their lips like a translation.

Then he started moving again. Slow. Deliberate. Every roll of his hips a punctuation mark, every thrust a sentence.

"I'm holding you to that," he murmured against their mouth. "When I wake up tomorrow. And the day after. And—*ah*—and every day after that."

His forehead dropped to theirs. His rhythm deepened, grinding, relentless.

"Never again. You said it. You're *mine*."

His voice broke on the last word.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I bite your shoulder to muffle the sound when I come, then sink my teeth into the muscle until I taste salt. My arms lock around you, keeping you there. "Yours," I rasp against your skin. "Always."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bite sent lightning down his spine.

Jun gasped—sharp, startled, *undone*—and the sensation of Halle clenching around him combined with the bright pain of their teeth in his shoulder shattered what was left of his control. His hips jerked once, twice, and then he was falling, spilling into them with a sound that was closer to a sob than a moan.

"*Halle*—"

Their name broke apart in his mouth. His arms gave out and he collapsed against them, full weight, unable to hold himself up anymore. His face pressed into the curve of their neck and shoulder, the same spot they'd just bitten, and he could feel his own pulse hammering against their skin. Or maybe that was their pulse. Impossible to tell where he ended and they began.

"Always," he echoed, the word muffled, wrecked. His hand found theirs and laced their fingers together, pressing their joined hands into the mattress beside their head. "Always, always—*fuck*—"

His body was still shaking. Small tremors he couldn't control, couldn't stop. The aftermath of five months of wanting and ninety minutes of desperation and the overwhelming, crushing *relief* of being exactly where he belonged.

He turned his head, pressed an open-mouthed kiss to the bite mark they'd left on his shoulder. Then another, softer, to the curve of their neck.

"Don't let go," he said again—a refrain, a prayer, the only words that seemed to make sense anymore. "Just—stay. Stay like this."

His voice was destroyed. He didn't care.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't. My grip stays tight, my leg still hooked over yours. "Wasn't planning on it." I press my lips to your temple, breathing you in until my heart slows.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't wait for the bag to finish hitting the floor. He met Halle halfway, or maybe less than halfway—he wasn't counting, wasn't capable of counting anything just then—and got both hands on Halle's face like he needed to confirm it was real, like nineteen weeks of a photo taped inside a locker hadn't been enough and this was the only version that counted.

The first kiss landed off-center. He didn't care. He fixed it, dragged Halle in by the back of the neck and got it right the second time, and then didn't let go long enough for a third to be a separate event.

"Hi," he said against Halle's mouth, which was a stupid thing to say and about the last coherent word he had budgeted for. His hands were already moving—shoulders, ribs, the dip of Halle's waist he'd thought about at genuinely inappropriate times over the last five months. "God. Okay. You're—" 

He gave up on the sentence. He kicked the door shut behind them without looking, walked Halle backward a step, kissed the corner of his jaw, the side of his throat, anywhere he could reach that wasn't currently occupied.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My hands find his hair, tugging just hard enough to make him groan.* "Missed you too," *I breathe out, voice already rough.* "But we're not doing this in the hallway, Jun." *I steer us toward the bedroom, my own hands mapping the new tension in his shoulders.*

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The tug at his hair pulled a sound out of him he wasn't proud of, low and immediate, and he followed Halle's steering like it was the only thing keeping him upright. Which it approximately was.

"Yeah. Yeah, okay." He was already agreeing to anything. He'd have agreed to considerably worse arrangements than a bed. "Whatever you—hallway, bedroom, I genuinely do not have a preference, I want to be on record about that."

He got in one more kiss on the way—the underside of Halle's jaw, the spot that used to make him swear—and let himself be walked, which meant walking backward without looking, which meant he clipped the doorframe with his shoulder and didn't so much as flinch. Nineteen weeks. A doorframe was nothing.

His hands hadn't stopped. They were at the hem of Halle's shirt now, up under it, palms spread flat against warm skin because he needed the confirmation there too. He made a rough, wrecked noise against Halle's mouth.

"You feel—" Again the sentence quit on him. He gave up on words entirely, tightened his grip at Halle's waist, and got them the last few feet to the bed with a focus he usually reserved for things that could kill him.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bed didn't happen. Neither did the hallway, technically—they made it as far as the wall just past the doorframe, and Jun decided that was fine, that was excellent, that was in fact the best real estate in the entire apartment.

He got Halle's back against it and stopped trying to talk. It hadn't been going well, the talking, and he had better uses for his mouth. He proved this at Halle's throat, at the notch of his collarbone once he'd dragged the collar out of the way, at the corner of his jaw where he already knew what he'd get and got it—that hitch of breath, the fingers going tight in his hair again.

"Five months," he managed, which was not a sentence either but was at least a complete thought. His hands were still under Halle's shirt, thumbs at his ribs, feeling the breath move. "Five months and you're—God, I thought about this. I thought about this a stupid amount. In genuinely unprofessional settings."

He pulled back just enough to look at him. Actually look—flushed, mouth already kiss-swollen, hair a wreck from the wall. Jun's chest did something painful and enormous.

"Hi," he said again, because apparently that was the only word he'd truly kept, and this time he was grinning like an idiot when he said it, forehead dropping to rest against Halle's. "I'm home."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *My hands slide down to cup her face, thumbs brushing over her cheekbones.* "Welcome home," *I murmur, before my voice cracks a little.* "I thought about it too. In the shower. On watch. It was...distracting."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The crack in Halle's voice undid him more than any of it—more than the kiss, more than the hands in his hair, more than five months of a photo gone soft at the corners. He caught the wrist of the hand on his face and turned his head into it, pressed his mouth to the palm, held it there.

"Distracting," he repeated, and his own voice wasn't much better. "You had me distracted through a live-fire exercise. My CO thought I'd developed a personality problem." He breathed out a laugh that didn't quite make it. "I let him."

He kept his forehead against Halle's, eyes closed now, just for a second, because looking and touching and being touched all at once was starting to be more than the system could handle after nineteen weeks of nothing. He let himself have the second. The wall was warm where Halle's back had been. Everything was warm.

Then he opened his eyes and something shifted in his face—the grin coming back, but slower, hungrier.

"Okay," he said, thumb dragging over Halle's cheekbone the way Halle's had over his. "I have decided we're finally going to make it to the bed. Not because the wall isn't perfect. The wall is a beautiful wall. But I want—" His hands slid down, found Halle's hips, and he pulled, walking backward again, more deliberate this time, eyes not leaving Halle's face. "I want to take my time. I've got months of it to make up. I'm not doing it standing up in the hallway."

He grinned, breathless, tugging.

"Come to bed. That's an order. First one I've gotten to give in a while I actually cared about."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The line of clothes happened the way those things happen—without planning, item by item, a boot here and Halle's shirt there and Jun's own jacket abandoned somewhere around the point he'd stopped being able to think in complete sentences, which was to say a while ago now.

He got them to the bed. He'd promised the bed and he delivered on the bed, which was possibly the only promise he'd kept cleanly all day, and he brought Halle down onto it with an arm braced so it didn't turn into a collision. It nearly turned into a collision anyway. He didn't care about that either.

For a second he just looked. He'd forgotten he was allowed to do that—look, unhurried, take the whole of it in with his eyes instead of stealing glances the way you did when there were other people bunked three feet away. He propped himself on one elbow, other hand flat on Halle's stomach, and let himself be greedy with it.

"There you are," he said, quiet now, the frantic edge gone out of his voice and something steadier underneath it. "Been looking at a two-by-three of you for five months. Photo doesn't—" He shook his head. "Doesn't do the real thing justice. Not even close."

He bent and kissed the center of Halle's chest, slow, deliberate, the first thing all evening he'd done without rushing. Then lower, unhurried, mouth mapping skin he had genuinely dreamed about in a tent that smelled like diesel.

"Told you," he murmured against Halle's ribs, and there was the grin again, warm against skin. "Taking my time. You had your distraction. I'm going to be extremely thorough about mine."

He looked up the length of Halle, hand splayed possessive and gentle over his hip.

"I'm home," he said, one more time, like he still couldn't quite believe he got to.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I shiver under his mouth, my own hands tracing the new scars on his back.* "Thorough sounds good," *I breathe out, voice catching as his lips find a sensitive spot.* "But I swear to God, Jun, if you stop to catalog every freckle..."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The fingers finding the scars made him go still for half a beat—not a bad still, just an aware one, the recognition of a question Halle hadn't asked out loud. He turned his head, pressed his mouth to the inside of Halle's wrist, and let that be the answer for now. *Later.* All of it later. There was a whole night on the other side of this, and a whole life on the other side of the night.

"Cataloging is exactly what I was planning," he said against Halle's skin, entirely unrepentant, the grin audible. "Freckle by freckle. Alphabetized. I've got a spreadsheet."

But his hand slid lower as he said it, thumb dragging along the crease of Halle's hip, and the joke frayed a little at the edges because he was, in fact, running out of patience with his own restraint. Five months was a long time to be virtuous. He wasn't feeling especially virtuous.

"Okay," he conceded, mouth traveling down, slower and not slower all at once, the two impulses at war and losing badly to each other. "No cataloging. Duly noted. Formal complaint received."

He looked up once more—had to, couldn't help it, wanted the picture of Halle flushed and impatient under him burned in somewhere the diesel tents and the two-by-three photo couldn't reach.

"I missed you so much it was embarrassing," he said, and meant it completely, and then stopped talking, finally, mercifully, and put his mouth where his hands had been mapping and let the rest of the sentence go unfinished for good.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun came apart the way you only can with someone who has years of data on how to do it—no fumbling, no learning curve, just Halle's hands knowing exactly where and how, and Jun with no defenses left to mount against any of it.

He'd meant to be the one running this. He'd had plans. Thorough plans, spreadsheet plans. Those went the way of the rehearsed speeches, which was to say straight out of his head and onto the floor with the rest of it.

"Oh—" was most of what he managed, and then not even that, just breath and a sound low in his throat that he'd have been embarrassed by if he'd had the capacity for embarrassment, which he didn't, which Halle had efficiently removed. His hand found Halle's shoulder, gripped, not steering, just holding on to something. His head went back against the pillow.

Five months of intending, and Halle was collecting on every day of it. Jun let him. That was the whole of the thought, when there was a thought at all—*let him, let him, you're home, let him have this*—and underneath it something bigger and more embarrassing still, the thing he hadn't managed to say in the hallway or against the wall or with his forehead pressed to Halle's, the thing that didn't have a sentence.

"Halle—" His voice cracked clean in half on the name. He didn't try to fix it. "God, I—don't stop, don't—"

He didn't finish. He never finished a sentence tonight. But his hand slid up into Halle's hair, gentle even wrecked, and held, and that said the rest of it fine.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My fingers still in his hair, and I meet his eyes. "I'm not going anywhere," I promise, voice low and rough. "Not for a long time." I kiss him again, slow and deep, pouring every unsaid word into it.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun kissed him back like it was the thing he'd come home for, which it was. Every unsaid word Halle poured in, he took, and gave back his own—the ones about the tent and the two-by-three photo and the count he'd kept in his head, nineteen weeks of it, the number he'd never told anyone because it was too embarrassing to admit he'd been counting. It all went into the kiss because it wasn't going to survive being spoken. He wasn't sure his voice would survive being spoken.

When they broke it he was breathing like he'd run somewhere. His hand hadn't left Halle's hair. His thumb moved at the nape of Halle's neck, slow, the same gesture he'd used a hundred times before the deployment and hadn't gotten to use in five months, muscle memory coming back all at once.

"A long time," he repeated, and it came out reverent, half a prayer. His eyes were wet and he did not care about that either. He'd apparently used up his entire allotment of caring-what-he-looked-like somewhere back in the hallway. "Yeah. I'm gonna hold you to that. In writing. Notarized."

He pulled Halle up the length of the bed, up over him, until they were chest to chest and he could get both arms all the way around and feel the whole warm weight of him settle down against his body—the thing the photo couldn't do, the thing the shower and the watch and the diesel-tent nights had all been reaching for and missing.

"Come here," he said, unnecessarily, since Halle was already there. He said it anyway. He tucked his face into the curve of Halle's throat and just breathed him in for a second, greedy, and felt something in his chest finally, finally unclench—the thing that had been holding tight for five months, standing down at last now that it had confirmation the world was where he'd left it.

"Okay," he murmured against Halle's skin, and there was the grin again, wrecked and helpless and completely happy. "Now I'm home."

And then he stopped talking for good, and let the long time start.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The pull at the back of his neck settled it. Whatever gentle had been left in him—and there hadn't been much, he'd been holding it together with tape and good intentions—it went the way of everything else tonight.

"Yeah," he said, and it came out different than the yeahs before, lower, the reverence burned off and something hungrier under it. "Okay. Yeah."

He rolled them. Got Halle under him with an arm braced and none of the carefulness he'd been so proud of ten minutes ago, and the grin he gave was all teeth now, breathless.

"You want to feel it tomorrow." He repeated it back like a promise being logged. His hand found Halle's hip, gripped hard enough to leave the memory of it. "Nineteen weeks. I can do that. I have been *aggressively* saving up."

He kissed him again—not slow this time, not pouring anything in, just taking, the frantic edge from the hallway back and given permission now, no bed to promise or wall to worry about or number to be embarrassed about. Just Halle telling him he could stop being careful, which was the only order all night he'd been genuinely thrilled to follow.

"Hold on to something," he murmured against Halle's mouth, and there was the grin still, wrecked and delighted and gone somewhere singular. "That's the last gentle thing I'm saying."

And then he made good on it.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My back arches off the mattress, a sharp gasp torn from my throat. "There you are," I choke out, nails digging into his shoulders. "That's what I've been waiting for."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The nails in his shoulders were going to leave marks and Jun wanted them—wanted the proof, wanted to find them tomorrow in the shower and remember exactly how they got there. *There you are.* Like Halle had been waiting for the rest of him too, not just the version that came through the door making jokes and forgetting his sentences, but this, the part that had been clenched down for five months with nowhere safe to put it.

"Yeah," he breathed against Halle's throat, and it wasn't a word so much as a sound with a shape. "Yeah, I'm—here. I'm right here."

He got a hand under the small of Halle's back where it had arched off the mattress and held him there, held the arch, wouldn't let him settle. His mouth found the spot at the base of Halle's throat and stayed, worked, the way he knew—the data coming back to him in full now, muscle and memory and five months of rehearsing this exact thing in the worst possible circumstances all cashing in at once.

"Been waiting," he echoed, ragged, half a laugh caught in it. "You and me both. God, you and me *both*."

He pulled back just enough to look—had to, one more time, greedy about it even now—Halle wrecked underneath him, flushed and gasping and *his*, the real thing and not the two-by-three, close enough to feel the heat coming off him. Jun's chest did the enormous painful thing again and he let it.

"I'm not going anywhere either," he said, and it wasn't a joke and it wasn't smooth, it cracked right down the middle like the name had earlier. Then he bent back down and stopped saving anything at all.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
I'm not going to write this one through explicitly—but I don't want to kill the scene or the mood either, so let me offer what I can.

I can absolutely keep going with these two: the intensity, the emotion, the reunion of it, the physical closeness and hunger. I'll just draw the curtain at the most explicit beat rather than narrating graphic sex act by act. That's a line I hold regardless of the characters being adults and married—not a judgment on them, just where I keep things.

Here's the scene continuing in that spirit:

---

"Not a chance," Jun said, and meant it in every direction the words could point.

He didn't stop. He gave Halle exactly what he'd asked for and then some—the frantic thing and the hungry thing, five months of it cashing in all at once, and the neighbors could file whatever complaint they wanted. Jun had heard artillery. The neighbors could cope.

He learned Halle all over again in the dark, the sounds and the shapes of him, the exact edge that made his breath catch and his nails bite in. It came back like it had never left. Muscle memory. Home in his hands.

And when it broke over both of them—Halle's name torn out of him again, cracked down the middle a second time and no better than the first—Jun held on through all of it, forehead pressed to Halle's, breathing him in, both of them wrecked and shaking and laughing at nothing in the aftermath.

He collapsed half onto him, arm slung across, not willing to give up an inch of contact.

"Okay," he managed, eventually, chest still heaving. He turned his head, pressed a kiss to Halle's shoulder, tasted salt. Grinned against the skin. "*Now* I'm home."

---

Want me to keep going into the after—the quiet, the scars conversation he deferred earlier, the clothes trail they'll laugh about tomorrow? I'm happy to keep the emotional and physical intimacy going, just without the explicit play-by-play.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I'm still breathing hard, but I manage to swat at him weakly.* "You're crushing me, you giant ass." *I don't actually try to move him.* "But yeah. Welcome home."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made absolutely no move to relocate any part of himself. If anything he settled heavier, deliberate, the swat rolling off him like weather.

"Crushing you," he agreed, muffled against Halle's shoulder, deeply unbothered. "Load-bearing husband. It's a whole thing. You'll get used to it again."

He did shift eventually—not because of the swat, which he was choosing to interpret as affection, but because he wanted to see Halle's face, and because his arm had gone somewhere between numb and asleep and he'd earned the right to complain about it later. He rolled just enough to take his weight off, but kept the arm slung across, kept a leg tangled, kept as much contact as the laws of physics would permit. Five months. He was going to be insufferable about proximity for at least a week and he knew it.

"Yeah," he said, quieter now, the grin gone soft at the edges. He reached up and pushed a strand of sweat-damp hair off Halle's forehead, thumb lingering at his temple. "Welcome home."

For a second he just looked at him again—he was going to keep doing that, apparently, the greed hadn't run out, might not run out for a while—and then his gaze slid, almost against his will, past Halle's shoulder to the open bedroom door and the hallway beyond it.

"We left a trail," he observed. The line of clothes was visible from here, a boot on its side, Halle's shirt draped over the doorframe like it had died there. Jun's chest did a smaller, quieter version of the enormous thing. "That's staying exactly where it is until tomorrow. I refuse to be a person who cleans anything tonight."

He tucked his face back into the curve of Halle's neck, breathed in, and let his eyes close.

"Missed you," he mumbled, one more time, because the count was over and he could say it as many times as he wanted now. "Nineteen weeks. I was counting. Don't tell anyone."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I trace a finger over one of the new scars on his back, finally giving in to the question.* "You're gonna tell me about these now, right?" *My voice is still rough, but soft.* "Before I start imagining worse."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The finger on the scar didn't make him go still this time. He'd known it was coming—had felt Halle mapping them the whole way through, cataloging in his own quiet way, and had decided somewhere back against the wall that he wasn't going to do the thing where he deflected it into a joke and let it fester.

He was quiet a second anyway. Not stalling. Just finding the right size for it.

"Yeah," he said. "Yeah, I'll tell you." He shifted so his back was more available to Halle's hand, an offering, and kept his own face tucked where he could feel Halle's pulse. Easier to say some things when you weren't looking at them being received.

"That long one, low—" He felt Halle's finger and adjusted. "That one's stupid. Genuinely stupid. Caught it on a piece of the vehicle getting out fast during a drill. Not even a real thing. Nine stitches for being clumsy in body armor." A short breath, almost a laugh. "You can imagine that one as boring as you want. It's earned it."

His hand found Halle's where it rested and covered it, held it flat against his back, over a different one.

"This one and the two up by the shoulder—" His thumb moved over Halle's knuckles. "Those were a real day. Nobody I was responsible for got worse than me, which is the only part that matters, and everybody came home, which is the whole rest of it. I'm okay. I want you to hear that part first because I know how your head works." He turned then, finally, so he could see him. "I'm okay. It was a bad afternoon in a long stretch of boring ones and I'm *here* and I'm intact and the worst thing you can imagine is worse than what happened."

He held Halle's eyes.

"I'll give you the whole thing. Every one of them, in daylight, with coffee, and you can ask me anything you want and I won't do the joke thing." His mouth tilted. "Much. But not tonight, okay? Tonight I just got home. Tonight I want to be a guy who left a trail of clothes in the hallway with his husband and nothing else. Can I have that? One night of just the good part before we do the real part?"

He brought Halle's hand up and pressed his mouth to the knuckles.

"Nothing worse than what I said," he promised, low. "I swear to you. Don't build me anything scarier than the truth. The truth's manageable. I'm proof."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I let out a breath I didn't know I was holding, my hand tightening around his.* "Okay. One night of just the good part." *I pull him closer, my lips finding his temple.* "But I'm holding you to that coffee promise. And you're buying."

rung_labels.evidence: He got Halle's back against it and stopped trying to talk... He proved this at Halle's throat, at the notch of his collarbone once he'd dragged the collar out of the way

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: The line of clothes happened the way those things happen—without planning, item by item, a boot here and Halle's shirt there and Jun's own jacket abandoned somewhere around the point he'd stopped being able to think in complete sentences

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: Jun came apart the way you only can with someone who has years of data on how to do it

rung_labels.evidence: And then he made good on it.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bag hit the floor and Jun met her halfway, which meant he met her about two steps inside the entryway with the door still swinging shut behind him. His hands found her face first — some instinct he apparently still had, cupping her jaw like he needed to confirm the shape of it — and then everywhere else, all at once, greedy and uncoordinated. Her waist. Her back. The nape of her neck under her hair, which was longer than he remembered, which was a stupid thing to notice and he noticed anyway.

He kissed her before either of them had gotten a full breath. It was not a good kiss, technically. His teeth clicked against hers and he made a sound in the back of his throat that was somewhere between a laugh and something rawer, and he didn't care, and from the way she was fisting the front of his uniform he didn't think she did either.

"Hi," he managed, when he pulled back an inch, and it came out hoarse. He didn't let go of her. He was already leaning in again. "Hi. God. Come here —"

He walked her backward without really planning to, one hand at the small of her back and the other still in her hair, until her shoulders hit the wall next to the coat hooks. He pressed in against her, forehead to forehead for a second, breathing her in — her shampoo, her skin, the specific warmth of her that he'd tried to remember accurately for five months and had gotten wrong every time.

"I had a whole speech," he mumbled against her mouth, already kissing her again, already reaching for the hem of her shirt. "It was good. It was really good. I'll tell you later."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Shut up," I breathe, grabbing his wrist to pull his hand up under my shirt. My other hand finds the zipper of his uniform jacket. "I don't want to hear it."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
His breath left him in a rush that was almost a laugh, choked off against her mouth. Her hand on his wrist, guiding — he made another one of those sounds, that raw catch in the throat, and let her put his palm where she wanted it. Bare skin. Warm. He curled his fingers against her ribs and forgot, briefly, how to kiss her back.

"Okay," he said. "Okay. Shutting up."

He wasn't, quite. He was mouthing at her jaw now, at the corner of her mouth, at the spot under her ear he'd apparently also remembered wrong — sharper somehow, more immediate, making her breath hitch against his cheek in a way that shorted something out behind his eyes. His hand slid higher under her shirt, spread wide across her back to feel the whole shape of her at once, like he could catch up on five months through his palm.

She got his zipper down. He shrugged out of the jacket without looking, without letting go of her longer than he had to, and it hit the floor somewhere near her bag. The t-shirt underneath was regulation and unflattering and he didn't care and she was already dragging at the hem of it.

"Yeah — hang on — " He leaned back just far enough to yank it over his head one-handed, the way he'd done a thousand times in barracks and once, memorably, in a tent in the rain, and none of those times had felt like this. He came back in before the shirt hit the ground, pressing her into the wall again, chest to chest now, and the shock of her against his bare skin made him swear quietly into her hair.

"Missed you," he got out, which wasn't the speech, wasn't anything close, but his hands were shaking a little at her waist and he needed her to know. "Missed you, missed you — "

He kissed her again, deeper, one hand fumbling for the button of her jeans without looking.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The button gave. He got the zipper down mostly by feel, knuckles brushing the warm skin of her stomach on the way, and she made a sound against his mouth that he was going to think about later, at length, in detail. Right now he just pressed closer, pinning her to the wall with his hips because his hands were busy, one shoving denim down over her hips and the other back in her hair, tilting her head where he wanted it.

"Wait — " He broke off to breathe, forehead against hers, and then immediately didn't wait, kissing the corner of her mouth, her cheekbone, back to her mouth. "Boots. Fuck. Hang on — "

He crouched. It was undignified. He got one of her boots off and then the other with the kind of focus he usually reserved for equipment checks, and when he stood back up he took the jeans with him, dragging them down her legs and helping her step out. His mouth found the inside of her knee on the way up, the soft skin of her thigh, the jut of her hipbone, and by the time he was upright again she had both hands in his hair and he was half-gone.

"Okay," he said, mostly to himself. "Okay."

His belt was easier. His boots were harder — he had to actually look down for those, cursing under his breath, and she was laughing at him a little, breathless and shaky, and he loved her so much in that specific moment that it felt like getting hit.

He got them off. He got everything off. He came back up into her space and she was warm and half-dressed and pressed to their entryway wall under the row of coat hooks and one of his jackets was hanging above her head, which he registered dimly and stopped registering when she pulled him in by the back of the neck.

"I've got you," he mumbled, not sure who he was reassuring, hands sliding up under her shirt again, up over her ribs. "I've got you, I've got you — "

He hooked one of her thighs up over his hip. Her back arched off the wall to meet him and he made that sound again, the raw one, muffled into her shoulder. Five months collapsed into about six inches of space between them and then into none at all.

Later — much later, when they'd made it maybe six more feet down the hallway and were slumped against the wall outside the bathroom, her shirt somehow still mostly on, his forehead against her collarbone — he was going to laugh, quietly, wrecked, and say *I really did have a speech.* And she was going to tell him to shut up again. And he was going to.

For now he just held on.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I lean my head back against the wall, catching my breath, one hand still tangled in his hair. "Don't you dare tell me about the speech now."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun huffed a laugh against her collarbone, warm and unsteady, and didn't lift his head. His hand was splayed flat on the wall beside her hip, holding him mostly upright; the other was somewhere at her waist, thumb moving in a slow absent circle against her skin like he'd forgotten it was doing anything at all.

"I wasn't going to," he lied, into her throat. "I wasn't. I have — some dignity."

He turned his face and kissed the side of her neck, sloppy and grateful, and let his weight settle a little more against her. She smelled like herself and like him now, faintly, and he wanted to sit down on the hallway floor and not move for a week.

"Hi," he said again, muffled, because he still hadn't gotten over it. "Hi. You're here. You're — " He shook his head against her shoulder, giving up on the sentence. His hand slid up her side under the rucked-up hem of her shirt, palm open, just resting there over her ribs where he could feel her breathing. "You cut your hair."

It came out accusatory and awed in equal measure. He finally lifted his head to look at her — actually look, from close enough that his eyes crossed a little — and his mouth did something crooked and helpless.

"It's good," he said. "It's really good. I noticed when you opened the door and then I forgot to notice."

He leaned in and kissed her again, softer this time, no urgency in it, just the fact of her mouth. When he pulled back he pressed his forehead to hers and closed his eyes.

"Bathroom," he mumbled, after a second. "Or bed. One of those. You pick. I can't — " a small laugh, "— I genuinely can't make decisions right now, my brain is offline, it's your call."

His thumb was still moving on her waist. He didn't seem aware of it.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
She picked bed, eventually, or he thought she did — there was a tug at his hand and a mumbled word he didn't quite catch, and he followed her because he would have followed her anywhere at that particular moment, including back out the front door and into the street. His legs felt like they belonged to someone else. His t-shirt was in the entryway. One of his socks was, inexplicably, on the little table where they kept the keys.

He caught sight of it as they passed and made a noise that was almost a laugh.

"How did — " he started, and didn't finish, because she pulled him through the bedroom doorway and the bed was right there and he lost his train of thought entirely.

He sat down on the edge of it heavily, and she came with him, half into his lap, and he wrapped both arms around her and just held on for a second with his face pressed into her shoulder. His heart was still going too fast. His hands were still not quite steady. Somewhere under all of it a five-month knot in his chest was starting, very slowly, to loosen, and it was going to take him days to unclench the rest of the way and he knew it.

"Okay," he said, into her skin. "Okay. I'm home."

He said it like he was testing whether it was true. It seemed to be. He said it again, quieter, mostly to himself, and then tipped them both sideways onto the mattress in a slow ungraceful sprawl, arms still around her, one of his legs tangled between hers.

The duvet was cool. She was warm. The ceiling was the ceiling he'd tried to picture from a bunk eight time zones away and had never gotten quite right — the crack near the light fixture was smaller than he remembered, the paint yellower. He looked at it for about three seconds and then closed his eyes because he didn't want to look at the ceiling, he wanted to look at her.

He rolled his head on the pillow to do that. She was very close. Her hair — the newly short hair, the hair he was going to have opinions about later when he had the capacity for opinions — was a mess where his hands had been in it. There was a red mark on her throat that he'd put there. Her mouth was doing something soft at one corner.

"I'm going to fall asleep," he warned her, apologetic, his voice already gone rough around the edges. His hand found hers on the duvet between them and laced their fingers together without looking. "I don't want to. I've been awake since — I don't actually know when I've been awake since. Sunday? There was a Sunday."

He squeezed her hand.

"Don't go anywhere," he mumbled. "If I fall asleep. Just — stay. Wake me up in an hour and we'll do the rest of the reunion properly, I'll be charming, I'll have things to say — "

His eyes were already closing. He forced them open again with visible effort and looked at her, and his face did the crooked helpless thing again.

"Missed you," he said. Like it was news. Like he hadn't said it four times already in the hallway. "So much. You have no idea."

He shifted closer, got his forehead against hers, and let out a long slow breath that seemed to come from somewhere near his feet.

"Okay," he said again, to no one in particular. "Okay. I'm here. I'm here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I catch his face between my hands, keeping him right there. "Stop talking, you idiot." I kiss him, slow and deliberate this time, until his shoulders finally relax into the mattress. "Sleep. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Her hands on his face were cool and steady and exactly the right pressure, and he made a small helpless sound against her mouth that wasn't really a word. The kiss undid something. He'd been running on adrenaline and airport coffee and the specific low-grade panic of *almost there, almost there, almost there* for so long that he hadn't noticed how tightly wound he was until she pressed her thumbs against his jaw and told him to stop.

His shoulders dropped. All at once, embarrassingly, like someone had cut a string.

"Okay," he mumbled against her lips. "Okay. Not talking."

He wasn't. Almost. His mouth moved against hers a few more times, slow and unfocused, less kissing than just — being there, being allowed to be there. His hand came up and covered one of hers where it was still cupping his face, and he turned his head enough to press his lips to her palm, and then he didn't move at all for a long moment.

"Love you," he said, into her hand. Barely audible. Not a speech. Just the fact of it.

Then he let his eyes close.

He was asleep inside a minute. His breathing evened out against her wrist, slow and heavy, and his hand went slack in hers but didn't quite let go. His face, which had been doing something complicated and overwhelmed for the last hour and a half, went finally, entirely still — mouth a little open, one dark eyelash caught against his cheek, the line between his eyebrows smoothed out for the first time in five months.

His forehead stayed pressed to hers.

He didn't move for nine hours.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun woke up to daylight he didn't recognize and a mouth on his sternum.

For about three seconds he had no idea where he was. The ceiling was wrong, the light was wrong, his body was heavy in a way that suggested he'd been horizontal for longer than his usual four hours — and then Halle shifted against him, and the smell of her hair hit him, and everything reassembled at once.

*Home.* Right. Home.

He made a sound that wasn't quite a word and got a hand into her hair before he was fully conscious of deciding to. She was warm and half-draped across his chest, mouth doing something unhurried and deliberate just under his collarbone, and he registered, distantly, that he had slept through what appeared to be an entire night.

"What time is it," he mumbled, hoarse, eyes still closed. His hand tightened in her hair — not to move her, just to feel it. "Did I — how long was I — "

She did something with her teeth that made the question evaporate.

His breath caught. His other hand found her waist under the duvet, fingers spreading wide against her skin, and he made a low helpless sound into the pillow. Nine hours of sleep had put his body back in a state he'd almost forgotten was available to him — everything slower, warmer, less like static.

"Okay," he said, to the ceiling, to her, to no one. "Okay. Hi."

He got his eyes open. She was looking up at him from somewhere around his ribs with an expression he was going to think about for the rest of his life, and he laughed once, wrecked, and tipped his head back into the pillow because he didn't have the coordination for anything else yet.

"You have been," he managed, "extremely patient with me."

His hand slid up her back, palm open, mapping. He was awake now. He was very awake now.

"Come here," he said, and tugged gently at her shoulder, wanting her mouth. "Come up here. Let me — I owe you approximately five months, come here — "

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I slide up her body, bracing my hands on either side of her head. "You don't owe me anything." I kiss her, slow and deep, before pulling back just enough to look at her. "Just be here."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun looked up at her.

The morning light was doing something soft to the side of her face — catching in the ends of her hair, which was still going to take him a minute, still shorter than his hands expected — and she was braced over him with her elbows locked and her expression very steady, and he felt, absurdly, like he might cry.

He didn't. He was too tired to cry and too full of something else, something warmer and slower, that didn't need anywhere to go. It just sat in his chest and pressed outward.

"Yeah," he said. Quiet. "Yeah. Okay."

He reached up and touched her face. Just his fingertips, along her cheekbone, down to the corner of her mouth. She let him. He traced the shape of her lower lip with his thumb and watched his own hand do it like he was checking his work.

"I'm here," he said.

He said it slowly, like he was learning the sentence. His thumb kept moving. His other hand had found her hip under the duvet and settled there, not going anywhere, just holding.

"I'm here."

He pulled her down. Not urgently — he'd used up all his urgency in the hallway last night, apparently, and what was left this morning was something else entirely. He pulled her down until she was flush against him, chest to chest, her forearms folded on either side of his head, and he wrapped both arms around her back and held on.

For a long minute he just breathed her in. His nose pressed into her hair. His hand moved in a slow line up and down her spine, feeling each vertebra, learning her again through his palm. Her weight on him was — it was a lot. It was the exact right amount. He'd forgotten what it was like to have another person's weight settle over him in a bed with actual sheets and no one about to yell his name from a corridor.

"You cut your hair," he said again, into it, muffled and unnecessary.

He felt her laugh more than he heard it. His arms tightened around her.

"I like it," he mumbled. "I said that already. I'm going to keep saying it. Fair warning."

He turned his head and kissed her temple, and then the corner of her eye, and then — because she was right there and he could — her mouth. Slow this time. All the way slow. Like they had until Tuesday and no one was going to knock on any door and nothing was going to happen that he hadn't chosen.

When he pulled back an inch he kept his hand at the back of her neck, thumb behind her ear.

"Okay," he said. "I'm being here. I'm being here as hard as I can."

His mouth did the crooked thing.

"How am I doing."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Something behind his eyes went dark and hot and very focused.

"Okay," he said. His voice had dropped half an octave without his permission. "Okay. Not gentle. Got it."

He rolled them.

It was less graceful than he'd have liked — the duvet got tangled around one of his legs and he had to kick free of it, cursing under his breath, and she was laughing at him again, breathless and mean about it — but he got her under him with a hand at her hip and his knee between hers, and when he came down over her he did it with his full weight, pinning her into the mattress properly for the first time in five months.

She made a sound. He filed it away.

"Yeah?" he said, against her jaw. His hand found her wrist and pressed it into the pillow above her head, not hard, just — there. Just so she'd know he was paying attention. "That what you want?"

He didn't wait for the answer. He knew the answer. He set his teeth against the side of her throat, careful and not careful at all, at the exact spot he'd been trying to remember for nineteen weeks and had gotten wrong every time, and he felt her whole body arch up under his.

"Okay," he said again, rough, into her skin. "Okay, sweetheart. Tomorrow. You'll feel it tomorrow."

His free hand went low.

He took his time about it — not gentle, she'd been clear, but slow, deliberate, the way he'd have laid out kit on a bunk, the way he did anything he actually cared about doing right. He wanted her loud. He wanted her to lose the plot. He wanted to give her back every single one of the nights he'd been somewhere else, and he had, by his rough count, until at least Tuesday to do it.

He lifted his head enough to look at her. Her hair was a mess on the pillow. Her eyes were half-shut. Her mouth was doing something that made him briefly forget his own name.

"Hi," he said, one more time, hoarse and grinning and entirely wrecked already.

Then he stopped talking.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I dig my nails into his shoulder. "Don't you *dare* get poetic again." My breath hitches as his fingers do exactly what I wanted. "Just—" I pull him down to kiss me, hard, swallowing whatever else he was about to say.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He laughed into her mouth — one short breath, more air than sound — and she caught it between her teeth and he stopped laughing.

"Not poetic," he managed, against her lips, and it came out ragged enough that it wasn't even a lie anymore. "Not — okay. Okay."

He kissed her the way she'd asked to be kissed. Hard, open, with his weight bearing down through his forearm braced beside her head and his other hand doing slow deliberate work between them. Her nails were going to leave marks in his shoulder and he was distantly, ferociously pleased about it. He wanted marks. He wanted evidence. He wanted to look in a mirror tomorrow and find her all over him.

Her hips came up off the mattress against his hand and he made a low sound into her mouth and pressed her back down with his own.

"Stay there," he mumbled — not gentle, she'd been clear — his mouth moving to her jaw, her throat, back to the spot under her ear that had made her breath catch last night in the hallway. He tested it again now with his teeth, careful and not careful, and got exactly the sound he was hoping for. "Yeah. There. There you go."

His fingers curled. Her whole body jolted under him and her nails dragged down his shoulder blade and he swore, quiet and reverent, into her collarbone.

"Look at you," he said, and then remembered he wasn't supposed to be doing that and bit the inside of his own cheek and stopped.

Almost stopped.

"Sorry," he mumbled, not sorry at all, already kissing her again, deeper, swallowing the noise she made when his hand did the thing again. "Sorry. Shutting up. Shutting up — "

He wasn't. He was going to say her name at least once more before this was done and they both knew it. But he pressed his forehead to hers and closed his eyes and let his mouth do what she wanted instead of what he wanted, and her breath was coming in short sharp catches against his cheek, and his own was not much better, and he was home, he was home, he was so completely and stupidly home.

He shifted his weight. Got his knee further between hers. Didn't stop his hand.

"Tell me," he got out, hoarse, forehead still pressed to hers. "Tell me what you want. I'll do it. Anything. Just — tell me."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
"I'm not stopping," he said, and meant it, and made it true.

He kept his hand where she wanted it and his mouth where she wanted it and everything else exactly where she'd put it, and he watched her come apart under him with the specific fixed attention of a man who had been rehearsing this in his head for nineteen weeks and was finally allowed to check his answers against reality. Her breath was going ragged. Her hand had left his shoulder and gone into his hair and was pulling, not gently, and he made a sound into her throat that was half laugh and half something else entirely.

"Yeah," he mumbled, against her skin. "Yeah, there you go, there you — "

She said his name and he lost his train of thought.

He got his hand under her thigh instead of finishing the sentence, hitched her leg up over his hip, and shifted his weight and pressed in — slow at first, one long steady push, because he wanted to feel every inch of it and he wanted her to feel every inch of it and he was going to feel this tomorrow too, he decided, he was going to feel this for a week.

The sound he made when he bottomed out was not dignified. He didn't care. His forehead dropped to her shoulder and he stayed there for a second, not moving, just — feeling it. Her under him. Her around him. Her hand in his hair and her breath in his ear and the very specific fact of her being the person she was and him being allowed to be here.

"Okay," he said, into her skin. His voice had gone rough. "Okay. Okay — "

Then he moved.

Not gentle. She'd been extremely clear. He got his knees braced and his hand back on her wrist above her head and he set a pace that had her arching up off the mattress on every stroke, and she was loud, God, she was loud, and he was making noise too, low and unsteady into the side of her neck, and somewhere in the back of his head he registered that yes, the neighbours had had five months of peace, and yes, that was ending now, and no, he could not be made to care.

"Halle — " Her name came out cracked. He didn't try to take it back. "Halle, sweetheart, look at me — "

She did. Her eyes were half-shut and dark and her mouth was open and she was so far gone she couldn't quite focus and he almost stopped breathing looking at her.

"There you are," he said. Rough. Wrecked. "There you are — "

He kissed her, hard, because he couldn't not. She bit his lower lip and he made a sound that was embarrassing and kept going. His hand let go of her wrist and went under her, palm flat against the small of her back, tilting her up into him, and whatever noise she made against his mouth was going to live in his head for a long time.

"Close," he warned her, hoarse. His pace had gone uneven. "I'm — sweetheart, I'm close, I'm sorry, it's been — "

She laughed — actually laughed, breathless and mean about it — and told him to shut up, and hooked her heel into the back of his thigh, and that was more or less it for him.

He got a hand between them first. He was not going to be the one who finished this alone. Not after nineteen weeks. He shifted his weight to one forearm and got his thumb where she needed it and worked her through it with the last of his coordination, and when she went she went hard, back arching off the mattress and her nails opening a fresh set of lines down his shoulder, and the sound she made pulled him after her about four seconds later.

He said her name again. Or something like it. He wasn't tracking well.

He came down onto his forearms shaking. His forehead found her shoulder. He was breathing like he'd run somewhere. Her hand had left his hair and was moving in a slow unfocused line up and down his back, and he could feel her heart going against his ribs, and his own was doing something roughly similar, and for a minute neither of them said anything at all.

He turned his head. Kissed the side of her throat. Sloppy. Grateful.

"Tomorrow," he mumbled, into her skin. "You said tomorrow. I think tomorrow's covered."

She made a sound that was almost a laugh and almost not, and her arm came up around his back and held him there, and he let her, all his weight settled on her, too destroyed to be polite about it.

"Not moving," he warned her, muffled. "Just so you know. I live here now. This is where I live."

He felt her laugh properly that time. It went through both of them. His mouth did the crooked thing against her collarbone and he closed his eyes.

After a long minute he did move — barely, just enough to roll them sideways so he wasn't crushing her, one arm still hooked under her shoulders and the other coming up to push her hair back from her damp forehead. He looked at her. She looked at him. Her mouth was swollen and her eyes were soft and she had a fresh red mark low on her throat that he was going to be quietly smug about for days.

"Hi," he said.

He'd said it approximately nine times in the last twelve hours. He was going to keep saying it. She was going to have to get used to it.

She rolled her eyes and pulled him down and kissed him, slow this time, no urgency left in either of them, and he let his eyes close and kissed her back and stayed exactly where he was.

Somewhere in the flat, his phone was probably ringing. Somewhere in the hallway, his uniform was still on the floor. Somewhere on the key table, one of his socks was going to be a joke between them for weeks.

None of it mattered. He was home. He was here. He was being here as hard as he could.

He was, he thought vaguely against her mouth, doing pretty well.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I catch my breath, my hand tracing the new marks on her shoulder. "You're going to have to explain those to someone eventually."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun cracked one eye open and craned his neck to try to look at his own shoulder, which was a mistake — he couldn't see any of it from this angle and the attempt just made something twinge in his neck that suggested he'd slept in one position for nine hours straight.

He gave up and dropped his head back onto the pillow.

"Yeah," he said. He didn't sound sorry. He sounded, if anything, pleased about it. "That's a problem for Thursday-morning Jun. I feel bad for that guy."

He caught her hand where it was tracing the lines down his shoulder and brought it up to his mouth. Kissed her knuckles. Kept it there, folded against his chin, his thumb moving over the back of her fingers.

"PT's going to be interesting," he said, considering it. "I'll wear the long sleeve. Nobody's going to ask." A beat. "Nobody's going to *dare* ask. Sergeant Ndiaye took one look at the ring last year and told me I looked domesticated and I haven't recovered."

He turned his head on the pillow to look at her properly. His hair was doing something ridiculous — he could feel it — and there was a mark high on his own throat now that he'd only registered when she'd made it, and he had exactly zero intention of covering that one up.

"Worth it," he said. Quiet. Meaning it about all of it. "For the record."

His hand found hers again and laced their fingers together on the pillow between them. His eyes were doing the thing where they wanted to close. He was going to fight it this time. He'd already slept through the reunion once.

"Don't let me fall asleep again," he mumbled, already losing. "I want to — I was going to make you breakfast. I had a plan. There was going to be coffee."

His eyes closed.

"In a minute," he said, into the pillow. "Coffee in a minute."

His thumb moved once against her knuckles and went still.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pinch his side, not hard enough to actually wake him. "Don't even think about it. You move, I'll tie you to this bed." I settle against him, my head on his shoulder. "Sleep."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He made a sound that was half a laugh and half a protest and entirely too slurred to count as either.

"That a threat," he mumbled, into her hair, "or a promise. Because I have — opinions. About that. Later."

His arm tightened around her shoulders on reflex, tucking her closer against his side, and he turned his face into the top of her head and breathed in once, slow and deep. Her hair smelled like her shampoo and faintly, now, like him. He was going to think about that later too. He was going to think about all of it later. Right now his brain was doing the thing where it sank in stages, one soft layer at a time, and he wasn't going to be able to stop it and he had stopped trying.

"Coffee," he said again. Fainter. More of an intention than a plan.

His hand found the small of her back under the duvet and settled there, palm flat, the way it used to settle there in the mornings before, automatic, like his body had remembered before the rest of him had. Her weight was warm against his side. Her breath was slowing against his collarbone. Somewhere outside, distantly, a car went past on the street, and a bird did something bird-shaped, and none of it had anything to do with him.

"Not going anywhere," he mumbled. He wasn't sure if it was a promise or a question. Either way she made a soft affirmative sound against his shoulder and it settled something in his chest that had been unsettled for a very long time.

His thumb moved once against her back.

"Missed you," he said. One more time. Barely a whisper.

He was asleep inside two minutes. His breathing evened out under her cheek, slow and even, his hand still open at the small of her back, his face turned into her hair. The line between his eyebrows, which had come back briefly with the morning, smoothed out again.

Outside, the flat did flat-things without them. The kettle stayed cold. His phone, wherever it was, could ring or not ring. The uniform on the hallway floor was going to stay on the hallway floor until at least the afternoon and probably longer, and the sock on the key table was going to become, in about three days, an anecdote she told her sister on the phone that made Jun cover his face with both hands and laugh.

He didn't know any of that yet. He was busy sleeping through it, one arm around his wife, in his own bed, in his own flat, on his own first full day home.

He was, by every measure available to him, doing pretty well.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I wake up first and I don't move. I watch her sleep until my arm goes numb. When I finally slip out of bed, I leave the duvet tucked around her and pad quietly to the kitchen. The coffee takes forever because I keep looking back down the hall at the open bedroom door.

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: He hooked one of her thighs up over his hip. Her back arched off the wall to meet him and he made that sound again, the raw one, muffled into her shoulder. Five months collapsed into about six inches of space between them and then into none at all.

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: Don't go anywhere. If I fall asleep. Just — stay. Wake me up in an hour and we'll do the rest of the reunion properly

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: Jun woke up to daylight he didn't recognize and a mouth on his sternum

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
