rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: He got his knees braced and his hand back on her wrist above her head and he set a pace that had her arching up off the mattress on every stroke

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun caught Halle's face in both hands and kissed him like he'd been starving for it. Which he had been. Ninety minutes had been the longest five months of his life, and he didn't care how that sounded because he knew exactly how it sounded and he meant every desperate, unsubtle word of it.

His thumbs traced Halle's jaw. The skin was real. The breath was real. This was happening.

He pulled back just far enough to look—really look—and his voice came out wrecked.

"You're taller," he said, which was ridiculous, because Halle was not taller. But he was here. He was solid and he was warm and he was not a video call that cut out at the worst moment or a voice on the phone that couldn't touch him back.

Jun kissed him again, and his hands slid into Halle's hair, and he made a sound he would have been embarrassed about if he'd had any capacity left for embarrassment.

He was home. Finally.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath against your lips. "Missed you so much it *hurt*." My hands grip your hips, pulling you closer like I can't believe you're real either.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughed, or maybe sobbed—he couldn't tell the difference anymore and didn't care to distinguish. The grip on his hips anchored him in a way that made his chest ache.

"You have no idea," he managed, forehead pressed to Halle's. "No idea."

His hands hadn't stopped moving—cupping jaw, sliding down neck, settling on shoulders like he needed to confirm through touch what his eyes still couldn't quite believe. Five months of holding a phone. Five months of reaching for empty space in the dark. Five months of saying *I love you* to a screen because there was nothing else to do.

His thumb found the pulse point at Halle's throat and pressed there, just gently. Just to feel the heartbeat. Just to prove it was real.

"I dreamed about this," Jun admitted, voice rough. "More times than I can count. But you're—" He shook his head, a helpless smile breaking across his face. "You're better. You're *here*."

He kissed the corner of Halle's mouth, then his cheek, then the spot just below his ear. Mapping. Remembering. Claiming.

"Stay," he breathed against the skin there. "Just—stay right here. Let me have this for a minute before we have to be normal people again."

His arms finally wrapped around Halle properly, pulling him into a full embrace, face buried against his neck. He breathed in—shampoo, laundry detergent, the familiar scent that had become his definition of safety half a world away.

Ninety minutes home. He was never leaving again.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The hallway wall was cold against Jun's back. He couldn't have said when they'd made it there or which of them had moved first. It didn't matter. Nothing mattered except the pressure of Halle's body against his and the fact that he could *feel* him now—not the ghost of an embrace remembered from months ago, but actual warmth, actual weight, actual breath.

His hands found the hem of Halle's shirt and hesitated there, fingertips grazing bare skin at the small of Halle's back. The touch made them both shiver.

"God," Jun murmured against Halle's mouth. "I forgot what this was like. Just—having you *there*."

He wasn't talking about the wall. He wasn't talking about the shirt.

He'd gotten so used to reaching across the bed and finding nothing. To waking up disoriented, expecting weight beside him, and remembering all over again. To existing in that hollow half-state where a relationship was maintained through texts and patchy video calls and the ache of wanting to simply *be in the same room*.

Now they were in the same room. Now Halle's hands were on him and his hands were on Halle and the flat was quiet except for their breathing and the sound of finally, finally.

Jun pulled back just enough to look—at Halle's face, flushed and close and *here*—and something in his chest went tight.

"I don't want to let go," he said, and it came out more vulnerable than he intended. "I know that's—I know we should—I just—"

He kissed Halle's jaw instead of finishing the sentence. Then his throat. Then the spot above his collarbone where the pulse was beating hard and fast.

"Later," he decided. "We'll be normal people later."

Right now, the hallway was enough.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My fingers curl into the fabric of your shirt. "Forget normal," I murmur, voice rough. "We've been normal for five damn months." I pull you back to me, kissing you like I'm trying to erase the distance all at once.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun let himself be pulled back in, and the sound that escaped him was somewhere between a laugh and a groan. Halle had always been better at this—the immediacy, the willingness to throw caution to the wind. Jun had spent five months composing careful messages, choosing the right words, maintaining something careful and constructed across thousands of miles. But Halle just *wanted* him, openly and without apology, and that certainty undid him every time.

"Five months," Jun echoed, the words pressed into the curve of Halle's neck. "One hundred and fifty-three days. I counted."

He'd counted more than that. He'd counted the hours. The minutes. The number of times he'd drafted a text and deleted it because *I miss you so much I can't breathe* wasn't the kind of thing you sent when someone was trying to do their job in a war zone.

But Halle wasn't in a war zone anymore. Halle was right here, solid and warm and pulling at Jun's shirt like he intended to get them both naked in the hallway, and Jun was suddenly, viscerally aware that they had the whole night. The whole week. The whole indefinite stretch of days where he didn't have to say goodbye in the morning.

His hands finally pushed Halle's shirt up, palms flat against bare skin. Halle's stomach rose and fell under his touch, and Jun traced the lines of muscle and bone like he was memorizing a map.

"You're here," he said again, quieter now. "You're *here*."

He walked them backward, toward the bedroom, unwilling to break contact. The flat was exactly as he'd left it—Halle's shoes by the door, a coffee mug on the counter that probably belonged to the before-Jun, the same throw blanket on the couch that had been his companion through countless empty evenings.

None of it mattered. The only thing that mattered was the body against his, the heartbeat he could feel through their clothes, the real and solid proof that the deployment was over and this was happening and he was never going back to that hollow half-life again.

The bedroom door hit his shoulder and he reached back to push it open without looking, without breaking the kiss, because he'd spent five months not being able to touch and he wasn't about to start now.

"I need you to know," Jun said against Halle's mouth, "that I thought about this every single day. Every single day, Halle. I need you to know that."

His forehead dropped to Halle's shoulder, and he stood there for a moment, breathing hard, overwhelmed by the simple reality of having a body to hold.

"Okay," he said, mostly to himself. "Okay. I'm good. I'm—"

He lifted his head, looked at Halle, and smiled—crooked and helpless and completely gone.

"Take me to bed."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bedroom was dim, curtains drawn against the late afternoon light, and Jun didn't bother to turn on a lamp. He didn't need to see. He'd spent five months memorizing Halle from pixelated video calls and it wouldn't have mattered if the room had been pitch black—he knew this body, these hands, the specific way Halle moved when he was trying to hold himself together.

They fell onto the bed in a tangle of limbs, and Jun followed Halle down, covering him, bracketing him with arms and legs and every part of him he could offer. The mattress dipped. The sheets were cool—clean ones, Jun realized distantly, because Halle had probably changed them sometime this week in anticipation. The thought made his chest ache.

"You're real," he said again, wonderstruck, palms mapping the planes of Halle's chest. "You're warm. You're—"

Words failed. He bent and pressed his mouth to Halle's collarbone, tasting salt and skin and *here*, and felt hands in his hair, pulling him closer, and lost the thread of whatever he'd been trying to say.

Later, tangled together in sheets that smelled like them both, Jun traced lazy patterns on Halle's shoulder while his breathing slowly evened out. The room was quiet except for the sound of their heartbeats finding synchronization again.

"I don't know how to stop staring at you," Jun admitted, voice drowsy and unguarded. "You should know that. It's going to be a problem."

His phone buzzed somewhere in the flat—probably the group chat, people sharing updates about the rest of the unit coming home. Jun didn't move to check it. There would be time. There was nothing but time now.

He pressed a kiss to Halle's temple, lingering there, breathing him in.

"I'm never deploying again," he said, and the quiet certainty in his voice was the closest thing to a vow he'd ever made. "I don't care what they offer. I'm not leaving again."

Ninety minutes home. He had the rest of his life.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I turn my head to catch your lips again, lazy and slow this time. "You'd better not," I murmur. My hand finds yours on my shoulder, lacing our fingers together. "I don't think I could survive a rerun."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun squeezed Halle's fingers, holding on like the gesture alone could make up for all the nights he'd reached for a body that wasn't there.

"You won't have to," he said, the words soft and certain against Halle's mouth. "I'm here now. I'm *staying*."

He shifted closer, pulling their joined hands to his chest where his heart was still beating faster than resting rate probably warranted. Let Halle feel it. Let him know what this did to Jun—just having him near, just being allowed to touch.

"The unit chat is probably losing its mind," Jun noted, not making any move to check his phone. "Rodriguez promised he'd drink himself into the ER when he finally got home. Chen's probably already crying into a steak dinner. I don't care."

He turned his head, nose brushing Halle's cheek, eyes falling shut.

"I spent five months watching you through a screen," he said, quieter now. "Watching you eat dinner alone. Watched you fall asleep on the couch waiting up for my calls. I know you did that, you know. Don't think I didn't notice."

His thumb traced circles on Halle's knuckles.

"I'm going to be insufferable," Jun admitted, a hint of his old humor surfacing. "Just so you're prepared. I'm going to text you from the other room. I'm going to cook you breakfast every morning. I'm going to—"

He stopped, something catching in his throat.

"I'm going to be so annoying about loving you. You should probably have that warning."

His lips found Halle's jaw, lingering there.

"I have a lot of time to make up for."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun forgot how to think.

That was the thing—the thing he'd forgotten in all those months of careful, distant correspondence and carefully timed phone calls and carefully worded messages that never quite captured the truth of what he felt. He'd forgotten what it felt like to simply *experience* without the buffer of distance, without the cold edge of a screen between them.

Halle's hands were clever and unhurried, and Jun arched into the touch like his body remembered something his mind had tried to catalog and file away for later. There was no later now. Later was here, now, happening, and Jun was falling apart in the best possible way.

"Oh," he managed, the syllable escaping him unbidden. His fingers found Halle's hair, curling into it, anchoring himself to something solid while everything else dissolved. "Halle, I—"

He didn't finish. Language felt inadequate. He'd written Halle letters—a dozen of them, never sent, stored in a folder on his phone because putting pen to paper felt too permanent and too painful at the same time. He'd told Halle things in those letters that he couldn't say out loud, not because they were secrets but because speaking them aloud made them too real.

But this was real. This was real, and Halle was here, and Jun was shaking apart under hands and mouth and the whole overwhelming weight of *finally*.

His breath caught. His chest. His throat. Somewhere in the tangle of sensation, his eyes were burning and he couldn't tell if it was from the intensity or the emotion or the simple, devastating relief of being held by someone who knew exactly how to take him apart and put him back together.

"Hundred and fifty-three days," Jun gasped, the number escaping him like a confession. "I thought about this—I thought about *you*—every single—"

His voice broke. He pulled Halle up, needing to see his face, needing the confirmation of eyes and breath and the specific curve of that mouth, and when their gazes met, something in Jun's chest cracked open.

"I love you," he said, and it wasn't enough, nothing would ever be enough, but he needed Halle to hear it anyway. "I love you, I love you, I've loved you every single day of this and I'm going to love you every single day of whatever comes next—"

Halle kissed him, swallowing the rest, and Jun let himself be undone.

---

Later—much later—they lay in the wreckage of the sheets, sweat cooling on their skin, and Jun was crying. Not dramatically, not with sobs. Just a quiet overflow that he couldn't seem to stop, tears tracking silently down his temples into his hairline while Halle's fingers traced idle patterns on his hip.

"I'm sorry," Jun said, laughing wetly at himself. "I don't know why—this isn't—I just—"

Halle shushed him, pulling him closer, and Jun went willingly, burying his face against Halle's neck.

He'd kept it together through the airport. Through the drive home. Through the moment he'd first seen Halle standing in the doorway of their flat, solid and real and *here*. He'd kept it together because that's what he did—he held himself upright, he functioned, he moved forward one step at a time because falling apart wasn't an option when you were seven thousand miles from home and the only thing keeping you going was the knowledge that eventually, eventually, eventually.

But now he was here. Now he was safe. And the weight of all those days caught up with him all at once, and he couldn't stop the tears, and Halle just held him through it, steady as a heartbeat, present as gravity.

"I've got you," Halle murmured against his hair. "I'm here. I've got you."

Jun nodded against his neck, clutching him tighter.

"I know," he whispered. "I know. That's the thing—I finally know."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I just hold you until you're quiet. Then I brush my thumb under your eye. "You're gonna be stuck with me for a long time," I say, voice rough with sleep and emotion. "Think you can handle that?"

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughed, the sound still wet at the edges, and caught Halle's hand against his cheek. He turned his head to press a kiss to the palm—the same palm that had mapped his skin, that had pulled him apart and put him back together, that belonged to the person who had kept him tethered to sanity across five months of impossible distance.

"Handle it?" Jun repeated, something wondering in his voice. "Halle, I've been handling it for six years. I handled it before you even knew I existed. I handled it through two years of asking you for coffee and getting shot down—do not laugh, I remember every single time—"

His whole body tightened, the wave cresting, and he held her gaze as it crashed over him—held it and held it and let her name spill out of his mouth like the only word that still made sense.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I cry out, my fingers digging hard into your shoulders as I shatter against you. It’s messy and loud and I don't care who hears. I hold onto you through it, pulling you deeper. "Jun," I gasp, my voice wrecked. "Right here."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's whole body shuddered through the crash, through the bright, obliterating wave of it, and he didn't close his eyes. He watched Halle's face—the way her mouth fell open, the way her eyes went dark and wide, the way she said his name like it was the only word she remembered how to make. He felt her clench around him, pull him deeper, and the sound he made in response wasn't a word at all. Just a broken, guttural thing dragged up from the place where language stopped mattering.

He held on. Actually held on—his arms wrapped around her, his face buried in the curve of her neck, his entire body trembling with the aftershocks. For a long moment, he couldn't speak. Could barely breathe. Could only lie there with Halle in his arms and the neighbors' renewed enmity and the distant, dawning realization that he was home. Actually home. Not a video call. Not a letter. Not a voice on a satellite phone that cut out every third word.

*Home.*

When he finally found his voice, it came out hoarse and amused and still a little shaky. "We're definitely getting a noise complaint." He pressed a kiss to her shoulder, her collarbone, the corner of her jaw. "Worth it. Totally worth it. I'll bake them a casserole. I'll write them an apology letter. I'll—"

He stopped, pulling back just enough to look at her face, and whatever joke he'd been about to make dissolved on his tongue. His brow furrowed, not with concern but with the overwhelming weight of *this moment*, this impossible, miraculous moment he'd been trying not to hope for in case hoping jinxed it.

"I was afraid," he said quietly, the admission slipping out before he could catch it. "That I'd come back and it wouldn't... that something would be different. That I'd be different. That you'd feel like a stranger." His thumb traced her cheekbone, reverent. "You don't. You feel like home. You feel exactly like home."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I catch your hand, press your palm flat against my chest so you can feel my heart still hammering. "You're home," I say, voice rough. "That's all that's ever mattered."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's breath caught as Halle pressed his palm flat against her chest, the rhythm of her heartbeat hammering against his hand like proof. Like evidence. Like every letter he'd written and every promise he'd made was being stamped *confirmed* right here, right now, against the warm skin of her chest.

He couldn't speak for a moment. Could only feel—the steady thud-thud-thud under his palm, the rise and fall of her breathing, the way her hand held his in place like she was afraid he might float away if she let go.

"Home," he repeated, and the word cracked in the middle. "Yeah. That's—yeah."

He didn't bother trying to stop the tears this time. Let them track down his temples, into his hair, onto the pillow that smelled like fabric softener and Halle and everything he'd been trying not to miss too much in case the missing swallowed him whole. His thumb moved against her skin, a tiny, unconscious rhythm, matching her heartbeat.

"I'm not going back," he said, and it came out fiercer than he'd intended, almost defiant, like he was daring the universe to argue with him. "I put in the paperwork. Three weeks ago. Transfer to a stateside training post. It's not official yet, but it's—it's in motion. I should've told you on the phone but I didn't want to jinx it, and then I thought I'd tell you at the door, but then the door opened and I forgot every single thing I'd planned to say."

He laughed, wet and unsteady, and turned his head to press a kiss to the inside of her wrist. "So you're stuck with me. Full-time. No more deployments. I'm gonna be the most annoying husband in the continental United States. You're gonna get so sick of me."

The hand on her chest pressed just a little firmer, like he was trying to memorize the feel of her heartbeat from the inside. "I love you," he said, and it was simpler than everything else he'd said tonight, stripped down to the bones. "That's it. That's the whole thing. I love you and I'm home and I'm never leaving again. Everything else is just details."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I let out a watery laugh, shaking my head. "You think I haven't been waiting for you to be annoying full-time?" I pull you down until your head rests on my chest, my fingers combing through your sweat-damp hair. "Welcome home, husband."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The moment Halle stepped into him, the remaining ninety minutes of restraint Jun had managed since landing evaporated entirely. He didn't care about the bag hitting the floor, or whether the front door had even clicked fully shut behind them. 

His hands found Halle's waist, heavy and urgent, his fingers digging into the fabric of their shirt to drag them flush against his chest. He let out a low, rough sound—halfway between a sigh and a grunt of relief—and buried his face in the crook of Halle's neck first, just to breathe them in. The familiar, warm scent of home, of *them*, hit him like a physical blow. 

He didn't stay there for more than a second. Jun pulled back just enough to find Halle's mouth, his lips parting in a hard, demanding kiss that had absolutely no patience in it. Five months of cold bunks and empty nights were poured into the pressure of his mouth against theirs, greedy and completely unashamed of how badly he needed this. He crowded Halle back against the nearest solid surface, his thigh instantly wedgeing between theirs to anchor them both.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I gasp into the kiss, my hands fisting in his jacket. *Finally.* My whole body feels electric and starved at once. I bite his lip lightly, just to hear him react.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The sharp pinch of Halle’s teeth against his lip drew a dark, jagged growl from the back of Jun’s throat. It was a jolt of pure heat that went straight to his spine, shattering whatever microscopic thread of restraint he had left. 

He didn't want to be gentle. He didn't want to go slow. 

His hands abandoned Halle’s waist, his fingers tearing at the zipper of his own heavy uniform jacket with clumsy, desperate impatience. He didn't care about tearing the fabric; he just needed the barrier gone. He shrugged the heavy coat off his shoulders and let it drop uselessly to the floor to join Halle’s bag, immediately bringing his hands back to where they belonged. 

His palms slid up under Halle's shirt, his calloused hands making direct, greedy contact with the warm bare skin of their ribs. He shuddered at the touch, a breathless, ragged sound escaping him as he pressed his weight fully into them, pinning Halle securely against the wall. His thigh nudged higher, insistent and heavy, making his desperation entirely unmistakable. 

Jun deepened the kiss, his tongue sliding past Halle's lips to claim their mouth with a bruising, hungry intensity. He was half-blind with the sheer relief of having them in his arms again. He wanted to consume them, to be consumed, to drown out the last five months of quiet, sterile isolation with the loud, chaotic heat of Halle's body against his. 

"God, Halle," he breathed, the words muffled and rough against their lips as he tore his mouth away for a fraction of a second, only to press his face into the side of their neck, his teeth grazing the sensitive skin of their jaw. "Tell me we aren't making it to the bedroom. Tell me right now."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't need a verbal answer. The way Halle kept kissing him, desperate and relentless, was answer enough. The bedroom was twenty feet down the hall, but right now, it might as well have been on another continent. He wasn't going to make it. He didn't want to.

With a low, gravelly groan, Jun hooked his hands under Halle's thighs, lifting them effortlessly to wrap their legs around his waist. He wanted them closer, wanting absolutely no space between them. He used his weight to pin them firmly against the wall, his head burying back into the crook of Halle's neck with a needy, open-mouthed kiss that turned into a sharp, possessive bite. 

"Good," he growled against their skin, his breath hot and ragged. "Because I'm not letting you go."

His hands slid up from their thighs, one gripping Halle's hip to keep them anchored high against him, while the other reached with blind, frantic impatience for the hem of Halle's shirt. He bunched the fabric in his fist, tugging it upward to get it over their head. He didn't care where it landed. He just needed it gone. 

The moment the fabric cleared, his bare chest pressed flat against theirs, the heat of the skin-on-skin contact making him shudder. He captured Halle's mouth again, his tongue sliding deep, tasting them, utterly consumed by the friction of their bodies and the tight, desperate squeeze of Halle's legs around his hips.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh breathlessly against his mouth. "Bedroom's overrated." My hands slide into his hair, tugging just enough to sting. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The rough rumble of a laugh vibrated in Jun's chest, pressing directly against Halle's bare skin. The sharp sting of their fingers in his hair didn't make him back off; instead, he leaned into the pressure, his eyes darkening as he stared down at them for one breathless, burning second. 

"Not planning on it," he muttered, his voice thick and entirely stripped of his usual composure. 

He didn't give them a chance to reply. Jun adjusted his grip, his powerful forearms locking beneath Halle's thighs to hold them securely against his hips as he crowded them hard against the wall. The solid plaster behind Halle anchorered them, but it was Jun's body doing all the trapping. 

His hand abandoned one thigh, sliding upward with frantic, trembling haste to find the waistband of Halle's pants. He wasn't going to waste time with neatness. His fingers fumbled with the button and the zipper, his breathing harsh and uneven in the small space of the hallway. Every brush of his knuckles against their lower stomach made his own muscles coil tighter. 

"I missed you so much it felt like chest pain," he growled against Halle's lips, the confession raw and entirely devoid of pride. He kissed them again, a deep, bruising tilt of his head that drank in their breath, his tongue tangling with theirs in a desperate, demanding rhythm. 

With a final, impatient tug, he worked his hand past the loosened fabric, his calloused palm cupping the bare, burning curve of Halle's hip. He squeezed, hard enough to leave a mark, dragging them flush against his center so they could feel exactly how close he was to the edge.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn’t give a single damn about tomorrow. He didn't care about the trail of denim, cotton, and heavy leather boots they left scattered across the floorboards like a breadcrumb trail of pure, unadulterated desperation. All that mattered was the sudden, breathtaking reality of Halle's bare skin against his, warm and real and finally, *finally* within reach.

He backed Halle up another step, his hands sliding down to grip their bare hips with bruising force, lifting them slightly to align their bodies. The cool air of the hallway hit his bare back, but he was burning from the inside out. He buried his face in the crook of Halle’s neck, his chest heaving as he inhaled the scent of them, mixed now with the sharp, intoxicating heat of their shared exertion.

"Let them stay there," Jun growled, his voice a low, vibrating rasp against Halle's skin. He nipped at the column of their throat, his hands tracing the curve of their waist, memorizing the shape of them all over again. "I'm not looking at anything but you."

He pressed closer, his thighs crowding theirs, the friction of their naked bodies sending a jolt of pure adrenaline through his veins. He was shaking, a fine, desperate tremor in his hands as he cupped Halle's face, forcing them to look at him. His dark eyes were blown out, heavy-lidded and fiercely possessive. 

"Halle. Look at me," he breathed, his thumb sweeping over their cheekbone before sliding down to trace their lower lip. "I'm home. I'm right here."

He didn't wait, sealing his mouth over theirs again, the kiss deeper, wetter, and utterly demanding, his hands sliding down to cradle their thighs and lift them higher, desperate to close the final, agonizing inch between them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to get a full breath, my fingers digging into his shoulders. "Prove it."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The challenge was a match dropped into a pool of gasoline. Jun didn't hesitate. A dark, breathless sound rumbled in his chest, his eyes locking onto Halle's with a fierce, burning intensity that promised absolutely no mercy. 

"Fucking gladly," he rasped.

He didn't waste another second. Jun shifted his grip, his calloused hands anchoring Halle's hips with a bruising, unyielding hold, lifting them just enough to align their bodies perfectly against the wall. With a sharp, ragged exhale, he drove forward, burying himself inside them in one deep, heavy, desperate motion.

The sensation of finally being *there*, where he belonged, made Jun's entire body shudder. He let out a choked groan against Halle's neck, his forehead pressing hard against their shoulder as he clung to them like a drowning man. His muscles coiled tight, every nerve ending in his body screaming with the sheer, overwhelming relief of it. He was home. Really, truly home.

He didn't give either of them time to catch their breath. Jun began to move, his pace fast and entirely lacking in finesse, driven by five months of starvation. Each stroke was deep and hard, his hips slamming flush against theirs, the hot, rhythmic friction of their skin filling the quiet hallway. He was desperate, greedy, his fingers digging deep into the soft flesh of Halle's thighs to hold them steady against his relentless, driving rhythm. 

He lifted his head, his face flushed and his breathing harsh, looking down at them to watch the way their expression shattered. He wanted to see every single detail of what he was doing to them. 

"Tell me," Jun demanded, his voice a broken, gravelly command as he hit them deep again, his chest heaving. "Tell me you feel me, Halle. Tell me I'm here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun barely registered the transition from the hard plaster of the hallway to the yielding mattress of their bedroom, only that suddenly he was flat on his back, the cool sheets a stark contrast to the burning heat of his skin. 

He didn't have the strength—or the desire—to protest the sudden shift in control. The moment Halle’s hands and mouth found him, any lingering need to dominate evaporated, replaced by a helpless, shuddering surrender. Five months of starvation had left his nerve endings raw, and the sudden, deliberate shift in pace was absolute torture. 

Every touch of Halle's fingers, every hot, agonizingly slow slide of their mouth against his skin, made his entire body jerk. Jun’s hands immediately flew to Halle's hair, his fingers tangling in the strands, not to push them away but to anchor himself to the earth as his hips arched off the mattress. 

"Halle—*fuck*," he gasped, his head rolling back into the pillows. 

The slow, systematic way Halle was taking him apart was driving him entirely out of his mind. He was used to rough, fast, military efficiency, but this exquisite patience was threatening to shatter him completely. His chest heaved, his stomach muscles coiling tight and rigid as Halle's mouth moved lower, marking him, tasting him with a deliberate focus that made Jun's vision go dark at the edges. 

He closed his eyes, his teeth grinding together to hold back a desperate sound. He was completely exposed, entirely at their mercy, and his hands trembled where they gripped the sheets, turning his knuckles white. 

"Don't... don't make me wait," he choked out, his voice a broken, gravelly plea as he tilted his pelvis up, silently begging for the friction, for the heat, for anything to quiet the screaming ache in his blood. "Halle, please. I'm going to lose it."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My mouth leaves his skin just long enough to form words. "Lose it, then." I watch his face, my palm pressing against his chest to keep him still. "I want to see."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The weight of Halle’s hand on his chest felt like an anchor and a brand all at once. Jun’s ribs expanded in ragged, shallow jerks beneath that palm, his heart hammering so violently against his breastbone he was certain Halle could feel every single beat. 

At the command, a broken, helpless sound spilled from his throat—a surrender he would have never given anyone else in the world. His eyes snapped open, dark and completely unfocused, staring up at Halle through a haze of pure, agonizing pleasure. 

"You're cruel," he panted, the accusation entirely lacking any real bite, thick with a desperation that bordered on physical pain. 

His fingers, still tangled in the sheets, tightened until the fabric groaned under the strain. He tried to lift his hips, tried to seek out the unbearable heat of Halle's mouth and hands, but the firm, heavy press of Halle’s palm kept him anchored to the mattress, forcing him to endure the slow, exquisite torture. He was completely at their mercy, stripped of his uniform, his armor, and his pride. 

He couldn't hold it back. The five months of cold, silent nights, the endless weeks of wanting, and the sheer, overwhelming reality of finally being touched like this all coalesced into a single, unstoppable wave of heat. 

Jun's jaw clenched, the muscles in his neck and shoulders straining as his back arched off the bed. A low, desperate groan tore from deep in his chest, raw and entirely unrefined. He let himself unravel right there under Halle's unwavering gaze, his eyes locking onto theirs, pleading and completely undone. He was shaking, his entire body trembling with the force of his release, completely consumed by the sight of the person he loved watching him shatter.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The sharp pull at the back of his neck dragged Jun down, his chest crashing flush against Halle's with a heavy, breathless impact. Her words—sharp, demanding, and utterly devoid of patience—sliced straight through the lingering, soft haze of his release, instantly igniting something far more volatile in his blood. 

He didn't need to be told twice. 

With a low, dark growl that vibrated deep in his throat, Jun seized her wrists, pinning them to the mattress above her head. His calloused fingers locked like iron bands around her skin. He didn't cushion his weight this time; he pressed her down, his heavy, solid frame crushing her into the mattress, making sure she felt every single pound of him. 

"You want to feel it tomorrow?" he rasped, his eyes dark, blown out, and entirely dangerous. He leaned down, his mouth hovering a fraction of an inch from hers, his breath hot and ragged. "Fine."

He didn't wait. Jun drove into her again, hard and unyielding, a brutal, driving rhythm that had no room for softness. His hips slammed against hers with bruising force, the wet, heavy friction of their bodies echoing in the quiet bedroom. He wanted to leave marks. He wanted to brand her so deeply that the memory of him would ache in her bones for days. 

His teeth found the junction where her neck met her shoulder, biting down hard enough to leave a deep, dark mark, his tongue immediately sliding over the sting before he bit again, harder. He was relentless, his movements primal and desperate, fueled by nineteen weeks of starvation and the absolute permission to take exactly what he wanted. 

He freed her wrists only to slide his hands down her body, his fingers digging mercilessly into her hips, lifting her to meet every heavy, deep thrust. He was panting, his forehead pressed against hers, his eyes locked onto her face to drink in every shattered breath and tight clench of her jaw. 

"I'm going to bruise you, Halle," he promised, a ragged, breathless warning as he hit her deep, his chest heaving. "I'm going to make sure you can't walk tomorrow without thinking of me."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I gasp, arching into the sharp bite of his teeth. "Good." My hands scramble against his back, nails dragging down his skin. "I'll wear it like a fucking trophy."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The sharp sting of Halle's nails dragging down his back didn't make Jun flinch; it made him burn. He let out a sharp, ragged hiss of a breath, his muscles locking up for a fraction of a second before the pain translated directly into pure, unadulterated adrenaline. 

"A trophy," he growled, the word vibrating against the wet skin of her shoulder where his teeth had just been. He lifted his head, his dark eyes blazing down at her, entirely wild and consumed by her. "I'll give you a dozen."

He gripped her hips even tighter, his calloused thumbs digging into the soft skin of her waist to anchor her as he drove into her with a heavy, relentless pace. Every slam of his hips was a declaration, a desperate, physical demand for her to remember exactly who she belonged to. He wanted to lose himself in her completely. The five months of sterile, quiet isolation, the endless, grinding routine of deployment—all of it was being violently obliterated by the sound of her breath catching, the claw of her nails, and the overwhelming heat of her body wrapped around his.

Jun leaned down, capturing her mouth in a kiss that was almost bruising, his tongue sliding deep to taste her gasp. He was panting, his chest heaving against hers, sweat slicking his shoulders as he poured every ounce of his starved, desperate love into the rhythm. He didn't want to think; he just wanted to feel her, to mark her, to make sure that when he finally closed his eyes tonight, he would know beyond a shadow of a doubt that he was finally, truly home.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
"Let them listen," Jun rasped, the words half-lost in a harsh, ragged exhale against her temple. 

He didn't care. He didn't have the capacity to care about anything beyond the boundaries of this mattress, the damp heat of her skin, and the tight, desperate way she clung to him. The quiet of the last five months had been a slow, suffocating weight; the noise they were making now was the only proof he had that he was alive, that he was actually back in their room, in their bed, buried so deep inside her that he couldn't tell where his own body ended and hers began.

He didn't slow down. If anything, her demand only made him more reckless. His hands, slick with sweat, gripped her hips with a crushing force, anchoring her to the mattress as he drove into her again and again. The rhythm was punishing, raw, and completely stripped of any hesitation. He slid his hands up her torso, his calloused fingers digging into her ribs, pulling her up to meet him, wanting every single fraction of an inch he could possibly take. "Halle, look at me. Don't close your eyes."

He needed to see her face when it happened. He needed the visual proof of her surrender to match the tight, pulsing heat of her body clamping down around him. His movements became faster, shallower, driven by a sudden, frantic desperation as the pressure behind his hips reached a breaking point. He bit his own lip, drawing the metallic taste of blood, his head shaking as he fought to stay under just a second longer, to stretch the agony of it out until she was right there with him.

With a final, blind surge of effort, Jun buried himself inside her as deeply as he could go, his entire body locking up, rigid and straining. A dark, shattered sound tore from his chest, his eyes wide and burning as he stared down at her, completely undone, his release tearing through him in heavy, violent waves that left him utterly breathless and shaking against her.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp, breathless cry, my back arching off the mattress. My hands fly to his face, holding his gaze as I shatter completely, my body clenching around his in a series of deep, shuddering pulses. I don't close my eyes.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The tight, rhythmic pulses of Halle’s body clenching around his sent a secondary, helpless shudder through Jun’s spent muscles. He let out a long, trembling groan, his forehead dropping to rest against hers as her hands held his face. He didn't pull out. He couldn't. He was entirely drained, his limbs heavy and shaking, but the sheer, overwhelming proximity of her was an anchor he refused to let go of. 

He leaned heavily into the touch of her hands, his rough, unshaven cheek scraping against her palms. He kissed the fleshy base of her thumb, his lips hot and damp, his chest still heaving in ragged, shallow jerks against her ribs. 

"God, Halle," he breathed, the words a fractured whisper between their lips. He closed his eyes for just a second, tasting the salt of sweat, before forcing them open again to look at her. She was flushed, her breathing as wrecked as his, her eyes still holding that fierce, raw focus that made his chest ache with a sudden, violent swell of emotion. 

He stayed buried inside her, the heavy, pulsing warmth of their connection the only thing keeping him grounded. His hands, still resting on her hips, twitched, his fingers curling slightly into her skin to keep her pressed flush against him. Every small, involuntary twitch of her inner muscles made him squeeze his eyes shut, a breathless, quiet hiss escaping through his teeth. 

With a slow, heavy breath, he shifted his weight, careful not to crush her but refusing to lose an inch of contact. He slid his arms under her shoulders, pulling her body completely up against his, and buried his face in the damp crook of her neck. He inhaled deeply, the scent of her skin, sweat, and sex filling his senses, finally obliterating the sterile, metallic smell of the military transport and the barracks that had haunted him for nineteen weeks. 

"Don't move," he mumbled against her skin, his voice a gravelly, exhausted rasp. He tightened his arms around her, holding her so close it was almost suffocating. "Just... stay right there. Don't let me go yet."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I let out a slow, shaky breath, my arms wrapping around his back, fingers tracing the marks my nails left. "I'm not going anywhere," I murmur, my voice rough. I press a kiss to his temple, feeling the frantic beat of his heart start to slow against my chest. "Welcome home."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The word *home* seemed to vibrate straight through Jun’s chest, settling deep in his bones with a heavy, grounding ache. He let out a long, ragged exhale, the last of the frantic tension finally draining from his shoulders, leaving him completely limp against her. 

As her fingers traced the raw, stinging lines her nails had carved into his back, a slow, involuntary shiver ran down his spine. It hurt, a sharp, localized heat, but it was the best thing he had felt in five months. It was proof. He was actually here, lying in their bed, covered in her sweat and his own, with the scent of her filling his lungs until he felt drunk on it.

He shifted his weight slightly, rolling just enough to the side so he wouldn’t crush her, but he refused to break the contact. He kept one heavy, hair-dusted thigh hooked over both of hers, pinning her to the mattress beneath him, while his arm remained wrapped tightly around her waist, locking her ribs against his chest. 

"Say it again," he muttered, his voice incredibly rough, a low, gravelly vibration against the skin of her neck. He pressed his face deeper into her collarbone, his lips brushing the warm, damp skin there. He sounded completely wrecked, stripped of the commanding officer he had to be for nineteen weeks, reduced to nothing but a man desperate for his wife. "Halle. Say it again."

He squeezed her waist, his hand twitching against her hip, still possessive even in his exhaustion. He wanted to hear the words until they finally stopped sounding like a dream he was going to wake up from in a cold, metal bunk three thousand miles away.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I smile, feeling the exhaustion starting to settle deep into my muscles. I turn my head just enough to press my lips against the shell of his ear, my voice low and certain. "Welcome home, Jun." I let my hand rest over his heart. "For good this time."
