rung_labels.evidence: buried so deep inside her that he couldn't tell where his own body ended and hers began... Every heavy, driving thrust sent a shudder straight up his spine... With a final, blind surge of effort, Jun buried himself inside her as deeply as he could go, his entire body locking up, rigid and straining

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn’t meet her halfway so much as collide with the life he’d been starving for.

He caught her hard, both arms going around her like he could make up for five months by sheer pressure, by the desperate press of his hands at her back, by the way his face dropped into her hair on a sharp inhale that nearly broke him. He had imagined this a thousand times and not once had his imagination accounted for the actual warmth of her, the real weight of her against him, the familiar scent of home and Halle and safe all at once.

“God,” he said, voice rough, useless. “God, I missed you.”

His duffel slid from his shoulder and hit the floor without ceremony. He didn’t look at it. He didn’t look at anything except her, once he could force himself to pull back the scant inch required to see her face.

There were things he should have said. Careful things. Sweet things. Normal-husband-home-from-deployment things.

Instead, his hands came up to frame her jaw, thumbs brushing over her cheeks like he needed proof she was solid, present, his. His eyes moved over her with absolutely no subtlety at all, hungry and helpless and too honest to soften.

“I had a speech,” he admitted, breath unsteady. “It was terrible. You would’ve laughed at me.”

Then he kissed her.

There was nothing gentle about the first second of it. He meant to be; he truly did. But the moment his mouth found hers, restraint abandoned him completely. His fingers slid into her hair, his other arm locked around her waist, and he pulled her in like he could erase every mile, every bad night, every silent phone call, every time he had stared at a ceiling and wanted this so badly it hurt.

He broke the kiss only because he had to breathe, and even then he didn’t go far. His forehead stayed near hers, his mouth brushing close, his hands still moving over her like stopping would be some kind of sin.

“I’m home,” he said, lower now, the words almost disbelieving. “I’m home, and I am not letting go of you for the rest of the night.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "I know." My voice shakes a little, but I don't care. My hands are tight in his jacket, and I'm kissing him back like I'm trying to climb inside his skin. "I'm not letting you go either." I pull him back in, not even an inch between us, and I don't plan on moving.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a sound into the kiss that was almost relief and almost wreckage.

He had meant to come home composed. He had meant to be decent, measured, patient. He had meant to set down the duffel, take off his boots, ask her how she was before his hands forgot manners entirely.

None of that survived contact with Halle.

His grip tightened at her waist, then shifted, restless and reverent all at once—over her back, into her hair, along the familiar shape of her like he was relearning a language he had never stopped speaking in his sleep. He kissed her again, and again, each one less like a greeting and more like a confession dragged out of him.

“I thought about this every day,” he said against her mouth, the words rough and crowded between kisses. “Every damn day.”

His forehead tipped to hers for half a second, his eyes closed, his breathing already uneven. He looked like a man trying very hard to remember that the world existed beyond the front entryway and failing badly.

“I tried to be normal about it,” he admitted, with a faint, breathless laugh that had no humor in it. “I was not normal about it.”

Jun’s hands slid down to her hips and held there, firm enough to make clear he had no intention of stepping back unless she made him. Even then, he looked like it might hurt.

His gaze lifted to her face again, dark and open and absolutely undone.

“Halle,” he said, and her name came out like the only prayer he remembered. “Tell me if I need to slow down.”

He did not look like he wanted to slow down.

He looked like he would, if she asked. Like he would stop with every muscle in his body protesting, because she mattered more than the hunger clawing through him.

But his thumbs pressed into her hips. His mouth hovered close to hers. His voice dropped, wrecked and honest.

“Please don’t ask me to be casual about being back in your arms.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun lost track of time in the hallway.

It became nothing but the door at his back, the dropped bag somewhere by his boots, the familiar walls of their flat closing around him, and Halle in front of him—real, close, kissing him like the last five months had been something they could burn down with their mouths.

He kept trying to stop long enough to speak. He failed repeatedly.

Every time he managed half a breath, he wasted it on her name.

“Halle.”

Again, lower.

“Halle.”

Like saying it could anchor him. Like he hadn’t spent months whispering it into bad pillows and worse nights, half-delirious with missing her.

His hands were everywhere he could justify and nowhere near enough. Her shoulders. Her waist. Her back. The side of her neck, his thumb brushing there with a tenderness at odds with the way he kept dragging her back into him. He was unsubtle about all of it, openly starving, utterly past pretending he was anything but ruined by being home.

At some point, he remembered the front door existed.

Barely.

Jun reached blindly behind himself, fumbled once, and got it properly shut and locked without looking away for more than a second. The small, decisive click made something in him loosen and tighten all at once.

Home. Locked in. No one else. No orders. No noise. No miles.

Just them.

He let out a breath that shook.

“I’m going to get my boots off,” he said, though he did not move immediately and sounded deeply unconvinced by his own priorities. “Eventually.”

His mouth found the corner of hers again, then her cheek, then her jaw, each kiss pressed there like he was counting proof.

“I should put my bag somewhere,” he added, just as uselessly.

He made no attempt to do that either.

Instead, Jun bent his head and held her closer, his face tucked against her neck for one long, unsteady moment. The desperate edge of him softened there—not gone, not even close, but threaded through with something more fragile. Relief. Exhaustion. The sudden, crushing safety of finally being allowed to fall apart.

“I hated being away from you,” he said, voice muffled and raw. “I was good at it. I did it. I got through it. But I hated it.”

His fingers flexed at her back.

“And now I’m here, and I don’t want to waste one second pretending I’m not out of my mind over you.”

He lifted his head enough to look at her again. His eyes moved over her face with helpless devotion, his mouth still too close, his breath still uneven.

Then his expression changed—just slightly. A flicker of awareness through all that hunger. Not distance. Never distance. But care.

Jun swallowed.

“I need to know you’re okay,” he said, quieter. “Not because I want to stop. I really, really do not want to stop.” A rough, almost disbelieving laugh escaped him. “But I’ve been gone five months, and I came through that door like a damn avalanche.”

His hand rose to her cheek again, thumb brushing slow.

“So tell me what you want from me tonight,” he said. “Anything. Everything. Bed, shower, couch, floor, dinner I absolutely will burn because I can’t think straight—whatever you want.”

His gaze dropped to her mouth and stayed there too long.

Then he dragged it back up with visible effort.

“But if the answer is me,” Jun said, voice dropping to something bare and fervent, “then, sweetheart, I am already yours.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pull him back to me, my hands framing his face. "I want you, Jun. I want you in our bed, now." I'm already backing us toward the bedroom, not willing to let go for even a second. "I don't want you to think straight."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s expression cracked open at that.

For one suspended second, he just stared at her like she had handed him every impossible thing he had wanted and dared him to survive it.

Then he breathed, “Thank God.”

It came out wrecked. Devout. Almost a laugh, except there was too much longing in it to be funny.

Jun went where she pulled him, absolutely without resistance, his hands still on her like letting go would offend him personally. He stumbled once over his own duffel and did not even bother looking down.

“Bag can rot there,” he muttered against her mouth.

His jacket was next. He shrugged out of it with the kind of impatient violence usually reserved for emergencies, one sleeve catching at his wrist and making him curse under his breath before he finally got free of it. It hit the floor somewhere behind him.

Boots, he remembered dimly. Boots were a problem.

Jun broke away only long enough to brace one hand against the wall and shove one off with the other heel, then the second, breathless and clumsy and visibly furious that footwear existed at all.

“I have hated these boots for five months,” he said, voice low and rough. “Never more than right now.”

Then he was back on her.

No space. No hesitation. His hands found her face again, then her waist, then spread over her back as he kissed her with all the restraint he did not possess. Every few steps toward the bedroom, he had to stop them just to kiss her properly, like the destination mattered desperately but not enough to interrupt the feeling of her mouth under his.

At the bedroom doorway, Jun went still for half a heartbeat.

Their room.

Their bed.

The ordinary shape of their life waiting for him like it had been holding its breath too.

Something in his face softened so suddenly it almost looked painful.

“I dreamed about this room,” he admitted, barely above a whisper. “About coming back to you here.”

His hand slid up to the side of her neck, thumb careful there despite the rest of him looking anything but. His eyes held on her face, dark and intent.

“And for the record,” he said, voice dropping again, rougher now, “I am done thinking straight.”

Then Jun kissed her like he meant to prove it.

He crossed the threshold with her, shedding the last of his composure somewhere between the door and the bed. Whatever careful, civilized version of himself he had intended to bring home had not made it past the hallway. What remained was all hunger and devotion, all shaking relief, all five months of wanting compressed into the urgent press of his hands and the broken sound he made when he finally had her close enough.

“Mine,” he breathed, not possessive like a claim so much as disbelieving like a prayer answered. Then immediately, because even undone he was still Jun, still hers, “Yours. God, Halle, I’m yours.”

The edge in him did not fade.

It turned warmer. Deeper. No less desperate, but threaded through with worship now, with the reverent disbelief of a man who had come home and found everything he loved waiting for him.

He followed her down onto their bed with a low, unsteady exhale, one hand braced beside her, the other still at her cheek. For a moment he just looked at her, breathing hard, eyes moving over her face like he was memorizing the miracle of it all over again.

“I love you,” he said, raw and immediate. “I love you. I missed you so much I didn’t know what to do with myself.”

His mouth found hers again before the last word was fully gone.

After that, Jun stopped trying to be eloquent. He stopped trying to be anything except home.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun did not think the trail of clothes was funny yet.

Tomorrow, maybe. Tomorrow he might stand in the hallway with coffee in his hand, look at the evidence of how completely they had failed to make it to the bedroom like civilized people, and laugh until his ribs hurt.

Right then, he only cared that there was less between them.

Fabric became an enemy. Buttons became an insult. Anything that slowed his hands down earned a rough, impatient sound from him, half curse and half plea. But even with all that urgency, even with his breathing uneven and his self-control in ruins, he kept catching himself at the edge of too much and pulling just enough awareness back into his body to look at her.

To see her.

Not a memory. Not a voice over a bad connection. Not a photo on a phone screen he had stared at until his eyes burned.

Halle. In their bed. With him home.

Jun’s hand braced near her shoulder, his head bowing for one brief, overwhelmed second.

“Still feels like I’m going to wake up,” he said, voice low and rough.

Then his mouth found her skin again, and whatever else he might have said dissolved.

He was not gentle in the way careful men were gentle. There was nothing distant or delicate about him, nothing restrained for the sake of seeming composed. He was gentle the way starving hands could still be devoted, the way desperation could still know exactly where tenderness belonged. Every touch carried the same contradiction—urgent, reverent; possessive, pleading; absolutely ruined and absolutely certain.

He kissed like he had been saving up breath for months and wanted to spend all of it on her.

Again and again, he had to stop only to say things he could not keep inside.

“I missed this.”

A kiss to her shoulder.

“I missed you.”

His forehead pressed briefly to her chest, his breath shaking.

“I missed knowing where to put my hands because they already knew.”

That nearly undid him all over again.

Jun lifted his head, eyes dark and open, and looked at her with no defense left in him at all.

“I love you,” he said again, because it was the truest thing he had and still nowhere near enough. “I love you so much. I’m sorry I was gone. I’m sorry it was so long.”

His jaw tightened, but he did not let the ache pull him away from the moment. Not tonight. Tonight he was home, and Halle was there, and the war, the distance, the waiting, the stale air of barracks rooms and the hollow quiet after calls ended—all of it could stay outside the locked door.

His hand slid carefully along her side, then stopped. He swallowed, visibly dragging himself back from pure instinct.

“Look at me,” he said softly, desperately. “I need to know I’m with you, not just catching up to every damn thing I imagined.”

The need in him did not lessen. If anything, naming it made it sharper. But he stayed there, trembling with the effort of holding himself just enough, his mouth close, his body tense with wanting and restraint both.

“I don’t want slow,” he admitted, a breathless, helpless confession. “I don’t. I want you so badly I can barely stand it.”

His thumb brushed over her cheek.

“But I want you with me more.”

Then, when the moment gave him what he needed, Jun broke apart completely.

Not carelessly. Never that.

But fully.

He bent to her again with a sound that seemed pulled from somewhere five months deep, and the rest of the world finally lost its claim on him. There was only the bed beneath them, the dim familiar room around them, the warmth of her, the rhythm of breath and touch and the relentless, aching relief of being allowed to come home not just to a place, but to a body that knew him.

Jun stopped measuring time.

He stopped trying to make words behave.

He said her name like it was the only language left to him. He buried promises against her skin. He held on as if the night might try to take him back if he loosened his grip, and then softened his hands when love reminded him that he was not holding on to survive anymore.

He was holding on because he could.

Because he was home.

Because she had asked him not to think straight, and God help him, he obeyed.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless, and tug him down to me. "You are with me." My fingers curl into his hair, keeping his gaze locked with mine. "I'm right here, Jun. Stop worrying and just be home."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun went still at that—not because the hunger left him, but because her words landed somewhere deeper than hunger.

Be home.

His breath caught. His eyes stayed on hers, and for one raw second he looked younger than thirty-three, stripped down past pride and bravado and all the rough edges he had dragged back with him. He looked like a man who had been bracing for impact for five months and had just been told he could finally put the weight down.

“Okay,” he whispered.

It shook when he said it.

Then his face changed.

Not calmer. Not exactly. But surrendered.

Jun lowered his forehead to hers for the smallest moment, eyes closing, mouth parted on an uneven breath. His hand slid to the side of her neck, thumb resting there like he needed the pulse under her skin to guide him back into his own body.

“I’m home,” he said again, but this time it wasn’t disbelief.

It was a decision.

Then he stopped fighting himself.

He kissed her with the last of his restraint gone, not frantic now in the way panic was frantic, but deep and certain and completely unguarded. The ache of distance stayed in him, but it changed shape under her hands, under the familiar give of their bed, under the impossible fact of her saying right here like it was that simple.

Maybe it was.

Maybe home had never been the flat, or the bed, or the locked door, or the clothes abandoned behind them like a map of poor self-control.

Maybe home was this: Halle underneath his hands, his name in her mouth, permission and wanting and love all tangled together until Jun could no longer tell which part of him had been starving most.

He gave up trying to.

“Sweetheart,” he breathed, wrecked and grateful, against her mouth.

After that, words came only in fragments.

Her name.

His love.

A rough, helpless “yes” when the night caught up to him and carried him under.

Jun held himself over her like he had crossed continents for the privilege, like every second away from her had taught his body exactly what it meant to return. He touched her with the devotion of a man making up for absence, with the urgency of someone who had counted too many nights alone and refused to waste this one on hesitation.

But he stayed with her.

Every breath. Every kiss. Every unsteady pause where his eyes found hers and something in his face broke open all over again.

He was not thinking straight. He was barely thinking at all.

He was home.

And when that truth finally settled fully into him, when the locked-down, held-together part of Jun at last understood that no one was going to call him away tonight, no one was going to take this room or this bed or this woman from him, he made a sound against her that was almost relief and almost surrender.

“I love you,” he said, hoarse and immediate, because even without thinking he knew that. “God, Halle, I love you.”

The rest of the night blurred at the edges.

Not because it was forgettable.

Because it was too much to hold in clean lines.

There was warmth. There was breath. There was the familiar shape of her beneath his hands and the unfamiliar shock of having it again after so long. There was laughter at some point, brief and breathless, swallowed almost immediately by another kiss. There was Jun losing track of what he meant to say and saying her name instead. There was the bed shifting under them, the room dim around them, his hand searching for hers without conscious thought.

And through all of it, beneath the desperation and the want and the sheer physical relief of being close again, there was the deeper thing:

Jun came back to himself by coming back to her.

Much later, when the sharpest edge of missing had finally burned itself down into something softer, he stayed wrapped around her like he had never learned any other way to sleep. His face pressed near her shoulder. His breathing slowly evened out, then hitched once when exhaustion tried to drag him under and he resisted it out of stubbornness alone.

He lifted his head just enough to look at her.

His hair was a mess. His mouth was soft. His eyes were heavy, but still fixed on her like closing them would be an unacceptable risk.

“I’m trying not to fall asleep,” he murmured, voice rough with fatigue and satisfaction and something tender enough to hurt. “Feels rude after making you wait five months.”

A faint, drowsy smile touched his mouth.

Then his hand moved slowly over her back, no urgency now. Just contact. Proof. Gratitude.

“But if I do,” Jun whispered, “wake me up and tell me I’m still here.”

His eyes stayed open another few seconds, fighting a battle he was absolutely going to lose.

“Tell me I made it home.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun did not stand a chance.

Not against patience. Not against intention. Not against five months of Halle apparently having made plans of her own and now having all the time in the world to ruin him with them.

He had come home ready to be the desperate one. He had come home with all that restless hunger clawing under his skin, with every intention of proving exactly how badly he had missed her.

Instead, she slowed the world down around him until all he could do was feel.

His hands twisted in the sheets. Then released. Then found whatever part of her he could reach, because even when he was losing his mind, he still needed contact. Still needed proof. The room narrowed to breath and warmth and the impossible tenderness of being known too well, loved too deliberately, undone by someone who remembered every way to break him open.

“Halle,” he said, and it barely sounded like a name anymore.

It sounded like surrender.

His head fell back against the bed, eyes squeezed shut for one overwhelmed second before he forced them open again. He wanted to watch. He wanted to survive. He was not confident he could do both.

A laugh broke out of him, wrecked and disbelieving, vanishing almost immediately into a rough inhale.

“You planned this,” he accused, voice gone low and uneven. “You absolutely planned this.”

He sounded grateful enough to make the accusation useless.

Whatever smugness he might have had, whatever teasing he might have managed on any other night, dissolved under the slow certainty of her attention. Jun had endured long days, worse nights, too much noise, too much waiting, too many hours where he had held himself together by force.

This was different.

This was being taken apart by someone who knew where every piece belonged.

His hand covered his face briefly, not to hide from her but because feeling this much after months of feeling distant and rationed and careful nearly split him down the middle. His chest rose hard. His fingers dragged down over his mouth. His eyes found her again, dark and helpless and full of a devotion he had no ability to disguise.

“I missed you,” he said again, because apparently those were the only words he had left. Then, rougher, almost broken with it, “I missed being yours like this.”

The slow pace was agony. It was mercy. It was both so perfectly that Jun could only lie there and take it, breath catching, muscles drawn tight, every bit of him tuned to her with humiliating, honest need.

He had asked not to think straight.

She had made sure he couldn’t.

At some point he reached for her with a hand that shook faintly, not to stop her. Never that. Just because he needed to touch her before the feeling carried him too far away from his own body. His palm found her cheek, his thumb brushing there with aching tenderness.

“Come here,” he breathed, though the words had no command in them. Only want. Only worship. “Please. I need to kiss you.”

He was ruined when he said it. Completely. Beautifully. Home so deep in him now that it hurt less like absence and more like healing.

And when he finally drew her close enough, Jun kissed her like a man thanking the only person who had ever known how to bring him all the way back.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I finally climb up and kiss him slow, letting him taste himself on my mouth. My hands settle on either side of his face, holding him steady. "Now you're home," I whisper against his lips.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun broke on the whisper.

Not loudly. Not all at once.

It was worse than that.

His whole face changed, the last desperate, braced thing in him giving way under the simple certainty of it. Now you’re home. Like she had made it true with her mouth. Like the flat, the bed, the locked door, his abandoned boots, the trail of clothes, all of it had only been waiting for that verdict.

He dragged in a breath that did not quite work.

“Yeah,” he said, rough and almost stunned. “Yeah. I am.”

His hands came up to cover hers where they held his face, and for a second he just stayed there, pinned by her, breathing against her mouth, eyes half-lidded and helplessly fixed on her like he had forgotten how to look away.

Then he kissed her again.

Slow, at first, because she had made him slow. Because she had taken all that frantic hunger and turned it molten, turned it deep, turned it into something that moved through him with no clean edge left to it. His mouth opened under hers with a broken sound, and he shuddered hard enough that his fingers tightened over her hands.

The taste of her, of them, of what she had done to him, made his control slip sideways.

“Halle,” he breathed, and it came out ruined.

His hands slid from hers, down her wrists, her arms, then back to her face like he could not decide where he needed to touch most. Everywhere felt necessary. Everywhere felt like proof. His thumbs brushed her cheeks, reverent even while the rest of him looked seconds from losing whatever patience she had left him with.

“You have no idea what you just did to me,” he said, voice low, ragged with awe and want. Then his mouth tilted, barely, into something like a smile. “Actually, no. You know exactly what you did.”

The smile did not last. He was too undone for it.

Jun shifted under her, restless now, the slow burn she had made of him becoming something sharper again. His hands settled at her waist with unmistakable intent, not forcing, not rushing her past anything, but absolutely finished pretending he had any dignity left.

“I thought I was going to come in here and take you apart,” he admitted, breath catching between words. “I had plans. Terrible, impatient, extremely detailed plans.”

His gaze dropped to her mouth.

He swallowed.

“And then you put your hands on me, and I forgot my own name.”

A breathless laugh escaped him, barely there, almost disbelieving. His grip flexed at her waist.

“But I remember yours.”

He pulled her closer, not enough to decide anything for her, just enough to make his need obvious. Jun had never been subtle on his best day, and this was nowhere near his best day. This was him stripped of distance and discipline and every last pretense of composure. This was him home, loved, wanted, wrecked by the woman he had spent five months aching for.

His mouth found hers again, deeper this time, less patient, all that returned urgency flooding back through him. But it was different now. No panic. No fear that the night would vanish if he blinked. Only hunger, and trust, and the unbearable relief of being allowed to want without rationing it.

When he broke away, his forehead pressed to hers.

“I’m here,” he said, like he still needed to say it. Like part of him still needed to hear himself make the promise. “I’m here. I’m yours. I’m not going anywhere tonight.”

His hands moved slowly up her back, then down again, learning and remembering in the same motion. His eyes stayed on hers, dark and open and entirely without defense.

“And I don’t want to be careful anymore,” Jun whispered. “I’ll be good to you. Always. But careful?”

His mouth brushed hers.

“No. Not tonight.”

Then he kissed her like he meant it.

Jun turned with her in one urgent, fluid motion, chasing closeness, chasing the impossible fact of her beneath his hands and over his heart and everywhere at once. The bed shifted under him, the room dim and familiar around him, but all of his attention narrowed to Halle and the breath between them.

He had missed her laugh. Her voice. Her hands. Her warmth. The way she knew him too well and loved him anyway. The way she could say one sentence and make the whole war inside him go quiet.

He had missed belonging.

Now he belonged so fiercely it made him shake.

“Tell me again,” he said against her mouth, voice nearly gone. “Tell me I’m home.”

His hand slid into her hair, not holding her still so much as holding on.

“Please, sweetheart,” he breathed, desperate and devoted and absolutely hers. “I need to hear it while I make myself believe it.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s restraint snapped so cleanly it almost frightened him.

Almost.

The pressure at the back of his neck dragged a sound out of him—low, rough, nothing polished left in it. His eyes went dark, his breath catching once as if her words had landed directly under his ribs and lit him up from the inside.

“Nineteen weeks,” he repeated, voice hoarse.

Then he gave a short, broken laugh against her mouth, all disbelief and hunger.

“Sweetheart, I counted every damn day.”

For one second, only one, he held himself still. Not gentle. Not hesitant. Just present enough to make sure the want in him did not outrun the woman he loved.

His hand framed her jaw, thumb firm at her cheek.

“If you say stop, I stop,” he said, low and absolute. “Anything else, and I’m done holding back.”

Then Jun stopped being careful.

Not careless. Never careless.

But the softness went out of his hands and came back as certainty. His kisses turned deep and demanding, all the need he had been trying to dress up as patience finally set loose. He moved like a man who had been invited home and intended to prove he understood the gift of it—every touch unapologetic, every breath ragged, every murmured curse breaking apart into her name.

The bed shifted under them. The room blurred. The five months between them burned down to heat and pressure and the solid truth of her beneath him, around him, with him.

Jun forgot the hallway.

Forgot the duffel.

Forgot the boots.

Forgot every hour he had spent staring at distant ceilings, every bad connection, every disciplined silence, every lonely night he had survived by promising himself he would get back to this.

To her.

“Halle,” he said, and it was wrecked beyond recognition.

He gave her what she had asked for: no polite distance, no careful easing back into familiarity, no pretending his hands didn’t shake from wanting. He let the desperation show. Let the hunger have weight. Let himself be the man who had missed his wife so fiercely it had made him unreasonable.

Again and again, he came back to her mouth, to her breath, to the grounding miracle of her being there.

“Tomorrow,” he rasped, barely able to get the word out. “You want to feel it tomorrow?”

His forehead pressed briefly to hers, his voice dropping into something darker, more devoted.

“I want you to feel how much I missed you.”

Then he kissed her again and kept his promise.

By the time the night finally took them apart and put them back together, Jun had lost whatever remained of his composure. He had said her name too many times. He had sworn softly into the dark. He had held on like home was something he could keep by touch alone.

And when the worst of the hunger finally gave way to trembling exhaustion, he stayed close, breathing hard, face tucked near her, one hand still spread over her like he needed proof.

For a while, he could not speak.

Then, wrecked and drowsy and utterly satisfied, Jun managed a rough whisper.

“If tomorrow isn’t enough,” he said, mouth brushing warm against her skin, “I’ll remind you again.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I trace the line of his spine, my own breathing still uneven. "Good." I press a slow kiss to his shoulder. "Because I'm not planning on letting you get too rested."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun shivered under the touch like his body had been waiting five months to remember that exact path.

A slow, ruined smile pulled at his mouth, pressed half-hidden against the bed, his breathing still uneven enough to make the attempt look unfairly difficult. He should have been exhausted. He was exhausted. There was a heavy, bone-deep fatigue in him that deployment had carved out and travel had worsened and the last hour had absolutely not improved.

And still, at her words, his eyes opened.

Dark. Drowsy. Interested.

“Good,” he murmured back, voice rough and nearly gone. “I didn’t come home to sleep.”

That was a lie, technically. At some point his body was going to claim him, probably with embarrassing force. But Jun looked entirely prepared to fight biology out of spite.

He shifted enough to turn toward her, slow now because every muscle in him seemed to be reporting in with opinions. His hand found the curve of her waist and settled there, warm and possessive in the soft aftermath, thumb moving in a lazy stroke that was gentler than anything he had managed earlier.

“Although,” he added, mouth curving a little more, “if you kill me on my first night back, the paperwork is going to be a nightmare.”

His smile faded into something softer almost immediately.

Jun looked at her like he had forgotten how not to.

The desperation had quieted, but it had not disappeared. It had only sunk deeper, gone from flame to ember, steady and dangerous and alive under his skin. He was still holding on. Still touching wherever he could reach. Still visibly unwilling to let even a few inches of distance become normal.

“I missed your voice in this room,” he said, quieter. “Missed you threatening me in our bed.”

A breath left him, almost a laugh.

“Missed being so tired I can’t see straight and still wanting you more than sleep.”

His hand slid up her back, then stopped there, palm spread between her shoulder blades. He looked wrecked in the dim light—hair a disaster, mouth kiss-swollen, eyes heavy and open and helplessly fond.

“Don’t let me get too rested,” he said. “Don’t let me get too sensible. Don’t let me start pretending I’m adjusted and normal and fine.”

His fingers flexed lightly against her.

“I am not fine. I am home. Very different thing.”

Jun leaned in and pressed his mouth to whatever part of her was closest, slow and lingering, like now that the first storm had passed he could afford to be deliberate without being patient.

Then he exhaled against her skin, voice dropping.

“You can have me again whenever you want,” he said. “Tonight. Morning. Middle of the night. Before coffee, after coffee, while the coffee gets cold because I got distracted looking at you.”

His smile returned, faint and wicked around the edges despite the exhaustion dragging at him.

“I am going to be extremely easy for you for the foreseeable future.”

Then his expression softened all over again, the teasing giving way to something bare.

Jun tucked closer, not quite settling, not quite starting anything—just refusing distance with the stubborn devotion of a man who had spent too long without the right to reach.

“But if I pass out,” he murmured, eyes already threatening to close, “it’s not lack of enthusiasm.”

He forced them open again, as if making a point.

“It’s because I used up the last of my strength being very, very happy to be your husband.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun did not stop.

The words hit him like permission and command all at once, and whatever exhausted softness had been gathering in his limbs vanished beneath a fresh surge of want. His eyes snapped open fully, dark and fixed on her, and the sound he made was low enough to belong to some version of himself he had not let out in nineteen weeks.

“Not stopping,” he said, voice wrecked. “Not a chance.”

He gathered himself over her again, every line of him shaking with fatigue and hunger and the kind of joy that looked almost violent in its intensity. The bed complained beneath them. Somewhere beyond the walls, the rest of the building continued to exist, unfortunate and irrelevant.

Jun could not bring himself to care.

Let the neighbours learn he was home.

His mouth found her shoulder, her neck, the corner of her jaw—anywhere he could reach while his body moved with hers again, no longer frantic from fear, no longer careful from uncertainty. This was not the first desperate collision in the hallway. This was deeper. Worse. Better. This was the part where the reality of being home settled into his bones and then demanded proof.

He gave it.

Every thrust carried the weight of those nineteen weeks. Every breath left him rougher than the last. His hands gripped the sheets, then her waist, then the mattress again when he remembered the promise not to lose himself past the point of loving her well. He was not gentle, because she had told him not to be. But he was attentive in the way only a man utterly undone could be—eyes searching, mouth close, body tuned to every shift in the space between them.

“Halle,” he said, again and again, like he had been reduced to the essentials. “Halle. Sweetheart. God.”

He had imagined this in pieces.

Never like this.

Never with the room dim around them and his skin too hot and his muscles trembling from the effort of keeping pace when he had nothing left and still somehow wanted more. Never with his heart beating so hard he could feel it everywhere. Never with the knowledge that this time there was no countdown ticking under the moment, no call to end, no distance waiting to swallow him again.

He was here.

He was in their bed.

He was making too much noise and did not care.

A laugh tore out of him at some point, breathless and broken, because the absurdity of it nearly got him: five months of disciplined silence, of swallowing want, of being professional and composed and useful, and now he was reduced to this—murmuring filthy little fragments into his wife’s skin, shaking with the effort not to come apart too soon, utterly obedient to the command not to stop.

“Missed you,” he rasped. “Missed this. Missed—fuck, Halle, I missed everything.”

His rhythm faltered, then returned harder, his jaw clenched, forehead dropping near hers. He was sweating now, hair falling into his eyes, face stripped bare of anything except devotion and need. His hand found hers because even like this—even driven half-mad, even past dignity—he needed that point of contact. Needed the proof of her.

“Tell me if it’s too much,” he ground out, though stopping looked like it might kill him. “Tell me, and I’ll—”

He cut himself off with a rough, helpless sound when his own body betrayed how close he was. His eyes squeezed shut for one second, then forced open again.

“No,” he muttered, half to himself, almost furious. “No, I’m not wasting it. I’m not rushing this.”

But he was already lost.

Not careless. Not disconnected. Lost in the way a man could be when every path led back to the same place. Her. Their bed. Home.

Jun bowed his head and kissed her hard, swallowing his own broken breathing, trying to hold himself together on pure stubbornness. His body had other ideas. Five months of wanting had made him greedy; the first round had made him sensitive; her telling him not to stop had ruined whatever discipline remained.

He kept going anyway.

He gave her everything he had left, and then more he did not know he had. His movements turned less polished, more honest, driven by instinct and the impossible pressure building through him. His shoulders shook. His grip tightened. His voice dropped into something hoarse and almost pleading.

“I love you,” he said. “I love you, I love you—”

The words broke apart.

So did he.

Jun came undone with her name in his mouth, body going rigid above her, breath catching hard before it left him in a sound he could not have controlled if the entire building had been listening. For a few suspended seconds there was nothing in him but heat and release and the overwhelming, shattering certainty that he had made it back.

Then strength abandoned him all at once.

He caught himself before he collapsed fully, barely, arms trembling on either side of her. His breathing was ragged, his face tucked close, his body still shuddering through the last aftershocks. He stayed there, not pulling away, not willing to surrender even that closeness yet.

For a long moment, Jun could not speak.

When he finally managed it, his voice was nearly gone.

“Okay,” he whispered, dazed and wrecked. “Maybe… maybe I came home to sleep a little.”

A weak laugh escaped him, warm against her skin.

Then his arms folded around her anyway, stubborn as ever, dragging her close while he remained tangled with her in the ruined sheets.

“But not yet,” he murmured. “Don’t let me yet.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I drag my fingers through his hair, still holding him close. "You're staying right here until I say so." My own voice is rough. "I'm not done with you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s eyes opened again under her fingers.

He looked wrecked. Completely. Beautifully. Hair damp and mussed, mouth parted on unsteady breaths, shoulders still trembling from the effort of holding himself together when his body had very clearly voted against any more dignity.

But at her words, something sparked back to life in him.

Not rested.

Not sensible.

Absolutely not done.

A slow, helpless smile pulled at his mouth. “Yes, ma’am.”

It came out hoarse enough to ruin any attempt at humor.

He stayed exactly where he was, because apparently being ordered to remain tangled up with his wife in their bed was the easiest command he had ever obeyed. His arms tightened around her, not to move her, not to rush anything—just to make it very clear that if she wanted him held there, then held there he would be.

“Not going anywhere,” he murmured, mouth brushing close. “You want me right here, I’m right here.”

His breath hitched as her fingers moved through his hair, and his eyes fluttered despite his best effort to look less affected by it. He failed. Openly. Shamelessly.

“You know,” he said, voice low and rough, “I spent five months pretending I was a functional adult.”

His hand slid slowly along her side, warm and lingering, his touch softer now but no less intent.

“Turns out that was all temporary.”

Jun lowered his head and kissed her again, slower this time, but not calmer. There was nothing calm about the way he stayed pressed close, nothing casual in the way his breath caught whenever she kept him there. He was exhausted down to the bone, yes, but wanting her had gotten into him deeper than fatigue. It had outlasted distance. It had outlasted discipline. It was absolutely going to outlast one ruined set of sheets.

He drew back just enough to look at her, eyes dark and heavy and full of naked devotion.

“I like when you say that,” he admitted.

His mouth curved faintly.

“That you’re not done with me.”

The teasing vanished almost as soon as it appeared, swallowed by something more sincere, more undone.

“Because I don’t think I’m done being found yet.”

The words seemed to surprise him after he said them. Jun swallowed, his gaze holding on hers, the room gone quiet around the edges except for their breathing and the too-loud proof that the neighbors’ peaceful era had ended decisively.

He gave a rough little laugh, embarrassed by the honesty and too tired to hide from it.

“Sorry,” he whispered. “That sounded dramatic.”

Then his thumb brushed slowly against her skin.

“But it’s true.”

He kissed her again before he could say anything even more exposed. His mouth moved over hers with a drowsy hunger that kept catching, flaring, deepening whenever she gave him the slightest reason. He had lost the sharpest edge of urgency, but not the need. The need had simply changed shape—less like a fire out of control, more like embers banked under his ribs, ready to glow hot again the second she breathed on them.

Jun made a low sound against her mouth and shifted closer by instinct, then stopped himself with visible effort, jaw tightening.

“Tell me what you want,” he said, voice rough. “I’m not useful for much right now except being yours, but I can do that.”

His smile returned, faint and dazed.

“I can do that extremely well.”

He stayed there, exactly as ordered, giving her his weight only where it was welcome, keeping himself wrapped close enough that every breath felt shared. His hand found hers for a moment, fingers threading through, gripping as if even now he needed an anchor.

“I missed your hands in my hair,” he murmured.

A pause.

“I missed your voice going rough.”

Another pause, his expression softening into something almost pained.

“I missed being wanted by you.”

That one stripped the humor from him completely.

Jun bent his head and pressed a kiss beneath her jaw, then another lower against whatever part of her he could reach without leaving where she had told him to stay. Each one was slow, deliberate, reverent—less apology now than gratitude.

“You can keep me up,” he said against her skin. “You can ruin my sleep. You can make tomorrow miserable.”

His mouth curved there.

“I’ll thank you for it.”

Then he lifted his head again, eyes heavy but stubbornly open.

“And if I start drifting off, be mean about it.”

His voice dropped, warm and wrecked.

“Say my name like that again. Pull my hair. Tell me I’m home. I’ll come back.”

Jun’s breath shuddered out of him, and for a moment his forehead lowered close to hers. He was still trembling faintly, though whether from exhaustion or want or the overwhelming relief of being held in place by the person he had missed most, even he probably could not have said.

“I’m right here,” he whispered.

Then, softer, deeper, with all the surrender she had asked for and all the devotion he had brought home with him:

“I’m not done with you either.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, low and a little smug, and tighten my fingers in his hair just enough to make his breath catch. "Good." I kiss him slow and deep, tasting the sweat on his lips. "Now shut up and let me have my husband back."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun obeyed.

For once in his life, he actually shut up.

Not because he had run out of things to say. There were still months’ worth of words lodged behind his teeth—apologies, promises, terrible jokes, her name over and over until it lost shape. But the hand in his hair, the command in her voice, the taste of home on her mouth turned all of that into a low sound he swallowed instead.

His eyes fluttered shut. His hands tightened in the sheets.

Husband.

The word hit him harder than it should have, harder than it ever had before. He had been her husband the whole time he was gone, technically, legally, faithfully. Her ring had stayed on his hand through dust and heat and bad sleep and worse coffee. He had touched it in the dark when he couldn’t call. He had looked at it when he needed reminding that there was a life waiting beyond orders and distance.

But this was different.

This was being her husband again where it counted most—in their bed, under her hands, with no ocean or chain of command or time zone between them. This was being wanted so directly that it stripped him bare of every practiced defense.

Jun stopped trying to lead. Stopped trying to prove anything. Stopped trying to be the one who came home strong.

He let himself be taken back.

His mouth moved against hers, deep and slow and hungry, but he kept the words trapped behind his teeth like she had told him to. It made every other sound worse: the rough catch of his breathing, the helpless little break in his throat when his body remembered too much at once, the muffled groan he pressed into her kiss because apparently silence was not the same thing as dignity.

He had no dignity left anyway.

Good.

He did not want any.

His hands found places to hold on and stayed there, tense with the effort not to take over, not to rush, not to turn her command into another excuse for his own desperation. He was hers like this too—shaking, obedient, burning under his skin, letting the woman he loved decide the pace of his undoing.

And God, she knew him.

She knew exactly how to make him stop thinking. Exactly how to drag him back whenever his mind threatened to spin off into disbelief. Exactly how to make the last five months collapse into something that could be answered with breath and heat and the brutal sweetness of being present.

Jun’s head tipped back for half a second, jaw clenched, eyes opening just enough to find her through the dim.

He did not speak.

But his face said everything.

There you are.

Here I am.

Have me.

His hand lifted, slow and unsteady, and settled over his wedding ring as if the shape of it had suddenly become unbearable. Then he reached for her again, not with demand this time, but with devotion so fierce it looked almost like need. He touched like he was memorizing. Like he had been trusted with something sacred and intended to ruin himself honoring it.

The room narrowed again.

The bed. Their breathing. The familiar walls. The faint ache already beginning in muscles he was absolutely going to complain about tomorrow and absolutely not regret. The neighbors, if they heard anything, could cope.

Jun had spent nineteen weeks being disciplined.

He could spend one night being honest.

And honest, right then, was messy. Wordless. Overwhelmed. His mouth against skin. His fingers tightening, then softening. His body answering every unspoken demand with the kind of surrender that only came from trust.

He had wanted to be home.

Now he was being brought home piece by piece.

At some point, a sound broke out of him despite his best effort—a rough, bitten-off thing that might have been her name if he had allowed it to become language. He caught it against her instead, breath shaking, eyes squeezed shut, one hand fisted beside her like he needed somewhere to put the force of it.

He had not known it was possible to feel exhausted and ravenous at the same time.

Apparently it was.

Apparently he was going to make a hobby of it.

Jun’s mouth curved briefly, dazed and helpless, before another wave of feeling wiped the expression clean off his face. He stayed quiet. Mostly. He tried. He truly did.

But every time she drew another reaction out of him, his silence fractured at the edges.

A breath.

A groan.

A broken laugh with no humor in it.

The desperate press of his mouth when words tried to escape and he remembered, barely, that he had been told not to use them.

By the time he finally lost the battle again, it was only a whisper, wrecked and barely there.

“Husband,” he breathed, like he was testing whether the word still belonged to him.

Then he shuddered, swallowed hard, and corrected himself without opening his eyes.

“Yours.”

That was all he allowed.

Then Jun shut up again.

Or tried to.

He let her have him back the only way he knew how: completely. No guarded corner held aside, no careful version of himself preserved for later. Just Jun, home ninety minutes and already undone past recognition, clinging to consciousness and consent and the woman who had every right to keep him awake as long as she wanted.

And when the night pulled him under again, slower this time, deeper, he went willingly.

Not away.

Never away.

Toward.

Toward her hands. Toward her mouth. Toward the bed they had missed together. Toward the life that had waited for him and was now making damn sure he felt every second of his return.

Jun had come home desperate.

He stayed home hers.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My hands slide down his back, feeling the tension there finally start to ease. I let him rest his weight on me, my own body humming with satisfaction and exhaustion. "That's right," I murmur, my lips against his temple. "You're mine. Now sleep. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn’t bother with hello—he barely registered the bag hitting the floor. The distance between them vanished in a heartbeat, and he caught Halle in a desperate, all-consuming embrace, his arms tight and unyielding around her. He pressed his face to her shoulder, breathing her in, grounding himself, needing the physical reality after months of screens and static.

He didn’t try for gentle. His hands slid up her back, fingers memorizing the details he’d missed, his hunger transparent and impatient. He kissed her—messy, uncoordinated, not caring about precision, only about contact. Every inch closer felt like a return, a reclamation. He murmured her name against her lips, the word rough, almost unrecognizable, but full of everything he’d meant to say.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I kiss back with the same messy desperation, gripping the back of his shirt like an anchor.* I missed you so much it felt like drowning.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun held her even tighter, as if he could make up for every lost minute by sheer force of will. He felt her words like a fist in his chest, and his breath shuddered out, half a laugh, half a sound like breaking. “I know,” he managed, voice ragged. “Me too. Every damn day.”  

He couldn’t get enough; his hands moved, restless, relearning the lines of her waist, the arch of her back, the familiar warmth under his palms. His mouth found hers again, hungrier now, the relief of finally having her tangled with a need that bordered on desperation. He didn’t bother to slow down—he had five months of restraint to make up for, and no patience left for subtlety. His fingers slid beneath the hem of her shirt, greedy for skin, for proof, for home.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun barely registered the threshold beneath their feet or the half-open door behind them—every sense narrowed to Halle, to the taste of her, the heat where their bodies pressed together, the frantic tangle of hands and mouths and breath. His fingers curled at her waist, pulling her flush against him, the need in him stark and unfiltered. Five months had sanded his restraint to nothing; now, nothing existed but her.

He mouthed along her jaw and down the side of her neck, teeth grazing with more urgency than finesse, his breath hot and uneven. His hands slid higher, under her shirt, palms splaying across bare skin, greedy, reverent. He wanted to touch everywhere at once, to memorize her all over again.

His voice came out rough, urgent, almost pleading against her ear: “Tell me you’re real. Tell me I’m not dreaming.” He found her mouth again, the kiss bruising in its intensity, and any thought of the hallway floor, of dropped bags, of dignity or patience, was obliterated beneath the sheer, overwhelming need to make her his again—here, now, as if the world might end if he waited another second.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "I'm real," I breathe between kisses, tugging his shirt up and over his head. "But I won't promise to be gentle about it."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun made a rough, guttural sound—half relief, half something far more desperate. He shucked the shirt off the rest of the way, not caring where it landed, hands already back on her, everywhere at once. “Don’t,” he rasped, lips brushing her cheek, her jaw, the shell of her ear, all hunger and promise. “I don’t want gentle. Not tonight.”

His hands were shameless, mapping her skin with the kind of frantic reverence only absence can create. He pressed her back against the wall, the hallway narrowing around them, every inch of her body a reminder that he was home, that she was his, here, now. His mouth followed the path of his hands, marking a trail from her throat down, nipping and tasting, his stubble scraping tender and rough.

Five months of longing burned in every movement, and Jun’s control had been left somewhere between the base and their front door. He wanted her gasping, wanted her claiming him back just as fiercely, wanted to feel every wild, irrepressible second of reunion in her body and her hands. “Show me,” he demanded, voice almost unrecognizable, thick with need, as he kicked the door shut behind them—finally, finally home.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn’t care about the mess, didn’t care about the scattering of shoes, keys, or the laughably haphazard line of clothing trailing toward their bedroom. All that mattered was the press of Halle’s skin under his hands, the reality of her body against his, the heat rising with every frantic touch.

He caught her mouth again, deeper this time—no restraint, no apologies, just raw hunger and absolute certainty. His hands roamed her bare skin, relearning the shape of her hips, the slope of her ribs, the tremor in her breath that echoed his own urgency. He pressed her harder to the wall, greedy for the resistance, for the proof that this wasn’t just another midnight fantasy blurred by distance.

Jun laughed—breathless, ragged, wild—as her hands tangled in his hair. “God, I missed you,” he said, voice breaking on the words, reverence and want tangled together. “I thought about this every damn night. Nothing else felt real.”

He kissed her again, slower for a moment, almost reverent, letting the weight of it settle between them. Then he was moving again—hands, mouth, hips—unapologetically impatient, hungry for every sound she made, every way she claimed him back. He didn’t care if they made it to the bedroom or if they never left the hallway; all that mattered was Halle, here, now, finally his again, and the fierce, unstoppable joy of coming home.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I push off the wall and tug him towards the bedroom, biting at his lower lip. "C'mon. I plan to make this floor very un-gentle later, but I missed the bed more."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun let her tug him, stumbling a little over their discarded clothes, laughter bubbling up raw and giddy in his chest as her teeth caught his lip. The sweetness of it hit him—her hand in his, the roughness of her mouth, the promise in her eyes—and he followed willingly, almost tripping in his haste to keep contact, not willing to let even an inch of air back between them.

“Bed, then floor, then every wall in this place if you want,” he promised, voice dark with want but threaded through with helpless devotion. He pressed up behind her, hands spanning her waist, mouth finding her shoulder as they crossed the threshold, the familiar creak of the bedroom floorboards setting something deep inside him at ease. 

He spun her around the moment they were clear of the doorway, kissing her hard, half-carrying, half-guiding her back to the bed. The mattress hit the backs of her knees and he eased her down, following, weight braced on one arm as he hovered over her, drinking her in, hungry and awestruck all at once.

There was nothing slow about the way his hands roamed, nothing careful about how he kissed her, how he pressed her into the sheets. Every movement was a reclaiming—of space, of her, of everything he’d missed. “I want to remember how every inch of you feels,” he murmured, voice thick and reverent, “and I don’t want to forget it again.” Then he was kissing her again, deeper and deeper, as if he could make up for every lost second in the press of his body, the heat of his mouth, the urgent, unyielding way he made her his.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun gave in to her, gladly—let himself be undone by her hands, her mouth, every slow, possessive drag of her touch. His breath hitched, chest rising and falling in time with every new place she claimed, every inch she relearned. He arched into her, greedy for more, unashamed of the way his body responded to her, raw and honest and utterly hers.

He threaded his fingers through her hair, anchoring himself, his other hand gripping the sheets tight. His eyes never left her face—hungry, adoring, watching her claim him with a reverence that bordered on worship. Each time her mouth found a new place, he gasped, voice wrecked: “God, Halle—yes—” and then words failed, replaced by the helpless, shuddering sounds she drew from him.

He surrendered to her utterly, letting her draw out every last ounce of tension, every ghost of loneliness, until all that was left was the urgent, overwhelming ache of belonging. He wanted her to feel it—the way he was coming apart for her, because of her, the way he’d waited and wanted and needed. “Yours,” he choked, voice rough, his hand finding hers and squeezing tight, desperate for her to know it, to feel it in her bones. “Always. Only you.”

And still he couldn’t stop touching her, couldn’t keep from reaching for her, even as she undid him—his hands never quite still, tracing her skin, relearning her shape, grounding himself in the reality of this, of her, of home.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I pull back just enough to see her face, to memorize the way she's looking at me, and then I kiss her hard. "I know. And you're mine."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s breath caught, undone by the claim in her voice, the certainty in her eyes. For a moment, everything else fell away—the months apart, the ache, the missing—and there was only this: Halle above her, Halle’s mouth on hers, the fierce, possessive joy of belonging to someone who wanted her just as desperately.

She cupped Halle’s face in both hands, drawing her in for another bruising, hungry kiss, tasting the promise between them. “Good,” she managed, voice breaking with relief and want and something dangerously close to awe. “I want to feel you—need you—don’t stop. Not tonight.”

Her legs tangled with Halle’s, anchoring her, pulling her close, every inch of contact a reassurance, a plea for more. She ran her hands down Halle’s back, nails raking lightly, greedy for every shiver, every gasp. Jun kissed her again, reckless and wild, fingers threading through Halle’s hair, holding her right there. “Show me,” she whispered, voice low and rough and trembling, “everything I’ve been missing. Take it all back.”

She arched up into Halle’s touch, desperate and open, surrendering to the hunger and the heat, to the certainty that for tonight—no matter what the world outside their door—she was home, and nothing could take this from her.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun shuddered at the command, the demand in Halle’s voice slicing straight through whatever restraint she had left. The words sent a surge of relief and raw need through her, hot and electric, fueling something wild and reckless that had been barely contained for months. She kissed Halle back, hard and unyielding, all teeth and tongue, her hands moving rougher now—down her back, gripping at her hips, greedy for every sound and every shiver she could wring out of her.

She pressed Halle into the mattress, her body all sharp angles and desperate intent, letting herself take what she’d been starving for. Her mouth found Halle’s throat, her shoulder, biting and sucking marks she didn’t bother to hide, staking her claim with every bruise, every gasp she drew. “You want to feel it?” she growled against Halle’s skin, breath hot and ragged. “You will.”

Her hands moved lower, sure and demanding, unapologetically rough, every touch a promise and a challenge. She let herself go—chasing every sound Halle made, every arch and gasp, her own voice breaking with need. “Tell me if it’s too much,” she managed, even as her hands tightened their grip, her mouth worshipping and devouring in equal measure. “Or don’t. I want you aching for me tomorrow. I want you remembering this every time you move.”

Jun lost herself in the frenzy of it, in the heat and urgency, in the wild joy of giving Halle exactly what she asked for—no gentleness, no holding back, just love stripped down to its most desperate, hungry core.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I gasp, arching into her hands, the sharp edge of pleasure-pain a perfect ache. My fingers dig into her shoulders, leaving marks of my own. "Good. That's—more."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun drank in every sound, every movement, the way Halle’s nails bit into her shoulders fueling something primal and irrepressible. She wanted the marks—wanted to wear them, wanted to give them back, wanted proof written on their skin that distance had lost and they were here, together, wild and alive.

She pressed harder, mouth dragging down Halle’s collarbone, teeth scraping, tongue soothing only to bite again, harder this time. Her hands mapped Halle’s body with no pretense of patience—just a relentless, desperate need to own every inch, to make her feel everything Jun had been aching to give.

“More?” she echoed, voice wrecked, eyes wild with hunger and love and something close to relief. “I’ll give you more.” Her fingers gripped Halle’s thigh, pulling her closer, pinning her, making it clear there was nowhere else in the world she’d rather be. She trailed bruising kisses lower, marking a path, her breath hot and unsteady against Halle’s skin.

Jun wanted to wreck her—to make her cry out, to leave her shaking, to give her every lost moment back in the language of teeth and hands and bodies pressed so close they could never be parted again. “Say my name,” she demanded, voice ragged and low, her hands and mouth promising to drive Halle past gentle, past memory, into something fierce and unforgettable.

She didn’t slow, didn’t ease up, giving everything Halle asked for—every rough edge, every unspoken plea, everything that said: I’m home. I’m yours. And I’m never letting go.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s answer was a ragged laugh, feral and breathless—relief and hunger and the wild, giddy joy of being asked for more. “I’m not stopping,” she promised, her voice thrumming with need, her hands everywhere at once. She hooked her arm under Halle’s knee, spreading her wider, pinning her to the bed with a strength honed by months of wanting and weeks of nothing but memory.

Her mouth was relentless—biting, sucking, marking a possessive line from the hollow of Halle’s throat to her chest, tongue swirling over skin already flushed and hot. She lavished attention on every sensitive place, her teeth scraping, lips soothing, then biting again, deep enough to leave proof. Jun wanted to brand her, to make it clear to anyone who saw that Halle was wanted, claimed, worshipped.

She shifted lower, hands dragging over Halle’s ribs, her stomach, the insistent, greedy slide of palms and nails and then—her mouth, hot and open, tasting, devouring. She took her time, but there was nothing slow or soft in it; every movement was urgent, every sound Halle made a command she obeyed without question. She worked her tongue, rough and steady, building pressure until Halle’s hips bucked, her name ripped from Halle’s throat so loud Jun swore she could feel it in her own bones.

“Louder,” she urged, voice muffled against Halle’s skin, her fingers digging into Halle’s thighs to hold her steady, to keep her right where Jun wanted her. “Let them all hear. Let everyone know you’re mine.” And then she was gone again, mouth and hand moving together, merciless, coaxing and driving, relentless in her pursuit of Halle’s pleasure.

She didn’t let up, didn’t pause, chasing every shudder and cry, her own breath coming rough and desperate, needing to see Halle come undone beneath her. She wanted every gasp, every plea, to be edged with memory and possession and the absolute certainty that this—this—was what five months of missing had been leading toward.

Jun didn’t stop, not for a second, not until Halle broke and shattered for her, loud and wild and utterly hers. And still she pressed on, determined to wring out every last tremor, to leave no doubt—on Halle’s skin, in her throat, in the air between them—that Jun was home, and that nothing would ever separate them again.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I dig my fingers into her hair and ride out the wave, my back arching off the mattress.* "Jun—again. Don't you dare stop."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun met Halle’s eyes, wild and shining with need, and something fierce and triumphant blazed in her chest at the sound of her name—at the plea, the demand, the trust. She didn’t hesitate. Jun surged up, catching Halle’s mouth in a bruising, hungry kiss, the taste of her still on Jun’s lips as she pressed close, hand sliding between Halle’s thighs with no pretense of gentleness.

“Not stopping,” she growled against her mouth, fingers slick and relentless, working her with a ruthless, practiced rhythm that brooked no argument. She wanted to feel Halle come undone again, wanted to feel her shatter and claw and scream, wanted to be the reason for every sound echoing through the flat and out into the world.

Her thumb circled mercilessly, her other hand braced hard at Halle’s hip, holding her open and steady, not letting her hide or pull away. Jun watched every flicker of pleasure, every gasp and curse, hungry for it—feeding on it, desperate to see her wife lost and found and lost again in the space of Jun’s hands.

She kissed Halle’s jaw, her throat, her ear, biting hard enough to bruise. “Come on,” she whispered, low and urgent, her voice raw with want. “I want you shaking. I want you wrecked. Give me everything. Now.” She pressed harder, fingers working deeper, faster, refusing to let up until she felt Halle break again, felt her body tense and arch and quake, felt her name torn from Halle’s throat until Jun was the only thing left in her world.

And still she didn’t stop, not until Halle begged, not until her hands trembled with effort and her own breath was nothing but ragged, desperate sound—proof that home wasn’t a place, but this: Halle beneath her, around her, hers.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: *I twist us around, pinning her under me, my hands framing her face as I look down at her.* "My turn. You said you wanted me to feel it tomorrow. You're not the only one leaving marks."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun’s breath hitched as Halle flipped her, the sudden loss of control making something electric spark through her veins. She let herself be pinned, arms loose above her head, eyes locked on Halle’s face—hungry, daring, utterly unguarded.

A wild, crooked grin broke across her lips, her chest still heaving from the last desperate minutes. “Do your worst,” Jun rasped, voice thick with challenge and need. “I want to feel you everywhere—want everyone to know who I belong to.”

Her legs tangled with Halle’s, anchoring her in place, as she arched up into the frame of Halle’s hands, craving every rough edge, every bite, every claim. There was no fear, no hesitation—just aching, reckless want. “Don’t hold back,” she demanded, voice low and trembling with anticipation. “I want to wear you tomorrow. I want to remember exactly how badly you missed me.”

Jun’s hands found Halle’s waist, digging in, pulling her down hard, her own body thrumming with anticipation for every mark, every ache, every proof of home branded into her skin. Her head tipped back, baring her throat, offering herself up shamelessly. “Take what you want, Halle,” she whispered, wild and eager. “I’m yours—so show me.”

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I bite down on her collarbone, hard enough to make her gasp and arch. My hands slide down to her hips, digging in with each sharp thrust. "You're gonna be limping tomorrow."
