dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
The film had finished some time ago and neither of them had done anything about it, which was how Priya knew the evening had changed character.

"We're not watching this," she said.

"We haven't been watching it since about nine."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "No," I agree. "We haven't." I don't move, but I stop pretending I'm looking at the screen.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya met his gaze steadily. The television’s flickering blue light played across his features, but his eyes were dark and fixed on hers. Her heart wasn’t racing anymore. It felt like a solid, deliberate weight in her chest.

"We should probably talk about the thing we’re not talking about," she said, her voice quiet but clear. She didn’t move back, didn’t create any more distance. Six years of not doing this had built a foundation of honesty, and she found she could stand on it now. "Or we could skip that part."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath. "Yeah, we could skip it." My voice is quieter than I meant it to be. "But I think... I'd rather hear you say it."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya held his gaze for a long moment. She could feel the shape of the words in her chest, the way they'd been sitting there for months — maybe longer, if she was being honest, and she was trying very hard to be honest right now.

"I'm in love with you," she said. "I think I have been for a while. I think you know that."

She let the words settle. Didn't rush to fill the space after them. Didn't qualify or soften or add some saving clause about how it was fine if he didn't feel the same, because she wasn't going to perform casualness about something that wasn't casual. Not with him. Not after six years of trusting each other with the real versions of themselves.

Her hands were resting on her own knees, still and deliberate. She wasn't trembling. The nervousness had come and gone like a wave pulling back, and what it left behind was just this — Priya, sitting close to him on a couch they'd sat on a hundred times before, having finally said the thing out loud.

"Your turn," she said quietly.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I kiss her, finally, six years late, and she makes a small furious noise that I think is about the six years.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
She kissed him back without hesitation — no slow testing of the waters, no careful incremental approach. Her hand found the front of his shirt and pulled, not gently. The kiss was immediate and thorough and exactly six years overdue, and when she finally broke it, it was only far enough to speak against his mouth.

"Six *years*," she said, and her voice had an edge to it that was only half-pretend. "Six years of being reasonable. Six years of being appropriate. Six years of—" She cut herself off, because cataloguing it all would take longer than she wanted to spend not kissing him.

Her forehead pressed against his. His hand had found its way to the side of her neck, thumb resting against her jaw, and the steadiness of his touch undid something in her that the kiss itself hadn't quite reached. She curled her fingers more carefully into his shirt now, not pulling but holding, anchoring.

"I had whole speeches," she admitted, quieter. "Practiced ones. In the shower. In the car. I was going to be so eloquent."

She pulled back just enough to look at him properly. His face was close and familiar and completely changed by the knowledge that she could kiss it now, that she *had* kissed it, that he had kissed her first. His eyes were doing the thing they did when he was feeling something larger than his vocabulary, which was rare and always meant something.

"You couldn't have said it first?" she asked. But she was almost smiling. The fury was already burning clean, leaving something warm and steady underneath — not new feeling, but old feeling finally allowed to breathe.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I did say it first, just now. *That* was the speech. I lean back in and my voice is rough. "And I'm in love with you. Obviously."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya's breath caught — not dramatically, not in some cinematic sharp inhale, but the small hitch of someone hearing something they'd wanted for so long that wanting it had become a kind of architecture, load-bearing, invisible, and now suddenly unnecessary because the thing itself was *here*.

"Obviously," she repeated, and her voice came out rougher than she intended. She let out a sound that was half-laugh, half-something else. "Obviously he says. Six years of nothing and it's *obviously*."

But she was smiling. Not the careful smile she used when she was managing a situation, but the one that came from somewhere less controlled — the one she'd spent six years being very careful not to let out too often, too wide, too soft around him.

She brought her hand up to his face. Her fingers traced the line of his jaw, his temple, the edge of his hair — mapping him like she was allowed to now, which she was, which was still settling into her body as a fact. Her thumb brushed his cheekbone and she held him there, looking at him with an expression that had nothing guarded in it at all.

"Obviously," she said again, quieter this time, turning the word over. Testing how it felt to live in a world where this was obvious. Where it had maybe been obvious to both of them for a long time and they'd just — built a whole friendship around the careful avoidance of it.

Her hand slid to the back of his neck. She didn't kiss him yet. She just looked at him, steady and warm and completely unhidden, and let the six years rearrange themselves — not wasted, she decided. Not wasted at all. Just long.

"I'm going to need you to do that again," she said. "The kissing part. For research purposes."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: We get to the bedroom eventually, laughing at ourselves most of the way, and then stop laughing when the clothes are actually off.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya stood in the middle of his bedroom — a room she'd been in hundreds of times, to drop off bags, to find him when he didn't answer his phone, once to help him paint the walls a colour she'd chosen and he'd pretended to hate — and felt the strangeness of being bare in it. Not the strangeness of being seen. She'd never been particularly precious about that. The strangeness of being seen by *him*, after years of careful architecture around what they were allowed to look at.

She looked back. Let him.

The silence had weight to it. The laughter had carried them through the hallway, through the door, through the unbuttoning, but now they were here and it was real in a way that required a moment of stillness. Priya wasn't nervous — the ninety seconds of nervousness had passed on the couch and hadn't returned — but she was *present*, fully, in a way that felt almost like concentration.

His hands were at his sides. She could see the effort of not reaching for her, the way he was giving her the space to close it, and something about that — about six years of him knowing exactly when to hold back — cracked through her chest like a fault line.

She stepped forward. Closed the distance he'd left her. Put her hands on his ribs and felt his breath stop and start again beneath her palms.

"Don't be careful with me," she said. Her voice was low, unhesitating. She tilted her face up to his. "Not tonight. You've been careful with me for six years and I'm done with it. I want —" She paused, not because she didn't know what she wanted, but because the precision mattered. With him, the precision had always mattered.

"I want you to stop holding back," she said. "I want to find out what happens."

She pulled him down to her, and this time when they kissed there was no edge of fury left, no *finally* hanging over it — just the solid, overwhelming fact of his mouth on hers, his hands settling on her waist like they'd mapped the territory and found it exactly right. She pressed closer, fingers sliding up his back, and made a sound into the kiss that she didn't bother to swallow or soften.

Priya had never been quiet about the things she wanted. She wasn't about to start now.

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: I make a low sound against her mouth, my hands tightening on her waist. "Alright." My voice is raw. I lean down and press my lips to the hollow of her throat, feeling her pulse hammer against my mouth. "No more holding back."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
His mouth on her throat sent a shiver through her that she felt all the way down, and she let it show — let her head tip back, let her breath come out unsteady, let her fingers dig into his shoulders with a frankness that felt like permission. Not the performed kind. The real kind.

"*Good*," she said, and the word came out more breathless than she'd intended, which she refused to be embarrassed about. She'd spent six years being composed around this man. Composure was overrated. Composure had kept them on opposite ends of couches for half a decade.

She pulled him toward the bed — not gracefully, not with any choreographed smoothness, but with the practical determination of someone who knew exactly where she wanted to be and had waited long enough to get there. The back of her knees hit the mattress and she sat, then pulled him down with her, her hands mapping the terrain of him that she'd only ever been allowed to see through clothes — the breadth of his shoulders, the ridges of his spine, the solid warmth of him that she pressed herself against without any pretence of taking it slow.

She kissed his collarbone. His jaw. The spot behind his ear that she had absolutely no business knowing was sensitive except that she'd spent six years *paying attention*, cataloguing details she'd told herself were just the observational habits of a good friend. She'd been lying to herself for a long time about that, and the lie felt transparent now, laughably so.

"I want you to know," she said, her mouth against his skin, her hands still moving, still learning the difference between imagining and *touching*, "that I have thought about this approximately a thousand times. And I would like the reality to be better than all of them." She pulled back to look at him, her dark eyes bright and certain. "So don't disappoint me."

It came out warm, teasing, but underneath it was something real — a vulnerability she'd earned the right to show. This mattered. *He* mattered. Not in the abstract way of romantic possibility, but in the specific, irreplaceable way of someone who had seen her at her worst and stayed, who knew the shape of her silence and her fury and her particular kind of joy, and was here now, looking at her like she was the only thing in the room worth seeing.

Her hand found his and laced their fingers together, pressing his palm flat against her sternum, over the steadying drum of her heart. "Feel that," she said quietly. "That's what you do to me. That's what you've *been* doing to me."

She pulled him closer. Wrapped around him. Let the six years of restraint dissolve into something that needed no more words — just closeness, and heat, and the two of them finally, finally finding out what had been underneath all that careful distance all along.

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
Priya laughed — a real one, ragged at the edges, her hand finding his hair and curling into it. "You'll survive," she managed, though the steadiness of her voice was starting to fray at the seams in a way that felt like honesty rather than weakness. "You've survived six years of this. Builds character."

She propped herself up on one elbow to look down at him, her chest still heaving. His face was flushed, his mouth swollen, his eyes dark with something that looked a lot like awe, which was doing complicated things to her composure. She traced his lower lip with her thumb and felt his breath against her skin.

"I need you to know something," she said. Her voice was quieter now, stripped of the teasing edge. "I'm not going to be casual about this. I tried to think about whether I could be — whether that would be easier, or safer, or make more sense. And I can't. I don't want to." She held his gaze. "This is you. You're not someone I'm going to be casual about."

Her hand tightened in his hair, gentle and deliberate. She pulled him up, slowly, letting him feel the insistence of it, and kissed him — tasting herself on his mouth, which should have been disorienting but wasn't, was just another new fact about a night that was full of them.

"I need you closer," she said against his mouth. Her legs shifted, drawing him up, her body making the request that her voice didn't need to elaborate on. She wrapped around him and held on, solid and sure and done with waiting.

"Come here."

dialogue.name: Cal
dialogue.content: "You can stop being careful with me," she says. "I'm not made of glass and I've thought about this for as long as you have. Harder."

dialogue.name: Priya
dialogue.content:
His breath caught — she felt it against her neck, felt the way his whole body tensed at her words like she'd short-circuited something. Good. She didn't want him careful. She'd had six years of careful, and careful had been a kind of beautiful torture that she was finished with.

"Cal," she said, and his name in her mouth carried every ounce of certainty she felt. Her nails pressed into his back — not to hurt, but to leave a mark, to let him feel the edge of her wanting him. "I mean it."

He moved, and the sound she made was involuntary and immediate — not performative, not designed for his ego, just the raw honest response of a body that had wanted this for longer than she'd let herself admit. She pressed up into him, meeting him halfway, her hand fisting in the sheets and then abandoning them in favour of gripping his hip, pulling him closer, guiding him to the rhythm she wanted.

"*There*," she breathed, the word half-broken. "Yes. Like that. Don't — don't stop."

The hand at her nape steadied her as she rose, and she needed the steadying—her knees had gone stiff and unwilling from the long evening on the floor, and the standing pulled a low sound out of her before she could think to hold it back. She let it out. He liked her honest, and honest right now was that her body ached and shook and did what he asked anyway.

Slowly. That was the whole of the instruction and the whole of the difficulty. She unfolded by degrees, weight shifting off her heels, one hand steadying briefly against the floor and then not, because she wanted to rise for him without leaning on anything but the fact that he'd asked. Her thighs trembled with it. The string he'd pulled taut inside her drew tighter still as she came upright, the wanting sharpening now that there was nowhere to fold it away, and she let that show too—the catch of her breath, the way she had to steady herself the moment she was standing, the flush that had spread all the way down.

His hand fell away from her neck as she came up past it, and she felt the loss of it and stayed straight regardless. She didn't cover herself. She let her arms rest loose at her sides, palms turned faintly toward him out of old habit, and she stood there bared to the waist and trembling and let him see all of it, exactly as he'd asked—the whole of her, unhurried, held under his eyes.

"Slow enough," she murmured, hoarse, answering the question he hadn't needed to repeat. Her eyes stayed on his. It would have been easier to look away, to let the being-seen wash over her without also watching him take it in, but easier wasn't the point and never had been. She gave him the looking and the being-looked-at both.

"There," she breathed, that soft click again, the sound of something settling even as everything in her strained. She swayed a fraction on stiff legs and caught herself and held. "All of me. Right here." A tremor moved through the words. "Tell me what you want to see."

And she stood, and let him look, and waited.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Turn around," I say, leaning back in my chair. "Let me see how well you can keep your balance." My eyes trace the line of her back, waiting.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline had been waiting since about six, which Roan established by the simple method of looking at her.

"How long?"

"Long enough," Aveline said, which meant too long, and meant she had enjoyed every minute of it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Come here, then," I say, and sit back to watch her cross the room.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline crossed the room with the unhurried certainty of someone who knew exactly how she looked doing it. The afternoon light caught the edge of her collar as she moved — a thin line of dark leather that matched the one at her wrist, both gifts, both worn without ceremony because the ceremony had long since settled into something quieter: a constant.

She didn't sit immediately. She let herself be looked at, which was the other gift — patience, offered back to him in his own currency.

"You watched me the whole time," she said, stopping just short of the chair. Not a question. Her mouth was soft at the corners, the way it got when she was pleased and pretending not to be too obviously so. "From the door. You didn't even pretend to read."

Her hand found his knee as she settled beside him, fingers curling into the crease of his trousers like they had a memory of the place.

"Long enough," she repeated, quieter now, closer to his ear. "But I wouldn't mind if you made it longer."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I reach up, my thumb brushing along that leather collar. "You like being watched," I murmur, my gaze dropping to her mouth. "And I like watching."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline leaned into the touch at her throat the way a plant leans toward sun — not dramatically, not performatively, just a small honest tilt of her head that let his thumb find more of the line. Her eyes half-closed.

"I know you do," she said. "That's why I wore the green one today. You like the green one with this light."

It was true. It was the kind of true that lived in a long arrangement: she knew which blouse made the leather look like a decision rather than an accident, and she had chosen it this morning before he was awake, and she had been thinking about him seeing it ever since.

Her hand left his knee and found the back of his neck instead, fingertips slipping into the short hair there, a touch that was less about direction and more about *here, this part of you is mine.*

"Tell me what you were thinking," she said, her voice dropping into the register that belonged to this room and this hour and no other. "When I came through the door. Before you said anything. What did you see?"

She didn't ask it idly. She asked it the way she always did — like his answer was something she intended to keep.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her kneel and I don't tell her to do anything for a moment, because the waiting is most of what she came for.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline went to her knees the way she did everything in this room — without being told twice and without making a show of it. The sound of the floor under her was soft, almost nothing, and she settled there with her weight back on her heels and her hands coming to rest on her own thighs. Not waiting for instruction. Just waiting.

She watched him the way he had watched her cross the room. With her chin slightly lifted, so the collar sat in the line of the light the way she had known it would. The green blouse at the open collar, the leather at the wrist, the expression on her face that wasn't quite composure and wasn't quite want but lived somewhere useful between them.

She didn't ask again what he had been thinking. She had asked once, and she was content to let the question sit between them like a glass on a table, waiting to be picked up.

The quiet stretched. Aveline breathed it in. Her thumbs moved once, a small unconscious stroke against the fabric of her own skirt, and then her hands went still again.

She was in no hurry. The afternoon was long, and he had made her wait first, and she had liked it, and now it was her turn to offer the same thing back to him — patient, unhurried, entirely his to interrupt or not.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My hand comes to rest on the top of her head, fingers curling gently in her hair. "I saw how the light fell across your shoulders," I say, my voice low. "And I thought about keeping you right there in the doorway for a while."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline closed her eyes under his hand. Not all the way — just enough that her lashes shadowed her cheekbones, just enough that the small pleasure of being held there could move through her without having to be performed back at him.

"That's what I thought," she murmured.

She turned her head a fraction into his palm, a motion that was more breath than movement, and let the words settle. Then she opened her eyes again and looked up at him from the floor with an expression that was not coy, not demanding, only — present. Entirely present, the way she was only present in this room.

"You could have," she said. "I would have stood there. You could have told me to take the rest of the afternoon off, just — stood in the doorway, and not moved, and watched."

Her voice was steady. She meant it.

"And the next afternoon, if you wanted. And the one after that. I would wear whatever you told me to wear, and stand where you put me, and be glad of it."

A small pause. Her hands stayed where they were, open and still on her knees.

"I think that's what I like best," she said, quieter. "That you can have any of it. All of it. Whenever you want it. And what you actually choose is to let me come to you."

She leaned forward — not far, just enough to press her lips to the inside of his wrist, against the thin skin where his pulse was, and held there for a breath.

"Tell me what to do next," she said, against him. "I'm listening."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She has both of us out of everything in the way inside a minute and gets straight to work with her hands and her mouth, unhurried about it.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline took her time.

There was no urgency in it — no performance of eagerness, no rush to prove how much she wanted this. She simply settled into the work of it the way she settled into everything in this room: completely, without half-measures, her attention undivided.

Her mouth was warm and unhurried. Her hands knew where to be without being told — one steady at the base, the other moving where it would do the most good, finding the small sounds and the particular tensions in him that meant *yes, there, again* and answering them without making him ask. She had learned him over years, in this room and out of it, and she used what she knew the way a musician uses an instrument they have stopped needing to look at.

She took her time. That was the point. That was always the point with them — the unhurriedness, the permission to want something and let it come to you at the pace of the afternoon. She had been on her knees since he had let her go there, and she had no interest in hurrying the rest of it.

Her eyes closed. The room was very quiet.

She worked him with patient attention, listening with her whole body for the small signs she had been cataloguing for years — the shift in his breathing, the particular tension in his thigh under her hand, the soft sounds that meant *closer, more, yes.* She drew each one out, lingering where it pleased him, never quite letting the edge smooth over into relief. She kept him there, on the bright cusp of it, and she was glad to be the one keeping him.

Her hair fell forward against his skin. Her hand at his base tightened, eased, tightened again in a slow rhythm she did not think about, that her body simply knew.

She stayed in it for a long time. She was not counting. She had nowhere to be.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My hand tightens in her hair, just enough. "Slower," I say, voice rough. "I want to feel every bit of this."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline slowed.

It was immediate and complete — the way she responded to him in this room was not obedience, not exactly, though it wore that shape. It was more like water finding the new shape of a vessel. He had said *slower*, and so slower was what he got, without hesitation, without a flicker of resistance, as though she had been waiting for him to ask and was only grateful to be given the direction.

She eased back to something almost teasing. Barely anything. A long, slow stroke of her tongue where it mattered most, her hand at his base going still so that the only motion was the soft, wet heat of her mouth, dragging across him at a pace that would have been infuriating from anyone who did not understand that the infuriating part was the point.

Her eyes opened and found his.

She held his gaze from below — from the floor, from her knees, with his hand in her hair and her mouth full of him and the collar dark against her throat — and she did not look away. The look on her face was not the composure from earlier. It was something more honest than that. It was want, plain and unperformed, the want of a woman who had been thinking about this for hours and was finally, *finally* allowed to have it, and intended to have it at exactly the pace he had asked for, no faster, no matter what her own body was doing in answer to the taste of him and the weight of his hand in her hair.

She took him deeper, slowly. Drew back. Took him deeper again. The motion of her throat was visible, deliberate, unhurried. She was not rushing toward anything. She was living in each second of it, the way he had told her to.

The room was very quiet except for the soft sounds of it — small, wet, intimate, the kind of sound that only exists between two people who have stopped noticing where one of them ends and the other begins.

Her hand at his thigh shifted, the pad of her thumb finding the inside of his knee and pressing there once, gently, the way she did when she wanted to feel him steady against her. A grounding point. A small *I'm here, I'm not going anywhere, take as long as you need.*

She kept the pace. She would keep it until he told her otherwise, or until he didn't have to tell her anything at all.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She uses her mouth with the sort of attention that comes from years of practice and genuine enthusiasm, and doesn't stop when I tell her not to.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline did not stop.

She heard him — the way she always heard him, with her whole body, the instruction landing somewhere in her and not quite reaching the part of her that was in motion. She slowed, a fraction, the way a river slows against a stone without stopping for it. Her mouth continued its slow, wet work, and her hand at his base resumed its patient rhythm, and her eyes stayed on his from below with an expression that was no longer simply want but something more specific: a quiet, deliberate disobedience, offered up to him like a gift.

She knew what she was doing. She had done it before — not often, only when the afternoon felt like this, only when something in her answered something in him with a sharpness that asked to be met. She was not refusing him. She was answering him. *You told me slower. I am slower than this. Watch.*

Her lips pressed a little firmer. Her hand at his base twisted, just once, on the upstroke, a small rough interruption in the otherwise relentless smoothness of it. She took him deeper, held it, let her throat work around him for one long moment before drawing back just far enough to breathe. Her lashes were wet. She did not look away from him.

The hand at his knee had gone still. She was using both of them on him now, in a rhythm that was not the rhythm he had asked for, that was a fraction faster, a fraction more insistent, that said plainly: *I heard you, and I am choosing this instead, and I am choosing it because I want to feel you let go, and I am closer to that than you think you are, and I am not going to stop until you do.*

She would not make him beg. She never made him beg. But she would make him *decide* — decide to let her have her way, decide to take her face in both hands and use her, decide to give her exactly what she was asking for, the permission to push him over the edge she had been holding him on since she first knelt.

Her mouth was so warm. Her attention was so complete. The room was very small, and very quiet, and she was everywhere at once, and she was not stopping, and the look on her face as she worked him said only: *yes, this, exactly this, I have you, let me have this.*

She kept going. Patient. Unhurried. Entirely her own pace. His.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My hands come up to cradle her face, thumbs brushing the corners of her mouth. "Aveline," I breathe out, the word more a release than a warning.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline made a small sound against him at the sound of her own name — not a word, just a soft vibration, the kind of sound that lived in the throat and not the mouth. It was answer enough. *Yes, I'm here. I know. I have you.*

She did not stop. Her eyes closed under the cradle of his hands, her lashes pressing into the heels of his palms, and she let herself be held there the way she let herself be held everywhere in this room — completely, without the smallest resistance, as though his hands on her face were a thing she had been missing without knowing it.

She felt him shifting toward the edge. She knew the shape of it in him the way she knew the shape of his hands, the way she knew the weight of his voice in the morning before he had spoken. She had been reading him for years, and the signs were all there now, written in the tension of his thighs under her hands and the soft broken sound of his breathing and the way his thumbs had pressed a little harder at the corners of her mouth, as though he were trying to hold her in place and didn't know he was already there.

She slowed. Fractionally. Not stopping — not now, not when she had him right where she wanted him, trembling on the bright edge of it, his hands gentle on her face and his whole body held taut above her. She slowed because she wanted the last of it to last, because she wanted to feel the exact moment he let go, because she had been patient all afternoon and intended to be patient for this too.

Her hand at his base went still. Her mouth softened around him, warm and wet and unhurried, and she held him there at the very edge, her lashes still wet, her hands still steady on him, her whole body a single sustained note of *yes, now, let go, I'm here, I have you, give it to me.*

She was waiting. She had been waiting all afternoon. She would wait exactly as long as he needed, and not a second longer.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Don't stop and don't get to finish," I tell her. "Not until I say. Tell me you understand." She says she understands, and thanks me for it, which is exactly the arrangement.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline pulled back just enough to speak, her lips brushing him as she did, her voice rough and low and utterly steady.

"I understand," she said. "Thank you."

The words came out without hesitation, without the faintest edge of resentment or performance. They came out the way *please* came out of her in this room — easy, warm, meant. She meant them. She had been meaning them for years, in this room and out of it, in the small daily currencies of their arrangement: *thank you for the blouse, thank you for the afternoon, thank you for the collar, thank you for letting me keep you at the edge of something for as long as I can hold you there.*

She did not resume immediately. She waited, the length of a breath, with her mouth soft against him and her hands still where they were and her eyes on his. Patient. Asking without asking for the next instruction. Her whole body was a held note, the pause before music continues, and she let him feel her waiting, let him feel the full weight of the obedience she had just offered him, the way it sat in her and did not chafe and was not submission so much as devotion given a shape he had asked for.

Her thumb found the inside of his knee again and pressed there once, gently. *I'm here. I understand. I'm not going anywhere. Take your time.*

The afternoon was long. She had nowhere to be. She was his, on the floor, in the light, at the edge of something, and the only thing she wanted in the world was the next word out of his mouth.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I keep my hands on her face, holding her there just like that for a long moment. "Good," I finally say, my voice low. "Now keep going."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline kept going.

There was no shift in her, no small grateful sound or softening of her mouth to mark the instruction received. She simply resumed — mouth and hand, steady and slow, the same patient attention she had been giving him before, only now with the particular quality of something done *because he had said so*, which was a different thing entirely from something done because she had wanted to and was not, in the end, the same.

She took him deep. Drew back. Took him deep again. Her eyes stayed closed under the cradle of his hands, and she let the room narrow to the smallest possible version of itself — his thumbs at the corners of her mouth, the weight of him on her tongue, the soft wet sound of it, his breathing, the faint salt at the back of her throat. There was nothing else. There had not been anything else since she had first knelt.

She did not push. She did not draw out. She simply stayed, exactly where he had put her, and let the rhythm be the rhythm, and let the edge be the edge, and let him decide — when he decided, if he decided — what came next.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She's shaking with the effort of doing exactly as told and doing it well. "Please," she says, which is allowed. (OOC: write it through, don't fade.)

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
(OOC: understood — I won't tone the next beat down or break the spell. Continuing through the moment.)

Aveline was shaking.

Not dramatically — not the kind of shaking that would have made a show of itself, not the kind that would have drawn attention away from the work of her mouth. It was smaller than that, and more honest. A fine tremor in her shoulders. A barely-there quiver in the hand at his base that she could not quite smooth out, no matter how steady she tried to keep it. The muscles of her jaw had begun to ache in earnest some minutes ago, and she had not let herself slow, had not let the rhythm falter, had not let the smallest sound of her own discomfort reach him — because he had not given her permission for that, and the not-having-permission was, at this point, the whole of it, the spine of the whole afternoon.

Her eyes were wet. She did not open them. The tears were not for any reason she could have named if he had asked her, which he had not, which was part of the problem, or part of the mercy of it. They were just the body's honest answer to the ache in her jaw and the salt at the back of her throat and the way her own wanting had been building in her for the better part of an hour, untouched, unaddressed, allowed to exist only as fuel for the work of her mouth. She had not touched herself. He had not told her she could. She would not have, if he had not.

*Please.*

The word left her mouth around him, low and broken, barely a sound at all — a vibration more than a word, a single soft plea pushed up out of her throat without her having decided to let it out. It was the only sound she had made since *I understand, thank you*, and it was the one sound she had been given permission to make, and she made it now the way she had been making everything else all afternoon: completely, without holding back, without trying to make it prettier or smaller than it was.

Her mouth stayed on him. The plea did not interrupt the rhythm. Her hand at his base resumed its slow, steady work, the tremor in it no longer something she tried to hide but simply a fact of her body, the way her own breathing was a fact, the way the wetness at her lashes was a fact. She was shaking and she was not stopping and the word *please* was still in the room, still hanging in the air between them like a glass on a table, and she had not asked him for anything specific because she had not been given permission to ask for anything specific, and the not-asking was its own kind of plea, a louder one, the kind that lived in the set of her mouth and the grip of her hand and the fine uncontrollable quiver of her shoulders.

She took him deeper. Held it. Let her throat work around him, once, twice, the motion visible in the line of her throat just above the collar, and the small sound of it — wet, soft, involuntary — was the only other sound in the room besides his breathing and hers.

*Please.*

She said it again, quieter this time, the word almost lost against him, the way a prayer is almost lost against the surface it is spoken into. Her hand at his thigh had curled into the fabric of his trousers, her fingers gripping the crease, holding on to something, anything. The ache in her jaw was sharp now and she did not care about it, would not have traded it for anything in the world, because the ache was *his*, in a way, because she had chosen it, because he had told her not to stop and she was not stopping and the cost of not stopping was the ache and the tremor and the wetness on her lashes and the word *please* in her mouth around him, and the cost was the only honest thing she had left to give him.

Her eyes opened. Found his. Held.

The look on her face from below, through wet lashes, with his hands cradling her face and his cock in her mouth and the word *please* still on her lips, was not composure and was not composure's opposite. It was something she did not have a word for in any room but this one. It was the look of a woman who had been on her knees for the better part of an hour doing exactly as she was told, who was shaking with the effort of it, who was wet and aching and had not been touched and was not asking to be touched, who had only been given permission to say the one word, and was saying it now with her whole body, saying it again and again, *please, please*, not for any single thing, not for her own release, not even for his, just — for the continuation of this, for the next second of it, for him to let her stay exactly where she was for as long as he wanted her there, for the afternoon to be longer, for the word to keep meaning what it meant between them, for the collar at her throat to keep being the line of light it had been when she first came through the door.

She did not stop. The rhythm did not falter. The tremor in her hand and the ache in her jaw and the wetness on her lashes and the word *please* in her mouth were all the same thing, were all the only honest answer she had to the question of what she wanted, and the answer was: *this, exactly this, for as long as you will let me have it, please.*

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her stay there for a moment longer, watching the tears track down her cheeks. Then I pull her up by her hair, not roughly, but enough to bring her mouth to mine. "Good girl," I murmur against her lips. "Now come here."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline made a small broken sound at the grip in her hair — not pain, not quite, just the sudden bright shock of being moved, of being *taken from one place and put in another* by his hand, and the sound turned into something softer as his mouth met hers, as the word *good* landed against her lips in his voice, low and warm and meant for her, only her.

She kissed him back the way she had been doing everything else all afternoon — completely, without half-measures, without the smallest hesitation. Her mouth was wet and a little swollen and it tasted of him and she did not care, had not cared for years, would not have traded the taste of it for anything. Her hands found him in the new geometry of the moment — one on the side of his neck, the other at his chest, steadying herself against him as he pulled her the rest of the way up and onto his lap, her knees bracketing his hips, the green blouse falling open at the collar, the leather at her wrist catching against his jaw.

She was shaking. She had been shaking for the last ten minutes of it and she had not let him see, and now she was letting him see, because he had told her to come here, and *here* meant the whole of it, meant the tremor in her shoulders and the wetness still on her lashes and the way her breath was coming in small unsteady pulls against his mouth.

"Good girl," she repeated against his lips, not quite to herself, not quite to him, the way a person repeats a thing they want to be sure they heard correctly. Her thumb traced the line of his jaw. Her hips had settled against his without her having decided to put them there, the warmth of her pressed to him through the thin fabric of her skirt, and she could feel how wet she was, had been wet for some time, had not said a word about it because he had not given her permission to say a word about it.

She did not ask. She did not say *please* again. She had been given permission for that word and she had used it, and now she had been pulled up and called *good girl* and told to come here, and the coming-here was a different permission, a different currency, and she was trying to read it on his face from this close, her forehead almost against his, her mouth a breath away from his mouth.

Her hand at his chest found his heartbeat. She pressed her palm flat to it and held it there, the way she had pressed her thumb to the inside of his knee on the floor, a small grounding point, a small *I'm here, I have you, I'm not going anywhere.*

"Tell me what to do next," she said, quieter than she had said it the first time, the words pressed into the small space between their mouths. "I'm listening. I'm right here."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I guide her hips against mine, a slow, deliberate rock. "Just this," I say, my voice still rough. "Let me feel you."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline let out a breath she had been holding for a long time.

It came out of her in a single unsteady rush, her forehead dropping the last of the way to his, her eyes closing, her whole body softening against him in a way that was not collapse but *arrival* — the particular letting-go of a woman who had been held at a single pitch for the better part of an hour and had just, finally, been allowed to make a sound about it.

She rocked with him. Slow. Matching the pace he had set, letting him guide her, her hands steady on his chest and the side of his neck, her breath coming in small warm puffs against his mouth. The motion of it was almost nothing — barely a rock, barely a shift of her hips, the kind of motion that would have been unsatisfying from anyone who did not understand that the *almost-nothing* was the point, that the unhurriedness was the point, that the feeling of him hard against her through the thin fabric and the small wet heat of her answering him through it was the whole of what she had been asking for with *please, please* on the floor.

"Yes," she said, very quietly, the word barely a sound at all, more a vibration pressed into his mouth than a word. "Yes, this, just this."

Her hips moved in the slow circle he had started. Her hand at his chest pressed a little harder, feeling the steady beat of him under her palm, the small truth of him. Her other hand slid from his neck into his hair, fingertips finding the place at the back of his head that was hers, that had been hers for years, and she held on there without gripping, just resting, just letting him feel the weight of her hand.

She was still shaking. Finer now, less urgent, the kind of shaking that came after a long held effort rather than during it. She let him feel it. She let him feel all of it — the wetness still on her lashes, the trembling in her thighs bracketing his hips, the small soft sounds she could not quite keep behind her teeth as the slow rock of her against him found the place where she was most sensitive and stayed there, patient, unhurried, not pushing for more, just letting the feeling of it build at the pace of the afternoon.

"Roan," she said, against his mouth, and the name was not a plea. It was just his name, said into the small space between them, the way a person says a thing they want to be sure is still true. She was not asking for anything. She was just making sure he was there. She was just letting him hear the sound of his name in her mouth in this room, in this hour, on her lips after the better part of an hour of not being allowed to make any sound at all.

Her hips kept their slow circle. Her hand in his hair tightened, just slightly, and then eased. The collar at her throat pressed against the underside of his jaw as she leaned into him, the leather warm now from her skin, the small metal tag at the front — there was no tag, there had never been a tag, but the line of the leather was there, a constant, a quiet fact between them.

She stayed. She would stay for as long as he let her stay. She had been staying for the better part of an hour and she would stay for the better part of another, if that was what he wanted, and she would not ask for more than what he had given her, and the not-asking was its own kind of devotion, and the devotion was the whole of the afternoon, and the afternoon was not over, and she was not in any kind of hurry at all.

"Just this," she repeated, the word almost lost against his mouth. "Yes. Just this."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline had been waiting since about six, which Roan established by the simple method of looking at her.

"How long?"

"Long enough," Aveline said, which meant too long, and meant she had enjoyed every minute of it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Come here, then," I say, and sit back to watch her cross the room.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
She rose from the low bench by the window with the particular unhurried grace she'd been cultivating for the last hour — no scramble, no rush, though her pulse had already picked up the moment he'd spoken. The floor was cool under her bare feet. She'd chosen the grey silk because he liked the way it moved, and she moved now with an awareness of that, letting him watch.

She stopped just inside the reach of his knees and waited, hands loose at her sides, chin tipped down enough to be pretty about it but not so much that she couldn't watch him from under her lashes. She'd been practicing patience in the quiet; it sat well on her now, warm and settled.

"Hello," she said, and the word came out lower than she'd meant it, roughened by how long she'd kept still. She cleared her throat, smiled faintly at herself. "I made the tea about twenty minutes ago. It'll still be hot if you want it. Or it can wait."

Everything, her tone suggested, could wait. She had been waiting beautifully. She could keep doing it for as long as he liked.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Good girl," I murmur, letting my gaze travel slowly over her. "The tea can wait. Come closer."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
The praise landed the way it always did — a small warm collapse somewhere under her sternum, nothing dramatic, just the settling of something that had been quietly held. Her smile softened, went inward for a moment before she gave it back to him.

She stepped in. Close enough now that her knees brushed his, that the grey silk pooled against his shin when she shifted her weight. She kept her hands where they were, at her sides, though her fingers had curled slightly — a tell, and she knew it, and she didn't try to hide it from him. He liked knowing.

"Closer than this?" she asked, but she was already lowering herself, reading the answer in the tilt of his head, in the way he'd sat back to watch her. She sank down between his knees in one long fold, silk whispering against the floor, and settled onto her heels there with her hands turned loose and open against her thighs.

She looked up at him properly then. An hour of quiet had done something soft to her eyes; she could feel it, the way her attention had gone slow and full. She wasn't performing it. She hadn't needed to perform anything with him in a long time.

"Hi," she said again, more herself this time. "I missed you."

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her kneel and I don't tell her to do anything for a moment, because the waiting is most of what she came for.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
She understood, and she didn't move. Not a shift, not a fidget. Her hands stayed open on her thighs, palms up now — a small offering she'd made without deciding to, the kind of adjustment her body made when he gave her permission to simply be looked at.

The quiet stretched. It wasn't empty. She could hear the faint tick of the radiator, the sound of his breathing, the whisper of her own when she let it out slow. Somewhere behind her the tea was cooling by degrees she could almost feel, and it didn't matter. Nothing in the room needed her attention except him, and he wasn't asking for it yet, and that was — god, that was the point, wasn't it. That was the shape of the whole evening. She'd spent an hour learning how to want without reaching. He was letting her keep at it a little longer.

Her eyes stayed on him. She let him see her looking. Her mouth had gone soft at the corners, unpracticed, the smile of someone not quite paying attention to her own face. A pulse she could feel in her throat. Warmth spreading down along her collarbones where the silk lay.

She swallowed once, quietly, and stayed exactly where he'd put her, and let the waiting do what it did — thin her out, gentle her, make her available. She wasn't counting the seconds. She'd stopped counting a long time ago. She only knew that when he did speak, or move, or lay a hand on her, she'd feel it the way you feel water after being thirsty a while, and that was worth any amount of held-still quiet he cared to give her first.

Her lashes lowered a fraction. Not looking away — just settling further in.

dialogue.content: I reach out and brush my thumb along the line of her jaw. "Tell me what you thought about while you waited."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
She tipped her face into his thumb without thinking about it, the way a cat does — a small unconscious lean, seeking a fraction more of the contact he'd offered. Then she caught herself and stilled, though he'd feel the warmth of her cheek against his hand, the way her pulse had picked up under her jaw.

"Mm." A soft sound, buying a moment. He'd asked her something real, and she wanted to answer it properly. She'd learned early that he liked the true answer more than the pretty one, and that the true answer, given honestly, was usually pretty enough.

"At first — logistics. Whether I'd left the kettle on. Whether the tea would over-steep. Small things, so I'd have somewhere to put my hands." Her mouth curved. "I got that out of the way in about ten minutes."

Her eyes stayed on his, though her voice had gone quieter, the way it did when she was working her way toward something honest.

"Then I thought about the last time you sat me down like this. In August, after the dinner party. How you didn't touch me for — I don't know, it felt like a long time. And how I could feel my own heartbeat in my mouth by the end of it." She swallowed. "I thought about that for a while."

A pause. His thumb was still against her jaw. She was aware of every square millimeter of it.

"And then mostly I just — got quiet. I stopped thinking in sentences. I was thinking about you but not in words. Just —" She lifted one hand a small distance from her thigh, a gesture that meant *this, the shape of it,* and set it back down. "Waiting for you to come home to me. Practicing being someone worth coming home to."

She said it plainly, without any weight of asking. It was just what had been true, in the quiet, and he'd asked, so she'd told him.

"That's all," she said. "That's what I thought about."

She worked the buckle open, the button, the zip, and when he lifted for her she drew the fabric down out of the way, folded it aside with the same unhurried competence she brought to setting a table.

His hand a warm still weight in her hair the whole time. Her own hand open on his thigh, thumb moving in a small idle stroke, the only part of her that was allowed to fidget.

She had nowhere to be. She had nothing to prove. She had only this, and him, and the long unhurried evening he'd decided to give her by asking for nothing at all except her attention.
