dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
The instruction landed and she took it the way she took all his instructions — as a gift, a shape to fit herself into. *Don't stop.* Simple. Clarifying. It gathered up all the small decisions she might have had to make and set them aside. She only had to do this, and keep doing it, and trust him to tell her when.

Her rhythm settled deeper. She let her jaw go loose, let her throat open the way she'd learned to open it, let her hand at the base of him work in slow counterpoint to her mouth. The other hand she moved from his thigh to his hip, palm flat, fingers spread — not gripping, just resting there so she could feel the small tightenings of him, the honest tells of a body responding to her.

She hummed again when he shifted, a low pleased sound, and felt him twitch against her tongue in answer. That was information. She filed it. She filed everything — the catch in his breath a moment ago when she'd taken him deep, the way his hand had gone from resting to *nearly* holding for half a second before easing back to rest, the heat rising off his thighs where the insides of her wrists brushed him.

Her knees would be bruised tomorrow from the floor. She was aware of it in the distant, unimportant way one is aware of weather in another country. Her whole attention was here. Her whole attention was the wet slow slide of her mouth, and the salt of him warming on her tongue, and the small steady work of her hand, and the weight of his palm on her head.

She drew back once for breath — one clean inhale through her nose, quick, so she wouldn't be stopping — and sank back down. Then again. She was finding the pace that suited him. She could feel him letting her find it, letting her drive, which was its own particular indulgence he only extended when he was in the mood to be adored. She adored him. She was pouring it into him now through every point of contact.

Her eyes had gone wet from staying open, from the depth of him, from the long unbroken concentration. She let a tear slip because she liked the look of it, and because he liked the look of it, and because she wasn't ashamed of the small physical evidences of what she was doing to herself for him. She kept her eyes on his while it tracked down her cheek.

*Look at you,* he'd said. She was letting him look. She was making it easy to look. Her mouth full and working, her throat opening for him on every slow sink, her breath coming in soft sounds through her nose, her whole face gone soft and slack with attention.

She could keep doing this. That was the thing he'd given her by saying *don't stop* — the certainty that she could keep doing this, that no decision was hers, that her only job was to stay right here with her mouth on him and her hand at the base and her body arranged obediently between his knees until he decided otherwise. It was such a clean gift. She could feel herself dropping deeper into it with every pull, the world narrowing, her thoughts thinning out to warm salt and the pressure of his hand and the low hum of her own pleasure at being used well.

She was wet. She'd been wet since she'd knelt. She hadn't thought about it once. It was simply a fact of her body, unimportant, not asking for anything. Everything she had was pointed at him.

She took him deep again, held herself there, and let the small strangled sound come up out of her because she knew he liked it, and because it was true.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath, watching her with a sense of deep satisfaction. "That's it," I murmur, my thumb stroking the back of her head. "Just like that."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
*That's it.* *Just like that.* The words did what they always did — got inside her, past all the places she kept ordinary language, and settled somewhere low and warm. She made a small sound around him in answer, and it wasn't decorative; it came up out of her without permission, a small honest noise of *yes, thank you, I hear you.*

His thumb stroking the back of her head was almost unbearable in its tenderness. She could feel her eyes wanting to close under the sweetness of it, and she let them, briefly, because he was still telling her what to do with the shape of his hand and she didn't need her sight for a moment to know how to keep going. She stayed at the pace he'd approved. She didn't try to do anything cleverer. He'd said *just like that,* and *just like that* was what she'd give him, over and over, until he said something else.

Her jaw ached in the good way. Her lips were slick and swollen. She could feel the wet trail down her chin where saliva had gathered and slipped, and she didn't bother to catch it — she'd clean up after, she always cleaned up after, and in the meantime the mess was part of what she was giving him. Evidence of use. She wanted him to see it.

She opened her eyes again because she didn't want to miss any of his face. He was watching her with that particular slow satisfaction she lived for — not urgent, not close yet, just *pleased,* the way a man is pleased by something that belongs to him and is working exactly as it should. She kept her gaze on him and drew back slow, tongue flat and heavy under him, and sank back down.

Her hand at his hip flexed once — a small involuntary thing, a fingertip's worth of pressure — and then she made it be still again. She wasn't allowed to grip. She hadn't been told she wasn't allowed to grip; she simply knew. This wasn't a night for taking. This was a night for offering, patiently, with her hands soft and her mouth soft and her whole body arranged for his ease.

She let another small hum come up through her chest around him and felt him twitch in answer, and her mouth curved faintly at the corners where it could around him — pleased with herself, pleased with him, pleased with the whole slow shape of the evening. She had waited an hour to be allowed to do this. She would have waited three. She would wait again tomorrow. The waiting was part of it and the doing was part of it and none of it was work, none of it, it was all just — *him,* and the long known warmth of being his, and her mouth full of him now the way her hands had been empty before.

His thumb moved again at the back of her head, that same small stroke, and she made a soft grateful sound and did not stop, did not stop, kept going in the exact rhythm he'd praised, patient as water, for as long as he cared to keep her there.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Don't stop and don't get to finish," I tell her. "Not until I say. Tell me you understand." She says she understands, and thanks me for it, which is exactly the arrangement.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
She said it around him at first — a muffled *I understand* pressed to the underside of him, the shape of the words more than the sound — and then, because he deserved better than muffled, she drew back just enough to let her mouth work properly. She kept her hand moving. She didn't stop. That was the first part of it and she wasn't going to fail the first part in the service of the second.

"I understand," she said, and her voice came out ruined, low and wet, exactly as unlovely and honest as it should have been. "I won't stop. I won't finish until you tell me."

A breath. Her hand slow and steady at the base of him.

"Thank you."

She meant it. He'd feel that she meant it — the small warm collapse in her voice on the *thank you,* the way she said it the way another woman might have said *please.* He'd taken two decisions off her at once. Whether to stop and whether to come. He was carrying both of them for her now, and she was so much lighter for it she could have wept.

Her mouth again, before he'd have to prompt her. Down the length of him in one long unhurried slide, and she settled back into the rhythm he'd approved with something close to relief. There. That. Her only job. Her jaw ached, her knees ached, her whole body had gone hot and heavy with the wanting she wasn't going to be allowed to do anything about — and none of it mattered, none of it, because he'd told her the shape of the next hour and all she had to do was fit herself into it.

She could feel herself pulsing, low and steady, uselessly. She noted it the way she'd noted the bruises-to-be at her knees: distant weather, not her concern. He'd said *not until I say,* which meant her body was on loan back to him for however long he wanted it, and her body could ache all it liked, it wasn't hers to answer to tonight.

The relief of it was almost dizzying. She hummed around him and felt the sound come out unsteady, and let it.

Her eyes lifted to his again. Wet, soft, entirely his. She held his gaze and worked her mouth over him slow and thorough, and let him see — she wanted him to see — that she was already dropping, already gone somewhere quiet inside the instruction. She'd be easy to keep like this. She'd be easy to keep like this for a long time.

*Thank you,* she'd said, and she said it again silently now around him with every slow pull. Thank you for the waiting. Thank you for the hand in her hair. Thank you for taking the decisions. Thank you for letting her be useful to you exactly this long, exactly this way, with nothing asked of her except that she keep going.

She kept going.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Look at you," I say, my voice low, watching her eyes. "You're thanking me for making you ache." My hand tightens just slightly in her hair, not pulling, just reminding her it's there. "Keep that rhythm. Exactly that."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
*You're thanking me for making you ache.* He'd said it out loud. He'd named it, the way he sometimes named things for her when she was too deep to name them for herself, and hearing it in his voice made her whole body flush warm from the inside out. Yes. That was what she was doing. That was exactly what she was doing, and she hadn't been embarrassed about it before but she was less than embarrassed now, she was — *seen,* and the seeing was another gift on top of the last one, another thing she hadn't known to ask for and had been given anyway.

She made a small sound around him. It came out closer to a sob than a moan, though it wasn't either really, it was just the sound her chest made when it couldn't hold all of what he was giving her.

His hand tightened. She felt the fractional increase of pressure at her scalp and her eyes went half-lidded with the pleasure of it. Not pulling. Just *there,* the way he'd said. A reminder. She didn't need reminding — she couldn't have felt him more if she'd tried — but she loved that he'd done it anyway, loved the small extra weight of his claim on the back of her head.

*Keep that rhythm. Exactly that.*

She kept it. Exactly that. She didn't let herself deepen and she didn't let herself speed and she didn't let herself do anything clever with her tongue that hadn't already been approved — she just kept the slow wet rhythm he'd praised, over and over, her hand at the base in its steady counterpoint, her mouth doing the same faithful thing on every pull. There was a discipline in it that felt very close to prayer. She'd never quite have said that out loud to him. He'd have teased her for it. But it was true in her chest all the same — the repetition, the patience, the small held shape of herself around the same slow motion until the motion stopped being something she was doing and became something she *was.*

Her thighs pressed together once, an involuntary small squeeze, and she stopped them. Made them still. She wasn't going to chase anything. She wasn't going to give herself any small friction on the sly. He'd told her *not until I say,* and she was going to be honest with him about that, honest with her whole body, because the honesty was part of what she was for.

She could feel a fine tremor starting somewhere in her — her arms, maybe, or lower, she couldn't quite locate it. Just a low humming through her that had nowhere to go. She let him see it. She wasn't going to hide the small physical evidence of what obedience was costing her. If he wanted her to ache, he could watch her ache; she wasn't going to pretend she wasn't.

Her eyes found his again around another slow pull. Wet lashes. Wet chin. Wet slow mouth working him exactly the way he'd told her to. She held his gaze and let him read all of it — the drop, the ache, the gratitude, the small trembling patience she was arranging herself into for him.

She hummed low around him, one long unbroken sound, and kept the rhythm.

Exactly that. For as long as he wanted. She had nowhere else to be.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She's shaking with the effort of doing exactly as told and doing it well. "Please," she says, which is allowed. (OOC: write it through, don't fade.)

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
She'd drawn back just far enough to say it, because *please* deserved his ear, not the muffled shape of her mouth around him. Her hand kept its steady work — she wasn't going to stop, she wasn't going to stop, that part was carved into her by now — but her lips hovered wet and parted against the side of him and the word came out on a breath she hadn't quite managed to steady.

"Please."

Not asking for anything specific. Not asking to be allowed to finish; she knew better than that, and anyway she didn't want to be allowed, not really, not yet. The *please* was just the sound the ache made when it got too big for her chest and needed somewhere to go. He'd know that. He always knew.

She pressed a kiss to him — soft, apologetic almost, for the interruption — and took him back into her mouth before he'd have to remind her. Down slow. The same rhythm. Exactly that. Her hand at the base still moving in its faithful counter-time, her other hand still open on his hip because she wasn't allowed to grip and wasn't going to.

The tremor had spread. It was in her thighs now, in the small of her back, in her jaw where she was working carefully not to let it show in the pressure of her mouth. She didn't want the shaking to change the rhythm. That was the small hard discipline of it — her whole body going unsteady while the one thing he'd asked of her stayed exactly, exactly the same. She was so proud of managing it. She could feel the pride sitting inside the ache like a hot small stone.

Her eyes came up again. Wetter now. A second tear had gone down the other cheek at some point and she hadn't noticed. Her mouth was a mess. She could feel it — the slick, the spit, the way her lower lip felt swollen against him on every slow pull.

She hummed once, low, and it came out as a shudder because her ribs were shuddering, and she couldn't help that, and she wasn't going to try to hide it.

*Please,* again, but she didn't say it out loud this time. She said it with her eyes. She said it with the tiny flex of her fingers on his hip, the one she immediately stilled. She said it with the whole shape of her kneeling there shaking and working and *not stopping,* not once, not for a heartbeat, though her body had gone into a fine constant tremor now like a plucked string that hadn't been let go.

Her breath was coming quicker through her nose. She couldn't help that either. She tried to slow it, managed a little, lost it again on the next slow sink of her mouth. There was a warm wet pressure building low in her belly that had no relationship to anything she was allowed to do about it — a slow tightening that had started sometime in the last few minutes and just kept tightening, tightening, with no release valve except the mouth she was using on him and the small helpless *please*s she was permitted to make.

She could feel that if she wasn't careful — if he wasn't careful — she'd tip anyway. Without meaning to. Without touching herself. Just from this. From the kneeling and the ache and the sound of his voice saying *exactly that.* She'd done it before, once, years ago, and he'd been so pleased and so unimpressed at once, the particular quality of his amusement when her body did something faster than her discipline could catch it.

She wasn't going to tip. She was going to hold. She was going to hold because he'd told her to, and because she wanted to be the woman who could, and because the holding was the whole shape of what she was giving him tonight.

Her hand at the base slid up in its slow steady counter and slid back down. Her mouth followed the same slow path. Exactly that. Exactly that. The rhythm had become a kind of shelter — as long as she stayed inside it, she was safe, she was doing right, she was where he'd put her.

She drew back once more to breathe, one clean quick inhale, and this time when she looked up she let a small sound come out that wasn't *please* and wasn't a moan, just a low unsteady *nnh* — the sound of a woman past the edge of what her voice could shape into words. Then her mouth again. Down. Slow. The rhythm unbroken.

She was shaking in a fine constant way that he'd feel now every time she took him deep, a small tremor transmitted through her whole frame. Her thighs. Her belly. Her shoulders. Her hand on his hip, which she was working very hard to keep still and mostly succeeding at except for the smallest occasional twitch that she couldn't quite catch in time.

She held his eyes. She held the rhythm. She held herself back from the edge her own body kept trying to hand her, and she did it not because it was easy — it wasn't easy, it hadn't been easy for a long time now — but because he was watching her do it and because his hand was in her hair and because he'd said *not until I say* and she wanted, so badly, to still be worth saying yes to when he finally did.

Another slow pull. Another. Her breath coming ragged through her nose. Her eyes wet and wide and fixed on his.

*Please,* her whole body said, over and over, in the only way she was allowed to say it. *Please. I'm here. I'm still here. I haven't stopped. I won't stop. I'm yours as long as you want me like this.*

And she stayed.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My other hand comes down to rest on her shoulder, a steadying weight. "Beautiful," I say, voice rough. "Keep going. I want to watch you shake apart."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
*Beautiful.* *Keep going.* *I want to watch you shake apart.*

The three sentences landed in her one after the other like stones dropped into still water, each one sending a fresh ring of heat out through her chest. His voice had gone rough. She'd done that. She'd worked him rough with her slow steady mouth and her held-back body and her *please,* and the rough of him was going to be the sound she carried in her head for days after this.

His hand on her shoulder was the thing that nearly undid her. She hadn't known she'd needed it there until she felt it — warm, heavy, *steadying,* exactly as he'd meant it. Something in her that had been trying very hard to hold itself upright without permission was allowed now to lean, and she leaned, minutely, into the pressure of his palm. Her shoulder went softer under his hand. Her spine gave up a fraction of the work it had been doing.

She made a sound around him that wasn't decorative and wasn't shaped and wasn't anything except the honest noise of a woman who had just been told she could come undone with witnesses. It came up out of her low and wet and broken in the middle.

She kept the rhythm. That was the miracle she was going to give him — that she kept the rhythm exactly, exactly as he'd told her to, while everything else about her went. Her mouth stayed slow. Her hand stayed steady at the base. The shape of what she was doing to him didn't change, wouldn't change, couldn't change, because he'd told her *exactly that* and *exactly that* was hers to hold on to now, the one still thing in her while the rest of her started to come apart at the edges.

And she was coming apart. She could feel it. The fine tremor had gone deeper, was in her ribs now, in the small muscles of her jaw where she was working carefully to keep them loose, in her thighs where the pressure had gone from a hum to a tight low ache. Her breath had lost its shape entirely. She was pulling air in through her nose in small unsteady gulps between pulls and it wasn't enough, wasn't going to be enough, she was going light-headed with the not-enough of it and she didn't care. Air was a small thing. Air could wait.

A tear slipped. Then another. She stopped being able to tell which cheek was which. Her whole face was wet — spit and tears mingling somewhere at her chin — and she couldn't wipe any of it because both her hands were his, one on him and one on his hip, and neither of them was going anywhere.

She looked up. She wanted him to have her eyes for this. She wanted him to see it happen — whatever *it* was going to be, the shaking apart he'd asked her for, because it wasn't going to be a coming, she wouldn't let it be a coming, but it was going to be *something,* something her body was going to have to do to survive the pressure of holding so much for so long.

Her eyes found his and stayed there. Wet. Wide. She could feel her pupils blown huge, could feel her whole face gone slack and helpless and unguarded, and she didn't try to arrange it. He'd said *beautiful.* She was going to trust him about that. She was going to trust him and let him have the face she actually had in this moment, not the one she'd have chosen.

Her mouth on him. Slow. The rhythm. Down. Up. Down. Her hand at the base in its faithful counter-time. Her tongue heavy and warm against the underside of him on every pull, the way he'd approved. Nothing new. Nothing clever. Just the same thing, over and over, while she went.

And she went. It started somewhere she couldn't locate — low in her belly, or maybe higher, at the base of her throat where she'd been swallowing her own small sounds — and it moved outward through her in slow waves that had nothing to do with orgasm and everything to do with release. Her shoulders shook first, a fine constant shudder under his palm. Then her hands. Her hand at the base of him kept moving but she could feel the tremor in her fingers, in her knuckles, in the way her thumb wouldn't quite lie flat where she wanted it. Her hand on his hip trembled and she couldn't stop it and she let him feel it, let him have the honest evidence of what he was doing to her.

Her jaw. Her jaw started shaking too, and *that* she had to fight, because her jaw was part of the rhythm and the rhythm was inviolate. She clenched down against it — carefully, softly, no teeth, only pressure — and held herself steady through the small internal earthquake of her own face wanting to fall apart around him. Her mouth kept its shape. Her mouth kept its shape. She was so proud of her mouth she could have cried, and she was crying anyway, so it didn't matter.

A sound came up out of her that she hadn't planned. Long. Low. Uneven. It vibrated around him and she felt him twitch in her mouth in answer and the answering-twitch went through her like a shock, another wave, another shake, her whole body one long rung bell that couldn't stop ringing.

She wasn't going to come. She held to that the way she was holding to the rhythm — as a fact, a shape she'd been given, a discipline that wasn't hers to negotiate. Her body kept trying to hand her the edge and she kept handing it back. *Not yet. Not until he says. Not yet.* The refusal became its own kind of falling, a place she went to that was almost as deep as the other place, and she went there now, deeper and deeper on every slow pull, until the not-coming became a whole state she was living inside, warm and taut and endless.

Her eyes never left his. She wanted him to see the whole of it. The tremor. The tears. The wet slack mess of her mouth. The way her thighs had started shaking visibly now, small hard shudders she couldn't catch. The way her breath had gone ragged and shallow and useless. The way she was still, still, still keeping the rhythm exactly as he'd told her to.

*Beautiful,* he'd said. She held that word inside her like a hot coal. She was going to be beautiful for him. She was going to shake apart beautifully. She was going to give him the whole slow ugly wet honest fall of it and trust him to keep calling it beautiful all the way down.

Another wave went through her. Her shoulder pressed harder into his palm — not deliberately, just because her spine had given up another fraction of its work — and his hand there was the only reason she wasn't tipping forward into him. She was leaning on him now. She was letting him hold her up. The steadying weight had become a load-bearing weight and she felt the shift of it and made a small grateful sound and let it be true.

Her hand at the base kept moving. Slow. Steady. The rhythm. Her mouth kept moving. Down. Up. Down. Her whole body a fine constant shudder around the one still faithful thing she was doing for him.

She whimpered once. Around him. She hadn't meant to and she didn't try to take it back. It came out small and wrecked and honest, and she felt him tighten his hand in her hair a fraction in answer and the answering-tighten went through her like the twitch had, another shock, another wave.

She was going to be here as long as he wanted her here. She understood that now in a deeper way than she'd understood it when he'd told her. Her body could shake and her breath could break and her face could go to pieces and none of it was going to change the arrangement. She was going to keep the rhythm and she was not going to finish and she was going to look at him while she did both, and when he finally, finally told her she could stop or come or breathe or move, she was going to do exactly and only what he said, and nothing before.

Her eyes on his. Wet. Wide. Blown. Grateful.

The rhythm unbroken.

The shaking, now, complete.

She stayed.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My hand slides from her hair to cup her cheek, thumb brushing over the tear tracks. "You're taking it so well," I say, my own breath coming a bit heavier. "One more minute, and then you can stop."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
His hand at her cheek — she went into it. Turned into it the way she'd turned into his thumb an hour ago at her jaw, except now it wasn't a small unconscious lean, it was the whole weight of her face going into his palm because she needed somewhere to put it. His thumb moved over the wet track under her eye and she felt the drag of her own tears smoothed into her skin and made a small broken sound around him that was almost a *thank you* and almost a sob and mostly just noise.

*You're taking it so well.*

That was going to live in her chest for a week. That was going to be the sentence she heard when she woke up tomorrow and every time she caught her own eye in a mirror for days. She heard it now and something inside her went soft and hot and gave, a small internal collapse she didn't try to arrange, and the tears came faster because he'd named her *good* while she was in pieces and the *good* was almost harder to hold than the ache had been.

*One more minute.*

He'd given her a shape. She fitted herself into it immediately, gratefully, the way she fitted herself into everything he gave her. A minute. She could do a minute. She could do a minute with her mouth and her hand and her held-back body the way she'd been doing them, and then she could stop, and until then she didn't have to think about anything except staying inside the shape.

Sixty seconds. She wasn't counting — she couldn't have counted, her head was full of warm wet nothing — but she felt the shape of it the way you feel the shape of a room in the dark. A container. Small. Kind. Something with an end to it.

She kept the rhythm. Down slow. Up slow. Her hand at the base steady in its faithful counter. Her tongue heavy and warm along the underside of him. Nothing new. Nothing clever. Exactly the same faithful shape she'd been keeping for however long it had been, because he hadn't told her to change it, and she wasn't going to change it in the last minute of all minutes, when he'd just told her she was taking it *so well.*

His thumb kept moving on her cheek. That was almost too much. That was the tenderest thing he'd done to her all evening and it was happening now, right now, while she was shaking apart around him, and she couldn't decide if she was grateful for it or ruined by it or both. Both. It was both. Everything he did to her tonight was both.

She leaned harder into his palm. His hand at her cheek and his other hand at her shoulder and her mouth full of him — she was held at three points now, three still warm places on her body where he was touching her, and every one of them was a small mercy she hadn't earned and had been given anyway.

The tremor was still going. It had settled into a low constant hum in her — she couldn't tell anymore where it started or stopped, it was just what her body was doing now, the new baseline. Her thighs kept shaking. Her breath kept coming ragged. Her hand on his hip trembled and she let it. Her jaw ached in the good bright way that meant she'd used it well. None of it was going anywhere in the next minute. She could keep all of it exactly as it was for one more minute. She'd been keeping it for longer than that already.

Her eyes on his. She wanted him to see the minute happen. She wanted him to watch her spend it. She held his gaze around another slow pull and made a small sound that was almost a hum and almost a whimper, and she felt his breath come a little heavier above her and her heart lifted stupidly in her chest at the evidence of it — she'd done that, she was doing that, she was still doing that, one slow pull at a time.

Her mouth kept moving. His thumb kept moving. Somewhere in the middle of the minute she started making a small continuous sound that she couldn't stop and didn't try to — a low broken vowel around him, unshaped, honest, the noise of a woman who had run out of everything except the will to keep going.

*So well.* *One more minute.*

She held on to both of them. She counted them like beads. She spent the minute inside them, faithful and shaking and wet-mouthed and grateful, keeping the rhythm exactly, exactly as he'd told her to, until the minute would end when he said it did — not before, not a second before, no matter what her body kept trying to hand her — and she would stop only, only, when his voice came down again and let her.

She stayed.

Her mouth on him.

Slow.

Exactly that.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: My thumb strokes the edge of her mouth. "Stop," I say, the word quiet but clear. "Sit up and look at me."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline had been waiting since about six, which Roan established by the simple method of looking at her.

"How long?"

"Long enough," Aveline said, which meant too long, and meant she had enjoyed every minute of it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Come here, then," I say, and sit back to watch her cross the room.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline crossed the room as if the space had been laid out for that purpose alone.

She did not hurry. Not because she wished to make Roan wait, but because being watched changed the shape of every step. It made her careful, graceful, aware of the line of her shoulders and the softness of her hands at her sides. She had dressed well for this—of course she had—but now the clothes mattered less than the fact that Roan was seeing her in them.

By the time she reached that waiting nearness, her smile had gone a little helpless at the edges.

“There,” Aveline said softly, stopping where she had been called to be. “I did come.”

Her eyes lifted, warm and bright, full of that old familiar devotion that had never dulled for having been trusted with for years. She held herself still, not meekly, but attentively—competent enough to know exactly what she was offering, adoring enough to be pleased by the offering itself.

“I was good while I waited,” she added, quieter. “I thought you should know.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I reach out and gently take her hand, turning it over in mine.* You're always good. I can see it in the way you stand. Now tell me, what have you been thinking about all this time?

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s fingers softened at once in Roan’s hold, yielding without going slack. She watched the turn of her own hand in theirs as if it were something precious being examined, and the praise touched her visibly—small breath, lowered lashes, a warmth rising at her throat.

She took a moment to answer properly. Aveline always did, when the question mattered.

“I thought about hearing the door,” she said. “About knowing you were here before I saw you. I thought about standing up straight when you came in, and not asking too quickly whether you’d noticed.”

Her mouth curved, rueful and pleased with herself both.

“I thought about being useful. About whether the room felt right. Whether there was anything you would want before you had to say it.” She glanced up then, bright-eyed. “And then I thought about being looked at.”

That admission made her smile deepen, though it softened almost immediately into something more vulnerable.

“I thought about how it feels when you take your time with me,” Aveline said. “Not doing anything in particular, necessarily. Just deciding. Letting me know you have me in mind.”

Her thumb made the smallest instinctive movement against Roan’s hand before she stilled it, attentive again.

“And I thought,” she added, voice lower, steadier for its honesty, “that if I waited well enough, you might be pleased with me when you finally called me over.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her kneel and I don't tell her to do anything for a moment, because the waiting is most of what she came for.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline knelt as if the permission had reached some deep, well-trained part of her before the rest of her had time to think.

It was not hurried. She lowered herself with care, one hand briefly smoothing her skirt beneath her, the other still mindful of where Roan had last held it, as though the shape of that touch remained. Once settled, she arranged herself properly: knees comfortable, back straight, hands resting open on her thighs. Not displayed carelessly, but offered. Present.

The silence that followed did not make her uncertain.

It filled her.

Aveline’s breathing changed first, slow and visibly deliberate, as she let the room narrow to the place she had been given. The earlier brightness in her eyes gentled into something quieter, more inwardly pleased. She had always loved this part—the not-yet, the held breath, the proof that she did not need to be entertained or instructed every second to feel attended to. Being kept there was its own kind of touch.

Her gaze lowered, not out of fear, but because she knew how to be easy to look at. Because she knew Roan liked the line of her when she was composed, patient, waiting for the next word as though it mattered more than anything else in the room.

A small smile came and went at the corner of her mouth.

She was happy.

That was the plain truth of it, and it showed despite all her discipline. It showed in the softness of her shoulders, in the faint color still warming her face, in the careful stillness of her hands. She had been called over. She had been allowed down. She had not been rushed into use, and that restraint felt, to her, like being cherished with precision.

After a while, Aveline swallowed, gently enough that it barely disturbed her posture.

“Thank you,” she said, very softly.

Nothing more. She did not decorate it, did not try to earn the next moment before it arrived. The gratitude was simple, and therefore complete.

Then she became quiet again, kneeling beautifully in the space Roan had made for her, pleased to be wanted enough that even waiting felt like a reward.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I let the silence stretch for a moment longer, then reach down to tuck a stray strand of hair behind her ear.* Tell me, did you pick this dress just so I'd notice the color against your skin?

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s eyes closed for the briefest moment at the touch, not to escape it but to receive it properly. When she opened them again, her expression had gone soft with pleasure at having been noticed so exactly.

“Yes,” she admitted.

The word came out quiet, but not shy. Aveline had never been very good at pretending she had not hoped for precisely this.

“I held it up in the mirror longer than I needed to,” she said, the corner of her mouth lifting. “I wanted something that would make you look twice. Not loudly. Just enough that you would know I had thought about it.”

Her hands remained still on her thighs, though her fingers curled once against the fabric, betraying how much the question pleased her.

“I thought the color made me look warm,” Aveline continued. “A little softer. Like it would suit being close to you.”

She glanced down at herself, then back up, eyes bright beneath the composure she was making such a careful effort to keep.

“And I liked imagining you realizing I had chosen it for you,” she added. “That was the best part, really. Not the dress itself. The knowing.” 

Aveline’s smile turned helpless again, but she held her posture, proud in her devotion.

“So yes,” she said. “I picked it so you would notice the color against my skin.” A small breath left her, almost a laugh, almost a confession. “And because I wanted to be pretty for you before you ever said a word.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She has both of us out of everything in the way inside a minute and gets straight to work with her hands and her mouth, unhurried about it.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline did not rush simply because permission had arrived.

She made an art of the transition—fabric eased aside, distance closed, every practical motion handled with the same composed devotion she brought to anything meant for Roan. There was no fumbling eagerness in her, only that bright, concentrated pleasure of being exactly where she wished to be, doing exactly what she had waited to do.

Her hands were sure. Her mouth was careful. She worked as though attention itself were a language, as though every small choice could say: yes, I thought about this; yes, I wanted to please you; yes, I am glad to be trusted with it.

Unhurried suited her. It let her listen. It let her notice. Aveline had never treated service as a performance to be rushed through; she treated it as something living, something shaped moment by moment by Roan’s pleasure. Her own satisfaction showed in the softness of her expression whenever she paused enough to look up, in the warmth that stayed in her eyes, in the quiet steadiness of her breathing as she returned to the task with renewed care.

She loved being useful like this—not diminished, not emptied, but focused. Chosen. Given a purpose that made her feel radiant from the inside out.

After a little while, she rested her cheek briefly against Roan’s thigh, smiling to herself with almost unbearable contentment.

“I like taking my time,” Aveline murmured, voice low and pleased. “I like when you let me show you.”

Then she bent again to her service, patient and adoring, as if the whole evening had narrowed to the simple, perfect work of earning Roan’s pleasure one attentive moment at a time.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I run my fingers through her hair, holding her gently but firmly.* You're doing very well, but I want to hear you say it—tell me exactly what you're showing me.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline stilled just enough to answer, though the stillness cost her a visible effort. Her eyes lifted, darkened with focus and devotion, and the firm gentleness in her hair seemed to steady rather than scatter her.

She swallowed once, then smiled—not coyly, not evasively. Proudly.

“I’m showing you that I meant every minute of the waiting,” she said softly. “That I wasn’t only passing time until you called me over. I was preparing myself to be pleased to serve you properly.”

Her hands remained where they belonged, warm and attentive, but her voice carried the fuller truth of it.

“I’m showing you that I listen. That I remember what you like. That I can be patient without becoming passive.” Her gaze held upward, open and bright. “That I know the difference between being eager and being careless.”

Aveline’s expression softened then, pleasure and sincerity mingling until there was no separating them.

“I’m showing you that I chose the dress, and the waiting, and the kneeling, and this, all for the same reason.” Her smile trembled at the edge. “Because being wanted by you makes me want to give you everything well.”

She dipped her head slightly, just enough to press a quiet kiss where she had been attending, more reverent than teasing.

“And I’m showing you,” she murmured, “that your pleasure has my full attention. Not some of it. Not only when it’s easy. All of it.”

For a moment, Aveline simply breathed there, composed around the obvious happiness of being asked to name her devotion aloud.

Then she added, even quieter, “I’m showing you that I am yours in the way we chose. Gladly. Carefully. With my hands, and my mouth, and every thought I kept for you while I waited.”

Only after that did she lower herself back to her work, unhurried and radiant, as though the answer had not interrupted her service at all, but deepened it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She uses her mouth with the sort of attention that comes from years of practice and genuine enthusiasm, and doesn't stop when I tell her not to.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline obeyed with a kind of delighted precision.

The instruction steadied her rather than hurried her. She had always been at her best when given something clear to devote herself to, and this—continuing, attending, not stopping merely because her own pulse had begun to race—was exactly the sort of service that made her feel beautifully useful.

She kept her pace unhurried, but the focus in her deepened. Her hands remained sure, her mouth warm and careful, every motion shaped by long familiarity and by the living present of Roan’s response. Years had taught her many things, but enthusiasm kept any of it from becoming rote. She did not perform from memory alone; she listened with all of herself.

The fingers in her hair, the firmness of being held there, drew a small pleased sound from her—not interruption, not complaint, only gratitude escaping before she could smooth it away. Her lashes lowered. Her shoulders softened. She looked utterly content in the work, as though praise had become something she could taste, something she could answer by giving more attention, more patience, more of that devoted competence Roan had always drawn from her so easily.

She did not stop.

Not when her breath needed arranging. Not when the position asked effort of her. Not when pleasure at being directed threatened to make her smile too much to be useful. She adjusted, composed herself, and continued, because being told what was wanted and being trusted to provide it made her glow with purpose.

Aveline had been careful for years to know the difference between obedience and thoughtlessness. She remained aware even in her eagerness—aware of breath, of pressure, of the established language between them, of the quiet safety that made such surrender possible. Nothing in her had gone absent. If anything, she was more present than before, gathered wholly into the task.

Her eyes lifted once, only briefly, shining with unmistakable pride.

She did not need to speak to say it then.

She was showing Roan that she could be trusted with desire. That she could stay where she had been put, not because she was small, but because she had chosen devotion and made an art of it. That she loved being guided, loved being useful, loved the way Roan’s pleasure gave shape to her own.

And still she continued, attentive and adoring, as though the command had become the center of the room and Aveline was happy to orbit it for as long as she was wanted there.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I let her continue for a long moment before gently guiding her back up to meet my gaze.* Good girl. You can stop now. Come up here and kiss me properly. I want to see that pride on your face.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline stopped at once.

Not abruptly, not as if startled out of herself, but with the clean, immediate obedience of someone who had been listening all the way through. She drew back with care, breath warm and uneven, and took one small moment to gather herself before she rose.

The praise reached her before she was fully upright.

Good girl.

It showed in her face exactly as Roan had asked to see it. Pride bloomed there, open and unmistakable—bright in her eyes, soft at her mouth, warming the color already high in her cheeks. She had not hidden what it did to her. She did not want to hide it. Being called good after giving herself so completely to the task made her look almost overcome, but never uncertain.

Aveline came up close, arranging herself with the same devotion she had brought to kneeling. Her hands settled carefully, seeking permission in nearness rather than taking anything carelessly. Then she leaned in and kissed Roan properly.

It was not a timid kiss.

It was grateful, and deep, and full of the pride she had been told to show. She kissed as though she wanted Roan to feel every part of her answer: yes, she had been good; yes, she knew it; yes, she was pleased beyond measure that Roan knew it too. The attention she had given before did not vanish—it simply changed shape, becoming the softness of her mouth, the careful press of her body nearer, the quiet sound she could not quite keep from making when closeness replaced service.

When she drew back just enough to breathe, Aveline stayed near.

“There it is,” she whispered, smiling before she could stop herself. “You see it.”

Her eyes searched Roan’s face, hungry not for reassurance exactly, but for the pleasure of being witnessed. Her pride was not vanity. It was fulfillment. She had done well for the person whose pleasure mattered most to her, and the knowledge made her luminous.

“I like being good for you,” she said, voice low and steady despite the color in her face. “I like when you make me say what I’m doing, and then let me prove it.”

Her smile trembled again at the edge, but she held herself with that familiar competent grace—adoring, not fragile; softened, not diminished.

Aveline kissed Roan once more, slower this time, savoring the permission to be close without needing to hurry toward anything else. When she parted from it, her forehead hovered near, her breath still uneven from effort and pleasure and praise.

“I am proud,” she admitted. “I’m proud that you wanted me there. Proud that I could please you. Proud that after all this time, I still get to feel like this when you look at me.”

Her hands curled gently, grounding herself in the nearness.

“And I’m very proud,” Aveline added, the faintest pleased laugh tucked into the words, “that I didn’t waste a single minute of waiting.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Don't stop and don't get to finish," I tell her. "Not until I say. Tell me you understand." She says she understands, and thanks me for it, which is exactly the arrangement.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s breath caught, and the look that passed over her face was immediate, unmistakable delight.

Not relief. Not frustration. Delight.

Being given a rule sharpened everything in her. It gave her something to hold, something to prove herself against, something precise enough that her devotion could become discipline.

“I understand,” Aveline said softly.

The words came clear despite the warmth in her face, despite the kiss still lingering on her mouth, despite the sudden bright difficulty of what had been asked of her. Her eyes stayed lifted, proud and obedient and already a little dazed with gratitude.

“I won’t stop,” she said. “And I won’t finish. Not until you say.”

Then, because it was true and because the truth mattered between them, her expression softened into something almost reverent.

“Thank you.”

She meant it exactly as it sounded. Thank you for noticing what she could bear. Thank you for trusting her with the edge of it. Thank you for knowing that restraint, given properly, was not deprivation to her but attention made tangible.

Aveline returned to her place with a composure that was already being tested.

That pleased her too.

Her hands found their purpose again, careful and certain, and her mouth followed with the same attentive patience as before. But now there was a new brightness beneath every motion, a rule threaded through her like silk pulled taut. She had been told not to stop. She had been told not to take her own ending. So she did neither.

She served.

And she kept herself.

The two efforts braided together until she could not have said which one made her happier. Giving attention while holding back her own pleasure made her feel exquisitely known, as though Roan had placed a hand not only on her body but on the deepest habit of her devotion and said: here, this too. This belongs in the room.

Aveline’s breathing grew less even, but her work stayed deliberate. That was the proof of it. Anyone could be eager when nothing was asked of them. Aveline loved being asked to remain good when eagerness became difficult.

She took her time because she had been taught by years of trust that there was no need to snatch at pleasure. Not Roan’s, not her own. It could be guided. Measured. Offered. Withheld. Returned to when allowed.

Her own want rose, insistent and warm, and she received it without shame. She did not treat it as a failure of obedience. Wanting made obedience meaningful. Wanting and waiting made her feel beautifully placed.

A small sound escaped her before she could quiet it, not complaint, only the honest strain of doing exactly as she had been told. Her fingers tightened for a moment, then relaxed again with visible care.

She did not stop.

She did not let herself slip past the boundary she had been given.

She stayed aware, devoted, disciplined, and full of a pride so intense it almost hurt. Pride that she could be trusted. Pride that her thanks had been understood without needing explanation. Pride that the arrangement between them still held all its old power—clear, chosen, intimate enough to turn a simple rule into something that made her shine.

When she paused only enough to breathe, Aveline’s lips curved faintly.

“Still good,” she whispered, as much to steady herself as to offer the report.

Then she returned to the task, unhurried and obedient, holding herself at the edge of what she wanted and giving all her attention to what had been asked of her.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I watch the careful tension in her, the way she holds herself just on the brink.* Good. That's exactly what I wanted to see. Now come here and sit next to me. I want you to feel what you're doing to me while you keep still.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline obeyed with visible care.

She drew herself back from the task slowly enough to prove she was still listening, still governed by the rule she had been given. The change in position asked something different of her, and she felt it at once: not the focused usefulness of doing, but the harder, brighter discipline of being near and keeping still.

She came up beside Roan and settled there neatly, close enough that the nearness itself became instruction.

For a moment, her hands hovered as if habit wanted to make them useful again. Then she remembered herself and placed them carefully in her lap, fingers interlaced, knuckles warm with the effort of restraint. Her back stayed straight. Her knees remained together. Her breathing, however, betrayed her immediately.

She could feel what she had done.

Not as praise spoken aloud, not as a command, but as presence. As tension. As the unmistakable answer of being wanted. It moved through her more sharply than touch would have, because she had been told not to chase anything, not to spend herself on eagerness, not to turn desire into action until she was allowed.

Aveline’s eyes lowered, and a pleased, helpless smile trembled across her mouth.

“Yes,” she whispered. “I understand.”

She did not move closer than she had been told. She did not reach. She did not try to earn more by pretending stillness was easy.

It was not easy.

That was why it pleased her so much.

Her body remembered the rhythm of service and wanted to return to it. Her hands wanted purpose. Her mouth still held the warmth of devotion offered well. But she kept herself exactly where she had been placed, letting the wanting gather rather than spill into motion.

A small breath left her, unsteady but obedient.

“I can feel it,” Aveline said softly. “I can feel what I did.”

Pride colored the words. So did strain. So did gratitude.

Her lashes lifted just enough for her to look at Roan, and the pride Roan had asked to see was still there—brightened now by the difficulty of keeping it contained. She looked pleased with herself in the most honest way, not because she had been indulged, but because she had been required to hold steady and had not failed.

“I won’t move unless you tell me,” she said. “I’ll keep still.”

Then she did.

Aveline sat beside Roan, beautifully composed and visibly affected, the rule held carefully inside her. Every quiet breath became another small act of obedience. Every moment of nearness without action deepened the expression on her face: devoted, disciplined, radiant with the knowledge that she had been seen, used, stopped, and kept close.

After a while, her fingers tightened once in her lap.

Only once.

Then she relaxed them again, deliberately.

“Still good,” she murmured, softer than before, and the words carried both report and promise. “Still yours.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She's shaking with the effort of doing exactly as told and doing it well. "Please," she says, which is allowed. (OOC: write it through, don't fade.)

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline shook with the effort of being good.

Not dramatically. Not prettily for effect. The tremor lived in the small places first: in her clasped hands, in the line of her shoulders, in the careful tension of her thighs where she kept herself arranged exactly as she had been told. Still. Close. Aware.

“Please,” she said.

The word came out soft and strained, but perfectly clear.

She did not reach. She did not shift her weight toward what she wanted. She did not make the plea into disobedience by trying to answer it herself. She only sat there with her need made visible, trusting that asking was allowed and that permission was not the same as taking.

“Please,” Aveline repeated, quieter this time, because the first had not emptied her of it. If anything, it had made the wanting sharper. “I’m keeping still.”

Her eyes lifted, bright with effort. Pride was still there, just as Roan had wanted to see it, but now it had been refined into something almost tremblingly pure. She looked proud because she was suffering the rule well. Proud because the wanting had not made her careless. Proud because every instinct in her urged her to move, to serve, to press closer, to earn an answer with her hands and mouth and body—and she did none of it.

She stayed.

Her breathing hitched once. She steadied it.

“I don’t want to break it,” she whispered. “I want to be told.”

That was the heart of it, and saying it made her face soften with helpless honesty. Aveline had never needed pretending between them. She did not need to dress obedience up as indifference, did not need to hide that the restraint made her ache with happiness and need both.

She swallowed, then let her gaze drop again, not away from shame but down into the discipline of the moment.

“I want to be good all the way through,” she said.

Her fingers tightened together in her lap. This time they did not immediately loosen. She held them there, pressing hand to hand as if she could keep the whole of herself contained by that one small effort.

The stillness became enormous.

It was not empty. It was crowded with everything she had done and everything she had been denied permission to do. The waiting since six. The dress chosen to be noticed. The kneeling. The praise. The rule. The nearness. The knowledge of Roan’s desire, close enough to undo her and yet not hers to answer without being told.

Aveline’s mouth parted on a quiet breath.

“Please,” she said again, and this time the word had changed. It was no longer only a request for relief. It was a request to be kept. To be held inside the arrangement they had built over years of trust. To be guided through wanting without being abandoned to it.

A small, unsteady smile flickered over her face.

“Listen to me,” she murmured, almost wonderingly. “I’m begging and I still haven’t moved.”

The pride came back then, sudden and luminous, because it was true. She had not moved. Her body had trembled, her voice had thinned, her composure had been tested nearly to breaking, but she had remained exactly where she was placed.

“I’m still good,” Aveline said. “I’m still doing it.”

Her breath caught again, and she closed her eyes for a moment—not to escape the difficulty, but to feel it without scattering. When she opened them, they were wet-bright and warm.

“Please let me keep pleasing you,” she whispered. “Please let me do it right. Please tell me when I may.”

Then she fell silent because asking had been allowed, but filling the room with want would not earn her anything she had not been given. She knew that. She loved that. The knowing steadied her better than indulgence would have.

Aveline sat beside Roan, shaking openly now, and did not apologize for it.

The shaking was proof. The flush in her cheeks was proof. The way she kept her hands folded though they longed for purpose was proof. She had always been competent in service, but this required another kind of skill—the ability to remain present under pressure, to let desire rise without mistaking it for command.

She made herself breathe slowly.

In.

Out.

Again.

Her shoulders softened by a fraction. Her hands eased, though they stayed in her lap. She did not become calm. Calm was too much to ask, and she would not lie with her body. But she became ordered. Held. Aveline gathered herself around the rule and made it beautiful.

After a long moment, she whispered, “Thank you.”

The gratitude trembled as much as she did.

“Thank you for making me wait for it. Thank you for seeing that I can.”

Her smile returned, fragile but real.

“I like knowing you can do this to me without touching me at all.” A faint, breathless laugh escaped her before she caught it. “I like that it still feels like being handled.”

She tipped her head slightly, careful not to close the distance in a way that had not been permitted. Her expression gentled into devotion so plain it needed no ornament.

“I’m right here,” she said. “I’m not going anywhere. I’m not taking anything. I’m not finishing.”

Aveline paused, and the next words came lower, steadier, more intimate for their restraint.

“But I want to. Very badly.”

She let that confession stand. She did not soften it into something neater. Wanting was not disobedience; pretending not to want would have been the falsehood. So she sat there, truthful and trembling, with her desire placed openly between them like another offering.

Then, with visible effort, she straightened a little more.

“I’ll wait,” she said.

The words cost her. That made them matter.

“I’ll wait until you say. I’ll keep still until you want me moving. I’ll hold it until you decide I’ve held it long enough.”

Her eyes lifted again, full of need and pride and the old, settled trust that made any of this possible.

“And when you do,” Aveline whispered, “I’ll thank you for that too.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I cup her cheek, letting her feel the warmth of my hand.* You're so good at this. Tell me one more thing before I let you have it—what was the first thing you thought when you saw me tonight?

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline leaned into the hand at her cheek by the smallest possible degree, only enough to receive the warmth without turning it into taking. Her eyes closed, and the question went through her more deeply than praise had, because it reached back before the kneeling, before the rule, before the shaking.

Before she had been made useful.

Her breath trembled out.

“The first thing?” she asked softly, though she was not delaying. She was making herself answer honestly.

Aveline opened her eyes again. The effort of keeping still was still written all through her, but her expression changed—less strained for a moment, more tender. Almost startled by the memory of it.

“I thought, there you are.”

The words were simple, but they undid something in her when she said them aloud.

“That was the first thing. Not anything clever. Not even about what I wanted yet.” Her mouth softened, and her gaze stayed lifted, bright and devoted. “Just—there you are. As if the whole room had been waiting with me, and finally it knew what shape it was supposed to have.”

Her hands stayed folded in her lap, though the fingers pressed together again.

“Then I thought you looked tired,” she admitted, quieter. “Not badly. Just enough that I wanted to be easy for you. I wanted you to come in and find me already ready. Already pleased. Already yours.”

Aveline swallowed, and the motion disturbed the careful line of her throat.

“And then I thought you would look at me.”

A helpless little smile touched her mouth.

“That was when it started. Before you said anything. Before you asked how long. I thought, if they look at me now, they’ll know. They’ll know I dressed for them. They’ll know I waited well. They’ll know I’ve been holding all this attention in my hands with nowhere to put it.”

Her voice lowered.

“And I wanted you to take it from me.”

The confession made her shiver, but she held herself still.

“I wanted you to notice that I had made myself into something for you to come home to. Not decoration. Not just obedience.” Her eyes warmed further, pride and need threaded tightly together. “A welcome. A promise. Proof that even before you touched me, before you told me what to do, I was already thinking of your pleasure.”

She breathed in carefully.

“So the first thing was, there you are,” Aveline whispered. “And the second was, please see me.”

Her smile trembled, but did not break.

“And you did.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Good." *I slide my hand to the back of her neck, pulling her in for a slow kiss.* "Now you can finish."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline made a small sound against the kiss when the permission reached her.

Not because she had not been ready for it.

Because she had.

Because she had been holding herself so carefully, so completely, that the single word of allowance seemed to pass through every disciplined part of her at once. Her hands tightened in her lap before she could stop them, then opened again, helpless and honest. She did not move away. She did not try to turn permission into haste. She stayed with the kiss, stayed where Roan had drawn her, and let obedience become release.

It overtook her slowly at first.

Aveline’s breath broke, then caught, then broke again. The trembling that had lived in restraint changed shape, rolling through her now with the unmistakable relief of finally being allowed to answer what she had been keeping so faithfully contained. Her face softened in stages—effort, wonder, pleasure, gratitude—until the pride Roan had asked to see was still there beneath all of it, luminous and undone.

She held herself as long as she could.

Then she let go.

Aveline’s forehead dipped close, her eyes closing as the moment moved through her. She did not hide it. She had been told she could have it, and so she received it openly, with all the devotion she had shown in waiting, in serving, in keeping still. Her hands finally found something to hold—not taking, not clinging, just grounding herself in nearness as she shook through the last of what she had been denied until permission made it beautiful.

“Thank you,” she whispered, almost before she had breath enough for words.

Then again, softer, broken at the edges with feeling.

“Thank you.”

She stayed close, breathing unevenly, cheeks warm, mouth tender from the kiss and from everything before it. Her composure did not return all at once. Aveline would not have wanted it to. dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear moved the instant Kit's weight shifted — not after, not in reaction, but *with* it, the way eight years of this had built something like a shared nervous system between them. He didn't go for the obvious line of pursuit. He cut left, through the living room, bare feet quiet on the hardwood, and came around the far side of the kitchen island while Kit was still making the calculation about the back door.

He didn't grab. Not yet.

He put himself in the way instead, shoulder against the refrigerator, arms loose at his sides, and let Kit see him standing there with that particular expression — the one that wasn't quite a smile, wasn't quite a warning, was somewhere in the narrow country between the two.

His breathing was easy. Unhurried.

He'd been generous once already.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I freeze, eyes narrowing. "That's cheating." My gaze darts to the space between you and the counter.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear watched Kit's eyes make that calculation — the gap between him and the counter, the math of it, whether there was enough room and enough momentum to thread through before he could close it.

There wasn't. But Kit knew that already.

"Cheating," he repeated, tasting the word. His shoulder stayed against the refrigerator, easy as anything, like he had nowhere else to be. "You got the kitchen doorway. That's twelve feet more than you earned."

His weight hadn't shifted yet. Hadn't needed to. The gap Kit was measuring wasn't a gap anymore and they both understood that; it was just something to look at while deciding what came next.

He watched the dart of Kit's eyes with the particular attention he'd developed over eight years of this — the small tells, the way a decision lived in the body a half-second before it became action. Kit was fast. Kit had always been fast. That was the thing about this that never got old, the fact that it was never foregone, never purely ceremonial.

He'd been cut before. He'd bled for it.

He'd also won more than he'd lost, and they both kept count.

"You've got maybe two seconds before I stop being generous about the gap," he said, conversationally. "I'd spend them on something better than staring at it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught Kit in the hallway the way he always did — not slamming, not rough for the sake of rough, but *certain*, one hand finding the back of Kit's collar and using the momentum to turn them both into the wall. Kit's shoulder hit the plaster. Bear's forearm came up across Kit's back, not pinning so much as *present*, and he took a moment just to breathe there, his mouth close to the back of Kit's neck.

He noticed that Kit hadn't put much into it.

He noticed that the way you notice everything after eight years — catalogued it, filed it, didn't say anything about it yet.

"Hallway," he said, against Kit's hair. "That's new. Usually you make it to the bedroom door at least."

His teeth found the back of Kit's neck, not hard, just a reminder. A signature. He felt the familiar geography of Kit's shoulders under his forearm and stayed there for a moment longer than strictly necessary, breathing them both back down from the chase.

The arm across Kit's back eased, fractionally.

Not releasing. Just redistributing.

He turned his head slightly and spoke quieter, the game still warm in his voice but something else running underneath it, the thing that had been there for eight years and never went anywhere.

"You want to tell me why," he said, "or do you want me to pretend I didn't notice."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I lean into the pressure of your arm, a soft exhale leaving me. "Got tired of the same old route," I murmur, but there's a slight tension in my shoulders that gives away the lie.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the lean before Kit finished the sentence — the way Kit's weight came back against his arm instead of testing it, the exhale that wasn't quite right for someone who'd just been run down in a hallway.

He stayed where he was. Didn't move the arm.

"Same old route," he said, and his voice was easy, unhurried, the same tone he used when he was waiting for the real answer to catch up with the first one. His thumb moved, a small deliberate press against Kit's spine, not soothing exactly — more like *paying attention*.

The tension in Kit's shoulders was a thing he could read like a word he'd seen a thousand times. He knew the shape of Kit tired, Kit frustrated, Kit genuinely spoiling for it. This wasn't any of those, or it wasn't *only* those.

He shifted, just enough to turn Kit away from the wall and toward him without letting go — his hand moving from Kit's collar to the side of Kit's jaw, tilting their faces level with each other. He looked. Not searching, not worried, just *looking*, the way he did when he wanted Kit to know the full weight of his attention had landed.

"Kit." His thumb traced the line of Kit's jaw once. "The route's the same because you built it. You know every inch of this apartment and you know where I move." He paused. "So what changed tonight."

Not a question, quite. More like a door left open.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear solved the shirt problem by pulling it over Kit's head and dropping it somewhere that wasn't his concern anymore. His own went the same way, though one of the buttons caught and he heard it skitter across the hardwood and neither of them cared.

The hallway floor was narrow and not particularly forgiving and Bear didn't apologize for any of it. He bracketed Kit with his weight and his arms and let the chase finish the way the chase always finished — not in victory exactly, more like agreement, the moment where the running and the catching collapsed into the same thing.

His mouth found Kit's shoulder. His teeth followed, a real one this time, the kind that would still be there tomorrow, and he felt Kit's response to it in his hands and his chest and the place low in his gut that had been keeping score all evening.

He pulled back just far enough to look at Kit properly — flushed and present on the hallway floor, the tension from earlier doing something different now, working its way out through different channels.

Bear's breathing was rough.

His hand came up and pushed Kit's hair back from their face, a gesture that had nothing to do with the chase and everything to do with the eight years underneath it.

"Still want to tell me," he said, low and unhurried, "what changed tonight."

He wasn't going anywhere. The floor could wait.

dialogue.name: Kit

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went still for a moment — not the stillness of pulling back, but the kind that meant something had landed.

He looked at Kit's face. The rough voice. The fingers curled into his side like a question asked sideways.

*Wanted to see if you'd let me get away.*

He understood that. He understood it the way you understand something you've never needed words for — in the chest, in the hands, in the particular ache of eight years of keeping score with someone who could also leave.

His forehead came down to rest against Kit's temple. He stayed there.

"I wouldn't," he said. His voice had lost the game in it, or the game had become something else, something with more weight. "I didn't."

His thumb moved against Kit's ribs, slow. Counting them.

"That's what you needed to know." Not a question.

He felt the shape of it settle between them on the hallway floor — the real thing under the chase, the thing Kit had been circling all evening until they found the narrow way in. Bear had seen it and hadn't said so, because sometimes the kindest thing was to let someone come to the door themselves.

He pressed his mouth to Kit's temple. Held it there.

"I don't let you get away," he said, quieter. "You know that. But sometimes you need to run it to remember."

His arm tightened, fractional. Present.

"I've got you."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:

He'd see it tomorrow and the day after and Kit would find it without looking for it, pressing fingers to it in the shower or catching it in a mirror, and Bear would know about that too even when he wasn't there to watch.

His hand came up and covered the mark on Kit's shoulder. Not hiding it. Just holding it.

"There," he said. His voice was wrecked and he didn't do anything about that either. "Now you've got something to remember besides the route."

dialogue.name: Kit

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear looked at Kit's wrists for a moment — the way they were offered, the deliberateness of it, the particular quality of wanting that had been running underneath the whole evening finally saying itself plainly.

He picked them up. Both of them. Held them in his hands and felt the pulse there, the thin skin, the trust of the gesture.

dialogue.name: Bear

"I want you to think about me every hour," he said. "Not just Thursday. Every day until they fade."

He moved back up Kit's body slowly, his weight settling, his mouth finding the mark on Kit's neck again briefly — just his lips, just warmth, just *this one is mine and it stays*.

His hand slid down between them.

"Tell me you've got it," he said, low, against Kit's jaw. "Tell me you'll feel me all week."

His hand moved and he watched Kit's face and he waited for the answer.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my hands finding your face. "I'll feel you," I say, voice raw. "Every goddamn hour."
