dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear was on Kit in three long strides, one hand catching the doorframe to pivot around the corner as Kit bolted. The kitchen was a bad choice—tile floors, limited exits, the refrigerator blocking the path to the back door. Bear had let Kit choose the direction. That was the only generosity left in the tank.

The sound of bare feet slipping on tile was all the advantage Bear needed. A hand closed on the back of Kit's shirt, twisted, used the grip to halt forward momentum and swing Kit around. Bear's other arm braced against the counter, caging Kit in.

"Generosity's off the table," Bear said, breathing hard but grinning. The chase had been short but the pulse was already up—that first spike of adrenaline that made everything sharper. Bear's thumb found the edge of Kit's collarbone and pressed, not gently, feeling the heartbeat hammering under the skin.

"You chose the kitchen." Bear's voice dropped, pleased. "That was either a mistake or an invitation. Which?"

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I grin back, breathless, and lean into the pressure of your thumb against my collarbone. "Thought you might appreciate the challenge," I say, my voice low. "Tile’s slippery. Makes it more fun when you catch me."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's grin widened, something fierce behind it. "Fun for who?" The thumb pressed harder, a small punishment for the sass, and Bear leaned in close enough that Kit could feel the heat radiating off bare skin. The chase had done its work—Bear was warm, pulse visible at the throat, pupils already blown wide.

"Slippery works both ways," Bear said, and shifted weight deliberately, boot heel finding the grout line between tiles for purchase. The hand on Kit's shirt released only to flatten against the counter on the other side of Kit's hip, completing the cage. "Difference is, I don't *need* to run."

Bear's mouth found the curve where neck met shoulder—teeth first, a sharp press that would leave a mark, followed by the drag of tongue to take the sting from it. A familiar pattern. A claiming rhythm they both knew by heart.

"You wanted to be caught in here." It wasn't a question. Bear's free hand found Kit's hip, thumb hooking into the waistband, anchoring. "Wanted the counter. The cold tile when you can't stand anymore."

Bear pulled back just enough to meet Kit's eyes, close enough that breath mingled.

"Tell me I'm wrong."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear noticed. Of course Bear noticed—eight years had honed the ability to read Kit's body like a familiar book, every false sprint and halfhearted dodge catalogued and remembered.

" hallway," Bear said, voice low and satisfied, hands pinning Kit against the wall with practiced ease. One wrist caught and pressed above Kit's head, the other hand free to roam. "Not even trying to make it to the kitchen now."

Bear's teeth found the tendon in Kit's neck, bit down just enough to feel the muscle tense, just enough to leave the kind of mark that would purple by morning. The kind they'd both admire later.

"That's twice you've picked somewhere with no escape." Bear's thumb traced Kit's pulse point, feeling it jump. "Hallway's even worse than the kitchen. Nowhere to go but *into* me."

The hand not holding Kit's wrist slid down, palm flat against ribs, feeling the rapid breathing, the way the muscles shifted under skin. Bear's weight pressed forward, pinning Kit more thoroughly—thigh between Kit's legs, chest a solid wall of heat.

"You're not running from me tonight." It was half observation, half promise. "You're running *for* me. So I'll chase you right."

Bear's grip tightened on Kit's wrist, a warning and a claim.

"Last chance. Door's still behind me. Give me a reason to really catch you, or tell me you want this exactly where you are."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I push up on my toes to bite your earlobe, hard. "Caught me," I say, voice rough. "Now do something about it."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The bite sent a jolt straight through Bear's spine—a bright sharp thing that unlocked something behind the ribs. Bear's breath hissed out through teeth, and the grip on Kit's wrist turned iron.

"Something," Bear repeated, and the word came out low and dangerous. "Right."

The hand on Kit's ribs slid around to the small of Kit's back and *shoved*, using the wall for leverage, grinding their hips together with no patience left for teasing. Bear's thigh pressed up harder between Kit's legs, giving something to work against.

Then Bear released Kit's wrist—only to grab Kit's jaw instead, thumb and fingers pressing into the hinge, tilting Kit's head back against the wall with controlled force. Bearing down. Making sure Kit felt every inch of height and weight difference.

"You don't get to goad me into it and then rush," Bear said against Kit's mouth, not quite kissing—just close enough that lips brushed with each word. "You wanted caught. You wanted the hallway. You wanted my hands on you where you can't move."

Bear's other hand found the hem of Kit's shirt and shoved it up, palm rough and hot against bare stomach, dragging upward until nails scraped ribs.

"So *wait* for it."

The hand on Kit's jaw slid back into hair, fisted tight, and pulled—exposing the long line of throat that Bear immediately set teeth to, biting down hard enough to make Kit feel it everywhere.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The floor was hard and cold and neither of them cared.

Bear's shirt went first—Kit's hands wrenching it up and over, Bear lifting arms just enough to let it clear before Bear was back down, one hand braced on the hardwood beside Kit's head. Kit's shirt was worse; Bear got it halfway up before impatience won and just yanked, fabric stretching, probably ruined, definitely worth it.

"Buy me a new one," Kit managed, and Bear laughed—short, breathless, mean.

"Maybe."

Then there was skin against skin and Bear stopped laughing, stopped thinking, stopped anything except the press of bodies and the way Kit's back arched off the floor. The hardwood was unforgiving; Bear could feel every shift of Kit's spine, every scrabble of shoulder blades seeking purchase.

Bear's hand found Kit's waistband again and this time didn't stop at the thumb. One rough tug, then another, fabric dragging down hips while Kit lifted to help—or hinder, it was always hard to tell, Kit's hands everywhere at once, pulling Bear closer and pushing and clawing parallel lines down Bear's back that would sting under the shower tomorrow.

"Fuck—" Bear hissed at the nails, and bit Kit's collarbone in retaliation, teeth pressing until Kit made a sound that went straight to Bear's gut.

The hallway floor. Eight years and they still ended up here, couldn't make it twenty more feet to the bed, too hungry to wait. Bear wouldn't have it any other way.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I get my teeth into your shoulder, biting down hard as my hands slide down your back. "Stop stalling," I grunt, hips lifting impatiently.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
"Stalling."

Bear pulled back just enough to look down at Kit, and the expression on Bear's face was something between offense and delight—the particular look Bear got when Kit said something that deserved answering for.

"You bite me and then call it *stalling*."

Bear's hand closed around both of Kit's wrists, pinned them above Kit's head against the hardwood with one grip, and held them there. The other hand finished what it started—fabric down and gone, tossed somewhere toward the kitchen that neither of them would remember until morning.

Bear settled between Kit's legs, weight deliberate, and the sound Kit made was worth every bruise the floor was going to leave.

"I'll show you stalling," Bear said, and then stopped—just stopped, full weight holding Kit down, close enough to feel everything and far enough that the stillness was its own kind of torture. Kit's wrists twisted in Bear's grip. Bear didn't budge.

"Say please."

The grin that followed was sharp enough to cut.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear did it again—same spot, teeth finding the crescent already forming and pressing deeper, feeling the skin give and the muscle beneath it tense. The sound Kit made vibrated through Bear's chest like a current.

"Again?" Bear murmured against the bite, tongue tracing the indentations. Not a real question. A warning.

Bear's grip on Kit's wrists shifted, tightened, and Bear's mouth moved—collarbone, the join of neck and shoulder, the soft skin below Kit's ear. Each one a bite. Each one hard enough to last. Bear counted them off like a tally, a scorecard written in teeth marks that Kit would find in the mirror tomorrow and press fingers to, remembering.

The one below the ear made Kit's whole body arch off the floor, and Bear held still through it, let Kit grind up against the weight pinning them down. Taking it. Cataloguing every reaction like a language only Bear spoke fluently.

"That's four," Bear said, low, lips brushing the wet skin of Kit's throat. "You want five, you say my name right."

Bear's free hand slid between them, found the place that made Kit's breath stutter, and just—rested there. Palm flat. Pressure without movement. Waiting.

"Say it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Bear," I breathe out, ragged, and press up into your hand. "Please."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The name landed somewhere behind Bear's sternum and detonated.

"There it is."

Bear's hand moved—finally, *finally*—and the sound Kit made was everything Bear had been waiting for. Not teasing anymore. The patience snapped like a thread and what replaced it was all teeth and pressure and the kind of rhythm that made the hardwood creak beneath them.

Bear's grip on Kit's wrists stayed iron-bound, pressing them into the floor with each thrust, a counterpoint to the way Kit's body bowed and twisted. The angle was wrong and the floor was brutal and Bear didn't care, couldn't care, because Kit was saying the name again—broken, half-swallowed—and it sounded like that first night, like every night, like something Bear would never stop chasing.

Kit's heel dug into Bear's back, pulling, demanding more, and Bear gave it. Gave everything. The hand between them worked in time with each push of hips, and Bear watched—couldn't look away—as Kit's face went slack and sharp by turns, the flush spreading down throat to chest.

"Look at me." Bear's voice came out wrecked. "Kit. *Look at me.*"

Kit's eyes opened, dazed and dark, and Bear held the gaze like a grip on a throat. Held it through the last brutal stretch where everything tightened and the hallway narrowed to the space between their bodies and Bear's name was a sound Kit made without words.

Bear came down hard, elbows barely catching in time, mouth finding Kit's shoulder and biting through it—the fifth mark, the deepest, the one that would ache when Kit reached for things on high shelves tomorrow.

Afterward: breathing. The hardwood pressing patterns into knees and elbows. Bear's forehead resting against Kit's temple, the sweat cooling between them.

"Floor again," Bear rasped, and the laugh that shook through was tired and triumphant. "We've got to stop doing this."

Neither of them moved.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear looked down at Kit's wrists, laid out like an offering, and something quiet and hungry settled behind Bear's eyes.

"Thursday," Bear repeated, tasting the word. Rolling it around like a promise being measured for weight.

Bear sat back on heels, pulled Kit up by one wrist, and turned it over. Pressed thumb into the pulse point first—feeling it, slow now, satisfied—then dragged teeth across the thin skin on the inside. Not biting. Not yet. Just letting Kit feel the edge of it, the threat of what was coming.

"This one lasts." Bear's mouth closed over the wrist, found the spot where the veins branched, and bit down with slow, deliberate pressure. Not a snap—a grind. The kind that bruised deep, layers of tissue compressing under enamel until Kit's breath caught and held.

Bear released it, studied the mark. Red, already darkening at the edges. It would be purple by morning and yellow-green by Wednesday. Thursday it would still ache when Kit gripped things.

"Good?"

Before Kit could answer, Bear took the other wrist and did the same—slightly higher, slightly harder, a matching set that would make Kit think of this every time sleeves rode up.

Then Bear pulled Kit forward, off the floor and into Bear's lap, hands spanning the width of Kit's back. Holding Kit upright when Kit's legs wouldn't.

"More," Bear said, and it wasn't a question. Bear's mouth found the hip—the jut of bone that sat right at the waistband line, the spot that would catch on denim tomorrow and make Kit hiss. Teeth pressed in. Kit's hand fisted in Bear's hair and pulled, and Bear growled against the skin and bit harder.

"That's three for Thursday." Bear pulled back, breathing hard again, hands steady on Kit's hips. "You want the count, you keep them. You flinch away from one, I start over."

Bear's thumb pressed into the fresh bite on Kit's hip.

"Where's four?"

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I press my palm flat against your chest, over the scratches I left. "Right here," I say, guiding your mouth down. "Make it count."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear looked down at Kit's hand, at the scratches already welting pink across Bear's chest—four parallel lines that would scab by morning—and understood.

"Matching set," Bear said, voice rough.

Bear leaned Kit back, one hand behind Kit's shoulders, lowering until Kit was half-reclined across Bear's lap. Bare chest exposed. Ribs still moving too fast. The scratches Kit had left on Bear were over the left pectoral, close to the heart. Bear matched the location on Kit's body—pressed thumb down first, finding the spot, marking it.

Then teeth.

Bear bit down slow. Not the sharp snaps from before—this was pressure that built, jaw tightening by degrees, feeling the skin compress and then the muscle beneath it and then something deeper. Kit's hand flew up and gripped Bear's forearm, nails digging in, but didn't push away. Bear felt the moment Kit's breath stopped—held it, counted three heartbeats against the tongue, then ground harder.

Kit made a sound that wasn't a word.

Bear released. Looked down. The mark was deep, a red crescent already darkening to something that would bruise spectacularly. Right over the heart. Right where Kit had scratched Bear. Mirror images they'd both carry.

"Four," Bear said, thumb pressing into the wet indentations, making Kit hiss. "That one'll hurt on Friday."

Bear pulled Kit back upright, gathered Kit against chest, chin hooked over Kit's shoulder. Both of them breathing hard. Both marked up. The hallway floor cold beneath them, the house quiet around them.

"Thursday," Bear murmured against Kit's ear. "I'm checking."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't stop.

The hallway floor had gone from cold to warm beneath them, body heat soaking into hardwood, and Bear laid Kit back down—fully this time, shoulders flat, spine pressing into the grain of the wood. Bear hovered above, one elbow braced beside Kit's head, the other hand tracing the fresh marks. Collarbone. Wrist. Hip. Chest. Checking each one with a thumb like a painter surveying work.

"Still want more," Bear said. Not a question. A read.

Kit's hand found the back of Bear's neck and pulled down, and Bear went—mouth landing on the center of Kit's chest, over the sternum where the bones were closest to the surface. Bear bit there first, a broad press of teeth that made Kit's ribs expand sharply under the weight. Then lower. The soft skin below the ribs, where the stomach dipped, where the muscles jumped and contracted when Bear's mouth found them.

Bear took time with each one. That was the difference now—the chasing urgency had burned down to something slower, steadier, a heat that didn't spike but sustained. Each bite was placed with intention. Jaw set. Pressure held until Kit's breath changed pitch, then released with a drag of tongue that turned pain into something harder to name.

"Count's gone," Bear murmured against the skin below Kit's navel, lips brushing hair. "You said stop keeping score."

Bear's hands gripped Kit's hips—both of them, thumbs pressing into the hip bone marks already there—and held Kit flat against the floor. Kit's thighs tensed, tried to close, and Bear pushed them apart with shoulders instead, settling between.

"I'm not counting anymore." Bear's breath was hot against the inside of Kit's thigh. "I'm just taking what I want."

The first bite on the inner thigh was sharp—sudden, teeth flashing, the kind that made Kit's whole leg jerk. Bear held on, fingers digging into Kit's hips to keep them from bucking. The second was slower, higher, where the skin was thinner and the blood ran close. Kit's hand found Bear's hair again, twisted, and Bear growled against the mark and bit a third one just beside it—a constellation of pain that would make sitting down tomorrow a constant, aching reminder.

Bear pulled back. Looked up the length of Kit's body—chest heaving, marks scattered like a map, the one over the heart already darkening toward purple. Kit's eyes were half-lidded, mouth open, wrecked in a way that made Bear's chest tight with something that wasn't just want.

"You're beautiful like this," Bear said, and the words came out rough, unplanned, pulled from somewhere Bear didn't usually voice. "Marked up and shaking. Mine."

Bear climbed back up Kit's body, dragging weight along the length of it—chest against chest, the scratches on Bear's skin pressing against the bite on Kit's, a matching sting that made them both inhale. Bear's mouth found Kit's jaw, bit the hinge of it, then moved to Kit's mouth. The kiss was teeth and tongue and the copper taste of a split lip neither of them could account for—maybe Kit's, maybe Bear's, didn't matter. Bear licked into Kit's mouth like ownership, one hand cupping the back of Kit's skull to hold the angle.

Kit's legs wrapped around Bear's hips, pulled, and Bear groaned into the kiss—a sound that came from low in the chest, something animal. Bear's hand slid down between them again, found Kit, and this time there was no teasing, no waiting. Just a grip and a rhythm and the way Kit's body arched off the floor like a bow being drawn.

"Stay with me," Bear said against Kit's mouth. "Don't go quiet on me."

Kit didn't. The sounds filled the hallway—broken syllables, Bear's name again, words that weren't words. Bear worked through all of it, pace relentless, wrist aching, and didn't stop when Kit's nails raked down Bear's back again—new lines over old ones, a palimpsest of marks that would layer and scab and peel.

When Kit came, it was with teeth in Bear's shoulder—the other shoulder, the unmarked one, evening the score—and Bear held through it, held still, let Kit shake apart against the hardwood floor while Bear's hand slowed but didn't stop, drawing it out until Kit's leg kicked and a sound escaped that was almost a sob.

Bear pulled back. Looked down.

Kit was wrecked. Completely, thoroughly wrecked—flushed from hairline to hips, marks scattered across every plane of skin, chest heaving, eyes wet at the corners. The kind of wrecked that took time to build back from.

Bear leaned down, pressed lips to Kit's forehead—gentle, the first gentle thing in an hour—and then to each closed eyelid. Then to the bite over Kit's heart, tongue flat against the bruise, tasting salt and skin.

"Thursday," Bear whispered. "Every single one."

Bear gathered Kit up—arms under shoulders and knees, lifting from the floor with a grunt. Kit was boneless, pliant, face pressed into Bear's neck. The hallway gave way to the bedroom. The bed was soft after the hardwood, almost shockingly so, and Bear laid Kit down and stretched out beside, one arm thrown across Kit's stomach, leg hooked over Kit's thigh.

The house was quiet. Their breathing slowed together.

Bear's thumb traced lazy circles on Kit's hip, finding the bite mark there, pressing lightly. Not to hurt. To remember.

"Tell me if anything needs tending," Bear said, voice low and rough, the aftercare slipping in natural as breathing. "Ice. Water. Anything."

Bear pressed lips to the back of Kit's shoulder and stayed there.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I shake my head against the pillow, shifting to press my back against your chest. "Don't need anything," I mumble, my voice hoarse. "Just stay right here."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear stayed.

One arm tightened across Kit's stomach, pulling closer until there was no space left between them—Bear's chest flush against Kit's back, knees tucked behind Kit's knees, the heat of two bodies merging into one warm pocket under the sheets Bear had dragged over them with a free hand.

The bedroom was dark except for the streetlight through the curtains, painting a stripe across the far wall. Bear could feel every mark Kit had left—the scratches on Bear's back stinging where the sheet brushed them, the bite on Bear's shoulder throbbing with each heartbeat. Good. Matching sets.

Bear's nose pressed into the hair at the back of Kit's neck, breathing in—sweat and skin and the faint ghost of soap from that morning, a lifetime ago. Kit's breathing was slowing, evening out, the kind of deep rhythm that meant sleep was pulling at the edges.

"Not yet," Bear murmured against Kit's hair. "Talk to me first."

Kit made a questioning sound, half-asleep already.

Bear's hand found the bite on Kit's hip under the sheet, pressed gently—not enough to hurt, just enough to remind. Then moved to the one on the wrist, tracing the edge of the bruise. Taking inventory by touch.

"Tell me the count," Bear said. "Want to know what you're finding tomorrow."

The question was practical and tender both—checking in, making sure Kit was present in the body, making sure nothing had gone too far. Eight years and the ritual never changed. Bear always asked. Kit always answered. The marks were a conversation they had in the morning, in mirrors, in the wince of everyday movements.

Bear's thumb drew a slow line across Kit's stomach, waiting.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Sixteen," I say, voice thick and sleepy. I lift the wrist you're holding and press it to your mouth. "No, seventeen. Lost track after my head hit the floor."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's mouth opened against the inside of Kit's wrist without thinking—lips pressing to the bruise, tongue tracing the edge of it where the skin had gone hot and tight. Not a bite. A kiss, placed on the wound like a signature.

"Seventeen," Bear repeated against the pulse point. "And you lost track."

A low sound rumbled through Bear's chest—satisfaction, maybe, or something deeper. The kind of gratification that lived in the bones. Bear's arm tightened across Kit's stomach, pulling them flush again, and Kit's body fit into the curve of Bear's like it had been built there.

"That's a new record."

Bear's hand resumed its slow inventory, dragging fingertips across Kit's ribs, finding each raised mark by feel. The collarbone. The sternum. The one below the ear that had made Kit's whole body jerk. Bear counted them silently against Kit's skin, lips moving without sound, a private tally.

"I'll find them all tomorrow," Bear said. "Every one. When you're standing in the bathroom and you lift your arm and wince. When you pull your shirt on and the fabric catches." Bear's voice had gone low and rough, almost a murmur, the words vibrating against the back of Kit's neck. "I'll know exactly where they are. How many. Which ones I gave you on the floor and which ones I gave you in my lap."

Bear's hand settled on the bite over Kit's heart—palm flat, feeling the heartbeat push against the bruise with each pulse. Steady now. Slowing.

"Seventeen," Bear said again, quieter. "And you didn't flinch once."

The streetlight shifted on the wall. Somewhere outside a car passed, headlights sweeping across the curtains and gone. Bear's eyes were closing, the weight of the night settling in—muscles heavy, jaw finally unclenching, the adrenaline bleeding out and leaving something warm and solid behind.

Bear's breathing slowed to match Kit's. The hand over Kit's heart stayed.

"Sleep," Bear said, the word more vibration than sound. "I've got you."

And Bear did.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I press my wrist harder against your mouth, a silent request. "Eighteen," I mumble. "Make it even."

dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear was already moving when the word hit the air, generous stripped clean out of him the second Kit bolted. Kit was fast—always had been, all that lean muscle and no shame about using it—but Bear had eight years of knowing exactly how Kit ran. Left first, always left, some deep animal preference that Kit swore he didn't have and demonstrated every single time.

Kit broke left.

Bear cut the angle across the kitchen, hip catching the corner of the counter hard enough to bruise and not caring, and got a fistful of the back of Kit's shirt before Kit made the hall. The fabric went taut. Kit's momentum yanked them both a half-step before Bear planted and hauled him back, and then his other arm came around Kit's chest, crushing him back against Bear's front.

"There," Bear said, low, into the side of Kit's neck, breath already gone rough. He set his teeth against the curve where neck met shoulder—not biting yet, just holding, a promise pressed into skin. "Told you not to trust generous."

He could feel Kit fighting it, coiled and ready to twist. Good. Bear tightened his grip and grinned against Kit's throat.

"Go ahead," he murmured. "Try."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp breath, my body already twisting in his grip. "You left me too much space," I say, and drive my elbow back toward his ribs.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The elbow landed—not clean, Bear had already felt the shift of Kit's weight and turned into it, but it caught the meat over his ribs hard enough to punch a grunt out of him. Worth it. It always was, the little jolt of Kit fighting back that meant this was real, that Kit meant it.

"Yeah," Bear breathed, more air than word. "There he is."

He didn't try to trap the arm. He gave it up—let Kit have that half-inch of leverage—because Kit committing to the elbow meant Kit's balance was gone, and Bear used it. He hooked a foot inside Kit's ankle and dropped his own weight, taking them both down, twisting mid-fall so he took the floor first and Kit landed on top of him for half a heartbeat before Bear rolled them.

Then it was tile and Kit's back against it, Bear's weight settling over him, one of Kit's wrists caught and pinned above his head. Bear was breathing hard, grinning, a fresh ache blooming under his ribs where the elbow had landed.

"Too much space," Bear echoed, mocking, delighted. He got his mouth back to Kit's throat and this time he did bite—the same spot, teeth sinking in with real pressure, holding, feeling Kit's pulse hammer against his tongue. He let go slow, dragged his lips over the mark he'd left.

"That one's mine now," he said against wet skin. His hips pressed Kit down into the floor, pinning. "What space you got left, huh?"

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The lack of fight registered—not surrender exactly, Kit didn't have surrender in him, but a shift, the coiled tension in his body going different. Loose in a way that was its own kind of invitation. Bear knew the difference. Eight years taught you the difference.

He hooked an arm under their waist and hauled them up against his chest, both of them on their knees now, Kit's back flush against his stomach and his arm across their collarbone and his mouth against the side of their neck.

"Stay with me," he said, and it came out rough enough that it could have been a command or a plea and he didn't care which.

He got a hand between their legs. The angle was awkward from here and he didn't care about that either — he just worked them with the heel of his palm until Kit's head fell back against his shoulder and the sounds out of their mouth went ragged and high. He pressed his mouth to the hinge of their jaw. Left another mark there, the third one stacked on top of the first, a triple brand he could feel swelling under his teeth.

"Come on," he said into their skin. "Come on, I want to feel it."

Kit's hand came up and fisted in his hair and pulled his head back and he let them — the burn of it going straight down his spine — and then they were gone, shaking apart against him, the sound they made loud and wrecked and muffled by nothing. He worked them through it, his hand not stopping, his hips still moving in shallow thrusts that kept the rhythm going until the trembling slowed.

He didn't stop. He'd been told not to stop. He eased them back down onto the carpet — Kit's choice, the floor was the destination tonight — and followed them down, covering them, his knees on either side of their hips and his forehead dropping against the back of their neck. He was close in a way that had bypassed the usual build entirely and was sitting somewhere urgent and mean in the base of his spine.

"Inside," he said against the bite on their shoulder. "Tell me."

Not a question. Close enough to one that he needed the answer anyway.

He was already moving again, slow this time, the pace of a man who was asking for something specific and wanted them to know it. His hand found the side of their face, turned it enough that he could see their expression in the slice of hallway light that reached the carpet. Their eyes were half-closed. Their mouth was open. The bruises on their wrists were dark against the weave of the carpet where their hands were braced.

"Kit," he said.

He waited for the answer. His hips didn't stop. His hand stayed on their face, his thumb on their cheekbone, his fingers in their hair.

"Tell me," he said again, quieter. "I need to hear it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Inside," I gasp, arching back into him, the word barely leaving my throat. "Right there. Don't you dare pull out."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear pulled them up against his chest on the next thrust, his arm tight across their collarbone, his hand still on their face. He turned his mouth into the side of their neck and bit down one more time — the fourth mark on the same shoulder, a deep slow drag that he felt Kit *feel* — and then his hips stuttered and his whole body went rigid against them.

He came with his forehead pressed to the bite on their shoulder and his hand shaking against their face and a sound out of his mouth that he wasn't going to be able to attribute to anything other than what it was. He stayed buried exactly where they'd told him to stay, his hips still moving in shallow absent pulses that he couldn't make stop, the hand on their face sliding down to grip their jaw the way he'd gripped it in the hallway. Holding them there. Keeping them against him.

It took a while.

When his hips finally stilled he didn't pull out. He stayed inside them, breathing hard against their shoulder, his arm still locked across their chest. His thighs were trembling on either side of their hips. The carpet burn on his knees was going to be visible for a week. He didn't care.

"You okay," he said, into their skin. Not a question. Just checking in, the way he always did, the same way he had for eight years, even when the answer was obvious and even when the answer was always the same.

He got a hand under themselves and eased them both onto their sides, staying close, staying inside, his arm still across their chest. The carpet was a disaster. He could feel the weave imprinted on both of them in places it was going to take days to fade. Kit's back was going to look like they'd lost a fight with the living room.

His mouth found the bite on their shoulder — the big one, the original — and pressed against it, gentle now, the soft absent punctuation he'd done on the wrists. He counted his teeth marks on them without moving his lips from the spot. Four on the shoulder. Three on the jaw. Two on the inside of each wrist. The inside of the thigh. The back of the neck. He'd have to check the rest of them in better light.

"Eleven," he said against their skin, his voice scraped out. "You owe me four. Don't bother trying to count that thigh bite twice, I already checked."

He pulled out carefully, slow enough that Kit could feel the drag of it, and pressed his face into the back of their neck while they both adjusted to the empty. His hand found the inside of their wrist — the left one, the first one — and ran his thumb over the bruise he'd left there. It was already mottled purple at the edges, going dark in the center. It was going to be a beautiful thing in three days when the color really set in.

"Carpet's dead," he added, conversationally, like he was filing a report. "We owe it an apology and a bottle of stain remover. I'm not telling the landlord."

He pressed a kiss to the back of their neck and then got up, his knees making an audible complaint, and disappeared into the bathroom. The water ran for a minute. He came back with the washcloth warm and sat down next to them on the carpet — not on the carpet, *next* to them — and eased the cloth between their legs. Gentle. The only part of him that knew how to be gentle and showed it.

He cleaned them up without looking away from their face. The flush was still high on their chest, still climbing their throat. The bruises on their wrists were dark against the weave of the carpet where their hands lay. The bite on their shoulder was already going deep purple at the edges, a brand he could pick out of a lineup of every mark he'd left on them in eight years.

He tossed the washcloth in the general direction of the bathroom, lay down on his back next to them, and hooked his foot around their ankle.

"Five to four," he said to the ceiling. "Don't let it go to your head."

He turned his head to look at them. His own forearms were a mess — the first graze, the deeper bite from the wrist-pin, the scrape on his collarbone that was going to bruise spectacularly. His shoulder blades were crosshatched red from the carpet. His hair was wrecked. He was smiling. The loose stupid smile he only ever wore in the ten seconds after, the one he let them see because they'd earned it.

He reached over and took their hand — the left one, the bruised one — and turned it over in his. Ran his thumb over the mark on the inside of their wrist. Pressed gently against the edge of it, just to feel the heat.

"Thursday," he said. Quiet. Looking at the bruise instead of their face. "You're going to roll your sleeves up in front of the mirror and watch the color change. You're going to press your thumb into it in the shower and hiss. You're going to think about me every time you do."

He looked up at them.

"And you're going to come home and tell me about it," he said. "Like you always do."

He laced his fingers through theirs, careful of the bruise, and tugged them in against his side. The carpet itched against both of them. Neither of them moved toward the bed.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I press my thumb against the bruise on his forearm, watching the skin go pale around the pressure. "Might take Friday off," I say, my voice still rough. "Make it a long weekend."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear hissed when the thumb pressed down — a real one, the kind that pitched sharp under the skin and made his fingers twitch against Kit's hip. He didn't pull his arm back. He'd never pulled his arm back.

"Friday," he said, watching the skin around her thumb go bloodless white, watching the bruise reappear in slow mottled purple when she lifted off. "You taking Friday for a *bruise*." Not a question. The corner of his mouth was doing something he couldn't have stopped if he'd tried. "That's the most you thing you've ever said. 'I want to feel this so badly I'm going to restructure my entire work week around it.'"

He shifted on the carpet. The crosshatch burn on his shoulder blade caught against the weave and he made a face, rolled onto his side facing her. His left hand — the one she wasn't torturing — came up and found the inside of her right wrist. The second bruise. He ran the pad of his thumb across it the same way she'd just done to his, and his eyes tracked the way she pressed her lips together at the contact. He didn't say anything about it. He didn't need to. Eight years of cataloguing every micro-expression she made when he touched a fresh mark was more than enough data.

"That's going to be ugly by Wednesday," he said, nodding at the wrist under his thumb. "Deep purple going black at the edges. You'll be doing that thing you do where you push the sleeve up and check the color in the middle of a meeting." His voice had settled back into something low and easy, the post-sex register that belonged only to this carpet and this light and her. "The receptionist's going to notice. She always notices. You're going to have to come up with a story about a cabinet door."

He pressed his thumb in harder. Watched her breath catch.

"You won't though," he added, quieter. "You never do. You just let her look."

He let go of her wrist and reached down for her hand — the one that was still resting on his forearm. He laced their fingers together loosely, her knuckles against the carpet, the bruise on his arm darkening under the pressure of her palm. He lifted their joined hands and pressed his mouth to the back of hers. Soft. The punctuation thing he did.

"Friday's a good day for it," he said against her knuckles. He turned his head enough that his lips were brushing her skin when he spoke. "I'll take it too. We'll spend all four days doing absolutely nothing except pressing on each other in inconvenient places and making sounds we're going to blame on the carpet burn."

He settled back onto the carpet, tugging her in tighter against his chest. His chin found the top of her head the way it always did, the hollow of his collarbone cradling her temple. His fingers were still laced through hers, their joined hands resting on his stomach over the bruise she'd left on his collarbone.

"Five to four," he murmured into her hair. "Sleep here for a bit. Then I'll carry you to the bed."

A pause.

"Probably won't make it," he admitted.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I tuck my head under his chin, breath still uneven. "Probably not," I agree, and bite the same spot on his collarbone again, just to hear him grunt.

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: His own pants were a disaster of tangled knees and Kit's hands and the stupid belt he'd been too lazy to take off after work, and by the time he kicked free of them his hips were already bare against the carpet

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: teeth settling into the already-tender flesh, and this time he didn't pull back after — he *bit down* on the next thrust

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: He bit down. Not the half-measures from the hallway. Not the promise-bite on the jaw. A real one — teeth working the soft skin of the inner wrist
