dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let three heartbeats pass before following, just enough to make it a real run and not a catch. Kit knew the house, knew its corners and the way the hallway narrowed near the bathroom, and Bear let that advantage stand. Generous was one thing. Stupid was another.

The kitchen doorway flashed past, then the living room, and Bear caught the sound of Kit's bare feet on hardwood, the quickening rhythm of someone who knew what was coming and couldn't quite decide if they wanted to be caught.

They both knew.

Bear took the hallway at speed, shoulder brushing the doorframe, and found Kit at the bedroom door, hand on the frame, breathing hard. Not from exertion. Not yet.

"Close," Bear said, slowing to a walk.

Kit's eyes were bright. "You let me make it."

"I did." Bear closed the distance in two steps. "I'm done being generous."

The doorframe was solid oak. Kit's back hit it hard enough to feel it, Bear's hand planted beside their head, the other catching Kit's jaw, tilting it up. The game had rules. They'd written them together, years ago, and they both remembered.

"Well?" Kit managed.

Bear bit down on the junction of Kit's neck and shoulder, hard enough to bruise, hard enough to earn a sound that would keep for days. One hand, two now, pinning Kit's wrists above their head against the doorframe. Not gentle. Not pretending to be.

"Close enough," Bear said, and went back for more.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp gasp, then a low laugh. "You're still being generous. I'm not pinned yet." I twist, testing the grip on my wrists.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear tightened the grip on Kit's wrists, shifting weight forward until there was no give left, no room to move. The play in Kit's eyes had sharpened into something more alert, more present.

"Not pinned?" Bear leaned in, close enough that the words ghosted across Kit's throat. "This isn't your mattress, sweetheart. You wanted the doorframe, you got the doorframe."

One hand still holding both wrists. The other sliding down, finding the curve of Kit's hip, anchoring there with enough pressure to feel the muscle beneath jump. Bear had put on muscle this year, and Kit had noticed. Kit noticed everything.

"Still feeling generous?" Bear asked, and finally — finally — bore down.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the moment Kit stopped pulling away, the deliberate softening of resistance that meant more than any words. Eight years and Kit still did that — still made Bear earn the catching and then handed it over like a gift.

"That's better," Bear murmured, and finally released Kit's wrists.

The freedom was its own kind of restraint. Kit knew better than to run now — knew that Bear's patience had thinned to something sharper than a chase. The hallway was narrow enough that there was nowhere to go that wasn't closer to the bedroom, closer to the bed, closer to whatever came next.

Bear cupped Kit's face with one hand, thumb tracing the line of Kit's jaw, the corner of their mouth. Kit's eyes were dark, breathing unsteady. The hallway light caught the sweat at Kit's temples, the flush spreading down their chest.

"Last chance," Bear said, because they always said it. Because Kit deserved to hear it. "Tell me to stop."

Kit didn't.

Bear closed the distance between them and the bedroom door in two steps, pulling Kit along by the hip, by the wrist, by whatever grip caught first. The game had rules. They'd written them together, and they both remembered.

They both always remembered.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let him pull me into the room, stumbling once before my back hits the bed. "You're still overdressed," I point out, reaching for the hem of his shirt.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let Kit's fingers find the hem and tug, lifting both arms when directed, letting the shirt disappear somewhere behind them. The muscle was new enough that Kit's eyes tracked it deliberately, and Bear didn't mind being looked at. Eight years and Kit looking still felt like something.

"Complaining about my clothes now?" Bear asked, and pushed Kit back against the mattress, following down. "Thought you wanted to be caught."

Kit's hands were already wandering, map-reading territory that hadn't changed in years but somehow still warranted attention. Bear caught those hands, pressed them flat against the headboard, leaned in close enough that their breath mingled in the small space between them.

"Remember the safe word?" Bear asked, though they both knew Kit hadn't forgotten. It was asked anyway. It was always asked.

Kit's answer came in the form of a laugh and a kiss that said everything words would have ruined.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went down with Kit, knees finding the hardwood, the impact swallowed in the graceless tangle of limbs and half-removed clothing. The floor was cold. Kit was not. Bear filed both facts away and moved on.

"Badly and fast," Bear repeated against Kit's mouth, breath ragged. "That's your plan."

Kit's laugh vibrated where their chests pressed together, hands finally getting buttons to cooperate, or close enough. Bear let it happen, let Kit's fingers work, let the urgency build in the space between intention and action. Eight years and there was still this — the scramble, the imperfect landing, the way Kit's hair fanned across the floor in a dark halo that Bear wanted to run fingers through.

Bear did.

"Still being generous," Kit managed, and Bear bit down on the soft skin below Kit's ear in answer. Not generous. Not anymore. Bear's hands found Kit's hips, lifted, pulled close, and whatever argument Kit had been building dissolved into a sound that Bear would remember for days.

The hardwood was going to leave marks. Neither of them cared.

Bear moved, and Kit moved with, and the game continued in the language they'd built together — bites and breaths and the cheerful arithmetic of two people who kept score and never wanted to stop.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I bite my own lip to keep the noise down when he presses into me, my fingers scrambling for purchase on the floorboards. "Still not gentle," I gasp out, half a question, half a demand.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
"Gentle?" Bear's laugh came out low, wrecked. "Sweetheart, you ran."

Bear's hands found Kit's knees, guided them wider, and pressed deeper in the same motion. The floorboards groaned beneath them. Kit's head tipped back, throat exposed, and Bear followed the invitation without hesitation. Teeth found skin, followed the line down, paused where pulse hammered visible beneath the surface.

"Tell me to be gentle and I'll consider it," Bear said, meaning it the way they always meant it — Kit could ask for anything, and Bear would give it if the rules allowed. But Kit wouldn't ask. Kit never asked.

Kit's answer came as nails raking down Bear's back, a arch off the floor that changed the angle, that made Bear's thoughts scatter like startled birds. The scratches burned. Bear filed them away with the bruises blooming on Kit's neck, the marks that would show for days, the ones Kit would trace in the mirror and remember.

"Gentle is for people who didn't run," Bear said, and meant it as praise.

The hardwood was cold against Kit's shoulder blades. Bear's hand found the curve of Kit's spine, lifted, pulled Kit closer with every thrust. The rhythm wasn't kind. Bear had never promised kind. But it was theirs — this language they'd written in skin and scratches and the breathless sounds Kit made when Bear found the right spot, the one that turned words into fragments.

"Still keeping score?" Bear asked, because they always asked. Because Kit's answer mattered more than the game.

Kit's fingers found Bear's hair, pulled, and that was answer enough.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear gave Kit what was asked for, teeth finding new purchase, breaking skin in the same place Kit had demanded. The copper-bright scent of it mixed with sweat and the warm smell of exertion, and Bear's vision narrowed to the feel of Kit beneath them, around them, the desperate clutch of Kit's legs and the way Kit's voice broke on something that might have been a name or might have been nothing at all.

The floor was going to hurt later. Bear filed that away too, along with the scratches on their back, the bruises forming on their ribs where Kit had gripped too hard, too lost in the moment to be careful. Eight years and Kit still didn't know their own strength. Bear loved that. Bear loved all of it.

Kit was close. Bear could feel it in the way Kit's body tensed, in the broken rhythm, in the sounds that Kit usually swallowed but couldn't quite manage now. Bear lifted up on one elbow, just enough to see Kit's face, and watched the way pleasure and something sharper than pleasure moved through those features.

"Look at me," Bear said, and meant it as a command and a gift both.

Kit's eyes opened, unfocused, finding Bear's face, holding there. Bear thrust harder, deeper, without mercy, without the pretense of restraint. Kit's back arched off the floor. The safe word didn't come. Bear watched Kit come apart, watched the sounds finally win, watched the way Kit's whole body shook with it, and kept moving through all of it.

"Again," Bear said, because Kit could take it. Because Kit wanted it. "Give me another one."

And Kit, god help them, tried.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I try, my body still shuddering from the first wave, and my hand finds his jaw to pull him into a messy, breathless kiss. "Yours," I gasp against his mouth, the only word I can manage.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear heard the word, felt it more than heard it, pressed into the soft skin of Kit's mouth, swallowed whole. Eight years and that word still meant something. That word always meant something.

"Mine," Bear confirmed, the word a brand, a promise, a claim that went both ways. Bear's hand found the back of Kit's neck, held there, kept Kit close through the aftershocks still rippling through that too-tight body. "Mine."

Kit made a sound that might have been agreement or might have been protest at Bear's stubborn refusal to follow them over the edge. Bear's hips stuttered, the rhythm finally faltering, and Kit's legs tightened, hooked over Bear's thighs, pulled closer like Kit wanted to take everything and then ask for more.

Bear gave. Bear always gave Kit what they asked for.

The second time Kit came, it was quieter, a shaking thing that emptied Kit out and left them gasping against the hardwood floor. Bear felt it happen, felt the way Kit's body clamped down, felt the way Kit's nails left crescents in Bear's shoulders, felt the wordless sob that meant more than any safe word ever could.

Bear followed. Bear always followed. The pleasure crested and broke, and Bear pressed deep, held there, felt the way Kit's heartbeat raced against the inside of their pressed-together bodies.

The hallway was cold. The floor was hard. Bear didn't move.

"Yours," Bear said finally, the word rumbling out of a chest still heaving, pressed into the curve of Kit's neck where the first bite was already purpling. "That what you wanted to hear?"

Kit didn't answer. Kit's fingers found the marks on Bear's back, traced the scratches, counted them. Both of them kept score. Both of them always had been.

Bear pulled out slowly, carefully — the only gentleness left in a night that had been all teeth and pressure and the cheerful violence of two people who loved each other without being gentle about it. Kit hissed at the loss. Bear caught the sound and kept it.

"Bed?" Bear asked, though the floor had its merits. The floor had witnessed something. The floor would remember.

Kit's answer was to pull Bear down on top of them again, into the cold of the hallway, into the warmth of being exactly where they belonged.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear looked at the offered wrists, the blue veins visible beneath pale skin, the fine trembling that Kit couldn't quite hide. Thursday. Four days. Bear could do that.

"Both?" Bear asked, because the question mattered. Because Kit was asking for something that would mark deeper than the bites on the shoulder, something that couldn't be covered with a collar or a shirt.

Kit nodded. Bear took the left wrist first.

The teeth found the delicate skin of the inner wrist, the place where pulse lived just beneath the surface. Bear bit down slowly, deliberately, felt the skin give, felt the perfect balance between pressure and harm. Kit made a small sound. Bear gave it another moment, another heartbeat of holding there, before releasing.

The mark was already purpling. It would be dark by morning.

"Other one," Bear said, not a question.

Kit offered it. Bear repeated the process with the same careful attention, the same deliberate bruising. This wrist got a little harder, a little longer — Kit had asked for hurt, and Bear didn't disappoint. When Bear pulled back, the mark was deeper than the first. Kit would find it in the mirror. Kit would feel it when they dressed, when they typed, when they did anything at all.

"Thursday," Bear confirmed, and pressed a kiss to each mark in turn. An afterthought. A benediction. "I'll check."

Kit's eyes were wet at the corners, the good kind of wet, the kind that meant something had been given and received. Bear settled back down, pulled Kit close, let the cold of the hallway floor matter now that the heat had faded. Kit's wrists would ache. Bear's jaw would ache. Both of them would carry the shape of this night for days.

"Generous," Kit murmured against Bear's chest.

"Never," Bear said, and meant it as a promise.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I trace my fingers over the new marks on his back, feeling the raised skin. "You're gonna have to sleep on your stomach tonight."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the touch on those scratches, the careful tracing that meant Kit was cataloging, counting, noting the damage they'd done. The skin was already hot, already tight, and pressing into it sent a bright spark of pain that Bear filed away with everything else from the night.

"Good," Bear said, and there was gravel in the voice, something worn down to the core. "Stomach's fine. You can be the big spoon."

Kit's laugh vibrated through them both, a tired sound, a satisfied one. The hallway floor had gone cold enough that Bear could feel the difference between the parts of Kit pressed against them and the parts pressed against hardwood. Soon they would move. Soon the bed would matter.

But not yet.

"You're going to feel those tomorrow," Bear added, shifting just enough to see Kit's face. The marks on Kit's neck were already darkening, the twin bruises on the wrists visible even in the dim light. Thursday. Bear would check on Thursday. Bear would always check. "Every time you type. Every time you reach for anything."

Kit's smile was slow, dopey with exhaustion, and perfect. "That's the point."

Bear settled back down, let Kit's fingers keep their gentle inventory of damage, and let the night hold them both. Four days. The marks would last four days. The memory would last longer.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear heard it. Bear felt it in the way Kit's body curled closer, seeking warmth where the floor had leached it away, seeking contact where words had run out.

"Don't stop," Kit had said. Bear understood.

Not the chase. Not the biting. Not the scorekeeping that had dissolved somewhere between the hallway and the bedroom door they never reached. Just this — just the staying, just the holding on, just the weight of Bear's body pressed against Kit's on a floor that had gone cold and would ache in the morning.

"Wasn't planning to," Bear said, and shifted to pull Kit fully on top, away from the hardwood, into the warmth of skin against skin. Kit went willingly, limbs heavy with exhaustion, head finding the hollow of Bear's shoulder like it always did, like it had done a thousand times before.

The scratches on Bear's back burned. The bruises on Kit's wrists would throb when the adrenaline faded. None of it was gentle. None of it needed to be.

Bear's hand found the back of Kit's neck, thumb tracing the edge of the bite mark there, the one that would show above every collar Kit owned. Thursday. They'd talked about Thursday. Bear would check. Bear would always check.

"You're heavy," Bear said, though the words had no teeth.

Kit's laugh was muffled against Bear's chest. "You're the one who wouldn't move."

"Wouldn't let you freeze, either."

Kit's fingers found the scratches again, pressed lightly, and Bear's breath caught on something that wasn't quite pain anymore. Kit knew where they were. Kit knew what they'd left. Eight years of reading each other's skin like a language they couldn't stop speaking.

The hallway would need warming. The bed was right there, ten steps away, and neither of them moved.

"This is keeping score," Bear said quietly. "You know that."

Kit hummed, a noncommittal sound, and pressed closer.

"Yeah," Kit admitted. "I know."

They stayed on the floor until the cold won, until Bear's knees protested, until the scratches started to sting in a way that demanded attention. Kit let Bear pull them up, let Bear lead them the few steps to the bed, let Bear arrange them exactly where Bear wanted them — on their stomach, wrists tucked under a pillow, the bruises visible and untouched.

"Gonna check them in the morning," Bear said, settling onto stomach as promised, face turned toward Kit. "And every morning until Thursday."

Kit's smile was soft, dopey with satisfaction. "Generous."

Bear reached across the space between them, found Kit's hand, laced their fingers together over the pillow. The mark on Kit's inner wrist pressed against Bear's palm. Four days. Four days of Kit feeling it, of Kit remembering.

"Never," Bear said, and meant it all the way down to the bone.

The room was dark. The marks were set. Bear watched Kit's eyes drift closed and didn't look away, not yet, not when there was still this — still the proof of something that didn't need to be gentle to be true.

Kit's breathing evened out. Bear stayed awake a little longer, just to watch, just to have it.

Some things didn't stop. Some things were never supposed to.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I press my bruised wrist against his lips in the dark. "Still hurts."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's lips found the mark without needing to see it, pressing a kiss to the swollen skin. It was warm, tender, the kind of attention that cost nothing after everything else the night had demanded.

"Good," Bear murmured against the pulse point. "Hurt means it worked."

Kit's fingers twitched in the dark, the ones still laced with Bear's. Bear knew that twitch. Knew what it meant — Kit wanted more, wanted to be touched again, wanted the ache to sharpen into something that couldn't be ignored. Bear understood. Bear felt it too, the dull throb in the jaw, the scratches tightening on the back, the way exhaustion and satisfaction warred for dominance.

"Go to sleep," Bear said, and kissed the mark again. "Thursday's not here yet."

Kit made a small sound of protest, but their eyes were already closing, already losing the battle against the weight of the night. Bear watched the struggle happen, watched Kit's breathing slow, watched the way their fingers loosened but didn't let go.

The room smelled like them. The floor outside the door would remember. Bear's back would remind them both every time they lay down for the next few days.

Bear closed their eyes, let the pain settle in, let the marks become part of the landscape of a body that Kit had mapped a thousand times and still traced like it mattered.

"Still here," Bear said, to the dark, to Kit, to no one.

The answer was Kit's hand tightening once before going slack with sleep. Bear held on.

Some things didn't stop.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I squeeze his hand back, a last bit of pressure before sleep fully takes me. The ache in my wrist is a steady, grounding thrum. "Still here," I mumble into the pillow.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the squeeze, held it, let it anchor there in the dark. Kit's voice had been slurred with sleep, the words barely words at all, but Bear heard them anyway. Heard everything Kit didn't say and everything Kit meant.

The house was quiet now. No more footsteps, no more chase, no more sounds that belonged to the game. Just the two of them breathing in the dark, the steady rhythm of it syncing up the way it always did after. Bear's chest rose and fell under the weight of Kit's presence, close enough to feel even when not quite touching.

Bear didn't sleep yet. Bear rarely did first.

Instead, Bear watched the shape of Kit in the dark, the way exhaustion had softened all the sharp edges, the way Kit's lips were still slightly parted, still bruised from Bear's mouth. The marks on Kit's neck caught what little light came through the curtains, darker than Bear had expected, darker than Thursday would be.

Thursday would come. Bear would check. Bear would always check.

The wrist still pressed against Bear's palm, warm with blood pooling beneath skin, the gift that Kit had asked for and Bear had given. Four days. Three now, with morning coming. Three days of Kit feeling it, of Kit remembering.

Bear let the thought settle, let it become part of the night's inventory — the scratches on the back, the bruises on the ribs, the ache in the jaw, the weight of Kit's hand still loosely tangled in Bear's own. All of it evidence. All of it theirs.

Kit shifted in sleep, nose brushing Bear's collarbone, a small sound escaping that might have been Bear's name or might have been nothing at all. Bear tightened the hand that held Kit's, just slightly, just enough. Kit didn't stir but the fingers tightened back.

Still here.

Bear closed eyes that had been open too long, let the darkness take over, let the pain become part of the background hum of a body that had earned every bruise. Thursday would hurt. Tomorrow would hurt. Tonight already had.

Worth it. Always worth it.

Bear slept eventually, the way Bear always did — one hand still holding Kit's, the other resting on the back of Kit's neck, keeping them close even in dreams.

The marks would still be there in the morning.

Some things didn't stop.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I wake before he does, the first real light catching the edge of the bite on my shoulder. I press my thumb into it just to feel the sting, then roll carefully to look at him. He's still on his stomach, the scratches on his back angry and red. I lean over and breathe a soft laugh against his skin. "Morning, bear."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Bear closed the distance between them and the bedroom door in two steps, pulling Kit along by the hip, by the wrist

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Bear's hands found Kit's hips, lifted, pulled close

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: teeth finding new purchase, breaking skin in the same place Kit had demanded

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: The teeth found the delicate skin of the inner wrist, the place where pulse lived just beneath the surface. Bear bit down slowly, deliberately, felt the skin give, felt the perfect balance between pressure and harm.

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: The room was dark. The marks were set. Bear watched Kit's eyes drift closed

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear was moving before Kit's foot hit the hall runner — that half-second head start had been a gift and now it was rescinded. The kitchen was small, the hallway narrow, and Kit was fast but Bear was faster over short distances and knew every squeaky board between here and the bedroom.

Kit made it to the bathroom doorway. Almost made it past. Bear caught a fistful of the back of Kit's shirt and used the momentum against them, spinning them into the wall with a solid thump that knocked a framed photo crooked.

"That's what you get for telling me not to be generous," Bear said, pinning a forearm across Kit's collarbones, close enough to feel Kit's breath hot and quick against their jaw. The other hand had already found Kit's wrist and pressed it to the plaster above their head.

Bear grinned, showing teeth. Kit's pulse was ticking visible under the thin skin of their throat, and Bear leaned in without hurry and set their mouth to it — not biting yet, just letting Kit feel the shape of the threat, letting them squirm against the wall and figure out how much of that squirming was trying to get away and how much was the opposite.

"Where were you going?" Bear murmured against Kit's neck. "You had a plan, right? You had a whole strategy back there."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Bathroom," I gasp, arching against the wall. "You're in my way." I twist my wrist in your grip, not to break it—just to feel the hold tighten.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's grip tightened obligingly around Kit's wrist, thumb pressing into the tender inside where the pulse was going. The twist earned Kit a low sound in Bear's throat — approval, or warning, hard to tell which and probably both.

"Bathroom," Bear repeated, like they were considering it. "That's your story."

They shifted their weight, using the forearm across Kit's collarbones to hold them flat while their thigh worked between Kit's knees and pushed them apart a few useful inches. Not enough to be helpful. Just enough to make Kit's stance worse, to make the wall the only thing keeping them upright.

"I'll let you go to the bathroom," Bear said, and set their teeth against Kit's throat — properly this time, a slow closing pressure just shy of what would leave a mark tomorrow, held long enough that Kit could count the seconds if they wanted to. Then released. Then licked the same spot, unhurried, considering. "In a minute. After I decide if you actually needed to go or if you were just seeing how far you could get."

Bear pulled back enough to look at Kit's face — flushed high on the cheekbones, mouth open, eyes doing that thing they did. Bear's grin widened.

"Yeah," Bear said. "That's what I thought."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear read the not-fighting for exactly what it was, and rewarded it by not making it easier. The hand on Kit's wrist stayed where it was. The thigh between Kit's knees stayed where it was. The forearm across Kit's collarbones eased off a fraction — not out of mercy, just to see what Kit did with the extra half-inch.

Kit didn't do much with it. That was answer enough.

"Look at you," Bear said, quiet, almost fond. "You didn't even try."

They dragged their nose along the line of Kit's jaw, slow, taking their time now that the chase part was over and the rest of the evening was theirs. Kit smelled like soap and heat and the particular sharpness they got when their pulse was up and staying up. Bear filed that away and kept moving — mouth back down to the spot they'd bitten, tongue over it once to check the color, then teeth again a half-inch lower where the shirt collar dipped.

This one they held longer. Long enough to feel Kit's throat work under their mouth when Kit swallowed. Long enough to be a mark for sure, tomorrow, in a spot Kit's t-shirts wouldn't quite cover.

"Bathroom's right there," Bear murmured against Kit's skin, tilting their head toward the doorway two feet away that Kit had almost made it through. "You want to try again? I'll give you another head start. Three seconds this time. Real sporting of me."

Bear's grin was pressed to the corner of Kit's jaw. They weren't loosening their grip.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Three seconds?" I tilt my head back against the wall, exposing more of my throat. "Generous again. Don't think I'll make it that far."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear made a low sound at the tilt — Kit knew exactly what they were doing, offering up throat like that, and Bear was not remotely above taking what was offered. They set their teeth to the new expanse of skin without any of the earlier deliberation, just a quick sharp closing that made Kit's whole body jump against the wall.

"No," Bear agreed against Kit's pulse. "I don't think you will."

The hand on Kit's wrist finally moved — not to release, just to relocate, sliding down Kit's arm and around to catch a fistful of the back of Kit's shirt instead. The forearm came off Kit's collarbones. Bear stepped back exactly half a step, enough to give Kit room to move if Kit wanted to move, and watched Kit's face to see whether Kit would take it.

"Go on then," Bear said. "Three seconds. I'm counting."

They weren't letting go of the shirt.

"One."

Bear's grin was all teeth. The thigh between Kit's knees hadn't moved either.

"Two."

Kit was still against the wall. Bear had known they would be. That was rather the point of the exercise — offering an out that wasn't actually an out, watching Kit choose the wall over the doorway two feet away, cataloging the choice for later reference and immediate use.

"Three," Bear said, and hauled Kit off the wall by the fistful of shirt, and turned them toward the bedroom instead of the bathroom. "Time's up. You had your chance."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The hallway runner was thin over hardwood and neither of them cared. Bear got Kit down with a hand at the back of Kit's neck and one at their hip, controlled but not careful, and Kit's shoulder blades hit the floor with a sound Bear filed away as satisfying.

Kit's shirt came off inside out and got flung somewhere toward the bathroom. Bear's own shirt lost a button that pinged off the baseboard — Kit's doing, and Bear made a mental note to make them pay for it later. Belt buckles were a nuisance. Bear got theirs undone one-handed while the other hand was busy holding Kit's jaw, thumb hooked under the hinge of it, keeping Kit's head tilted the way Bear wanted it.

Kit's jeans were a worse problem. Bear solved it by dragging them down Kit's hips with more force than finesse, taking the underwear with them, leaving the whole tangle bunched around Kit's thighs because getting them off entirely would have required letting go of Kit and Bear was not letting go of Kit.

"This is what you get," Bear said, low, settling their weight down over Kit and pinning one of Kit's wrists to the floor beside their head. Their mouth found the second bite mark on Kit's throat and pressed against it — checking, claiming, whatever. "For the kitchen thing. For the wall thing. For that look you gave me over coffee this morning, don't think I forgot."

Bear's free hand slid down Kit's ribs, fingertips dragging, feeling Kit breathe under them in short shallow pulls. Kit's hip bone under Bear's palm. Kit's thigh where the jeans had it trapped. Bear pressed their forehead against the side of Kit's and just breathed for a second, staying there, letting the wanting sit heavy between them before doing anything about it.

"Tell me you're good," Bear said against Kit's temple. Quiet. The one moment of actual checking, brief and non-negotiable, because eight years was eight years and some things you did every time.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, turning my face into yours. "I'm good," I murmur, my free hand fisting in the back of your shirt. "C'mon, Bear."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear made a sound against Kit's temple — not quite a laugh, closer to a growl with the edges worn off — and turned their head just enough to catch Kit's mouth with theirs. The kiss wasn't gentle but it wasn't rushed either, now that the check was done and the answer was the one Bear had known it would be. Just deep, and hot, and taking. Kit's lower lip caught between Bear's teeth on the way out and held there a second longer than strictly necessary.

"C'mon Bear," Bear repeated back, mocking soft, the words shaped against Kit's mouth. "Like you're the one making the schedule here."

The hand on Kit's wrist ground it a little harder into the floorboards — not to hurt, just to remind. The other hand went back to Kit's hip and stayed there, fingers digging in over the bone, thumb pressed to the crease of Kit's thigh where the bunched denim was making everything worse and better at once.

Bear shifted their weight, deliberate, letting Kit feel every pound of it settle. Their own jeans were still half-on and that was going to become urgent in a minute but not this minute. This minute was for holding Kit down on the hallway floor and watching them try to arch up into it and not letting them get very far.

"You want to hurry me up," Bear said, mouth at the corner of Kit's jaw, "you're going about it wrong."

They dropped their head and set their teeth to Kit's collarbone — third mark, and this one Bear didn't bother pretending to be gentle about, a real bite that made Kit's whole body pull taut under them. Bear held it. Held it. Released, slow, and licked the shape of their own teeth off Kit's skin.

"There," Bear said, satisfied. "Now I'll consider it."

Their hand left Kit's hip and went to finish the problem of their own belt, which took longer one-handed than it should have and Bear refused to be hurried about that either. Kit's fist was still in the back of Bear's shirt. Bear could feel it shaking a little, and grinned into Kit's throat, and took their time.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The second bite went in on top of the first, or near enough, Bear's teeth finding the mark they'd just made and sinking in deeper. Kit's whole body jolted under them and the fist in Bear's shirt twisted tight enough Bear heard a seam give somewhere. That was the second garment Kit owed them tonight. Bear was keeping a tally.

Bear held the bite until Kit made the sound Bear had been waiting for — that specific one, low and wrecked, not a word — and then released and dragged their tongue over the shape of it, tasting salt and the faint metal edge of skin gone that far.

"Greedy," Bear said, approving, against the ruined patch of Kit's shoulder. "Look at you asking for it twice."

Bear finally got their belt undone, then the button, then shoved the denim down enough to be functional and not one inch further. The rest could wait. Everything could wait except this — the settling of Bear's hips down against Kit's, skin to skin finally, both of them going still for one shared breath at the shock of it before Bear moved again.

The hand that had been on the belt went back to Kit's jaw, thumb dragging over Kit's lower lip, tugging it down. Kit's mouth was already open. Bear pushed the thumb in without ceremony and Kit's tongue came up to meet it, and Bear felt that all the way down.

"That's the mouth that told me not to be generous," Bear said, low, watching Kit's face. Bear's thumb pressed down on Kit's tongue, held it there. "That's the mouth that told me to hurry up."

Bear leaned down, replaced the thumb with their own mouth, kissed Kit deep and slow and filthy while their free hand slid between them and got a grip on Kit's thigh, hitching it up against Bear's hip. The bunched denim was in the way. Bear made it work.

"I'll hurry up," Bear murmured against Kit's mouth, "when I feel like it."

The hand pinning Kit's wrist hadn't moved once.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: My hips jerk up against yours, a helpless motion. "You feel like it now," I pant against your mouth, teeth clicking.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear laughed against Kit's mouth — actually laughed this time, breathless and dark, because Kit was nothing if not consistent and eight years hadn't taught them a damn thing about when to shut up.

"Do I," Bear said.

The hand on Kit's thigh tightened, fingers digging into muscle, and Bear rolled their hips down against Kit's once — slow, deliberate, giving Kit exactly enough to make it worse. Kit's head tipped back against the floorboards and Bear watched the line of their throat go long and abandoned and the fresh bite mark on the collarbone go dark.

"Say please," Bear said.

The thumb was back at the corner of Kit's mouth, dragging. Bear's own breath wasn't as steady as they'd like it to be and Kit would clock that if Kit were in any state to clock anything, which — Bear glanced at Kit's face and revised — Kit was not, quite. Good. That was where Bear wanted them.

"Come on." Bear ground down again, a fraction harder, watched Kit's eyes lose focus. "One word. You said all the other ones fine."

Bear's mouth went back to the shoulder, to the mark, tongue soothing over it in a way that was not soothing at all given what teeth were about to do next if Kit held out much longer. The wrist Bear was pinning had gone lax under Bear's hand — Kit not even pretending to fight it now, just held there because Bear was holding them there, which was the entire point of the whole evening and had been since the kitchen.

"I've got all night," Bear lied, against Kit's skin.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went still for half a second — the kind of still that meant they were recalibrating, taking in the shape of what Kit had just handed them and figuring out where to start.

Then Bear moved.

Both of Kit's wrists in one of Bear's hands, pressed to the floorboards above Kit's head, held there — not tight, just definitively. Bear's free hand came up to cup the side of Kit's face, thumb dragging across Kit's cheekbone once, almost tender, which was the tell that things were about to get significantly less so.

"Thursday," Bear repeated, considering. "That's four days."

"You want to be careful what you ask for," Bear said, and did not mean it, and Kit knew Bear did not mean it, and that was fine.

Bear started at the throat because that was where Bear had been threatening all evening and threats got paid. A bite at the side, high enough Kit's collar wouldn't hide it, held long. Released. Bear ducked their head and set the next one lower, at the hollow above the collarbone on the other side from the first — matching set, Bear was thinking, symmetry — and bit until Kit's breath caught and stayed caught.

Bear counted three seconds in their head and let go.

The shoulder next, opposite the ruined one, because Kit had said mirror and Bear was going to give them both sides to look at. This one Bear worked at longer, teeth then tongue then teeth again in a slightly different place, laying down a spread of marks that would bloom overnight into something Kit couldn't ignore putting a shirt on.

"Every time you turn your head Thursday," Bear said against the meat of Kit's shoulder, voice gone rough, "you're going to feel this one."

Bear moved down. The soft place under the collarbone where the skin was thinner — a real bite there, precise, the kind that would purple properly. Kit's whole body pulled tight under Bear's weight and Bear pressed them back down with a palm splayed flat between Kit's ribs, holding them to the floor while Bear finished what Bear was doing.

Kit's wrists hadn't moved from where Bear had put them. Bear noticed. Bear rewarded it by biting the inside of Kit's bicep next, close to the pit of the elbow where the skin was thin and private and Kit would feel it every time they reached for anything all week.

"Good," Bear murmured, mouth traveling back up. "Stay right there."

Bear got their teeth into the side of Kit's neck under the jaw — the one from earlier, reopened, the one Kit had offered up against the wall — and this time did not let go quickly. Held it. Held it. Kit was making a sound now that was mostly breath and Bear could feel Kit's pulse hammering against their tongue.

When Bear finally released, Bear pulled back just enough to look. Kit's throat and chest and shoulders were a map. Bear catalogued them with something close to satisfaction and something closer to want, and dropped their forehead against Kit's for a second, breathing.

"Thursday," Bear said quietly, close to Kit's mouth. "Promise."

Then Bear's hand slid down from Kit's ribs, and Bear's hips settled back where they'd been, and Bear stopped talking about it and started making good on the rest.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I arch up, my back leaving the floor. "Now," I gasp, hands fisting in the shirt still bunched at your waist. "Bear, now."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't argue this time. There was a point past which drawing it out stopped being fun for either of them, and Kit arching up off the floor like that with both hands finally moving — finally allowed to move, finally *wanting* to grab instead of just being held — was well past it.

"Yeah," Bear said, rough, and it wasn't quite agreement so much as a sound falling out of them. "Yeah, okay."

Bear let go of Kit's wrists. Kit's hands stayed where Bear had put them for a half-second out of pure habit before remembering they were free, and Bear filed that away too, along with everything else that would matter later when Bear had brain cells for anything but this.

Both of Bear's hands went under Kit — one at the small of the back, hitching Kit up off the floorboards, the other hooked under Kit's thigh, lifting it higher against Bear's hip. The bunched denim was still an obstacle. Bear made it not one, mostly by refusing to acknowledge it.

Then Bear pushed in, and the whole hallway went quiet except for the sound they made together — Kit's breath punching out of them in something that wasn't a word, and Bear's own low sound bitten off against Kit's jaw.

Bear held there. One heartbeat, two, forehead pressed hard to Kit's temple, letting them both feel it. Kit's fingers had gone tight in the shirt at Bear's waist, tight enough Bear could feel individual knuckles.

"There you go," Bear said, barely, mouth against Kit's ear. "There. There you are."

And then Bear moved, and did not stop moving, and did not go easy about it — Kit had asked for *now* and Bear was answering with *this*, deep and steady and building, the hand under Kit's back keeping Kit arched up off the floor so Bear could feel every sound Kit made travel up through their whole body.

The mark on Kit's shoulder was right there under Bear's mouth. Bear set their teeth to it again — not biting, just holding, just keeping Kit's shoulder between their teeth like an anchor, like a place to put the sounds Bear was trying not to make.

"Hold on to me," Bear got out, ragged, against Kit's skin. "Kit. Hold on."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't stop. Bear couldn't have stopped if the house had come down around them, and Kit knew it, and had said it anyway because saying it was part of the point.

"Not stopping," Bear said, or tried to say, the words coming out mostly against the hinge of Kit's jaw and not entirely intact. "Not — Kit, I'm not."

Kit's arms had come up around Bear's shoulders, one hand fisted in the back of Bear's hair, the other flat between Bear's shoulder blades and pulling Bear down harder, closer, no space left between them for anything. Bear went with it. Bear got their forearm braced against the floor above Kit's head for leverage and drove in deeper on the next stroke and Kit's whole body took it in a long shuddering arch that Bear felt in their teeth.

The hallway runner was sliding under them. Bear's knee was going to be bruised tomorrow from the hardwood through it. Bear did not care about either of these things. Bear cared about the sound Kit was making — small and open and none of it performed, just torn out of them by increments — and about the specific angle that was getting that sound out of Kit, and about not losing it.

"That," Bear said, ragged, "yeah, that, stay — stay right there —"

Kit's leg hitched higher around Bear's hip on its own, and Bear got a hand under Kit's thigh and pushed it higher still, and Kit's next breath went out of them like they'd been hit. The hand in Bear's hair pulled. Bear let their head go where Kit was pulling it, mouth back to the wrecked shoulder, and this time Bear did bite — not hard, not compared to the earlier ones, just teeth held in the skin like something to grip while Bear's hips found a rhythm that stopped being deliberate and started being something else.

Kit was saying Bear's name. Not loud. Just under the breath, on every exhale, *Bear, Bear, Bear*, like a metronome, like they didn't know they were doing it.

"I hear you," Bear got out. "I've got you. I've got you, come on —"

Bear's own thighs were shaking. Bear noticed distantly and dismissed it. The hand that had been braced above Kit's head moved, slid down, found Kit's jaw and turned Kit's face toward Bear's — needed Kit's mouth, needed to be kissing them for this part, and Kit came up to meet it with a small desperate sound that went straight through Bear's chest.

The kiss was bad. It was more breath than kiss, more teeth than either, Kit gasping into Bear's mouth on every stroke and Bear swallowing the sound and giving nothing back except more of the same. Bear's rhythm broke and reformed and broke again. Kit's fingers were digging into the back of Bear's neck hard enough to hurt tomorrow and Bear was going to have a matching set of half-moons to go with everything Bear had put on Kit and that was — good. That was exactly right. That was the way this went.

"Close," Kit said against Bear's mouth, or Bear thought Kit said, it might have been a shape more than a word. "Bear — close — "

"Yeah," Bear said. "Yeah, come on, I've got you, come on — "

Bear got a hand between them. Bear had been ignoring the geometry of it for the sake of not stopping, but Kit had said *close* and Bear was not going to make Kit ask for it, not now, not after Kit had held their wrists where Bear could reach them and asked for marks and stopped keeping score. Bear's hand closed around Kit and Kit made a sound Bear was going to remember later, when Bear had the capacity to remember things, and Kit's whole body pulled taut against Bear's from shoulder to hip.

"There," Bear said, mouth at Kit's ear, rhythm holding by sheer will. "There you go. That's it. Come on, Kit, let me have it — "

Kit came apart under Bear with their face pressed into the side of Bear's neck and Bear's name breaking in half in their mouth, and Bear felt every second of it, every clench and shudder and the whole long shaking exhale after. Bear kept moving through it, slower, gentler for exactly as long as Kit needed it that way — and then Kit's hand slid down Bear's back and gripped Bear's hip and pulled, meaning *keep going, don't be careful*, and Bear didn't need telling twice.

Three more strokes and Bear was gone.

Bear buried their face in the crook of Kit's neck — in the ruined shoulder, in the tangle of marks Bear had put there — and made a sound that wasn't a word and wasn't quiet and didn't need to be, and Kit's arms locked around Bear's back and held them through it. Bear's whole body shook once, hard, and then again smaller, and then Bear was just breathing against Kit's throat with their weight settled full down on Kit and neither of them moving to fix it.

The hallway was very quiet. The runner was definitely ruined. Somewhere down by the baseboard, Bear could see the button that had pinged off it earlier, catching the light.

Bear stayed where Bear was. Kit's hand had come up to the back of Bear's head, fingers combing slow through Bear's hair, no particular pattern to it. Bear turned their face and pressed a kiss to the underside of Kit's jaw — soft, this one, no teeth involved at all — and felt Kit's answering breath go out long and easy.

"Hi," Bear said eventually, muffled, against Kit's throat.

Bear could feel Kit smile. Bear didn't need to see it.

"Don't move yet," Bear added, though Kit hadn't been trying to. "Give me a minute."

Bear's hand found Kit's and laced their fingers together on the floorboards, and stayed there, and breathed.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I press my lips to your temple. "Take two."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear took two. Bear took closer to five, honestly, and Kit didn't say anything about the discrepancy, just kept their fingers moving slow through Bear's hair and their other hand laced with Bear's on the hardwood.

Somewhere in the middle of it Bear registered that Kit's back had to be complaining about the floor by now, and that Bear's full weight on top of Kit wasn't helping, and did not immediately do anything about either of these things because Kit hadn't asked and Bear was not, currently, capable of executive function.

Eventually Bear shifted — just enough to get their weight off Kit's ribs, rolling half onto their side and dragging Kit with them so Kit ended up tucked against Bear's chest instead of pinned under it. The runner came with them in a tangle. Bear's jeans were still around their thighs. Kit's were still around theirs. The whole situation was undignified in a way Bear found difficult to care about.

"Floor was a bad call," Bear said, into Kit's hair. Not really complaining. Just noting.

Bear's hand found the small of Kit's back and stayed there, palm flat, thumb moving in a slow idle circle. The other hand was still tangled up with Kit's between them. Bear tipped their head down and looked at what Bear had done to Kit's shoulder in the light coming in from the kitchen — really looked, now, with the wanting-to satisfied and just the having-done left behind.

The marks were already coming up. The one at the collarbone was going to be spectacular. The shoulder itself was a mess in the specific way Kit had asked for, and Bear pressed their mouth to the edge of it, gentle, checking the skin wasn't broken anywhere that mattered. It wasn't. Close, in one spot. Not quite.

"You're going to be sore," Bear murmured. Approving. A little proud, if Bear was honest with themself, which Bear generally was in the aftermath if not before it. "Everywhere. Not just Thursday."

Bear kissed the mark once more, soft, and then rested their forehead against Kit's temple and let their eyes close for a second.

"Owe me a shirt," Bear added, after a beat. "And a button. Keeping track."

Bear's thumb kept moving on Kit's back. Bear was not, in fact, going to make Kit pay for the shirt or the button, but saying so would spoil it, and Kit knew that, and Kit's quiet huff of breath against Bear's collarbone said Kit knew that Bear knew Kit knew.

"In a minute," Bear said, not specifying what for, "we should get up. Bed. Water. That bathroom you were supposedly going to."

Bear did not move. Neither did Kit. That was fine. A minute could mean a lot of things.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Your shirt's fine," I murmur, my fingers trailing down your spine. I can feel the seam I tore. "Bed's too far. Bathroom's still two feet away."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear made a sound that was mostly agreement and partly complaint, and did not open their eyes.

"Bathroom's two feet away if you can stand up," Bear pointed out, reasonable, into Kit's hair. "Which you cannot."

Kit's fingers had found the torn seam and were worrying at it, making it worse, and Bear filed that away as another thing Kit owed for and also did not care about. Kit's hand felt good on Bear's back. Everything felt good, in the specific loose-limbed way it always did after, when Bear's whole body had gone from wanting to having and hadn't yet remembered it also lived on a floor.

"Give me the count of ten," Bear said. "Then I'll get us up."

Bear did not start counting. Bear's hand at the small of Kit's back slid up under the tangle of what used to be Kit's shirt situation and settled between Kit's shoulder blades instead, palm flat over the warm skin there. Kit's breathing had gone slow. Bear could feel it moving Kit's ribs against Bear's own.

"Water first," Bear amended, because Bear was starting to think about logistics in a distant sort of way and dehydration was a real thing. "Then bathroom. Then bed. Bed's non-negotiable, I'm not sleeping on the runner."

Bear cracked one eye open and looked down at Kit — chin tucked against Bear's collarbone, hair a disaster, one mark blooming dark at the side of their throat where Bear could see it in the kitchen light. Kit looked pleased with themselves in a soft undefended way that Bear was not going to comment on because commenting on it would put it away.

Bear kissed the top of Kit's head instead.

"You did good," Bear said, quiet, meaning several things at once — the wall, the wrists, the asking, the not-keeping-score. Kit would sort out which ones later or not at all, either was fine. "C'mere. Two more minutes. Then I'll carry you if I have to."

Bear would not have to. Bear knew this. Bear was going to offer anyway, because the offering was part of it, and because in about ninety seconds Bear was going to need to be the one doing the getting-up, and knowing that was coming made the two minutes now feel like something Bear had earned.

Bear's thumb went back to its slow circle between Kit's shoulder blades. The house was very quiet. Somewhere the fridge clicked on, and Bear didn't move, and neither did Kit, and the count of ten went unspoken and uncounted for a good while longer than ten.
