dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't need to be told twice. The instant Kit's heels clicked against the hardwood in retreat, the lazy, generous facade vanished. A slow, predatory grin split his face, and he gave Kit exactly one heartbeat of a head start before he lunged forward.

He loved the chase. He loved the scramble of it, the sudden rush of heat in his veins, and the familiar, fierce joy of hunting someone who wanted to be caught just as badly as he wanted to catch them. 

His heavy footsteps thudded in rapid pursuit, easily closing the distance Kit had managed to steal. He didn't make a sound to warn them, save for the low, rumbling laugh that vibrated in his chest as he reached out, fingers hooked and ready to snag fabric or skin.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp laugh, twisting away from his grasp at the last second. "Not yet, you don't!" I dart toward the living room, knowing full well he'll corner me there.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The near-miss only put a sharper edge on Bear's grin. His fingers brushed the fabric of Kit’s shirt, catching nothing but a fleeting slip of warmth before they twisted out of reach. He didn't hesitate; he pivoted on the heel of his foot, the old hardwood creaking under his weight as he redirected his momentum with the practiced ease of someone who had done this a thousand times.

He didn't chase straight down the hall. Instead, he took the wider, smarter angle, cutting through the dining room threshold to intercept them. He knew every inch of this house, every squeaky floorboard, and exactly how Kit liked to move when they were cornered. 

As they burst into the living room, Bear was already there, his broad frame blocking the easiest route around the heavy oak coffee table. He came to a heavy, skidding halt, his chest rising and falling with a thick, heavy breath. He looked massive in the dim light of the room, his eyes dark and locked entirely on his partner. 

"You're running out of room, sweetheart," Bear rumbled, his voice low and vibrating with a rough, gravelly warmth. He took a slow, deliberate step forward, his hands slightly raised, fingers twitching in open anticipation of the impact. He was herding them now, deliberately narrowing the space between them and the soft cushions of the sofa.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't waste a fraction of a second. The moment he saw that slight yield in Kit’s shoulders—the subtle, delicious surrender of someone who knew they were caught—he closed the remaining distance with a heavy, deliberate stride. 

He caught Kit just at the threshold where the hallway opened into the living room. His large, calloused hands clamped down on Kit's waist, his grip firm and unyielding as he used his momentum to drive them back a step, pinning them firmly against the sturdy wooden doorframe. The impact was solid, a blunt thud of weight and heat that knocked the breath out of both of them in a shared, ragged gasp.

Bear crowded in close, his broad chest pressing flush against Kit’s, completely bracketing them with his bulk. He leaned his full weight into them, a heavy, grounding pressure that he knew they liked just as much as he did. He buried his face into the curve of Kit’s neck, inhaling the familiar, sharp scent of their skin mixed with the heat of the brief chase.

"Too easy," Bear murmured, his voice a low, gravelly vibration against Kit's collarbone. His teeth grazed the warm skin right above their collar, a playful, warning nip that promised a mark later. He lingered there, his breath hot, his fingers digging just a little deeper into their hips to hold them still. "You're getting lazy, sweetheart. That's a point to me."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I grin, breathless and pinned. "You just got lucky." I arch into the pressure of his hands, my own coming up to tangle in his hair. "My turn now?"

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's head tilted back slightly as Kit's fingers tangled in his hair, a low, rumbling chuckle vibrating deep in his chest. He relished the sharp, grounding tug on his scalp, his body reacting instantly to the way Kit arched up and into his weight. 

"Lucky?" Bear repeated, his voice dripping with mock offense. He pulled back just an inch, his dark eyes gleaming down at Kit, full of lazy, fond satisfaction. "That was pure, calculated genius, sweetheart. Don't go rewriting history just because you got caught out."

He felt the shift in Kit's energy, the familiar, electric spark of competitive heat that always flared when they were pinned. When Kit asked if it was their turn, Bear's grin widened, showing a brief flash of teeth. His grip on Kit's hips didn't slacken; instead, he squeezed, his thumbs digging into the warm dip of their waist, anchoring them both against the doorframe. 

"You want a turn?" Bear murmured, leaning back down so his lips brushed against the shell of Kit's ear, his hot breath stirring their hair. "Then take it. But I'm not just giving it to you."

He braced his weight, shifting his heavy boots slightly to give them a solid, unyielding base. He was practically daring Kit to try and flip the script, to wrestle him down or find a way to claw their way on top. His muscles tensed in happy anticipation, ready for the impact of whatever Kit was about to throw at him.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The shift in Kit was all the permission Bear needed. He didn't bother trying to guide them toward the bedroom, nor did he care about the lack of a mattress. The hardwood floor was right there, cold and unyielding, and they were already halfway to it.

With a low, feral grunt, Bear gathered Kit closer, his heavy thigh sliding between theirs as he bore them down. He used his own bulk to cushion the worst of the impact, his large hand cupping the back of Kit's head to protect it from the floor, but the landing was still solid and heavy enough to rattle their ribs. 

Then came the chaotic, impatient scramble of fabric. 

Bear’s hands, usually so steady, were clumsy with sudden, ravenous urgency. He gripped the hem of Kit’s shirt and hauled it upward. A button popped, skittering across the hardwood with a sharp *clack*, but neither of them paid it any mind. He yanked the fabric over Kit’s head, his calloused palms scraping hungrily against the warm skin of their ribs, his fingers digging in to anchor them. 

When a sleeve got stubbornly caught around an elbow, Bear let out a rough, frustrated huff. He didn't waste time trying to untangle it gently; he simply used his teeth to help tug the fabric down, his mouth grazing the sensitive skin of Kit's shoulder in a sharp, demanding nip. He left a hot, damp trail of kisses and shallow bites along their collarbone, marking his progress while his hands worked blindly at the waistband of their pants. 

He was heavy on top of them, a thick, suffocating weight of muscle and heat, completely pinning Kit to the floor as they fought their way out of the rest of their clothes. He was grinning against their skin, his chest heaving with rough, excited breaths.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I manage to shove my own pants halfway down my thighs before I give up and just wrap my legs around him. "Enough," I pant, nails digging into his shoulders. "Just get on with it."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The sharp, stinging bite of Kit’s nails sinking into his shoulders was like a jolt of pure electricity straight to Bear's spine. He let out a low, rough growl, his chest vibrating hard against Kit's as he abandoned the useless struggle with their tangled denim. 

"Impatient," Bear rumbled, though there wasn't a single shred of complaint in his voice. 

He didn't need to be told twice. He freed his hands from their clothes, shifting his weight to prop himself up on his forearms, framing Kit's head. He looked down at them, his face flushed, eyes dark and completely consumed by the sight of them pinned beneath him, breathless and demanding. A fierce, possessive heat flared in his gut.

With a blunt, heavy shove of his hips, Bear rid himself of the last of his own obstacles, his jeans pooling uselessly around his knees. He didn't care about the awkwardness of it, or the cold hardwood pressing against his shins; all he cared about was the searing, skin-on-skin friction as he settled his full weight back down between Kit's thighs. 

He locked his hands into the carpet on either side of Kit's head, bracing himself. His breath came in thick, ragged pants, hot against Kit's mouth just a second before he leaned down and took it. 

The kiss was hard, messy, and deep, a bruising clash of teeth and tongues that tasted of adrenaline and years of shared heat. As he pressed into them, finding that perfect, familiar alignment, Bear let out a long, shuddering groan. He sank into the connection, slow and heavy, letting Kit feel every single ounce of his weight and his absolute lack of restraint. 

He gripped the back of Kit's thigh, hauling it higher around his waist to lock them together, his fingers digging deep enough into the flesh to leave faint, pale marks that would undoubtedly turn dark by morning. 

"You're mine," he muttered against Kit's lips, his voice thick and gravelly with a raw, unchecked hunger. "All yours, sweetheart. Take it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn't need to be told twice. He leaned down, his mouth finding the exact same patch of flushed, heated skin on Kit's shoulder, and sank his teeth in. He didn't hold back; he knew exactly how much pressure Kit wanted, the sweet spot between pleasure and the sharp, grounding sting of pain. He bit down until he felt the muscle tense beneath his jaw, a low, satisfied vibration rumbling in his own throat as he held them there, marking them deeply.

He tasted salt and heat, the metallic tang of pure adrenaline. When he finally released them, leaving a wet, angry red crescent of toothmarks that would definitely purple by tomorrow, he licked over the spot once, a rough, soothing gesture before he drove forward again.

The impact of their hips meeting was loud in the quiet room, a blunt, heavy rhythm that echoed off the bare walls. Bear's hands slid down from the floor to grip the undersides of Kit's thighs, hauling them up even higher, forcing Kit to take every bit of his size and weight. The hardwood floor beneath them was unforgiving, but neither of them cared about the bruises they'd both be sporting. 

"Good?" Bear grunted, his voice barely more than a gravelly whisper against the side of Kit's neck. He was sweating now, his forehead pressing against Kit's temple, his breath hot and ragged as he kept a steady, punishing pace. He locked his fingers with Kit's, pinning their hands to the floor, his thumbs rubbing over their knuckles with a heavy, possessive friction. "Tell me, Kit. You like that?"

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Love it," I gasp, my voice breaking as I arch up to meet him. My other hand fists in his hair, pulling his mouth back to mine. "Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The sharp, bruising yank on his hair sent a jolt of pure, electric heat straight to Bear’s core. He let out a rough, muffled growl against Kit’s lips as he crashed back down into the kiss, meeting their mouth with a desperate, devouring hunger. He didn't need the warning; he couldn't have stopped now if the house were burning down around them.

He set a relentless, driving pace, his heavy hips slamming into Kit’s with a blunt, rhythmic force that had them both sliding slightly against the slick hardwood. Bear braced his toes against the floor, anchoring himself, using every ounce of his superior size to pin Kit down and fill them completely. The friction was searing, a white-hot focal point of sensation that made his head spin. 

With every hard, upward thrust, Bear let out a thick, ragged groan, his breath puffing hot and damp against Kit’s cheek. He loved the wild, unraveled sound of Kit’s voice breaking. He loved the desperate grip of their fingers in his hair, the sharp sting of it pulling at his scalp, grounding him in the middle of the storm. 

He reached down, his large hand finding the back of Kit’s neck, his fingers tangling in their hair to tilt their head back, exposing the pale line of their throat. He pressed a hard, suctioning kiss to the pulse point fluttering there, his teeth grazing the skin in a silent promise of another mark. 

"Not stopping," Bear panted, his voice a gravelly, ruined whisper near Kit's ear. His chest heaved against theirs, slick with sweat, his heart hammering a frantic rhythm against Kit’s ribs. "Going to... ruin you for the bed, sweetheart. Keep matching me. Come on." 

He shifted his grip, locking his hands under Kit's hips to lift them slightly, tilting their pelvis to take him even deeper as he drove into them again, completely lost to the raw, heavy rhythm of it.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
A dark, viciously pleased growl rumbled up from the deepest part of Bear's chest. He looked down at Kit’s offered wrists, his eyes turning almost black in the dim light, burning with a sudden, fierce spike of adrenaline. 

He didn't hesitate. He brought his large hand down, his broad fingers wrapping completely around both of Kit's wrists in a single, heavy bracket of flesh and bone. He squeezed, letting them feel the immense, crushing strength of his grip before he pinned their hands flat to the hardwood above their head. He put his weight into it, his forearm pressing down to lock them in place, ensuring there was absolutely no escape.

"Thursday," Bear repeated, the word a rough, breathless rasp against Kit’s cheek. He let out a low, predatory chuckle that was entirely devoid of gentleness. "I'll give you Friday, sweetheart. I'll make sure you feel me every time you move."

To prove it, he shifted his lower body, his hips backing off for one agonizing second before he drove forward with a slow, heavy, bruising force that made the floorboards beneath them groan. He held himself deep inside them, letting the sheer, stretching fullness of the connection sink in while he targeted his next mark.

He leaned down, his mouth tracing a hot, wet line from the hollow of Kit's throat up to the sensitive junction where their neck met their shoulder. He didn't just nip this time. He gathered a thick fold of skin between his teeth and bit down with slow, deliberate, punishing pressure. 

He felt the sharp jump of Kit's pulse against his tongue, the frantic, beautiful heat of them. He ground his teeth together, sinking them in deep enough to guarantee a dark, purple-black bloom of a bruise that would last for days. He kept the pressure steady, his breath hitching as he felt Kit tense beneath him, his own body wound so tight it was screaming for release.

His free hand slid down to grip the flare of Kit’s hip, his thick fingers digging in so hard his knuckles turned white. He anchored them both, his thumb pressing deep into the soft flesh right above the bone, deliberately leaving a matching set of marks to mirror the heavy grip on their wrists. 

"You're going to be black and blue," Bear panted against the ruined skin of Kit's shoulder, his voice thick, gravelly, and utterly consumed by them. He began to move again, a hard, relentless, driving rhythm that left no room for breath. "Every time you look in the mirror. Every time you bend down. You're going to think of me."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp, bitten-off sound against his mouth, my body arching under the perfect pressure of his weight and teeth. "Good," I gasp, my hips lifting to meet each punishing thrust. "Don't you dare be gentle."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
"Gentle?" Bear let out a rough, breathless laugh that was more of a growl, his teeth scraping against the fresh, angry red mark on Kit’s shoulder. "You've got the wrong man for gentle, sweetheart."

He took them at their word. He shifted his weight, pressing his forearm harder against Kit's pinned wrists, feeling the rapid, frantic flutter of their pulse under his skin. He didn't ease up; instead, he drove forward with a sudden, bruising force that elicited a loud, satisfying *creak* from the hardwood floor beneath them. 

Every muscle in his back and shoulders coiled tight as he set a punishing, unrelenting pace. He was all heavy, driving mass now, his chest slick with sweat as he slid against Kit’s skin, the friction hot and electric. He watched Kit's face closely, his dark eyes tracking every twitch of their jaw, the way their eyes blown wide with dark, unfiltered pleasure. 

He reached down with his free hand, his thick fingers hooking under Kit’s hip to lift them higher, tilting them to take him even deeper. He wanted to feel every contraction, wanted to leave no doubt about who owned this space, this moment, and every inch of their skin. 

"Look at me," Bear panted, his voice a ruined, gravelly command. He leaned down, his face inches from Kit's, his breath hot and smelling of the copper tang of their skin. "Look at what you're asking for."

He slammed into them again, a heavy, blunt stroke that made his own head swim, his heart hammering against his ribs like a trapped beast. He was right on the edge, the heat in his lower belly turning into a tight, screaming coil, but he held on, determined to drag every last gasp out of Kit before he let himself go.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let out a sound that was barely human—a low, ragged growl that died in the back of his throat. He didn't stop. He couldn't have if he tried. 

Every muscle in his broad back and shoulders bunched and strained as he drove forward, matching Kit’s desperate, upward arches with a heavy, bruising finality. He squeezed Kit's pinned wrists even tighter, the wood of the floorboards creaking under the sheer, unyielding pressure of his weight. He wanted Kit to feel the absolute limit of his strength, the terrifying and beautiful reality of being completely mastered by someone who loved them to the bone.

The friction was a white-hot, blinding focus, a rhythm so intense and consuming that the rest of the room simply ceased to exist. There was only the heat of their slick skin, the sharp, metallic tang of sweat and adrenaline, and the frantic, echoing slaps of their hips meeting in the quiet room. Bear’s breath came in short, ruined gasps, his chest heaving violently against Kit's. 

He felt the sudden, tight clench of Kit’s body around him, the exquisite, desperate spike of their own release beginning to take hold. It shattered the last of Bear’s control. 

With a thick, guttural groan, Bear drove into them one last time, deep and heavy, his hips locking flush against Kit's. His whole body went rigid. A violent, trembling spasm racked his massive frame as he let himself go, pouring every ounce of his heat and strength into the connection. He buried his face in the crook of Kit’s neck, his teeth scraping blindly against the freshly bruised skin of their shoulder as he rode out the wave of his own heavy, pulsing climax. 

He held them pinned, his forearm still anchoring Kit’s wrists to the floor, his other hand dug so deep into Kit’s hip that his fingers would leave a perfect, matching set of dark bruises by morning. He was completely deadweight now, a massive, suffocating blanket of muscle and heat, but he didn't pull back. He stayed exactly where he was, his heart hammering like a trapped bird against Kit's ribs, his breath coming in long, shuddering drafts against their wet skin. 

He let out a low, exhausted laugh, the vibration deep and gravelly in his chest. "Thursday," he panted, his voice ruined and thick. He pressed a heavy, damp kiss to the bite mark on Kit's shoulder, tasting the salt of their skin. "You're... definitely going to feel that on Thursday, sweetheart."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I can't feel my legs. My wrists are going to have his fingerprints for a week. I let my head thunk back against the floor, grinning up at the ceiling. "Perfect."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let out a long, rumbling breath that puffed warm against Kit's collarbone. Slowly, reluctantly, he rolled his bulk off them, though he didn't go far. He flopped onto his side with a heavy, exhausted sigh, immediately hooking one thick, heavy leg over Kit’s thighs to keep them anchored to him and the floor. 

The hardwood was cold against his back, a stark contrast to the radiating heat of Kit’s body, but he was too depleted to care about moving to the rug, let alone the couch. He propped himself up on one elbow, his chest still heaving, and looked down at his partner.

"Perfect," Bear grunted, his voice a ruined, gravelly rasp. A slow, lazy smile tugged at the corner of his mouth, fond and utterly self-satisfied. He reached out, his large, calloused hand tracing down the inside of Kit's arm to where his fingers had just been clamped. Already, the pale skin of Kit’s wrists was blooming with a thick, angry red bracelet of his grip. 

He ran his thumb over the mark, a surprisingly gentle gesture compared to the violence of a moment ago. 

"You're going to be walking like a newborn calf tomorrow," he murmured, his eyes shifting up to the wet, dark crescent of toothmarks on Kit's shoulder. The skin there was swollen and leaking a tiny bit of heat, destined to be a deep, ugly purple by the time Thursday actually rolled around. Bear leaned down and pressed a soft, lingering kiss right to the center of the bite, his beard scratchy against Kit's collarbone. 

"I'm taking two points for that," he muttered against their skin, his thumb rubbing comforting circles into the side of their hip, right where his hand had left another deep, heavy impression. "One for the chase, and one for the follow-through. Don't even try to argue."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I reach up and pat his cheek, my arm feeling heavy and pleasantly useless. "Take three. I'm feeling generous." I let my hand drop back to the floor with a soft thud. "Now get off me, you're crushing my circulation."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let out a low, rumbling huff of a laugh, his chest vibrating against Kit's shoulder. "Three points," he muttered, sounding thoroughly pleased with himself. "I'll take 'em. But don't go pretending it was charity, sweetheart. I earned every single one of those."

He didn't move immediately, deliberately lingering for one more heavy, teasing heartbeat just to hear Kit groan, before he finally rolled off. He landed on his back with a heavy, dramatic *thud* that seemed to vibrate through the floorboards, letting out a long, exhausted sigh as the cool air of the living room hit his sweaty, flushed skin. 

But he didn't let Kit get too far. Even as he freed them from his full weight, he reached out and slung one massive, heavy arm over Kit’s chest, dragging them sideways until they were tucked firmly against his flank. He rested his chin on the top of Kit's head, his fingers lazily tracing the curve of their shoulder, right over the angry red mark he'd just left. 

"There," Bear grumbled, his voice thick and gravelly with sleepiness and satisfaction. "Circulation restored. But you're still stuck here. I'm not letting you up until my legs work again, and that's going to be a while." 

He squeezed Kit's side, his thumb brushing over the faint, blossoming bruise on their hip, already feeling the deep, familiar warmth of the afterglow settling into his bones. "We're sleeping on the floor. Deal with it."

dialogue.content: I elbow him in the ribs, but it's a weak, half-hearted thing. "Your legs not working is a you problem." I settle in anyway, tucking my head under his chin. "Fine. But you're making breakfast tomorrow."

“You’re going to regret that, sweetheart,” Bear rumbled in her ear, already moving to pin her arms behind her back, his fingers digging in just enough to sting. The score was definitely his—at least for now.

dialogue.content:
Bear grunted at the jolt of Kit’s foot catching his calf—she was faster than most, and far meaner. But he’d been waiting for something like that. He shifted his weight, anticipating the move, and let himself stagger just enough to lull her into thinking she’d gained the upper hand. In the same motion, he swung her around so her back hit the fridge with a gentle thud, crowding in close, his mouth at her ear.

“I know so,” Bear growled, his voice low and smug. One knee wedged between her legs, pinning her in place, while his grip on her wrists tightened. “But you’re welcome to keep trying.”

He nipped again, this time at the line of her jaw, teeth scraping, daring her to make her next move.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the fight drop just a notch in Kit’s body—enough that he knew she’d chosen this, let him have it, for now. He didn’t loosen his grip; if anything, he leaned in harder, pressing his advantage with a low, satisfied rumble in his chest.

He slipped one hand from her wrists to her waist, fingers digging in where he knew she’d bruise, and pulled her tighter to him. His other hand tangled in her hair, tugging her head back so he could mouth at her throat, teeth scraping and biting, leaving little stinging marks along the way. Every time she shifted or tried to twist free, Bear only grinned against her skin, holding her fast.

“You’re not going anywhere,” he murmured, voice rough and thick with promise, “until I say so. You want to keep score, you better start fighting for it.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I arch against him, a slow roll of my hips. "Who said I was keeping score?" I bite out, breathless but grinning. "Maybe I just like the view from here."

dialogue.name: Bear

Bear huffed out a laugh, dark and pleased. “Liar,” he accused, lips trailing the edge of Kit’s jaw, his voice a low vibration against her skin. “You never stop keeping score.” He punctuated the words with another nip, this one just below her ear—harder, leaving a mark he knew she’d feel tomorrow.

His hand on her waist slid lower, fingers pressing bruises into her hip, holding her exactly where he wanted. The hand tangled in her hair tightened, not cruel but insistent, controlling the angle of her head so he could study the flush rising in her cheeks, the spark in her eyes.

“You like the view, you can keep it,” Bear rumbled, pinning her tighter with his knee. “But you’re still not getting away.” He let his teeth scrape down her neck, slow and deliberate, daring her to push back, to try and wriggle free. He lived for the moment she’d snap and make him earn it again.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear didn’t care about the hardwood or the scattered mail underfoot, just the heat of Kit’s skin and the scramble of hands and teeth. He pressed her down, using the solid weight of his body to keep her in place, pinning her wrists above her head with one big hand. The other skimmed rough over ribs and hip, yanking at stubborn fabric until it gave way or else simply got shoved aside—neither of them ever bothered with neatness when it counted.

He braced himself over her, eyes gone dark with the thrill of the chase won, but not finished. Bear ducked his head to bite at Kit’s shoulder, lingering just long enough to leave proof, then dragged his teeth down her arm, claiming space as his own. “Still not running?” he taunted, voice rumbling as his hips pressed her into the floor, the friction deliberate and slow. “You got one more chance, Kit—make it count.”

Even as he said it, he knew she’d make him pay for every inch he took. That was half the fun—maybe more.

With his free hand, Bear traced a rough path down her side, nails scratching just hard enough to leave red tracks, claiming her inch by inch. He ducked down again, this time biting the curve of her breast through what was left of her shirt, satisfied at the way she arched and gasped beneath him.

Bear didn’t need telling twice. He bit down again, harder, right beside the first mark—slow, deliberate, putting his whole jaw into it until he felt her tense and shudder beneath him. The bruises would rise dark and proud, proof for days. He mouthed over both marks, soothing the ache with his tongue, then bit once more, gentler, just to remind her he was still in control.

His grip on her wrists never wavered, pinning her above her head as he rocked into her, savoring every gasp and twist. “You want more?” he rumbled, voice thick. He dragged his mouth up her neck, nipping and sucking new marks wherever he found bare skin. “You have to earn it, Kit. Let’s see how much fight you’ve got left.”

He loosened his grip just enough to let her strain against him—never enough to break free, just enough to remind them both how good it felt to try. Every scratch, every bruise, every bite was another point on the board, and Bear meant to leave her begging to settle the score.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I yank one wrist free and shove my hand into his hair, pulling hard. "I've got plenty," I gasp, then kiss him like I'm trying to win something else entirely.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s head snapped back from the force of Kit’s grip in his hair, the pain sending a jolt of heat straight through him. He let her pull, let her claim the space between them for a heartbeat—and then he kissed her back, savage and hungry, teeth clashing with hers. It wasn’t gentle, wasn’t sweet—this was a fight in its own right, mouths warring for dominance, breathing each other’s air.

He wrenched her other wrist up, holding it tight against the floor, but let her keep his hair, let her pull until his scalp burned. He liked the sting—liked her wild for him, matching him move for move. His tongue pushed into her mouth, demanding, and his hips ground down harder, pinning her in place, making it clear that even if she won this round, he’d take the next.

Bear broke the kiss just long enough to bite her lower lip, hard, then dragged his mouth down her throat, marking a new line of bruises as he went. His voice was ragged, feral, right against her ear: “Plenty’s just the start, Kit. Show me all of it.” He loosened his grip on her wrist, daring her to break free, all muscle and promise and bared teeth—waiting to see what she’d do next.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s eyes went dark with satisfaction at Kit’s demand, the explicit permission a thrill every time. He took her wrists in one broad hand, pinning them above her head, his grip firm but never cruel. He lowered his head and met her gaze, something wild and tender flickering in his expression.

“You’ll get them,” Bear promised, his voice a rough vow. He caught her lower arm in his mouth, biting along the inside of her forearm—hard enough to bruise, teeth sinking in until he felt her gasp and twitch. He didn’t let up until he was certain the mark would last, then soothed it with his tongue, slow and possessive.

He worked his way down—her bicep, the curve of her shoulder, collarbone—each bite deliberate, each bruise a tally in their game. His free hand slipped under what was left of her shirt, dragging it up so he could mouth over her ribs and belly, laying claim to every inch of skin he could reach. Where the bone was close under her skin, he bit harder, holding until he heard the smallest, helpless sound escape her lips.

Bear braced himself over her, breathing heavy, watching the red and purple already blooming across her skin. “You’ll see them every time you look,” he growled, pride and hunger tangled in his words. “You’ll feel them every time you move. That’s a promise, Kit.”

He leaned in again, catching her mouth with his, slow this time, savoring the taste of her fight and her surrender—knowing she’d be counting every mark, every ache, for days.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I break the kiss to laugh, breathless and raw. "Good," I say, my voice shaking. I hook a leg around his hip and pull him down against me. "Now stop talking and make good on it."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear answered with a sound that was more growl than laugh, the heat in him flaring at Kit’s words and the way she pulled him in. He gave her what she wanted—what she’d demanded—pressing his weight down until she was pinned beneath him, nothing between them now but sweat and skin and the bruises he’d promised.

He drove his hips into hers, grinding slow and deep, his teeth finding her throat again. He bit hard enough to draw a sharp gasp, holding it, letting her feel the pressure, the ache that would last and last. He trailed down to her collarbone, then lower, leaving a constellation of marks—some sharp, some blooming and deep—each one a signature, a claim.

Bear’s free hand found her thigh, shoving her leg higher around his waist, fingers digging into the muscle until she writhed. He bit the inside of her knee, another mark in a place only they would know. He didn’t let up, didn’t go gentle; every bruise, every scrape, every burn of his teeth was a wordless promise kept.

He didn’t bother with more talk. He showed her—over and over—until she was marked and shuddering and there was no doubt who’d won, or who’d be wearing the story for days. And when he finally let her hands go, Bear didn’t so much as look away, just brushed his thumb over the swelling bite on her wrist, fierce pride in his eyes.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear bore down, every muscle taut with purpose, his body a wall of heat and hunger above her. He didn’t hesitate, didn’t slow—not when she begged, not when she bucked up hard beneath him. He pressed her wrists to the floor, pinning her without mercy, his grip unyielding as his mouth moved down her throat, teeth scraping, sucking, biting at the delicate skin until she arched and gasped for him.

He moved lower, dragging his teeth over every hollow and curve, biting hard at the jut of her collarbone and the swell of her breast. He closed his jaw until she whimpered, holding the pressure for a long, breathless moment before letting go, leaving another angry red mark to blossom purple by morning. He soothed each ache with his tongue, not gentle but thorough, as if the contrast would make the sting last longer.

Bear’s free hand traveled rough and sure over her ribs, marking a jagged trail down her belly, nails raking lines that would sting every time she twisted or stretched. He forced her thighs open with his knee, crowding in until she had no leverage, no room to run, only him—his weight, his hands, his mouth, and the relentless press of his hips.

He bit the inside of her thigh, hard enough to make her jolt and curse, and grinned against her skin. He mouthed bruises up the sensitive skin, then used his teeth on the muscle just above her knee, not stopping until she was shaking with the effort of holding still—or fighting against him, it hardly mattered. Every sound she made, every shudder, every ragged breath was another point scored, another proof of what they were to each other.

He shifted, letting go of one wrist so he could tangle his fingers in her hair, pulling her head back to expose her throat again. He kissed her, deep and messy, teeth dragging her bottom lip until she tasted copper. His hips never stopped, grinding against her, relentless, every thrust another bruise he promised she’d feel for days.

Bear’s voice was a low, broken thing now, all heat and pride. “You’ll wear every mark, Kit. Every one.” He bit down at the base of her throat, a deep, claiming bruise, and didn’t let go—not until her body bucked and he felt her come undone beneath him, wild and fierce and marked all over.

He followed her, shuddering against her, teeth still in her skin, and didn’t stop until there was nothing left but sweat and the sound of their breath, and the shared certainty that neither of them needed to keep score tonight. Bear loosened his grip, nuzzling the worst of his marks, his voice rough and fond. “Still want more?” he rumbled, already knowing the answer, already aching for the next round.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let my head thump back against the floor, breathing hard. My whole body's singing. "Yeah," I say, reaching up to trace the bite on his shoulder. "But you're paying for my heating bill if you keep my clothes in pieces."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let out a low, satisfied laugh, the sound rolling through his chest as he sprawled over Kit, pressing her down for another breathless moment just because he could. Her fingers on his shoulder made him grin—he could already feel the bruise forming, a matched set to the ones he’d left on her.

“Fair trade,” he rumbled, not bothering to move yet. “But you’re the one who keeps getting in the way of your own buttons.” He leaned down to brush his mouth over the mark she’d made, a gentle kiss to soothe the ache, then bit it again—not hard, just a warning, a promise.

Bear shifted his weight off her enough that she could breathe, but not enough to let her up. He ran his palm down her side, thumb catching every blooming bruise, a silent tally. “You want more, you know where to find me,” he murmured, nosing at her ear. “But don’t think I won’t collect next time you try to run.”

He let her up just enough to roll her into his side, still tangled together, still hungry. “And if you’re cold, you know damn well how to fix that.” His smile was sharp, eyes glinting with pride and challenge, even as his hands started to wander again—never quite finished, never quite gentle, and always ready for another round.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I push up on an elbow, wincing at the new bruises. "Fix it?" I say, and bite his jaw, light but pointed. "Fine. Your shirt's mine now."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear tipped his head back at the bite, the sting making his grin go crooked and wild. He didn’t flinch; instead, he let her teeth dig in, savoring it, letting her claim a little ground before he came for it again. Her words drew a deep, pleased rumble from his chest—he liked her greedy, liked her mouth on him, liked the promise in her voice even more than the threat.

“My shirt, huh?” Bear said, voice rough with laughter. “Suppose that’s fair, considering you’re wearing the rest of me.” He reached up, fingers curling slow and proprietary over her hip where the bruise was already darkening, thumb rolling over the mark just to make her wince again. “But you better wear it with the marks showing. Otherwise, what’s the point?”

He rolled her easily, trapping her half beneath him, his teeth closing on her ear, not quite biting, just a warning. “You can take whatever you want, Kit,” he growled, “but don’t forget who it belongs to.” His hand drifted up her back, nails dragging just light enough to make her shiver. “You want to keep warm, you stay right here. And next time you try to run, I’ll take more than your shirt.”

Bear’s smile was all teeth, his eyes bright with challenge. The game never really ended between them—it just paused to let them catch their breath.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless, and sink my teeth into the meat of his shoulder. "It's a deal," I say against his skin, then push him off enough to stand. I snag his discarded flannel from the floor and pull it on, my own bruises already starting to ache in the cool air. "Now make good on that heating bill and get the thermostat."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's grin was the last thing Kit saw before he moved.

He hadn't let Kit get that far out of generosity — he'd let Kit get that far because the kitchen had two exits and the hallway had none. Kit was fast, always had been, but Bear knew this apartment the way he knew the back of his own hands. Eight years of this, and he'd mapped every shortcut, every dead end, every surface Kit might try to vault over.

He didn't run. Not yet. He walked fast, deliberate, giving Kit a head start that wasn't really a head start — just enough rope to feel the thrill of almost making it. The sound of Kit's feet on the hardwood told him the direction: bedroom. Good. Fewer options.

Bear picked up his pace, boots heavy, rounding the corner just in time to see the bedroom door swing shut. He caught it with his palm before the latch clicked, and the momentum carried him inside.

Kit was on the other side of the bed, breathing hard, eyes bright. That look — the one that said *come and get it* without a single word.

Bear leaned against the doorframe and folded his arms, taking his time, letting his gaze drag over Kit like a physical thing.

"You picked the room with one way out," he said, conversationally, like they were discussing the weather. His pulse was steady. His eyes were not. "You sure about that?"

He wasn't asking permission. He was giving Kit three more seconds.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I grin back, edging along the bed frame. "Maybe I wanted you to corner me." My fingers grip the wood, ready to push off. "Three seconds is generous. You're slipping."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's eyebrow went up. "Generous," he repeated, like he was tasting the word.

He pushed off the doorframe. Slowly. Not because he was slow, but because Kit was watching his shoulders, his hands, reading his body language the way Kit always did — trying to predict the lunge. Bear had learned a long time ago that the trick wasn't being faster than Kit. The trick was being patient enough to make Kit move first.

"Three seconds was a gift," he said, rounding the foot of the bed, mirroring Kit's movement on the opposite side. The bed between them was maybe five feet of mattress. Nothing. "And you just spent it talking."

He watched Kit's grip tighten on the bed frame. Good. The anticipation was half the game — Kit knew it, Bear knew it. The best moments were the ones right before contact, that breath where everything was potential.

Bear shifted his weight to his left foot. Not a lunge. Just enough to make Kit's muscles tense, to make Kit commit to a direction. Eight years, and he still knew how to read every micro-adjustment Kit made, the way Kit's weight tipped toward the door — even now, even cornered, Kit's instinct was still to run.

"Go on, then," Bear said, quiet, almost a murmur. His eyes never left Kit's face. "Try it."

He wanted Kit to try.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
He caught Kit by the waist just as Kit feinted toward the living room, not even a real attempt to escape. Bear’s arm hooked around him, solid and unyielding, and he used Kit’s own momentum to turn them both and press Kit back against the hallway wall.

“Not even a real try,” Bear murmured, his chest against Kit’s back, his voice low near Kit’s ear. He pinned Kit there, not roughly, but with the weight of his body and the certainty of someone who’d done this hundreds of times. His other hand came up to brace against the wall beside Kit’s head.

He could feel the rapid rise and fall of Kit’s breathing, could see the quick pulse in the side of his neck. The thrill of the chase was there in the air between them, but this was the better part: the catch, the held moment before the next move.

“You’re thinking too hard,” Bear said, his lips brushing the shell of Kit’s ear. He could feel the slight shiver that earned him. “You always do when you let me get this close.”

He pressed his hips forward, just enough to make the point of his control clear, and let his teeth graze the tendon where Kit’s neck met his shoulder. Not a bite. Not yet. A promise.

“You’re not done,” he stated, not a question. “Neither am I.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let my head fall back against his shoulder, a low laugh escaping me. "You know me too damn well." I shift against him, testing his grip just enough to feel it tighten in response. "So what's your move now, Bear?"

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the vibration of Kit's laugh through his own chest, a familiar and welcome challenge. The shift against him was deliberate, playful, and his grip tightened instinctively—not to restrain, but to claim.

"Move?" Bear echoed, his voice a low rumble against Kit's skin. "I'm already where I want to be."

He wasn't lying. This was the culmination of the chase, not an endpoint but a plateau. He held Kit pinned with the solid weight of his body, but his hands were free. He brought the one from the wall down, not to grab, but to skim his fingertips along Kit's side, tracing the line of his ribs through his shirt, feeling the quickened breath beneath.

"You let me get here," he continued, his lips moving against the sensitive skin of Kit's ear. "So the next move is yours." He applied a fraction more pressure with his hips, a firm, unmistakable pressure. "Are you going to try to turn? To twist out? Or are you going to see what happens if you stay right... here?"

As he spoke, he let his teeth close over the tendon he'd been teasing. Not a playful nip, but a firm, deliberate press—the first real promise of a mark. He held it, feeling the muscle tense under his mouth, feeling the catch in Kit's breath. His own pulse was a steady, heavy drum in his ears. He released the bite but stayed close, his breath hot against the damp skin.

"My move," he murmured, "is whatever you force me to do next." It was an open invitation, a dare. He waited, every muscle coiled and patient, to see what Kit would give him.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The hallway floor was hardwood and unforgiving, and Bear didn't give a single damn.

Kit's shirt had ended up somewhere near the bathroom door — Bear had pulled it over his head with more enthusiasm than finesse, heard a seam protest, filed it under *not my problem.* His own shirt was half-unbuttoned, the rest of the buttons having lost the argument with Kit's impatient fingers. They'd solve the rest later. Or they wouldn't.

He had Kit beneath him now, the cold floor a stark contrast to the heat between them. Bear's forearm was braced beside Kit's head, his other hand gripping Kit's hip hard enough to bruise — and that was the point. He wanted Kit to feel this tomorrow, wanted to see the purple-blue bloom of his fingerprints when Kit's shirt came off for bed tonight.

"There," Bear breathed, half a growl, pressing Kit flat against the floor. The chase energy was still there, thrumming through his blood, but it had transformed into something hotter, more focused. He ducked his head and bit — properly this time, the meat of Kit's shoulder, enough to make Kit's back arch, enough to leave a mark that would sit alongside the collection of fading ones already scattered across Kit's skin like a map of every time Bear had caught him.

He soothed the bite with his tongue, then pulled back just enough to look at Kit — flushed, chest heaving, that reckless grin still pulling at his mouth even now. Even pinned. Even caught.

Bear's thumb traced a slow circle on Kit's hip bone. His voice was rough when he spoke.

"You're keeping score right now, aren't you." Not a question. "Thinking about where to bite me back." He lowered his mouth to Kit's throat, not biting, just breathing, feeling Kit's pulse jump against his lips. "Good. I'm counting on it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I get my teeth into the side of his neck, a sharp, claiming bite of my own. "One-all," I gasp, my hands pushing his jeans down his hips. "Now shut up and move."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the bite like a brand, Kit's teeth sinking into the side of his neck with a sharpness that made his hips jerk forward involuntarily. A low sound escaped him — not quite a groan, not quite a growl, something primal and pleased that he'd never have admitted to under interrogation.

*One-all.* He'd hear about that later. He'd *see* it later, the crescent marks in his skin when he caught his reflection shaving tomorrow morning. Fair enough. He never covered them.

Kit's hands were shoving his jeans down, and Bear shifted to help, kicking them off with none of the grace he pretended to have in any other part of his life. The hallway was narrow, the floor was hard, and Kit was *right there* beneath him, flushed and fierce and still keeping score like the competitive bastard he'd always been.

"Shut up and move," Kit had said.

Bear braced himself above Kit, one hand flat on the cold floor, the other still gripping Kit's hip. He looked down at him — wild-eyed, lips parted, marks already rising on his shoulder and neck — and for one sharp, suspended moment, something heavier than desire settled in his chest. Eight years. Eight years and Kit still looked at him like this, still challenged him, still *wanted* this.

He didn't shut up, because he never did. But he moved.

He rolled his hips forward, slow and deliberate at first, watching Kit's face the way he always watched — cataloging the catch of breath, the way Kit's fingers dug into his back, the half-second where Kit's eyes went unfocused before sharpening again. Bear buried his face in the curve of Kit's neck, mouthing the marks he'd already left, and gave him what he'd asked for.

Not gentle. They'd never been gentle with each other. But thorough — Bear was always thorough. Every thrust was deliberate, angled to make Kit's composure crack in exactly the right place. He knew this body the way he knew the apartment: mapped it, memorized it, returned to it over and over like a man who knew what he had.

Kit's nails raked down his back, and Bear hissed, his rhythm stuttering for half a beat before he recovered and drove forward harder.

"Count *that*," he muttered against Kit's skin, his voice wrecked.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear did it again.



He bit down on the same spot, harder this time, feeling the give of skin and muscle under his teeth, feeling Kit's whole body shudder beneath him. The sound Kit made went straight through him — raw, unguarded, the kind of sound that only ever surfaced in moments like this, when the walls between them were down to nothing.

He held the bite longer than the first, not enough to break skin but enough that he'd feel the imprint of his teeth when he pulled back. Enough that the mark would be deep, angry, unmistakable. His hand found Kit's jaw, tilting his head to bare more of that shoulder, and he licked over the wound when he released it — hot, slow, proprietary.

"Again?" Bear asked, his voice rough as gravel. His hips hadn't stopped, a steady relentless rhythm that kept Kit pinned to the floor as surely as any grip. "Or somewhere new?"

He didn't wait for an answer. His mouth moved lower, finding the ridge of Kit's collarbone, and he bit there too — different angle, different pressure, building a constellation of marks that would take a week to fade. His hand slid from Kit's jaw down his throat, not squeezing, just resting there, the weight of it a question Kit had answered a thousand times before.

Kit's fingers were digging into his shoulders hard enough to leave their own marks, and Bear welcomed them. The score was irrelevant in the moment — they'd tally later, in bed, counting bruises and comparing damage like the ridiculous competitive men they were. Right now there was only the give and take, the push and pull, the way Kit arched into every bite and Bear gave him more each time because Kit *wanted* more and had never once been shy about saying so.

Bear's rhythm faltered when Kit bit his ear — sharp, sudden, the lobe caught between teeth — and he dropped his forehead against Kit's shoulder with a breath that was half laugh, half groan.

"Two-one," he managed, and bit down on the meat of Kit's shoulder again because keeping score meant nothing if you weren't playing to win.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I laugh, breathless, hooking my leg around his to pull him closer. "Two-one my ass." I arch up to sink my teeth into the curve of his jaw. "Now it's tied."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear felt the bite on his jaw like a spark, Kit's teeth catching the edge of bone where muscle met skin, and his hips snapped forward hard enough to make the breath leave both of them.

*Tied.*

"Keep telling yourself that," he muttered, his voice scraped raw, and rolled his hips in a slow, deliberate grind that he knew would make Kit's argument fall apart mid-sentence. His hand found Kit's hip again — the same one he'd been gripping all along, and he could already feel the bruise forming under his palm, dark and deep and *his*.

He pulled back enough to look at Kit properly. The hallway light was wrong — too bright, too honest — and it showed everything: the flush spreading down Kit's chest, the marks scattered across his shoulder like a war report, the way his lips were swollen and parted, the way his eyes had gone dark and blown wide. Bear had seen this face a hundred times, a thousand, and it still hit him like the first time, every time.

He didn't say that. He never said that, not here, not in the middle of it. He showed it instead, the way he always did — by paying attention, by remembering exactly how Kit liked to be touched, by being the person who knew that Kit's left side was more sensitive, that Kit came undone faster when Bear's mouth was on his neck, that Kit needed to be held down *just enough* to push against.

Bear shifted his weight, driving deeper, and watched Kit's composure fracture in real time. He dipped his head and licked a slow stripe up the side of Kit's throat, over the pulse hammering there, and settled his teeth against the spot just below Kit's ear.

"Three-two," he breathed against Kit's skin, and bit down.

The sound Kit made would keep him going for days.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear's breath caught.

Not at the words — Kit had said things like this before, had made requests that would make anyone else flinch, had asked for Bear's hands and teeth and weight with the same casual certainty with which he asked for coffee in the morning. That wasn't new.

What stopped him was the wrists. The way Kit put them out, palms up, offered like a gift — like a *please* — and something in Bear's chest went tight and fierce and dangerously soft all at once.

He caught both of Kit's wrists in one hand. Not tight. Not yet. He held them there, just above Kit's head, pinned against the hardwood, and looked down at him for a long, measured beat.

"Thursday," Bear repeated. His voice was barely there. "You want them to hurt on Thursday."

He shifted his weight, settling deeper, and watched Kit's eyes flutter. His thumb traced the thin skin of Kit's inner wrist — the blue veins there, the delicate architecture of tendon and bone. He knew this terrain. Knew exactly how much pressure a wrist could take, knew where the nerve pathways ran, knew the difference between a mark that ached beautifully for days and one that actually damaged. Eight years. He'd learned.

"I'll give you Thursday," he said, and tightened his grip just enough that Kit felt the *potential* of it. "I'll give you next *week*."

He brought Kit's wrists together above his head, held them there with his left hand — the grip firm now, deliberate, the kind of pressure that would leave its own story in red impressions that would fade to purple to yellow-green over the coming days. With his right hand free, Bear traced the line of Kit's forearm down to the soft inside of his elbow, then back up, mapping the route.

Then he lowered his mouth to the inside of Kit's wrist — the left one first — and bit.

Not gentle. Not vicious. *Precise*. He knew the safe distances from the joint, knew where the flesh was soft enough to hold a mark deep and long. He bit and held, feeling Kit's pulse hammer against his teeth, feeling the way Kit's whole body tensed and then melted into it. He released, examined the deep purple crescent already rising on the pale skin, and did it again two inches higher.

He moved to the other wrist. Same treatment. Methodical. Unhurried. His hips had gone still, buried deep, and the stillness was its own kind of cruelty — Kit could feel everything and nothing, could only lie there and take the slow, deliberate work of Bear's mouth on his skin.

The wrist marks were just the beginning. Bear released Kit's wrists but kept them pinned — Kit could have moved them, probably, if he'd wanted to. That wasn't the point. The point was that Kit *didn't*.

Bear pushed up just enough to survey what he had. Kit beneath him, wrists crossed overhead, marks blooming across his shoulder and neck and jaw, chest heaving, that defiant spark still burning in his eyes even now. Even wrecked. Even pinned. Still keeping score.

Bear leaned down and spoke against the hollow of Kit's throat.

"I'm going to make you count," he murmured, and then he moved — his mouth, his teeth, his hands — working down Kit's body with the focused patience of a man who had all night and intended to use every minute of it. The chest. The ribs, where the skin was thin and the marks would show dark and angry. The curve of his hip, the inside of his thigh, the soft skin below his navel. Each bite placed with care, each one held long enough to bruise deep, each one soothed with a slow drag of tongue before Bear moved to the next.

He bit the inside of Kit's left thigh — hard — and Kit's hips bucked off the floor.

"That one's mine," Bear said against the mark, and meant it in about six different ways.

He kept going. Lost count himself, somewhere around nine or ten, because Kit's hands had found his hair and were pulling, and the sharp sting at his scalp made it difficult to concentrate on anything except the man beneath him and the heat between them and the relentless, beautiful rhythm of giving Kit exactly what he'd asked for.

When he finally worked his way back up to Kit's face — flushed, wrecked, gasping — Bear braced himself on his forearms and looked at him. Really looked. The marks he'd left were a landscape, a record, a promise kept. Some would fade by the weekend. Some would be there next Thursday, exactly as requested, a dull ache that Kit would feel reaching for a coffee mug and remember *this* — the hallway floor, the chase, the catch.

Bear pressed his forehead against Kit's. His voice was wrecked when he spoke.

"You're going to have a hell of a time explaining those at work."

His hips moved again — slow, deep, picking up the thread they'd dropped — and his mouth found the mark he'd left below Kit's ear, worrying it gently with his teeth, giving it one more day of staying power.

"You want more," he said. Not a question. His hand found Kit's hip again, thumb pressing into the bruise already forming there. "You always want more."

He gave it to him.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I laugh, a broken sound as I drag him down for a kiss. "Let them ask." I shift my hips, urging him on. "And yes. Always more."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
The kiss was messy, uncoordinated — the kind of kiss that happened when two people had been at this long enough to stop caring about technique and just *wanted*. Bear's mouth slanted over Kit's, hard and claiming, and Kit bit his lower lip, and Bear let him because fair was fair and the score was a lie they both enjoyed telling.

*Let them ask.*



Something about that — the casual defiance of it, the way Kit said it like he'd wear Bear's marks like trophies — made something in Bear's chest go molten. He broke the kiss and pressed his mouth to Kit's ear.

"They'll ask," he said, his voice ragged, his hips picking up the pace Kit had urged. "And you'll smile. And you won't tell them a goddamn thing. And that'll drive them crazy."

He knew this because Kit had done it before. The faded bite on Kit's collarbone last month that his coworker had *definitely* noticed. The fingerprint bruises on Kit's hips that had shown above his waistband at the gym. Kit never covered them, never explained them, just carried Bear's marks through the world with that infuriating, intoxicating lack of shame.

Bear's hand found Kit's throat again — not squeezing, never squeezing, just resting there with the weight of *I could* — and his other hand braced against the floor as his rhythm went from deliberate to urgent. The hallway was cold against his bare skin. Kit was burning under him. The contrast made him dizzy.

"More," he echoed, almost a laugh, because *more* was the word that had defined eight years of this. More chase. More bite. More marks. More mornings waking up next to a man who matched him bruise for bruise and came back hungry for more.

He dropped his head to the curve of Kit's neck and shoulder — the place he'd already bitten twice — and sealed his mouth over it. Not a bite this time. A *suck*, deep and slow, the kind of mark that wouldn't just bruise but would bloom dark and ugly and *permanent* for days, then shift through every color of healing before it faded. Thursday's mark. The one Kit had asked for.

His hips stuttered, lost the rhythm, found it again. The sound Kit was making — that broken, breathless, *more-more-more* sound — was undoing him faster than he wanted to admit. Bear pulled back from the mark he'd left and looked at it. Dark. Angry. Perfect.

"That one'll still be there next week," he said, his voice barely holding together. He pressed his forehead against Kit's temple, breathing hard, his whole body tight with the effort of holding on when every instinct told him to let go. "You can check. Every morning. In the mirror. Right where I put it."

His hand moved from Kit's throat to the back of his neck, gripping, holding Kit's head tilted exactly where he wanted it. He kissed the mark he'd just made, soft and obscene against the violence of it, and felt Kit shudder beneath him.

Bear was losing the thread. The patience, the control, the deliberate *I'll-make-you-count* composure — it was all fraying, Kit's hands and teeth and the heat of him pulling Bear under like a riptide. He gave up fighting it. Drove forward harder, faster, his forehead pressed against Kit's shoulder, his breath coming in ragged bursts against Kit's skin.

"Keep score all you want," he growled against the marks he'd made, the words broken between thrusts. "I'm not done. I'm not even *close* to done."

And he meant it. The hallway floor was unforgiving and his knees would ache tomorrow and he didn't care — not even a little — because Kit was beneath him saying *always more* and Bear had never once in eight years been a man who ran out of *more* to give.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear heard the words — *don't stop* — and something inside him clicked into place. The competitive edge, the score-keeping, the playful brutality of the chase — it all burned away, leaving behind only the raw, driving need to give Kit exactly what he’d asked for. What he was begging for.

He didn’t stop. Couldn’t. The rhythm he set was relentless, deep, each thrust angled with the precision of eight years of learning this body. His hands were everywhere — gripping Kit’s hips, bracing against the floor, tangling in his hair. He held nothing back.

The sound of it filled the hallway: the ragged duet of their breathing, the soft, obscene slide of skin, the dull thud of Bear’s knees against the hardwood with every snap of his hips. He buried his face in the curve of Kit’s neck, mouthing the marks he’d left, tasting salt and skin and the faint, addictive scent of Kit’s sweat.

He could feel Kit coming apart beneath him — the tightening of muscles, the hitch in his breath, the way his fingers dug into Bear’s back like he was trying to anchor himself. Bear shifted, driving deeper, and Kit’s back arched off the floor with a gasp that was almost a sob.

“That’s it,” Bear muttered against Kit’s throat, the words broken and raw. “Just like that. Take it.”

His own control was threadbare. The fire in his blood wasn’t just desire — it was the need to possess, to mark, to leave an imprint that went deeper than skin. He wanted Kit to feel him for days, wanted the memory of this — the cold floor, the frantic breath, the sound of their bodies — to surface every time he shifted in a chair or pulled on a shirt.

Bear pushed up on his hands, needing to see Kit’s face. He was wrecked — flushed, eyes glassy, lips parted on shallow, desperate breaths. The marks Bear had left were a constellation across his skin, and there was no victory in them now, only a fierce, tender pride.

“Look at me,” Bear commanded, his voice a low rasp.

Kit’s eyes focused on his, and Bear felt the connection arc between them — not just physical, but something older, deeper, forged in years of trust and challenge and nights exactly like this.

He didn’t look away. He held Kit’s gaze as he moved, slow and deep and deliberate, watching every flicker of sensation cross Kit’s face. The way his brow furrowed. The way his teeth sank into his lower lip. The way his breath stuttered when Bear rolled his hips just so.

Bear lowered his head, his mouth hovering just above Kit’s. “I’m right here,” he breathed, the words a vow. “I’m not going anywhere.”

He kissed him then — not the messy, competitive kiss from before, but something slower, deeper, a kiss that tasted like promise and surrender. Kit’s hands came up to frame his face, holding him there, and Bear let himself be held.

The pace quickened again, driven by Kit’s rising urgency. Bear could feel the tension coiling in Kit’s body, the beautiful, inevitable climb toward release. He braced himself, one hand cradling the back of Kit’s head, the other gripping his hip, and gave him everything.

“Let go,” Bear murmured against Kit’s mouth. “I’ve got you.”

And when Kit shattered — a silent, arching cry, his body seizing beneath Bear’s — Bear followed him over the edge, his own release a raw, guttural groan muffled against Kit’s shoulder. He held on through the aftershocks, his body shuddering, his breath coming in ragged gasps that mingled with Kit’s.

For a long moment, there was only the sound of their breathing slowing, the cool air on sweat-damp skin, the distant hum of the refrigerator from the kitchen. Bear didn’t move. He stayed buried deep, his forehead resting against Kit’s, his hand still cradling his head.

“Don’t stop,” Kit had said.

Bear hadn’t. He’d given him everything. And as he lay there, feeling Kit’s heartbeat gradually slow against his own chest, he knew he’d do it again. Tomorrow. Next week. Thursday. Whenever Kit asked.

He pressed a soft, lingering kiss to Kit’s temple, right next to the mark he’d left earlier.

“Score’s settled,” he murmured, his voice rough with exhaustion and something dangerously close to devotion.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I stay there for a minute, my fingers tracing the bite on his shoulder. "Says who?" I finally breathe out, my voice hoarse. "I'm calling it a draw for now." I shift, wincing at the floor and the fresh bruises. "Carry me to the shower. My legs don't work."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear let out a low, rumbling laugh that vibrated against Kit's chest. He pushed himself up onto his elbows, looking down at the flushed, beautifully marked man beneath him. The floor was brutal, and he could feel the ache already settling into his own knees and back.

"A draw," he repeated, his voice still thick and spent. "Convenient, coming from the man who's currently pinned to the floor."

He brushed a damp strand of hair from Kit's forehead, the gesture abruptly gentle. Then, with a grunt of effort that was only half-play-acting, he gathered Kit up. One arm under his knees, the other behind his back. Kit was dead weight, limp and sated, and Bear staggered slightly as he found his footing in the narrow hallway.

"Legs don't work," Bear echoed, starting the slow walk toward the bathroom. "I'd call that a victory, but I'm generous."

He shouldered the bathroom door open, the cool tile a shock after the hallway's warmth. He set Kit down on the closed lid of the toilet, keeping one hand on his shoulder to steady him. Bear's own legs weren't entirely steady, but he'd die before admitting it.

He turned on the shower, adjusting the temperature until steam began to curl into the air. When he turned back, Kit was leaning against the wall, eyes half-closed, that infuriating, satisfied smirk on his lips. Bear's gaze traced the map of marks he'd left—the deep, ugly bruise on Kit's shoulder, the constellations along his ribs, the darker shadows on his hips and thighs.

"Thursday," Bear said, his voice soft. He stepped closer, his thumb brushing over the mark below Kit's ear. "And Friday. And Saturday."

He pulled Kit to his feet, steadying him as he swayed, and guided them both under the hot spray. The water hit his shoulders, washing away the sweat and the faint stickiness of exertion. He turned Kit gently, letting the water run over his back, over the landscape of bruises Bear had created.

His hands were careful now, soaping a washcloth, washing away the evidence of their intensity while preserving the marks beneath. He worked methodically, starting at Kit's neck, moving down his arms, his chest. His touch was proprietary, but also... tender. The aggression of the chase and the bite was spent, leaving behind the quiet, possessive care that always followed.

He pulled Kit back against his chest, wrapping his arms around him, resting his chin on Kit's shoulder. The steam wrapped around them.

"Your turn," he murmured into Kit's ear, handing him the washcloth. "Do your worst. But the shoulder's off-limits. That's mine."

His hands settled on Kit's hips, his thumbs pressing gently into the deep bruises he'd left there. He watched the water sluice over them, knowing they'd ache for days. Perfect.

Kit:
I take the cloth, my fingers brushing his. I start with his back, tracing the scratches I left. "These are mine," I murmur, leaning back against him. "And the bite on your neck. Don't think I forgot."

Bear:
Bear felt the washcloth move over his back, the rough fabric catching on the raised welts Kit's nails had left. He hissed softly, not in pain, but in the sharp, satisfying reminder of it.

"Yours," he agreed, his voice a low rumble against Kit's back. His hands tightened on Kit's hips, pressing into the bruised flesh there. "And these are mine. We're a matched set."

He tilted his head as Kit's fingers brushed the bite mark on his neck, the one that throbbed with his pulse. "That one's going to show," he said, a note of pride in his tone. "Wear it like a badge of honor."

He took the cloth from Kit's hands, rinsed it, and began to wash Kit's front again, his motions slow, deliberate, circling the marks on his chest and ribs. "You know," he said, his voice dropping, "for a draw, you look like you lost a fight with a particularly enthusiastic bear."

He pressed a kiss to the wet skin of Kit's shoulder, right next to the deep bruise. "And I look like I tangled with a feral cat." His thumb traced the scratches down his own side. "I'll take it."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I snort, catching his hand and pressing a kiss to his knuckles. "Feral cat, my ass." I turn in his arms, the water sluicing between us. "You love it."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear looked down at Kit, water streaming between them, Kit's fingers still wrapped around his hand. The steam had turned the bathroom into something soft and private, the world outside reduced to a distant hum.

"Love it," he repeated, and didn't bother denying it. His free hand came up to cup the side of Kit's jaw, his thumb tracing the line of his cheekbone. "You think I'd let anyone else draw blood and live to tell about it?"



The bite on his neck pulsed with every heartbeat. He'd see it tonight, if he remembered to look in the mirror before bed. He'd see it tomorrow morning, and Thursday, and every day until it faded. And then Kit would give him another one.

Bear leaned down and pressed his forehead against Kit's, the hot water beating against his shoulders. His hand slid from Kit's jaw to the back of his neck, holding him there with a grip that was gentle but unmistakable.

"Eight years," he said, quieter now. The teasing edge had softened into something rawer, the way it sometimes did when the adrenaline faded and the steam made everything feel like a confessional. "Eight years and you still make me chase you through this apartment like it's the first time."

His thumb moved in a slow circle at the nape of Kit's neck.

"And you still let me catch you."

He said it like he knew exactly what it meant — that the letting was as much a gift as the catching. That Kit choosing to be cornered, choosing to put his wrists out, choosing to say *don't stop* and *always more* — that was the real thing. The chase was just the language they'd built to say it.

Bear pressed a kiss to Kit's forehead. Then the bridge of his nose. Then the corner of his mouth, lingering there.

"You're keeping that washcloth," he murmured, "because you still owe me my back, and I'm not done holding you to it."

He pulled Kit closer under the water, his arms wrapping around him, solid and warm. The marks on their bodies would ache tomorrow. The floor would leave them both stiff. The shower would run cold eventually.

None of that mattered.

"Draw," he said, tasting the word again, and huffed a quiet laugh against Kit's wet hair. "Fine. Draw. But I get the last bite tonight, and that's non-negotiable."
