dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile looked back over her shoulder, eyes bright with exactly the kind of bad idea she should have outgrown years ago.

“It did last time,” she said, which was not actually reassuring.

At the top of the stairs, she slowed just enough to listen for anyone nearby, then immediately ruined her own attempt at stealth by laughing under her breath.

“Sorry,” she whispered, not sounding sorry at all. “This is stupid.”

She reached the bathroom door, tried the handle, and found it empty. The little victorious expression on her face was wildly disproportionate to the achievement. She slipped inside, flicked on the light, and turned the lock with a soft click.

Then she leaned back against the sink, smoothing both hands down the front of her dress like she was trying to look composed and failing beautifully at it.

“Well,” Odile said, voice low but already threaded with amusement, “it locks.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stupid's my favorite flavor," I say, following you in and pushing the door shut behind me. I catch your eye in the mirror over the sink, my grin matching yours. "So, what's the plan now that we've achieved illegal entry?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s composure lasted until Fen said “illegal entry,” at which point she made a strangled little noise that was supposed to be a quiet laugh and absolutely was not.

She clapped one hand over her own mouth, eyes widening at herself in the mirror.

“Do not make it sound like a crime,” she whispered, though the whisper had too much delight in it to be convincing. “I’ll get distracted.”

She pushed away from the sink and stepped closer, close enough that the music downstairs became more like a pulse through the floorboards than actual sound. Her hands found the front of Fen’s shirt, not tugging yet, just resting there like she was pretending to consider her options.

“The plan,” Odile said, very solemnly, “is that I am going to be extremely graceful and quiet.”

She held the serious expression for maybe half a second before her mouth betrayed her.

“Obviously doomed,” she added.

A board creaked somewhere beyond the door.

Odile froze instantly, one finger lifting to her lips, eyes bright and laughing even while she tried to look scandalized. She listened, breath held, then slowly looked back at Fen with a grin that was much too pleased by the danger of it.

“…Still worth it,” she mouthed, and leaned in.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile had the door hard against her back and still somehow managed to look like this was all part of her very sensible plan.

It was not.

The louder music downstairs made her grin flash wide and wicked for one helpless second before she bit it back, because apparently increased cover had only made the whole thing funnier to her. Her shoulders shook once with a laugh she tried to swallow, and the attempt came out as a soft, ridiculous squeak.

“Oh my god,” she whispered, immediately mortified and delighted with herself. “I am already failing.”

She pressed the back of one hand to her mouth, eyes glittering above it, then dropped it again because that did absolutely nothing to help. The bathroom light was much too bright, the mirror much too honest, and Odile looked entirely too pleased to be trapped between bad judgment and a locked door.

Her fingers tightened in Fen’s shirt, not pulling hard, just enough to betray that all her teasing had stopped being theoretical.

“This is your fault,” she murmured, which was blatantly unfair and delivered with the warm, breathless conviction of someone looking for any excuse at all. “You encouraged me.”

A burst of laughter rose from downstairs, followed by someone shouting along to the song. Odile’s gaze flicked toward the ceiling, then back, and the risk of it hit her visibly—her eyes went wider, her mouth parted, and then she looked like she might laugh again just from nerves.

She leaned her head back against the door with a tiny thump.

“Quiet,” she reminded herself under her breath.

Then, after half a beat, even lower:

“Probably.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I kiss her anyway, swallowing the sound she makes against my mouth.* "Yeah, I encouraged you," I murmur against her lips. "Worst decision I ever made." My hands slide down to her hips, keeping her pinned to the door. "You're terrible at quiet."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile kissed back like she had every intention of arguing and had forgotten the entire concept halfway through.

The accusation made her laugh into the kiss again, small and muffled and completely incriminating. She turned her face just enough to get air, cheeks flushed, eyes narrowed in offended delight.

“I am not terrible,” she whispered.

Then a beat passed.

“I am challenged.”

Her hands slid up from Fen’s shirt to Fen’s shoulders, fingers curling there as if that might help her keep track of herself. It did not. The firm press of the door behind her, the music below, the tiny stupid click of the lock still fresh in her memory—every piece of it seemed to make her worse.

Odile tilted her head back against the door again, smiling like she was trying not to and losing.

“You’re saying that like it isn’t one of my better qualities,” she murmured, voice dropping softer, warmer. “All this suspense. Very character-building.”

A noise passed outside in the hall—footsteps, maybe, or just the old house shifting under too many party guests.

Odile went instantly still.

Her eyes darted to the door. Her lips pressed together hard. For three full seconds, she appeared to be the picture of discipline.

Then her expression cracked.

Not with sound, thankfully, but with the sheer visible effort of not laughing. Her shoulders trembled once. She lifted one hand and covered her mouth, looking scandalized by herself again.

When the hallway stayed quiet, she exhaled through her nose, slow and shaky, and looked back with a grin that was much too pleased.

“See?” she mouthed.

Then, in the tiniest whisper:

“Extremely graceful.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile discovered very quickly that “not enough room” was, inconveniently, one of the funniest things that had ever happened to her.

She bit down on a laugh, failed silently for once, and had to turn her face toward the door with her eyes squeezed shut like she was praying for restraint. She was not praying. She was trying not to make the sort of noise that would get them remembered at every party for the next decade.

Her dress was not where it had been thirty seconds ago. One strap had given up entirely. Her hair had started to come loose. She looked, in the unforgiving bathroom mirror, like the physical embodiment of a bad decision halfway through becoming worse.

“Oh, this is fine,” she whispered, breathless and bright-eyed. “This is completely normal party behavior.”

Something downstairs crashed—probably a cup, hopefully not a person—and a roar of laughter followed it.

Odile froze, then immediately relaxed with visible relief, her mouth curving.

“Excellent,” she murmured. “They’re destroying the kitchen. We’re invisible.”

She said it with absolute confidence and then glanced at the locked door as if it had personally betrayed her before.

The lock sat there. Innocent. Tiny. Not nearly substantial enough.

Odile pressed her lips together, clearly trying to recover some dignity, but dignity had not been invited into this bathroom. Her hands braced behind her against the door, then flexed, then slid uselessly against painted wood as another shaky laugh threatened to escape.

“I need you to understand,” she whispered, solemn and ruined, “that if anyone knocks, I am going to become a ghost. Instantly. No body. No evidence. Just a haunting with excellent shoes.”

A muffled voice passed somewhere in the hallway.

Odile went utterly still.

Her eyes widened.

For once, she managed silence perfectly.

The voice moved on. Footsteps retreated. Downstairs, the music swelled again.

Odile let out the smallest possible breath and looked unbearably pleased with herself, flushed and exhilarated and trying very hard not to grin.

Then she did grin.

“See?” she mouthed.

A beat later, barely audible:

“Graceful.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Graceful and invisible," I whisper back, pulling her closer by her hips. "Your ghost story is missing the part where you shriek like a startled cat."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s offended expression was immediate, absolute, and completely undermined by the way she had to bite her own lip not to laugh.

“I do not shriek,” she whispered, with the fragile dignity of a woman whose evidence had already been destroyed. “I vocalize under pressure.”

The pull closer knocked what little composure she had left out of alignment. Her hands lifted, then hesitated, then settled somewhere that looked like an attempt to steady herself and felt very much like giving up on that effort. Her eyes flicked to the mirror and widened at the state of both of them.

“Oh, we look so guilty,” she breathed.

That set her off again—not loudly, thank god, but enough that her shoulders shook and she had to bury her face for half a second, smothering the laugh against warm skin instead of letting it escape into the hallway like evidence.

Downstairs, the music thudded harder. Someone cheered. The entire house seemed committed to helping and threatening them in equal measure.

Odile lifted her head, flushed and grinning, and tried very seriously to glare.

“Also,” she whispered, “startled cats are very elegant. Terrible comparison.”

A floorboard creaked outside the bathroom.

Odile went rigid.

Her eyes snapped to the door. One hand flew to her mouth. The other clutched uselessly at whatever she could reach, as if physical stillness might somehow make the lock more convincing.

Another step passed. Slower this time.

Odile’s expression transformed from wicked delight to pure, luminous panic.

Then came a lazy knock on the door.

Her soul visibly left her body.

“Um—” she managed, much too high, then immediately clapped both hands over her mouth in horror.

A pause.

From the hall, someone called, muffled, “Bathroom occupied?”

Odile stared at the door like it had asked her for a confession under oath.

Then, with the care of someone defusing a bomb, she leaned just barely toward it.

“Occupied,” she called back, in a voice that was almost normal, if normal meant strangled and suspiciously breathless.

The person outside mumbled something indistinct. Footsteps shifted.

Odile did not breathe.

The footsteps moved away.

For a second, she remained frozen exactly where she was, eyes enormous, lips pressed so tightly together they nearly disappeared.

Then she turned her head very slowly, mortification and triumph warring across her face.

In the tiniest whisper imaginable, she said, “I handled that beautifully.”

A beat passed.

Her mouth twitched.

“Do not laugh,” she warned, already losing the fight herself. “If you laugh, I’m going to laugh, and then we’re both dead.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile lasted, with heroic determination, for about half a minute.

Then her composure snapped into a muffled, helpless sound against Fen’s shoulder—small, sharp, and absolutely not subtle.

She froze immediately after, as if silence might retroactively erase it.

Her eyes flew open.

For one absurd second, she looked offended at herself.

Then she bit down again, harder this time, not enough to hurt on purpose, just enough to give the noise somewhere else to go. Her hands found Fen’s shoulders and gripped tight, fingers curling, knuckles pale.

Downstairs, the song changed. Someone yelled the opening lyrics with drunken enthusiasm. Odile’s expression flashed with wild gratitude.

“Thank god,” she breathed, barely audible, though the words shook at the edges.

The bathroom mirror had become impossible. Every time she caught sight of herself—flushed, disheveled, trying and failing to look like a woman capable of good decisions—her mouth trembled with another laugh she could not afford.

“This is—” she whispered, then stopped because finishing the sentence seemed dangerous.

A tiny, strangled noise escaped anyway.

Odile clapped one hand over her own mouth, eyes huge, and shook her head as if scolding herself.

No.

Absolutely not.

She leaned back against the door, breathing unevenly through her nose, every ounce of her concentration devoted to being quiet and every bit of her expression announcing that she was losing.

Another muffled voice drifted somewhere beyond the hall.

Odile went rigid again.

Her hand stayed over her mouth. Her eyes locked on the door. Her whole body held still with theatrical, catastrophic seriousness.

The voice faded.

No knock came.

For three seconds, she remained frozen.

Then her eyes slid back toward Fen, bright with panic, amusement, and something much warmer underneath both.

Very carefully, she lowered her hand just enough to whisper.

“I regret nothing.”

A beat.

Her mouth twitched.

“Except maybe having lungs.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I can't help but laugh, low and breathless against her ear. "Lungs are overrated anyway." My other hand braces against the door beside her head, careful not to make a sound. "You're doing great, ghost girl."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile made the catastrophic mistake of trying to smile at “ghost girl,” and the smile immediately broke into something much less controlled.

She turned her face hard into Fen’s shoulder again, the laugh and the other sound tangling together until neither one was safe to let loose. Her fingers tightened, then loosened, then tightened again like she had forgotten what hands were for beyond survival.

“Do not—” she whispered, barely managing it. “Do not encourage the haunting.”

Her voice cracked on the last word, and she looked furious about it for half a second before pleasure wiped the expression clean off her face.

The door at her back felt impossibly loud. The light over the mirror buzzed faintly. Downstairs, the party rolled on with blessed indifference, all bass and voices and someone shouting in celebration of absolutely nothing. Odile clung to that noise like a lifeline.

She drew in one shaky breath through her nose.

Then another.

Then immediately ruined the whole effort with a tiny, muffled whine she smothered against skin.

Her eyes snapped open, horrified.

“Sorry,” she mouthed, though she did not look sorry. She looked undone, delighted, and deeply concerned by how much worse she was about to become.

A sudden burst of footsteps pounded up the stairs.

Odile’s entire body locked.

Her mouth pressed shut. Her eyes went enormous. One hand flew out and flattened against the door as if she could physically command the universe to pass them by.

The footsteps reached the landing.

Stopped.

Odile did not breathe.

Someone outside laughed, called something down the hall, and then the footsteps retreated again, careless and merciful.

For a moment, she stayed frozen in place, suspended between panic and relief.

Then her head dropped back against the door with the softest possible thump, and she exhaled in a trembling rush.

“Oh my god,” she whispered. “Oh my god, I hate this.”

A beat.

Her flushed grin returned, helpless and brilliant.

“I love this.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile discovered, immediately and with devastating clarity, that bossing Fen around had consequences.

For about two seconds, she looked triumphant.

Then she looked alarmed.

Then she clapped one hand over her mouth so fast it was honestly impressive.

The noise still escaped around her fingers—muffled, breathless, much too close to a laugh and not close enough to plausible deniability. Her eyes went huge, then squeezed shut, then opened again toward the ceiling as if she were silently negotiating with every god she had ever ignored.

Downstairs, the party roared at exactly the right moment.

Odile’s relief was so visible it was almost funny.

Almost.

“Oh, that was lucky,” she whispered, voice shaking at the edges. “That was—mm—very lucky.”

Her head tipped back against the door, careful this time, no thump, because some part of her brain was still valiantly trying to do damage control while the rest of her had defected completely.

The lock behind her back gave a tiny metallic complaint.

Odile froze.

Her expression said, very clearly: absolutely not.

She reached back blindly, found the lock, and pressed her palm over it like she could personally keep the entire door assembled through force of will.

“No,” she breathed. “No, no, stay there, little hero.”

Another sound got away from her.

She bit it back too late.

Her eyes snapped open.

For one suspended second, she seemed ready to dissolve into embarrassed laughter. Instead, she dragged in a shaky breath and tried to turn it into dignity.

It did not become dignity.

It became a whisper, hot and helpless and utterly betrayed.

“I am going to be so normal after this.”

A beat.

Her mouth trembled.

“That is a lie.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I can't help but laugh, a low huff against her neck.* "You were never normal, Odile." *I keep her pressed against the door, my grip firm on her thigh.* "And you're not starting now."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile tried to look offended.

It was a brave effort, considering she was pinned to a bathroom door at a party, half-dressed, flushed to the roots of her hair, and making a truly heroic attempt not to come apart loudly enough to become local legend.

“I was—” she started.

Her voice failed her.

She shut her eyes, swallowed hard, and tried again in a whisper that had almost no authority left in it.

“I was normal adjacent.”

That was as far as dignity got.

Her laugh broke loose, breathless and helpless, and she buried it fast against Fen’s shoulder, fingers digging in as if she could anchor herself by force. It came out muffled, but not nearly muffled enough, and the sheer danger of that made her shake with another silent burst of laughter immediately afterward.

The lock gave another tiny, traitorous rattle.

Odile’s hand slapped back over it again.

“No,” she hissed at it, scandalized. “Absolutely not. You had one job.”

The absurdity of scolding a bathroom lock nearly finished her. Her mouth pressed tight, her eyes went bright and wet with laughter she could not afford, and she had to tilt her face up toward the ceiling for one desperate second, breathing through it.

From downstairs came a chorus of voices shouting along to the song, gloriously off-key.

Odile’s expression shifted into pure, wicked gratitude.

“Bless them,” she whispered. “Every terrible singer in that room.”

Then the rhythm of the whole situation caught her again—the door at her back, the heat between them, the pressure of keeping quiet and the impossibility of it. Her fingers slid from the lock to the edge of the doorframe, gripping there instead. She bit her lower lip, hard, and still the smallest sound escaped her.

Her eyes snapped open.

She looked mortified.

She looked thrilled.

She looked like she had absolutely no intention of stopping.

“Oh, I am going to blame you for everything,” she whispered, voice thin and shaking. “Everything. The lock. The noises. My complete lack of moral fiber.”

A pause.

Her mouth curved, helpless.

“My excellent taste.”

Another set of footsteps passed somewhere beyond the hall, slower this time.

Odile froze so completely she might have become the ghost she had promised. Her eyes locked on the door. One hand hovered in the air, fingers spread, as if she could hold the entire house in suspense by sheer panic.

The footsteps paused.

Her face went blank with terror.

Then someone outside gave a drunken little laugh and moved on.

Odile did not breathe until the sound faded down the hall.

When it did, she exhaled against Fen’s neck in a trembling rush and immediately had to clamp her mouth shut again, because relief had made her almost worse than fear.

For several seconds, she only clung there, shaking silently, eyes squeezed shut, shoulders rising and falling with uneven breaths.

Then she opened one eye.

Then the other.

Her grin returned slowly, luminous and disastrous.

“I handled that,” she whispered.

A beat.

“Again.”

Her composure lasted exactly long enough for her to sound smug about it, and then another small, helpless noise betrayed her completely.

Odile covered her mouth with one hand and stared at the ceiling like it had personally witnessed her downfall.

“Mmf,” she said, which was not language, but was very sincere.

Then, barely audible through her fingers:

“Still graceful.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The handle dipped.

Odile’s entire face changed.

Every reckless, delighted part of her went incandescent with panic, and still she caught the word before it could become anything louder than a breath.

“Don’t.”

It came out against Fen’s shoulder, barely there, shaking with warning and want in equal measure. Not the door. Not the person outside. Not the danger.

Don’t stop.

The handle jiggled again.

Odile clamped one hand over her own mouth and pressed the other flat to the door beside her head, as if she could hold it shut by scandalized force alone. The lock held with a tiny, heroic click, and her eyes rolled briefly shut in gratitude so intense it was practically religious.

From the hall, someone muttered, “Seriously?”

Odile’s shoulders shook.

Not with laughter this time.

Not only laughter.

She bit down on the heel of her hand, hard enough to make herself focus, and still a broken little sound slipped past it. Her eyes flew open, furious at herself, thrilled beyond reason, and so bright with it that she looked like she might actually haunt the room afterward.

“Occupied,” she called, or tried to.

It was a whisper. It was useless. It was also probably the bravest thing she had ever done.

The person outside tried the handle one more time.

Odile made a tiny strangled noise of disbelief into her palm, then squeezed her eyes shut and nodded once, frantic and helpless, as if agreeing with some private argument she had already lost.

Downstairs, someone screamed the chorus of the song.

Odile silently blessed them again. Every one of them. Saints of bad timing. Angels of terrible pitch.

The footsteps outside lingered.

Odile’s whole body trembled with the effort of staying quiet, and the effort only made it worse. Her breath came unevenly through her nose. Her fingers curled against the painted wood. Her mouth stayed covered, but her expression betrayed everything—panic, laughter, heat, disbelief, the awful glorious knowledge that she was far past the point of pretending she had any self-control left.

The footsteps finally moved away.

She did not relax.

That was the problem.

The moment the danger passed, the tension broke somewhere deeper, and Odile went with it. Her head tipped back against the door, her lips parted behind her hand, and the sound she made was muffled but unmistakably victorious and mortifying and not nearly quiet enough.

Her eyes widened at herself even as it happened.

Then she laughed, breathless and ruined, because apparently there was no dignity left to save.

“Oh no,” she whispered, almost soundless. “Oh, I’m awful.”

Her hand slid from her mouth to clutch at the doorframe again, fingers scrabbling for purchase. She tried to gather herself. Failed. Tried again. Failed worse.

The lock rattled softly behind her.

Odile gasped, then immediately clapped her mouth shut, glaring at the lock like it had developed a personal vendetta.

“Little hero,” she breathed, desperate and affectionate. “Please.”

The music downstairs surged louder, and that was it. That was all the permission her terrible brain needed.

Her composure came apart in pieces: the tense line of her shoulders, the tight bite of her lower lip, the attempt to keep her breathing measured. She buried her face where she could muffle herself, but the laughter came tangled with everything else, helpless and shaky and full of absolute disbelief that this was happening, that they were getting away with it, that she had been the one to suggest it in the first place.

For several seconds, she could do nothing but cling there, trembling hard, one leg still braced where it had no business being in a locked party bathroom, hair slipping loose, dress hopeless, eyes squeezed shut like that might make her invisible after all.

Then the wave passed through her and left her stunned.

Silent.

Mostly.

Her hand stayed over her mouth for insurance. Her chest rose and fell in quick, uneven breaths. Her eyes opened slowly, unfocused at first, then sharpening with the dawning, terrible awareness of the mirror.

She looked at herself.

At the door.

At the lock.

Then back at her reflection.

A laugh threatened immediately.

Odile shook her head once, very small, as if warning her own face not to betray her.

It betrayed her.

She turned her grin into Fen’s shoulder before it could become noise, shoulders shaking again with post-disaster laughter.

When she finally managed words, they came out thin, hoarse, and absurdly pleased.

“I think,” Odile whispered, “we may have lost the moral high ground.”

A beat.

Her eyes flicked toward the door.

Then, softer, with the last scraps of dignity she could gather:

“But I was very brave.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I finally let her leg down and she slides against the door, almost to the floor. I catch her and pull her close, my own breath ragged. "Brave, graceful, and a terrible liar," I murmur, kissing her temple. "But the lock held. Your little hero."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile sagged into the hold like her bones had briefly voted to become decorative.

For a few seconds, she did not trust herself to speak. Her forehead rested against Fen, her eyes shut, her breathing uneven and gradually returning from “fugitive” to merely “compromised.” One hand still clutched uselessly at the doorframe, as if the lock might need emotional support even now.

At “little hero,” her mouth twitched.

Then she laughed.

Not loudly—she had apparently rediscovered survival instincts now that they were no longer immediately useful—but enough that she had to press her face in tighter and shake with it, flushed and boneless and utterly pleased with herself.

“Do not make me emotionally attached to bathroom hardware,” she whispered, voice rough around the edges. “I’m vulnerable.”

She opened one eye and looked toward the lock with solemn gratitude.

“You were magnificent,” she told it, barely audible. “No one will ever know your service.”

Then her gaze drifted to the mirror.

That was a mistake.

Odile stared at the reflection: her hair half-fallen, dress in open rebellion, face bright and ruined with laughter, one strap still making a desperate bid for freedom. Her expression shifted slowly from dazed satisfaction to horrified delight.

“Oh,” she breathed. “Oh, I look like evidence.”

She lifted a hand to fix her hair, stopped halfway, and stared at her own trembling fingers.

A new laugh threatened. She pressed her lips together hard.

“No,” she whispered to herself. “No. Be normal. Become a respectable woman who has simply been washing her hands for ten minutes.”

Her eyes flicked down to the sink.

The sink, which had not been used.

She looked back at the mirror.

“Eleven minutes,” she amended. “Very thorough. Hygiene is important.”

A muffled burst of laughter rose from downstairs again, followed by the bassline thudding through the old floorboards. Odile tilted her head back against the door, careful this time, and let out one shaky, satisfied breath.

Then she glanced toward the hallway and immediately sobered—well, sobered for Odile. Her eyes widened with the delayed awareness that eventually they had to leave the bathroom and rejoin society as if she had not just negotiated spiritually with a door lock.

“We need a plan,” she whispered.

A beat passed.

Her face went blankly serious.

“My plan is currently: fix dress, fix hair, avoid eye contact with anyone waiting for the bathroom, never acknowledge upstairs plumbing again.”

She swallowed, then looked toward Fen with a grin she visibly tried to suppress and absolutely failed to.

“And if anyone asks,” Odile added, very softly, “I had a nosebleed.”

She considered that.

“No. Bad. Too dramatic. I was helping you with—” Her brow furrowed. “No, that’s worse.”

Her hand covered her mouth as another helpless laugh tried to escape.

After a moment, she lowered it, still smiling, still flushed, and braced herself more carefully against the door.

“Okay,” she whispered, gathering the shredded remains of her dignity. “I can do this.”

She looked at the mirror again.

Her expression faltered.

“I cannot do this.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh quietly, catching her by the waist to steady her. "Just fix your hair. I'll block the door until you look less like a crime scene." My fingers gently work to fix the rebellious strap of her dress. "Breathe, ghost girl. We'll walk out like we just had a very serious discussion about plumbing."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile inhaled obediently, then immediately made a face at herself in the mirror.

“Plumbing,” she whispered, as if testing whether the lie would survive contact with reality. “Yes. Very serious. Very damp. Possibly structural.”

She lifted both hands to her hair and paused, staring at the wreckage with the grim focus of a woman assessing storm damage.

“Oh, good,” she murmured. “It’s only obvious from every angle.”

Still, she went to work. Fingers combed through loosened waves, tucking pieces back into place with increasingly desperate precision. One pin had vanished entirely, which she accepted with the solemnity of a battlefield casualty.

“We leave the missing hairpin,” she decided under her breath. “No one goes back for the hairpin. The hairpin knew the risks.”

Her gaze flicked to the mirror again as the dress strap settled back where it belonged, and her mouth softened before she could help it. For one unguarded second, she looked less scandalized and more fond—still flushed, still breathless, but warmed through with the aftermath of the terrible idea they had absolutely survived.

Then the bathroom handle rattled again.

Odile’s soul attempted a second evacuation.

She went still, eyes wide, one hand halfway to her hair.

A voice outside called, “Is someone in there?”

Odile stared at the door.

Then at the mirror.

Then, with the slow horror of remembering she was meant to sound like a normal person, she cleared her throat.

“Yes,” she called, much too politely. “Sorry. One minute.”

A pause.

“Are you okay?”

Odile closed her eyes.

Her expression became one of profound spiritual suffering.

“Fine,” she called back. “Just—plumbing.”

Silence.

Then, from outside, uncertainly: “Uh. Okay.”

Footsteps retreated.

Odile opened her eyes and looked at herself in the mirror with the hollow stare of someone who had just heard her own worst excuse leave her body and could never retrieve it.

After a beat, she whispered, “I panicked.”

Her mouth twitched.

“I said plumbing.”

She pressed both hands over her face, shoulders shaking silently, then dragged them down her cheeks and forced herself upright.

“All right,” she breathed. “New plan. We never return to this house. We move countries. The lock comes with us.”

She turned back to the mirror, pinched color back out of her cheeks as if that were possible, and tried to arrange her face into something calm.

It became smug instead.

“No,” she said softly to her reflection. “Less like that.”

She tried again.

This time she looked deeply guilty.

“Worse.”

A third attempt produced an expression of such exaggerated innocence that she immediately shook her head.

“Oh, absolutely not. That woman has committed tax fraud.”

Finally, she settled on looking slightly warm, mildly amused, and perhaps like someone who had spent too long arguing with a sink. It was not perfect, but it was survivable.

Odile smoothed her dress one last time, checked the rebellious strap, checked the lock with a tiny grateful glance, and lifted her chin.

“Okay,” she whispered. “I am composed. I am dignified. I am a respectable adult woman who has opinions about water pressure.”

Another beat passed.

Her grin broke through again, helpless and bright.

“And if anyone makes eye contact with me, I am going to die.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I smooth down my own shirt, still grinning like an idiot. "If you die, I'm telling everyone you were a ghost this whole time." I give the lock one last pat. "Ready to face the masses, plumber's assistant?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a soft, conspiratorial laugh, her hand sliding down to catch Fen's fingers as they navigated the stairs. The thump of the bass from downstairs grew slightly muffled, replaced by the creak of the wooden steps beneath their feet. 

"I tested it when I came up earlier," she murmured, leaning in close so her breath brushed Fen's neck, her voice laced with a quiet, wicked amusement. "It clicks. And if it doesn't, we'll just have to hold the handle."

She nudged Fen gently ahead of her as they reached the dimly lit upstairs landing, her eyes bright with anticipation. The sheer thrill of sneaking away right under their friends' noses was already making her pulse quicken, and she couldn't entirely suppress the grin spreading across her face. She kept her grip tight on Fen's hand, guiding them toward the door at the end of the hall.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I glance back at her, a smirk tugging at my lips.* "Thorough as ever." *My free hand finds the doorknob, testing it before pushing the door open.* "After you."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile slipped past Fen with a theatrical little bow, her shoulder brushing against theirs as she entered the small, tiled space. The bathroom was illuminated only by the amber glow of a nightlight plugged into the wall, casting long, intimate shadows across the room. 

The moment Fen was inside, Odile pressed the door shut and immediately turned the little brass lock. It engaged with a surprisingly loud, metallic *clack*. 

She winced, though the wide, delighted grin on her face betrayed how little she actually cared. "Oops," she whispered, though her "whisper" was easily loud enough to carry through the thin wood of the door. She leaned her back against the door, her hands finding Fen's hips to pull them closer into her space. "Well, we're officially locked in. No turning back now."

dialogue.name: Fen

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a soft, breathless gasp as her back met the wood of the door, her hands instantly sliding from Fen's hips up to their shoulders to anchor herself. The sudden surge in the bass from downstairs vibrated right through the floorboards and up into her heels, making her laugh—a low, delighted sound that she made absolutely no effort to muffle.

She tilted her chin up, her gaze dropping to Fen's lips with an expression that was half-teasing, half-ravenous. Wrapping her arms fully around Fen's neck, she pulled them down into her space, her fingers tangling in their hair. "Kiss me before someone comes up here looking for the plunger," she murmured against their mouth, her hips shifting forward to press flush against theirs.

dialogue.name: Fen

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a muffled, delighted laugh right against Fen’s mouth, the vibration of it buzzing warmly between them. 

"Is it really?" she whispered—or tried to, her voice still possessing a bright, carry-across-the-hallway quality that she was entirely oblivious to. "God, you're so smart. I knew I kept you around for a reason."

She didn't give them a chance to reply, eagerly stealing another kiss, deeper this time. She tasted like the sweet, fizzy drink she’d been nursing downstairs, but the heat of her mouth was all fire. The contrast of the cold bathroom tiles near her ankles and the burning press of Fen’s body against hers made her shiver, a low, needy hum escaping the back of her throat. 

Her hands slid down from their hair, her fingers tracing the line of their collarbone before slipping eagerly under the hem of their shirt. Her palms were warm against the bare skin of their back, her nails scratching lightly as she arched into them, completely unbothered by the wooden door creaking slightly behind her with the movement. 

"I don't think I want to wait," she murmured, her lips brushing against Fen's jawline as she trailed a path of breathless, damp kisses down to their neck. She nipped lightly at the sensitive skin right below their ear, her hands sliding down to grip the waistband of their pants. "So... what are we going to do about that?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a sharp, breathless laugh as her shirt was discarded, landing somewhere over the edge of the sink with a damp slide. The cramped space made everything a chaotic, desperate scramble of tangled limbs and half-shed fabric, but the sheer friction of it was driving her wild. When she felt the press of Fen's bare skin against hers, she gasped, the sound echoing off the hard tiles.

"Shh, shh," she whispered, mostly to herself, though she immediately followed it with a muffled, vibrating giggle right into the hollow of Fen's collarbone. She was doing a spectacular job of failing to be quiet, her breath coming in fast, shallow gasps that were entirely too loud for a shared house. 

With her jeans pooled half-down her thighs, she was severely restricted, but she didn't care. She hooked one leg around Fen's hip, anchoring herself as best she could in the tight gap between the door and the sink. The cool draft of the bathroom hit her bare back, making her shiver and press herself even tighter against the furnace of Fen's chest. 

"If someone knocks," she murmured, her voice dripping with wicked amusement as she nipped at the column of Fen's throat, "I'm telling them we're conducting a safety inspection. Very thorough. Very hands-on." 

She shifted, her hips tilting up to meet them with a sudden, needy desperation that completely ignored the risk of the squeaky door behind them. Her hands scrambled down to grip Fen's shoulders, her nails digging in as she pulled them closer, absolutely craving the friction.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Safety inspection?" *I manage a choked-off laugh, my voice rough.* "We're failing the noise ordinance." *My hands slide up her bare back, pressing her closer as the bass downstairs seems to thrum in time with my pulse.*

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile threw her head back, letting out a delighted, breathless laugh that she tried—and utterly failed—to muffle by burying her face in the crook of Fen's neck. The vibration of her own voice tickled her throat, and she squeezed her eyes shut as another wave of sheer, giddy excitement washed over her. 

"Oh, hush," she murmured, her lips brushing the warm, salt-sweet skin of their collarbone. "If they wanted a quiet party, they shouldn't have invited us. Besides, it's not my fault you're being so..." She trailed off, letting out a soft, needy gasp as Fen’s hands pressed into her bare back, pulling her flush against them. "...so distracting."

To prove her point, she shifted her weight, trying to find a better angle in the cramped space. The movement caused her bare shoulder blades to slide against the painted wood, and the door let out a loud, rhythmic *creak* that seemed to echo off the bathroom tiles. 

Odile winced, but her eyes flew open, sparkling with wicked amusement. She bit her lower lip, trying to hold back another laugh, but it escaped as a high, fluttering sigh. 

"Okay, maybe the door is a snitch," she whispered—though her voice still carried easily over the hum of the fan. She tangled her fingers in the hair at the nape of Fen's neck, her hips tilting up to meet theirs with a sudden, sharp hunger. The heat of them, combined with the cool draft of the bathroom, was making her dizzy. "But I don't care. Make us fail it, Fen. Seriously. I want everyone downstairs to know exactly what I'm doing to you."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The thirty seconds she managed to stay quiet were a masterclass in desperate self-control. Odile sank her teeth into the meat of Fen’s shoulder, her eyes squeezing shut as the sharp, agonizingly good friction of their hand sent a violent jolt of heat straight to her core. She whimpered against their skin, the sound muffled and vibrating, her fingers clawing frantically into the fabric of their shirt to keep herself anchored. 

But it was a losing battle from the start. 

When Fen shifted their touch, finding a rhythm that made her entire body go taut, the bite dissolved into a helpless, open-mouthed gasp. She let go of their shoulder, her head snapping back against the door with a soft *thud* as a loud, shuddering groan escaped her throat. It echoed beautifully off the tiled walls.

"Oh, *god*," she panted, her "whisper" now entirely devoid of any actual whispering. It was a breathless, raspy sigh that easily cut through the hum of the fan. 

She clung to them, her hooked leg tightening around their hip as she shivered, tilting her pelvis helplessly into the heat of their hand. The sheer, delicious risk of it was making her head spin. Every touch felt magnified, electrified by the knowledge that someone could walk up the stairs at any second. 

"Fen, you're... oh, fuck," she gasped, a giddy, breathless laugh bubbling up in her chest even as she arched her back, the door behind her creaking in loud, rhythmic protest. She brought a hand up to cover her own mouth, her eyes wide and sparkling with a mix of intense pleasure and wicked delight as she looked up at them. "I'm trying! I'm trying to be good, I swear!"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *My other hand comes up to gently pull her hand away from her mouth.* "Don't. I want to hear you." *I keep my rhythm steady, watching her face in the dim amber light as the door continues its rhythmic complaint.*

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
A shuddering gasp tore from Odile's throat the moment her hand was pulled free of her mouth, her fingers instantly curling tight around Fen’s wrist instead. She looked up at them, her chest heaving, her pupils so dilated they nearly swallowed the green of her eyes in the dim amber light. 

"You absolute menace," she panted, though she couldn't stop the dizzy, intoxicated grin that stretched across her face. 

She didn't even try to hold back the next sound—a low, throat-clearing groan that vibrated right against Fen's chest as their fingers kept up that agonizingly perfect, steady rhythm. Her head fell back against the door again with another soft *thump*, her hips tilting hopelessly, desperately, chasing the friction. The door creaked in loud, rhythmic sympathy with her movements, a dead giveaway to anyone who might be standing on the landing, but the sheer, wicked thrill of it only made her wetter.

"Fen—*ah!*" She cut herself off with a sharp, high-pitched cry, her toes curling inside her shoes. She clung to their shoulders, her nails digging in through the fabric of their shirt as she rode the wave of heat pooling rapidly in her lower stomach. 

She leaned forward, burying her face in the crook of Fen's neck, her breath hot and ragged against their skin. "If someone... if someone knocks right now, I'm blaming you," she whispered-moaned, her voice completely shot, trembling with the sheer effort of staying upright as she hovered right on the edge. "I'm telling everyone... exactly what you're doing to me."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The shift in position was sudden and dizzying, and Odile let out a loud, unvarnished cry as her leg was lifted fully over Fen's hip. The sudden, deeper friction of their bodies aligning sent a sharp jolt right up her spine, her back slamming against the door with a very solid, very unmistakable *thump*.

The door didn't just creak now; it rattled in its frame, the brass lock clicking rhythmically in its housing with every movement. 

"Fen—" she gasped, her hands scrambling to find purchase on their shoulders, her nails digging in deep. Any remaining attempt at self-control evaporated instantly. She threw her head back, a breathless, desperate groan spilling from her lips, echoing loudly off the tiled walls and the porcelain sink. 

She was entirely, deliciously loud. She let out a ragged, half-laughing gasp as she rode the wave of the movement, her eyes squeezed shut in sheer, overwhelming pleasure. The contrast of the cool draft in the bathroom and the burning, direct heat of Fen was driving her out of her mind. 

"They're... they're definitely going to hear us," she panted, her voice trembling and entirely devoid of a whisper. She opened her eyes, looking at Fen with a flushed, delirious grin, her gaze heavy and dark with heat. She pulled them down by the neck, desperate to feel their mouth on hers again, her lips sliding damply against their jaw. "I hope... *ah!*... I hope they like the soundtrack."

She arched into them, her hips moving in helpless, frantic sync, completely giving herself over to the noise, the heat, and the beautiful, reckless ruin of it all.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I catch her mouth in a messy kiss, swallowing the next cry.* "Let 'em listen." *The edge of the sink digs into my hip but I barely feel it, focused on the way her body tightens around me, the frantic rhythm of her breathing.*

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile melted into the messy kiss, her lips parting eagerly to swallow the vibration of Fen's voice. The sheer, shameless confidence in those three words—*let 'em listen*—sent a violent spike of heat straight to her core, making her toes curl inside her shoes. 

She wrapped her arms even tighter around Fen's neck, her fingers tangling frantically in their hair as she pulled them down, trying to eliminate every millimeter of space between them. The edge of the sink might have been digging into Fen, but Odile was entirely focused on the friction, the dizzying warmth, and the heavy, rhythmic thrumming of Fen's body against hers. 

The door behind her was practically singing now, the lock rattling in its socket with a frantic, metallic chatter that matched the wild pace of her heart. She didn't care. She leaned into the noise, her body tightening beautifully, helplessly, as she chased the friction. 

"Fen—*oh, god*," she whimpered against their mouth, the words breaking into a breathless, ragged sob of pleasure. 

She was right on the edge, her muscles clenching in tight, desperate waves. She threw her head back, her neck arching as a loud, uninhibited groan tore from her throat, echoing sharply off the tiled walls. A giddy, breathless laugh bubbled up right after it—she couldn't help it, the sheer absurdity of how loud they were being was too delicious—but it was quickly drowned out by a sharp, high-pitched gasp as she tilted her hips up, begging for the final, crashing wave. 

"Don't stop," she panted, her eyes half-closed and glazed with heat as she stared up at them, her hands gripping their shoulders like a lifeline. "Fen, please—right there—"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The brass doorknob suddenly jiggled, a sharp, heavy *clack-clack* of metal as someone on the other side tried to turn it, only to be stopped by the lock. 

Odile’s eyes went instantly wide, a sharp, choked gasp catching in her throat. Her entire body went rigid for a split second, her heart hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird. But instead of pulling back, instead of freezing in panic, her grip on Fen's shoulders tightened until her knuckles turned white. The sheer, terrifying thrill of it—the knowledge that someone was standing mere inches away, separated from them by nothing but a thin piece of painted wood—sent a violent, electric shock of pure adrenaline straight to her core. 

"Don't," she gasped out, the word a frantic, breathless command whispered directly into the hollow of Fen's throat. She tilted her pelvis up, her body practically begging for the friction, her voice shaking with a desperate, heavy heat. "Don't stop."

She didn't care who it was. She didn't care if they heard. If anything, the muffled sound of a frustrated sigh from the hallway only pushed her over the absolute edge. 

When Fen kept going, relentless and unbothered, Odile lost every single ounce of her remaining control. She threw her head back against the door, the wood rattling violently in its frame as she met them stroke for stroke. A loud, shuddering cry tore from her throat, completely un-muffled, echoing sharply off the cold bathroom tiles. She bit down hard on her own lower lip, her eyes squeezing shut as the tension that had been building all night finally, beautifully snapped. 

The climax hit her in a sudden, blinding wave of heat that made her entire body convulse. She clung to Fen like a drowning woman, her leg hooking even tighter around their hip as she rode the intense, rolling waves of release. She was sobbing for breath, her chest heaving against theirs, a series of weak, needy whimpers escaping her with every ragged exhale. 

On the other side of the door, the heavy, retreating thud of footsteps signaled that whoever had wanted the bathroom had finally given up and walked away. 

Odile let out a weak, breathless, completely hysterical little giggle, her forehead dropping heavily onto Fen's shoulder. She was trembling from head to toe, her skin flushed and slick with sweat, but the grin on her face was absolutely triumphant. 

"Oh my god," she wheezed against their neck, her voice completely shot, vibrating with a dizzy, post-coital giddiness. "We are... we are never being invited back here again."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I let out a shaky breath, my forehead resting against the door next to her head.* "Worth it." *I can feel her heart still hammering against my chest, and I don't move yet, just holding her up as we both try to catch our breath.*

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out another weak, shuddering laugh, her shoulders shaking against Fen's chest. She slowly let her hooked leg slide down, though her knees felt so much like warm wax she had to rely entirely on Fen's strong grip around her waist to keep from slipping straight to the bathmat. 

"Extremely worth it," she agreed, her voice a raspy, warm murmur against their collarbone. She nuzzled her face into the crook of their neck, inhaling the sharp, comforting scent of their skin mixed with the cool, damp air of the bathroom. 

She tilted her head back just enough to look up at Fen, her eyes still heavy-lidded but bright with a lingering, post-coital spark. Her hair was a wild, static-charged mess, and her cheeks were flushed a deep, brilliant pink. 

"Did you hear them sigh?" she whispered—though, true to form, it was a stage whisper that would have easily carried to the landing if the disappointed guest had lingered. She grinned, a hopelessly fond, wicked thing. "The sheer, tragic disappointment of a locked door. I almost feel bad. *Almost*."

She reached up, her fingers idly tracing the line of Fen's jaw, her thumb brushing over the damp skin of their cheek. "Though, to be fair, if they couldn't figure out what was happening in here with the door practically vibrating off its hinges, they have bigger problems." 

She giggled, the sound rich and happy, before leaning up to press a soft, lingering kiss to the corner of Fen's mouth. Her body was still humming, the aftershocks of the orgasm making her muscles twitch pleasantly as she leaned her full weight against them. 

"You were incredible," she murmured, her eyes softening as she looked at them. "Even if you did completely ruin my reputation as a respectable houseguest. How are we ever going to go back downstairs?"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I finally pull back enough to look at her, a slow, satisfied smirk spreading across my face.* "We'll just have to sneak back in looking suitably disheveled and smug." *I reach down to scoop her discarded shirt off the sink edge, handing it to her.* "Think anyone's counting minutes?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile took the shirt from Fen’s hand, letting out a dramatic, theater-worthy sigh as she looked down at the crumpled fabric. 

"Counting minutes?" she whispered, her voice still raspy and entirely too loud for the small space. She shook the shirt out, though it did little to help the wrinkles. "Darling, they weren't counting minutes. They were counting decibels. And I'm pretty sure we broke a record."

She pulled the shirt over her head, her head popping through the collar with her hair sticking up in a wild, static-haloed mess. She didn't even try to smooth it down, instead leaning forward to peer at her reflection in the small mirror above the sink. Her cheeks were flushed a bright, telltale pink, her lips slightly swollen, and her collarbone bore the faint, darkening mark of where Fen had bitten her. 

She let out a delighted, utterly unbothered laugh at her own reflection. 

"Oh, yes. Highly respectable," she murmured, turning back to Fen with her hands on her hips, her jeans still unbuttoned and hanging loose. "We look like we just survived a minor natural disaster. Which, technically, we did."

She stepped closer, her hands reaching out to smooth down the collar of Fen's shirt, her fingers lingering against their warm skin. She looked up at them, her eyes crinkling at the corners with absolute adoration and mischief. 

"If anyone asks, we were having a very heated, very intellectual debate about... politics. Or the economy," she proposed, her lips twitching. "That perfectly explains why I lost my voice, why my hair looks like a bird's nest, and why you look so incredibly pleased with yourself."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: *I snort, buttoning my own jeans with one hand.* "Intellectual debate my ass. They heard the door." *I run a hand through my hair, trying to tame it somewhat.* "C'mon. Let's go get a drink before they send a search party."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile caught up to him on the landing, grabbing the back of his shirt and tugging him toward the right door. "Improvising," she repeated, low enough that it barely carried under the bass thumping through the floorboards. "Is that what we're calling it."

The lock clicked when she turned it — small mercy — and she pulled Fen inside after her, easing the door shut with her shoulder. The bathroom was dim, lit mostly by the streetlight filtering through a frosted window, and it smelled faintly of someone else's perfume and the lemon cleaner the host probably kept under the sink.

She leaned back against the door, looking up at him with that grin still firmly in place, fingers already working at the hem of her dress.

"Thirty seconds before someone notices we're gone," she murmured. "Maybe a minute if Marcus is telling that story again."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a breath that was half laugh, half something else entirely, when the music swelled downstairs. "Perfect," she breathed, tilting her head back against the door. Her fingers found the buttons on his shirt — or maybe his belt, she'd lost track of her own ambition somewhere between the landing and here — and she worked them with the kind of focused efficiency that suggested she'd been thinking about this longer than the last four seconds.

Her grin faltered for exactly half a second when his mouth found her neck, replaced by something softer and considerably less composed. She pressed closer, the door cool against her back through the thin fabric of her dress, and one of her hands came up to fist in the front of his shirt, pulling him in like she was afraid the music might stop.

"Also," she managed, voice thinner than intended, "if you make me laugh I swear to god, Fen —"

She didn't finish the threat, because it turned into a sound she'd be embarrassed about later, muffled against his shoulder. The bass from downstairs thrummed through the wall at her back, conveniently covering exactly the kind of evidence they'd be leaving behind.

dialogue.content: I chuckle low against her skin, my hands sliding up her sides. "Wouldn't dream of it," I murmur, catching her mouth with mine.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile made a sound into the kiss that she would absolutely deny making later — something between a hum and a word that didn't quite form, swallowed before it could become incriminating. Her fingers tightened in his shirt, dragging him closer by a fistful of fabric, and she kissed him back like she was trying to win something, which she probably was.

The music shifted downstairs — something slower, heavier — and she registered it the way you register the ticking of a clock in a room you're trying to burgle. Present, but ignorable. Mostly.

"You," she managed, when they broke apart just far enough for air, "are a terrible influence." Her voice had gone rough at the edges, which was annoying. She ran her thumb along his jaw, feeling the stubble there, and grinned up at him — still grinning, even now, because she couldn't seem to stop. "I was a very well-behaved person before I met you."

From somewhere below and to the left, a burst of laughter — someone reacting to Marcus's story, presumably — and Odile's eyes flicked toward the door on reflex before sliding back to Fen, dark and a little breathless.

"Clock's ticking," she murmured, and pulled him back in.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile pressed her palm flat against the door behind her — a habit, she supposed, of confirming the thing was still closed — and bit down on her lower lip hard enough to hurt. The bathroom was too small for this, or maybe it was exactly the right size, which was a thought she was going to unpack later when she could think in complete sentences.

She was not, she realized with distant annoyance, as quiet as she'd planned to be. A small sound escaped her when his mouth found the spot just below her ear, and she covered it with the back of her hand, grinning against her own knuckles like an idiot.

"That's — " she started, voice pitched low enough to be plausibly deniable as a cough, " — not fair."

The laughter from downstairs swelled again, and for one horrible second she thought she heard footsteps on the stairs. She froze, hand tightening on Fen's shoulder, ears straining through the music. Nothing. Just someone crossing the hallway, probably, or the house settling. She exhaled shakily and let her head fall back against the door with a soft thunk.

"You know," she whispered, and her voice had gone unsteady in a way she was choosing to blame on the circumstances rather than on him, "if we get caught, I'm blaming you entirely. I was downstairs having a perfectly normal conversation about — someone's new job, or something. I was being *charming.*"

Her fingers curled into his hair, pulling him closer even as her words suggested she might push him away. The contradiction didn't bother her. It never did, with him.

"And if you make me — " she started again, and then didn't finish, because she'd already lost that particular battle twice tonight and a third loss seemed statistically inevitable. She pressed her forehead against his shoulder instead, breathing hard, and laughed — quiet, helpless, a little wild — into the fabric of his shirt.

"God," she managed. "We are the worst people."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Worst people at this party, maybe," I breathe out, my own laugh muffled in the crook of her neck. My fingers find the zip of her dress, tug it down just enough. "But I’d argue we’re the best at this."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed — actually laughed, low and warm against his collarbone — at the sheer audacity of that line. "The *best* at this," she repeated, and the way her voice cracked on the second word had nothing to do with laughter and everything to do with the way his fingers had found skin at the small of her back, where the zipper had given up its duties. "In a stranger's bathroom. With Marcus's story as a soundtrack."

She pulled back just enough to look at him, and her eyes had gone dark in the half-light from the window, pupils blown wide, hair starting to escape whatever had been holding it in place an hour ago. She looked, she suspected, like someone who had been making out in a bathroom at a party, which was because that was exactly what was happening.

"You know what, fine," she murmured, tilting her chin up, fingers tracing down the line of his throat, feeling his pulse jump under her fingertips. "Prove it."

The word landed somewhere between a dare and an invitation, and she watched his expression shift in the dim light — watched him decide to take it seriously, which was always her favorite version of him — and her grin softened into something less performative and considerably more dangerous.

Somewhere downstairs, a glass broke. Odile flinched, then relaxed into a breathless little exhale as the moment passed, the sounds of someone laughing it off filtering up through the floorboards.

"See," she whispered, sliding her hands up under the collar of his shirt, palms flat against his chest, "this is why I can't take you anywhere. You make me — " She bit the inside of her cheek, hard, and the sentence dissolved into a sharp inhale. " — you make me forget to be careful."

Her back arched off the door when he finally got the dress out of the way properly, and the cool air on her skin made her shiver, or maybe that wasn't the air. Her head tipped back, throat exposed, and she pressed her lips together in a line that was doing absolutely nothing to muffle the soft, involuntary sound that followed.

"Oh, *fuck*," she whispered, very quietly, and then immediately looked mortified with herself. "I said that too loud."

She hadn't, probably. The music was still thumping. But her cheeks had gone warm, and she tugged him closer by the front of his shirt, burying her face against his neck like she could hide the evidence there.

"You didn't hear that," she mumbled into his skin. "That was a cough. I'm coming down with something."

dialogue.name: Fen
