dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile lasted approximately twenty-eight seconds before the bite became something else entirely — a gasp muffled against his shoulder, her hips pressing forward into his hand with a desperation she was going to blame on the circumstances later. Her fingers had a death grip on the back of his shirt, knuckles white, and her forehead was still pressed to his neck like she could physically hold herself together through sheer force of will.

It wasn't working.

"Thirty seconds," she managed, barely a whisper, the words hot and damp against his skin. "That was — that was your estimate. You're — " A sharp inhale cut her off, and her teeth found his shoulder again, harder this time, which was the only thing stopping the sound that wanted to follow.

The music downstairs had shifted again — something with a heavier beat, bass thrumming through the floorboards under her bare feet — and she was absurdly grateful for it in a way she'd never be grateful for Marcus's music taste under normal circumstances. Her free hand came up to cover her own mouth, fingers pressed hard against her lips, which helped approximately as much as biting his shoulder had.

It didn't help at all.

She turned her face slightly, cheek pressed to his collar, and laughed — breathless, shaky, entirely involuntary — at the absurdity of it. Two grown adults. A locked bathroom door. Her underwear somewhere on the tile floor, which she was absolutely not thinking about right now.

"This is your fault," she whispered, the words coming out uneven, punctuated by the motion of his hand and the increasingly thin thread of her composure. "Entirely. Completely. I'm going to — I'm going to write it in my diary. 'Got felt up in a bathroom by a man with no respect for — ' "

She lost the sentence. Lost the thread entirely. Her back pressed harder against the door, hips rolling forward, and the sound she made against her own palm was muffled but not nearly muffled enough. Her eyes squeezed shut, and she could feel her pulse everywhere — in her throat, in her wrists, in the place where his fingers were doing that thing she was never going to be able to look him in the eye about later.

Downstairs, someone turned the music up again — a mercy she was going to send the universe a thank-you note for — and she took her hand off her mouth just long enough to drag him into a kiss that was more teeth than technique, swallowing whatever sound was trying to escape before it could betray them both.

When she broke away, her breathing was ragged and her pupils were blown wide in the dim light, and she looked at him with an expression caught somewhere between mortified and exhilarated.

"Twenty-eight seconds," she repeated, voice wrecked. "You owe me a new estimate."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I grin, breathless against her mouth. "Okay, new estimate." My voice is rough, matching hers. "Maybe we've got 'til someone runs out of ice."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's laugh came out cracked and breathless against his mouth, the kind of sound that had no business being as attractive as it was. "'Til someone runs out of ice," she repeated, and the fact that she could still form sentences at all felt like a minor miracle. "That's — that's generous of you. Very optimistic. I like that about you."

Her fingers had found his belt buckle at some point — she didn't remember deciding to do that, which was probably telling — and she was working it with the kind of single-minded focus that suggested her brain had triaged everything non-essential and discarded it. Speech. Volume control. The location of her missing underwear. All gone. Only this remained.

"Okay," she breathed, tilting her head back against the door, eyes half-lidded, watching him through her lashes with an expression that was doing very little to disguise how affected she was. "New terms. New estimate. I'm holding you to it."

She pulled him closer by the loosened belt, grinning — still grinning, god, she was never going to stop grinning — and pressed her mouth to the corner of his jaw, trailing lower along his throat. Her lips parted against his pulse point, and she felt it jump under her tongue, which was deeply, unfairly satisfying.

"For the record," she murmured against his skin, the words vibrating there, "if someone *does* run out of ice, I am climbing out that window and I am never speaking to you again." A pause. Her teeth grazed his collarbone, light, teasing. "I'm also keeping all of your records and your good hoodie, so. Consider that a hostage situation."

From downstairs, the muffled sound of someone opening the freezer — just the hinges, nothing more — made her freeze against him for a full second before she registered that no one was coming upstairs. She exhaled against his throat, a shaky laugh puffing out of her.

"I take it back," she whispered. "I'm not waiting for the ice. I'm not waiting for anything. I want — "

She stopped herself, cheeks going hot in the dark, and pressed her forehead to his shoulder instead of finishing the sentence. Her hands were still on his belt. Her dress was still half-zipped. Her dignity was somewhere on the tile floor next to her underwear, and she suspected it wasn't coming back.

"Just — " she started again, quieter, rougher, " — keep going. Please. And if Marcus knocks on that door, I'm pushing you out the window first."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's mouth opened on a sound she had absolutely no intention of making — something sharp and involuntary that she managed to swallow at the last second by biting down on the heel of her own hand, teeth leaving indentations in her skin. It didn't work. The next one escaped anyway, muffled but present, and her eyes flew open in the dark, wide and mortified and somehow still bright with something that wasn't embarrassment at all.

The new angle was — a lot. The door rattled faintly behind her when her shoulders pressed back against it, and she registered that distantly, the way you register a problem you're not going to solve right now. Her fingers had found his hair again, twisting in it hard enough to pull, and her other hand — the one she'd been using to cover her mouth — dropped to his shoulder instead, gripping, because she needed somewhere to put it and her mouth was otherwise occupied trying not to make noise.

She failed again immediately.

"Oh my god," she breathed, the words punched out of her, barely a whisper and not nearly quiet enough. Her head tipped back against the door, throat exposed, and she laughed — short, breathless, a little unhinged — at the ceiling. "Oh my *god*, Fen — "

She couldn't finish. Her teeth found his shoulder again, harder than before, and this time she didn't let go, just held on while her composure came apart in pieces. The music downstairs was thrumming through the floorboards, through the door at her back, through her, and she was grateful for it in a way that bordered on religious, but it wasn't enough — it was never going to be enough to cover the sounds she was making into his shirt, the small desperate noises that kept escaping between her clenched teeth.

Her leg tightened over his hip, drawing him closer, and the movement shifted everything again, and she made a sound against his shoulder that was absolutely not a cough. Her free hand came up to cover her own mouth this time, palm pressed flat, fingers trembling slightly, and she breathed hard through her nose while her body did its best to betray her.

Through the door — through the music, through the floor — she could hear voices. Laughter. The clink of glasses. Someone saying Marcus's name. Normal party sounds, distant and irrelevant, except that they weren't, they were *right there*, and every time someone laughed she tensed against him and every time she tensed against him it made everything worse in the best possible way.

She pulled her hand away from her mouth just long enough to gasp, "The — the window — I was *joking* about the window — " and then lost the rest of it to a sound she buried against his neck, her forehead pressed hard to his pulse point, feeling it hammer under her skin.

She was not going to be quiet. She'd accepted that. What she hadn't accepted — what she was only just now realizing with a hot, crawling awareness — was how much she didn't care. The lock on the door was flimsy. The music wasn't that loud. Anyone walking past in the hallway would hear. And Fen had stopped being careful, which meant he'd decided he didn't care either, and the two of them together not caring was doing something catastrophic to her higher brain functions.

"*Fen* — " she said, his name coming out wrecked and low, half-plea and half-warn-off, and her fingers curled into the fabric at his shoulders and *pulled*, because she didn't know what she wanted except more of whatever was happening right now, consequences be damned, ice supply be damned, Marcus and his story and every guest in this house be damned.

Her back arched off the door again, and this time the sound that escaped her wasn't small at all.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I grin against her shoulder, my own breathing ragged. "Let 'em hear," I murmur, voice low and rough. The door rattles again and I don't give a damn. "Worst-case scenario, we give Marcus a better story to tell."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed against his neck — a real laugh, helpless and slightly unhinged, vibrating through her chest and into his collarbone. She couldn't help it. The image of Marcus's face if he actually opened that door was doing more for her than it had any right to, layered on top of everything else that was already doing too much for her.

"Marcus," she managed, the word splintering halfway through, "is going to have — *so many questions* — about the — "

She lost it. Not the sentence — the thread entirely. Whatever he did next short-circuited the part of her brain responsible for coherent speech, and the sound that came out of her was not quiet. It wasn't meant to be quiet anymore. She'd surrendered that particular battle somewhere around the twenty-eight-second mark and hadn't looked back.

Her hand came up to her mouth on reflex — old habit, useless now — and she pressed her palm flat against her lips just long enough to feel herself shaking against it before she let her hand drop away. What was the point. What was the actual point. The door was rattling faintly in its frame every time her shoulders hit it, the lock doing its best but not designed for this, and somewhere below them a party was continuing as if two people weren't actively falling apart in a bathroom twelve feet away.

"*Oh* — " The syllable escaped her, high and sharp, and she didn't bother pretending it was a cough this time. Her forehead was still pressed to his shoulder, her breath coming in hot, uneven bursts against his skin, and she could feel his pulse under her lips where they'd found the side of his throat — fast, matching hers, which was something she was going to think about later when thinking was an option.

Her leg tightened over his hip, pulling him closer, and the sound she made when the angle shifted was muffled only by the fact that her teeth had found his shoulder again. She wasn't biting down this time. Just resting there, lips parted against the fabric of his shirt, breathing him in while her composure continued its steady, irreversible collapse.

"For the record," she gasped, and her voice was barely a whisper and not nearly a whisper at the same time — wrecked, breathless, threaded through with something that was definitely laughter even now, " — if Marcus — if he *actually* — oh god, *Fen* — "

She couldn't finish. Her fingers curled into his hair and pulled, hard, and the next sound that escaped her was pressed into his skin, half-swallowed, half-given-up-on, and she didn't care. She'd stopped caring. The music downstairs was loud enough to cover most of it but not all of it, and she could hear her own voice bouncing off the tile floor and the frosted window and coming back to her, foreign and raw, and even that wasn't enough to make her stop.

Her back arched off the door — the whole door rattled this time, a sound that would absolutely carry through the hallway — and she pressed her hand flat against it behind her, steadying, grounding, as if that could undo what had just happened to the lock. It couldn't. The door had given up its pretense of security somewhere in the last thirty seconds and they both knew it.

She pulled back just enough to look at him, and her face was flushed, her pupils blown so wide the dark of her eyes had almost swallowed the color, her hair a complete disaster, her mouth swollen and parted. She looked, she thought distantly, like someone who'd stopped pretending a long time ago.

"New estimate," she breathed, and her voice cracked on the word in a way that would've been embarrassing if she'd had any embarrassment left. Her thumb traced his lower lip, and her grin came back — softer now, less performative, more *wrecked*. "I think we've got about — " A sharp inhale. Her eyes fluttered shut. " — oh, *fuck*, I lost count — "

She pulled him back in before she could finish, one hand fisted in his shirt, the other sliding up the back of his neck, and kissed him like the door wasn't a problem, like the party wasn't twelve feet away, like the only thing in the world that mattered was the taste of him and the sound he made when she bit his lower lip and the way his hands felt like they were the only solid thing left in a room that had started spinning approximately three minutes ago.

Somewhere below, a burst of applause — Marcus had finished his story, apparently — and Odile laughed into the kiss, breathless and wild and entirely, irreversibly gone.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The handle jiggled — once, twice — and Odile's breath caught on something that was almost a laugh and almost a moan and entirely, unmistakably neither.

"Don't," she said, and the word came out low and wrecked and meant the opposite of what it sounded like it meant, and she tightened her leg over his hip and pulled him closer instead of letting go, instead of stopping, instead of doing any of the sensible things that the rattling doorknob was loudly suggesting she do.

"Occupied," she called out, voice pitched to carry, and it cracked on the second syllable in a way that absolutely did not sound casual, and whoever was on the other side of the door hesitated — she could hear them hesitate, the soft shuffle of feet on the hallway floor — and then walked away. The footsteps receded toward the stairs. Someone murmured something. A door closed somewhere below.

Odile exhaled a laugh that was half-terror, half-delirium, and pressed her forehead hard against Fen's shoulder.

"Occupied," she repeated, quieter now, just for him, the word muffled against his shirt. "That was — that was my one good line and I *ruined* it. I sounded like — " A sharp inhale cut her off, her fingers curling into the back of his neck. " — I sounded like someone who was *definitely* occupied, which — "

She didn't finish, because whatever he did next made the sentence irrelevant, made everything irrelevant except the place where they were joined and the sound of her own breathing coming apart in the dark bathroom. Her hand slid up into his hair and held on, and her hips rolled forward, and the small, desperate sound that followed was pressed into his collarbone like she could push it through his skin instead of letting it out into the air.

The door was still rattling faintly every time her shoulders hit it. She could feel it — the give of it, the way the lock had stopped pretending to be a lock somewhere in the last minute. Anyone who tried that handle again would get it open. Anyone walking past in the hallway would hear. The music downstairs was still thumping but it had developed a gap between tracks, a few seconds of near-silence that made every other sound in the house suddenly, horrifyingly audible.

She didn't stop.

Her back arched off the door and the next sound out of her was not small and not muffled and not anything she could plausibly call a cough. It bounced off the tile floor and the frosted window and came back to her, and she heard herself hearing it, and the flush that crawled down her throat and across her chest was equal parts mortification and something much, much worse — the sharp, dizzying awareness that she didn't care, that she'd *chosen* not to care, that Fen had said *let them hear* and she'd agreed without saying so and meant it.

"Oh god," she breathed, and the words were barely words anymore, just shapes her mouth was making around the breath she couldn't catch. "Oh god, Fen, I can't — "

She could. That was the problem. She absolutely could, and the angle was exactly right, and his hands were exactly where she needed them, and every time she thought she had a handle on the sounds trying to escape her throat another one broke loose and she had to bury her face against him to swallow it, which worked for about half a second before the next one came.

Her fingers had a death grip on his shoulders now, knuckles white, and she could feel herself shaking — not from cold, not from fear, from the effort of holding herself together when her body had decided, very firmly, that it was done being held together. Her pulse was everywhere. In her wrists. In her throat. Behind her eyes. Low in her belly, coiling tighter with every movement, every shift of his hips, every place where skin met skin in the narrow dark of the bathroom.

The next track started downstairs — something heavy, bass-driven, a mercy she sent up a silent prayer for — and she took advantage of the cover to let out a breath she'd been holding for what felt like a minute. Her forehead was still pressed to his shoulder, her lips moving against his shirt, forming words she couldn't quite get out.

"I — " she started, and her voice cracked. "I need — "

She didn't finish. She pulled back instead, just far enough to look at him, and her face was a ruin in the half-light — flushed, pupils blown, mouth open, hair plastered to her temples with sweat. She looked at him the way she'd looked at him at the bottom of the stairs forty-five seconds and a lifetime ago, except now the grin was gone and what was left underneath it was raw and wanting and completely undefended.

"*Please*," she said, and the word came out like it had been dragged out of her, low and desperate and not at all the kind of word she ever said out loud, and her hand came up to cup his jaw, thumb tracing his cheekbone, and her eyes were bright and dark and entirely focused on him. "Please, I — I can't — "

Her back hit the door again and the lock gave up entirely this time, the door swinging open a half-inch before catching on the chain — the *chain*, the one she hadn't noticed, the one that had saved them — and she didn't stop, couldn't stop, wouldn't have stopped if the door had swung open all the way and Marcus himself had been standing there with a fresh drink and a question about the hors d'oeuvres.

Her hips moved and the angle shifted and the sound that came out of her was loud enough that the chain rattled in sympathy, and she pressed her hand over her own mouth again but it was too late, it had already escaped, and she could hear it echoing off the tile and the window and coming back to her, and the flush that burned across her skin was incandescent.

"*Fen* — " she said against her palm, his name coming out broken in half, and her leg tightened over his hip and her fingers curled into his hair and she pulled, hard, and the next sound was muffled only by the fact that she'd buried her face in his neck and was breathing him in like oxygen, like he was the only solid thing left in a room that had stopped existing approximately two minutes ago.

The coil in her belly was wound so tight it ached. She could feel it — every muscle in her body drawn taut, her jaw clenched, her toes curling against the tile floor where she'd lost one shoe and couldn't remember when. She was so close it was almost worse than not being close at all, this suspended, trembling moment where everything was held in her throat and behind her teeth and she couldn't — she *couldn't* —

"Come on," she gasped into his neck, the words hot and damp and desperate, "come *on*, I — "

And then whatever he did — the angle, the pressure, the way his mouth found the spot below her ear at the exact right moment — broke the last thread she'd been holding onto, and the sound that came out of her was not quiet and not muffled and not anything she could take back. It tore out of her like something uncaged, raw and ragged and half-laughed, and her whole body arched against the door and the chain rattled and she pressed her face into his shoulder and *sobbed* once, breathlessly, her fingers twisted so tight in his shirt she was going to tear the fabric.

She came apart in pieces. Her hips stilled, then jerked, then stilled again. Her breath came in short, sharp bursts against his neck, each one a small, helpless sound she couldn't have stopped if she'd tried. Her leg trembled over his hip and her fingers loosened in his hair and then tightened again, holding on, holding *him*, as if he were the only thing keeping her upright, which at this point he was, because her knees had stopped working approximately four seconds ago.

The bathroom was very quiet when it was over. The music downstairs thudded on, indifferent. The chain swung gently in the doorway. Odile breathed against Fen's shoulder, ragged and slow, her whole body loose and trembling and boneless, and she laughed once into his collarbone — a small, wrecked, helpless sound — and pressed her lips to the side of his throat without quite meaning to.

"Oh," she said, very quietly, into his skin. Just that. Just *oh*, as if she'd run out of all the other words.

She stayed there for a moment — forehead to his shoulder, breath evening out, pulse still hammering visibly at her throat — and then she pulled back, just enough to look at him. Her face was flushed, her hair a disaster, her lipstick somewhere in the vicinity of her chin. She looked, she suspected, like a woman who had just been comprehensively undone in a stranger's bathroom, which was because that was exactly what had happened.

"Well," she managed, and her voice was hoarse and cracked and threaded through with something that was definitely, impossibly, still laughter. She reached up and tucked a piece of hair behind her own ear, which did nothing to fix the general state of things. "Marcus is going to have to top that story at the next party."

She was still catching her breath. Her fingers were still trembling where they rested on his shoulders. The chain was still swinging faintly in the open half-inch of doorway, letting in a thin blade of hallway light, and she could hear the party continuing below as if nothing had happened, which it hadn't, except that everything had, and she was going to have to go back downstairs in approximately ninety seconds and make eye contact with people and drink water and act like a person who had not just made sounds that were probably audible from the landing.

She looked at him. Grinned. Still grinning. Always grinning.

"Your turn," she said, rough and low, and her thumb traced his lower lip, and her eyes were dark and steady and entirely, wickedly focused. "Clock's ticking. And I believe you owe me a new estimate."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my forehead resting against hers. "Estimate's shot," I murmur, my voice still rough. "But I'm thinking... we've got until someone notices the door's chained from the inside."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's laugh came out cracked and breathless, her forehead still pressed to his.

"Chained from the inside," she repeated, and the words came out somewhere between a wheeze and a giggle, her voice still hoarse and shot. "That's — that's a very specific vulnerability. Very *visible* vulnerability. I hadn't thought about that."

She had, actually. She'd thought about it approximately three seconds after it happened, which was when the adrenaline had hit and she'd realized that the thin blade of hallway light spilling through the gap meant anyone walking past could see the chain hanging loose and put two and two together. She'd chosen not to care. She was choosing to continue not caring. This was becoming a pattern.

Her fingers were still trembling where they rested on his shoulders, and she flexed them once, experimentally, feeling the ache in her knuckles from how hard she'd been gripping him. Her whole body felt like it had been wrung out and hung up to dry — loose, warm, pleasantly wrecked in a way she was going to feel in her knees tomorrow. She was still catching her breath, each inhale a little ragged at the edges, and she could feel her pulse hammering visibly at her throat where his forehead rested against hers.

She pulled back just enough to look at him. Really look at him. His face was flushed, his pupils blown, his mouth red from where she'd bitten it, and there was a damp patch on his shoulder from where she'd pressed her face into his shirt and breathed too hard for too long. He looked, she thought distantly, like someone who had been paying very close attention for the last several minutes, which he had been, and the thought of that — of him, focused entirely on her, reading every sound she made — sent a small, hot pulse through her that had no business existing right now.

"New estimate," she murmured, and her voice was still rough, still cracked, but steadier now, finding its footing. Her thumb traced his lower lip again, slower this time, feeling the swell of it where she'd bitten. "Until someone notices the chain. I can work with that. That's — that's actually quite generous of you. Very optimistic. I *like* that about you."

She was parroting her own words back at him from five minutes ago and she knew it. She didn't care. Her brain was running on fumes and good humor and the particular kind of reckless warmth that only came from having just been thoroughly undone in a small, inappropriate space.

Her hands slid down from his shoulders, slow, mapping the shape of him through the ruined fabric of his shirt — the warmth of his chest, the tension in his stomach, the line of his hip where her fingers found his belt again, still loose from where she'd abandoned it. Her palm flattened against his stomach, feeling the muscles jump under her touch, and her grin softened into something less performative and more intent.

"For the record," she said, quieter now, her voice dropping into the register she used when she was being serious about something she wanted to pretend wasn't serious, "you've been very patient. And I have been — *extremely* selfish. Like, embarrassingly selfish. I'm going to have to make a donation to charity later to balance the karmic scales."

She tilted her chin up, lips brushing his jaw as she spoke, her breath still uneven but steadying with every word.

"So," she murmured against his skin, and her hand slid lower, finding him through the loosened fabric, and her eyes flicked up to watch his face in the half-light. "Your turn. And I want to hear you this time. None of that — " She bit the inside of her cheek, grinning. " — stoic, manly, *nothing-affects-me* business. I want the whole thing. I want the sounds. I want the — "

She paused, her thumb tracing a slow, deliberate line, and watched his expression shift.

"Yeah," she breathed, softer, watching him. "Like that. Exactly like that."

Her other hand came up to cup the back of his neck, fingers sliding into his hair, and she pressed her forehead back against his, close enough that her next words landed directly against his mouth.

"So come on, Fen," she whispered, and her voice had gone rough again, low and warm and threaded through with the particular kind of tenderness she only let show in moments like this — when the lights were off and the door was chained and the rest of the world was twelve feet away and irrelevant. "Let me hear you. We've got until someone notices the chain."

She kissed him — slow, this time, not desperate — and her hand moved, and she listened, and the grin that had been her constant companion all evening finally, finally softened into something quieter, and she gave him her whole attention, the way he'd given her his, and the bathroom was very small and very quiet and the music downstairs thudded on and neither of them made a sound louder than they had to, except when they did, and neither of them cared.

The chain swung gently in the half-inch of open doorway. The party continued below. Nobody came upstairs.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp breath, my hands gripping her hips as I press her back against the door. "You're gonna have to work for it," I manage, voice tight. "I'm not as loud as you are."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's grin sharpened into something dangerous, her eyes darkening as her fingers tightened in his hair.

"Work for it," she repeated, and the words came out low and rough and threaded through with a laugh she was barely containing. "Is that a *challenge*, Fen? Because I want you to know — I want you to *really* sit with this — that you have just made a tactical error."

She kissed the corner of his mouth, slow and deliberate, and felt the muscle in his jaw jump under her lips.

"I am *extremely* competitive," she murmured against his skin. "It's one of my worst qualities. Top three, easily. Right up there with 'makes questionable decisions in bathrooms' and 'cannot resist a dare.'"

Her hand moved — slower now, more deliberate, learning the rhythm that made his breath catch — and she pulled back just far enough to watch his face in the thin blade of hallway light cutting through the gap in the doorway. She watched the way his jaw tightened, the way his eyes dropped half-shuttered, the way his hands flexed against her hips like he was trying to anchor himself to something.

"Also," she breathed, her thumb tracing a slow, deliberate line, "for the record — I don't believe you. The stoic thing. I think you can be *very* loud when properly motivated. I've just never — " She bit her lower lip, grinning. " — applied myself."

Her free hand slid down from the back of his neck, tracing the line of his throat, feeling the way his pulse hammered under her fingertips, and she pressed her palm flat against his chest. Right over his heart. She could feel it racing.

"See," she whispered, softer now, her voice dropping into that low register she used when she meant something, "this tells a different story than your *I'm not as loud as you are* line. This says you're already — " She tilted her head, studying him, delighted. " — oh, you're *so* affected. You're just *pretending* you're not. That's — that's adorable. Genuinely. I'm going to remember this forever."

She kissed him then — slower than before, deeper, swallowing whatever sound he might have made — and her hand kept moving, steady and intent, and she listened with her whole body for the moment his composure started to slip. She was patient about it. She'd just had her own crisis of volume control; she could afford to take her time with his.

"But fine," she breathed against his mouth, grinning, always grinning, "if you want me to *work for it* — "

Her teeth found his lower lip, tugged gently, released.

"— then I'm going to work for it. And I'm going to be *so* thorough. And you're going to forget all about being stoic, and you're going to make exactly the kind of sound that makes me feel like I've won the lottery, and *then* — "

She shifted her weight, pressing closer, her leg tightening over his hip, and her hand did something that made his breath hitch audibly in the quiet bathroom.

"— *then*," she whispered, her grin softening into something less performative and more tender, "we're going to have to go back downstairs and look Marcus in the eye. And I want that to be *very* difficult for you. I want you to be thinking about this the whole time. I want you to — "

She lost the thread. Not because she'd run out of things to say, but because the sound he made — small, involuntary, bitten-off at the edges — was exactly the thing she'd been waiting for, and hearing it did something catastrophic to her ability to form sentences.

"Oh," she breathed, and her voice cracked on the single syllable, "there it is. *There* it is. I *knew* it. I *knew* you had it in you."

Her forehead pressed against his, her breath coming faster, and her hand kept its slow, deliberate rhythm, and she listened — really listened — for every sound he made, filing each one away like treasure, like evidence, like proof that she'd been right about him all along.

"Again," she whispered, her thumb tracing his lower lip, catching the shape of whatever sound he was swallowing. "Come on. Give me another one. I want to collect the whole set."

The chain swung gently in the doorway. The music downstairs thumped on. And Odile — flushed, wrecked, grinning, triumphant — gave him her whole attention, and waited, and listened, and did not let him be quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: A low, ragged groan escapes me before I can stop it, and I bury my face in her neck. "You're a menace," I mumble into her skin, hips pressing forward into her hand.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile followed close behind, her hand finding the small of Fen’s back as they climbed, her mouth near Fen’s ear again.

“I tested it earlier,” she murmured, and the grin was audible in her voice. “Very innocent intentions, obviously.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I grin and speed up a little. "Good. Because my intentions aren't innocent at all." My hand finds hers as we reach the landing.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile squeezed Fen's hand, then pulled them the last few steps toward the bathroom door. She paused with her free hand on the knob, turning back just enough to catch Fen's eye in the dim hallway light.

"Just so we're clear," she said, voice low but bright with amusement, "if anyone comes looking, I'm blaming you entirely."

She pushed the door open and tugged Fen inside, already reaching behind her to click the lock into place. The bass from downstairs thrummed faintly through the walls.

"Thin walls," she added, almost as an afterthought, already working at the buttons of Fen's shirt with practiced fingers. "Try to keep me quiet, will you?"

The smirk she gave them suggested she knew exactly how unlikely that was.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's head fell back against the door with a soft thud, her breath catching in a way that was already too loud for a bathroom with thin walls.

"God, that's convenient," she breathed, referring to the music, her hands abandoning Fen's shirt to slide up into their hair instead. "Almost like the universe wants us to get away with this."

She pulled them closer, her hips pressing forward, and laughed — a low, breathless sound that she didn't bother to muffle.

"Almost."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I chuckle against her neck, my own hands sliding under the hem of her dress. "The universe and I are on the same page for once."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile gasped, a sharp intake of breath that she barely tried to stifle, her hips rolling against Fen's hand. She let her head fall back against the door with a soft *thunk*, her fingers tightening in their hair.

"That's the spirit," she managed, her voice already starting to fray at the edges. She'd said thin walls, and she'd meant it, but now her dress was rucked up around her hips and Fen's touch was deliberate and hot and she was finding she didn't care who heard. Downstairs, someone cheered at a song change, and Odile laughed again, higher this time, breathy.

"Fuck the walls," she decided, pulling Fen's mouth back to hers. "Let them wonder." Her own words dissolved into a muffled sound against their lips, her whole body arching into the contact. The lock held. The bass thrummed. And Odile, as promised, was not quiet at all.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile braced one hand against the sink, the other still tangled in Fen's hair, her dress bunched around her waist like an afterthought. She caught a glimpse of them both in the mirror — flushed, half-dressed, utterly compromised — and the sight pulled a breathless laugh from her throat.

"We're a disaster," she informed Fen, not sounding remotely sorry about it. "If someone knocks, I'm answering the door exactly like this. Let them learn something."

She bit her lip against a sound that definitely carried, her hips stuttering against the sink's edge. The music downstairs swelled into something with a heavy beat, and she let her head drop forward, forehead nearly touching Fen's shoulder.

"God, I love parties," she breathed, and then laughed again because it was absurd and perfect and the lock was still holding. "Remind me to send the host a thank-you card. *Very* sincere. Maybe flowers."

Her voice cracked on the last word, and she gave up entirely on being quiet, one hand flying to cover her own mouth a second too late. The bass covered most of it. Probably. She didn't care enough to check.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press my mouth to her shoulder to muffle my own groan, fingers digging into her hip. "You're not answering any doors," I growl, half serious. The thought of someone seeing her like this sends a possessive thrill through me.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile felt that growl rumble against her skin, and the possessive edge in Fen's voice sent a shiver straight down her spine. She pulled back just enough to meet their eyes, her own dark with amusement and something hungrier.

"Oh, you think so?" she managed, breathless, her fingers curling around the back of Fen's neck. "Possessive looks good on you."

She caught their reflection in the mirror again and deliberately held Fen's gaze there, a silent dare. Her hips rolled back against them, a slow, deliberate rhythm that made her own breath hitch.

"But if someone knocks," she continued, voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper, "you'd better make it worth the interruption. Give them a real show."

She was close, so close, and the way Fen's fingers dug into her hip was only pushing her faster toward the edge. The music downstairs shifted again, something with a driving bassline that vibrated through the floor, and Odile let her head fall back against Fen's shoulder, her mouth open, no sound coming out at all for a long, suspended moment.

Then she laughed, a shattered, breathless thing, and met Fen's eyes in the mirror again.

"Your move."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's teeth released Fen's shoulder slowly, deliberately, and the sound that escaped her instead was anything but quiet. A broken moan, half-laugh, half-gasp, pressed into the curve of their neck as her body tensed and shuddered against them.

"Thirty seconds," she breathed, the words slurred with lingering pleasure. "That's a new record. I think. I've lost track of all my records tonight."

She slumped back against the sink, boneless and grinning, her dress still rucked up and her hair a mess and her lipstick absolutely beyond saving. She caught Fen's eye in the mirror again and laughed, a genuine, delighted sound that had nothing to do with keeping quiet.

"We are *never* getting invited back," she declared, sounding far too pleased about it. "Unless they're very open-minded hosts. Which, given the playlist, maybe."

She turned in Fen's arms, still shaky, and pressed a kiss to the bite mark she'd left on their shoulder — apologetic and not sorry at all.

"Your turn to fix your hair. Mine's a lost cause."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh and run a hand through my own messy hair, not bothering to fix it. "Let 'em talk." I kiss her, slow and deep, still pressed against her. "Worth it."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile hummed against Fen's lips, the sound warm and lazy and deeply satisfied. When she finally pulled back, she was still grinning, her hands resting loosely on their hips.

"Worth it," she echoed, as if testing the word. "Understatement of the year. Frame it. Put it on the wall."

She glanced at the mirror again, taking in the full scope of the damage — her smeared lipstick, the hickey blooming on her collarbone that she definitely hadn't had before, Fen's thoroughly debauched reflection beside her.

"We could go back down," she mused, not moving. "Make small talk. Pretend we were just... looking at the host's art collection. Very intently. For twenty minutes."

She snorted at her own suggestion, then reached over to wipe a smudge of her lipstick from the corner of Fen's mouth with her thumb.

"Or," she added, "we could sneak out the back, blame the early exit on a fake emergency, and continue this at home. Where the walls are thicker and I don't have to bite you to keep from screaming."

She raised an eyebrow, the invitation clear, her thumb still resting against Fen's jaw.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath left her in a sharp gasp as Fen lifted her leg, the new angle sending a jolt of pleasure through her that made her forget, for a moment, how words worked. Her back hit the door again, the wood rattling softly in its frame, and she let her head fall back with a laugh that was more air than sound.

"There you are," she breathed, her voice ragged with approval. "I was wondering when you'd stop being careful."

Her fingers found the back of Fen's neck, nails pressing in just enough to leave marks of her own. The music downstairs had shifted to something with a driving beat, and Odile moved with it, with Fen, with the reckless, consuming rhythm they'd built between them. The mirror was forgotten. The sink was forgotten. There was only Fen's body against hers, Fen's hand gripping her thigh, Fen's mouth on her throat, and the sound of her own voice rising to meet the bass.

"Don't stop," she managed, though it came out more like a command than a plea. "Don't you dare stop. I want everyone downstairs to know exactly—"

The rest of the sentence dissolved into a moan that she didn't even try to muffle, her nails raking down Fen's back through their shirt. The lock held. The bass thrummed. And Odile, true to form, was not quiet at all.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I can't hold back my own groan, the sound rough against her skin. "They know," I manage, my voice strained. "Believe me, they know."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out a breathless laugh at Fen's strained confession, the sound catching in her throat as another wave of pleasure rolled through her. She pulled back just enough to meet their eyes, her own glazed but sharp with mischief.

"Good," she said, utterly unrepentant. "Let them be jealous. Let them be scandalized. Let them write a strongly worded letter to the HOA."

She was still trembling slightly, still pressed against the door with Fen's body warm and solid against hers. The music downstairs had shifted to something slower, almost mocking in its calm, and Odile became abruptly aware of the silence they'd left in its wake. Her own breathing was ragged. Fen's was no better. The bathroom smelled like sex and her perfume and the faint, lingering scent of the host's fancy hand soap.

She looked at Fen, really looked at them — their messy hair, their kiss-swollen mouth, the mark on their shoulder that she'd left with her teeth — and felt a surge of affection so fierce it almost knocked the breath out of her all over again.

"I love you," she said, the words slipping out before she could stop them, simple and honest and entirely unguarded. Then she blinked, as if surprised by her own sincerity, and a crooked grin spread across her face. "Sorry. Post-orgasm clarity. Very dangerous. Makes me say things."

She reached up to brush a strand of hair from Fen's forehead, her touch gentler now, lingering.

"We should probably rejoin civilization before someone actually calls the cops. Or before the host starts charging us rent for this bathroom."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath caught sharply at the sound of the handle jiggling, her eyes flying to the door for just a split second before snapping back to Fen. The interruption sent a jolt of adrenaline through her that only heightened everything — the heat of Fen's body, the press of their fingers, the thrum of the bass through the floorboards.

"Don't," she echoed, her voice a ragged whisper, urgent and raw. Her hand flew to the back of Fen's neck, pulling them closer, her hips rolling against them with renewed desperation. The handle rattled again — once, twice — and then stopped, followed by the sound of footsteps retreating down the hall.

Odile laughed, the sound punched out of her on a gasp, half-relief and half-triumph. "They gave up," she breathed against Fen's mouth, her words slurring together as the tension coiled tighter in her belly. "Coward. Missed the— *oh* —missed the best part."

Her leg tightened around Fen's hip, her heel digging into the back of their thigh, and she was so close now, so close, the interruption only sharpening the edge she was balanced on. Her head fell back against the door with another soft *thunk*, and she didn't bother to muffle the broken moan that escaped her, didn't care that the person who'd tried the handle was probably still within earshot, didn't care about anything except Fen's body and Fen's touch and the way Fen was looking at her like she was the only thing in the world.

"There," she gasped, her voice cracking, her nails biting into Fen's shoulder. "Right there, right there, don't stop, I'm—"

The rest dissolved into a sharp cry, her body arching against the door as the wave finally broke, and she clung to Fen like they were the only solid thing in a world gone liquid and bright. The music downstairs hit a crescendo, drums crashing, and Odile let it swallow her voice entirely, let herself be loud and undone and utterly unapologetic about it.

When she finally came back to herself, she was trembling, her forehead pressed to Fen's shoulder, her breath coming in ragged gasps. The bathroom was quiet except for the muffled bass and their own breathing. The lock had held. The door had held. And Odile, slowly, began to laugh.

"That poor bastard," she managed, her voice wrecked and giddy. "They're going to be traumatized. Should I send *them* flowers too?"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I chuckle, my own body still humming. "Send them earplugs instead." I press a lazy kiss to her temple, finally letting her leg down. "C'mon, let's get out of here before they come back with a crowbar."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile snorted, still leaning heavily against the door, her legs not entirely convinced they were ready to support her yet.

"Earplugs," she repeated, delighted. "Practical. Thoughtful. I'll include a note: *Sorry about the noise. No, wait, I'm not.*"

She pushed herself upright with visible effort, wincing slightly as she tugged her dress back down into something approaching decency. Her underwear was somewhere on the floor. She'd find it later. Maybe. The mirror confirmed what she already knew — she looked thoroughly debauched, her lipstick a faint pink smear around her mouth, her hair a nest of tangles, the hickey on her collarbone already darkening to a vivid purple.

She caught Fen's eye in the reflection and grinned, utterly unrepentant.

"Right. Escape plan." She smoothed her dress one more time, then gave up and turned to face them. "We go downstairs, we find our coats, we say something vague about an early morning and a pet sitter emergency. If anyone asks about the noise, we blame the plumbing. Old pipes. Very creaky."

She reached down, plucked her underwear from beside the sink, and tucked it into Fen's pocket with a pat.

"Hold onto that for me. Souvenir."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh, shaking my head. "Plumbing. Right." I adjust my own clothes, glancing at the door. "Let's hope they bought the pet sitter story." I offer her my hand. "Ready to face the jury?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile took Fen's hand with the gravity of someone accepting a dance at a formal ball, then immediately ruined the effect by snorting.

"Jury's still out on whether we're guilty," she said, "but the verdict's in on whether we had fun. Unanimous decision."

She cracked the door open just enough to peer into the hallway. Empty. The music downstairs had shifted to something slower, almost romantic, which felt like a personal attack given what they'd just done to the bathroom.

"Coast is clear. Host's name is... Mark? Mike?" She frowned, genuinely drawing a blank. "Whatever. We'll fake it. We're excellent at faking things. Except—" she gestured vaguely at her own disheveled state, the hickey, the hair, the general aura of recent sin, "—this. This we're terrible at faking."

She stepped into the hallway, still holding Fen's hand, and paused to look back at the bathroom door. The lock had held. The walls had not kept their secrets. Somewhere downstairs, someone was probably already crafting the group chat message.

Odile grinned, sharp and bright and utterly unrepentant.

"Let's go make our excuses. Try to look innocent. I'll try not to laugh." She squeezed Fen's hand. "No promises."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I pull my shirt collar up a little to hide the bite mark, giving her a wry smile. "You look about as innocent as a fox in a henhouse." I lead the way down the stairs, already rehearsing our flimsy excuse in my head.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed—quiet, but not quiet enough—her breath warm against Fen’s ear. "I tested it earlier. Trust me," she said, with a flash of teeth that was half mischief, half invitation.

She slipped her hand into Fen’s, letting herself be tugged along the edge of the crowd, heart hammering with anticipation and the thrill of maybe being noticed. At the bottom of the stairs, she glanced over her shoulder, checking the living room; nobody paid them any attention, which only made her grin wider.

Once they reached the landing, Odile nudged Fen toward the bathroom door and leaned in, her voice just above a whisper. "Go on. I’ll be right behind you." Her eyes sparkled, daring him, the flush in her cheeks entirely unrelated to the wine she’d sipped earlier.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I push the door open, glancing back at her with a low laugh. "Testing locks now, are we? Planning ahead."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile slipped in after Fen, pulling the door quietly shut behind them. The dull thud of the music downstairs barely carried this far, muffled and distant—enough to give her courage, not enough to drown her nerves. She flicked the lock with an audible click, then leaned her back against the door, hands behind her. “Some of us like to be prepared for emergencies,” she said, her voice teasing but a little breathless now that they were alone in the narrow, lamp-lit space.

Her gaze flicked to Fen, hungry and bright. The hum of possibility made her restless, almost giddy. She stepped forward, closing the distance, and let her fingers hook into his belt loops. “Besides,” she added, her grin wicked, “I like making my own opportunities.”

She looked up at him, her lashes low, daring him to challenge her. “You nervous?” she asked, though her own excitement was obvious in the shaky exhale she let slip. “Or just excited to see if I’m as quiet as I think I am?”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile startled faintly at the sudden swell of sound from below, but the timing made her laugh—a husky, delighted sound that filled the small bathroom. “That’s practically a blessing,” she murmured, voice pitched low but not nearly as steady as she wanted it to be. She let her hands drift up Fen’s chest, gathering fistfuls of fabric, tugging him closer until there was barely space between them.

Her heart beat wild and reckless against her ribs. She tilted her head up, lips brushing Fen’s jaw as she spoke. “You know, you’re not supposed to just take my word for it,” she teased, the words feather-light and trembling with anticipation. “You could always… test me.”

Odile’s eyes, dark and laughing, searched his face for a beat—then she caught her bottom lip between her teeth, failing spectacularly at looking innocent. She was already losing the battle for composure, but that only made her more determined. The thrill of nearly getting caught, the locked door, the music below—it all went straight to her head, and she leaned into the danger, grinning up at him.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I chuckle, pressing a kiss to the side of her mouth. "Oh, I plan to." My hands settle on her hips, pinning her gently to the door. "But you're already talking too much for a quiet test."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile shivered at Fen’s hands on her hips, caught between the cool paint of the door and the heat of his body. His words made her laugh again, a little too loud, and she clapped a hand over her own mouth in mock horror. “Oops,” she whispered against her palm, her eyes wide and gleaming with mischief. “That’s one strike already, isn’t it?”

She let her hand fall, winding her arms around Fen’s neck instead, pulling him closer still. The bathroom felt impossibly small now, the air between them charged and reckless. “I could try—” she began, but she broke off with another giggle, muffled this time as she pressed her mouth to his shoulder, biting down gently as if she could hold the sound in her teeth.

Odile’s pulse thrummed wild beneath Fen’s fingers. “If you want quiet, you’ll have to keep me busy,” she whispered, the challenge clear in her voice, though she was already struggling not to give herself away. The thought of being overheard—by anyone, at any moment—made her flush hotter, and she arched into his touch, shameless and grinning, ready to see how much trouble she could get them both into.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s laughter turned breathless as Fen’s hands found bare skin, her shirt tangled somewhere between elbow and shoulder, belt half-loosed and jeans askew—enough for the cold air to bite at her back, enough to make her feel deliciously exposed. The cramped space only made everything sharper: the edge of the sink digging into her hip, Fen’s mouth hot against her neck, the slippery friction of skin on skin.

She tried to bite down on her excitement, teeth pressed into her lip, but a gasp escaped anyway—soft, startled, too loud by half. Odile clamped a hand over her mouth, stifling another helpless giggle, eyes squeezed shut, shoulders shaking with the effort. The music thumped up through the floor, not nearly loud enough to drown her out if she really lost control.

She could hear her own ragged breathing, Fen’s heartbeat pounding against her chest, the rustle of fabric and frantic movement. Every sound felt amplified in the tiny room, thrilling and mortifying all at once. Her hands slid under his shirt, nails raking gently down his back, urging him closer. She arched against the door, reckless and needy, her voice a low, muffled whimper behind her palm.

Odile shot Fen a desperate, gleaming look—half apology, half dare—as if to say, *see how hard I’m trying?* But there was too much pleasure, too much danger, and the urge to be quiet warred with the need to let go. She buried her face in his neck, biting down softly, her breath hot against his skin, and tried—tried—to hold herself together, even as her body betrayed her with every trembling, eager movement.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I huff a laugh against her shoulder, my own breathing uneven. "Trying is a strong word for that," I murmur, sliding a hand up her back to steady her against the door. "Might need a more... hands-on approach."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile let out another muffled sound—this time equal parts indignation and delight—her hand still clamped tight over her mouth as Fen’s words vibrated against her skin. Her body arched instinctively into his touch, the cold bite of the doorknob digging into her hip barely registering through the haze of want and laughter.

She managed to pull her hand away just long enough to whisper, “You’re not exactly helping,” in a voice that trembled with both challenge and surrender. But then Fen’s hand slid higher, his grip firm, and her protest dissolved into a half-swallowed gasp. She bit down on her knuckles, eyes squeezed shut, trying and failing to muffle the next breathless laugh that bubbled out of her.

Odile’s hips shifted restlessly, her free hand scrabbling for purchase—on Fen’s shoulder, in his hair, on the edge of the sink—anywhere to anchor herself as the threat of being caught made every touch feel reckless and forbidden. The music downstairs pulsed through the floor, but it was a thin shield against the helpless little sounds she kept letting slip.

She turned her head, mouth brushing Fen’s ear as she half-whispered, half-laughed, “If someone knocks, you’re explaining this.” But there was no real fear in her voice—just giddy defiance and a breathless plea for more. Her resolve to be quiet was already in tatters, and she didn’t seem to mind at all.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile held on as long as she could, her teeth digging desperately into Fen’s shoulder, breath coming in sharp, ragged bursts. His hand slid between her thighs, and all her bravado dissolved into pure sensation—her hips jerked against his palm, a helpless shiver running up her spine. For a moment, she almost managed silence, her eyes squeezed shut, knuckles white where she gripped the edge of the sink.

But the effort fell apart with a choked, stifled moan—louder than she meant, muffled only by Fen’s skin. The sound startled even her, and she bit down harder, the taste of salt and skin grounding her as she struggled for composure. Her legs threatened to give out, knees going weak beneath the heat of his touch, and she clung tighter, nails digging crescents into his back.

She let out a helpless laugh, breathless and wild, the sound half-smothered against his shoulder. “Okay—okay—” she whispered, her voice shaking with pleasure and the giddy thrill of being so close to losing control. “Not as quiet as I thought—”

But there was no regret, only feverish delight in the risk, the frantic press of bodies in the tiny, locked room, the music below and the pounding of her own pulse in her ears. Odile’s free hand slid up into Fen’s hair, tugging him closer as if she could disappear into him, her body arching, eager and unashamed, for whatever came next.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Shhh," I breathe, but I'm grinning like an idiot. My other hand comes up to cover her mouth, gentle but firm. "They're gonna hear you downstairs, and I'm not explaining anything."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s laugh was strangled by Fen’s palm, the sound caught and trembling against his skin. Her eyes widened in mock outrage, sparkling with mischief above the gentle press of his hand. She tried to nod solemnly—*yes, yes, I’ll be good*—but her body betrayed her, hips rolling helplessly into his touch, tension winding tighter with every forbidden movement.

The sensation of Fen’s hand over her mouth sent a bolt of heat straight through her, her breath coming fast and shallow against his palm. The absurdity of the situation—their clothes half-off, her back to the door, the entire party oblivious just one floor below—made her want to laugh and moan and shout all at once. But Fen’s grip kept her anchored, forced her to swallow every sound, and the effort to stay quiet only ratcheted her excitement higher.

Odile’s eyes fluttered closed, lashes brushing Fen’s wrist, as she surrendered to the intensity of his hands, the pressure of his body pinning her in place. She arched into him, her muffled gasp vibrating against his palm, fingers digging into his shoulders, clinging tight as the pleasure threatened to overwhelm her. Her whole body trembled with the effort to stay silent, every muscle drawn taut between the risk of being caught and the sweet, dangerous thrill of letting go.

She peeked up at him, eyes glassy with pleasure and defiance, and tried to smirk around his hand—a silent dare, as if to say, *Just try to keep me quiet.* The challenge was clear in every line of her body, every helpless, eager movement: Odile was going to make this as difficult for him as possible, and she was loving every second of it.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile didn’t bother pretending anymore—her laugh broke free, muffled and wild, as Fen hauled her leg over his hip and all pretense of carefulness vanished. The sharp press of his hand and the rough steadiness of the door behind her sent a delirious jolt straight through her. She clung to him, arms tight around his neck, her body open and eager, giving up entirely on restraint.

The party downstairs became a distant, meaningless throb in her ears, drowned out by the frantic, breathless sounds spilling from her lips. Each movement threatened to knock something over—her heel scraped the side of the sink, her back thudded softly against the door—but Odile only laughed harder, reckless and radiant with pleasure. “Oh god—Fen—” she managed, voice breaking, delight and challenge tangled in every word.

She buried her face in his neck, teeth grazing his skin as she tried to muffle herself, but she was shaking now, her composure long gone. Her hips rolled up to meet him, desperate and defiant, every gasp and whimper echoing off the bathroom tiles. If anyone heard—well, Odile thought, dazed with delight, let them. The risk only drove her higher, her body arching, hands slipping under Fen’s shirt, clutching at warm, sweat-slick skin.

“Don’t stop,” she whispered, breath hot against his ear, her voice a ragged, urgent plea—louder than she meant, the words trembling with laughter and need. She didn’t care who heard. All she wanted was this: his hands, his mouth, the thrill of being caught, the wild, impossible joy of loving him right here, right now, with the whole world just a thin door away.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I kiss her to swallow her next laugh, pressing her harder against the door. "You're gonna get us kicked out," I mutter, but my voice is rough with my own lack of control.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile’s laugh dissolved into the kiss—messy, urgent, all teeth and breathless need—her mouth opening hungrily beneath Fen’s. His words, low and ragged, sent a thrill coursing through her that had nothing to do with fear and everything to do with the delicious recklessness of it all. She gripped him tighter, nails digging crescents into his back as she pressed closer, the door rattling faintly behind her.

She broke the kiss only long enough to gasp, her lips brushing his, voice shaking with laughter and want. “If we get kicked out, it’s your fault, not mine,” she managed, the words tumbling out on a wave of shameless delight. There was nothing soft or shy left in her—she was all fire and challenge, every inch of her body alive beneath his hands.

Odile’s leg tightened around his hip, urging him impossibly closer, her head falling back against the door as pleasure and danger blurred together. She moaned, louder now, uncaring, her voice echoing off the bathroom tiles. The thought of anyone hearing—friends just downstairs, the risk of footsteps on the stairs—only made her hold Fen tighter, fingers tangled in his hair, needing more.

She looked up at him, flushed and wild, eyes dark with heat and laughter. “Come on,” she whispered, reckless and eager, her voice a promise and a dare all at once. “Let them hear—let them wonder—” And then her mouth was on his again, greedy and unrestrained, daring him to match her for every frantic, glorious second they could steal.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The rattle of the handle jolted through Odile like a live wire—fear, thrill, and laughter all tangled together. For a single heartbeat, she froze, breath caught sharp in her throat, eyes flying wide as she met Fen’s gaze. But she saw the same wild dare reflected back at her, and the rush of being so close to discovery only drove her onward.

“Don’t,” she gasped, voice sharp with urgency, her hand clinging hard to his shoulder. Her whole body shuddered with the need to keep going, to outrun the consequences. She was trembling, not with shame, but with the giddy, unstoppable pleasure of being loved like this—pressed up against the locked bathroom door, her leg hooked high around Fen’s hip, the music and laughter below just a thin barrier away from her unraveling.

The bathroom was filled with the sounds they could no longer swallow: the frantic slap of skin on skin, the scrape of her heel on porcelain, her own ragged, stifled cries tumbling out every time Fen thrust into her. She tried to bury her face in his neck, muffling herself against his shoulder, but she couldn’t hold back the broken, desperate noises that slipped free—half-moan, half-laugh, all reckless need.

She arched against him, fingers knotted in his hair, hips surging up to meet every movement. Her body moved with fierce, greedy abandon, heedless of the danger outside, the handle rattling again before whoever-it-was gave up and wandered away. The sound only made Odile bolder, her voice thick with pleasure as she whispered, “Harder—don’t stop—god, Fen, please—”

Her body trembled with the edge of release, every muscle straining, breath coming in hot, helpless gasps that echoed against the tiles. She clung to Fen, nails scoring his back, her laughter turning to a frantic, breathless whimper as her orgasm crashed over her—wild, unstoppable, and far too loud for the little locked room. Her cry was muffled against his mouth, but it was unmistakable, raw and ecstatic, as she clung to him, uncaring, for as long as she could hold on.

Odile’s head lolled back, hair damp and wild, eyes shining with victory and delight. She grinned up at Fen, utterly unrepentant, breathless laughter spilling from her lips as she whispered, “If we’re getting kicked out, at least it was worth it.”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I'm breathing hard, forehead pressed against the door beside her head, trying to catch my breath. "You're a menace," I murmur, but I'm smiling like an idiot. "Think they heard?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile beamed up at Fen, her cheeks flushed and eyes still glazed with lingering pleasure. She let her head fall back against the door with a thud, grinning so wide it almost hurt. “If they didn’t before, they definitely did when you—” Her voice broke with a laugh, low and giddy, as she squeezed his hips between her thighs in a last, playful aftershock.

She slid her fingers through his hair, gentle now, and pressed a slow, messy kiss to the corner of his mouth. “I hope they heard,” she whispered, mischief glittering in her voice. “Let them wonder who had the best night at this party.” Her hands trailed down his chest, shaky but unashamed, as she tried to smooth the rumpled edges of his shirt—though it was a lost cause for both of them.

Odile’s body still trembled, aftershocks making her shiver as she drew Fen close, nuzzling his jaw. “You know,” she murmured, her voice warm and wicked, “next time you want me quiet, you’ll have to try a lot harder.” She kissed him again, slow and lingering, tasting laughter and sweat and the faintest hint of triumph.

She pulled back just enough to meet his eyes, her own shining with victory. “Now help me get my pants up before someone tries that handle again,” she said, not bothering to lower her voice—if anyone was listening, they’d already heard plenty. Odile’s laughter rang through the tiny bathroom, bright and unrepentant, as she began to wriggle herself back into her jeans, not quite steady on her feet, still wrapped in the thrill of what they’d done.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I help her with the zipper, still breathing heavily. "Next time we're using your place," I say, but I'm laughing too. "With soundproofing." I lean in to kiss her once more, slow and lazy now, savoring the taste of her. "You're impossible."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile grinned against his lips, the kiss slower now, sweeter in the aftermath but still humming with mischief. She braced herself on his shoulders and tugged her jeans up over trembling thighs, huffing out a triumphant little laugh as Fen fumbled with the zipper. “You say that every time,” she murmured, brushing her mouth against the corner of his, “and somehow we always end up somewhere worse. Admit it—you like the risk almost as much as I do.”

She stole one last, lingering kiss, her fingers threading through his hair as she tried—utterly in vain—to smooth out the chaos they’d made of each other. Her shirt was inside out; she shrugged and fixed it with a swift, efficient twist, fingers nimble despite the lingering tremor in her hands. Odile tucked her hair behind her ears, caught sight of herself in the mirror, and burst out laughing again—cheeks flushed, lipstick smeared, eyes bright with satisfaction. She looked utterly wrecked and didn’t care one bit.

She turned back to Fen, mouth quirking in a lopsided, wicked smile. “Impossible,” she echoed, rolling the word around her tongue like a private joke. “That’s rich, coming from you.” She glanced at the door, listening for footsteps—none, just the distant thrum of music and the muted clink of glasses. “Think anyone’s waiting out there, or can we sneak down like nothing happened?” she asked, voice pitched low and conspiratorial, as if the walls themselves might tattle.

Odile looped her fingers through his, squeezing tight. “If we get caught, just act innocent,” she said, eyes dancing. “You know—like you’re not the reason my knees are shaking.” She straightened her shirt, squared her shoulders, and winked. “Ready to face the music?”

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I tug my own shirt back into some semblance of order, still grinning like a fool. "Innocent? You're asking a lot." I run a hand through my hair, knowing it's hopeless. "But yeah, let's go. You first—if anyone's out there, they'll believe your lies easier."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile caught Fen's hand and pulled them along, weaving through the kitchen where someone had started a deeply questionable playlist. She grinned — the kind of grin that suggested she'd already decided how this was going to go and was mostly just enjoying the logistics.

"It *should*," she said, which was not the same as yes. She took the stairs two at a time, tugging Fen behind her, and paused at the top to listen. Music from below. Laughter. Someone dropping something glass. The ordinary party sounds that meant nobody was paying attention to the hallway.

She found the right door — second on the left, if she remembered the layout from the last time they'd been here for dinner — and pulled Fen inside. The lock was one of those simple thumb-turn deals. She flipped it. It clicked.

Odile turned around in the small space, back against the door, and looked at Fen with an expression that was deeply pleased with herself.

"See? Functional," she said, her voice already dropping quieter, conspiratorial, though she didn't lower it *nearly* as much as she probably thought she did. Her hands found the front of Fen's shirt. "We have maybe ten minutes before someone needs to pee."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I grin, leaning in to kiss her. "Ten minutes is plenty of time." My hands settle on her hips, pulling her closer against me. "I knew you had a plan."

dialogue.content: The request was rejected because it was considered high risk

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed — the sound muffled against Fen's mouth but not nearly as muffled as it should have been. She didn't seem to notice, or more accurately, she didn't seem to care. Her fingers were already working at Fen's shirt buttons, which she was significantly less deft at than she would have claimed.



"See, the music covers—" she started, and then Fen's mouth found that spot just below her ear, and the end of the sentence dissolved into something that was absolutely not an inside voice.

She tugged Fen's shirt free with a kind of urgency that suggested she'd been thinking about this for at least the last hour of polite party conversation. Her hands slid underneath, palms warm against skin, pulling them closer with an impatience that the small space practically demanded.

"Lock's working," she confirmed, breathless, as if anyone had asked. Her hips pressed forward against Fen's. "Door's— fine. Everything's fine."

Downstairs, the questionable playlist transitioned into something even louder. Someone cheered. Odile tilted her head back against the door, giving Fen better access, and bit her lower lip in a way that was clearly performative and only about sixty percent effective at keeping her quiet.

"We should be quick," she whispered. Then, slightly louder, with a grin that said she had no intention of being quick: "I mean — *relatively*."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Relatively," I echo, my hands sliding up under her shirt to press against the small of her back. "But I'm not hearing any complaints yet." I kiss her neck, tasting salt and perfume. "Tell me when we're at nine minutes."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's breath caught — audibly, *obviously* — and she pressed her lips together like that would retroactively fix it.

"Nine minutes," she repeated, her voice pitched low but still carrying a warmth that carried further than she seemed to realize. Her fingers curled against Fen's back. "You're — keeping track, then? That's very organized of you."

Her hips shifted, restless, seeking. The door behind her creaked faintly against the frame and she froze for exactly one second, glancing at the lock, then back at Fen with an expression that was less worried and more delighted — like the possibility of getting caught was a feature, not a bug.

"That wasn't me," she said, about the door, in a tone that implied she thought she was being very convincing. Her hand came up to the side of Fen's face, thumb tracing along their jaw. "That was — structural. Old house."

Downstairs, someone shrieked with laughter. The music bumped. Odile used the noise cover to pull Fen closer, her mouth finding theirs in a kiss that started teasing and deepened faster than she'd probably intended, her composure fraying at the edges in a way that was becoming increasingly visible.

She pulled back just enough to speak, forehead resting against Fen's, her breathing uneven.

"I changed my mind," she murmured. "No time limit. We leave when we get caught or when I stop caring, whichever comes first."

Her grin was sharp and conspiratorial. She had absolutely no intention of being the one to stop.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
