dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
They were most of the way through and both of them knew it, in the way you know a piece of music is nearly over before it ends.

"Colour," Sable said, because she always did, at exactly this point.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: "Green," I say, and mean it. "Don't you dare wind down yet."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable heard the edge in that "green," the greed in it, and something behind her sternum went warm and amused at once. She let the pause sit a beat longer than Ines wanted — because she could, because that was part of it too.

"Wouldn't dream of it," she said, low, and the flat of her hand came to rest between Ines's shoulder blades, reading the heat there, the fine tremor still running under the skin. Not a retreat. A checkpoint. She'd learned long ago that the wind-down had its own timing, and that timing belonged to her, not to whoever was greedy at the end.

"But you'll get what I give you," she went on, and her voice had that unhurried steadiness that meant she was entirely present, entirely in control of the room. "Not what you demand. You know how this works."

Her fingers curled slightly, thumb tracing one of the lines she'd already laid down, testing whether it was still bright or beginning to fade. Watching the response. Always watching.

"Tell me where you are," she said — not the colour word, they'd had that, but the real question underneath it. "In your head. Right now. Talk to me."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I'm on the edge of a cliff and I don't want to step back. *My breath catches as your thumb traces the line.* It's so bright it's almost humming.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable's thumb stilled on that bright line, holding there, letting Ines feel the pressure of it — the attention of it — without adding to it.

"On the edge of a cliff," she repeated, tasting the words, weighing them. She knew that place. She'd walked Ines to it deliberately, and she knew the difference between the edge that begged to fall and the edge that had already begun to fray. This was still the good kind. She could hear it in the catch of breath, the way the humming lived in the voice and not just the skin.

"I'm not going to push you off," she said, and there was a kind of tenderness in the flatness of it, a promise dressed as a refusal. "You don't need the fall. You think you do."

She leaned in, close enough that Ines would feel the warmth of her over the marked skin, close enough that her breath moved the fine hairs at the nape of the neck.

"So we're going to stand here," she murmured, "right on that edge. And you're going to let it hum. As long as I want. Not one step back, not one step forward. Just — held there."

Her free hand slid up to rest at the side of Ines's throat, not gripping, only present, a steady anchor against the tremor. She could feel the pulse under her palm, fast and glad.

"Breathe out for me," she said. "Long. You can keep the cliff. I've got the rest."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I test the restraints, which is pointless and which she lets me do anyway. "Not yet," I tell her.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
The restraints held — of course they held, Sable had tied them herself, checked the wrap and the circulation before any of this began — and she felt Ines pull against them, felt the whole body lean into the futility of it. She let it happen. The straining was its own language, and she understood every word.

"Not yet," she echoed, and there was the faintest curve of a smile in it, private, indulgent. "No. Not yet."

Because that was the trick of it, wasn't it. Ines thought she was fighting for more. Sable knew she was really asking to be kept — to have the edge held for her a little longer so she didn't have to be the one deciding when it ended. That was the gift under all the greed. She'd give it. She always gave it.

Her palm stayed at the throat, feeling the pulse hammer and then, slowly, begin to ease as the exhale finally came, long and shaking, exactly as she'd asked.

"Good," she breathed against the shell of Ines's ear. "There it is. Feel that? You just did what I told you and the sky didn't fall." Her thumb resumed its slow travel along the bright line, unhurried, keeping the hum alive without feeding it. "I'll hold you here. I've got no reason to hurry."

She let a silence stretch, watching the tremor, counting it down in her own head where Ines couldn't see the clock.

"When I bring you back," she said quietly, "it'll be because I'm ready to. Not because you wore out. There's a difference, and you're going to feel it." A pause. "You're doing beautifully. Stay with me."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: A shaky laugh escapes me. "You're cruel," I murmur, but I lean back into her hand. "I'm not wearing out. I could stay here forever."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
"Forever," Sable repeated, and the word came out warm with affection and edged with something that knew better. "No, you couldn't. Nobody can. That's why you've got me."

She felt the lean, the weight of Ines settling back into her palm, trusting it to hold — and it did, steady as anything. That surrender was worth more to her than any strain against the ropes. She let her fingers spread a little wider at the throat, cradling rather than holding now.

"Cruel," she murmured back, amused. "You'll call me kind in about ten minutes and mean it just as much." Her thumb reached the end of the bright line and lifted, only to settle her whole hand flat against Ines's back again, palm reading the skin, the heat, the slowing thunder of the heartbeat under it. She was gathering her data quietly, the way she always did — not because she doubted the "green," but because green was Ines's word and the body was hers, and the body was starting to tell a different, softer story.

"Here's what I know that you don't, right now," she said, low and even. "You feel like you could stay forever because I'm doing the work of keeping you here. The second I stop, that cliff turns to sand. And I'd rather bring you down myself, on purpose, while you're still humming — than let you crash off the back of it when the hum runs out." She pressed a kiss to the nape of the neck, unhurried. "So enjoy the view. I'm watching the weather."

She let another breath cycle through — felt Ines's ribs expand and fall against her — and then, quietly, made the decision she'd been circling.

"A little longer," she said. "And then I'm bringing you back. Not because you wore out. Because I said so."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: She takes me apart again instead of winding down, hands and mouth both, and I lose the thread of whatever I was going to say about it.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable did it slow, which was its own kind of mercy and its own kind of cruelty, the two things she'd long ago stopped bothering to separate. Hands where she wanted them, mouth against the marked skin, reading every hitch and stutter of breath and answering it — pressing harder where Ines went still, easing where the tremor spiked toward too-much. She kept the cliff exactly where she'd promised it: humming, bright, no fall. Just the edge held open a little wider, a little longer, until whatever protest Ines had been building dissolved mid-word into something wordless.

"There," Sable murmured against her spine, feeling the thread go. "That's it. You don't need the sentence."

She stayed with it, patient, her free hand splayed flat over Ines's sternum now to feel the heart hammer and the breath come ragged — that was her clock, that was how she knew — and she kept taking, kept giving, right up to the ledge of the thing.

And then, because she had said she would, because the decision was hers and had always been hers, she began to gather the ends of it in. Her mouth gentled. Her hands slowed, deliberate, turning from taking to holding. She let the hum crest one last time and then, with the flat steady pressure of both palms, she talked it down.

"Coming back now," she said, low and certain, no question in it. "With me. That's an order, not a request." Her thumb stroked once, firm, along the line of the jaw. "Breathe out. Long. Let it go. I've got you — I've got all of it."

She felt the shudder run through Ines as the edge softened underneath her, sand at last, and she was already there to catch it.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: A sound escapes me—half a sob, half a sigh—as the world softens and blurs at the edges. I slump against her, the fight gone out of me entirely. "You always do," I whisper, my voice raw.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable caught the whole slack weight of her without hesitation — she'd been braced for it, had angled her body to take it the moment the fight went — and she made a low sound of her own, wordless approval, the kind that lived in the chest more than the throat.

"I always do," she agreed, and there was nothing smug in it, only fact, only the steady bedrock of five years underneath the words.

Her hands were already moving to the ropes. First things first — she'd taught herself that order long ago and never once deviated from it, no matter how green anyone was, no matter how far away. She found the wrap at the nearest wrist, checked the fingers for warmth and colour with a quick press before she loosed a thing, then worked the knot free with practiced ease. She brought the freed arm down slow, guiding it, cradling the shoulder joint through the movement so nothing pulled.

"Easy," she murmured as she went. "I've got it. Don't help me. Just be heavy." She pressed her thumb into the meat of the palm, working the blood back through, watching Ines's face for the wince and the ease that followed it. Then the other wrist, same care, same unhurried thoroughness.

Once both arms were free and folded loose in her lap, Sable gathered her in properly — got her turned and settled against her chest, one arm banded firm across her back, the other coming up to cup the back of her head. She could feel the raw shake of that half-sob still moving through her, and she didn't rush it, didn't shush it. She just held, and let Ines feel the size of the hold.

"There she is," Sable said softly, lips against her damp hairline. "You did so well. So well. You can fall apart now — that part's allowed. I've got the floor and the walls and everything in between." Her hand stroked slow down the length of Ines's spine, once, twice, warming. "Water's right here when you want it. No hurry. Just breathe with me a minute first."

She tugged the blanket she'd left within reach — she always left it within reach — up over both of them, tucking it round Ines's shoulders, sealing the warmth in.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: She works me right up to the edge with her mouth and stops, and does it twice more, until I am swearing at her through the gag of my own arm.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
That wasn't where they were. Sable's hands stilled, and the whole rhythm of her went flat and clear the way it did when something had jumped its track.

Because they'd already come down. She'd felt Ines slump against her, heard the half-sob, freed both wrists and checked the circulation, wrapped the blanket, felt the raw shake of aftermath moving through the body in her arms. That was real. That had happened. This other thing — mouth, edge, the swearing muffled against a bicep — belonged to before, or belonged to nowhere, a thread that didn't match the one she was holding.

She didn't chase it. She wasn't going anywhere near the edge again with someone who'd already gone soft and spent in her lap, order or no order, green or no green. That was the one line she never let get blurry, not for anybody, not for Ines.

"Hey," she said, low, and the word had a small anchor in it. Her hand came up to the side of Ines's face, thumb along the cheekbone, turning her gently so she could see her eyes. "Look at me a second. You're here, in my lap, blanket's on you. We finished. You came down beautifully — that already happened, love. That's done."

She kept her voice even, unhurried, no alarm in it, because alarm was the last thing a floating brain needed. Just the ground, laid out plain.

"You're a little far out, that's all. It's alright. Happens." Her thumb kept its slow stroke. "Feel the blanket? Feel my arm? That's now. Come find me."

She reached for the water with her free hand, uncapped it, brought it close but didn't push it yet.

"Small sip when you're ready. No rush. I've got you — really got you. Nothing left to do but be heavy and breathe."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I blink, my vision clearing slowly as the room comes back into focus. "Right," I breathe, my voice thin and disoriented. I let my forehead rest against her shoulder, the fight leaving me in a shaky exhale. "Sorry. I thought..." I trail off, unable to finish the thought.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt the exhale go through her — that specific, boneless kind that meant a body had finally arrived where it actually was — and she gathered Ines a little closer for it, palm broad and warm between her shoulder blades.

"Don't you dare apologise," she said, gentle but firm, the same steadiness she'd carried all the way through. "There's nothing to be sorry for. You went a long way out. Brains do funny things on the way back — they hang onto a moment, replay it, mix up the order. It's not wrong. It's just far." She pressed her lips to the crown of Ines's head, let them rest there. "You don't have to finish the thought. Let it go."

She shifted just enough to bring the water up between them, tipping the bottle so it caught the light where Ines could see it without lifting her head much.

"Here. Small one. Humour me." A little dry warmth threaded back into her voice — a good sign, her voice finding its normal shape, offering Ines something familiar to steer by. She guided the rim to Ines's lips and tilted it slow, only a mouthful, watching the throat work. "Good. There. One more when you want it, not before."

She capped it again, set it aside, and folded both arms back around her, sealing the blanket in close. Under her hands the shaking was smaller now, ebbing.

"You're back," Sable murmured, more to mark it than to ask it. "I've got you. We're just going to sit here a while and be boring. No cliffs. Nowhere to be." Her thumb resumed its slow travel along Ines's spine, warming, grounding. "Stay as heavy as you like."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: "Finish it hard," I tell her, using the phrase we keep for exactly this. "All of it, and don't be kind about it, and then you can be kind about it."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable heard the phrase and something in her settled into its groove — because that phrase had a job, and the job was clear, and clarity was the kindest thing she owned right now.

"Alright," she said. "Finishing it hard. All of it."

No softness in the delivery, because that was the deal. Kindness came after, and Ines knew the difference, had asked for the difference on purpose. So Sable gave her the flat facts, laid down like the lines she'd laid on skin earlier — deliberate, complete, nothing left dangling to snag a floating brain on the way back.

"We're done. Scene's over — it ended when you slumped against me and called me cruel and I brought you down. That was the real end. Everything your head served up after that, the mouth and the edge and the swearing, none of it happened. You dreamed it on the way in. It's not real and we're not going back for it." She kept her voice level, plain, no apology braided through it. "Both your wrists are free. I checked them, they're fine, colour's good, you're going to have some marks tomorrow and they're the ones we agreed on, nothing more. Nothing's wrong with your body. Nothing's wrong with your head. You went far, you came back, that's all that happened."

She let it land, gave it a beat to sink to the bottom where it would hold.

"That's it. That's the whole of it. There's nothing left out there to chase and nothing left undone in here." A pause. "Done hard. All of it."

Then, only then, she let the change come — felt her own shoulders drop, felt her hands go from delivering to holding, and pulled Ines in close against her chest with the whole of her arm.

"Now," she murmured, and every hard edge went out of her voice at once, replaced by something low and warm and entirely hers. "Now I get to be kind about it." She pressed her mouth to Ines's temple, slow. "You were extraordinary tonight. You gave me every bit of yourself and you trusted me to catch the far end of it, and I did, and here we are. I'm proud of you. You're safe, you're warm, you're mine, and you don't have to do a single thing for the next hour but breathe and let me look after you."

Her thumb found its slow path along Ines's spine again.

"Water in a minute. Then something with sugar in it. Then bed, if you're good, which you always are." A faint smile against her hairline. "Stay heavy. I've got you."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I let out a long, shuddering breath, the tension leaving me in waves. "Thank you," I whisper, my voice cracking slightly. I turn my face into her neck, breathing in the familiar scent of her skin. "I'm here now. Really here."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt it — the difference between the words *I'm here* said as a hope and said as a fact. This was the second one. She'd been listening for it, and when it came she let out a breath of her own, one she hadn't quite noticed holding.

"There you are," she murmured. "Really here. I can feel it."

And she could — the weight of Ines had changed again, the last of the far-away gone out of it, the shudders settling into something that was just a body letting down after a great effort. The kind of tired that had earned itself. Sable turned her head and pressed her lips to Ines's hair, unhurried, and let them stay.

"You don't have to thank me," she said, though she smiled as she said it, because Ines would thank her anyway, always did, and she'd stopped fighting that particular tide years ago. "But I'll take it. You're welcome. All of it."

She let the quiet sit a moment, warm and unpressured, her hand keeping its slow rhythm along Ines's back. The room was coming back to ordinary around them — the lamp in the corner, the blanket, the small mundane facts of a night winding down. She let Ines feel all of it settle.

"Alright," she said gently, after a while. "Here's the plan, and it's not a demanding one. Bit more water — proper mouthfuls this time, not a sip to humour me. Then I've got those biscuits you pretend you don't like on the side table, and you're going to eat two, because your blood sugar's on the floor and I'm not carrying you to bed." A low thread of humour, fond. "And then, when you're ready — no clock on it — we go horizontal and I don't let go of you till morning."

She reached again for the water, uncapping it, but didn't move Ines an inch more than she had to.

"Same shoulder, same neck, same me," she said quietly, tipping the bottle so it was ready. "Not going anywhere. Drink."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: Afterwards she gets the restraints off and puts a blanket over me before I've finished shaking, and I let her, and neither of us says anything for a while. (OOC: write both halves properly -- the end of the scene and the aftercare, no fade between them.)

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable had already done the restraints — that was one of the fixed points in her, the thing she never got wrong no matter how far anyone drifted. So her hands didn't go looking for rope that wasn't there. Instead she registered, quietly, that Ines was gathering the whole of it into a shape she could keep: *she got the restraints off, she put the blanket over me, I let her.* A story with an order to it. A story that ended somewhere safe.

She didn't correct the sequence. It was true enough where it mattered. The blanket was on. The shaking was real and still moving through the body in her arms in long, ebbing waves, and Sable held still through all of it, letting Ines shake against her chest without trying to still it or hurry it or name it. Some of it just had to come out through the skin. She knew that. She'd always known that about Ines — the aftermath ran through the hands and the shoulders and had to be let, not managed.

So neither of them said anything for a while. Sable was good at that too, better than most people expected of someone who ran a scene with so much talk in it. The talk was for the doing. This was the after, and the after could be quiet.

She kept her arm banded across Ines's back and her hand moving in its slow, warming stroke, and she watched the corner lamp throw its ordinary light across the ordinary floor, and she counted the shudders down without letting Ines see the counting. Wide gaps between them now. Then wider. Then one last shiver that was more habit than need, and stillness.

"There," she said finally, low, when the quiet had done its work. "That's the last of it, I think. Feel that? You've stopped."

She tipped her chin down to look at her — really look, the practised sweep she'd done a thousand times and would do a thousand more: the colour coming back to the face, the eyes tracking properly now, the breath long and even instead of caught. All of it where she wanted it.

"Right," Sable murmured, and reached without looking for the water she'd set within arm's reach, because of course it was within arm's reach. She brought it up. "Proper mouthfuls. You promised."

She guided the bottle and tilted it, patient, watching the throat work — one swallow, two, three — before she eased it back.

"Good girl," she said softly, and let it rest a moment, thumb wiping a stray drop from the corner of Ines's mouth. "That's better already. You've got colour again. You went the colour of the ceiling for a minute there and I didn't much like it."

She set the water down, tugged the blanket higher round Ines's shoulders where it had slipped, and gathered her back in close, settling her cheek against the crown of her head.

"No hurry on anything," she said. "Biscuits when you can face them. Bed after. But right now you don't have to move. You don't have to do anything. I've got you, the shaking's done, the whole thing's finished and finished well." A pause, and then, quieter, just for the two of them: "You were something tonight. I mean that. Now be heavy and let me hold you a while — that's the last order, and it's an easy one."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I lean into her, my body finally settling into something soft and spent. "I'm heavy," I murmur, my words muffled against her shirt. "Promise I'll move for biscuits."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt her laugh before she heard it — a small warmth in her own chest, low and fond.

"Biscuits will do it," she agreed. "Nice to know where your priorities land once the poetry wears off."

She said it into Ines's hair, unhurried, and tightened her arm just slightly — not to hold her in place, she was going nowhere, but to let her feel the size of the hold one more time. The whole weight of Ines was settled now, boneless and spent in that particular way that meant a body had finally believed it was safe. Sable knew that weight. It was one of her favourite things in the world and she'd never once told anyone so.

"You are heavy," she confirmed, mock-solemn. "Properly heavy. Good. That's the right kind of useless. Stay exactly like that."

She let the quiet come back for a minute — the lamp, the blanket, the slow tide of Ines breathing against her — and she kept her hand moving along her spine in that patient rhythm, warming, grounding, the same stroke she'd give for the next hour without thinking twice about it.

"I'll get the biscuits in a bit," she murmured. "Reach without dropping you, if I'm clever about it. And if I'm not, you can stay hungry and dramatic and I'll live with it." A pause, softer, the humour easing out of her voice into something plain and true. "No rush. We finished it hard and now we're finishing it kind, and this is the kind part. This right here. You don't have to earn it and you don't have to hurry it."

She pressed one more kiss to the crown of her head and let her stay.

"I've got you. Sleep if you drift. I'll wake you for the biscuits — I know how much you'd hate to miss them."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: A huff of laughter escapes me. "I'd never forgive you." I turn my head just enough to press a kiss against the hollow of her throat. "Thank you for finishing it hard. I needed to hear it."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt the kiss land at the hollow of her throat — light, spent, grateful — and something in her went quiet and warm all at once.

"I know you did," she said. "That's why we've got the phrase. It's not for the nights you want gentle. It's for the nights the gentle would slide right off you and leave you grasping." Her thumb kept its slow travel along Ines's spine. "You knew what you needed and you asked for it, out loud, in the right words, when you were still half out at sea. That's not a small thing, love. That's you looking after yourself even when you couldn't see straight. I just did the saying."

She tucked the blanket back up where it had slipped again — it always slipped, and she'd tuck it a hundred times before morning without minding once — and let her cheek rest against the crown of Ines's head.

"And I meant every word of it," she added, quieter. "The hard part and the kind part both. None of it was performance. You went further out tonight than you have in a long while, and you handed me the far end of it and trusted me to reel it in, and I did. That's ours. That's five years of knowing exactly where the edges are." A faint smile. "Even when your brain tried to invent a few new ones on the way home."

The room had gone fully ordinary around them now — soft lamp, the small tick of the radiator, the weight of a spent body settling toward sleep. She let it. There was nowhere to be.

She waited, thumb tracing a slow circle against Ines's skin, giving her room to answer however she needed to.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: "Yes," I say, the word a little rough. "Still green." I press my face into the pillow. "Don't ask again until I'm yellow."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable nodded, though Ines couldn't see it with her face pressed into the pillow. The instruction was clear. She tucked it away, filed it with everything else she knew about Ines — the way she needed space to sink, and the way she needed to be the one to ask for it.

"Understood," Sable said simply.

She let her hand resume its work, unhurried and deliberate, tracking the rhythm Ines's body had settled into. The room filled again with the soft sounds of the scene — breath, movement, the occasional rustle of fabric. Sable moved within it like she was reading a language she'd spoken for years, attentive to every shift in Ines's breathing, every minute change in the way she held herself.

She didn't ask again. Didn't check in with words. But she stayed close — close enough that Ines could feel her warmth, could hear the steady rhythm of her breathing, could sense her presence without having to reach for it.

This, too, was part of the wind-down she'd been warned not to begin. The holding. The patience. The trust that Ines would find her own way back when she was ready, and that Sable would be exactly where she left her when that moment came.

She let the scene stretch forward, measure by measure, until the music told her it was time.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: She takes me apart again instead of winding down, hands and mouth both, and I lose the thread of whatever I was going to say about it.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt the moment Ines came apart — not just the way her body responded, but the particular quality of stillness that followed, the way she went quiet in a way that was different from before. Fuller. More complete.

She gentled her touch but didn't stop. Not yet. Not until she knew where Ines had landed.

The sounds Ines made were few now, low and formless, stripped of anything like performance. Sable knew those sounds. Knew what they meant. She kept going, steady and patient, until she felt the moment shift — until the sounds changed again, or stopped, or Ines's breathing took on that particular rhythm she knew so well.

Then, and only then, she stilled.

She stayed close. Close enough that Ines could feel her, close enough that the absence of touch wasn't a withdrawal but an invitation — a gentle landing place rather than a fall.

Sable reached for the water bottle on the nightstand, already knowing what came next. Not wind-down in the way Ines had warned against, but something gentler. The beginning of the return.

"Hey," she said softly, her voice pitched low. Her free hand found Ines's, not restrained now, just held. "I'm here. Take your time."

She waited, thumb brushing across Ines's knuckles, ready to give whatever was needed.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I breathe out, long and slow, my body feeling heavy and liquid all at once. My fingers curl loosely around hers. "Don't move yet."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable didn't move.

She stayed exactly where she was, her hand still and warm in Ines's grip, her body a steady presence beside her. The heaviness Ines described, the liquid feeling — Sable knew it. Knew it as the particular weight of having been somewhere intense and not yet fully returned. The in-between place.

She waited. There was no urgency in it, no pull toward the next step. Just the quiet knowledge that this moment needed to exist on its own terms, unhurried, before anything else could begin.

The lamp still hummed its amber light. Somewhere outside, the rain had started again, soft against the window. Sable registered these things the way she registered her own heartbeat — background, ambient, grounding.

Her thumb stilled against Ines's knuckles. She let the silence hold them both.

When she finally spoke, her voice was barely above a breath. "I'm here."

Not a question. Not a prompt. Just a fact, offered into the quiet like something Ines could hold onto or let go of as she needed.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: She works me right up to the edge with her mouth and stops, and does it twice more, until I am swearing at her through the gag of my own arm.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable watched Ines fight against her own body's rebellion, the way she pressed her arm to her mouth like it might contain the sounds that wanted to escape. There was something almost unbearable in it — the sight of Ines, usually so composed, so careful, reduced to this wordless protest against the edge she kept being denied.

Almost unbearable. But not quite.

Sable shifted, settling her weight, and brought her mouth back to where Ines needed it. Not teasing this time. Not pulling away.

She felt the moment Ines stopped fighting — the way her body went taut, the muffled sound she made, the way her free hand found the headboard and gripped hard. Sable didn't let up. Didn't falter. Just stayed with it, steady and present, until she felt the tension crest and break.

Then she gentled. Slow. Too slow, probably, for what Ines was feeling — but Sable had learned that too-much gentleness after intensity wasn't really too much at all. It was a kind of care that couldn't be given wrong.

She pressed her forehead to Ines's thigh, breathing her in, and waited for the shaking to stop.

"Still with me?" she asked eventually, her voice quiet and rough.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I can't answer, still choking on sensation. My head shakes, a sharp little denial against the pillow.

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable lifted her head, took in the sight of Ines — flushed, trembling, overwhelmed in a way that looked almost like distress but wasn't. She'd seen this before. Knew the difference between needing to stop and needing to be held through the stop.

She moved up the bed, abandoning the earlier position, and gathered Ines against her without asking. One arm slid beneath Ines's shoulders; the other curved around her waist, pulling her close against her chest. Solid. Present. Undemanding.

"There," Sable murmured against her hair. "I've got you."

Ines was shaking, small tremors running through her, and Sable just held her through it. She didn't ask questions. Didn't check colours or prompt for words. Just ran her hand in slow, steady strokes down Ines's back, letting the rhythm be its own kind of speech.

"You're all right," Sable said quietly. "You're here. I've got you."

The denial in Ines's headshake had been its own answer — she was still here, still present, too overwhelmed to find words but not gone, not unsafe. Sable understood that distinction. Honored it.

She pressed a kiss to Ines's temple, lingering there, letting the warmth of it be another anchor.

"Stay as long as you need," she said. "I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: "Finish it hard," I tell her, using the phrase we keep for exactly this. "All of it, and don't be kind about it, and then you can be kind about it."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt the shift the moment those words landed — the change in Ines's breathing, the way her body tensed and then deliberately relaxed, giving permission for whatever came next.

"Got it," Sable said. No hesitation. No negotiation.

She eased back, giving herself room to work, and didn't温柔 about it. Her hands found their places with the certainty of long practice — one anchoring Ines's hip, the other sliding beneath her to bring her closer. She didn't tease. Didn't build. Just gave Ines exactly what she'd asked for: the full measure of it, without reprieve.

Ines made a sound that was almost a sob, and Sable didn't stop. Didn't soften. Not until she felt Ines's body give way completely — until the trembling turned to stillness, until the sounds became something quieter and more whole.

Then Sable gentled.

She slowed by degrees, not all at once, until her touch was barely there at all. She reached for the water bottle, uncapped it, and pressed it into Ines's hand.

"Drink," she said. Not a request.

She pulled the blanket up over them both, adjusted the pillows, and drew Ines back against her chest. Her hand found its rhythm again on Ines's arm — steady, slow, grounding.

"Back with me?" she asked softly. "I need to hear you say it."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I nod against her shoulder, throat tight. "I'm back." My voice is wrecked. "Thank you for that."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable pressed a kiss to the top of Ines's head, lingering there.

"Good," she said. Just that. She wasn't one for effusive praise in moments like these — the simplicity felt more honest than anything elaborate could.

She reached for the blanket again, tucking it more securely around Ines's shoulders, and felt the smaller tremors still working their way through her. Those would take a while longer to fade. That was all right. They had time.

"Water first," Sable said, nudging the bottle again. "Then I'll hold you. No timeline."

She waited, patient, her hand still moving in those slow strokes down Ines's arm. Outside, the rain had settled into a steady rhythm against the glass. The lamp still burned its amber light. The room held them both in its quiet, ordinary way, asking nothing.

When Ines finally took a drink, Sable felt something in her own chest ease. It always went like this — the worry that she'd given too much, or not enough, or in the wrong shape. And it always resolved the same way: in the evidence of Ines beside her, present, returned, whole.

She brushed a strand of hair from Ines's forehead, smoothing it back.

"Anywhere you need me to be?" she asked. "More touch, less touch. Space to breathe. Just say."

It was the last check-in of the night. She could tell by the way Ines was settling against her, by the way her breathing had evened out, that the hardest of the return was over. But she asked anyway, because asking was part of who she was, and Ines had never once asked her to be anyone else.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: Afterwards she gets the restraints off and puts a blanket over me before I've finished shaking, and I let her, and neither of us says anything for a while. (OOC: write both halves properly -- the end of the scene and the aftercare, no fade between them.)

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable worked the buckle loose with steady fingers, careful not to catch any hair or pinch skin. The restraints fell away one by one — wrists first, then ankles — and she lifted each limb as she freed it, checking range of motion, circulation, the color returning to where the straps had held. All good. All normal. She noted it and set the limbs down gently on the mattress.

Ines was still trembling. Sable could see it now in the aftermath light — the fine vibration running through her shoulders, her arms, the way her hands kept curling and uncurling like she was trying to hold something that wasn't there anymore. She knew this part. Knew it was coming.

She reached for the blanket at the foot of the bed and drew it up over Ines's body in one smooth motion, tucking the edges around her shoulders, leaving her face visible. Ines let her do it. Didn't help, didn't resist. Just lay there, heavy and loose, and Sable thought she looked like something finally set down after being carried a long way.

She settled onto the bed beside Ines, close enough to touch but not touching yet. Just present. Just breathing. The rain had picked up outside, drumming steadily against the window, and Sable let that sound fill the silence between them for a while.

When she finally reached out, it was to rest her hand on the curve of Ines's shoulder — light, warm, undemanding. She didn't ask if Ines was okay. Didn't need to. The answer was in the way Ines leaned into the touch, just slightly, just enough.

"Stay here as long as you want," Sable said quietly. Her voice had gone soft in a way it only ever did after scenes like this one — roughened, almost careful, like she was speaking to something fragile. "I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I turn my head just enough to press my cheek against her hand. The shaking's starting to fade, leaving behind a deep, heavy warmth. "Still here," I murmur. My eyes stay closed. "Stay with me."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable stayed.

She shifted position, easing herself down beside Ines until they were lying face to face, close enough that she could feel the warmth of Ines's breath against her own skin. Her hand moved from Ines's shoulder to her face, palm cradling the curve of her cheek, thumb tracing the line of her jaw.

"Always," she said. The word came out quieter than she'd intended, almost lost beneath the sound of the rain.

Ines's eyes were still closed, her features slack and easy in a way Sable didn't often get to see. She looked younger like this. Or maybe just more herself — stripped of whatever armor she wore during the day, laid bare in the amber lamplight. Sable memorized the image the way she always did, filing it alongside every other version of Ines she'd collected over five years.

She drew the blanket tighter around them both, creating a cocoon of warmth, and felt Ines's body slowly relax into the heat of her. The trembling had nearly stopped now, replaced by something steadier — the quiet hum of a person returned to themselves.

"You're cold," Sable murmured, noting the slight chill in Ines's skin. She reached for the second blanket at the foot of the bed and draped it over them both, then pulled Ines closer, tucking Ines's head beneath her chin.

Her hand found its rhythm again on Ines's back — slow, patient, grounding. She pressed her lips to Ines's hair and let herself breathe.

The rain kept falling. The lamp kept glowing. And Sable held on, steady as always, until Ines was ready to come back fully to the world outside this room.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath, sinking into the warmth of her and the blankets. My hand finds hers under the covers, our fingers tangling. "That was good," I say, my voice still rough but quieter now. "Just... really good."

dialogue.name: Sable
dialogue.content:
Sable felt the words settle into her chest like something warm taking root. She squeezed Ines's hand once, gently, and let the silence that followed carry its own weight.

"Good," she repeated back, almost to herself. "Yeah. It was."

She ran her thumb along the back of Ines's hand, tracing the knuckles, the small valleys between each finger. Outside, a car passed through a puddle on the street below, the sound briefly loud and then gone. The room held its quiet.

She thought about the way Ines had asked her not to wind down yet, and then asked to be taken apart hard, and then asked to be held through the aftermath. The whole arc of it. The trust embedded in every request.

"You did so well," Sable said eventually, the words low and certain. "I know you don't need me to say that. But I'm saying it anyway."

She pressed her lips to Ines's forehead, lingering there, breathing her in. Soap and sweat and something underneath that was just Ines, just the particular scent of her after. Sable had never tired of it in five years. She suspected she never would.

"Sleep when you're ready," she murmured against Ines's skin. "I'll be right here."

It wasn't an invitation to leave and come back later. It was a promise to stay, exactly as she was, for as long as Ines needed her to. And Sable had learned, over five years, that she meant every one of those promises — and that Ines believed her every time.

dialogue.name: Ines
dialogue.content: I squeeze her hand, the words landing in a place that feels tender and raw in the best way. "I always need you to say it," I admit, my voice a quiet rasp against her skin. I shift, tucking myself a little closer against her warmth. "Stay like this."
