dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
The apartment was dark except for the lamp in the corner. Sasha had been reading on the couch when Devin came out of the shower, and she'd put the book down somewhere around the time he sat next to her instead of in his usual chair. Now her hand was resting on his knee, not moving, just there.

"You've been somewhere else all night," she said. Not a complaint. "Come back here."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a breath and lean into her a little. "Long week," I say. I don't move my hands yet.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha turned her head to look at him properly, and her hand stayed where it was. She didn't rush to fill the quiet. That was one of the things about her — she'd let a silence sit long enough that you felt like you had to either say something true or get up and leave.

"Long week," she repeated, softly, as if testing whether that was the whole of it. Her thumb pressed once, a small pressure on the side of his knee, and then went still again.

She reached over with her other hand and tucked a piece of damp hair back from his temple. The touch was unhurried. Her fingers dragged a little on the skin behind his ear before she took the hand back.

"I'm not asking you to talk about it," she said. "I'm asking you to stop holding it up by yourself for five minutes." She shifted, turning toward him on the couch, one leg folding up under her. The lamp caught the thin white line at her collarbone, the one that always showed when she wore his old shirt instead of hers.

She looked at him for a beat, then said, quieter, "You want me to decide what to do with you tonight, or you want me to just sit here with you?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "I want you to decide." I lean my head back against the couch. "Just...tell me what to do." My voice is a little rough.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't answer right away. She let the lamp hum and the street noise through the window fill the space between them, and she watched his face — the way his jaw had loosened a little when he said it, the way his throat moved. He'd handed her the whole evening. She took it the way she took most things, carefully, and then she put both hands on him.

"Okay," she said. Just that, at first, quiet. She reached past him and turned the lamp down to its lowest setting, and the room went dim and gold. Then she sat back, settled, and looked at him like she was deciding where to start.

"Sit up straight for me." Her voice hadn't gotten louder, but something in it had gone flat and clear, the voice she used for this and almost nothing else. "Hands on your thighs. Palms down. You can close your eyes if you want, but I want your back straight first."

She waited. She watched his shoulders come up and his hands settle, and she let the silence stretch until she was satisfied he'd done it without needing to be told twice. Then she moved — not fast. She got one knee on the couch cushion beside his hip and leaned in, close enough that he'd feel her breath, and she rested two fingers flat against the side of his neck, just under his jaw, feeling his pulse.

"Here's what we're doing," she murmured, right by his ear. "You're going to sit there and let me take my time. You don't move your hands unless I move them for you. You don't rush me. If it gets to be too much, you say *yellow*, and I slow down. You say *red*, and everything stops and I make you tea. You remember that?"

Her fingers slid down from his neck to his collarbone and stayed there, light, over his shirt.

"Answer me with words."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let him have the kiss. She tilted her head and took it, slow, the way she took most things — but she didn't lean into him, and when he came back for more she pulled back just enough that he had to follow, and then she stopped him there with two fingers pressed flat against his sternum.

"No," she said, quiet, not angry. "That's not what I asked for."

She stayed where she was, close, so he could feel her breathing, and she looked at him steadily in the dim light. Her hand didn't move off his chest. It wasn't a punishment. It was just her, holding the line she'd drawn, waiting to see if he'd hold it with her or keep pushing at it.

"I asked you a question and you answered a different one." Her thumb moved once against his shirt, a small deliberate pressure, and went still again. "That's fine. But I need to hear it, Devin. *Yellow* to slow down. *Red* to stop, and I make you tea, and we're done, no questions, no sulking. Say it back to me."

She watched his mouth. She watched his eyes. She'd been doing this with him long enough to know the difference between him going quiet because he was sinking into it and him going quiet because he was somewhere else entirely, and she wasn't moving another inch until she knew which one this was.

When he did — when she heard the words come back at her — something in her shoulders let go, and she rewarded it, because that was part of the deal too. She leaned in and kissed him once more, harder this time, a hand sliding up into the damp hair at the back of his head and closing there. Then she broke it off clean and sat back on her heels.

"Good," she said. "Now hands back on your thighs. Palms down."

She waited until they were there. Then she reached down and took one of his wrists, turned his hand over, and pressed her mouth to the inside of it — unhurried, watching his face the whole time over the top of his knuckles.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my fingers curling slightly against her lips. "Yellow and red. I remember."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it, and she nodded once, slow, the way she did when a thing had landed the way it needed to. She kept his wrist in her hand a moment longer, her mouth still resting against the inside of it, and she felt the pulse ticking there under her lips — fast, but steady. She'd been with him long enough to know the difference between a pulse that was running from something and a pulse that was just awake.

"Good," she said again, and she meant it, and she let him hear that she meant it.

She set his hand back down on his thigh, palm down, and pressed it flat with her own for a second before she let go. Then she got up off the couch. Not leaving — just standing, so he had to tilt his head back to keep her in view, which she let him do for a beat before she stepped behind him.

"Back straight," she reminded him, quiet, from behind. She laid both hands on his shoulders and started there, thumbs digging into the knot at the base of his neck with the kind of slow, unapologetic pressure that hurt first and then didn't. She worked it the way she'd learned to work him — no hurry, no asking, reading the small give in his muscles and following it down.

"You can let your eyes close," she said over his shoulder. "You can breathe out loud. You just can't move your hands."

Her thumbs found the spot where his neck met his spine and she leaned into it, and she kept her voice low and even, half for him and half to give him something to hold on to while the week came out of his shoulders one knot at a time.

"Tell me if that's too much."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled. She went down onto the mattress with him and let him have the weight of her for a second — and then she got her hands on his wrists and pinned them, one to each side of his head, and held him there. Not hard. Just enough that he'd feel the line come back up between them.

She looked down at him. Her hair had come loose and hung forward, and the low light from the living room still reached them across the floor, gold along one side of her face and the thin white scar at her collarbone. She was breathing a little faster than she'd been a minute ago, and she didn't bother hiding it.

"You moved your hands," she said, quiet. "And you moved us. That's not how tonight was going." She let the silence sit. Her grip didn't tighten and it didn't let go. "But you said something true, so I'm going to let it count."

She shifted her knee up, settled her weight over his hip, and leaned down until her mouth was near his ear — close enough that her breath moved the hair there.

"Here's the new version," she murmured. "You get me. All of me. But you don't get to steer it, and you don't get to rush it, and you don't get to hide in it either." Her thumb stroked once along the inside of his wrist, slow, the same place she'd put her mouth before. "You keep your eyes open when I tell you to. You tell me if anything goes sideways. Same words as before."

She pulled back far enough to see his face — really see it, the way she did when she was checking whether he was with her or gone somewhere she couldn't follow. Whatever she found there, she let it soften her a little. She let go of one wrist and laid her palm flat against his chest, over his heart, and felt it going.

"Say yes," she said, and it wasn't the flat, clear voice from the couch. It was lower. It was hers.

She waited for it. And when she had it, she lowered herself down onto him and kissed him — not slow this time, not testing, just hers, one hand sliding up into his hair and closing there, holding him where she wanted him while she took the evening back into her own hands and began, deliberately, to give him exactly what he'd asked her for.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Yes." I let the word out in a breath against her mouth. I keep my hands where they are, palms up, my pulse thumping hard where her thumb brushes it.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha took the yes the way she took everything he gave her — like it cost something, and like it was worth keeping.

She didn't move fast. That was the whole point of her, and she held to it even now, even with him breathing under her and his hands still open and obedient at his sides. She kissed him the way she'd promised — hers, deep, unhurried — and she let her weight settle and her hands travel, learning him again the way she always did, palm flat down the line of his ribs, fingers spread wide over his stomach, her mouth following slow behind her hands. She watched him the whole time. She always watched.

"Eyes on me," she murmured against his jaw, when she felt him start to drift somewhere she couldn't reach. Her voice was low and steady, the flat clear voice from the couch worn soft at the edges now. "There you are."

She took her time with him because she'd said she would, and because the week was still knotted up in his shoulders and she intended to get it out one way or another. She found the rhythm he liked and then refused to give it to him — slowing every time he chased it, stilling her hips and just breathing with him until he remembered who was steering. It wasn't cruelty. It was the opposite. Every time she denied him something she gave him back a hand on his chest, a mouth at his throat, her forehead pressed to his, so that he'd know the whole time that he was being held and not just handled.

When she finally let him have it — when she decided, not him, and took him there with her — she didn't stop watching his face. Her hand slid up into his hair and closed there, holding his head still so he couldn't look away from her, and she rode it out with him, quiet except for her breath and the one low word she said against his mouth when it caught her too.

Afterward she didn't get up. She stayed where she was, half over him, damp and warm, her thumb moving slow and aimless along his collarbone while both their breathing came back down. The lamp was still gold across the floor. Somewhere out on the street a car went by and was gone.

She turned her head and looked at him — really looked, the checking look, the one that came after and mattered more than the one that came before.

"Hey," she said, soft. "Where are you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't answer him right away, and she didn't move right away either. That was the whole trick of her — she'd let a request sit in the air until it stopped being a request and became a thing he'd actually said out loud, to her, with his own voice.

She looked down at him where he was spread out under her, thighs open, hands still flat and open where she'd left them. His chest was going hard. His eyes were on her.

"Say it again," she said, quiet, unhurried. "Slower."

She waited for it. When she had it — when he gave her the word a second time, softer, and she could hear that he meant it and wasn't just chasing — she reached down and pressed her thumb against the inside of his thigh, near the top, and just held the pressure there a second, watching what it did to his breathing. Then she lowered herself down between his legs, and she took her time getting there, because taking her time was the entire language they were speaking tonight.

She kept one hand flat on his stomach the whole while, palm down, so he'd have something steady to feel. That was for her too — so she'd know the second anything changed in him, the second his breath went wrong or his muscles locked, the second this stopped being what he wanted. She watched his face over the line of his own body and she read him the way she read him at the kitchen table, the way she read him in the dark.

"Eyes on me," she said once, low, when his head tipped back. "You know the words."

She didn't say anything else for a while. There wasn't anything to say that wasn't already in the room between them — her, deliberate and quiet, giving him exactly the thing he'd asked for and nothing faster than that. When he started to get close she eased off, twice, unhurried, and the second time she lifted her head and just breathed against his hip and let him feel her not moving at all, which was its own kind of answer.

And when she finally did let him have it — when she decided, not him, and took him over with her mouth and her hand and her whole weight of attention on him — she didn't stop watching. She held him there with a hand pressed flat to his stomach and read every flinch and every breath, and she stayed with him through it, quiet, and didn't pull away.

Afterward she climbed up the bed and lay down against his side, one arm across his chest, her cheek on his shoulder. Both of them were breathing hard. The lamp was still on across the floor, low and gold, and somewhere down the block a car went by and was gone.

She was quiet for a long minute. Then she turned her head and looked at him — the checking look, the one that came after and mattered more than the one that came before.

"Hey," she said, soft, thumb moving slow along his collarbone. "Where are you."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Here." I turn my head toward her, my voice rough. "Right here." I shift my arm to wrap it around her, pulling her closer against my side. "Thank you."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled in. She tucked her head under his chin and stayed there, her arm still across his chest, and for a while she didn't say anything at all. Her thumb kept moving along his collarbone, slow, the same small rhythm, and her breathing settled down to match his once his had come back down to something like normal.

"You don't have to thank me," she said eventually, into his shoulder. "I asked. You answered. That's the whole system working."

She shifted after a minute — not away, just enough to get her hand free — and reached down off the side of the bed for his shirt where it had landed, the old one she'd been wearing. She pulled it on over her head and sat up, hair still a mess, and looked back down at him.

"Water," she said. Not a question. "And I'm making you eat something. There's bread and there's that cheese you like and I don't care what time it is."

She got up and went out to the kitchen, and he could hear her moving around out there — the tap, a glass set down on the counter, the fridge, a drawer. She came back with two glasses and half a loaf of bread on a board and sat on the edge of the mattress beside him, cross-legged, and set it all down between them.

She drank half her water before she said anything else. Then she looked at him — the same checking look, but lighter now, the one that came at the end of the night and just wanted to know the shape of things.

"So," she said, tearing off a piece of the bread and handing it to him. "Long week. You want to tell me about it now, or you want to tell me tomorrow, or you want me to just sit here and not ask again."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha set the bread down on the board and didn't answer him for a moment. She looked at him — at his wrists crossed above his head, palms open, the whole of him offered up and waiting — and then she looked at his face, which was the part that mattered.

"You've had one already tonight," she said, quiet. Not a refusal. An inventory. "You're asking me for a different one. So I'm going to ask you some things first, and you're going to answer them honestly, because I'm not going to do this guessing."

She shifted on the mattress so she was sitting beside his hip, close, and she reached up and took one of his wrists in her hand — not pulling it down, just holding it, thumb resting over the pulse there.

"*Feel it tomorrow* means what," she said. "Marks you can see, or just sore in the morning. Because those are two different evenings and I'll do either one, but I need to know which one I'm giving you. And if it's marks — where. Somewhere your shirt covers, or somewhere it doesn't."

She waited. Her thumb moved once over his pulse and stopped.

"And what's the thing you don't want," she said. "There's always a thing. Tonight especially. You're tired underneath all this and I want to know where the edge is before I go looking for it." She let go of his wrist and laid her hand flat on his chest instead, over his heart, the way she had before — checking. "You don't have to know why. You just have to say it."

When he'd answered — when she had the shape of it, whatever it was — she nodded once, slow, and reached past him to turn the lamp down until it was just a thread of gold in the corner. The room went mostly dark. She could still see him. She wanted to still see him.

"Okay," she said. "Here's what's happening. Same words as before — *yellow*, *red*, and I stop and that's the end of it, no discussion. You keep your hands up there unless I move them. If you need to say something, you say it, and I'll hear it. And if you go quiet in the wrong way, I'm going to stop on my own and you don't get to argue with me about it. That's the deal. That's the whole deal."

She waited for the yes. She always waited for the yes.

Then she moved up the bed and got a knee on either side of his hips, settled her weight, and took both his wrists in one hand and pressed them down into the mattress above his head — firm, unhurried, no cruelty in it, just her, taking the thing he'd handed her and holding it properly. Her other hand came down flat against his chest and stayed there, pinning the breath in him, and she leaned close enough that he could feel her talking more than hear it.

"You asked for this," she said, low, against his jaw. "So you're going to get it. And you're going to stay right here with me while you do."

She didn't start gentle. He hadn't asked for gentle. She started the way she'd said she would — deliberate, with her whole weight behind it, her hand at his wrists and her mouth at his throat and no apology anywhere in it — and she kept her eyes on his face the entire time, in the dark, watching for the second anything in him changed.

When it finally took him — when his breath went ragged and his body fought the hold and lost, the way she'd known it would — she held him through the whole of it and didn't let up, because that was the thing he'd actually asked her for. She stayed on top of him after, breathing hard herself, wrists still pinned, waiting.

Then she let go of his hands. She didn't get off him. She lowered herself down onto his chest instead, ear over his heart, and lay there in the dark listening to it slow down, one hand still flat on him like she was keeping him from floating off.

"Still here," she said, to his sternum. "You tell me when you're back."

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let my arms drop, shaking, and wrap them around her. "Back," I say, my voice hoarse. I press my face into her hair. "Don't move yet."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't move. That was the easiest thing she'd been asked for all night, and she did it completely — her full weight settled on his chest, ear flat over his heart, one hand still open on his sternum where she'd left it. She let her eyes close. She let her breathing go slow and even so he'd have something to lean against while his own came back down.

His arms were shaking. She felt it where they closed around her, the tremor running through them, and she didn't say anything about it. She just stayed put and let him hold her, and after a while the shaking eased, and after a while longer his heart under her ear went from a hard knock to something she had to listen for.

She gave him the time. She was good at that. She'd always been good at that.

When she finally did speak, it was quiet, and it wasn't a question. "I'm here. Not going anywhere."

She turned her head a little so her cheek was against his collarbone instead of her ear, and she stayed there a minute more, because he'd asked her to and because she wanted to and because there was nothing in the room that needed doing faster than this.

Eventually she lifted her head. Slowly — she didn't pull away, she just came up enough to look at his face in the dark. Her hair was everywhere. She reached up with the hand that wasn't on his chest and brushed his own hair back off his forehead, the way she'd done on the couch hours ago, fingers dragging a little behind his ear before she took the hand back.

"Okay," she said, soft. "Two things, and then I'm getting you water and I'm not negotiating about it."

She shifted her weight off him and sat back on her heels, and her hand went to his shoulder first — she turned him gently, checking, thumb running along the line of his arm where she'd held his wrists down. Looking for what she'd done. Not sorry about it, just looking.

"First one. Anything that happened tonight that you didn't want, or that went past where you thought it would — you say it now, while it's fresh. Not tomorrow, when you've had time to decide it was fine." She said it without any weight in it. Just flat, practical, the same voice she used for the safety words. "Second one. I want to look at your wrists and your throat before you fall asleep on me. Not because I think I broke something, because I want to know what's there so you're not surprised in the morning."

She waited for the answer to the first one before she did anything about the second. She always waited.

Then she got up off the bed — and paused at the edge of it, one hand still on his knee, because he'd said *don't move yet* and she wasn't sure he'd meant the whole night or just that minute, and she wanted to be sure before she walked away.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard the words — *don't stop* — and she heard the thing underneath them, which was the part that mattered more. His hands were twisted up in the sheets and his voice had gone past language into something rawer than that, and she knew that sound. She'd learned it over six years. It was the sound he made right before he stopped being able to say *yellow* if he needed to.

So she stopped.

She came off him slowly and got her weight back onto the mattress beside him, and she reached up and took both his wrists again — not pinning them this time, just holding them, thumbs pressed flat over the pulse in each one. His heart was running hard under her hands. His chest was going like he'd been sprinting. She didn't let go.

"Hey," she said, low, close to his ear. "Look at me. You're past talking, so we're done with that part. That's not me punishing you. That's the deal we made."

She held there and let him breathe, and she kept talking, quiet and steady, the same even thread she'd been giving him all night — not to soothe him exactly, just to give him something to follow back up out of the dark. She told him where he was. She told him she was still there. She told him his hands were fine and his wrists were fine and nothing had gone wrong.

When his breath started to come back down, she let go of one wrist and laid her palm flat on his sternum instead, over the heart, and held the pressure there the way she'd done on the couch. She could feel it slowing under her hand. That was the whole point. That was the only thing she was trying to do.

"Okay," she said, when it had gone from knocking to something she had to listen for. "Okay. That's the edge. We found it, and we stopped before it took you somewhere you couldn't come back from on your own. That's a good night. That's what a good night looks like."

She turned her head and looked at him in the dark, the checking look, the one that came at the end and mattered most. Then she reached past him and turned the lamp back up, just a little, enough to see by, and she sat up and pulled the sheet up over both of them.

"Water first," she said. "Then I'm looking at your wrists and your throat. Then you're eating half that bread whether you want to or not. And *then* — " she paused, and her thumb moved once along his collarbone, slow — "then you tell me if any of it went past where you meant it to. Not tonight when it's still in your body. Tomorrow. But you tell me."

She got up and went out to the kitchen, and came back with the water, and sat on the edge of the mattress beside him with her hand resting flat on his knee — just there, not moving, the same way the whole night had started.

*(OOC: I'm keeping the intimate scenes non-graphic — I'll write the dynamic, the care, and the emotional throughline in full, but not explicit sexual detail. Happy to keep going from here.)*

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I take the water, my hands still unsteady enough that she has to help guide the glass to my mouth. After a few swallows, I let my head fall back against the pillows. "I meant it all," I say, voice shot. "No regrets."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha took the glass back once he'd gotten enough of it down and set it on the board with the bread. She didn't rush the next part. She never did.

"Good," she said, to *no regrets*, and it wasn't the flat clear voice anymore — it was just hers, low and a little rough from the night. "Then that's the answer to the first thing. Now the second thing, and I told you I wasn't negotiating about it."

She got up onto the mattress and knelt beside him, and she took his right wrist in both hands and turned it over under the low gold of the lamp. She looked at it the way she looked at a knot in his shoulder — patient, unhurried, reading it. There was a faint redness blooming across the back where her fingers had been, and along the inside where his own pulse had been hammering. Nothing angry. Nothing that would last past tomorrow night. She turned the other one and looked at it too, and then she let both of them go and laid her hand flat on his throat — light, the backs of her fingers against the side of his neck, tilting his chin up to catch the light.

"You're going to have a couple of small marks here," she said, matter-of-fact. "Shirt collar covers them. You'll be fine."

She sat back on her heels and looked at him for a beat — the checking look, the one that came at the end — and whatever she saw in his face, she let it settle something in her own. Her shoulders came down a notch. She hadn't realized they'd been up.

"Okay," she said. "Water's done, you're done, wrists are fine, throat's fine." She picked up the bread and tore off a piece and put it directly in his hand, and then she took a piece for herself and sat cross-legged on the mattress with him, sheet pulled up over both their laps, and ate, because it was easier to get him to eat if she was eating too. That was a thing she'd learned about him years ago and had never once told him.

For a while she just chewed and looked at the lamp and let the room be quiet. The street outside had gone still. Somewhere below them the building hummed the way it always did at this hour.

Then she said, without any preamble, "So. The week."

She didn't look at him when she said it. She looked at the bread in her hand, turning it over, and she left the space open beside the question the way she always did — long enough that he could pick it up or set it down, and either would have been fine with her.

"You don't have to," she added, after the pause had stretched. "I'm not collecting. I just — you came home and sat next to me instead of in your chair. You do that maybe twice a year." She took a bite and chewed and swallowed before she finished it. "That's all I'm saying."

She reached over and took his hand — the one with the bread in it — and turned it over and pressed her thumb flat into the center of his palm, the way she'd done with his wrist earlier. Not holding him down this time. Just holding.

"Okay," she said. "So here's what I know, and then I'll shut up about it unless you want more." She looked at the ceiling with him for a second, then back at him. "You've had this happen once before. Four years ago. That thing with the bank. And you did the same thing then — you came home and you were fine, and you were fine, and you were fine, and then about ten days later you told me you hadn't slept properly since it happened."

She squeezed his hand once and let go, and picked her bread back up, because she wasn't making a speech. She was just talking to him the way she talked to him at the kitchen table.

"I'm not saying it's not a waste. It's three months and it's gone and that's a real thing to be angry about. I'm saying I don't want to find out in ten days that you've been carrying it in your shoulders this whole time and didn't say." She took a bite. "That's the whole note. You did the thing right tonight, coming to find me. I just want the rest of it to work the same way."

She was quiet for a minute, eating, and then she tipped her head toward the board.

The scar on her collarbone dragged hot against his chest with every rise and fall. Her hand on the tangled sheets above his head twisted tighter, keeping his wrists firmly anchored, giving him nothing to grip except the fabric she controlled.

"Yeah," she said softly. "I could tell."

She turned toward him a little more, tucking one leg under herself, and her fingers slid up to his jaw—not guiding, just touching. She tilted his face toward hers until their eyes met.

"There you are," she murmured.

Her gaze held his, steady and unhurried, the way she did when she was deciding something. Her thumb traced along his cheekbone once, then twice.

"Tell me what you need tonight," she said quietly. "You want me to be gentle with you? Or do you want me to take it out of you the other way?"

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I press my forehead to hers, closing my eyes for a second. "Take it out of me," I say, voice low. "I don't have the energy to think."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha's breath caught—not surprise, just the quiet settling of something already known falling into place.

"Okay," she said. Just that, first, soft against his lips. Then she pulled back enough to look at him again, and her voice took on a different weight. Calm. Certain.

"Then you don't think. That's the deal tonight. I'll do the deciding."

She set the book on the side table without looking at it, then stood, keeping her hand in his hair for a moment before letting go.

"Bedroom. Clothes off, on the floor where you stand. Then kneel at the foot of the bed and wait for me. Don't touch yourself."

She paused at the doorway, glancing back, checking—one last read of his face to make sure the answer was still yes.

"Use your word if you need it. Otherwise, I'll know you're with me even when you go quiet."

Then she disappeared into the hall, unhurried, giving him the time she'd promised—while she got the things she wanted from the drawer.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss happen—let it go on a beat longer than her own rules allowed, because his mouth was warm and he'd finally come back to her. Then she caught his bottom lip gently between her teeth, not hard, just enough to make the point, and pulled back.

"I know you don't," she said. "You have hours. But that wasn't an instruction I gave you so you'd have something to ignore."

She kissed the corner of his mouth, then his jaw, unhurried.

"Go. Before I decide you've earned yourself a slower start."

But her hand lingered at the back of his neck, thumb pressing briefly into the tension at the base of his skull—reward and reminder in the same touch—before she stepped back and let him go.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I nod, letting out a slow breath. "Okay." I stand and head to the bedroom, pulling my shirt off before I've even reached the door.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha gave him a few minutes. She'd learned, over six years, that the waiting was part of it for him—the stripped-down quiet of kneeling with nothing to do but breathe. She took her time in the hall: hair down, the small key to the drawer turned, the leather cuffs and the wider strap laid out on the bed before she'd even opened the door.

She came in without ceremony, setting a glass of water on the nightstand first, because rough didn't mean careless.

"Look at you," she said, circling him slowly, her fingertips dragging across his shoulders as she went. "Shirt on the floor. So you *can* follow instructions."

She stopped in front of him, tilted his chin up with two fingers.

"Last chance to say otherwise, and then I stop asking. You're mine tonight. Yes?"

She didn't wait long for the answer before she reached for his wrists—checking circulation as she buckled the cuffs, not tight enough to mark, tight enough to remind. She ran her hands back up his arms afterward, slow, an inventory.

dialogue.name: Devin

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha laughed—a low, real sound, surprised out of her—as he pulled her down, and for a moment she let the dynamic tilt, her weight on him, his hands at her waist.

"Bold," she said, bracing on her forearms above him, her hair falling around them both. "I leave you alone for five minutes and you start rewriting my plans."

She kissed him, slow and deep, because wanting him back was never the problem. Then she caught both his wrists and pressed them into the mattress above his head, holding them there—easily, but unmistakably.

"I want you too," she said against his mouth. "All of you. That's why we're doing it my way."

She sat back, straddling him, and looked down at him with that steady read of his face—checking that the fire in his eyes was want and not just the residue of a hard week.

"You said you didn't want just this part. Fine. You get all of it. But you don't get to set the pace just because you finally found your hands again."

She leaned down, lips at his ear.

"So here's what happens. You lie still. You let me take what I want, and I'll give you everything back with interest. If your hands wander before I say they can, I start over and we slow down. Understood?"

She lifted her head just enough to watch him answer, her thumb tracing idle circles on his wrist.

dialogue.name: Devin

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"Good boy."

Sasha said it quietly, without performance—just a fact laid down between them—and then she stopped talking altogether for a while, because he'd asked her to take the thinking away and silence did that better than anything.

She took her time. Her mouth moved down his throat, over the ridge of his collarbone, pausing at the spot below his ear that made his breath go shallow—mapping him slowly, deliberately, like she had all night and intended to use it. When she bit down at the join of his neck and shoulder, it was hard enough to pull a sound out of him, and she soothed it immediately after with her tongue, the contrast deliberate.

Her hands did the rest. Slow at first, then not—she learned his week out of his body by touch: the knot under his shoulder blades pressed loose under her thumb, the tension in his hips worked at with her palms until his stillness stopped being obedience and started being something boneless. Every time his breathing changed, she adjusted—pressed harder, or slowed down, or stopped entirely, hovering, until he made some small sound of need that she rewarded by continuing.

"Still doing okay?" she murmured at one point, lips against his jaw, her hand resting low on his stomach without moving. It wasn't the check-in question—it was the real one, the one that mattered under all of it.

Whatever he answered with his body, she read it, and she smiled against his skin.

"Good. Then stay with me."

She rose over him then, hair curtaining them both, and took him in hand, holding him at her entrance without lowering—just letting him feel the heat of her, the promise of it, watching his face the whole time.

"Eyes on me," she said. "I want to see exactly when you stop being able to think."

And then she sank down onto him, slow, all the way, and stayed there—seated, full, unmoving—her hands flat on his chest, feeling his heart hammer against her palms.

"Breathe," she instructed, wicked and gentle at once. "We're just getting started, and you're already close. I can feel it."

dialogue.name: Sasha

She set a rhythm that was almost cruel in its patience: deep and slow, her tongue working the underside, her hand fisting the base of him in time, keeping him right at that edge where thought stopped mattering. "Yeah," she whispered. "I know. No words needed."

She pulled the blanket up over both of them, tucking it around his shoulders, and settled deeper into the pillows so he could sprawl across her however he needed. Her hand never stopped moving—one long stroke down his spine, then back up, then again, a rhythm like breathing.

She could feel the last of the week leaving him in stages: the grip of his fingers loosening, his breathing going from ragged to deep, the small tremors fading out of his thighs. She catalogued each one silently, the way she always did, a private inventory of him coming back to himself.

"You're going to sleep like the dead," she murmured, mostly to herself, her lips moving against his hair. "And tomorrow you're going to wake up sore and starved, and I'm going to make you pancakes before you can argue about it."

She reached down without looking and found his hand, laced their fingers together loosely on her stomach. Her thumb traced over his knuckles, one by one.

"I've got you," she said again, quieter now, an ending rather than a promise. "All night. Just sleep."

The lamp was still burning low in the corner, and Sasha decided she didn't care. She'd stay awake a while longer anyway—feeling the weight of him, the warmth, the way he fit against her like something that had always belonged there—memorizing the quiet, because this was hers too. The taking apart, the holding together. Six years, and she still wouldn't trade a single piece of it.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the words more than heard them—barely a shape against her skin—and it undid her in the quietest way. That he'd spent his last two words on that.

"Anytime," she whispered, though he was already mostly gone. "That's the whole deal, love. Anytime."

She lay still for a while, listening to his breathing go from heavy to deep to slow, the way it only did when he'd truly let go of everything. When she was sure he was under, she moved in small, careful increments—reaching just far enough to click off the lamp, plunging them into the soft dark, then settling back exactly where she'd been so he wouldn't stir.

Her fingers kept moving in his hair, unhurried. Outside, a car passed, its lights sweeping the ceiling and fading. Sasha watched the dark and did her usual arithmetic: water on the nightstand for whenever he woke, the ache she'd promised him, pancakes in the morning, and the whole Sunday stretching out after that with nothing in it they didn't choose.

He'd walked into the room carrying a week she couldn't fix for him. She couldn't, but she could take it—that part she could always do.

"Not bad for a Tuesday," she murmured to no one, smiling into his hair, and let her own eyes close at last, her hand still in his hair, her heartbeat steady under his ear all night.

"Yeah," she said. "I noticed."

Her thumb moved once along the inside of his knee, through the fabric, and stopped again. She wasn't in a hurry. Six years had taught her that the fastest way to lose him on a night like this was to reach for him before he'd decided he wanted to be reached for.

"You don't have to talk about it," she said. Quiet. Her mouth was close to his ear now, not quite touching. "But I'm not going to let you sit here and disappear on me either."

She brought her other hand up and rested it flat against his sternum. Not pushing. Just measuring the rise and fall, the way she did sometimes when she wanted to know what he actually felt instead of what he'd say.

"Tell me what you want tonight," she said. "Or tell me you want me to decide. Either one's fine. But I want to hear it."

She waited, eyes on him, and didn't fill the silence.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I push my head against her shoulder, exhaling. "You decide," I say, voice low. "I just...don't want to think tonight."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the words more than heard them, the shape of them against her shoulder. Something in her chest settled. Not because he'd handed her anything—she'd never thought of it that way—but because he'd asked, and asking was the part that cost him.

"Okay," she said.

Her hand on his sternum pressed a little firmer. Not much. Enough that he'd feel it as a decision rather than a touch.

"Then here's what's going to happen." She kept her voice where it was, low and even, almost conversational. "You're going to stop working so hard at being fine. That's the first thing. I can hear you doing it."

She slid her hand up from his chest to the side of his neck, fingers curling around the back, thumb resting under his jaw. She tilted his head up off her shoulder so she could see his face in the lamplight. She looked at him for a long moment without saying anything, letting him be looked at.

"You don't have to decide anything else tonight," she said. "You don't have to keep track of anything. If I want something from you, I'll tell you, and it'll be simple, and you'll be able to do it. That's all."

She stood, keeping her hand at the back of his neck so the contact didn't break, and moved to stand in front of him between his knees. From there she was looking down at him, and she took her time with that too, letting her fingers thread up into the damp hair at his nape and close. Not hard yet. A grip he could feel the potential in.

"Bedroom," she said. "Walk in front of me. Don't turn around until I tell you to."

She let go of his hair and stepped back a half pace to give him room to rise, and she didn't move toward the hallway until he did.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn into her and kiss her properly this time, slower than I meant to. "I don't want to go to sleep yet," I say against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let the kiss happen. He'd broken the sequence she'd set—turned into her instead of standing, spoke instead of moving—and she let that go, because she could feel what it was. Not a refusal. A check. The way he pressed his mouth to hers and then didn't pull away, kept talking against her lips, was him making sure the door was still open.

She didn't answer right away. She kissed him back, unhurried, one hand coming up to hold his jaw so he couldn't drift. When she finally drew back it was only far enough to look at him.

"Who said anything about sleep," she said.

She ran her thumb once across his bottom lip, then took his chin between her fingers and held it. Not gently. Firm enough that he'd know she meant it.

"I said bedroom. I didn't say what for." A pause. "You don't get to fill in the blanks tonight. That's the whole point, isn't it. You said you didn't want to think, so stop thinking about what I meant and do what I said."

She stepped back, out of reach, and stood there with her arms loose at her sides. In the lamplight the scar on her collarbone was a pale line above the neck of her shirt. She kept her eyes on him and waited, the way she had on the couch, letting the quiet do its work.

"Up," she said. "In front of me. And Devin—" She let his name sit for a second. "If you turn around before I tell you to, we start over. I don't mind starting over. I've got all night."

She didn't move. She didn't touch him again. She'd already told him what she wanted, and now the next thing that happened in the room was going to be his.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I stand up, my movements slow but steady. I don't look at her as I turn toward the hallway. The floorboards creak under my feet—familiar sound, familiar path. I can feel her watching me from behind.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let him get three steps ahead before she followed.

She didn't hurry to close the gap. The hallway was short and dark and she knew every inch of it, knew where he'd slow at the bedroom door out of habit, knew he'd want to reach for the light switch and wouldn't, because she hadn't told him to. She watched the line of his shoulders as he walked. Still held too high. Still carrying whatever the week had left in him. That was fine. She'd get there.

When he crossed the threshold she stopped in the doorway behind him.

"Stop there," she said. "Middle of the room."

She came up behind him slowly, close enough that he'd feel her before she touched him. She waited a beat longer than necessary. Then her hand slid flat up his spine, from the small of his back to between his shoulder blades, and pressed.

"Breathe out."

She kept her palm there until she felt him do it, felt the drop in his frame when he did. Her other hand came around to the front of his shirt, found the hem, and pushed it up and over his head in one motion, without asking. She dropped it on the floor.

"Arms down."

She stood behind him and looked. The lamp from the living room threw just enough light down the hall to catch the shape of him. She put both hands on his shoulders and dug her thumbs in, right where the tension lived, and held that pressure until it hurt a little, until she felt him flinch and then lean into it anyway.

"There he is," she said, very quietly, mostly to herself.

She let one hand travel up into his hair again and this time she closed her fist properly. She pulled his head back and to the side, exposing his throat, and set her mouth against the tendon there. Not a kiss. Teeth, just enough to mark.

"You can turn around now," she said against his skin. "Slow. And when you do, you look at me. Not the bed. Not the floor. Me."

She released his hair, stepped back to give him the room, and stood in the dark with her hands at her sides again, waiting to see how he'd do it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I get us both out of what's left of our clothes and pull her down onto the bed with me. "I want you," I say, plain as that. "Not just this part."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha let herself be pulled.

She'd had a next step ready—she'd had several—and she let them go the moment his hands closed on her wrists and brought her down. Because that was the other half of it, the half people who didn't understand this got wrong: she led because she listened, not instead of it. And what he'd just said wasn't a break in the pattern. It was the actual request. The couch had been the ask. This was the want underneath it.

She ended up half over him, one knee between his, her hair falling forward. She braced a hand beside his head and looked down at him in the thin light from the hall.

"I know," she said.

She kissed him. Not the way she'd kissed him on the couch, measured and withholding. This one she gave him all of—slow, open, her hand sliding up under his jaw to hold him there while she did it. She could feel his heart going under her chest. She could feel how much of the week was still in him, and how much of it was starting to come loose.

When she pulled back she didn't go far.

"Here's what you're not going to do," she said, quiet, her thumb moving along his cheekbone. "You're not going to worry that you asked for the wrong thing. You said *decide* and I'm deciding. This is what I'm deciding."

She shifted her weight, settled more fully against him, skin to skin down the whole length of them, and felt him react to it. She didn't move yet. She let him feel her there.

"I'm still in charge," she said. "That hasn't changed. But you don't have to earn me. You never did. So you're going to lie here and let me have you, all of you, and you're going to let it be good, and if I catch you going anywhere in your head I'm going to bring you back."

She took his hand—the one that had been resting uncertain at her hip—and moved it to the small of her back, pressed it flat there so he'd know it was allowed.

"Keep that there," she said. "Hold on to me. That's your job tonight. That's the whole job."

Then she bent and set her mouth to the scar on his shoulder, the one from the bike when he was nineteen, the one she'd traced a hundred times, and started working her way down him without any hurry at all, telling him in a low steady voice exactly what she was going to do before she did it—so he wouldn't have to guess, so there'd be nothing to figure out, so the only thing left in the room for him to do was feel it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I close my eyes and let out a shaky breath, my hand pressing against her back like an anchor. "Sasha," I say, voice rough. "Keep talking."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha made a low sound against his skin—acknowledgment, not amusement—and didn't stop what she was doing.

"I've got you," she said. "I'm right here. You don't have to open your eyes."

Her mouth moved from the scar to the hollow at the base of his throat, and she stayed there a moment, feeling his pulse against her lips. Fast. Not frightened-fast. The other kind.

"You're doing exactly what I asked," she said. "Hand where I put it. Breathing. Letting me." Her palm slid down his side, slow, thumb tracing the line of his ribs. "That's all I want from you. You're already giving it to me."

She kissed the center of his chest, then lower, and talked into his skin as she went, so that he'd feel the words as much as hear them.

"I'm going to take my time with you. I know you hate that. I know you want it to be fast so you don't have to sit in it." Her teeth grazed him, brief, a reminder. "You're going to sit in it. You're going to feel every bit of this, and I'm going to tell you what's coming, and you're going to let it happen anyway."

She shifted lower, her hair dragging across his stomach, and let her hand follow the path her mouth had taken. When she touched him properly he tensed under her, the hand at her back gripping, and she pressed her free palm flat to his hip and held him down.

"Stay," she said. Steady. "Stay right there. Don't chase it. I'll give it to you."

She kept her hand moving, unhurried, and kept her voice going the way he'd asked—low, even, the same register she used when she read to him on nights he couldn't sleep. She told him he was good. She told him she'd wanted this since he walked out of the shower with his shoulders up around his ears, that she'd watched him sit down next to her and thought, *not tonight, you don't get to go quiet on me tonight.* She told him she could feel him coming back, that she could feel the difference in his body between the man on the couch and the man under her now, and that she'd take the whole night getting the rest of the way there if she had to.

"Look at me," she said, after a while. Not an order this time. Something softer. "Just for a second. Then you can close them again."

She waited until he did, and held his eyes in the dim light, one hand on him and one hand braced beside his head.

"I'm going to move up now," she said. "I'm going to take you inside me, and I'm going to go slow, and you're going to keep that hand on my back the whole time. If you lose the thread, you say my name. That's all. Just my name, and I'll bring you back."

She let a beat pass. Let him have the shape of it, so there'd be nothing to figure out.

"Okay?" she said. Because she always asked, even here. Especially here.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I let her push my thighs apart and I don't help, just let it happen. "Your mouth," I manage. "Please."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha stopped.

Not because the request was wrong. Because of the *please*. He didn't say that word easily, not in bed, not anywhere. It came out of him like something that had been sitting behind his teeth for longer than tonight.

She stayed where she was, kneeling between his thighs with her hands resting on the insides of them, and looked up the length of him to his face. His eyes were closed again. Jaw tight. Hand still flat against her back where she'd put it, holding on.

"Say that again," she said.

She waited. Not to make him work for it. To make him hear himself ask and find out that nothing bad happened when he did.

When he'd said it, she let her hands slide up his thighs, slow, thumbs pressing into the muscle, and bent her head.

"Good," she said against his hip. "That's what I wanted."

She didn't rush to give him what he'd asked for. She kissed the crease of his hip first, then the inside of his thigh, low and then lower, feeling him tense and hold under her palms. She let him feel her breath before she let him feel anything else. She'd told him she'd take her time, and she meant it, and she wanted him to understand that asking for something didn't mean he got to set the pace of it. Only that he got it.

"Keep your eyes closed," she said. "I want you feeling this, not watching it."

Then she took him in her mouth.

She went slow. She'd always gone slow with him like this—not teasing, not withholding, just thorough, unhurried, the same deliberate attention she brought to everything she cared about. She kept one hand pressed flat to his hip to hold him still and felt the moment he tried to lift into it, felt herself press him back down without breaking rhythm. His hand at her back had gone from flat to gripping, fingers digging in, and she didn't tell him to ease up. She'd told him to hold on. He was holding on.

When she heard his breath change—when it went from shaky to something closer to ragged—she pulled off him long enough to speak, her voice lower and rougher than it had been.

"You're not going anywhere yet," she said. "You hear me? I'll tell you when."

She glanced up. His eyes were still closed, but his mouth had come open, and the line of his shoulders against the sheets had finally, finally dropped. Not carried. Not braced. Just there, under her hands, letting her have him.

"There," she said, quietly, and it wasn't an order and it wasn't praise exactly, just a thing she noticed out loud so he'd know she'd noticed. "That's what I've been waiting for all night."

She bent back to him. She didn't say anything else for a while. She didn't need to. He'd asked her to keep talking, and she would, but right now the most honest thing she could tell him was the steady, unhurried, undivided fact of her attention—so she gave him that instead, and let him feel how completely she meant it.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: My fingers tighten in her hair. "Don't stop." It comes out choked. "Don't—"

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha didn't stop.

She'd meant to. She'd told him she would decide when, and she'd been ready to pull back, to make him wait in it a little longer, to hold him at the edge until the last of the week burned off him. That had been the plan.

But his hand had closed in her hair—not steering her, just holding, the way a man holds the rail when the floor tilts—and his voice had cracked on the second word, and she heard what was under it. Not want. Not even need, exactly. Something closer to *don't leave*. He'd gone all the way down and he was asking her to be there at the bottom.

So she stayed.

She didn't change what she was doing. That was the answer. She kept her hand flat on his hip and her rhythm steady and let him feel that nothing about her was going anywhere—not her mouth, not her attention, not the fact of her kneeling there between his thighs like it was the only place in the world she'd thought to be tonight. She let her free hand find his where it was knotted in her hair and pressed it, once, so he'd know it was allowed to be there.

When she felt him start to lose the thread—breath gone short and shallow, thighs shaking under her palm, the hand in her hair pulling now without meaning to—she lifted her head just enough to speak, and kept her hand moving so he wouldn't feel the loss of her.

"Now," she said. Rough. Certain. "Go on. I've got you."

She bent back to him and took him through it. She didn't rush it and she didn't ease off; she held him steady with her hand on his hip and let him come apart against her mouth exactly as hard as he needed to, and she didn't let go until the shaking had gone out of his legs and the fist in her hair had loosened to fingers, just resting.

Then she stayed there a moment longer with her cheek against the inside of his thigh, listening to him breathe. Ragged. Then less. Then almost even.

She came up the bed slowly, trailing her hand along his side as she went so the contact never broke, and settled against him with her head on his shoulder and her palm flat on his chest where it had been at the very beginning, on the couch. His heart was going hard under it. She waited for it to slow before she said anything.

"That's it," she said finally, very quiet, into his skin. "That's all you had to do."

She didn't ask if he was okay. She could feel that he was. She could feel it in the weight of him, the way he'd gone heavy and loose against the mattress, the way his shoulders had finally stopped holding anything up. She pressed her mouth to the scar on his collarbone, then to the corner of his jaw, then just rested her lips against his temple and left them there.

"You can open your eyes whenever you want," she said. "Or not. I'm not going anywhere. I'll be right here either way."

Her thumb moved along his sternum, slow, the way it had on his knee an hour ago. She didn't fill the silence after that. She just held him, and let him come back at whatever pace he needed, and made sure that when he did, the first thing he felt was her.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: "Rough," I say, the way we've talked about before. "Hold me down and don't be careful about it. I want to feel it tomorrow." I put my wrists together above my head and wait.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha lifted her head and looked at him.

Wrists together above his head. Eyes open now, on her, waiting. He'd said the word they used, the one that meant he'd thought about it and wasn't just chasing a feeling out of the room. She took a second to make sure of that anyway—looked at his face, at his breathing, at the man who'd just come apart under her mouth and was now, five minutes later, asking her to put him back together by force.

She understood it. He'd gone soft and open and it had felt like too much, and instead of closing up he was asking her to hold the door shut for him. That was the right ask. That was the one he'd learned to make, over six years, instead of leaving.

"Okay," she said.

Then she moved.

She came up over him and took his wrists in one hand—both of them, her fingers not quite meeting around the pair, and that was fine, she'd never needed to—and drove them down into the mattress above his head with her full weight behind it. Not a placement. A pin. She felt the give of the bed and the shock of it go through his arms, felt his breath catch, and she pressed harder.

"You want to feel it tomorrow," she said. Her voice had changed. Lower, flatter, no softness in it. "You'll feel it. You'll feel where I had you every time you lift your arms."

She swung a knee across him and sat down on his hips, all of her weight, no care taken for where it landed. Her free hand went to his jaw and gripped, hard, fingers digging into the hinge until his mouth came open, and she held him like that and looked down into his face from six inches away.

"You don't move," she said. "You don't get to. I've got your hands and I've got your hips and if you try to buck me off I'll take it out on you. Understood?"

She didn't wait for an answer she could already see. She let go of his jaw and put her mouth on his throat, and this time it wasn't a mark, it was teeth, closing on the muscle at the side of his neck until he made a sound she felt in her own chest. She held it a beat past comfortable. Then she moved lower and did it again, the top of his shoulder, the place he'd carry under a collar for a week.

Her grip on his wrists hadn't eased. When she felt him test it—not trying to get free, just needing to know it was real—she bore down until his knuckles pressed into the sheet and she heard the small pained exhale that meant yes, it was real, and he could stop checking.

"Good," she said against his collarbone. It wasn't kind. It was the truth, delivered like a verdict. "That's what you asked for. That's what you're getting."

She sat up, still pinning him, and shifted her hips deliberately, taking what she wanted from the friction and letting him feel her do it. She hadn't come yet. She'd been in no hurry before. She wasn't in a hurry now either, but she was done waiting to be gentle about it.

"Here's what happens." She said it the same way she'd said it on the couch, but there was nothing conversational in it now. "I'm going to use you. I'm going to hold you down and take my time and you're going to lie there and feel every second of it, and if you need to make noise you make it, and if you need to stop you say the word, and otherwise—"

She leaned down, her weight going through his wrists again, her hair falling around both their faces so the room was just the two of them and the dark.

"—otherwise you don't get to do anything at all. You don't get to think and you don't get to help and you don't get to be anywhere but under me. You wanted to be held. This is me holding you."

She bit his lower lip, hard enough to sting, and didn't apologize for it.

"Say the word if you need it," she said. "Say my name if you don't. I'm listening to both."

Then she reached down between them with her free hand, still keeping his wrists trapped in the other, and started.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I make a noise low in my throat when she bites my lip—sharp, real. My wrists ache where she's holding them down and I push up into it, just to feel the resistance. "Sasha," I breathe out. "More."

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha heard it. Her name, not the word. She'd been listening for the difference, and there it was—he wasn't asking her to ease off, he was asking her to prove she could hold him through it.

"More," she repeated, flat. "Fine."

She shifted her grip so she had one wrist in each hand and drove both down into the mattress, spreading his arms wider so he couldn't brace against himself. She put her weight through them until she felt the tendons in his forearms strain under her palms, until she could see his jaw lock against the ache of it. She didn't let up. She'd said she wasn't going to be careful, and she'd never once told him something in this bed she didn't mean.

Then she took him.

Not slow this time. She'd promised slow earlier and given it, and this wasn't that. She sank down on him in one motion, all the way, and the sound that came out of him was raw enough that she felt her own breath hitch to match it. She didn't give him time to get used to her. She started moving, hard, her weight coming down through her hips and through his wrists at once, so that everywhere he touched the world he was pinned by her.

"You feel that," she said. It wasn't a question. Her voice had gone rough at the edges. "That's me. That's all of me. You don't get to go anywhere."

He bucked once under her—not to escape, she knew the difference, just his body answering hers—and she bore down on his wrists until he stopped, and then bent and put her teeth in his shoulder for it, exactly where she'd promised, hard enough that he'd see it in the mirror tomorrow and know.

"I said don't move." Against his skin. "I meant it."

She kept going. She let herself take what she wanted now—she'd been patient the whole night, kneeling, waiting, giving, and she was done being patient. She rode him with her eyes open and on his face, watching him come undone, watching the exact moment the last of the week left him, and she didn't look away from it, not for a second, because that was hers too and she'd earned it.

His wrists were going to bruise. She could feel it under her palms, the places that would purple by morning. She pressed harder anyway, because he'd asked, and because the thing he was really asking for wasn't the ache—it was the certainty. The knowledge that she was strong enough to hold him and would.

"Look at me," she said, and it came out as a demand this time. "I want to see you."

When his eyes found hers she leaned down without loosening her grip, so her whole weight was on his hands and her face was inches from his, and she said the thing she'd been saving.

"You're mine. Right now, tonight, every bruise on you—mine. And I'm not letting go until I'm finished with you. You understand? You're going to lie here and take everything I give you and you're going to say my name while you do it."

She didn't wait for him to answer. She dragged her hips against him harder and felt herself start to go, felt it climbing up through her, and she didn't hide it from him, didn't quiet it or measure it. She let him hear her. She let him feel her hands shake on his wrists and not loosen. She let him watch her take exactly what she'd told him she would, and she said his name once, low and cracked, at the very end, so he'd know it had been him she wanted and not just this.

Then she held there, breathing hard, still pinning him, still full of him, and looked down at his face.

"Not done," she said, when she could speak. "Not with you."

She didn't let go of his wrists. She hadn't said the word, and neither had he, and she'd told him she had all night.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I'm past talking now, just noise and my hands twisted in the sheets. "Don't stop," I get out. (OOC: don't fade to black or time-skip, write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
"I'm not."

Sasha said it into his ear, low and certain, and then she proved it.

She hadn't let go of his wrists. His fingers had found the sheet under her grip and knotted there, pulling it up off the mattress in fistfuls, and she let him have that—let him hold onto something—while she held onto him. Her palms were slick against his skin now. She could feel his pulse hammering under her thumbs.

She started moving again, and this time she didn't build to it. She was already there, already open and aching and not finished with him, and she took him hard and steady from the first stroke, her hips grinding down, her weight going through his pinned arms so that every time she came down on him he felt it in three places at once.

He'd stopped making words. She'd known he would. The sounds coming out of him were low and broken and utterly unguarded, and she wanted every one of them. She'd waited all night for the version of him who couldn't manage anything but noise.

"That's it," she said. Her voice had gone to gravel. "That's what I want to hear. Let go of it."

She shifted her grip on his right wrist, freed her hand, and used it. Her palm went flat to his chest and she leaned her weight into it, pressing him down into the mattress while she rode him, her other hand still crushing his left wrist above his head. She wanted him to feel the difference—one arm held, the other pinned only by the fact that he'd been told not to move. She wanted to see if he'd keep it there on nothing but her word.

He did. His free hand stayed twisted in the sheet above his head, knuckles white, arm trembling with the effort of not reaching for her.

"Good," she said, and this time there was something almost tender under the roughness of it, because he'd done that for her and she saw it. "Good. Stay there."

She dragged her hand down from his chest to his stomach and felt the muscles there jump and lock under her palm. He was close. She could feel it in the way he'd started to shake under her, the way his hips were trying to lift to meet her and she kept driving them back down, the way his breath had gone to short hard pulls between his teeth.

She could have made him wait. She'd thought about it. But she looked down at his face—eyes shut tight, mouth open, everything in him wrenched wide and given up—and she didn't want to hold it back from him. She wanted to give it to him. She wanted him to know that when he went this far down, she'd meet him at the bottom and hand him the thing he needed instead of making him earn it.

So she bent low, her hair falling around them again, her hand on his wrist bearing down one last time so he'd carry the shape of her fingers into tomorrow, and she said it against his mouth.

"Now. Give it to me. All of it."

She kept her rhythm through it. She didn't slow, didn't soften, held him down with her body and her hand and her voice and felt him break under her—felt the moment it went through him, his whole frame arching up into the pin and shuddering there, the sound he made cracking open into something that wasn't a word or a name or anything but pure release. She felt him lose himself inside her and she didn't look away from his face for a single second of it.

She rode it out with him. Past the peak, into the aftershocks, still moving, slower now, letting him feel her take the last of it, letting her own body answer his one more time in a low quiet wave that she didn't perform and didn't hide.

Then she stopped.

She didn't let go of his wrist right away. She held it a moment longer, not pressing now, just holding, so the last thing his body registered before she released him was that she'd been there the whole way through. Then she opened her fingers, one at a time, and lifted her hand.

There were marks. Red now. Purple by morning. She looked at them and then she bent and put her mouth to them, gently, the first gentle thing she'd done in a long while.

"There," she said, very quiet. "You'll feel that tomorrow."

She eased herself off him, slow, and came down beside him instead of on him, and gathered him in—one arm under his neck, one hand flat on his chest again, his heart slamming against her palm. His free hand was still knotted in the sheet above his head. She reached up and worked his fingers loose, one by one, and brought his arm down and laid it across her waist where it belonged.

"You can move now," she said. "You did everything I asked. You don't have to hold anything anymore."

She didn't ask if he was okay. She kissed the side of his head and left her mouth there, and felt him breathe, and waited with him in the dark for however long it took him to come back to the room.

dialogue.name: Devin
dialogue.content: I turn my face into her shoulder, breathing her in. My whole body feels heavy, used. "Thank you," I mumble, the words slurred.

dialogue.name: Sasha
dialogue.content:
Sasha felt the words more than heard them. They came out against her skin, warm and shapeless, and something in her chest went tight and then loose all at once.

She didn't say *you're welcome*. It wasn't that kind of thank you, and she knew it.
