"Two," she said, before Ari could. "That one's mine. You don't get credit for the ones you didn't earn."

The third came a beat after, and this one she did not count for Ari. She let the silence open again and stood in it, breathing evenly, the leather resting loose in her hand against her thigh.

"You said steadier than you expected." She had heard it in the voice—the small surprise Ari had not meant to show. "Don't get attached to that. Steady is where we start. It isn't where I'm taking you."

She stepped closer, close enough that Ari would feel the shift in the air behind them, and laid her free hand flat between the shoulder blades, over the place the first two had landed. The skin was warming. Not marked yet. Just awake.

"Four days of thinking," she said, quieter now, almost conversational, her palm not moving. "And here you are, tied to my wall, counting for me, and you've managed three. I have all night, Ari. I have nowhere else I would rather be, and nothing else I would rather be doing than standing here waiting for you to say a number."

She took her hand away.

"So say it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard it before she saw it.

Not the number. The absence of it—and underneath the absence, a change in the breathing. It had been even, a little quick, the rhythm of someone holding a line. Now it wasn't. It had gone shallow and uneven at the top, the way breath went when the body had stopped consulting the person it belonged to.

She did not strike again.

She set the implement down on the edge of the table without looking, the leather making a soft, final sound against the wood, and came around to the front. Unhurried, but not slow either. Two years had taught her the difference between someone deciding not to speak and someone who had briefly lost the thread of how, and she was not going to guess which one this was from behind.

"Ari."

She said the name the way she had said *colour* at the start: not a question, a procedure. Her hand came up under the jaw again and lifted, and this time she did not wait for Ari's eyes to find hers—she went and found them herself.

What she saw there she took in without comment. Wide. Wet at the edges. Not distressed—she knew distress, she had a whole catalogue of it—but *far*. Three light strikes and a handful of sentences, and Ari had gone somewhere Vex had not sent them yet.

"That was faster than I planned," she said. Her voice had dropped the cool edge entirely. What was left was flat and steady and very close. "I don't mind fast. I mind not knowing where you are."

Her thumb moved once along the jawline. Slow.

"Colour."

She held the eye contact and held the jaw and did not let either one go. She was not asking to be reassured. She was asking because the rules said she asked, and the rules did not bend for how badly either of them wanted to keep going—that was the entire point of having them.

"I'll take the answer in a word. I'll take it in a nod if the word won't come. But I will have it before I touch you again, and I'll stand here as long as that takes." A pause, short. "Then you'll give me the number. In that order."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My throat works before the word comes out. "Green. Still green." I blink, and a tear tracks down my cheek. "Three."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green," Vex repeated. "Three."

She did not let go of the jaw yet. She watched the tear finish its track and did nothing about it—did not wipe it, did not name it. It was information, and she had received it, and Ari would know she had received it by the fact that she did not look away.

"Both of those cost you something," she said. "I saw it. That's not a criticism. I'd rather have a word that costs you than silence that costs me."

Her thumb came to rest just under the cheekbone, still, and she stayed there a moment longer than the check required. Long enough to count Ari's breaths. Four. The fifth came in deeper than the others, reached the bottom, and she felt the small drop in the shoulders under her other hand before she saw it.

"There you are."

She let go.

She did not go back to the table. Not yet. She stayed in front, where she could be seen, and folded her arms loosely, the way she did when she was thinking about something and had decided not to hide the fact.

"I'm going to change something," she said. "Not because you did anything wrong. Because I've learned something, and I don't ignore what I learn about you." A pause. "You went further on three than I had you going on ten. So I'm not going to build the way I said. I'm going to hold you where you are for a while instead. Same weight. Same pace. And you are going to stay with me the whole time, out loud, so I don't have to come around and find you."

Her voice was level, almost administrative. But she had not stepped back yet, and Ari would notice that.

"That means every number. No skipping, no letting me take them. If I have to say one for you, I'm going to stop and come around and look at you, and you're going to have to tell me green again, and we're going to lose time." She let that settle. "I don't want to lose time. I've been thinking about this since Tuesday too."

Now she stepped back. Now she went to the table, and picked up what she had set down, and tested it once against her palm the way she had at the start—same flat sound, same unhurried hand.

"Yellow is still there. Red is still there. Neither of them has moved." She came around behind. Ari would hear each step, and she let them land. "I'm going to start again at four. You'll say it when it comes. Breathe first."

The fourth strike, when it came, was exactly as light as the first had been. Placed exactly where the first had been. Not a step forward. A hand held out, at the same height, for as long as it needed to be held.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex stopped.

Not because of the shaking—she had been watching that build for some time, had tracked its arrival in the wrists first, then the shoulders, then the long muscles either side of the spine, and had decided it was the kind she allowed. The body shook when it had been held in one place long enough to stop bracing. That was the point of holding it there.

She stopped because of the asking.

She stood behind Ari with the leather still lifted and let the words finish landing in the room. She did not answer them right away. Two years, and she could count on one hand the times Ari had asked her for anything in here without first being taken to pieces for it. It was not a thing she had trained. It was a thing she had waited for, and the waiting had been part of what she was doing on Tuesday, and Wednesday, and every day since.

She lowered her arm.

"Say that again."

Her voice had not risen. If anything it had gone quieter, the way it did when she wanted a thing badly enough to be careful about it. She set the implement down—not on the table, on the floor beside her foot, where she would not have to turn away to reach it—and came around to the front.

Ari's face was wet. The shaking was visible from here, a fine continuous tremor that ran through the restraints and hummed faintly in the anchor point above. Vex put both hands on Ari's upper arms, above the cuffs, and pressed. Not hard. Just enough weight to give the tremor something to push against.

"Look at me while you do it."

She waited. She did not fill the silence with instruction or reassurance. She had given the instruction; the reassurance was in her hands, and her hands were not going anywhere.

"I heard you the first time," she said, low. "I want you to hear yourself. You've spent two years making me dig for that. Tonight you handed it to me. I'm not going to pretend I didn't notice, and I'm not going to let you pretend you didn't do it."

Her thumbs moved once, slowly, along the inside of each arm.

"So. Colour first. Then the sentence, clean, the way you'd say it if you weren't shaking." A pause. "And then, if I like what I hear, you'll find out what it gets you."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I suck in a shaky breath. "Green. Please, Maitresse—don't stop."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Please, Maitresse," Vex said. "Don't stop."

She did not say it back the way she said the numbers. She said it slowly, and let it be heard, and did not soften what it was: a thing Ari had chosen to put in her hands. She had asked for it clean and it had come out shaking, and she found she did not mind. The shaking was hers too. She had built it, one flat hand's-width at a time, over however long it had been—she knew exactly how long; Ari did not, and that was correct.

"Good," she said. And then, because it was true and because Ari had earned it and because she had told them at the start they could have it back at the end: "That was very good."

Her hands stayed on the upper arms a moment longer. Then she moved one—not away, but up, the flat of her palm crossing the shoulder to rest against the side of Ari's neck, thumb settled in the hollow under the ear where the pulse ran close. Fast. Very fast now. She stood and counted it against her own, which was not as steady as her voice, and let Ari feel her doing it.

"Here is what that gets you."

She stepped in until there was no space left to decide about, until the tremor was running through her as well as the restraints, and spoke close, low, without theatre.

"I don't stop. I was never going to. But you asked, and so now it's yours as well as mine, and you don't get to leave that at the door on your way out tonight." Her thumb pressed once against the pulse and eased. "The other thing it gets you is this: I'm going to build now. I said I'd hold you where you were, and I have. You've been steady there long enough. The next one is heavier. The one after that is heavier again. I'll stop climbing when I decide, not when you flinch, and you'll say every number in a voice I can hear."

She took her hand from the neck and stepped back and picked up the leather from the floor beside her foot, and the whole time she did not look away, so that Ari could watch her choose to.

"Yellow. Red. Still there. Still yours." She came around behind, and let each step land. "You've told me green three times tonight. I've believed you each time. I'm believing you now."

The strike, when it came, was not light. It was not cruel either. It was precisely one degree more than everything that had come before it—placed on warm skin that had been prepared for it, with a hand that had been waiting all week to be allowed this. The sound in the room changed. Fuller. Less air in it.

"That's the first one you asked for," Vex said, very quietly. "Count it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not strike.

The leather stayed where it was, lifted, and she stood behind Ari and let the silence do what silence did in this room. Then she lowered her arm, and set the implement down on the floor beside her foot again, and Ari would hear the quiet sound of that and know what it meant before she moved.

She came around to the front.

"You used the phrase," she said. "I heard it. It's yours to use, and you've used it correctly, and I'm going to give you what it buys. In a moment." Her hand came up under the jaw and lifted, the same as it had every time, and her eyes found Ari's and held them. "But I told you what happens if I have to say a number for you. I don't make rules I'm not willing to keep. So."

She waited exactly as long as it took.

"Colour."

Her thumb rested against the wet track on Ari's cheek and did not move. Her face was calm. Underneath the calm was something Ari had seen perhaps a dozen times in two years, and it was not displeasure, and it was not softness either. It was the look of someone who had been handed a thing she wanted and intended to be very, very careful with it.

"And the number after that. Then you'll have what you asked for. All of it. I'm not going to make you ask twice."

She let go of the jaw and did not step back. She stayed where she was, close, and let her voice drop to the register she used for the things she did not say outside this room.

"Look at you." Flat. Unhurried. Not a performance. "Tied to my wall, shaking, crying, and the first full sentence you manage in an hour is *more*. You didn't ask to be let down. You didn't ask for water. You asked me to hit you harder and talk to you worse, and you did it in the voice of someone who's been waiting four days to be allowed to." Her hand came up, and two fingers traced the line of the collarbone where the leather had first rested, cool and deliberate. "You're greedy. You've always been greedy. You just spent two years making me pull it out of you a piece at a time so you could pretend it was mine. It isn't. This is yours. I'm only the one holding it."

She stepped back. Picked up the leather. Tested it once against her palm.

"I'm going to give you what you asked for," she said, "and I'm going to say what I see while I do it. None of it will be softened. All of it will be true. If any of it stops being something you want to hear, you know the two words that fix that, and I will hear them over anything I'm saying."

She came around behind. Each step landed.

"Colour," she said, from behind now, low and level. "Then the number. Then you'll find out exactly how much I've been holding back."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold your gaze, throat tight. "Green. Four." My voice cracks a little on the number.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green," Vex said. "Four."

She did not correct the number. She had heard it crack down the middle and had made a decision about that in the space of a breath: Ari had said it, and had said it looking at her, and the ledger would take it as given. Two years of exactness had earned her the right to know when exactness was the point and when it was only pride.

"It cracked," she said. "I'm keeping that too."

The strike came without a pause, and it was heavier again—not by much, by exactly the degree she had promised, landing low across the back where the muscle had been warmed for an hour and could carry it. The sound was full. It filled the room the way the earlier ones had not, and she let it finish before she spoke.

"Five," she said. "That one I'm taking. You'll get the next one back."

She did not hurry. That was the thing about building: the weight went up and the pace did not, and the body learned that it could not brace against the next one because it did not know when the next one came. She stood behind Ari with the leather loose at her side and watched the shaking change—less fine now, more in the knees, the way it went when the legs had stopped pretending to hold and had begun to hang.

"You asked me to say what I see," she said. Low. Even. "So here's the first thing. You're not standing anymore. You're being held up. By straps I put on you, at a height I chose, and you're grateful for it, and if I took them off right now you'd go to the floor and you'd thank me from there."

The sixth landed high, between the shoulders, on skin that had already learned this particular weight and had nothing left to be surprised with. She waited for the number. She would wait exactly as long as it took, and the leather rested against her thigh, and her voice went on without it.

"Second thing. You've been crying for most of an hour and you haven't once asked me to stop. Not yellow. Not red. Not *please, that's enough*. You've asked for more, and you've asked for me not to stop, and you've asked me to talk to you like this. That isn't endurance, Ari. Endurance is when you want it to end and you don't say so. This is the other thing. This is what you look like when you're getting exactly what you want and you're ashamed of how much you want it."

She stepped closer, and laid her free hand flat over the place the sixth had landed, and pressed.

"Third thing. Four days. I know what you did with those four days. I know what you did on Wednesday night when you thought I was asleep, and I know you didn't finish, because you wanted to arrive here like this—like something wound so tight that three light strikes could pull you apart. That wasn't obedience. Nobody told you to. You did it because you're greedy, and because you knew that if you came to me already halfway gone I'd have to spend the whole evening watching you closer than I've ever watched you, and being watched is the only thing you want more than being hit."

She took her hand away.

"None of that is soft. None of that is false. Tell me if either one changes."

She lifted the leather.

"Number. Then seven. Then I'll tell you what you look like from back here, and you won't like it, and you'll ask me to keep going anyway." A pause, barely one. "Yellow, red. I'm listening under everything I say."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green," Vex said.

She had waited for the number. She had waited the length of time she always waited, which was exactly as long as it took, and the number had not come, and she had watched the not-coming from behind—the way the head hung, the way the breath went in and did not quite make it back out as anything shaped. She knew that place. She had put Ari in it deliberately, and she was not going to punish them for arriving.

She did not go to the front. She had said she would, and she was going to tell Ari why she wasn't.

"I told you I'd come around if I had to say a number for you," she said. Low, from behind, close. "I'm not going to. Not because I've stopped keeping my rules. Because you've gone past the place where the numbers live, and I sent you there, and I'm not going to drag you back up just to hear you say *seven*. That would be for me. Tonight isn't for me."

She laid her free hand flat on the back of Ari's neck and held it there.

"So the rules change once more, and this is the last time. You have three words. Green, yellow, red. That's all I want from you. I'll count. I'll ask, and you'll answer with one of those, and if you can't manage the word you'll nod for green and shake your head for anything else, and I'll stop and come around. That is the whole of what's required of you now. Everything else, I'm carrying."

Her hand tightened once on the neck. Then let go.

"Seven."

The strike landed where the fifth had, low and full, and she said the number in the same breath so there was no gap for Ari to fall into.

"You asked what you look like from back here. I'll tell you." She did not raise her voice. She did not need to. "You look like something that's been put away wet. Every mark I've made, I can see. They're not bruises yet. They're the colour of a thing that's been touched too many times in the same place, and they go up your back like a ladder, because I put them there in order and I don't put anything anywhere by accident. There's a line where your shoulders stopped trying about twenty minutes ago and just hung. Your hands are open. You've stopped gripping the cuffs. You're not holding on to anything anymore. I am."

"Eight."

Higher, between the shoulders, heavier by a hair. She watched the ripple go down the spine and out into the legs and let the sound finish.

"You've soaked through the collar of that shirt with your own face. You've been crying so long it's stopped meaning anything and started just being weather. And underneath it—I know you can hear me, I can see you hearing me—you're *pleased*. You are pleased with yourself. You've been waiting two years for me to say out loud that you're the one who wants this, and I've said it, and you're taking it like a reward. Greedy. Right down to the bone."

"Nine."

She let a longer silence go after that one. Long enough for the body to start wondering. Long enough that she heard the breathing change—shorter, higher—the way it did when it had begun to anticipate and could not find anything to anticipate against.

"Colour."

She said it flat, into the silence, and waited, and did not lift the leather. She heard the answer—or saw it; she was watching the head—and took it, and did not comment on how it came.

"Good."

"Ten."

That one was the heaviest yet, and she had known it would be the heaviest since the moment she picked the implement up, because she had decided where she was going to stop climbing and she had just arrived. The sound was a full thing in the room. It did not have air in it. She lowered her arm the moment it landed and did not lift it again, and stood there, and let Ari feel the difference between a pause and an ending.

"That's the top," she said. "You heard the number. You'll remember that one. I'm not going higher tonight, and I want you to notice that it's me deciding that, not you, not your legs, not the safeword. I decided. You'd have let me keep going. I know you would. That's exactly why I don't."

She set the leather down on the floor. Not the table—the floor, by her foot, where it had been. Then she stepped in and put both hands on Ari's back, flat, over the ladder she had made, and held them there. The skin under her palms was hot enough that she could feel the shape of each strike separately, and the tremor ran up through her wrists into her own shoulders, and she let it.

"Here is the last thing I see," she said, quieter, mouth close to the back of Ari's head. "You are not a thing that's been put away wet. I said that to hear how it landed and I watched it land, and you liked it, and that's yours to have. But this is what's true from back here. You are someone who trusted me enough to arrive already broken open, and told me so, and then stood in it for an hour without once reaching for the door I left unlocked. I've never had anyone do that for me. I've never asked anyone to. I'm not going to soften that either."

Her hands moved. Slowly, up, over the shoulders, down the outside of the arms to where the cuffs sat, and she pressed two fingers against the inside of the left wrist, where she had begun, and found the pulse, and held it. Fast. Not as fast as before. Coming down.

"Colour," she said. "Then I'm going to keep my hands on you and not take them off, and I'm going to start bringing you down, and it's going to take longer than you want and that's mine to decide too." A pause. "Nod if the word won't come. I'm right here. I have been the whole time."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I nod. Then, like pulling it from deep water: "Green." I lean my forehead against the wall and just breathe.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green," Vex said. "Good. That's the last one I'll need from you for a while."

She felt the forehead go to the wall through the cuffs—the small shift in the anchor point above as weight redistributed—and she did not correct it. She had told Ari to breathe. Ari was breathing. Everything else was hers.

She did not let go of the wrist. She stood with two fingers on the pulse and her other hand flat on the warm back and counted, not out loud, and waited for the number she wanted, which was not a strike count but a rate. It took a while. She had all night. She had said so, and she had meant it in both directions.

When the pulse had come down enough that she could feel the space between beats, she moved.

"I'm taking the right wrist first," she said. "You'll feel me at the buckle. Don't help."

She worked it the way she had checked it at the start—unhurried, in order, thumb under the strap so the leather did not drag across skin when it came free. The cuff opened. She did not let the arm drop. She caught it at the elbow and the wrist both and brought it down slowly, folding it in against Ari's own chest, and held it there until she felt the shoulder understand it had been let go.

"Left."

Same procedure. Same speed. When the second cuff came free she stepped in fully, so that she was against Ari's back with both arms around, and took the weight before the legs could decide whether they still wanted it. They didn't. She had known they wouldn't.

"Down," she said. "With me. Not on your own."

It was not graceful and she did not try to make it so. She got them both to the floor with Ari's back against her front and her own back against the wall, one arm across Ari's chest and the other hand cupped at the back of the head, and she sat there and did not say anything at all for a length of time she measured only in breaths—theirs, then hers, until they were close enough to the same.

The blanket was where it always was, folded on the low table's second shelf, and she reached it without disturbing anything and brought it around both of them. The water was beside it. She uncapped it one-handed and held it to Ari's mouth and tipped it, a small amount, and waited, and tipped it again.

"You don't have to talk," she said, low, near the ear. "I'm going to. You can just have it."

Her hand at the back of the head moved once, slowly, through the damp hair.

"Ten. You'll feel every one of them tomorrow and none of them will have broken the skin. I'll look at your back in the light before you sleep and again in the morning, and I'll put the cream on, and you'll let me. Your wrists are fine. I checked them coming off. The left one's going to have a line from the strap for about an hour and then it won't."

She shifted the blanket higher over Ari's shoulders.

"You asked for all of it. You got all of it. I didn't hold anything back that I said I'd give you, and I stopped exactly where I decided to before I picked the leather up. Nothing tonight was an accident, and nothing tonight was you failing. I want that in your head before anything else gets in there, because I know what tries to get in there afterward, and it doesn't get to be first."

She took the water back, capped it, set it down. Both arms around now.

"What I said about Wednesday," she said, quieter. "I meant it. I'm not taking it back. But I'm going to say the other half of it here, on the floor, where it counts. You did that because you trusted me to notice. I noticed. I'm not going anywhere."

Her chin came to rest against the top of Ari's head, and she let her own breath out long, and did not hurry any part of what came next.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shuddering breath that's half a sob, pressing back into you. My hands come up to grip your forearms around me, holding on. "Thank you," I whisper, raw.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the grip close on her forearms and did not loosen hers in answer. She tightened it. Just enough that Ari would feel the difference between being held and being held back.

"Don't thank me yet," she said. It was not a refusal. Her voice had gone somewhere it did not go in the standing part of the evening—lower, slower, with the edges filed off. "You're still coming down. Everything feels bigger from in there. Thank me in the morning, if you still want to, when you've had your feet under you for an hour and you know what you're thanking me for."

She let the sob move through both of them. She did not shush it. She had never once shushed anything Ari's body needed to do on this floor, and she was not going to start now that it was gratitude coming out instead of the other thing.

"That's it. Let it go where it's going."

Her thumb found the inside of Ari's wrist again—not to check, this time, or not only to check. Habit. Two years of it. She held the pulse and felt it settle by degrees against her own, and when the shuddering had gone from the whole body down to just the hands, she spoke again.

"I'm going to tell you what's going to happen next, so you don't have to hold any of it."

She said it the way she had laid out the evening at the start: a procedure, a thing with an order.

"We're going to sit here until I say. Then I'm going to get you up, and you're going to lean on me the whole way, and I'm going to put you in the chair with the blanket and turn the small lamp on, not the big one. I'm going to look at your back. I'm going to put the cream on and you're going to sit still for it, and I'll tell you what I see, and none of it will be a surprise because I've already told you. Then there's something to eat—it's already made, it's in the kitchen, you didn't see it because you weren't meant to. You'll eat it whether you're hungry or not. Then bed. Then I'm going to lie behind you and keep my hand on you and you're going to sleep, and I'm not, not for a while, because I'll be watching you breathe."

She moved the hand at Ari's head down to rest against the side of the neck, the pulse-point, and left it.

"That's all decided. You don't have to want any of it. You just have to let it happen."

A pause. Her chin shifted against Ari's hair.

"Since Tuesday," she said, very quietly, almost not to Ari at all. "You said that at the beginning and I told you to put it away. I said you could have it back at the end."

Her arms tightened once more, deliberately.

"This is the end. Have it back. Since Tuesday for me too. I was thinking about exactly this—this part, the floor, your hands on my arms. Not the rest of it. This."

She did not say anything after that for a while. She held on, and kept her hand on the pulse, and let the room be quiet around them, and did not once look at the clock.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I nod against you, my fingers tightening slightly on your arms. My voice is rough. "Okay." I swallow, leaning harder into you. "Not letting go yet."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex slid two fingers beneath the cuff at Ari's wrist, testing the tension against the bone, making sure the leather lay flat against the skin without pinching. Satisfied, she moved to the other side and did the same, her touch cool, deliberate, and entirely clinical. 

"Good," she said softly. 

She stepped back, letting her eyes travel the length of Ari's body to ensure the alignment was true and the weight was distributed properly along the frame. Her gaze was steady, assessing breathing, posture, and the subtle tells she had learned over two years of careful study. 

Turning to the low table beside them, she surveyed the implements laid out in their customary order. Her hand hovered briefly before selecting a heavy, supple leather paddle. She brought it back to the edge of the frame, tapping it once against her own thigh with a dull, solid thud to gauge the weight.

She stepped in close, close enough for Ari to feel the shift in air, though she made no immediate contact. 

"Eyes on me," Vex directed, her voice quiet, low, and perfectly level. "Take three full breaths, all the way to the bottom of your lungs. Then we begin."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My eyes snap to hers, holding steady as she asked. I draw in the first breath, slow and deep, feeling my ribs expand against the restraints. The scent of leather and her faint perfume fills my lungs. The second breath steadies my pulse. The third... I let it out as a soft sigh, body going pliant against the frame. "Ready, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari's gaze for a moment longer, marking the shift in posture—the yielding slackness in the shoulders, the steadying rhythm of the chest against the leather. Only when she was satisfied that the focus was entirely centered did she break eye contact.

She stepped behind the frame, her movements quiet and deliberate. She laid her left palm flat against the small of Ari’s back, fingers splayed to feel the anchor of bone and muscle, grounding them both before the leather made contact. 

"First one to wake the skin," she said, her tone conversational, matter-of-fact.

The paddle came down with a sharp, clean crack across the meat of the right thigh. It wasn't full force, but it carried weight—enough to leave a sharp sting in the air and send an immediate flush of heat blooming beneath the surface. 

Vex kept her left hand firmly in place, feeling the instantaneous flinch and release in the lower spine. She didn't strike again right away. Instead, she smoothed the edge of the leather paddle over the spot she had just marked, tracing the perimeter of the warmth.

"Breathe it down," she instructed quietly, leaning in just enough that her voice carried clearly without being raised. "Count them for me. We'll do five to settle."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s hand remained steady against the small of Ari’s back, her palm warm and heavy, anchoring the baseline. She didn't immediately scold the lapse in counting; she simply let the words hang in the quiet room, measuring the nervous heat and lingering anticipation behind them. Two years together meant she knew exactly how Ari’s mind wound itself tight in the days leading up to a scene.

"I know you have," she murmured, her voice calm, low, and close. "You carry it in your shoulders. But Tuesday is gone, and the week is done. You are here on the frame, and your mind belongs in this room."

She shifted her stance, centering her weight. The edge of the leather paddle lifted, resting for a single, cool beat against the meat of Ari's left thigh—a quiet warning to balance the first strike—before she drew it back.

The second strike came down with clean, deliberate force, landing squarely across the left side to match the right. The sound cracked sharply against the walls, followed by the immediate, dull sting that set the nerves humming. 

Vex kept her left hand planted, feeling the involuntary hitch in Ari's ribs, the instinctive tighten-and-release of muscle against restraint. She waited, letting the burn bloom fully into the skin before she spoke again.

"That was two," she said, her tone level and instructive, leaving no room for drifting thoughts. "Breathe it out, Ari. Give me the count on three."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a slow, shaky breath. "Three," I manage, focusing on the deep ache radiating through my thigh. My knuckles tighten around the frame's bar for a second before I consciously relax them.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex watched the knuckles whiten against the bar and then deliberately loosen. That conscious release of tension earned a faint, approving tilt of her head, though her focus never wavered from the work. 

"Eager," she murmured, a trace of dry amusement undercutting the steady calm of her voice. "Taking the number before the leather earns it."

She gave Ari no time to overthink the correction. The paddle drew back and descended with practiced precision, striking the center of the right thigh just an inch higher than the first mark. The contact was solid, a heavy *thwack* that drove the heat deeper into the muscle rather than just skittering across the surface. 

Her anchoring hand pressed firmly against Ari’s lower back, riding out the immediate jolt that traveled up the spine, keeping the hips squarely positioned against the frame. 

"That was three," she stated evenly, letting the flat of the paddle rest against the rising warmth of the welt to draw the sting. "Now take your breath. Fill the lungs, all the way down, and let the heat spread."

She waited, feeling the rise and fall of Ari's ribs through the palm resting against bone. Her thumb stroked once, rhythmically, over the notch of the spine.

"Give me four when you are ready."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noticed the shift immediately. It was there in the shallow stutter of the ribs, the slight tremor running down through the calves, the telltale surrender of composure before the work had even truly deepened. Two years of observing Ari meant she recognized the exact threshold where anticipation overtook reality, pulling the mind under before the body had properly caught up.

She lowered the paddle, letting it hang loosely at her side, and brought her free hand up to join the other against Ari’s back. Both palms pressed flat, broad and heavy, smoothing firmly down over the shoulder blades to ground Ari securely against the frame. 

"Look at you," she murmured, her voice low and calm, devoid of mockery but sharp with precise observation. "Barely started, and already coming undone."

She stepped closer, letting Ari feel the steady, unhurried warmth of her presence at their back. She could feel the rapid flutter of the pulse against the restraint, the heightened nerve endings firing beneath the surface. It was easy for Ari to spiral into the headspace, but Vex was exacting; she had no intention of letting the mind drift untethered before the body had processed the foundation.

"Breathe," she commanded softly, her thumbs pressing into the knot of tension between the shoulder blades and working a small, deliberate circle. "All the way down into my hands. Don't hide in your head, Ari. Stay on the skin. Stay in this room with me."

She held that firm, grounding pressure, letting the silence of the room settle over them until she felt the rhythm of Ari's breathing begin to lengthen against the leather.

"Colour," she said, quiet, clinical, and steady. "Confirm it for me before we take four."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I whisper, my voice rough but steady. "Still green." I press back slightly into her hands, grounding myself. "Sorry, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex felt the press of Ari’s weight leaning back against her hands, seeking the boundary she offered, and she leaned into it just enough to provide a solid wall. She kept her palms flat, soaking up the tremor, letting the heat of her own hands seep into the tense line of Ari's spine.

"No apologies on the frame," she said quietly, her voice brushing just past Ari's ear. "You don't apologize for an honest reaction. You simply stay with it."

She gave the shoulder blades one last, firm press—a clear punctuation mark—before stepping back to her working distance. The cool air of the room rushed into the small space between them, sharp and bracing after the warmth of her touch.

She weighed the paddle in her right hand once more, letting Ari hear the faint creak of the leather grip. The baseline was reset; the mind was anchored back into the physical room, right where she required it to be. 

"Green is acknowledged," she said, her tone returning to that crisp, deliberate cadence. 

Without hesitation, she drew back and brought the paddle down for the fourth strike. It caught the meaty curve just below the left buttock, landing with a resonant, cracking thud that carried noticeably more bite than the third. It was clean and squarely placed, waking an entirely fresh band of nerve endings and sending a deep, stinging bloom across the skin.

She immediately set her left palm back against the small of Ari's back, riding the jolt, holding the alignment firm.

"That was four," she murmured into the quiet. "Breathe it in, Ari. Own the space it takes up, and tell me what comes next."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex let the silence stretch, measuring the tremors running through Ari’s frame with practiced detachment. She did not rush. Time in this room belonged entirely to her, and she gave Ari every second necessary to sit in that exposed, unraveled space where pride gave way to raw need. 

Hearing Ari ask aloud—surrendering the quiet defiance that usually took half a scene to strip away—was noted, cataloged, and accepted without gloating. Vex appreciated the stubborn streak, but she valued the honesty of the break even more.

She stepped in close once again, laying the flat of the paddle across the back of both thighs, letting the cool leather press against the blooming heat of the welts. She rested her free hand against the nape of Ari’s neck, fingers curving gently around the base of the skull to offer a solid, unyielding point of reference.

"Listen to you," Vex murmured, her voice steady and intimate against the quiet of the room. "No games left to hide behind. Just asking for what you need."

She felt the flutter of the pulse against her fingertips, the shallow, uneven rhythm of the breathing. She gave the neck a firm, anchoring squeeze, ensuring Ari’s head stayed aligned, keeping the focus pinned to the physical reality of the wood, the straps, and the skin.

"I hear you," she said softly, though there was steel beneath the quiet reassurance. "And you will have it. But we finish what we set out to do properly. No rushing through the foundation."

She drew the paddle away, stepping back into her stance. She gave Ari three slow seconds to gather whatever breath was left, watching the fine shiver along the spine.

The fifth strike landed with clean, decisive authority dead-center across the hips. The crack echoed sharp and dry off the floorboards, delivering a full, deep sting that finished the sequence and locked the heat into a solid, unbroken band across the lower body.

Vex immediately set the paddle down on the side table with a dull clatter, stepping back to the frame to place both warm hands flat against Ari's waist, holding the hips firmly against the wooden uprights while the shockwave traveled up the spine.

"Five," she stated, leaning over the frame so her breath warmed Ari's shoulder. "That is five, Ari. The set is closed."

She kept her hands locked in place, absorbing the shudders, waiting for the first deep, grounding exhale. 

"Breathe into my hands," she commanded quietly. "Give me your colour, and tell me where your head is."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I suck in a sharp breath, my whole body arching against the frame before slumping into her hold. The heat across my hips is deep and solid, anchoring me fully in the moment. "Green," I breathe out, turning my head just enough to rest my cheek against the wood. "My head is right here, Maitresse. With you."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept her hands on Ari's hips for several long seconds, feeling the initial tremor ease into a heavy, yielding stillness. The heat radiating off the skin beneath her palms was even and high—a clean, deep bloom across the thighs and lower hips, exactly the foundation she had intended to lay. 

"Good," she said softly. Her voice brushed close to Ari's ear, entirely devoid of urgency. "Right here is where you stay."

She smoothed one palm up the center of Ari's back, tracing the line of the vertebrae with deliberate, grounding pressure to ensure there was no lingering hitch in the breathing. With her other hand, she reached under Ari's jaw, pressing two fingers gently against the carotid artery to gauge the pulse. It was elevated, as expected, but settling into a strong, rhythmic thrum.

Satisfied with the somatic check, she stepped back from the frame, her boots clicking softly against the floorboards. She moved to the side table, setting the paddle aside and picking up a small glass of water that had been staged there before they began. 

She returned to Ari's side, stepping directly into view so there were no surprises. With clean, unhurried precision, she slipped her free fingers beneath Ari's chin, lifting it gently from the wood of the upright. 

"Two sips," Vex directed, bringing the rim of the glass to Ari's lips. "Slowly. Then we move to the next part of the work."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not pull the glass away, nor did she smile. Her gaze remained pinned to Ari’s, entirely unreadable, letting the weight of the demand settle in the air between them. The phrase had been agreed upon, written down, and committed to memory months ago. Hearing it spoken clearly, without evasion or retreat, brought a cold, sharpened focus to the room.

"Water first," she said, her voice dropping an octave, perfectly steady and low. "You don't speak over an instruction, Ari. Drink."

She held the rim steady against Ari's bottom lip, waiting until the required two sips were taken before she pulled the glass back. She turned, stepped over to the table, and set the glass down with a soft, final click. 

When she turned back, the measured, clinical warmth of the warm-up was gone. What replaced it was the quiet, predatory calm that Ari had explicitly asked for. 

She walked the perimeter of the frame, letting the leather of her boots mark each slow, heavy step. She stopped at Ari's hip, leaning down so her words were delivered directly into the curve of Ari's ear, sharp and unsparing.

"Look at you," she murmured, each syllable cleanly articulated. "Begging for it before the welts have even cooled. You spend all week pretending you have a spine, pretending you belong to yourself, and the moment you’re strapped to the wood you can’t wait to be stripped bare."

She ran her hand slowly up the back of Ari’s thigh, her fingers pressing into the tender, heated flesh where the paddle had landed, deliberately testing the pain tolerance.

"You don't want gentleness," she whispered, her fingers curling slightly into the skin, demanding stillness under the burn. "You want to be hollowed out. You want every scrap of your pathetic little dignity taken away until there’s nothing left to hold onto except the sound of my voice and the mark I leave on you."

She straightened up and stepped back to the table. She laid the wide leather paddle aside. From the roll, she picked up a heavy, multi-tailed suede flail—dense, stinging, and unforgiving. She shook out the tails with a dull rustle.

"You asked for all of it," Vex said from behind the frame, her voice cool and devoid of pity. "So you will take every single inch of it. Chin up, Ari. Take your breath."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I flinch under the pressure of her fingers, a sharp inhale catching in my throat. My knuckles are white around the bar again, but I force my chin up like she asked. "Yes, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex noted the white-knuckled grip on the bar, the sharp hitch of the chest, and the stubborn tilt of the chin. It was precisely where she wanted Ari balanced: stretched taut between defiance and complete unraveling.

"That's it," she said, her tone smooth, dry, and cutting. "Hold yourself up for it. Let's see how long that posture lasts."

She raised the flail, letting the suede tails drape over Ari’s heated skin for a fraction of a second—a cool, whispering contrast against the fire already burning there—before drawing back her arm with clean, fluid purpose.

The strike descended across the upper thighs and the curve of the seat. It didn't have the dull, singular impact of the paddle; instead, a dozen heavy tails bit simultaneously with a tearing, electric snap. The sound cracked through the room like dry wood breaking, instantly wrapping a blanket of sharp, stinging fire across the existing ache.

Vex did not pause to let Ari find a rhythm. The tails lifted, hissed through the air, and came down again in rapid succession, painting a cross-hatch of sharp heat across the other side. 

*Crack. Whack.*

The suede landed heavy, dense, and uncompromising. 

Vex stepped in close immediately after the second strike, pressing her left forearm across Ari’s shoulder blades, using her own body weight to pin Ari flat against the frame and ride out the violent surge of muscle tension. She leaned in until her lips brushed the shell of Ari’s ear, her breathing controlled, her voice dropping into that dark, low register.

"Feel that?" she whispered, cold and clear. "Every sharp little edge of it. That’s your choice burning away. You think you’re so clever, so capable, but out here you’re just meat and nerves waiting for permission to fall apart."

Her free hand gripped Ari’s jaw, turning their face slightly toward hers, her fingers digging just firmly enough to demand full, unbroken attention.

"You don't get to hide inside your head," she said, eyes tracking the dilation of Ari's pupils, reading the pulse leaping in the throat. "You stay right on the surface where every single lash registers. Breathe, Ari. Take the air I give you."

She held the jaw for another heartbeat, assessing the clarity in the gaze and the depth of the chest's heave against the wood, before releasing her hold and stepping back, letting the tails of the flail hang loose at her side.

"Tell me what you are," she commanded, quiet and lethal. "And tell me your colour."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the single word drop into the room, stripped of any cleverness or deflection. She caught the raw edge in the tone, the flat, desperate economy of it. She noted, too, that Ari had bypassed the first question entirely, unable to assemble the syllables for anything beyond the bare operational minimum.

She didn't let the omission slide, but she registered the green. It was the license to push past the surface and take Ari down to the floor of the headspace they had both prepared for.

"Green," Vex echoed, the word crisp and low. "Good. The baseline holds, even if your mouth can't manage the rest."

She stepped back into position, her eyes raking over the back of Ari’s thighs and hips. The pale skin was already mottling, shifting from an angry pink into a dense, dark crimson where the paddle and the first lashes of suede had crossed. She could see the fine, involuntary twitching in the hamstrings, the small tremors that traveled up the calves each time Ari tried to brace against the wood.

"You don't get to go quiet inside yourself, Ari," she said, her voice dropping into that measured, chilling cadence that gave no quarter. "You don't get to retreat into some soft, quiet corner of your mind and let your body take the beating alone. You asked for all of it. You asked to have the softening stripped out. So look at what’s left."

The flail cut through the air with a dry, sharp hiss. 

*Crack.*

The suede tails wrapped cleanly across the lower curve of the buttocks, catching the tender crease of the thighs. The sting was immediate and searing, laying a fresh grid of fire over the dull, heavy ache beneath. 

Before the sound had fully died against the walls, Vex swung again, pivoting her wrist to catch the opposite angle.

*Whack.*

The sound was heavier this time, the tails biting deep into the meat. 

"Nothing," Vex murmured over the strike, step-sliding forward so her voice pressed directly against Ari's ear over the ragged sound of their breathing. "Not a single clever argument. Not a shred of the posture you hide behind all week. Out there you manage people, you make decisions, you pretend you're in control. In here, you are strapped to my wood, completely stripped of function, waiting for the only person who knows how thoroughly useless you actually want to be."

She stepped back and delivered three clean, rhythmic blows in rapid succession—left, right, center. 

*Snap. Crack. Thud.*

The suede landed with relentless precision, working the heat into an unbroken, throbbing band from the lower hips down to the backs of the knees. The room smelled of sweat, conditioned leather, and rising body heat. The sound of the impacts filled the space, sharp and rhythmic, leaving no room for any other thought to take root.

Immediately following the third strike, Vex closed the distance. She dropped the handle of the flail, letting it dangle against her leg, and stepped chest-to-back against Ari. Her left arm came around Ari's chest, locking tight just under the collarbones to pull Ari firmly back against the solid wall of her body, while her right hand flattened over the heated, pulsing skin of the lower back.

The contact was immovable, anchoring Ari’s shaking frame between the timber in front and the living heat behind.

"Feel that," Vex ordered, her breath hot against Ari's neck, her own pulse completely steady. "That isn't an idea. That isn't something you can analyze or explain away tomorrow. That is every nerve ending you have reporting to me."

She squeezed Ari's chest firmly, forcing the ribs to expand against her arm, demanding the lungs draw full, deep drafts of air.

"Breathe," she commanded, low and absolute. "Fill your chest against my arm. Take it down into the belly. Don't you dare drift off, Ari. You stay right here in the burn."

She kept her hand pressed hard against the heated skin, letting Ari feel the cool contrast of her palm against the fire she had just built, waiting for the breathing to catch, hitch, and force itself through the shock.

"Colour," she said into the shell of Ari's ear, sharp and unrelenting. "Speak it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I press back into her, the solid warmth of her body anchoring me. The burn is all-consuming, a deep, throbbing ache that's chased away every other thought. "Green," I gasp, the word raw. "Still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept her arm locked across Ari’s chest for three long, deliberate breaths, letting Ari’s frantic heartbeat hammer directly against her forearm. She felt the heavy, ragged rise and fall of the ribs, the dead weight of a body that had completely stopped fighting the wood. The skin beneath her right palm was scorching, radiating an intense, feverish heat from the unbroken mesh of red and purple welt lines crisscrossing the thighs and seat.

"Green," Vex said, her voice a low, gravelly rasp right against Ari's ear. "Good. Because I am nowhere near finished taking you apart."

She did not release Ari gently. She pulled her supporting arm away with deliberate abruptness, stepping backward and leaving Ari suspended by the leather wrist cuffs, the chill of the room instantly biting into the damp, heated skin of their back. 

She let

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I sag forward against the straps for a moment, my head dropping. The sudden emptiness where her body was is jarring, and I let out a shaky breath I didn't know I was holding.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex watched Ari sag into the leather cuffs, noting the heavy drop of the skull and the sudden, defensive hunch of the shoulders. She didn't move immediately to correct it; she let Ari hang there for five long seconds, feeling the pull of gravity and the sudden, stark absence of her support.

Then her boots clicked against the floor, deliberate and unhurried, stopping just beside the upright.

She reached out and took a fistful of Ari's hair near the crown, not viciously, but with an unyielding grip that brooked no resistance, pulling Ari’s head up and back until the line of the throat was taut and the eyes were forced toward the ceiling.

"Did I give you permission to collapse?" Vex asked, her voice dropping into a razor-sharp whisper right against Ari’s ear. "Did I tell you that you were done holding your own weight?"

She didn't wait for an answer Ari couldn't give. Her free hand came down hard against the center of Ari’s chest, shoving the torso back against the uprights, forcing the spine straight and the chest open. 

"Look at you," she murmured, her knuckles resting against Ari’s jaw, keeping the head tilted back. "Hanging like an abandoned thing the second I take my hands off you. You’re pathetic when you get like this. Completely helpless. You talk all week about your responsibilities, your control, and the second I take the skin off your thighs, you turn into a puddle of nerves waiting for someone else to carry you."

She released the hair, letting Ari’s head stay up by sheer force of the command, and stepped back to the table. She laid the suede flail down with a soft, final thud. 

In its place, she picked up a heavy, stiff harness-leather strap—dense, unyielding, and capable of driving a deep, dull ache right through the superficial fire the flail had left behind. She folded it double in her grip, testing the snap of it against her own palm with a sharp, heavy *thwack*.

She walked back behind the frame, letting the strap drag lightly over the raised, burning welts on Ari’s seat, feeling the involuntary shudder that ran through the flesh at the contact.

"You asked for all of it," Vex said, her tone cool, flat, and absolute. "You said you didn't want it softened. So you will stand on your own two feet, you will keep your chest off the wood until I tell you otherwise, and you will take the weight of this."

She squared her stance, centering her balance, and brought the double leather down with full, measured force across the meat of Ari’s left hip.

The sound was a deep, wet crack that echoed off the bare walls, instantly slicing through the surface sting and driving a heavy, concussive jolt straight down into the bone. 

Vex didn't pause. She pivoted her hips and brought the second strike down across the right side, mirroring the first with devastating symmetry.

*Crack.*

The impact shuddered through the entire wooden frame. 

She stepped in instantly, planting her forearm hard across the back of Ari’s neck, locking Ari in place before the body could double over from the shock. She leaned her full weight over the frame, her face inches from Ari’s temple, her breathing deep, even, and calm.

"Take it," Vex commanded, the words rough and close. "Swallow the cry, Ari. Breathe the fire right down into your gut. You don't leave this room, and you don't leave this body. Colour."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: A choked noise escapes my throat, sharp and involuntary. I lock my knees, trembling violently, but I don't slump forward again. The ache is bone-deep now, a solid, grounding throb that pushes everything else out. "Green," I force out, my voice thin and strained. "Still green, Maitresse."
