dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn’t wait for Halle to bridge the rest of the gap. He caught Halle by the waist, fingers digging through fabric, and hauled them in until there wasn’t an inch of daylight left between them. 

The heel of his boot found the door behind them and kicked it shut with a heavy, unceremonious slam. He didn't care if the deadbolt caught. He didn't care about the duffel bag he’d abandoned on the porch, or the ninety-minute drive from the airfield, or the half-dozen careful, romantic things he’d rehearsed in his head on the plane. 

His face hit the crook of Halle’s neck first. He inhaled hard, a rough, shuddering sound dragged up from the bottom of his chest, drinking in the scent of home and skin like a man dying of thirst. Five months of bad coffee, cold bunks, and hollow phone calls vanished in a heartbeat.

He didn't give Halle time to settle. His hands slid up from their waist to grip Halle's jaw, rough calluses catching against soft skin, and he tilted their face up. His mouth came down on Halle’s with bruising, shameless hunger—hot, heavy, and completely stripped of any intention to take things slow.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I groan into the kiss, hands fisting in his shirt. *My own duffel bag hits the floor with a thud.* Five months is too damn long.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun crowded into Halle, driving his weight forward until the solid wood of the front door stopped them both. 

He didn't give Halle room to breathe, let alone pull away. His tongue tangled with Halle’s, reckless and deep, a low, guttural vibration rising in his chest when he felt those fists twist into his uniform. Every scrap of patience he’d tried to muster on the flight back had burned off the second Halle opened the door.

One of his hands slid down from Halle's jaw, a heavy, calloused palm dragging over their shoulder, down their ribs, and hooking hard beneath Halle’s thigh to hoist it up against his hip. He pressed in, letting Halle feel the absolute lack of restraint behind every single inch of him. 

He broke the kiss just enough to drag in air, his forehead resting hard against Halle's, his chest heaving. His mouth stayed close, lips brushing Halle's with every wrecked, ragged word. 

"Too fucking long," Jun rasped, his voice raw. "I'm not waiting another second. Bedroom, or right here?"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
That was all the answer Jun needed. 

Right here, then. 

He took Halle’s mouth again, harder this time, swallowing every breath Halle had to offer. His hands were already moving, frantic and clumsy with a five-month backlog of pure adrenaline. He yanked at the hem of Halle's shirt, desperate for the heat of bare skin, his blunt fingernails scraping lightly against ribs as he shoved the fabric up and out of the way. 

The cold hallway air didn't stand a chance against them. Jun crowded Halle flush against the door, hips driving forward, utterly unashamed of the aching, rigid proof of just how long he’d been starving. Every single inch of him was wound tight, vibrating with the sheer sensory overload of Halle under his hands, in his arms, against his chest.

"Fuck the bedroom," Jun growled against Halle’s lips, trailing open-mouthed bites down along Halle's jawline to the sensitive dip beneath the ear. His breathing was ragged, torn up by the frantic beat of his own heart. 

He reached down blindly, his hands dropping to the waistband of Halle's pants, working at the fastenings with trembling, impatient fingers. He didn't want gentle. He didn't want slow. He wanted Halle completely undone, right on the hardwood, before the scent of jet fuel and travel even had time to wash off his skin.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I shove his jacket off his shoulders, my fingers tangling in his dog tags. "Here," I manage, the word half-lost against his mouth. "Now."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The jacket hit the floor with a dull, heavy thud, joins the wreckage of their bags, but Jun didn’t give a damn about it. The cold metal of the dog tags bit into his collarbone under Halle’s grip, grounding him in the absolute best way possible.

"Good," Jun breathed against Halle's mouth, a rough, feral sound that was half-laugh and half-groan. "Fucking perfect."

He didn't bother with finesse. His thumbs hooked into the waistband of Halle’s pants, dragging fabric down over hips with ruthless efficiency. His own belt came undone next—clumsy, hurried movements of calloused hands that had spent nineteen weeks aching for this exact friction, this exact heat. 

He didn't wait to fully strip. He shoved his own trousers down just far enough to free himself, hot and aching and demanding, his pulse hammering so hard in his ears he couldn't hear anything over the sound of their combined breathing. 

Jun braced one heavy forearm against the door beside Halle's head to keep them pinned, the wood creaking softly under his weight. With his other hand, he reached down, gathering Halle up by the back of one thigh and hauling it high around his waist. 

He looked down into Halle's eyes for a fractured, breathless half-second, his dark eyes dilated, completely wrecked with a hunger he had no interest in hiding. 

"Look at you," he muttered, his voice raw, thick with six years of devotion and five months of pure starvation. 

He shifted his hips forward, finding Halle's heat with the blunt, urgent head of his cock, not teasing, not waiting, just aligning them before driving straight in with one heavy, unrelenting thrust.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Tomorrow was a problem for another lifetime. Right now, the only universe that existed was the narrow stretch of hardwood beneath their boots and the breathless, suffocating heat of Halle wrapped around him.

The breath tore out of Jun’s throat in a fractured, ruined gasp as he buried himself to the hilt. Every muscle in his back locked rigid, his fingers digging into the solid timber of the front door hard enough that his knuckles went white. Five months of cold, empty ache collapsed in on itself in a single, devastating second.

"Jesus," he swore into the crook of Halle’s neck, his voice trembling with a raw, shuddering intensity. "Jesus, Halle."

He didn’t give either of them time to adjust. He couldn't. His body was entirely on instinct now, driven by nineteen weeks of deprivation that demanded everything at once. He pulled back just an inch before driving hard back in, his hips snapping forward with a heavy, bruising cadence that rattled the brass mail slot on the front door behind them.

His arm hooked deeper behind Halle’s thigh, taking their full weight effortlessly, anchoring them flush against his chest so there was no escaping the friction. Every thrust was deep, unforgiving, and completely stripped of patience, rocking them both against the wood with a rhythmic, unhurried violence born of pure, unadulterated greed. 

He found Halle’s mouth again blindly, swallowing down every gasp and shudder, his tongue claiming theirs with rough, desperate insistence. He kissed them like a man who hadn't eaten in months, his free hand coming up to tangle ruthlessly in Halle's hair, holding them still, holding them right where he needed them. 

"Look at me," Jun rasped, pulling back just an inch, his chest heaving violently against Halle's, sweat already slicking his temples. His dark eyes burned down, heavy and possessive, watching every flicker of expression on Halle's face as his hips kept up that relentless, bruising rhythm. "Stay with me. Right here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I gasp, nails scraping over his scalp as my head thuds back against the door. "I'm not going anywhere," I rasp out, my voice wrecked.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The drag of Halle’s nails against his scalp sent a sharp, electric jolt straight down Jun’s spine, obliterating the last frayed edge of his restraint. 

"You're goddamn right you aren't," Jun growled, the words scraping rough against the shell of Halle’s ear. 

He didn't give them an inch of mercy. He adjusted his grip, both of his large hands hauling Halle up higher, wrapping Halle’s legs securely around his waist so he could drive his weight into every single stroke. His hips snapped forward with renewed, relentless urgency, each heavy thrust burying him completely, the impact shuddering through them both and rattling the brass deadbolt above their heads.

It was hot, frantic, and entirely devoid of elegance. Jun’s chest rose and fell in ragged heaves, his skin burning everywhere it met Halle’s. He pressed his face hard into the crook of Halle’s neck again, groaning low in his throat—a sound dragged straight from his ribs, raw with five months of unbearable absence and the sheer, overwhelming reality of finally being inside them again. 

His teeth grazed over Halle's collarbone, a harsh, possessive nip that gave way to a slick, open-mouthed press of his lips. He was completely consumed, losing the cadence of thought, every nerve firing on the friction, the heat, the tight, suffocating grip of Halle around him. 

"Halle," he choked out, his voice cracked down the middle. He pulled his hips back just enough to slam forward again, bottoming out hard, his calloused hands digging into Halle’s hips with bruising force to hold them completely still for him. "Right there. Fuck—don't let go."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The stumble from the hallway to the bedroom was a blur of tangled limbs, bruised knuckles catching against the doorframe, and the desperate, frantic scramble to bridge the distance without breaking contact. 

When the back of Jun’s knees hit the edge of the mattress, he went down hard, taking the impact with a heavy, breathless grunt. The familiar give of their bed—the one he’d spent five months trying to conjure the memory of in concrete barracks and noisy tents—felt almost unreal beneath his bare back. 

He didn't have time to process it. Halle was immediately there, over him, stripping away the last fragile pretense of control. 

Jun’s head fell back against the pillows, his chest heaving violently, ribs expanding against the rush of cool bedroom air and the scorching heat of Halle’s skin. A ragged, shattered sound tore out of his throat as Halle’s mouth and hands went to work. He’d spent nineteen weeks dreaming of taking, of driving, of being the one to run them both into the ground—but having Halle turn the tables, taking him apart with that deliberate, agonizing thoroughness, drove him completely out of his mind.

"Halle—fuck," Jun choked out, his voice cracked and raw. 

His fingers reached out instinctively, blunt nails knotting into the sheets, twisting the fabric into white-knuckled fists as he fought for purchase against the overwhelming tide of sensation. Every touch of Halle’s hands, every slick, deliberate drag of Halle’s mouth felt magnified tenfold, searing hot against skin that had starved for it. His hips arched up off the mattress unbidden, seeking friction, seeking pressure, chasing the exact cadence Halle set with shameless, desperate greed.

He let go of the sheets, his hands coming up instead to find Halle—calloused palms sliding over Halle's shoulders, fingers tangling fiercely into hair, not to push away, but to anchor. To hold Halle right where they were. 

"Don't stop," he rasped, shuddering hard as his eyes squeezed shut, his entire body trembling under the weight of Halle's mouth. "Take it. Take whatever the fuck you want, Halle—I'm yours."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My fingers tighten in her hair, guiding her exactly where I want her. "I know," I breathe out, the words shaky. "I've missed the taste of you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The sharp tug at his scalp sent an electric jolt straight through Jun’s spine, arching his back clean off the mattress. He surrendered to the pull without a single scrap of resistance, tilting his head back into the pillows, his throat bared and unguarded to the bedroom air and the heat of Halle’s skin.

A broken, shuddering breath tore from his chest, his pulse hammering so violently against his ribs it felt loud enough to rattle the floorboards. To have Halle holding him down, dictating the angle and the depth of every touch, completely unraveled whatever frayed edges of control he’d managed to hold onto. 

"God, Halle," Jun choked out, the words scraping raw and breathless from the bottom of his throat. 

His calloused hands moved blind, sliding up over Halle’s waist, blunt fingers digging hard into warm hips just to keep them anchored close, desperate to maintain that suffocating, skin-on-skin pressure. Every nerve ending felt raw, hyper-attuned to the weight of Halle over him, the drag of Halle's grip in his hair, and the devastating, deliberate way he was being taken apart. Five months of bearing down, of keeping his back straight and his guard up, dissolved into nothing on their bed. 

He let out a ragged, trembling groan, his hips shifting instinctively against the sheets, chasing the friction, chasing the heat. His dark eyes flickered open, pupils blown wide and dark, locking onto Halle with an intensity that was wholly stripped of pride. 

"Have me, then," he rasped, his voice thick and wrecked, his hands tightening against Halle's hips with bruising, desperate certainty. "Don't hold back a goddamn thing."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The pull was hard, sharp, and stripped clean of hesitation. 

When Halle came down, Jun met the impact dead-on, welcoming the sudden, crushing weight of Halle’s chest against hers like an impact she’d spent months waiting to absorb. The breath rushed out of her in a sharp, jagged hiss, but she didn’t yield an inch. Her fingers hooked tight behind Halle’s neck, blunt nails biting into skin to keep Halle trapped right there, mouth to mouth, breathing the same scorched air.

"Then wreck me," Jun rasped, the words half-snarled against Halle’s lips before she hauled Halle in for a kiss that had nothing soft left in it. 

Her mouth was hot, open, and demanding, teeth catching Halle’s lower lip hard enough to sting, tasting the familiar heat of home with a ferocity that bordered on feral. She was done taking it slow, done waiting for permission to fall apart. Her hands slid ruthlessly down Halle’s back, fingers digging into muscle, gripping Halle’s hips with bruising force to haul them flush against her own.

She arched up off the mattress, driving her hips into Halle’s with rough, relentless friction. Every muscle in her body was wound tight, trembling from the sheer sensory assault of Halle’s weight pinning her down, the burn of Halle's hands, and the desperate, suffocating cadence they were building together. 

"Harder," Jun breathed against Halle's mouth, her voice wrecked, broken down to the core by five months of starving. Her thighs locked around Halle's waist, anchoring them together so tightly there wasn't room for a whisper of doubt between them. "I want to wake up sore, Halle. Don't give me a single goddamn inch."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I bite down on her shoulder, my hips snapping forward with enough force to shake the bedframe. "You'll feel me for a week."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The bite dug deep enough to bruise, a sharp, electric shock of pain that ripped a ragged, breathless cry straight from Jun’s throat. 

She didn’t flinch. She arched straight into it, her neck baring completely as her heels dug into the mattress, bracing against the violent shudder of the headboard slamming into the drywall behind them. Every heavy, merciless snap of Halle’s hips drove the air from her lungs, bottoming out so hard and deep that her vision blurred at the edges.

"Good," Jun choked out, a raw, fractured sound that was half-laugh, half-sob torn from the bottom of her chest. 

Her legs clamped tighter around Halle’s waist, locking them together with frantic, bruising strength. She didn't want room to breathe; she didn't want an inch of space. Her hands clawed their way up Halle’s back, blunt fingernails dragging hard over sweat-slicked skin, scoring lines down Halle's shoulder blades before her hands locked into Halle’s hair again, pulling with ruthless, desperate demand.

She dragged Halle's mouth away from her shoulder just enough to collide their lips together, messy and frantic, tasting the metallic hint of her own skin where Halle’s teeth had marked her. 

"Make it two," she gasped against Halle’s mouth, her hips rolling up to meet every brutal thrust with wild, unhinged ferocity. Her chest heaved, slick and burning, the room spinning around the unrelenting cadence rattling the bed frame beneath them. "Ruins me, Halle. Don't you dare stop."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The headboard cracked hard against the drywall with every brutal strike, a steady, violent percussion that Jun couldn’t have cared less about. If the people downstairs had complaints, they could take it up with the brass who’d kept her gone for nineteen weeks. Right now, the only sound that mattered was the wet, unforgiving slap of skin against skin and the ruined, shameless noise tearing out of her own throat.

Jun’s fingers dug deeper into Halle’s back, her short, blunt nails sinking into slick skin, dragging downward as she pulled Halle even tighter against her. There was no space, no breath, nothing soft left to soften the collision. Her hips rolled up violently with every snap of Halle’s, meeting every bruising thrust with an unhinged, hungry rhythm of her own. The friction was searing, devastating, hitting the exact, raw center of an ache she’d carried across an ocean.

"Right there," Jun cried out, her head whipping back into the pillows, her throat exposed and gleaming with sweat in the dim bedroom light. "Fuck, Halle—yes. Harder."

Her thighs shook where they were locked tight around Halle’s waist, her inner muscles clenching down with a desperate, crushing grip. Every single stroke felt heavy enough to split her wide open, rattling through her ribs and driving the air from her chest in short, shattered gasps. She was completely at Halle’s mercy, stripped down to raw nerve endings and five months of sheer, unadulterated need.

Her hands left Halle’s back, coming up to clamp hard around Halle’s jaw, forcing Halle down until their mouths were a breath apart. Jun was shaking from head to toe, the heat pooling low in her belly tightening into a knot so fierce it bordered on agony. Her dark eyes were wild, blown wide with an intensity that burned straight through the haze.

"Look at me," Jun panted, her voice cracking as another heavy thrust slammed into her, lifting her clear off the sheets. She let out a choked, half-sobbed groan, her hips shuddering against Halle's with relentless, frantic need. "Don't you dare slow down. I'm right there—take me over, Halle. Finish it."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't slow down. I can't. My pace is brutal, frantic, and I watch her fall apart beneath me. "Come on, Jun," I gasp, my own control fraying. "Show me."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
That was the final fracture. 

Jun’s hips bucked violently off the mattress, meeting every frantic, punishing strike with a raw, shuddering desperation that abandoned every scrap of caution. The tension that had been winding tighter and tighter in her gut snapped like a severed cable, shattering white-hot behind her eyes.

"Halle—" The name tore out of her throat, broken, wild, and utterly stripped of pride.

Her inner walls clamped down in violent, rhythmic spasms, seizing around Halle with an iron, suffocating grip that pulsed with every beat of her hammering heart. Her back arched clear off the twisted sheets, her spine bowing as a jagged, breathless sob ripped from her chest. The pleasure was so sharp, so devastatingly heavy, that it turned her vision into a blind, roaring blur.

Her heels hooked ruthlessly into Halle’s hips, locking them together so deeply there wasn’t a hair's breadth of air between their skin. She couldn't have pulled back if her life depended on it; she didn't want to. She wanted to drown in it. Her hands tangled furiously in Halle’s hair and at the nape of Halle’s neck, yanking Halle down, crushing their faces together with bruising force.

She swallowed down Halle’s breathless gasps, her mouth slick, hot, and trembling violently against Halle’s lips. Every continuous, unrelenting thrust Halle drove into her sent another devastating shockwave rippling straight through her core, wringing out ruined, high-pitched groans against Halle's mouth. Tears of sheer, overloaded sensory exhaustion spilled hot over her temples, catching in her hairline. 

"Right there—fuck, don't stop, *don't stop*," Jun choked out, her voice reduced to gravel and raw need, her hands shaking as her fingers dug deep enough into Halle’s shoulders to leave marks that would last for days. She held on with everything she had, shuddering helplessly through the violent, rolling aftershocks, completely undone.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I collapse against her, the aftershocks still wracking my own body. My face is buried in her neck, breathing her in, my heart hammering against her ribs.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
The crushing weight of Halle collapsing on top of her was the best goddamn thing Jun had felt in five months. 

Her lungs fought for air beneath the heavy press of Halle’s chest, but she didn’t shift to make room. Instead, her arms came around Halle like iron bands, locking tight across Halle’s shoulder blades, holding Halle down against her with every shred of strength left in her shaking limbs. 

Jun’s cheek pressed hard into Halle’s hair. She dragged in a long, ragged inhale through her nose, drinking in the scent of sweat, salt, and home. Her own pulse was still hammering a furious, deafening cadence in her ears, her ribs rising and falling violently in sync with the heavy thud of Halle's heart. Down below, her muscles fluttered around the lingering, agonizing fullness, twitching with small, involuntary spasms that made her hiss softly through her teeth.

One of her hands moved, calloused fingers sliding slowly up through the damp strands at the back of Halle’s neck, cupping the base of Halle's skull. Her grip was possessive, steady, anchoring them both to the mattress as the room settled into a heavy, humid quiet, broken only by the sound of their wrecked breathing.

"Don't move," Jun rasped into Halle’s hair, her voice blown out and completely shot. She pressed a rough, open-mouthed kiss against Halle’s temple, her lips slick with sweat. "Stay right the fuck there." 

Her legs stayed tangled loosely around Halle's hips, her thighs trembling with deep, satisfying exhaustion. The bed was ruined, the door down the hall was probably scratched to hell, and she was already certain she wouldn't be walking right by sunrise. It was exactly what she had wanted. 

Her fingers tightened slightly in Halle’s hair, blunt nails pressing into Halle's scalp in a slow, grounding rhythm. 

"I've got you," she murmured against Halle's skin, a low, rumbling vibration in her chest. "I'm right here."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't move. My breathing starts to even out, my body heavy and boneless against hers. I turn my head just enough to press a clumsy, exhausted kiss to her collarbone. "Missed you," I mumble, the words slurred.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't get a word out either. Halle was just *there*, all at once, warm and solid and real, and five months of thinking about it didn't hold up against the actual thing. His hands were in Halle's hair and then his mouth was on Halle's and he was backing them both into the doorframe, bag skidding somewhere behind them, forgotten.

"Hi," he said against Halle's mouth, rough, breathless, like he'd only just remembered he knew the word. "Hey. Hi."

His hands weren't idle. They never were — palms sliding down Halle's back, under the hem of their shirt, fingers spreading flat against bare skin like he was checking it was still there. Still his.

"I had a speech," he said, and it came out like a confession, muffled against Halle's jaw. "It was good. You would have — " He kissed the corner of their mouth, once, hard. " — it's gone. I don't care."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
*I laugh, breathless, and slide my hands under his jacket.* "Yeah, I had one too. Something about patience."

*I pull back just enough to look at him.* "Fuck patience."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun laughed too, low and unsteady, mostly just air against Halle's throat. *Fuck patience* was the best thing he'd heard in five months. Better than the speech, probably. Definitely better than the speech.

"Okay," he said. "Okay. Good."

His hands found the front of Halle's shirt and held on, not pulling, just holding — like the floor had gone unsteady and Halle was the only fixed thing in the room. Which was roughly true. He'd spent a hundred and thirty-something nights lying awake in a cot doing arithmetic about how many hours were left, and now the number was zero and his body hadn't caught up yet. His heart was still running the old count.

He got his forehead against Halle's, eyes shut, breathing them in. Laundry soap and coffee and something underneath that was just *Halle*, the smell his brain had apparently been keeping a copy of this whole time, filed somewhere he couldn't reach it. Now it was right here. He made a sound he wasn't proud of.

"Give me a second," he said, and it wasn't a request to slow down, exactly. More like a warning. "I've been — I'm not gonna be good at this. I've been thinking about it for nineteen weeks. It's not gonna be — "

He kissed them again instead of finishing, deep and deliberate this time, hand sliding up to cradle the back of their head. Backing them the rest of the way out of the doorway, toward the hallway, toward anywhere that wasn't standing up. He kicked the door shut behind them without looking.

"Bedroom," he said against their mouth. "Or couch. I don't care. Just not standing up. I'm not made of iron."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I kiss her and keep kissing her and we don't manage to get further into the flat than the hallway for a while.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun got them as far as the wall — the one just past the coat rack, the one with the scuff on it from the time they'd moved the bookshelf — and stopped there because his legs had apparently made a decision without consulting him. His jacket was somewhere on the floor by then. He didn't remember taking it off and had a vague suspicion he hadn't, that it had just given up.

His mouth didn't leave Halle's for long enough to say anything useful. When it did, it was to breathe against the hinge of their jaw, open-mouthed, half a laugh still in it, because *fuck patience* kept coming back around and hitting him funny. Five months of being a person who didn't touch anybody, and now his hands couldn't figure out where to settle — hip, ribs, the small of Halle's back, back up to their shoulders like he was trying to memorize the whole shape of them at once and kept losing his place.

The hallway was too narrow and too bright and he didn't care. He got a thigh between theirs and his palm flat against the wall above their head for leverage, and the part of his brain that still worked — a small part, down near the bottom — noted that they were going to knock the picture frame off its nail if they kept this up. He decided he'd deal with that later. He'd buy a new frame.

"Nineteen weeks," he said, low, mostly to their throat, "and I couldn't tell you one single thing about — "

He cut himself off. Lifted his head. Actually looked at them for the first time since the door, really looked, and whatever he'd been about to say went sideways in his chest. Halle looked *tired*. Halle looked like they'd been holding a house together alone for five months and hadn't been sleeping much either. Something in Jun went quiet and hard at the same time.

He got a hand up to their face, thumb along their cheekbone, and held still for a second even though every other part of him was screaming.

"Okay," he said, quieter. "Okay. Two things. First — " he kissed their forehead, quick and rough, " — I missed you so bad it made me stupid. Second, I want to take you to bed and I want to do it properly, not in a hallway with my boots still on. So." He pulled back an inch, eyebrows up, mouth twitching. "Which way am I carrying you, or are your legs still working."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I shake my head and hook my fingers in his belt loops. "Legs are fine. Just... lead the way." *I let go of him long enough to kick off my own shoes, then take his hand.* "C'mon. Before I change my mind and take you right here."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun took the hand and didn't waste any more time on it. He walked them down the hall with his boots still on, which he'd just said he didn't want, and didn't care, because Halle was in front of him and the bedroom door was open and the count in his chest had finally, finally stopped.

The bedroom smelled like them. That hit harder than he expected — the whole flat smelled like them, but the bedroom was worse, or better, the sheets and the pillow and the lamp they'd left on. He'd thought about this room from a tent in the middle of nowhere, in a rack with a curtain, at 3 a.m. with his boots off and his body humming with nothing to do. He'd never managed to get the smell right in his head. Now he had it.

He turned Halle around at the foot of the bed and kissed them slow, one hand at the back of their neck, the other working their shirt up their ribs with more patience than he actually had. Boots got kicked off somewhere. His belt got done one-handed and badly, twice, and the second time he just gave up and let Halle handle it.

"Lie down," he said, and it came out rougher than he meant, so he said it again softer against their mouth. "Lie down. I want to look at you."

He was already down to his undershirt and jeans, and the undershirt went when Halle pulled at it, and then there was skin, a lot of it, and Jun had to close his eyes for a second because it was too much input after five months of almost none. Warm. Real. His.

He got a knee on the mattress and followed them down, and spent a while doing nothing useful at all — mouth on their collarbone, hands mapping hip and thigh, the long muscle down the outside of their leg like he was checking the territory against a map he'd been drawing wrong. He was talking, low and half-audible, none of it a speech: *missed you, missed you, you have no idea, I thought about this, I thought about this so much.*

He got his mouth lower. Slower than he'd planned, on purpose, because the tiredness in Halle's face was still sitting behind his eyes and he wanted to take the weight of them for a while, at least this. Halle's hand fisted in his hair and he made a noise against their skin and kept going, unhurried, thorough, the way you do a thing you've been waiting nineteen weeks to do properly.

Somewhere in there he stopped counting. Which was the whole point.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: The bag stays where it fell. So do most of our clothes, in a line down the hall that we are both going to find funny tomorrow.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun came back up eventually, spent, and got himself arranged along Halle's side with his arm across them and his face in their shoulder, and lay there breathing like he'd run somewhere. The ceiling of their bedroom had a hairline crack in it he'd never noticed before. He noticed it now. He had a lot of time to notice it, because he wasn't moving for a while.

His hand moved, though — slow, absent, up and down Halle's arm, shoulder to elbow, elbow to shoulder, the kind of motion a person made when they were half asleep and half checking. He'd stopped counting. It felt strange, like a sound he'd gotten used to being gone.

"Your sheets are different," he said eventually, into their shoulder, voice wrecked. "Blue now. They were grey."

That was the whole observation. He didn't elaborate, but the fact that he'd catalogued it, that he'd come home and the first thing his brain had filed away in this room was *the sheets changed*, said a lot about where he'd been and what he'd been doing there. Nineteen weeks of holding on to details like that. Grey sheets, the chipped mug, the way Halle said his name when they were annoyed. He'd kept all of it. He was glad the sheets were blue. He was glad the flat had kept moving without him, that it wasn't a museum of the day he left.

He got up once, on legs that weren't entirely his, and came back with two glasses of water because he'd been raised right and also because Halle looked like they hadn't had enough of anything in a while. He put one on the nightstand on their side and drank half of his standing up, in his undershirt and nothing else, and looked at them in his bed — their bed, he corrected himself, theirs, always had been — with an expression that was trying very hard to be casual and failing at it.

"So," he said. "You didn't sleep much while I was gone."

It wasn't a question, exactly. He said it the way you said a thing you already knew, giving them the chance to argue with him if they wanted. He set the glass down and came back to the mattress, and this time he lay on his back and pulled Halle in against his side, arm around their shoulders, which was a different thing than the first arrangement and an intentional one. He wanted them held. He'd been thinking about holding somebody for five months and it turned out the somebody was specific and the holding was the point.

"I'm not going anywhere for a while," he said to the ceiling. "Eleven weeks, minimum. Probably longer. There's a thing in the spring I might be able to dodge if I ask nicely, but I haven't asked yet, so don't — " He stopped, because that was getting ahead of it, and he'd promised himself he wouldn't come home and hand Halle a calendar like a bill. "Anyway. I'm here. That's the headline."

His thumb was working at the edge of their shoulder again. Outside, somebody's dog was losing an argument with a car. The lamp was still on and neither of them had reached for it, which he took as permission to keep looking.

"I'm gonna sleep for about fourteen hours," he said, "and then I'm gonna fix that hinge on the bathroom door that's been squeaking since before I left, because I heard it when I came in and it's been bothering me for five months. And then I'm gonna take you out somewhere and be a person in public with you, because I've been a person in public with nobody for a long time and it's started to feel weird."

He turned his head on the pillow to look at them properly. He didn't say the rest of it. He didn't need to — the way he was looking at them said it, and he was too tired for a speech anyway. He'd had a good one, once, and it was gone, and this was better.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
"I haven't slept right since you left," I admit, my voice rough. *I press my face into the side of his neck.* "Eleven weeks is a start."

I slide my leg over his. "The hinge is the priority, huh?"

(OOC: Great scene, thanks for writing with me.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun snorted, which turned into a cough because he was still catching his breath from the last hour and a half.

"No," he said. "The hinge is not the priority. The hinge is a *chore*. I'm gonna fix the hinge because if I don't have something small to do with my hands tomorrow I'm gonna follow you around the flat like a dog and you're gonna hate it by Tuesday."

His hand had stopped moving on their arm. He was quiet for a second, and the quiet had weight to it — the specific weight of a man deciding whether to say the thing he'd been carrying around in a tent for nineteen weeks or leave it where it was.

He said it.

"Priority is you. It's been you the whole time. Every time somebody asked me what I was getting back to, I said the flat, or the job, or I made a joke, because the actual answer was 'I want to be in the same room as my wife and not have to think about it.'" He said it flat, no performance in it, eyes on the crack in the ceiling. "That's not a nice thing to say to your sergeant at two in the morning. So I didn't say it. I'm saying it now."

He turned his head on the pillow again. Looked at them. Whatever he saw, it softened something in his face that five months hadn't.

"So no. Hinge is not the priority. Hinge is Tuesday. You're — " he gestured vaguely at all of them, at the leg thrown over his, at the whole warm weight of them against his side, " — you're the whole list. Everything after this is errands."

His arm tightened, just slightly. Outside, the dog had given up. The lamp was still on, and he still didn't reach for it.

"Sleep," he said, quieter. "I've got you. I'm not going anywhere."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt the last of the day drain out of him somewhere around the time his hand stopped moving on their arm. Not sleep yet — something just before it, where the ceiling went soft at the edges and the crack in the plaster stopped being interesting.

He thought about the lamp. He thought about it for a while, actually, because reaching for it meant moving his arm off Halle, and his arm had opinions about that. In the end he stretched one leg out and hooked the switch with his toes, the way he always did, the way that had annoyed Halle exactly once and then become the way it was done. The room went dark except for the streetlight doing its usual stripe across the wall.

"There," he said, to nobody in particular. "Five months of hotel lamps and I still got it."

His voice had gone down to almost nothing by the end of the sentence. He could feel his own pulse in his fingertips, slowing. Somewhere down the hall the front door was shut and the bag was still where it had fallen and there was a pair of boots in the entryway that would probably be a tripping hazard in the morning. He'd deal with it. Or he'd step over it and swear and deal with it later. He wasn't going to make a plan. He'd spent nineteen weeks making plans and he was done with them for the night.

He turned his head just enough to press his mouth to the top of Halle's head — an unremarkable kiss, nothing behind it, the kind you gave somebody you were going to see in the morning — and settled back into the pillow.

"Wake me up if I snore," he said. "I don't think I snore. But it's been a while, so I don't actually know anymore."

The stripe of streetlight sat on the wall. The flat creaked the way it always had, one board by the closet, one radiator ticking down from whatever it had been doing all day. He listened to all of it the way you listened to a song you hadn't heard in a while and could still hum.

Somewhere around then he stopped being awake, and it didn't feel like falling. It felt like putting something heavy down.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
I wake up before you do, tangled in the sheets and with your arm gone heavy across my ribs. For a minute, I just listen to you breathe.

Then I shift, just enough to press my lips to your shoulder. "You don't snore," I whisper, my voice still thick with sleep. "You talk. Something about requisition forms."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun surfaced slowly, in stages — the light first, then the arm, then the fact that the arm was asleep because he'd been lying on it wrong for however many hours, and finally the words, which had been said close enough to his ear that they'd gone in before he was awake enough to stop them.

"Requisition forms," he said, into the pillow, voice like gravel. He didn't open his eyes. "That's — that's what I talk about. I have nineteen weeks of nothing in my head and *that's* what comes out."

He rolled onto his back with a grunt, shaking the pins and needles out of his hand, and lay there squinting at the ceiling until the crack came back into focus in the same place it had been. Same crack. Same room. He was still here. That took a second to land properly, and when it did, something in his chest loosened that he hadn't known was still tight.

He turned his head on the pillow. Halle was already up, or at least awake — propped on one elbow, hair a disaster, looking at him with that particular expression people got when they'd been watching somebody sleep and had gotten caught at it. He didn't call it out. He just looked back, unguarded, for longer than he usually allowed himself.

"What time is it," he said, and then, before they answered, "No. Don't tell me. If it's after eleven I'm gonna feel bad and I'd rather not."

He got his good hand up and laid it on their forearm, thumb moving once across the inside of their wrist, feeling the pulse there. Real. Warm. The requisition forms could go to hell.

"You been up long?"

The question was ordinary. The way he asked it wasn't — quiet, and a little careful, because "up long" was a different question than it sounded like, and they both knew it. He was asking whether Halle had slept. He was asking it with his thumb on their pulse, which was the only way he knew how.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun got pulled down and went, and the hand that had been resting careful on Halle's wrist came up to the back of their neck and *held* — not gentle, not checking. The question he'd been asking without asking it got answered, and he took the answer.

"Okay," he said, low, against their mouth. "Okay. You got it."

The carefulness went out of him like water off a dropped plate. Nineteen weeks of holding still, of not touching, of being a person who kept his hands to himself — it came off all at once, and what was underneath was a man who had been counting the hours and had opinions about what to do with them. His mouth moved off their mouth and down, hard, teeth at the hinge of their jaw, palm flat on their sternum pressing them back into the mattress, and he didn't ask twice.

"You want to feel it tomorrow," he said into the side of their throat, and it wasn't a question, it was a confirmation, filed away. "Then you're gonna. I'm not gonna be careful. You asked."

He got a knee between theirs and his weight behind it, one hand fisted in the sheets by their head and the other one working — hip, thigh, the inside of their leg, everywhere at once and none of it polite. The bedframe complained. He ignored it. Somewhere in the back of his head the part of him that fixed hinges and put glasses of water on nightstands was still awake and watching, but it had been outvoted, and it knew it.

"Tell me if it's too much," he said, and it was the only soft thing left in his voice, the one thread of it he wasn't willing to cut. Then he stopped talking and did what he'd been thinking about for nineteen weeks, which was a lot, and none of it was gentle.

Halle:
I don't say anything. I just hold onto him and let him.

Jun:
Jun didn't need anything back. That was the thing he'd figured out somewhere around the third month away — that what he wanted wasn't a response, it was *access*, the plain fact of being allowed. Halle holding on and letting him was the whole answer. He took it.

He worked them over without hurry and without mercy, both at once, the way you did a thing you'd been rehearsing in your head until it stopped being a fantasy and started being muscle memory. His hand at their hip, his mouth lower, the weight of him pinning them to the mattress whenever they moved wrong. The sheets got kicked down to the foot of the bed and stayed there. The lamp was still on and he didn't care; he wanted to see it, wanted the record of it, wanted to be able to close his eyes later and have the picture still there.

When they got close he didn't let up. When they came he didn't stop until they were done, hands shaking, and only then did he come back up over them, braced on both arms, breathing hard through his nose, looking down at them like he'd just come back from somewhere and was checking the room was still standing.

"Okay," he said, rough. "Okay. That's — yeah. That's what I wanted."

He got himself down onto his elbows, weight half on them, face in the pillow next to their head, and stayed there for a while. His hand found theirs in the sheets and held it, loose, no grip in it at all — just there, palm to palm, both of them damp and stupid and breathing.

"For the record," he said into the pillow, muffled, "I *was* gonna be nice. I had a whole plan. Water, back rub, the works."

He turned his head enough to look at them sideways. His mouth was doing something that wasn't quite a smile yet.

"You ruined it. Good call."

Halle:
I laugh, breathless, and turn my head to kiss his knuckles where our hands are tangled together. "You can do the back rub later. I'm not going anywhere."

Jun:
Jun made a sound into the pillow that was approximately agreement and approximately a man who had just been given permission to stop being careful and had used it up.

"Later," he repeated. "Yeah. Later. I've got — " he gestured vaguely with his free hand at the room, the flat, the whole world, " — eleven weeks. I've got time. First time in five months I've had time."

He rolled onto his back, mostly, taking their hand with him so it stayed tangled on his chest, and stared at the ceiling. The crack was still there. The streetlight was still doing its stripe. Somebody downstairs was running water and the pipes in the wall ticked along with it. All of it ordinary, all of it the same as it had been the day he left, and he was in the middle of it instead of looking at a photograph of it. That was the whole thing. That was what he'd been trying to get back to.

"Back rub's a good idea though," he said, after a minute. "You look like you've been carrying a house."

He didn't move to do it yet. He was too comfortable, and too wrung out, and Halle's hand was on his chest and he wasn't going to be the one to break that. He turned his head on the pillow to look at them properly — the sleep-flattened hair, the marks coming up on their neck, the whole unpolished fact of them — and let himself look for longer than was strictly necessary.

"I'm glad I came home to you," he said. Flat, no performance. It was the kind of thing he usually dressed up as a joke. He didn't this time. He'd spent five months not saying the plain version of things to anybody, and it turned out the plain version was easier than he'd remembered.

Then he reached over with his free hand and finally, finally turned the lamp off, because it was morning and neither of them needed to be awake yet, and the dark of their own bedroom was the best thing he'd seen in nineteen weeks.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I reach over and smooth my thumb over his eyebrow. "You look tired too," I murmur. "But you're here now. That's the part that matters."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun let his eyes close under the thumb. It was an odd, small thing — nobody had touched his face like that in five months, and the few people who'd touched his face at all in that time had been a medic with a penlight and a barber with clippers. He stayed very still for it, which was its own kind of answer, and didn't make a joke about it, which was a bigger one.

"Mm," he said, which meant *yeah* and also *keep doing that* and also, faintly, *don't stop, I'm not done being touched yet.*

His hand was still flat on his chest with theirs tangled in it. He could feel his own heartbeat through both palms, slower now than it had been in months, and he noticed it the way you noticed a noise stopping — only after the fact, only by the quiet.

"You know what I did the first night in country," he said, eyes still shut, voice low and going lower. "Couldn't sleep. Too loud, too hot, rack was too narrow. So I did the math. Hours left. Got it down to a number I could hold in my head. Four thousand and something. And then every night I'd knock a few hundred off it." He turned his head a fraction, into the pillow, into her hand. "It was the only thing I was good at over there. Counting down to you."

He was quiet for a second after that, like he'd surprised himself saying it.

"Anyway." His mouth moved, half a smile, tired. "Number's zero now. Don't know what I'm gonna count instead. Probably nothing. Probably gonna have to just — be here." He squeezed their hand once, brief, no grip. "Turns out that's harder than counting. We'll see how I do."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun heard it and something in his chest turned over — a click, like a bolt going home. *Don't stop.* He'd been half-finished, sprawled and wrung out, and it turned out he wasn't done. He'd been holding back a reservoir of it for nineteen weeks and the first round had barely cracked the seal.

"Didn't plan on stopping," he said, and it came out low and rough, nothing gentle left in it. "You said don't be gentle. I listened."

He rolled back over onto his hands and knees, one arm braced beside their head, and looked down at them for a second — the marks coming up on their neck, the sheet shoved to the foot of the bed, the lamp still burning on the nightstand because neither of them had bothered. They were a mess and they were *his* mess and he'd been staring at a tent wall thinking about exactly this for five months.

He got his hand under their knee and pulled it up over his hip, and then there wasn't any more talk in him. He came down onto them slow the first time and hard the second, and after that there was no counting to it, no plan, just the plain physical arithmetic of being home. His mouth stayed at their throat, at the hinge of their jaw, and what he said wasn't words so much as a running low noise of *there, there, yes, like that*, and every time they moved under him his grip on their hip tightened like he was afraid of losing the thread.

The bedframe gave up being subtle about it. Somewhere below, a dog started barking at nothing, and Jun — who had spent five months being the quietest possible person in a barracks full of people who needed to sleep — did not care in the slightest. He got his forehead against theirs and his eyes shut and kept going, driving into them with the whole weight of his hips, and when he felt them start to tighten around him again he didn't slow down, he *didn't*, he chased it, and he said their name into the space between their mouths, once, like it was the only word left.

"Come on," he breathed. "Again. With me. Now."

And then he stopped thinking about it entirely and just held on, hips snapping, breath ragged, every muscle in his back working, and when they came he came too, teeth against their shoulder, muffling something that might have been a word and might not have been. The whole length of him went rigid and then went slack, and he stayed exactly where he was, buried, forehead on theirs, breathing hard through his nose, because pulling out felt like the wrong direction.

"...There," he managed, after a while. "There. *Now* we're even."

He got his weight off them carefully, rolled to the side, and lay on his back with his arm thrown over his eyes. His chest was still heaving. The crack in the ceiling was back. So was the streetlight. So was every ordinary thing in the room, and he was in it, and they were next to him, and the count was still zero and stayed zero.

"Neighbours hate us," he said, from under his arm. "Don't care."

He lifted the arm enough to look at them sideways, sweat still cooling on his chest, and his mouth pulled into something slow and unguarded that was almost a grin.

"Back rub's still on the table," he said. "But I'm gonna need a minute. Maybe two."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I drag my fingers down the center of his chest. "Two minutes. Then you're on back rub duty." I roll onto my side and tuck my face against his shoulder. "I'm not letting you off the hook."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun stayed under his arm for the full two minutes and maybe a few extra, because he'd earned them and because he knew Halle was counting. Then he rolled his head and caught them watching him, and something in his face gave.

"Fine," he said. "Fine. Roll over. I owe you."

He got up off the mattress, which his body had opinions about — everything in him was stiff in a way that was new and also deeply familiar from the last time he'd been home — and filled the glass on their side of the nightstand and drank the rest of his own standing up. Then he came back and got a knee on the mattress, and Halle rolled onto their stomach, and he looked at their back for a second before he touched it. There was more of them than there'd been in his head. The whole shape of a person, real, under his hands, and every knot in it his to find.

He started at the shoulders. Not the polite kind of back rub — the kind that found the places and worked them, thumbs in hard along the ridge of muscle beside the spine, palm flat to spread the weight. He found a knot under the left shoulder blade and stayed on it until it gave, and when it did he felt Halle breathe out under him and something in his own chest loosen in sympathy.

"Right here," he said, low, working his knuckles along the muscle. "You've been carrying everything in this shoulder. I can tell. Left's worse than right, which means you were carrying it with one arm. Probably the bag. Probably the shopping, over and over, for five months."

He didn't need an answer. He moved down their back, slow, thorough, using the heel of his hand on the long muscle that ran to their hip, and found more of the same — a body that had been holding itself up alone and hadn't been asked to put anything down. He put his weight into it. The bed creaked under his knee and he ignored it.

"When I was a kid my mom used to do this," he said, to their spine. "When I couldn't sleep. Same thing. Find the knot, stay on it, don't stop just because it hurts." He worked a thumb in at the base of their neck and felt them go boneless a little, and his mouth pulled. "She'd say the body keeps score. All the stuff you don't say, it goes in the shoulders." A pause. "So what's in yours. What'd you not say for five months."

He asked it flat, the way he asked everything, hands still moving, giving them somewhere to put it or not. Down at the small of their back he slowed, palms flat, spreading warm. Then he got up onto his knees and did the arms, both of them, one at a time, elbow and wrist and the hard pad of the hand, because he had a theory that nobody ever did the hands and the hands were where people held the most. He pressed his thumb into the center of Halle's palm and held it there.

"That's the whole thing," he said, quietly, still working. "That's the back rub. Two minutes' worth, roughly. I took my time."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: My eyes are closed and my face is pressed into the pillow. "You," I say, voice muffled. "Everything I didn't say was about you." I turn my head to the side. "Did you really count down from four thousand?"

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's hands stopped for a second on Halle's arm, thumbs still pressed into the meat of their palm, and he looked at the back of their head rather than at anything else in the room.

"Yeah," he said. "Four thousand three hundred and change. I did it in the rack, first night, because I couldn't sleep and there was nothing else to do with my head."

He started moving again — same rhythm, same weight, up the forearm now, elbow, the long muscle of the upper arm. It was easier to talk with his hands busy. That was probably why he'd started the back rub in the first place.

"I didn't have a notebook. They don't like you keeping notebooks about when you're getting out, it's a whole thing. So I did it in my head and I checked it every night before I slept. Four thousand three hundred. Knock off twenty-four, knock off twenty-four. Sometimes I'd get confused about whether I'd already knocked off that day and I'd have to start the week over, go back and redo it." He worked a thumb into the crook of their elbow. "Sounds stupid. It wasn't stupid at the time. It was the only thing in my day that had an end to it."

He switched arms. Started at the shoulder, where the good knot had been, and found that the right side was better — less buried, more give. He stayed on it anyway.

"Somewhere around week twelve it got bad enough that I quit sleeping and just did the math. Lying there, counting, all night. Sergeant found me asleep sitting up in the mess at breakfast and gave me hell about it and I told him it was the food." His mouth twitched, but it didn't get all the way to a smile. "He knew. He didn't push it. Guys like that always know."

He moved down to Halle's hand, palm up, and worked the pad of his thumb across the heel of it in slow circles, the way he'd done on the other side.

"The last week I stopped counting," he said. "Not on purpose. Just — the number got small enough that it stopped being a thing I needed. Four hundred, three hundred, whatever. Somewhere in there my brain decided it could hold it without checking every night." He pressed into the center of their palm and held it, like before. "That was a good week. First good week in a while."

He let go of the hand and sat back on his heels, and now there was nothing left to do with his own hands, so he put them flat on his thighs and looked at Halle properly.

"That's the whole answer," he said. "Yeah. I really did." A beat. "You asked what was in my shoulders. That was in my shoulders."

He didn't ask the follow-up question out loud, but it was sitting there in his face — *so what was in yours, besides me* — and he was patient enough to leave it on the table and not pick it back up himself.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I turn onto my back and pull him down by the wrist. "My shoulders are empty now. You can put something else in them tomorrow." I kiss his knuckles again, slow. "But today, you're done counting."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun had planned to say something when the door opened. He had in fact planned several things, over roughly nineteen weeks, and had rehearsed at least two of them.

Halle got the door open and he forgot all of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I don't say any of the things I planned either. I drop the bag and close the distance.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He forgot all of them the second he saw her.

His bag hit the floor hard enough to rattle, and he did not even look down. His hands were shaking and his chest was too tight to breathe right, and he laughed once, short and wrecked, because none of his rehearsed lines had survived.

"Hi," he said, and then, "God — I missed you."

He held his arms out and stepped forward and did not stop. He did not want dinner first. He did not want to ease in slow or be polite about it.

"I don't want to wait," he said. "I missed you so bad it hurt. Tell me I can — please tell me I don't have to wait."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content:
*I wrap my arms around you so tight it probably hurts. My face is buried against your neck, breathing you in.*

"Missed you so much I thought I'd go crazy," I murmur, voice rough. "Don't wait. Not a second more."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
He broke the second he heard it.

A wrecked sound tore out of him, half laugh and half sob, and he locked his arms around her and held on like he was afraid the floor would drop out again. His whole body shook against her. His face pressed hard into her hair and he breathed in, deep and shuddering, like he'd been holding his breath for five months straight.
