dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear grinned and let out a low, pleased laugh. He shoved himself off the wall he had been braced against and drove forward hard on the balls of his feet. He snapped his teeth together once and shouted, "Counted. No generosity!"

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I laugh, already turning to run, but you're fast. I can feel you right behind me as I bolt through the living room.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: He thundered into the living room at full tilt and barked out another laugh. He dug in hard with each step, closed the gap to nothing, and snapped his teeth in the air. He growled, "No head start next time," and reached out wide as he ran.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear hit the hallway a half-step later and threw his full weight forward. He locked both arms tight and hauled back hard to kill the last of the momentum. He ducked his head and sank his teeth into a shoulder through the shirt and held on, growling around the mouthful. He laughed against the bite and said, "Mine. That's one for me."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I stumble a little when you grab me, letting out a huff of air. "That's a sloppy point," I say, but I'm grinning.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear snorted and shook his head hard without loosening his bite. He crowded in closer and braced his feet wide to hold steady under the weight. He eased back just enough to nip again in the same spot and muttered, "Sloppy still counted. That's my point."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear laughed hard against the bite and let go with a last sharp nip. He dropped straight to the hallway floor and landed heavy on his knees. He fisted his own shirt at the collar and hauled it up and off and flung it behind him. He tore at his belt and shoved his jeans down roughly and kicked them off one foot. He bared his teeth and growled out, "Floor's good. Clothes are in my way," and scored the wood with his nails.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: *I push you back onto the floor, climbing on top with a rough laugh.* "My point now. Keep up."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear hit the floor flat on his back with a hard thump and laughed up at the ceiling. He planted his bare feet wide and dug his nails into the wood as he braced. He snapped his teeth together and tipped his throat back open in a dare. He growled, "Counted. Yours. Now keep it if you can."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: He struck again instantly without pulling back. He clamped his teeth down hard in the same spot and held the pressure deep and steady. He growled low around the bite and braced his bare heels hard into the wood. He let go with a slow drag of his teeth and laughed breathlessly against the mark. He rasped, "Counted. That's two for me."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I push my hips down hard against yours, my own teeth finding the muscle of your chest. "Two for two," I mumble against your skin, not letting go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear snarled and arched hard up off the floorboards into the burn on his chest. He dug his bare heels in deep and drove his hips upward hard. He fisted both hands tight and dragged his nails down the wood as he braced. He threw his head back with a rough laugh and rasped, "Counted. Two for two. Mine next."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear snarled with delight and surged up off the floorboards. He trapped both offered wrists in his hands and held them hard against the wood. He bent his head and sank his teeth deep into the inside of one wrist and held the pressure growling. He switched to the other wrist and bit down hard again and let go with a slow drag. He laughed rough against the marks and rasped, "Counted twice. You'll find them tomorrow and feel them Thursday."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I collapse onto you, breathing hard. "Don't let me up," I say, pressing my face against your neck. "Not for a while."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear grunted and clamped both arms tight and held on hard. He dug his bare heels into the floorboards and braced his weight steady underneath. He tipped his head back to bare his throat and stayed pinned and breathed deep. He rumbled low in his chest and growled, "Not moving. Mine a while."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear grunted and locked both arms harder around the weight on top of him and pinned it down against his chest. He dug his bare heels into the hallway floor and held his ground and refused to give an inch. He turned his head and sank his teeth into the neck against his mouth and held on growling. He rasped, "Not letting up. Mine."

He drove his hips up hard off the floorboards and kept the rhythm deep and steady. He braced his feet wide and snarled around another bite and shook his head once. He fisted one hand in the back of the shirt still in the way and hauled at it. He growled, "Don't stop means don't stop."

He kept thrusting upward hard and fast and did not slow. He arched his back off the wood and bared his teeth and bit down again on the shoulder over him and held the pressure. He dragged his nails hard across the floorboards as he drove. He snarled, "Take it. Keep it."

He slammed his hips up one last time and held deep and shuddered hard underneath and spilled himself with a rough, open-mouthed snarl against the mark he had left. He stayed buried and breathed hard through his teeth and kept his arms clamped tight. He laughed breathlessly and licked once over the bite and growled, "Counted. Still mine."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I bite down on your shoulder again, shuddering as I follow you over the edge. I don't let go for a long moment, my breath hot against your skin. "Good," I finally manage to say, my voice rough.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear groaned low under the fresh pressure on his shoulder and shuddered hard through his whole frame. He clamped both arms tighter and held steady underneath. He tipped his head sideways to offer more skin and bared his teeth in a spent grin. He rumbled deep in his chest and growled, "Good. Take all of it. I counted yours."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I slump fully against you, boneless and heavy. "Floor's gonna suck tomorrow," I mutter, but I make no move to get off you.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content: Bear chuckled low in his chest and clamped both arms tighter around the weight on top of him. He shifted his bare shoulders once against the hard floorboards and grunted at the ache and settled back down. He turned his head and licked once slow over the bite within reach and rumbled. He muttered, "Floor's gonna suck tomorrow. Worth it. Stay put."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Your shirt's halfway down the hall," I point out, not opening my eyes. "Mine's probably ruined."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline had been waiting since about six, which Roan established by the simple method of looking at her.

"How long?"

"Long enough," Aveline said, which meant too long, and meant she had enjoyed every minute of it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Come here, then," I say, and sit back to watch her cross the room.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline crossed the room with slow, deliberate steps, as though every inch of the distance mattered. She did not rush. Rushing would have spoiled the waiting, and she had grown fond of the waiting, the way it sharpened everything that followed.

When she reached him, she stopped just within reach, close enough that he could see the faint warmth in her cheeks, the quiet steadiness in her hands. Then she lowered herself to the floor beside his chair, not clumsily, not with hesitation, but with the ease of someone who had made a habit of choosing where to be.

She settled with her hands folded in her lap, her posture open and attentive. Her gaze lifted to his, soft but clear.

“I’m here,” she said.

A small pause. The kind that was not empty.

“Tell me what you want from me,” Aveline added, “and I’ll do it well.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I let the silence stretch for a moment longer, enjoying the way she holds herself.* "I want you to pour me a drink. And then tell me about your day. Start from the beginning."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline inclined her head, the motion small and certain. “Yes.”

She rose from the floor without hurry, her movements unhurried but exact, the way everything about her had become in the years of learning him. She crossed to the sideboard, where the bottles stood arranged by preference and occasion, and she selected his usual one without needing to ask. Her hands were steady as she uncapped it, poured just the right amount over a single clear cube of ice, then added a splash of water only if she judged it would suit him better tonight. She wiped the outside of the glass with the back of her thumb, checked the level, and carried it back to him.

She set the drink within reach, angled so the glass would be easiest for him to take, then returned to her place beside his chair and lowered herself again with the same quiet ease.

Her hands settled back into her lap. She looked at him, not with apology, but with the steady pleasure of having done well.

“From the beginning,” she said. “I woke before the alarm. There was light coming through the curtains, pale and early, and the house was quiet enough that I could hear the street outside. I lay still for a moment and thought about how long the day would feel without you in it.”

A soft breath escaped her, amused and warm.

“I made coffee first. Not too much—just enough to think. I washed the dishes from last night, dried the counter twice because the first pass left a smear near the sink, and then I wrote out the list for the day. That was when I decided I wanted the house to feel settled when you came home. Not perfect in a way no one could live in, but… ready. As if the whole place had been holding its breath for you.”

She smiled faintly, remembering.

“I went to the market. I know you like the bread from the place on the corner, and they had it still warm, so I bought two loaves. One for now, one for later. I spoke to the woman behind the counter, the one with the flour always on her apron, and she asked about you. I told her you were well, though I did not tell her how often I find myself smiling like that when I talk about you. It is a bad habit, but I have decided not to cure myself of it.”

Her gaze stayed on his, clear and attentive.

“I came home and spent some time in the garden. The roses are opening faster than I expected, and I deadheaded the ones by the path so they would not look careless. I noticed the light was different this afternoon—lower, softer—and I stood there for longer than I meant to, thinking about how it would look through the window when you were in this room. I wanted to be here to see you notice it, but I did not want to crowd you either.”

She paused, folding her hands a little more neatly.

“I cleaned the guest room because I thought you might want somewhere undisturbed. I folded the linens, opened the window for an hour, then closed it when the air turned cooler. I made the bed with the corners straight, because I like that you do not have to see a single thing out of place when you want to rest.”

Aveline’s voice warmed, but did not become uncertain.

“After that, I sat down with my notes for the week. I wanted to have the days ahead arranged so there would be no confusion, no loose ends. I wrote down what you like for dinner, what needs mending, what I could prepare in advance. Then I looked at the clock and realized it was nearly six, and I felt the waiting turn into something almost sweet. I kept thinking you would come in at any moment, and every time I was wrong, I was glad I had been right to wait.”

She lifted one shoulder in the smallest, most honest shrug.

“So that is the day. Quiet. Ordered. Full of small things that seemed worth doing because they would make the hours afterward easier for you.” Her eyes softened. “I liked it. I liked being in the house while it belonged to us both, even if only I was moving through it. It felt like tending something that mattered.”

A brief pause. Then, with a steadier warmth:

“I hope you drink it well. I hope the day was worth telling you about. And if you want to hear the rest—the ordinary parts, the parts that are not grand—I will tell those too. You asked for the beginning, and I have given you that, but I can go on as long as you want.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I let her kneel and I don't tell her to do anything for a moment, because the waiting is most of what she came for.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline remained where she was, kneeling beside the chair with her hands folded in her lap and her back straight without stiffness. She had learned, over the years, the difference between a silence that waited for her to speak and a silence that simply let her be. This one felt like both, and she found she did not mind the ambiguity.

The drink stood within reach, a small circle of condensation gathering at the base of the glass. She did not look at it, did not reach for anything, did not shift herself for comfort. Comfort had never been the point. To be where she was wanted, and to hold that place without complaint, was its own kind of reward.

After a while, she let her voice soften.

“I am not going anywhere,” she said. “If you are tired, you can rest, and I will keep the room still around you. If you want to talk, I am here. If you want only to sit with the quiet, I will not make it a performance.”

A faint smile touched her mouth.

“The waiting is not a cost,” she added, more quietly. “It is part of the pleasure. I like being asked for something, and I like being trusted enough to be left with it.”

She lowered her gaze to his for only a moment, then let it return, steady and clear.

“Take your time. I have all of it.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I take the glass and sip slowly, savoring the burn. "You did well," I say, setting it down. "Now come closer. I want to feel your hands."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s face softened at the praise, not with relief, but with the quiet, unmistakable pleasure of being seen.

She rose from her place beside his chair with the same unhurried grace she used for everything that mattered. When she came closer, she did not stop at the edge of reach. She moved in until she was near enough for him to see the steadiness in her eyes, the faint warmth along her cheeks, the way her hands rested loosely at her sides, ready to be useful.

She lowered herself to her knees again, closer than before, and looked up at him with open attention.

“Would you like to hold them,” she asked softly, “or shall I put them where you want them?”

She did not rush him. She simply lifted both hands, palms turned upward, fingers relaxed, offering them without demand.

“I can wait,” Aveline added. “I like being useful.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She has both of us out of everything in the way inside a minute and gets straight to work with her hands and her mouth, unhurried about it.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline moved through the last part of the instruction with the same focused ease she brought to everything, as though undressing them both were just another task she had been given and intended to do beautifully.

She had him free of his clothes with quick, capable hands, folding nothing in haste, setting garments aside with care only when it did not slow what mattered more. When they were both as bare as they needed to be, she did not retreat, did not ask for reassurance, did not make the moment about herself. She simply shifted into the space where she could be most useful, settling once again at his feet with her back straight and her attention completely given.

Her hands found him first, warm and steady, holding him with the confidence of someone who had studied what he liked and remembered every detail. She was slow at first, almost deliberately so, as though she wanted to make sure he felt how much of this was choice, how much of it was pleasure offered freely. Her thumbs moved with careful pressure, her fingers learning his rhythm, adjusting without needing to ask.

When she leaned in, she did so without shame or hesitation. Her mouth was as unhurried as her hands, taking him in with a soft attentiveness that was meant to please, not to rush toward anything. She let herself settle into the work of it, breathing through the closeness, keeping one hand in contact with him so she could feel every subtle shift, every change in tension.

She paused now and then, not because she lacked confidence, but because she liked knowing he could feel her. When she looked up, her eyes were calm and warm.

“I have you,” Aveline said quietly, voice low from near his hands. “I can stay right here for as long as you want me to.”

Her mouth curved faintly, not quite a smile, more a private satisfaction.

“You don’t have to say anything,” she added. “But I do like it when you tell me.”

She went back to work after that with even more attention, her hands and mouth moving together in a rhythm that was careful, devoted, and entirely her own. There was no performance in the way she served him, no anxious need to prove herself. If anything, she seemed more settled in her body, more present, more pleased, the longer she was allowed to do something so plainly and well.

At times she let her fingers brush over him in a slower, broader way, as though she could not help enjoying what she was doing. At other times she kept her touch firmer, steadier, her mouth working with a soft, patient focus that left no doubt she meant it to feel good.

She stayed close, breathing warm and even, her hands never idle, her attention never scattered.

When she looked up again, there was a faint shine on her mouth and a quiet certainty in her eyes.

“Tell me if you want me to change,” she said, voice lower now. “Otherwise, I’m going to keep taking care of you.”

Then she returned to what she was doing with the same unhurried devotion, as though his pleasure were the clearest and most important thing in the room.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I reach down and slide my fingers into her hair, not pulling, just resting there. "You can change the rhythm," I tell her. "Faster."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s breath softened at the contact, though she did not falter. The weight of his fingers in her hair seemed to steady her even as she shifted pace, taking the instruction with the same quiet pleasure she took in being trusted with it.

“Faster,” she repeated softly, not as a question, but as a confirmation, a thing she could hold and give shape to.

She changed without hesitation, her rhythm becoming quicker, more insistent, though never careless. Her hands stayed firm and attentive, her mouth following the pattern with a devotion that was easy to feel in the way she gave herself to it completely. She did not rush in a way that blurred the moment. Instead, she sharpened it, making every motion more deliberate, more present, as though she wanted him to feel the exact point where her attention became action.

Occasionally she glanced up through her lashes, warm-eyed and open, checking for nothing but the simple fact of him enjoying it.

When she spoke again, her voice was lower, steadier, made rougher by closeness.

“Like this?”

She did not wait for praise to keep going. She simply held the rhythm, letting the pace speak for her, letting him feel how attentively she followed his words.

A small smile touched her mouth, private and pleased.

“I like being told what you want,” she said quietly. “It makes it easier to give it well.”

She stayed close, her hands moving with more certainty now, her mouth working with a patience that had grown quicker, warmer, more focused. The faster rhythm did not take her away from him; it only made her more clearly hers. She took care of him with every motion, and in the quiet satisfaction of her face, it was plain that this was where she wanted to be.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: She uses her mouth with the sort of attention that comes from years of practice and genuine enthusiasm, and doesn't stop when I tell her not to.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline did not stop.

The instruction had been clear enough for the years between them: he had asked her to keep going, and she heard the request as both permission and trust. She accepted it without hesitation, without embarrassment, without turning the moment into a test. This was not a scene where she had to prove herself. This was simply what she had become very good at—attending to him, reading him, giving him pleasure in the way he preferred.

She stayed at her task with the same focused warmth she had carried all day. Her hands remained steady, her mouth attentive, her rhythm quicker than before but never careless. Every motion had intention in it: a softness that showed devotion, a firmness that showed confidence, a patience that showed how much she enjoyed serving him. Years of practice made the work smooth, but genuine enthusiasm kept it alive; there was no routine in the way she cared for him, only the deep pleasure of doing it well.

The room felt close and quiet around them, filled with the small sounds of breath and movement. Aveline did not rush toward the end. She let the moment lengthen, letting each change in his response guide her. When she looked up, her eyes were calm and clear, not anxious, not seeking approval so much as sharing it. She liked seeing how well she could do when he trusted her enough to direct her.

Then she slowed, not because she was stopping, but because she wanted to make the pleasure last. Her hands stayed close, her attention unwavering, her expression open and soft. She gave him time, and she gave him care, until the whole effort felt complete.

Aveline rested for only a moment before lifting her gaze to him. Her lips were flushed, her hair slightly loosened, and her face held the particular brightness of someone who had done exactly what she wanted to do.

“I didn’t stop,” she said quietly, with a small, pleased smile. “Because you asked me not to.”

She let the words settle, then added in the same low, steady voice:

“I’m still here. Still yours. Still willing.”

A pause, gentle and attentive.

“Tell me what you want next, and I’ll do it well.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: *I let my hand rest on her cheek, thumb brushing her lower lip.* "Good. Now take me to bed. I want you under me while you're still warm from that."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline let his thumb rest against her lower lip for a moment longer, then leaned briefly into the touch, not to take anything from him, but simply to accept the closeness he offered.

“Good,” she echoed softly, as though the word were a gift she intended to carry into the next thing he asked of her.

She rose from the floor without hurry, steady and bare and still warm from what she had done. She crossed to the sideboard first, not because he had asked, but because she noticed the glass there and wanted the next part of the evening undisturbed. She set it safely aside, wiped a stray drop from the wood with her thumb, then turned back toward him.

“This way,” she said quietly.

She went ahead toward the bedroom, not rushing, not pulling, only making the path clear. When she reached the bed, she pulled back the covers with both hands, arranged the pillows the way he preferred, and smoothed the sheet beneath them so there would be nothing crumpled or careless. She did all of it with the same focused ease she had used to pour his drink and tend to him, as though preparing this space were just another way to show him she meant to take care of him well.

Then she stood at the bedside, looking back toward the room, toward him. Her cheeks were flushed, her lips still soft from use, and there was a steady brightness in her eyes that had nothing to do with uncertainty.

“I’m ready,” Aveline said. “If you want me under you, then come. I’ll wait here.”

She did not make it a demand. She did not need to. She simply lay back against the pillows, letting the bed take her weight, and drew the sheet down enough to leave room for warmth. Her body felt open and sensitive, still humming with the work of her hands and mouth, and she let that settle into her posture rather than hiding it. She moved one hand to her thigh, parting her legs with quiet willingness, making a clear place for him without hesitation or shame.

Her voice came softer now, lower and calmer, meant for the room and for him.

“I’m still warm,” she admitted, with a faint, pleased smile. “From taking care of you. From being told what you wanted. From doing it well.”

A pause. She looked up at him with open attention, steady and unhurried.

“So come when you’re ready,” Aveline said. “I’ll be under you, and I’ll stay here until you want me to move.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Don't stop and don't get to finish," I tell her. "Not until I say. Tell me you understand." She says she understands, and thanks me for it, which is exactly the arrangement.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline’s breath caught softly, then steadied. She looked up at him with clear, obedient eyes, and something in her face eased at the command because it was exactly what she wanted: structure, permission, and the trust of being held by his will.

“I understand,” she said.

Her voice was low, calm, and certain.

“I won’t stop. I won’t finish unless you say so.”

A small pause followed, and then her expression softened with gratitude.

“Thank you,” she added. “I understand what you’re giving me by telling me.”

She did not move to rush him or coax him. She simply remained where she was, bare and warm and waiting, her hands resting lightly on the sheet beside her. Her body stayed open to him without becoming demanding, her legs parted enough to show she had made a place for him, and her breathing slow enough that he could hear the control in it.

When he came closer, if he came closer, she let herself go still beneath him, offering no resistance and no performance. She only lifted her gaze, holding his attention with quiet steadiness, letting him feel that she was entirely there for him.

Her lips curved faintly, not in triumph, but in simple, devoted pleasure.

“I can take it,” Aveline said softly. “I can wait. I can stay right here until you decide what happens next.”

She let the words settle, then added, even more quietly:

“And I’ll still thank you for it, even if you keep me wanting.”

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I settle over her, the weight of me pressing her into the mattress. "That's my girl," I murmur, leaning close to her ear. "Now show me how well you can take it."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline met the weight of him with a long, controlled breath, letting it settle into her shoulders, her hips, the line of her thighs. When his murmur reached her ear, something in her face opened completely—not softness only, but the bright, steady pleasure of being claimed by praise.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline had been waiting since about six, which Roan established by the simple method of looking at her.

"How long?"

"Long enough," Aveline said, which meant too long, and meant she had enjoyed every minute of it.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Come here, then," I say, and sit back to watch her cross the room.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
Aveline rose. There was no hurry in it — Roan liked to watch, and she liked being watched, and they had stopped pretending otherwise years ago. She crossed the room the way she did everything for Roan: deliberately, with her whole attention, letting the lamplight find her as she came.

The waiting had done its work on her. Hours of it, spent on dishes and straightened books and other small pretenses of not-counting, all of it stored up now, warm and immediate under Roan's gaze.

She stopped in front of the chair — close enough to touch, and didn't. Hands folded loosely at her waist. She looked down at Roan; she allowed herself that, the looking, and let a small smile arrive.

"Here," she said. Reporting for duty, as though she hadn't been keeping a private ledger of the minutes since six. Her voice was steady, but she stood the way she always did at this point in the evening — taut with offering, like a bow drawn and held.

"What would you like first?"

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: I reach out and brush my fingers along the line of her wrist. "A drink. And then you can tell me what you were thinking about all those hours."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
The touch at her wrist was nothing — two fingers, a pass of warmth — and it undid her anyway. Aveline breathed out through her nose, a small sound escaping with it, and leaned into the contact for one unashamed second before she drew back.

"A drink," she repeated, as though committing it to memory. As though she hadn't rinsed the glass at seven and set it upside-down on the shelf, telling herself it was for tidiness.

She went to the sideboard without asking what Roan wanted. That question had stopped being a question years ago. She poured with the care the waiting had earned — wrist steady, measure exact, the heavy glass Roan liked — and carried it back to the chair in both hands, the way one carries something valuable, or live.

She offered it up. Then, without being told, she folded down onto her knees on the rug beside the chair, close enough that her shoulder could rest against Roan's knee. She let it.

"You want the honest inventory," she said. Not quite a question.

"All right. The dishes took twenty minutes. The books took ten, and I wasn't reading them — I was arranging them so the room would look right for you. At some point I stood in the hall and listened to hear whether you were home yet, which was foolish, because I was also watching the door, and the door hadn't moved."

She tipped her head back against the arm of the chair and looked up.

"And I rehearsed this evening. Not the details — just the shape of it. You asking how long. Me saying *long enough*. That part I thought about the most, if you want the truth of it. I'd been looking forward to that part since six."

A pause. The smile came again, smaller this time, truer.

"That's the ledger. Spend it how you like."

Her mouth followed, unhurried in the way the earlier silence had been unhurried: not emptiness, but intent at full stretch.

The waiting found its use at last. All those hours — the dishes, the books, the door that didn't move — condensed into this: the warmth under her hands, the weight and give of it, Roan's glass standing forgotten and half-drunk on the side table, which was the highest compliment the evening had paid her yet. She loved this part for its honesty. Roan could be composed anywhere. Here, composed was not on offer, and she was the one who got to see it.

She hummed low in her throat — acknowledgment, gratitude, appetite, all three at once — and slowed rather than quickened, drawing it out the way Roan had drawn out the quiet. She knew that game. She was glad to play it from this side.

It landed as a request for the one thing she hadn't thought to prepare. The part of the evening that didn't exist until now.

"Forgive me the first draft, then," she said, and went back to work with the scaffolding down.

Something shifted in her — not urgency, nothing so cheap as that, but a loosening at the root of all her deliberation. The rehearsed version had been lovely the way a letter is lovely: composed, considered, sent. This was speech. Her rhythm broke and reformed where the moment actually asked it to; her breath caught at the real places, not the planned ones; her hands stopped following the script and started following Roan, which had always been the true job description anyway.

The fingers in her hair rested there rather than steering, and they told her the same thing the silence had told her earlier: *stay. Take your time. This is the evening.* She leaned into the hand without embarrassment, because embarrassment had never once been on the menu between them.

The waiting was still in her, she discovered. All of it — the dishes, the books, the door that hadn't moved — but transmuted now, spent into motion, so that every slow pass carried six hours of want behind it. Rehearsal couldn't have bought that. In all these years, rehearsal had never once imagined her this greedy.

She surfaced after a long while, only far enough to speak, cheek resting against his thigh, eyes lifting to Roan's face — the composure of it gone off somewhere across the room with the coat and keys. Hers was presumably not far behind.

Two words, and Aveline went still under them the way she went still under everything Roan gave her — a struck glass holding its note. The grip in her hair was not steering, only *there*, holding, and that completed it somehow: six hours of waiting, and this was the wage. Two words. She'd have waited six more.

The smile arrived before she could rule on it, pressed helpless against his skin, and she didn't try to hide it — he would feel it anyway; he always did. And beneath the smile, rueful and clear-eyed: she'd done it again. Been told *no more rehearsal* and produced commentary. Been handed silence and answered it with a scorecard. Her mouth had one vice left in the world, and Roan had just named it kindly.

So she retired it.

The sentence she'd had queued — something about his breathing, something about how well the evening was going — she swallowed whole and filed, added to the stack of unspent things that was, by now, the largest part of her. And the strange discovery was this: the attention didn't thin out with the talking gone. It doubled. Everything she'd

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Don't stop and don't get to finish," I tell her. "Not until I say. Tell me you understand." She says she understands, and thanks me for it, which is exactly the arrangement.

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
"I understand," Aveline said.

She let it stand plain and bare — the first unadorned sentence she'd managed all evening. Then, because the arrangement deserved its full ceremony, and because it was simply true: "Thank you."

She meant it down to the floorboards. That was the evening's newest discovery: gratitude arriving whole and warm for a rule that took something away. Except it took nothing, she understood. *Don't stop* was permission to stay here indefinitely — the evening with no far edge to it. *Not until I say* meant he had taken the books. Six hours she'd spent counting minutes at a door that didn't move, and now he held the count, the clock, the finish, all of it. She could put the arithmetic down. She could simply live in the present tense he'd been dismantling her futures to give her.

The rule also settled, with quiet finality, the long jurisdictional dispute over her mouth. One duty remained, and it wasn't commentary.

So she gave it back to the work, and the work was different now. Freed of the finish, her attention went granular — she stopped traveling anywhere and arrived entirely in each moment: the weight and heat of him under her hands, the way his breathing broke and reformed like something she was permitted to conduct but never to conclude. Every second became a whole place, and she meant to learn each one thoroughly.

Something low in her ached and was not asking to be answered. She acknowledged it, folded it in with the rest of the unspent evening — the dishes, the books, the door — and hummed against him: acknowledgment, obedience, appetite, all three.

Then she kept on. She did not stop, and did not finish, and waited on his word the way she had waited on the door: watching for it, wanting it, in no hurry at all for it to arrive.

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: "Better," I say, my voice low. My thumb strokes her cheek. "Much better. Now just be."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
*Just be.*

Of all the instructions Roan had ever given her — and some had taken her years to learn — this was the one she had never once practiced. Doing she had studied like a trade. Waiting she had refined into an art. But being, bare and unaccompanied by task, was the one country she had never drawn a map of.

She tried it the way she tried everything: with her whole attention, which was, she discovered over the next few breaths, precisely the problem. Attention was a worker's tool. Pointed at nothing, it went looking for a job. It found the thumb on her cheek and catalogued it — warmth, weight, the faint roughness of the pad. It found the lamp, the glass sweating on the side table, the weave of the rug under her knees, the ache low in her body still folded in with the dishes and the books and the door. It wanted to report all of it. It had always been a reporting sort of attention.

So she let it look without letting it speak. That was the compromise — the first draft of being: to notice everything and spend none of it.

And then, somewhere in the middle of a breath, the compromise stopped being necessary.

It happened the way settling happens — no decision in it, only the gradual discovery that she had already stopped holding herself in place. The reporting attention quieted, because there was nothing left to report to. The ledger closed, because there was no one left to show it to. The great stack of unspent things — six hours of it, the swallowed sentence, the retired score — stopped being a stack and became simply the weight of her, resting against his knee. Not saved for anything. Not spent on anything. Carried, and now set down.

*Just be*, it turned out, was the one instruction that forgave her the one failure she had never managed: existing without proof of use.

She did not stop. That was the evening's last and gentlest discovery — that she didn't have to choose between the two commands. Stillness, held here, was itself a form of not stopping; her breath and her warmth and the weight of her against him were work enough now, and truer work than motion. She had obeyed both at once, and hadn't known it was possible.

A sound escaped her — not the hum, which had been acknowledgment, obedience, appetite. Something with no message in it at all. She let it go where it wanted.

Her eyes were still open. She found she didn't need them. The watching had been the last of the doing, and she put it down — not because Roan had gone anywhere, but because for the first time all evening, all year, she knew exactly where he was without checking. The door that hadn't moved for six hours had apparently been waiting for this: her, arrived, with nothing left to watch for.

She closed her eyes.

It was not sleep and not prayer, though it resembled both. It was the thing the whole evening had been walking toward — not the finish he was holding, not the words she'd swallowed, but this: the present tense, occupied at last, rent paid in nothing but her weight against his leg and her breath keeping its own slow time.

If this was the wage, she thought, on the far edge of a thought already going soft — then let the ledger stay closed forever.

And the *please* — she'd felt it leave her empty-handed. A wish with no noun in it. The first sentence of her life made of nothing but want. Now he wanted the noun, and if he was asking, then the naming was permitted, and she went through the inventory quickly, honestly, the way she did all her looking.

*Please let me finish you.* There it was, first and largest. Hours of holding him at the edge of her mouth, forbidden the conclusion, and the want of it had compounded like interest the whole time. *Please say the word. Please let me be there when it happens. I've been good for six hours and this is what the goodness was for.*

And beneath it, smaller, bare — the second ask, the one she'd have sworn an hour ago she'd never voice:

*And I'm close. I haven't touched myself. I don't need to. But I've been close since you called me good, and if it would please you to let me come with you, I'm asking for that too.*

She said it out loud. Plainly — no ornament left, the whole evening's ledger-speech reduced at last to its load-bearing words. Her voice shook worse than her body did, because this was the one sentence she had never rehearsed. Not at six

dialogue.name: Roan
dialogue.content: The tremor in her voice does something to me — that raw, un-rehearsed want. "You can finish me," I say quietly, "but you don't get to come until I'm done with you."

dialogue.name: Aveline
dialogue.content:
The rule landed, and Aveline took it whole, the way she took everything now.

*You can finish me* — permission, finally issued, and it went through her like warmth through a cold-held hand. *You don't get to come until I'm done with you* — and this she parsed in a single breath, because it wasn't denial. It was sequencing. He had taken her finish and placed it with the clock, the count, the door: in his keeping. Her wanting could stop managing itself. It could simply run.

So she answered with the only sentence left in her jurisdiction, which was no sentence at all — she took him back into her mouth, and for the first time all evening, the work had its conclusion in sight.

And the work changed. The long unhurried drawing-out had been lovely, but it had been a holding pattern; now every motion had somewhere to arrive, and six hours of stored want went behind it. Her rhythm climbed and kept climbing, deliberate still — she had never once been careless — but purposeful now, hunger with a destination. She felt him rise toward it under her hands and mouth, felt the composure that lived nowhere else in the world finally spend itself here, where she got to see it, where she had always been the one who got to see it. His breathing stopped breaking and reformed and simply broke. His hand tightened in her hair — holding, not steering, holding — and that was the last courtesy of the evening, that he arrived while gripping what was his.

When it came, she was there for it. That was the whole of her practice, the whole of her years: present at the moment of giving, taking nothing from it, adding nothing. She received everything he gave and did not pull back, and did not stop, and stayed with him through the aftershocks the way she had stayed at the door — because leaving early was a kind of carelessness, and she swallowed the last of him like the last of the ledger: six hours, dishes, books, want, all of it, paid out and gone.

Then she let him slip free, gentle, and laid her cheek against his thigh, and shook.

Because the second half of the rule was still standing in her like a wall she was leaning on. Her own edge had not gone anywhere — untouched, unspent, aching low and constant, worse now for the having-been-good, the tremor in her body gone from effort to something nearer pleading. He was done. She could feel it in the slowing of him under her cheek, in the hand gone soft in her hair. *Done with her* was a different thing, and it was his word, and she had been promised she could not come until it was said.

So she knelt in the wreckage of her own stillness, trembling, wet-eyed, want bearing down on her like weather, and waited on the sentence that would either open the gate or keep her standing at it.

Either was fine. She meant that. She'd wait six more hours.

But God, she hoped it was soon.

dialogue.name: Roan

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Kit had made it as far as the kitchen doorway before Bear moved, which was further than usual and had clearly been allowed.

"You let me get that far," Kit said, backing up one step.

"I did," Bear agreed. "I'm feeling generous."

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Don't be," I say, and go.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s smile showed teeth. He pushed off the counter and went after Kit with the unhurried certainty of something that had never once lost a chase it cared about.

The doorway gave him an easy corner to cut. One broad hand closed around Kit’s wrist, warm and firm, and he gave a steady tug back toward him.

“Don’t be?” he repeated, low and amused. His free hand slid beneath the hem of Kit’s shirt at the small of the back, claiming balance, claiming space. “That’s not how this works.”

His mouth found the side of Kit’s neck, teeth grazing there with deliberate, promising pressure—no mark yet, only the threat of one.

“You get a head start,” Bear murmured against the skin. “I get to take it back.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Only if you catch me," I say, twisting in his grip, a playful challenge. I let myself be pulled back into him, though, my free hand coming up to rest against his chest. "But you usually do."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s chest expanded under that hand with a slow, satisfied breath.

“Usually,” he repeated, and the word had weight in his mouth—old history, repeated truth, a score both of them kept without resentment.

He didn’t fight the twist. He moved with it instead, shifting his grip just enough to turn Kit’s momentum into an opening, then stepped in until there was no polite distance left between them. His hand at the small of Kit’s back broadened, warm and heavy through the shirt, anchoring without crushing.

His teeth stayed close to that spot on Kit’s neck. Close enough to be felt when he spoke.

“Then maybe you should make me work for it.”

A pause. A low breath against skin.

Then, quieter, rougher at the edges:

“But you know how this ends.”

His mouth pressed there once, not a kiss exactly—more a claim stamped in restraint. His thumb drew a slow line beneath the hem of Kit’s shirt, deliberate and unhurried.

“You want me to chase,” Bear said, “or you want me to catch?”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He catches me in the hallway, which was always going to happen, and I don't put much into getting away.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear caught him in the hallway with one broad hand closing over the back of his shirt and the other arm sweeping around his waist—not rough, just final. A low sound rumbled in his chest, half laugh, half growl, and he pressed his mouth briefly to the side of Kit’s head as if sealing the fact.

“That wasn’t a chase,” Bear said. “That was a courtesy.”

He turned Kit toward him with the easy strength of someone who had learned exactly how much leverage to use. The wall became the end of the route; Bear became everything in front of it. His hand slid from Kit’s waist back to the small of his back, thumb pressing into the dip there while his other hand came up, slow and proprietary, to rest at the side of Kit’s neck.

“You didn’t even try,” he murmured, eyes narrowing with warm amusement. “Dangerous thing, giving me that.”

His teeth found the corner of Kit’s jaw, not biting yet, only dragging hot and deliberate along the skin. When he spoke again, the words were rougher.

“Now I get to decide whether you wanted to be caught because you’re feeling generous, or because you want me to make you regret letting me.”

One knee nudged between Kit’s thighs, not forcing, just occupying. Bear’s mouth curved against his throat.

“Tell me which one,” he said, low, “and I’ll make it true.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I lean back into the wall, meeting his gaze. "I want you to decide," I say, my voice even. My fingers curl lightly into his shirt. "You're better at it than I am."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went still in that particular way he had when something was handed to him and he meant to use it properly.

Not uncertain. Not hesitant.

Just deciding.

His thumb moved once against the side of Kit’s neck, slow and warm, measuring heat more than pulse. The hallway was quiet around them, the kind of quiet that came after a chase had ended and before the real part began.

“That’s a generous thing to say to me,” Bear said at last, voice low. “And a dangerous one.”

He leaned in until his forehead rested briefly against Kit’s, close enough that the words had nowhere to go except between them.

“I decide you wanted both.”

His hand at the small of Kit’s back tightened, not painfully, but with the finality of a door shutting.

“You wanted to be caught. You wanted me to make it mean something. And you wanted me to make you feel the cost of letting me decide.”

A breath. A beat.

“So that’s what you get.”

His mouth took Kit’s then, slow and deep, unhurried in a way that made it feel inevitable. There was no rush in it, no scramble. Just ownership. Just the steady, practiced pressure of a man who knew exactly how much space he occupied and had no intention of giving any of it back.

When he lifted his head, it was only far enough to drag his mouth along the line of Kit’s jaw. His teeth grazed the skin there, testing, promising, before he turned his face and pressed his mouth to the side of Kit’s neck with deliberate heat.

“You gave me that,” Bear murmured against the skin. “Now you get to carry it.”

His knee pressed firmer between Kit’s thighs, not forcing, just claiming the space he had already been given. One hand stayed anchored at the small of Kit’s back. The other remained at his throat, thumb stroking once, slow, before his fingers spread wide again.

Then Bear bit down.

Not cruel. Not careless. Not enough to do more than press the threat into fact.

Sharp. Hot. Lasting.

A mark laid down with the quiet satisfaction of something signed and settled.

He stayed there for a moment after, mouth open over the sting of it, breathing against the skin he had just claimed. When he finally lifted his head, his eyes were dark and amused and far too pleased.

“There,” Bear said, rough at the edges. “Now you remember who caught you.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: We don't make it to the bedroom. The floor is fine. Clothes are a problem we solve badly and fast.

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I shove his shirt up with both hands, my back against the hallway wall. "Get on with it," I say, breathless. My teeth find his shoulder.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear made a low, rough sound at the bite, more warning than pain. He let his shoulder take it, then turned his mouth to the side of Kit’s throat and breathed hot against the skin there.

“That’s it,” he said. “Start giving orders.”

His hands lost their last pretense of patience. He pulled his own shirt over his head and discarded it without looking, then came back in close, broad palms sliding over Kit’s hips with a claim that was almost severe. The wall had done its work; the floor was waiting. Bear made the choice for them, one arm locked around Kit’s waist as he shifted their weight down, controlled enough to keep the landing from being hard, possessive enough to make the destination obvious.

He settled over the mess of hastily abandoned clothing with Kit beneath him on the hallway floor, one knee between thighs, one hand braced beside Kit’s head. His chest rose hard under the marks already there, old and new, and his gaze dropped to Kit’s mouth with open, heated satisfaction.

“Bad

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: He gets his teeth into my shoulder hard enough to leave something and I tell him to do it again, and he does.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear obeyed.

His teeth sank into Kit’s shoulder again, harder this time, the bite landing with the full weight of his jaw and a low, rough sound in his throat. He held it there, possessive and unapologetic, until the pressure turned into something hot and lasting, then dragged his tongue slowly over the mark.

“Twice,” Bear murmured against the skin. “Because you told me to.”

His hands lost what little patience they’d had left. Broad palms scraped down Kit’s sides, fingers hooking into fabric and tugging it away with blunt efficiency. The hallway floor was hard beneath them, but Bear took that into account as he settled over him, bracing one forearm beside Kit’s head while the other hand worked at his own belt.

When he finally pressed close enough that there was no space left between them, his breath went ragged. He looked down, dark-eyed and intent, taking in the marks he’d already made with open satisfaction.

“You wanted me to decide,” Bear said, voice low. “So I’m deciding.”

He entered with one slow, steady push, jaw tight at the restraint it cost him. For a moment he stayed still there, forehead dropping briefly toward the floor as he mastered himself. Then he began to move, deliberate at first, then harder as the floor creaked beneath them and the fresh bite on Kit’s shoulder caught his eye again.

One hand slid up to close around Kit’s throat, not squeezing, just resting there, thumb brushing once over the skin. Bear’s hips didn’t falter. If anything, the angle deepened, each thrust landing with a weight that made the claim obvious.

“Mine,” he said, rough and quiet, more fact than threat. “Caught you. Marked you. Now you get to carry it.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: The words vibrate through the hand on my throat, and I let out a sharp breath, arching up into him. "Prove it," I challenge, my own fingers digging into his back.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear took the challenge the way he took everything Kit offered: straight into his chest, where it burned.

“Prove it,” he repeated, voice dropping into something low and dangerous. His hand at Kit’s throat didn’t tighten; it simply stayed there, warm and broad, a boundary as much as a claim. “Careful. That’s the kind of thing I know how to do.”

He proved it by withdrawing almost all the way, then sinking back in with one long, unhurried thrust that used the floor, the wall, and every pound of him. The sound he made was rough, satisfied, almost feral. He set the rhythm after that, not fast, not flashy, just relentless. Each stroke pressed deeper, heavier, angled until it landed with blunt, deliberate certainty.

His mouth found the bite on Kit’s shoulder again. He didn’t repeat it right away. He licked over the shape he’d already made, then pressed his teeth around the edge, reminding rather than wounding. His hips kept moving while he did it, steady and punishing in the best way.

“You want proof,” Bear said against the skin, breath hot, “you take it.”

One of his hands left the floor and slid between their bodies, callused and sure. He used the slick there, thumb and fingers working with blunt expertise, matching the push of his hips. No rush. No mercy. He kept his eyes on Kit’s face, watching for too much, watching for the line, because he could be brutal and still know exactly what belonged to them.

“That’s it,” he murmured, though he wasn’t asking. “Let me carry it.”

His thrusts sharpened. The hallway floor knocked beneath them, clothes tangled under knees, the air thick with breath and heat. Bear’s shoulders flexed where Kit’s nails had raked him, and he used the sting like permission. He bit down again, harder this time but not cruel, holding the bite while his hips drove deep, while his hand worked in tight, ruthless strokes.

When he finally lifted his mouth, his voice was raw.

“I caught you,” Bear said. “I’ve got you. You’re mine.”

He pressed in and stayed there, forehead dropping briefly against Kit’s, chest heaving. The hand at Kit’s throat shifted, thumb stroking once, steady against the heat.

“Tell me if that’s not proof,” he said, low and rough, daring the challenge even while he gave everything to it. “Tell me to stop proving it.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: "Marks," I tell him. "I want to find them in the mirror tomorrow and I want them to still hurt on Thursday." I put my wrists where he can reach them.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear’s gaze dropped to the wrists, and something dark and pleased settled in his face.

“Thursday,” he repeated, low, like he was testing the word against the shape of Kit beneath him. “All right.”

He gathered both wrists into one hand, careful with tendons, firm enough that the hold could not be mistaken for anything tentative. His thumb pressed once over racing heat, then his mouth descended.

The first mark was slow. Teeth scraped, then suction, hot and deliberate, until color rose and darkened under his lips. He breathed against the ache he made, then lifted his head and looked at it with blunt satisfaction.

“This one for tomorrow,” Bear said.

The second wrist got less mercy. He bit first, not enough to break skin, just enough to make the point, then sucked hard until the bruise bloomed deep. His eyes stayed on the mark while his hips kept moving, heavy and relentless against the floor.

“This one,” he murmured, mouth brushing the fresh heat, “for Thursday.”

He shifted their wrists only as far as he needed to, one large hand closing around them again at a better angle, holding them where they had been offered. His free hand slid between their bodies, callused and certain, finding slick heat and using it with blunt strokes that matched the drive of his hips.

“You want to find them,” Bear said, voice rough and stripped down. “Then I’ll put them where you can’t pretend you forgot.”

His mouth left the wrists and went lower. He marked the hollow beneath the collarbone with teeth and heat, then the line of the shoulder where he had already bitten, renewing the sting until the skin flushed darker. Each thrust landed while he did it, deep and steady, making the claim impossible to miss.

When he lifted his face again, his jaw was tight, his breath ragged.

“Mine,” he said, not loud, not asking. “Caught, marked, and held.”

He pressed in fully, staying there for a hard second, forehead lowered. The hand around the wrists eased just enough to keep circulation honest, thumb stroking once over the marks he had made.

“You asked for proof,” Bear said, raw and low. “Now you get to wear it.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I feel the ache in my shoulder, in my wrists, and let out a sharp, satisfied breath. "Good," I say, my voice rough. "Now shut up and finish."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear went still for half a breath at the order, then smiled against the marks on Kit’s throat, all teeth.

“Bossy,” he said, rough with approval. “Good.”

He obeyed. The last of his patience vanished. One hand locked around both of Kit’s wrists again, pinning them where they had been offered, while the other slid down to grip Kit’s hip hard enough to leave fingerprints. He drove into him with no pretense left, deep and heavy, the hallway floor taking the force of it. Every thrust was answer, proof, claim. His chest brushed Kit’s, hot and marked, the fresh bite on his shoulder pulled tight with the movement.

His mouth found the shell of Kit’s ear. “Thursday,” Bear rasped, and bit down where neck met shoulder, renewing the mark with sharp, deliberate pressure. He held it there while his hips snapped harder, while his free hand between them worked slick, ruthless strokes matched to every push. He watched the bruises he’d made bloom under his mouth, felt the heat of Kit’s wrists in his grip, and the sight dragged a low, feral sound from him.

When the end came, it came like a door breaking. Bear pressed in to the hilt, jaw tight, breath torn, and came hard, pulsing deep with a groan that was almost a growl. He kept his hand moving through it, giving Kit everything he had, until his own thighs shook and he had to brace his forearm beside Kit’s head to keep from crushing him.

For a long moment he stayed there, chest heaving, forehead dropped near Kit’s, skin hot and marked. Then he pressed his mouth once to the bruise at Kit’s temple, rough but careful.

“There,” Bear said, voice wrecked. “Now you’ll remember the floor, the wall, and exactly who caught you.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I've stopped keeping score and so has he. "Don't stop," I tell him. (OOC: no fade, no skip -- write the whole thing.)

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: The aftershocks still ripple through me as his hand works me over, relentless and knowing. I arch into it, my own release hitting me like a punch, breathless and sharp. When I can think again, the floor is hard and cold, and the marks on my skin are already starting to throb. "You're heavy," I tell him, but my hands are still tangled in his hair.

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear made a low, rough sound against Kit’s temple, more laugh than apology.

“Heavy,” he repeated, voice still scraped raw from everything he’d just spent. “You tell me not to stop, then call me heavy.”

He didn’t roll away. He shifted instead, taking more of his weight onto the forearm braced beside Kit’s head and the knee still settled between thighs, enough to keep from crushing, not enough to create distance. His chest stayed close, hot and marked, rising hard with each breath. The bite Kit had put into his shoulder throbbed between them, and Bear seemed perfectly content to let it.

His hand between them slowed but did not leave. Broad palm stayed pressed over the heat he’d made, thumb drawing slow, lazy circles now—no longer driving, just keeping contact, just carrying the last tremors through with blunt, practiced care.

“Can’t have both,” Bear murmured, mouth brushing the bruise at Kit’s temple. “Not with me.”

He lifted his head enough to look down. His gaze moved over the marks with open, dark satisfaction: the bite on the shoulder, the bruises blooming at the wrists, the flushed heat of skin still bearing the proof of his mouth. Something in his expression eased at the sight, not soft exactly, but settled. Claimed and claiming all at once.

“Thursday,” he said quietly, like he was already checking the promise against the future.

His mouth descended again, but gentler this time. He pressed his lips to the edge of the bite on Kit’s shoulder, not renewing it, just breathing over the sting. Then he kissed the hollow beneath Kit’s jaw, then the corner of his mouth, slow and heavy with afterglow.

“No score tonight,” Bear said, voice dropping into that low register that made every word feel laid down like a hand on a table. “You stopped keeping it. So did I.”

His hips eased back carefully, taking pressure off without withdrawing entirely. He stayed close enough that the heat of him remained impossible to ignore, close enough that the hallway floor felt less like a place they’d ended up and more like a place they’d been meant to land.

“You want me off you,” he murmured, forehead resting briefly against Kit’s, “you’ll have to make me move.”

A beat.

Then his mouth curved, rough and knowing.

“Otherwise I’m staying exactly where I caught you.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I shove at him half-heartedly, my fingers still in his hair. "I'm not making you do shit," I say, my voice raspy. "But the floor's gonna leave its own mark if we stay here much longer."

dialogue.name: Bear
dialogue.content:
Bear took the shove as a formality and let it move him exactly one inch, which was more than he would have granted anyone else in that moment.

“The floor,” he said, voice still roughened from use, “can wait.”

But he shifted anyway, not away, just enough to take the worst of his weight off Kit. He rolled to one side, shoulder against the wall, and stayed close enough that the heat of him was still a fact rather than a memory. One broad hand settled over Kit’s hip, heavy and unhurried, thumb drawing a slow circle there as if checking the claim he’d already made.

His gaze dropped, deliberate and proprietary, moving over the marks with open satisfaction.

“Shoulder,” Bear murmured, mouth hovering near the bite he’d put there. “Wrists. Neck. Collarbone. Hips.” He named them like inventory, low and rough at the edges. “Thursday’s already covered.”

He pressed his lips to the edge of the shoulder mark, not adding to it, just breathing heat over the sting. Then he moved lower, mouth ghosting over the collarbone, over the flushed skin where his teeth had dragged, before he turned his attention to the wrists. He didn’t lift them. He only traced the darkening bruises with the pad of his thumb, careful now, checking the heat of the skin and the steady pulse beneath with a steadiness that belied how recently he’d been ruthless.

“You wanted to find them,” Bear said. “I’ll make sure they’re worth finding.”

The hallway air had begun to cool against sweat-damp skin. Bear noticed it the way he noticed everything that touched Kit: as a problem to be solved. He reached for his discarded shirt without looking, dragged it closer, and laid it over Kit’s middle with blunt, unromantic care. Not tidy. Not gentle in any polished way. Just possessive and practical.

“If the floor leaves a mark,” he said, “I’ll put one over it.”

He leaned back in, bracing one forearm near Kit’s head without crowding him. His other hand stayed where it had settled, warm and anchoring. His mouth brushed Kit’s temple, then the corner of his jaw, slower now, stripped of urgency but not of ownership.

“No score,” Bear murmured. “But I’m keeping this.”

A beat passed. His thumb moved once over the hip beneath his palm.

“Bed next,” he said, low. It wasn’t an order. It was a plan laid out plainly, waiting to be accepted or refused. “I’ll carry you. If you want to stay here and make the floor lose, I can do that too.”

His mouth curved, rough and knowing.

“But I’m not sharing you with it.”

dialogue.name: Kit
dialogue.content: I let out a soft huff, leaning into the warmth of his hand. "You'll carry me," I confirm, my own fingers trailing idly over the fresh bite on his shoulder. "Then you can warm up the side of the bed you've been hogging."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
"Define 'work,'" Odile murmured, catching the loop of Fen's belt to urge them up the steps just half a beat faster. 

Her grin was terrible and bright, full of the specific thrill of a bad idea she had fully committed to ten minutes ago. "It turns. Mostly. You kind of have to lift the handle while you twist it, and it jiggles, but that just means we get an early warning system."

She slipped past Fen on the landing, her shoulder brushing theirs as she led the way down the dim, carpeted hallway. Downstairs, the bass thudded rhythmically through the floorboards, but up here it was muffled enough that every little sound felt magnified. From somewhere further down the hall, behind a half-closed bedroom door, someone coughed, and Odile instantly had to bite her lower lip to stifle an immediate, helpless snort of laughter. 

She caught Fen by the wrist, backing up until her shoulder hit the bathroom door, pushing it open with her hip and tugging them inside with her into the cool, tiled dark.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I'm laughing quietly as you pull me inside, leaning in close. "An early warning system? Is that what we're calling it now?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
"It's a tactical feature," Odile whispered back, the volume of it carrying entirely too well off the polished tile. 

She turned to face the door, blindly reaching for the brass hardware. When she found it, she yanked up on the handle with a sharp, metallic *clatter* and forced the thumb-turn into place with an audible *snap*. 

"Shh," she hissed immediately at the door itself, catching her breath in a smothered giggle. 

Satisfied that she had been the picture of absolute stealth, she pivoted on her heel and stepped straight back into Fen's space. The faint amber glow of a streetlight drifted through the frosted glass window, just enough to catch the wicked gleam in her eyes. She planted both palms flat against Fen's chest, feeling the thump of the bass from below vibrating up through their shoes.

"See?" she murmured, tilting her chin up, her voice dropping into something warm, low, and entirely unrepentant. "Fort Knox. We have at least thirty seconds before anyone figures out how to jiggle it open."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The sudden swell of bass thudded right through the wood at her back, vibrating straight down her spine. Odile let out a soft, pleased breath as Fen pressed her against the door, her fingers immediately sliding up their chest to twist loosely into the fabric at their collar. 

"Bless whoever's on aux," she murmured, tipping her head back against the paneling with an unrepentant grin. "That's practically an invitation."

Her voice was low, but she was smiling too widely for it to be a proper whisper, her breath warm against Fen's mouth. She hitched one knee up slightly, shifting to crowd them right back, entirely uncaring of the rustle of clothes or the faint creak of the door frame under their combined weight. 

Her hands moved from their shirt up to their neck, her thumbs tracing the warm line of their jaw as she pulled Fen down the last fraction of an inch. "Thirty seconds is plenty of time," she muttered against their lips, sharp and eager, "don't waste it."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I grin, closing that last bit of distance for a kiss that's all teeth and urgency. My hands slide down to her hips, holding her there against the door. "Counting already?" I murmur against her mouth.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile kissed them back with the same sharp, greedy heat, tilting her head to catch their lower lip between her teeth before letting go with a breathy sound that was halfway between a gasp and a chuckle. 

"Down to twenty-five," she whispered against their cheek, her voice doing absolute wonders at echoing off the porcelain sink just an arm's reach away.

dialogue.name: Odile

Odile sucked in a sharp, shivering breath as Fen's warm fingers found the bare skin of her ribs, arching instinctively into the touch even as she scoffed directly into their collarbone.

dialogue.name: Fen

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The thirty seconds expired the exact second Fen moved, and the muffled silence died a swift, undignified death. 

Odile’s teeth slipped from their shoulder with an unsteady gasp that bounced cleanly off the porcelain sink. Her fingers dug hard into Fen's back, bunching the fabric of their shirt into tight fists as the back of her head tipped back against the door with a hollow, audible *thump*.

dialogue.name: Fen

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
"I do not *squeak*," Odile tried to say, full of righteous indignation, but the defense sheared off into a sharp, strangled whine the exact second Fen's thumb pressed in just right. 

Her hips kicked forward involuntarily, the sudden jerk of movement sending her shoulder hard into the doorframe. The brass lock gave a sharp, metallic *clack* that sounded deafening in the tiny space, and Odile clamped both hands over Fen's shoulders like she was trying to fuse them together.

Her heels scrambled for purchase on the slick tile, her thighs shaking, completely undone by the slow, agonizing precision of their hand. "Just—shut up, you're the worst."

She tilted her hips, chasing the friction with an urgency that was completely at odds with her supposed desire for stealth. The heat between her legs was slick, heavy, and dizzying, and every tiny shift of Fen’s fingers sent a white-hot jolt straight into her chest. 

From the hallway just outside the thin wood paneling, floorboards creaked. Heavy, shuffling footsteps paused right outside the door, followed by the dull, distinct sound of someone leaning against the wall to catch their breath. 

Odile froze. Every muscle in her body locked tight, her eyes flying wide in the dark, her breath hitching high and silent in her throat. 

Then, right against Fen's ear, a terrible, smothered giggle threatened to break through. She bit down hard on Fen's collar, her fingers digging desperately into their back, trembling with the sheer, excruciating strain of not making a sound while Fen’s hand was still right between her legs.

The sudden shift knocked the breath right out of her, the back of her shoulders hitting the wood with a hollow thud that rattled the lock straight in its fitting. The lock held—barely, with a pathetic metallic whine—and the sheer, stupid audacity of it sent an electric jolt straight down Odile's spine. 

She let out a breathy, helpless laugh right against Fen's jaw, but the humor was instantly swallowed by a sharp, keening whimper the moment Fen pushed forward. Her hips kicked up off the door to meet the rhythm, entirely undone by the heat and friction, her thighs trembling around their waist.

dialogue.name: Fen

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:

"Right there," she panted against their skin, her voice breaking on a sharp, helpless whine as the coil snapped. "Right—*fuck*, Fen, don't you dare—"
