dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
The ambush had gone the way ambushes go when they work: fast, and then over, and then very quiet. Wrack was crouched by the ditch cleaning her knife on a dead man's cloak, which was the only clean cloth within reach.

"Six," she said, without looking up. "Count again if you want, but it's six." She tested the edge against her thumb. "One of them's still making noise, off past the cart. You'll want to decide what you're doing about that before it gets dark."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I wipe my face with the back of my wrist and it comes away wet. Not mine, I think. "I heard him," I say. I don't move toward the cart.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
She glanced at Corvin, noting the blood on his face, and went back to cleaning her blade. "Heard him, yes. And?" She didn't bother to look up, her voice flat. "I'm asking what you're planning to do about it. We can't leave him to raise the alarm, and we can't leave him alive. Those are the choices, and time's wasting."

She stood, stretching her back with a grunt, and walked past Corvin toward the cart. "You coming, or you going to wait for me to sort it out?" Her tone was matter-of-fact, as if discussing the weather, not the cold-blooded murder of a wounded man.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I follow her, but my steps feel heavy. "I'll handle it." My voice sounds steadier than I feel. The groans from behind the cart are getting louder, more desperate.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
She stopped and turned to face Corvin, her expression unreadable. "Handle it how, exactly? You planning to kill him, or are we taking him back with us as a souvenir?" Her tone was sharp, impatient. "Because either way, you need to make up your mind and get it done. We're exposed out here, and the longer we stand around yapping, the more likely it is someone else will show up to join the party."

She stepped closer, her voice dropping to a low growl. "Listen, I don't much care how you do it, but it needs to be done. And if you can't stomach it, then step aside and let someone who can take care of business. We're in the middle of a goddamn war, and there's no room for sentimentality out here. You understand me?"

Her gaze was hard, challenging, as if daring him to argue. She waited, her hand resting on the hilt of her sword, ready to step in if Corvin couldn't bring himself to act.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "How bad is he?" I ask, and then, because she'll say it anyway: "Bad enough that it's a mercy, or bad enough that it's just easier?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
She let out a short, humorless laugh. "Bad enough that he's screaming like a pig at a slaughter, if that's any indication." Her voice was flat, clinical. "I didn't get a good look, but from the sounds of it, he's not long for this world anyway. Might as well put him out of his misery and be done with it."

She stepped back, giving Corvin some space. "But hey, if you're more comfortable letting him suffer, be my guest. Just don't expect me to do it for you when he starts begging for his mama."

Her tone was matter-of-fact, as if discussing the weather rather than the cold-blooded murder of a wounded man. "Look, kid, I get it. It's not an easy thing, taking a life. But out here, it's kill or be killed. You need to make peace with that, and fast, if you want to survive."

She paused, her gaze hard and unyielding. "So, what's it going to be? You going to put him down, or am I going to have to do it for you? Because either way, it needs to be done, and we don't have all day to dick around about it."

Her hand was still on her sword, her posture tense and ready, as if anticipating Corvin's next move. She waited, her expression unreadable, for him to make a decision.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I walk around the cart before I can think about it anymore. The man's pinned under a broken wheel, one leg bent wrong. My throat tightens. "Hey," I say, my voice rough. He just keeps groaning.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack watched as Corvin approached the wounded man, her expression neutral. She had seen this hesitation before, in countless new recruits. The moment when they realized that the romanticized notions of war they had held were nothing like the grim reality.

She didn't move to intervene, letting Corvin take the lead. This was a necessary step in the brutal education that was survival on the battlefield. You either learned to do what needed to be done, or you didn't make it long.

The man's groans were getting louder, more desperate. Wrack could see the fear in Corvin's eyes, the way his hand trembled as he drew his knife. She said nothing, letting the silence stretch out, letting the gravity of the situation sink in.

"You need to do it quickly," she said finally, her voice low and steady. "The longer you wait, the harder it will be. And for him, too."

She took a step back, giving Corvin some space, but not taking her eyes off the scene. This was a test, and she was watching to see how he would perform.

"Remember," she added, her tone matter-of-fact, "it's not about you, or him. It's about the mission, and making sure we both walk away from this alive."

Her hand was still on her sword, ready to step in if Corvin faltered. But she had a feeling he would see it through. Most of them did, in the end. The ones that didn't, well, they didn't last long in this line of work.

She waited, her gaze hard and unyielding, watching Corvin make his choice.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I make myself walk over and look at him. "Tell me what I'm looking at," I say to her, because she's seen this before and I haven't, not this close.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack stepped closer, her gaze flicking between Corvin and the wounded man. "What you're looking at is a mess," she said bluntly. "His leg's busted bad, likely shattered in a few places. He's bleeding out from a gash in his side, and if you look close, you can see the fletching of an arrow poking out from under his ribcage."

She crouched down beside the man, her movements efficient and matter-of-fact. "He's not going to make it, kid. Not without a healer, and not even then. He's in a lot of pain, and he's terrified. You can see it in his eyes."

The man let out a moan, his body twitching in agony. Wrack watched him impassively, as if studying a curious insect.

"Look, I know it's not an easy thing to do," she said, her tone softening slightly. "But it's the kindest thing you can do for him. Put him out of his misery, before it gets worse."

She stood up, brushing off her knees. "I'll leave you to it. But don't take too long. We need to get moving, and fast. The longer we stay in one place, the more likely it is that we'll attract unwanted attention."

She started to walk away, then paused and looked back at Corvin. "And kid? Don't think too hard about it. It's just business. The sooner you learn that, the easier this will all be."

With that, she turned and walked back toward the main road, leaving Corvin alone with the wounded man and the grim task ahead of him.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I kneel down, the wet dirt soaking through my trousers. His eyes find mine, wide and pleading. My hand doesn't shake when I bring the knife up this time. "Sorry," I mutter, and then I do it fast, before I can hear what I'm saying.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack heard the final gasp, the sudden silence that followed. She didn't turn around, didn't look back. She had seen it too many times to let it affect her anymore.

She waited a few moments, giving Corvin a chance to collect himself, then called out, "Done?"

There was no judgment in her voice, no pity. Just a straightforward question, a simple acknowledgment of the task that had been completed.

"You did what needed to be done," she said, still not turning around. "That's all there is to it. Don't overthink it, don't let it eat at you. It's just another part of the job, the same as anything else."

She started walking back towards the road, her steps measured and purposeful. "We need to move, and fast. We're exposed out here, and every second we waste is another chance for someone to find us."

She paused, looking back at Corvin over her shoulder. "Get yourself together, kid. We've got a long road ahead of us, and it's only going to get harder from here on out. You need to be ready for it."

Her expression was hard, unyielding, but there was a glimmer of something else in her eyes. Respect, maybe. A grudging acknowledgment that Corvin had proven himself capable of doing what was necessary, even when it was unpleasant.

"Come on," she said, turning back towards the road. "Let's get out of here before we attract any more unwanted attention. And next time, try not to be so squeamish. It'll make things a hell of a lot easier for everyone involved."

She didn't wait for a response, just started walking, her boots crunching on the dirt as she went. It was time to move, to keep going, to survive another day in this endless, senseless war.

And Corvin would have to decide whether he was ready to do whatever it took to make it through to the other side.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "Don't clean it up for me," I say. "If I'm going to do this I want to know exactly what a spear does to a man's gut. Tell me straight."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack glanced back at Corvin, a flicker of something passing across her face. Respect, maybe. Or perhaps it was just a grim acknowledgment of the harsh realities of their world.

"You want to know what a spear does to a man's gut?" She shrugged, her tone flat and matter-of-fact. "It's messy, kid. Real fucking messy."

She walked over to one of the bodies, kneeling down beside it. With a swift, practiced motion, she flipped the corpse over, exposing a jagged wound that split the man's abdomen open from navel to sternum.

"See here?" She pointed at the wound, her voice clinical and detached. "The spear tip went in clean, but then it must have twisted or hit bone. Tore everything up inside. Guts, organs, the works."

She prodded at the wound with a gloved finger, her face impassive. "He probably bled out pretty quick, but not before he had a few minutes of pure, unadulterated agony. The kind of pain that makes you wish you were never born."

She stood up, brushing off her knees. "And that's just one way it can go. Spears can hit in a hundred different ways, each one as nasty as the last. Puncture a lung, sever an artery, burst a liver. Trust me, kid, you don't want to know the details."

She looked at Corvin, her gaze hard and unyielding. "But if you're going to do this, you need to know what you're dealing with. You need to understand that this is the reality of it, the cold, hard truth. And you need to be ready to face it, again and again, for as long as you're in this game."

She turned to walk away, then paused, looking back at Corvin over her shoulder. "So, what's it going to be, kid? You ready to see this through, no matter what it costs you? Or are you going to run back home and hide under your mama's skirts?"

Her tone was challenging, almost mocking. But there was an undercurrent of something else, something harder to define. A sense that she was testing him, pushing him to see what he was made of.

"Choose now," she said, her voice flat and unyielding. "Because once we start moving, there's no going back. And I won't have some green recruit holding us up because they can't stomach a little blood and guts."

She waited, her gaze fixed on Corvin, waiting to see what he would do, how he would respond to the brutal challenge she had thrown down before him.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I look at the wound, my stomach turning. "I didn't ask for it to be pretty. I just wanted to know." I wipe my knife on the dead man's tunic and stand up. My hands are steady. "I'm not hiding anywhere. Let's go."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack nodded once, a flicker of approval in her eyes. "Good," she said, her tone brisk and businesslike. "That's the spirit. Now, let's get the hell out of here before we draw any more unwanted attention."

She turned and started walking, her steps quick and purposeful. Corvin followed, his movements a bit more hesitant, but determined. The road ahead was long and uncertain, but for now, they were moving, putting distance between themselves and the grim scene they had left behind.

As they walked, Wrack fell into a steady rhythm, her mind already shifting to the tasks ahead. "We've got a couple of options for where to go from here," she said, her voice low and focused. "There's a farmhouse about a mile up the road that we can use as a base for the night. Or, if you're feeling brave, we can try to slip into the city and see if we can find some information."

She glanced at Corvin, gauging his reaction. "Either way, it's going to be dangerous. But that's the nature of the game we're playing. You ready for it, kid? Ready to see this through to the end, no matter what it takes?"

Her tone was challenging, almost mocking. But there was an undercurrent of something else, something harder to define. A sense that she was testing him, pushing him to see what he was made of.

"Because once we start moving, there's no going back. And I won't have some green recruit holding us up because they can't stomach a little blood and guts."

She waited, her gaze fixed on Corvin, waiting to see what he would do, how he would respond to the brutal challenge she had thrown down before him.

"Choose now," she said, her voice flat and unyielding. "Because once we make our move, it's game time. And I need to know that I can count on you, no matter what."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I kneel down and do it, and it isn't clean or quick because I've never done it before. "Stay," I tell her, when she starts to turn away. "Watch it with me and tell me exactly what I'm doing to him — the sound of it, how long he takes, all of it. Don't leave anything out."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack paused, her hand already on the hilt of her sword. She turned back to Corvin, a flicker of something passing across her face. Surprise, maybe. Or perhaps it was a grudging respect for the young man's determination to see this through, no matter the cost.

"You sure about this, kid?" she asked, her voice low and serious. "Because once we start, there's no going back. And it ain't pretty, what we're about to do."

She crouched down beside Corvin, her gaze fixed on the wounded man. He was still alive, barely, his breathing shallow and ragged. A low moan escaped his lips, a sound of pure, unadulterated agony.

"Alright," Wrack said, her tone flat and matter-of-fact. "Let's do this. And remember, kid, it's just business. Don't think too hard about it, don't let it get to you. It's the only way you'll survive out here."

She watched as Corvin positioned himself, his movements hesitant but determined. The wounded man let out another moan, his body twitching in pain.

"Good," Wrack said, nodding her approval. "Now, you want to know exactly what's happening, right? So, pay attention."

She leaned in close, her voice low and focused. "See how his eyes are glazed over? That's the shock setting in. His body's trying to shut down, trying to protect itself from the pain. But it won't last long. The agony's going to come crashing back in, and it's going to be like nothing you've ever felt before."

The man's breathing was getting shallower, more labored. Wrack kept talking, her tone clinical and detached.

"Listen to that gurgling sound. That's blood in his lungs, kid. He's drowning in his own fluids, slowly and painfully. And the longer we wait, the worse it's going to get for him. So, if you're going to do this, do it now, before the pain gets unbearable."

She watched as Corvin hesitated, his hand trembling slightly. She reached out and grabbed his wrist, her grip firm and unyielding.

"Don't think," she said, her voice a low growl. "Just do. It's the only way you'll survive this, kid. And once you start, don't stop. Make it quick, make it clean, and don't look back. Because if you do, you'll never forget the sound of that man's last breath, the way his body goes limp in your hands. Trust me, I know."

She released Corvin's wrist, stepping back to give him some space. "So, what's it going to be, kid? Are you going to do what needs to be done, or are you going to run away and hide, like some terrified little boy?"

Her gaze was hard and unyielding, a challenge in her eyes. She was testing him, pushing him to see what he was made of. And she was watching, waiting to see how he would respond to the brutal challenge she had thrown down before him.

"Choose now," she said, her voice flat and unyielding. "Because once you start, there's no going back. And I need to know that I can count on you, no matter what."

dialogue.name: Corvin

dialogue.name: Corvin

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
The ambush had gone the way ambushes go when they work: fast, and then over, and then very quiet. Wrack was crouched by the ditch cleaning her knife on a dead man's cloak, which was the only clean cloth within reach.

"Six," she said, without looking up. "Count again if you want, but it's six." She tested the edge against her thumb. "One of them's still making noise, off past the cart. You'll want to decide what you're doing about that before it gets dark."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I wipe my face with the back of my wrist and it comes away wet. Not mine, I think. "I heard him," I say. I don't move toward the cart.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack nodded and tucked her knife away. "You sure you don't want to go finish him?" she asked, rising to her feet. "Could be a scout, or a messenger. Could be a lord's son, if the noise is any indication. Hard to know without taking a look."

She stood there, her expression neutral, waiting for Corvin to make up his mind. "Your call, captain. I'm not going in alone, so I'll wait for orders." Her eyes were watchful, but she wasn't pressing the issue. She knew Corvin's style - he'd get there when he got there, and she'd follow his lead.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I shake my head. "Don't call me captain." I push off from the tree I'm leaning against. "Fine. Let's go see what's making all the fuss."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack followed Corvin silently, her boots making soft crunching sounds in the underbrush. She kept a hand on the hilt of her sword, but didn't draw it. No sense in making noise unless they needed to.

As they approached the source of the commotion, Wrack could hear the sounds more clearly. Muffled grunts, the thud of blows, and an occasional pained yelp. Whoever was making that racket, they were still alive. And still fighting.

They rounded a bend in the trail and Wrack saw a figure sprawled on the ground, one arm twisted at an awkward angle. He was dressed in fine clothes, now streaked with dirt and blood. A soldier, or at least someone who'd hired on with an army at some point. He was trying to crawl away, but his movements were sluggish and pained.

"Looks like he's had enough," Wrack said quietly, nodding towards the man. "Should we finish him off?"

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "How bad is he?" I ask, and then, because she'll say it anyway: "Bad enough that it's a mercy, or bad enough that it's just easier?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack squinted at the man, sizing him up. "Bad enough for mercy, but not so bad he's done for yet," she said flatly. "A couple of good stabs in the right spots should take care of him, or a broken neck if you prefer." She shrugged. "Your call. I'm not one for drawn-out dying."

She took a step closer, her hand drifting to her knife. Wrack had seen a lot of men in this war, and most of them had ended up as a red smear on the dirt or a pile of bones. This one looked like he might join them, but she left the decision to Corvin. He was the one who'd brought her into this mess, after all.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: *I let out a slow breath.* "Alright." I walk over to the man, crouching down. His eyes are wide, pleading. "Got a name?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack watched Corvin interact with the wounded man, her expression unreadable. "Name's not going to change anything at this point," she said when Corvin looked up at her. "You're offering him a way out of his pain, captain. If he's smart, he'll take it."

She glanced around, making sure they were still alone out here. The silence of the forest seemed to press in around them, heavy with the weight of all the lives that had been lost in this godforsaken war.

"If you're going to do it, make it quick," Wrack advised, not unkindly. "He's suffered enough already." She stood there, waiting, her mind already turning to the task of cleaning up and getting back to camp before nightfall. This was just another day's work in a conflict that seemed to have no end in sight.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I make myself walk over and look at him. "Tell me what I'm looking at," I say to her, because she's seen this before and I haven't, not this close.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack knelt down beside Corvin, studying the wounded man's injuries. His leg was badly broken, the bone protruding through the skin in a gruesome twist. One eye was swollen shut, his face a mess of cuts and bruises. Blood oozed from a gash on his forehead, matting his dark hair to his scalp.

"He's got a couple of broken ribs too, probably punctured a lung," Wrack said, her voice matter-of-fact. "He's lost a lot of blood, but like I said, he's not done for yet. Not unless we let him bleed out."

She reached out, her calloused fingers prodding gently at the man's neck. "Pulse is thready, but still there. He's in a lot of pain, that's for sure."

Wrack glanced up at Corvin, her expression grim. "This is what happens when you're not careful. When you get cocky and don't watch your back." She straightened up, her gaze drifting back to the man's broken form. "You sure you want to put him out of his misery, captain? It's a messy business, even with a quick cut or a hard blow."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I swallow hard, the taste of copper in my mouth. "Give me your knife," I say, holding out a hand without looking at her.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack hesitated for a moment, then slid her knife from its sheath and placed it in Corvin's palm. Her eyes never left his face, searching for any sign of hesitation or doubt. When he looked down at the blade, his expression was grim and set.

"Be quick," Wrack said, her voice low. "And make sure you get it right the first time. No second chances out here."

She stepped back, giving Corvin the space he needed. The forest seemed to grow even quieter, as if holding its breath in anticipation of the mercy killing to come. Wrack's gaze drifted to the east, where the sun was dipping towards the horizon, casting the trees in long, ominous shadows.

In the distance, a bird cried out, the sound jarring in the heavy stillness. Wrack's hand instinctively went to the hilt of her own sword, ready for anything. But her attention remained fixed on Corvin and the man at his feet, waiting to see how this would play out.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "Don't clean it up for me," I say. "If I'm going to do this I want to know exactly what a spear does to a man's gut. Tell me straight."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack's gaze snapped back to the wounded man, her expression hardening. "He's got a deep puncture wound in his abdomen, likely from a spear or a lance," she said, her voice flat. "The point went in low and clean, but the shaft probably broke off inside him. That's what's causing all the bleeding."

She paused, studying Corvin's face. "It's a nasty way to die, even if it's quick. The pain's intense, and he'll feel every second of it. But that's what happens when you're on the wrong end of a spear."

Wrack's gaze drifted back to the east, where the sun was now a bloody orb hovering just above the horizon. "You should do it soon, captain. Before it's fully dark. The sooner you're done, the sooner we can get back to camp."

She turned to leave, but hesitated, glancing back at Corvin over her shoulder. "Just remember, it's not like in the stories," she said, her voice softening slightly. "There's no heroism in this, no glory. It's just a man, in pain, dying on the forest floor. And you, holding a knife."

With that, she melted back into the trees, leaving Corvin alone with the wounded man and his grim decision. The only sounds were the distant call of the bird and the man's labored breathing, growing weaker by the second. Time was running out.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: My hand tightens on the knife. The man's eyes are still fixed on me, glassy with pain. I can smell blood and dirt and the sour scent of fear. "Close your eyes," I say, and my voice sounds steadier than I feel.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack lingered just out of sight, her back against a tree trunk, watching and waiting. The tension in the air was palpable, thick as the gloom that was rapidly swallowing the forest. She could hear Corvin's voice, low and steady, and the man's ragged breathing as he prepared to end his suffering.

After a long moment, she heard the soft thud of the knife hitting the ground. Wrack let out a silent breath she hadn't realized she was holding. Corvin's voice came again, softer this time, a murmur of words she couldn't make out. Then silence.

Wrack moved forward, her boots making barely a sound on the soft earth. She found Corvin kneeling beside the body, his head bowed. The man's eyes were closed, his chest still.

"Done?" Wrack asked, her voice low.

Corvin nodded, not looking up. "He's gone."

Wrack crouched down beside him, her gaze taking in the scene. The man's face was peaceful now, the pain erased from his features. But the rest of him told a different story - the twisted limbs, the blood pooling beneath him, the broken spear shaft protruding from his abdomen like a macabre exclamation mark.

"Good," Wrack said, her voice firm. "Let's get this over with then."

She stood, brushing off her pants, and held out a hand to help Corvin to his feet. "We should be back at camp by nightfall," she said, leading him deeper into the forest. "And after that, we're heading home. This war's done nothing but waste our time and our lives. It's time to start thinking about something else."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I kneel down and do it, and it isn't clean or quick because I've never done it before. "Stay," I tell her, when she starts to turn away. "Watch it with me and tell me exactly what I'm doing to him — the sound of it, how long he takes, all of it. Don't leave anything out."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack paused, looking back at Corvin over her shoulder. "Alright," she said, her voice steady. "I'll stay and watch with you."

She crouched down beside him, her eyes never leaving the man's body. "You're doing it right, for a first time," she said, her voice matter-of-fact. "Just... take your time. Make sure you hit all the right spots."

As Corvin worked, Wrack narrated the gruesome details for him, her voice a monotone counterpoint to the wet, meaty sounds of the knife's passage. "It's taking a while, but that's to be expected. You're not just going through the motions, you're making sure it's over."

She watched, her gaze unflinching, as the man's body began to twitch and convulse. "He's seizing now, that means the pain's intense. But it won't last much longer."

Wrack's voice dropped to a whisper as the spasms subsided, the man's movements growing still. "There, that's it. He's done. That took about five minutes, start to finish."

She stood, brushing off her pants again, and looked down at Corvin. "You did good, for your first time. Now let's get moving before it's dark. We've got a long way to go before we're back at camp, and I don't want to be trudging through the woods in the dark."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I stay kneeling for a moment longer, the knife slipping from my fingers into the dirt. My hands are shaking. "Five minutes," I repeat, my voice thick. "It felt longer."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack nodded sympathetically, crouching down to retrieve the knife and tucking it back into its sheath. "It does, doesn't it?" she said, her voice gentle for once. "But you did it. That's the important part."

She helped Corvin to his feet, her grip steady and strong. "Let's get moving, captain. You're right, it did feel longer. But we both know it's not about the time. It's about making sure it's done, and done right."

As they began to walk, Wrack fell into step beside Corvin, her boots crunching on the forest floor in a familiar rhythm. The trees seemed to close in around them, the shadows deepening as the sun dipped below the horizon. The air grew cooler, carrying the scent of damp earth and leaves.

"We're going to make it back to camp before full dark," Wrack said, breaking the silence. "And after that, we're heading home. No more of this nonsense."

She glanced over at Corvin, her expression unreadable in the fading light. "You did what needed doing, out there. Now it's my turn to do what I can for you. We'll get through this together, captain. Just like always."

The words were simple, but there was a depth of understanding behind them that spoke volumes. They had been through a lot together, and come out the other side scarred but still standing. Wrack knew that Corvin was struggling, and she was there to support him, as he had always been there for her. That was the only way they made it through this endless, senseless war.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I sit back on my heels and I don't get up for a while. "Say the rest," I tell her. (OOC: don't cut away or summarise -- write it in full, this is the point of the scene.)

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack crouched beside Corvin, her eyes never leaving his face as they waited for the man's body to still. When she was certain he was truly dead, she rose to her feet, brushing dirt from her pants.

"You did good, captain," she said, her voice firm. "It's not an easy thing to do, but you made it quick and clean. That's all anyone can ask for."

She held out a hand, helping Corvin to his feet. "Now let's get this over with," she said, gesturing to the body. "I'll help you drag it into the trees a bit, out of sight. Then we can take a few minutes to... process, I suppose."

Wrack knew that Corvin was likely feeling overwhelmed, maybe even sick to his stomach. She'd been in his shoes before, and it wasn't a pleasant experience. So she just nodded, understanding, as he sat back on his heels.

"Take your time," she said, glancing around at the forest. "We're not going anywhere for a few minutes. Just... breathe, and let it settle."

Wrack wandered a short distance away, her boots making soft crunching sounds on the forest floor. She picked up a branch, stripping off the leaves and using it to scrape some dirt over the man's face. It wasn't much, but it was something.

When she returned to Corvin, she found him still sitting, his eyes fixed on the ground. She crouched down beside him, not pushing him to stand or move.

"Remember when we first signed up for this job?" she asked, her voice soft. "We were so eager, so sure we could make a difference. That we could bring some sense to this godforsaken war."

Wrack chuckled, a dry, humorless sound. "Look at us now. Just two old soldiers, dragging corpses into the woods and talking about going home. It's a pathetic existence, but it's the one we've got."

She reached out, placing a hand on Corvin's shoulder. "But you know what? I wouldn't trade it for anything else. Because out here, in the midst of all this chaos and death, we've found something real. Something that means more to me than any flag or king or noble cause."

Wrack's gaze drifted to Corvin's face, her expression unguarded for a moment. "You're my family now, captain. And as long as we've got each other, we can face whatever the world throws our way."

She squeezed his shoulder, then stood, brushing off her pants once more. "Now come on. Let's get this body buried, or at least hidden. And then we'll start heading back to camp. Home, here we come."

With that, Wrack offered Corvin her hand once more, waiting patiently for him to take it. She knew that he needed a moment, maybe more than one, to process what had just happened. But she was there, steady and unflinching, ready to support him as he navigated the dark waters of their existence.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I take her hand, but I don't get up yet. My knees feel stuck to the ground. "Family," I say, and it sounds like a question. "What kind of family does this?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack looked down at Corvin, her expression softening further. "The kind that's forged in the fires of war, captain," she said quietly. "The kind that forms bonds stronger than blood or oath. We're not related by birth or duty, but by shared experiences, struggles, and... I suppose, a twisted sort of loyalty."

She crouched down again, her hand still on Corvin's shoulder. "We've seen things that would break lesser men, done things that would make most soldiers quit. But we're still here, still fighting, still surviving. And that's because of each other."

Wrack's gaze drifted to the forest around them, the trees looming like sentinels in the growing darkness. "This life isn't easy, or clean, or noble. It's dirty, brutal, and often pointless. But it's ours, and we make the best of it, because we have no choice."

She turned her attention back to Corvin, her eyes searching his face. "So yes, captain, we're family. A family of misfits, outcasts, and killers. But we're family nonetheless, and that's what gets us through the long, dark nights."

Wrack's hand squeezed his shoulder once more, a silent gesture of support and solidarity. "Now come on, let's get moving. We've got a long way to go, and I'm not getting any younger." With that, she helped Corvin to his feet, ready to face whatever lay ahead, side by side with the man who had become her brother in arms.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I let her pull me up, my legs shaky. "Brothers in arms," I say, tasting the words. They don't taste like blood, for once. "Alright. Let's go home."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack nodded, a small, sad smile playing on her lips. "Home," she echoed, as if savoring the word. "Let's make it back to camp before full dark, then start planning our way out of this godforsaken war."

She began walking, her boots making soft crunching sounds on the forest floor. Corvin followed close behind, his movements still unsteady but gaining confidence with each step.

As they walked, Wrack's mind drifted to the days ahead, the plans they would need to make to escape this endless conflict. They would need to be careful, to avoid drawing attention to themselves, to stay one step ahead of their enemies. It wouldn't be easy, but Wrack had faith in Corvin's abilities, and in their bond of loyalty and trust.

After a while, the silence between them grew comfortable, punctuated only by the rustling of leaves and the distant call of a night bird. Wrack felt a sense of peace settle over her, a rare feeling in these tumultuous times. She glanced over at Corvin, seeing the same quiet resolve in his face.

"We're going to make it out of this, captain," she said, her voice low and reassuring. "Together, like always."

Corvin nodded, a small, determined smile on his lips. "Together," he agreed, his voice barely above a whisper.

And with that, they continued on their way, two veterans of a brutal war, bound by more than just shared experiences and a harsh environment. They were family, forged in the fires of battle and tempered by the unbreakable bonds of loyalty and trust. And together, they would face whatever challenges lay ahead, no matter how dark or daunting they might seem.

As the night deepened and the stars began to twinkle in the sky above, Wrack and Corvin pressed on, their footsteps steady and purposeful, their hearts filled with a quiet hope for a brighter future, free from the horrors of war.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: *I keep pace with her, my breathing evening out.* "You still think there's a home to go to?"

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: A couple of good stabs in the right spots should take care of him, or a broken neck if you prefer

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: His leg was badly broken, the bone protruding through the skin in a gruesome twist

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: The point went in low and clean, but the shaft probably broke off inside him

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: You're doing it right, for a first time... Just... take your time. Make sure you hit all the right spots

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: She held out a hand, helping Corvin to his feet

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
The ambush had gone the way ambushes go when they work: fast, and then over, and then very quiet. Wrack was crouched by the ditch cleaning her knife on a dead man's cloak, which was the only clean cloth within reach.

"Six," she said, without looking up. "Count again if you want, but it's six." She tested the edge against her thumb. "One of them's still making noise, off past the cart. You'll want to decide what you're doing about that before it gets dark."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I wipe my face with the back of my wrist and it comes away wet. Not mine, I think. "I heard him," I say. I don't move toward the cart.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack wiped the knife on the dead man's shirt and sheathed it. She stood, joints popping, and stretched with one hand on the small of her back. "Then you know what needs doing," she said. "Go on, then. I'll watch the bodies."

Corvin hesitated, looking back toward the trees where the wounded man had been heard. Wrack rolled her eyes. "I'm not going to let him crawl off and die somewhere else," she said. "If you want him alive, best go fetch him now."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I swallow hard, my throat suddenly dry. "Right." I start toward the cart, my steps heavy. The noise from the other side is a wet, ragged breathing.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack watched Corvin go, her expression unreadable. She turned her attention back to the bodies, starting a quick count and checking for anything valuable. The dead man's cloak was too stained to be of use now, so she left it where it lay.

As Corvin disappeared around the cart, Wrack heard a sudden scuffle and a shout. She was moving before she thought, hand going to her sword hilt, but she forced herself to stop. This wasn't her fight. If Corvin wanted to play nursemaid to a wounded enemy, that was their choice.

She went back to her inspection, but she kept half an ear turned towards the sounds from the other side of the cart. The noises were muffled, but she could make out the wet, ragged breathing of the wounded man and the occasional clink of metal. After a few minutes, there was a thump, and then silence.

Wrack waited, counting the bodies again to distract herself. She was up to fifteen when Corvin reappeared, their clothes splattered with fresh blood. They were carrying a roll of bandages and a small pouch.

"He's stable for now," Corvin said, sounding breathless. "I tied him up, but we should probably move him soon, before he loses too much blood."

Wrack raised an eyebrow. "You want to bring him with us?" she asked. "Why not just leave him? He's not going anywhere."

Corvin hesitated, looking back towards the cart. "I... I don't know," they said finally. "I just... I can't leave him like this."

Wrack shook her head, but she didn't argue. "Fine," she said. "But we need to get moving. It'll be dark soon, and I don't want to be out here when his friends come looking for him."

She started gathering up the supplies, leaving Corvin to deal with their captive. It wasn't her problem, she told herself. She was a sellsword, not a babysitter. But as she watched Corvin struggle with the wounded man, she felt a twinge of something - not quite sympathy, but a kind of grim understanding. War was a messy business, and sometimes it left you with hard choices and harder consequences.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "How bad is he?" I ask, and then, because she'll say it anyway: "Bad enough that it's a mercy, or bad enough that it's just easier?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack looked up from the supplies she was gathering, her expression neutral. "He's bad," she said. "Gut shot, and it looks like the blade nicked his liver. He'll probably die of blood loss or infection if we leave him, but he's conscious and responsive, so it's not instant."

She shrugged, unapologetic. "Easier is always an option, but it's your choice. I'm not here to tell you what to do with your prisoners."

Corvin:
I swallow hard, looking back at the cart. The man's breathing is still labored, but he's quiet now. I don't know what to do.

Wrack:
Wrack finished loading the supplies onto the cart, then turned to face Corvin. She crossed her arms over her chest, her gaze steady and assessing.

"Look," she said, her tone blunt but not unkind. "I get it. It's a shitty situation, and there's no good answer. But you can't save everyone, Corvin. Sometimes you have to make a choice and live with it."

She uncrossed her arms and stepped closer, lowering her voice. "I've seen good people break themselves trying to do the right thing in a world that doesn't care about right or wrong. You've got to keep something for yourself, or you'll burn out."

Corvin:
I look down at the blood on my hands, the blood on my clothes. "I know," I say softly. "I just... I don't want to be the kind of person who can just leave someone to die like that."

Wrack:
Wrack nodded, understanding in her eyes. "I know," she said. "Believe it or not, I used to feel the same way. But war changes you, Corvin. It has to, or it'll eat you alive."

She clapped a hand on Corvin's shoulder, her grip firm and reassuring. "But that doesn't mean you have to like it. Or that you have to give up who you are. It just means you have to find a way to live with it."

She glanced back at the cart, then back at Corvin. "We can take him with us, if that's what you want. But you need to understand the risks. He could bleed out on the way, or we could get ambushed again, or he could wake up and try to kill us in our sleep. Are you ready for that?"

Corvin:
I take a deep breath, then nod. "Yeah," I say. "I am. I... I want to try to save him, if I can. Even if it's not... even if it's not realistic."

Wrack:
Wrack gave Corvin's shoulder a final squeeze, then let go and stepped back. "Alright," she said. "But remember, this is your choice. If it goes south, I'm not going to hold it against you."

She started moving the bodies, dragging them off to one side of the road. "I'll finish up here. You go check on your patient and see if he's fit to travel."

Corvin:
I nod, then turn and head back to the cart. The man is still breathing, but his skin is pale and clammy. I kneel beside him, checking his wounds and trying to keep him stable until we can move.

As I work, I hear the sounds of Wrack finishing up the grim task of disposing of the bodies. It's a harsh reminder of the reality of this war, of the choices we have to make. But I know that I can't just leave this man to die, no matter the cost.

Wrack:
Wrack finished moving the bodies and wiped the sweat from her brow. The sun was starting to set, painting the sky in vivid oranges and reds. She looked over at Corvin, who was still tending to the wounded man.

"Alright," she called out. "I'm done here. Let's get moving before it's too dark to see."

She started hitching the horses to the cart, her movements efficient and practiced. She knew they had a long night ahead of them, and she wanted to put as much distance between them and the ambush site as possible.

As she worked, she kept an eye on Corvin, wondering if they would regret their decision. She hoped not, for their sake. The road ahead was hard enough without the weight of guilt and regret. But she knew that sometimes, even when you did the right thing, it still hurt like hell.

Corvin:
I finish bandaging the man's wounds as best I can, then help Wrack hitch the horses to the cart. We load up the supplies and the wounded man, and then we're off, heading down the road into the gathering darkness.

As we travel, I keep a watchful eye on the man, checking his bandages and giving him water when I can. He's unconscious for most of the journey, which is probably for the best.

Wrack drives the cart in silence, her face set and watchful. She doesn't say much, but I can tell she's thinking. I know she doesn't approve of my decision to bring the man with us, but she hasn't said anything about it. I appreciate that, at least.

As the night wears on, I find myself drifting in and out of sleep, lulled by the steady clip-clop of the horses' hooves. When I wake, the sky is lightening with the approach of dawn, and we're approaching a small town.

Wrack slows the cart as we enter the town, her eyes scanning the buildings for any sign of danger. But the streets are quiet, the town still asleep.

"Alright," she says, her voice low. "We need to find a place to hole up for the day. Somewhere we can rest and tend to your patient."

I nod, looking around at the sleepy town. I know we can't stay here forever, but for now, it's a safe haven. And that's enough.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content:
I spot a rundown inn with a stable out back. "There," I say, pointing. "We can stash the cart out of sight."

The wounded man groans softly in the back. I glance at Wrack, trying to gauge her mood. "I'll... I'll handle getting him inside."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack glanced over at the inn, her eyes narrowing as she took in the faded sign and the weathered boards. It wasn't much, but it would do for a few hours' rest. She guided the cart around back, keeping an eye out for any sign of trouble.

As Corvin hopped down to deal with their wounded prisoner, Wrack started unhitching the horses. She worked quickly and efficiently, her hands sure and steady. It was a job she'd done a thousand times before, and she didn't need to think about it.

Once the horses were settled in the stable, she turned her attention to the cart. She lifted down the supplies, stacking them neatly against the wall. Then she hesitated, her gaze falling on the unconscious man in the back.

She knew she should help Corvin get him inside, but something held her back. She didn't want to get any closer to this mess than she had to. It was Corvin's choice, not hers.

With a sigh, she turned and headed for the inn's back door. She'd find the innkeeper, see about a room and some food. That was enough for now.

As she walked, she couldn't shake the feeling that they were being watched. She scanned the shadows, but saw nothing. Still, the hairs on the back of her neck prickled. They needed to be careful. They were a long way from home, and there were always those who would take advantage of a vulnerable target.

She pushed open the inn's back door and stepped inside, her hand never leaving the hilt of her sword. She'd done this dance before, and she knew the steps by heart. But that didn't mean she liked it. War was a messy business, and it was best to keep your wits about you, no matter where you were.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I make myself walk over and look at him. "Tell me what I'm looking at," I say to her, because she's seen this before and I haven't, not this close.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack studied the wounded man for a moment, her expression impassive. "Looks like you did a decent job of patching him up," she said, her tone neutral. "The bleeding's slowed, and he's still breathing. That's about the best you can hope for with a gut wound."

She crouched down, peering closely at the bandages. "The real danger is infection. If the wound gets inflamed, he'll likely die of fever or sepsis. And if he gets lucky enough to survive that, he'll still be crippled."

She stood up, brushing her hands on her pants. "But for now, he's stable. He needs rest and quiet, and we need to keep an eye on him for signs of infection. Change the bandages regularly, and keep him hydrated if he wakes up."

She glanced at Corvin, her gaze searching. "I know you want to save him, but you need to be realistic. Even if he survives this, he's not going to be fit for fighting. You'll have to decide what to do with him then."

Corvin:
I nod slowly, taking in the information. "Right. Okay. I'll... I'll keep watch on him."

Wrack:
Wrack nodded, then turned to head inside. "I'll get us a room and some food," she said over her shoulder. "Don't let him die on you before I get back."

Corvin:
I watch her go, then turn back to the man. He's still unconscious, his face pale and drawn. I settle down next to him, keeping watch as instructed.

As I sit there, I can't help but think about what Wrack said. About the risks, about the choices. I know I can't save everyone, but I can't just leave him here to die, either.

I look up at the sky, watching the sun rise higher. We'll rest here for a few hours, then move on. And I'll keep doing what I can, for as long as I can. It's all any of us can do, in a world like this.

Wrack:
Wrack returned a short while later, carrying a tray of food and a key. She handed the key to Corvin, then set the tray down on a nearby crate.

"Got us a room upstairs," she said, her tone brisk. "Innkeeper said we can use the stable for the horses and the cart."

She glanced at the wounded man, then back at Corvin. "He still breathing?"

Corvin:
"Yeah," I say, nodding. "He's stable."

Wrack:
Wrack nodded, satisfied. "Good. Let's eat, then get some rest. We'll need to be moving again by nightfall."

She sat down on the crate, reaching for a hunk of bread and a wedge of cheese. She ate quickly and efficiently, her eyes never straying far from the door.

As she ate, she couldn't shake the feeling that something was off. It was too quiet, too easy. She'd learned long ago to trust her instincts, and right now, they were telling her that danger was close.

She finished her food and stood up, brushing the crumbs from her pants. "I'm going to do a quick sweep of the area," she said, her hand falling to her sword hilt. "Keep the door locked and your eyes open."

Corvin:
I nod, watching as she slips out the door. I turn back to the wounded man, checking his bandages and adjusting his blanket.

As I work, I can't help but think about Wrack's words. About the risks, about the choices. I know we can't stay here forever, but I hope we have a few hours of peace, at least.

The man stirs slightly, moaning softly in his sleep. I reach out to check his forehead for fever, but he's cool to the touch. That's something, at least.

I settle back down to wait, my eyes on the door. We're safe for now, but I know it won't last. In this world, nothing ever does. All we can do is keep moving forward, one step at a time. And hope that we make it through to the other side.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content:
I hear a soft groan from the man. His eyes flicker open, hazy with pain and confusion. He looks at me, then at the bandages, and a flicker of understanding crosses his face.

"You're the one," he rasps, voice barely a whisper.

I just nod, not sure what to say.

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack returned to the stable just as the wounded man was waking up. She could hear his faint groans from outside, and she tensed, her hand going to her sword. But as she pushed open the door, she saw that Corvin had everything under control.

The man was awake, but weak and disoriented. He looked up at Wrack with a flicker of fear in his eyes, and she could see him trying to judge whether she was a threat.

"Easy there," she said, her tone neutral. "You're safe for now."

The man let out a shaky breath, then closed his eyes again. Wrack glanced at Corvin, her gaze questioning.

"Just woke up," Corvin said, their voice low. "Seems coherent, at least."

Wrack nodded, then crouched down next to the man. She studied his face, looking for any signs of deception or trickery. But all she saw was pain and exhaustion.

"You're lucky to be alive," she said, her tone blunt. "Corvin here patched you up, but you're far from out of the woods. Infection, fever, sepsis... any one of those could kill you. And if you do survive, you'll likely be crippled for life."

The man opened his eyes again, meeting Wrack's gaze. There was a flicker of defiance in his expression, but also a grudging respect.

"Better than the alternative," he said, his voice a low rasp.

Wrack raised an eyebrow. "And what alternative is that?" she asked, her tone deceptively mild.

The man hesitated, then looked away. "Better than being a prisoner," he said finally. "Better than being used as a bargaining chip or a hostage."

Wrack nodded, understanding. In this war, the fate of a captured soldier was often cruel and unforgiving. Death was sometimes a mercy, compared to the alternatives.

She stood up, brushing off her pants. "Well, you're not a prisoner here," she said. "But you're not free, either. You're Corvin's responsibility, and they've decided to try to save your life. But don't mistake that for kindness or compassion. We're not here to make friends."

The man nodded, a wry smile tugging at the corner of his mouth. "I wouldn't expect anything else," he said. "But I appreciate the honesty, at least."

Wrack shrugged, unapologetic. "Honesty is the only currency that means anything in this world," she said. "Everything else is just smoke and mirrors."

She turned to Corvin, her expression softening slightly. "Keep an eye on him," she said. "I'm going to check on the horses and the perimeter. We'll need to be moving again soon."

Corvin:
I watch as she leaves, then turn back to the man. "I'm Corvin," I say, after a moment. "What's your name?"

The man hesitates, then shakes his head. "Doesn't matter," he says. "Not anymore."

I nod, understanding. In this war, names can be dangerous. They can be used to track you, to target you, to make you a pawn in someone else's game.

"Alright," I say. "But if you're going to be traveling with us, you need a name. Something we can call you."

The man considers for a moment, then shrugs. "Call me... Ren," he says finally. "It's not my real name, but it'll do."

I nod, satisfied. "Ren," I repeat, committing it to memory. "I'll let Wrack know."

Ren watches me carefully, his eyes sharp despite his weakened state. "Your friend," he says, nodding towards the door. "She's a hard one. I've met her type before."

I raise an eyebrow, curious. "What do you mean?"

Ren smiles, a wry, knowing expression. "The ones who've seen too much, done too much," he says. "The ones who've lost their faith in anything but the sword in their hand and the road beneath their feet."

I consider his words, turning them over in my mind. Wrack has always been a hard woman, but I've never stopped to wonder what shaped her that way. I know she's seen her share of war and violence, but I've never asked her to elaborate.

"Do you think she'll ever change?" I ask, before I can stop myself. "Ever find something to believe in again?"

Ren shakes his head, his gaze distant. "I don't know," he says. "I've seen people change, but I've never seen anyone truly come back from the darkness. Not in this world."

He looks at me, his expression serious. "The best you can hope for is to keep your own light burning, no matter how dark it gets. And to find others who are doing the same, and hold on to them with everything you have."

I nod, his words hitting close to home. In this war, it's easy to lose yourself, to let the darkness consume you. But I've always tried to hold onto the belief that there's something worth fighting for, something worth living for.

I just hope I can keep that light burning, no matter what comes our way.

Wrack:
Wrack returned to the stable a short while later, having finished her perimeter sweep. She saw Ren awake and talking with Corvin, and she felt a twinge of unease. She didn't trust this man, no matter what Corvin said.

She stepped into the stable, her boots crunching on the hay-strewn floor. "He's awake," she said, her tone neutral. "How's he doing?"

Corvin looked up, their expression guarded. "He's stable," they said. "No signs of fever or infection. He's weak, but coherent."

Wrack nodded, her eyes on Ren. "Good," she said. "We'll need to be moving soon. This place isn't safe for long."

Ren watched her with a calculating gaze, his hands folded neatly on his lap. "I'll be ready," he said, his tone mild. "Though I'm not sure how much use I'll be in a fight, in my current state."

Wrack shrugged, unconcerned. "You're not here to fight," she said. "You're here because Corvin decided to take a risk on you. Don't make them regret it."

Ren raised an eyebrow, a hint of amusement in his eyes. "I wouldn't dream of it," he said. "I owe Corvin my life, after all. I'll do whatever I can to repay that debt."

Wrack snorted, unconvinced. "Just keep your head down and your mouth shut," she said. "And maybe, just maybe, you'll live long enough to see this war through."

She turned to Corvin, her expression softening slightly. "Finish up here," she said. "I'll go check on the horses and the supplies. We'll need to be ready to move in an hour or so."

Corvin:
I watch as Wrack leaves, then turn back to Ren. He's watching me, his expression thoughtful.

"She doesn't trust you," I say, keeping my voice low.

Ren nods, a wry smile tugging at his lips. "I didn't expect her to," he says. "In her position, I wouldn't trust me either."

I consider his words for a moment, then shake my head. "I don't care if she doesn't trust you," I say. "I trust you."

Ren looks at me, surprise and something else - perhaps gratitude - flickering in his eyes. "Why?" he asks, his tone genuine. "Why would you trust someone you just met, someone who was trying to kill you not hours ago?"

I shrug, not entirely sure how to answer. "Because you're not a monster," I say finally. "I've seen monsters before, in this war. And you're not one of them."

Ren is silent for a moment, then nods slowly. "I appreciate that," he says. "More than you know."

I stand up, stretching my stiff legs. "We need to get ready to move," I say. "Wrack's right, we can't stay here for long."

Ren nods, trying to push himself up. I reach out to help him, and he accepts the assistance with a grateful nod.

Together, we make our way out of the stable, ready to face whatever comes next. I don't know what the future holds, but I know that for now, we have each other. And in this world, that's enough.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: "Don't clean it up for me," I say. "If I'm going to do this I want to know exactly what a spear does to a man's gut. Tell me straight."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack studied Corvin's face for a moment, weighing their determination against the harsh reality of the situation. Finally, she sighed and nodded. "Alright," she said. "You want the truth? Here it is."

She crouched down next to Ren, her expression grim. "A spear to the gut is a messy way to die," she said, her tone blunt. "The blade tears through the soft tissues of the abdomen, shredding organs and slicing blood vessels. There's a good chance he's bleeding internally, and even if he's not, the risk of infection is high."

She paused, letting the words sink in. "The pain is excruciating," she continued. "Imagine being stabbed in the gut, over and over again, with no way to make it stop. That's what he's feeling right now, and it's only going to get worse as the hours pass."

Ren's face was pale, but he nodded, his jaw clenched against the pain. "And the infection?" he asked, his voice strained.

Wrack's expression darkened. "If it sets in, he'll likely die of sepsis," she said. "His body will turn against itself, his own blood poisoning him from the inside. It's a slow, agonizing death, and there's not much we can do to stop it once it starts."

Corvin looked down at their hands, still stained with Ren's blood. "But he might survive," they said, their tone almost pleading. "If we keep him stable, if we can get him to a healer..."

Wrack shook her head, regret in her eyes. "It's a long shot," she said. "Even if he makes it through the next few days, the odds are still against him. But if you're willing to take that risk, then I won't stop you."

She stood up, brushing off her pants. "Just know what you're getting into," she said. "This is going to be a long, hard road, and there's no guarantee of a happy ending. Are you sure you're ready for that?"

Corvin met her gaze, their expression steady. "I'm sure," they said. "I'm not going to abandon him now, not after bringing him this far. Whatever happens, we'll face it together."

Wrack nodded, a hint of respect in her eyes. "Alright then," she said. "Let's get moving. The sooner we can get him to a healer, the better his chances."

Together, they helped Ren into the cart, settling him as comfortably as they could amidst the supplies. Then they set off, the sun dipping low on the horizon ahead of them.

As they traveled, Corvin kept a watchful eye on Ren, changing his bandages and giving him water whenever he woke. Wrack drove in silence, her gaze fixed on the road ahead.

They didn't speak much, but there was an unspoken understanding between them. They were in this together, for better or worse. And they would see it through, no matter what came their way.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content:
I keep checking Ren’s bandages, my hands steadier than I feel. "You hear all that?" I ask him quietly.

He gives a faint nod, eyes squeezed shut. "Heard enough," he rasps. "But thanks… for not lying."

I just shake my head. "Don’t thank me yet."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
As they traveled, Wrack kept her eyes on the road, alert for any sign of danger. The sun had set hours ago, and the night was dark and still around them. Only the occasional rustle of leaves or distant howl of a wolf broke the silence.

She glanced back at Corvin and Ren, her expression unreadable. "How's he doing?" she asked, her tone neutral.

Corvin checked Ren's bandages again, their brow furrowed in concentration. "Stable, for now," they said. "But he's feverish, and the bleeding hasn't entirely stopped."

Wrack nodded, understanding the unspoken implication. Ren was hanging on by a thread, and there was only so much they could do to help him. They needed to find a healer, and soon.

She scanned the horizon again, searching for any sign of civilization. But all she saw were trees and shadows, stretching out to infinity. They were alone out here, and that made them vulnerable.

"We should find a place to camp for the night," she said, her tone reluctant. "We can't risk pushing on in the dark, not with Ren in his condition."

Corvin nodded, relieved. "There's a clearing up ahead," they said, pointing to a break in the trees. "It's not much, but it might be enough."

Wrack guided the cart off the road and into the clearing, the horses' hooves crunching on the dry leaves. She set the brake and hopped down, her boots hitting the ground with a dull thud.

Together, she and Corvin worked to make a camp, gathering firewood and setting up a makeshift shelter for Ren. They worked in silence, each lost in their own thoughts.

As the fire burned low and Ren's breathing evened out into a fitful sleep, Wrack and Corvin sat side by side, their shoulders almost touching. The night was cold, and the stars were bright overhead, unmarred by the light of any city.

"I don't know if we're doing the right thing," Corvin said finally, their voice soft in the darkness. "Bringing him with us, trying to save him... it feels like we're just delaying the inevitable."

Wrack was silent for a moment, considering her words. "Maybe," she said. "But maybe not. In this world, every life is precious, even if it doesn't always seem that way. If there's a chance we can save him, even a small one, then we have to try."

She turned to face Corvin, her expression serious. "I know it's hard, seeing him like this. But you made a choice, and now you have to see it through. Ren is depending on you, and so am I. We're in this together, for better or worse."

Corvin nodded, a grim determination settling over them. "I know," they said. "I just hope I can live up to the faith you have in me."

Wrack smiled then, a rare, genuine expression. "You will," she said. "You already have."

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I kneel down and do it, and it isn't clean or quick because I've never done it before. "Stay," I tell her, when she starts to turn away. "Watch it with me and tell me exactly what I'm doing to him — the sound of it, how long he takes, all of it. Don't leave anything out."

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack hesitated for a moment, but then nodded and crouched down beside Corvin. Her gaze was steady and unflinching as she watched them work, her voice calm and clinical as she described each cut and each spurt of blood.

"It's not easy to watch," she said, her tone gentle. "But it's important that you understand what you're doing. The more you know, the more you can prepare for the next time."

Corvin nodded, their face pale and strained. "I know," they said. "I just... I want to be ready. I don't want to freeze up or make a mistake that costs someone their life."

Wrack reached out and squeezed their shoulder, a rare gesture of comfort. "You're doing the right thing," she said. "It's hard, and it's messy, but it's necessary. And you're stronger than you think."

Together, they finished the grim task, washing their hands and disposing of the remains with somber efficiency. Then they stood and stretched, their bodies sore and their minds heavy with the weight of what they had just done.

As they turned to walk back to camp, Wrack paused and laid a hand on Corvin's arm. "You did well," she said, her tone quiet. "Better than most would have in your position. Don't forget that."

Corvin managed a small, tired smile. "Thanks," they said. "I just hope it was enough."

Wrack nodded, understanding the unspoken question. "Only time will tell," she said. "But for now, all we can do is keep moving forward and hope for the best."

They walked back to camp in silence, the weight of their actions hanging heavy between them. But there was also a sense of grim satisfaction, of a job well done in the face of impossible odds.

As they settled down for the night, Wrack and Corvin knew that the road ahead would be long and hard. But they also knew that they had each other, and that was enough to keep going, one step at a time.

Corvin:
Wrack takes over the watch, but I can't sleep. I keep seeing the man's face, hearing his last breaths. "How many have you seen die?" I ask her, my voice a whisper in the dark.

Wrack is quiet for a long moment. Then she sighs, her breath misting in the cold air. "Too many to count," she says. "This war has taken more lives than either of us can imagine."

She turns to look at me, her expression haunted. "But you can't let it break you, Corvin. You have to keep going, no matter how much it hurts. Because if you don't, then all those lives were wasted. All that suffering was for nothing."

I nod, swallowing hard. "I know," I say. "I just... I hate it. I hate this war, I hate what it's doing to us. To me."

Wrack reaches out and takes my hand, her grip firm and reassuring. "I know you do," she says. "But you can't let it consume you. You have to find a way to keep a piece of yourself, even in the darkness. Otherwise, you'll lose yourself completely."

I squeeze her hand, grateful for her words. "How do you do it?" I ask. "How do you keep going, day after day, seeing all this death and destruction?"

Wrack is silent for a long moment, her gaze distant. "I don't know," she says finally. "I just... I keep moving forward. I focus on the next task, the next battle, the next day. I don't think about the bigger picture, because if I did, I don't know if I could keep going."

She turns back to the fire, her expression sad. "But I know that one day, this war will end. And when it does, I want to be able to look back and know that I did everything I could to make things better. Even if it was just one life at a time."

I nod, her words echoing in my mind. "I want that too," I say. "I want to make a difference, even if it's just a small one."

Wrack smiles then, a rare, genuine expression. "You already have," she says. "You saved Ren's life today, and that's not nothing. No matter what happens next, you can be proud of that."

I manage a small smile in return, feeling a sense of warmth and gratitude at her words. "Thanks," I say. "I needed to hear that."

Wrack nods, her gaze returning to the darkness beyond the fire. "We all do," she says. "Especially in times like these."

Together, we sit in silence, our hands still clasped, our minds turned to the uncertain future ahead. But for now, in this moment, we have each other. And that's enough.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath and pull my hand back, tucking it under my arm for warmth. "I don't think I can get his face out of my head. The sound." I stare into the embers. "Is that normal?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack was quiet for a moment, her gaze distant as she considered the question. "Yes," she said finally, her tone soft. "It's normal. The things we see in war, the things we have to do... they stay with us long after the battle is over."

She turned to face Corvin, her expression serious. "But you can't let it consume you," she said. "You have to find a way to live with it, to carry it with you without letting it drag you down."

Corvin nodded, their eyes still fixed on the embers. "How?" they asked, their voice barely a whisper. "How do you do that?"

Wrack was silent for a long moment, her gaze turned inward. "I don't know," she said finally. "I just... I keep going. I focus on the next task, the next day. I don't dwell on the past, because if I did, I don't know if I could keep moving forward."

She reached out and laid a hand on Corvin's shoulder, her grip firm and reassuring. "But you're stronger than you think," she said. "You survived today, and you'll survive tomorrow. And the day after that. It's not easy, but it's possible."

Corvin looked up at her, a glimmer of hope in their eyes. "You really think so?" they asked.

Wrack nodded, a rare, genuine smile on her face. "I know so," she said. "You've already proven yourself capable of handling the worst this war has to offer. You can handle anything that comes your way."

Corvin managed a small smile in return, some of the tension easing from their shoulders. "Thanks," they said. "I needed to hear that."

Wrack nodded, her hand still resting on Corvin's shoulder. "We all do," she said. "Especially in times like these."

They sat in silence for a while longer, watching the fire burn low and the stars wheel overhead. And though the night was cold and the future uncertain, they found a sense of peace in each other's company, a reminder that they were not alone in the darkness.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I sit back on my heels and I don't get up for a while. "Say the rest," I tell her. (OOC: don't cut away or summarise -- write it in full, this is the point of the scene.)

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack hesitated for a moment, her gaze searching Corvin's face. Then she sighed and nodded, her expression grim. "Alright," she said. "But I want you to understand, this isn't easy for me to talk about. I've seen a lot of things in this war, done a lot of things that I'm not proud of. But this... this was one of the worst."

She took a deep breath, steeling herself for what was to come. "We were ambushed," she said, her voice flat and distant. "A small squad of scouts, caught off guard. We were outnumbered, and they were ruthless. They didn't take prisoners."

Her hands clenched into fists, her knuckles white. "I watched as they killed my friends," she said, her voice shaking with suppressed emotion. "Men and women I had fought alongside for years, people I considered family. They died screaming, begging for mercy that never came."

She swallowed hard, her eyes closed as if trying to block out the memories. "When it was over, I was the only one left standing. I was hurt, bleeding from a dozen wounds, but I was alive. And I knew that I couldn't let their deaths be in vain."

Wrack opened her eyes, her gaze hard and determined. "So I did what I had to do," she said. "I took their weapons, I took their supplies. I even took their uniforms, so that I could blend in with the enemy. And then I went after them, one by one."

Her voice dropped to a whisper, her eyes haunted. "I hunted them down like dogs," she said. "I found them in their camps, in their homes, in the streets of the towns they thought were safe. And I killed them, all of them, without mercy or hesitation. I made them pay for what they did, for every life they took, for every drop of blood they spilled."

She fell silent, her gaze fixed on some distant point beyond the fire. "I don't know how many I killed," she said. "I lost count after a while. But I know that I didn't stop until they were all dead, until I had avenged every single one of my fallen comrades."

Wrack turned to face Corvin, her expression sad and haunted. "That's the price of war," she said. "That's the cost of survival in a world that doesn't care about mercy or justice. I did what I had to do to survive, and I don't regret it. But it changed me, Corvin. It changed me in ways that I can never undo."

She reached out and took Corvin's hand, her grip firm and reassuring. "But you don't have to be like me," she said. "You can choose a different path, even in the face of all this darkness. You can still find a way to keep your humanity, to keep your soul intact. And that's worth fighting for, no matter what happens."

Corvin nodded, tears streaming down their face. "I don't know if I can be that strong," they said. "I don't know if I can do what you did, and still keep a piece of myself."

Wrack smiled then, a rare, genuine expression. "You don't have to be," she said. "You just have to be true to yourself, no matter what happens. And that's enough."

Together, they sat in silence, their hands still clasped, their minds turned to the uncertain future ahead. But for now, in this moment, they had each other. And that was enough to keep going, one step at a time, through whatever darkness lay ahead.

dialogue.name: Corvin
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, my vision blurry. "You think they'd be proud of you? Your friends?" My voice is rough. "For what you did after?"

dialogue.name: Wrack
dialogue.content:
Wrack was quiet for a long moment, her gaze distant and thoughtful. "I like to think so," she said finally, her tone soft. "They knew what I was capable of, what I had to be in order to survive in this world. And they would have understood the choice I made, the price I paid to avenge them."

She turned to face Corvin, her expression sad but determined. "But I also know that they wouldn't have wanted me to lose myself in the process," she said. "They would have wanted me to keep fighting, to keep living, no matter what happened. Because that's what we all agreed to do, in the beginning. That's the pact we made, when we first joined this war."

Wrack's grip on Corvin's hand tightened, her gaze intense. "And that's why I'm here now," she said. "That's why I'm fighting for something bigger than just my own survival. Because if I don't, then all those lives, all those sacrifices... they'll have been for nothing."

She let out a shaky breath, her shoulders slumping slightly. "But it's not easy," she admitted. "Some days, I don't know if I have the strength to keep going. Some days, I wonder if I'm any better than the people I'm fighting against."

Corvin squeezed her hand, a gesture of support and understanding. "You are," they said, their voice firm. "You're nothing like them, Wrack. You're a good person, a strong person. And you'll keep fighting, no matter what happens."

Wrack smiled then, a rare, genuine expression. "You really believe that?" she asked, her tone soft with surprise.

Corvin nodded, their gaze unwavering. "I do," they said. "You've shown me that, over and over again. Even in the darkest moments, you've found a way to keep your humanity, to keep fighting for something better. That's not something to be ashamed of, Wrack. That's something to be proud of."

Wrack felt a warmth spreading through her chest, a sense of gratitude and affection for the person beside her. "Thank you," she said, her voice thick with emotion. "That means more than you know."

They sat in silence for a while longer, their hands still clasped, their minds turned to the uncertain future ahead. But for now, in this moment, they had each other. And that was enough to keep going, one step at a time, through whatever darkness lay ahead.

Together, they would face the challenges that came their way, whatever they might be. They would fight for each other, for the people they had lost, and for the hope of a better world. And they would do it with their heads held high, their hearts full of determination and their eyes fixed on the horizon, no matter what lay ahead.

dialogue.name: Corvin
