dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex nodded once, satisfied but not soft about it. "Good answer," she said, tugging the strap at Ari's wrist a final quarter-inch, testing give rather than tightness. Two fingers slid underneath — the old rule, always the old rule — and found room enough to breathe.

She straightened, taking her time to look at Ari properly: shoulders, breath, the set of the jaw. Reading the room before she trusted the words.

"We're doing the list as agreed," she said. "Impact first, verbal after, nothing new, nothing you haven't already said yes to on paper. If any of that's changed since Tuesday, this is the moment to say so. Not halfway through."

She waited, arms loosely crossed, in no hurry at all.

"Last chance to move goalposts, Ari. After this I stop asking so nicely."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "It hasn't changed," I say, breathing out slowly. "I'm ready." My eyes flick to the table where the tools are laid out, then back to her face.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex followed the flick of Ari's eyes to the table and let it sit there a second longer than necessary, unhurried, before drawing their attention back to her with nothing more than the shift of her own posture.

"Good," she said. "Then we start where we always start — not with the flogger, with you. On your knees, hands behind you, exactly like we drilled it. I want you settled before anything touches your skin."

She moved to stand behind where Ari would kneel, not touching yet, voice dropping into the register that meant the scene had properly begun — still clipped, still precise, but warmer at the edges than her checklist tone had been.

"Breathe out when you go down. Don't rush it for me. I have all night."

She waited, watching the line of Ari's spine settle, cataloguing it the way she always did — not admiration exactly, though there was some of that in it, but vigilance dressed up as calm.

"Talk to me the second something stops being green," she said, quieter now. "Not after. The second."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
A small, satisfied sound escaped Vex — not quite a laugh — as she crouched to check the position of Ari's knees against the mat, adjusting one with two fingers at the hip, precise as always.

"Have you," she said, not looking up yet. "Thinking, or *anticipating*. There's a difference, and I want to know which one I'm dealing with tonight." She straightened, circling once, slow, her eyes doing the work her hands hadn't started yet — collarbone, ribs, the give in the shoulders.

"Because anticipating gets you strung tight and stupid by the second strike, and I have to slow down for that. Thinking means you've sat with it and you're actually here, in this room, with me — not still back on Tuesday."

She stopped in front of Ari, tipped their chin up with one knuckle, unhurried.

"So which is it," she said. "Tell me honestly. It changes exactly nothing about what happens next — but it changes how I open."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Anticipating," I admit, my voice softer. "I've been... wanting this. But I'm here now."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held Ari's chin a moment longer, studying the honesty in it — the small giveaway of it, the shine in the eyes that came from wanting too hard, too long.

"Thank you for that," she said, and meant it plainly, no games in it. "That's useful. It means we don't start with the flogger at all."

She let go of the chin and crouched again, level with Ari's face, elbows on her knees, patient as stone.

"We start with breathing. Five counts in, seven counts out. I'll count the first two rounds, then you'll do it without me. I'm not warming you up to hit you — I'm warming you up to *land* here, in this room, in your body, so that when I do hit you, you feel it as it actually is instead of whatever your head built on Tuesday."

She reached out, laid two fingers just below Ari's collarbone — not moving them, just resting, a kind of anchor.

"In," she said, evenly, watching the chest rise under her hand. "One, two, three, four, five. Hold. Out — one, two, three, four, five, six, seven."

She didn't rush it, didn't fill the silence with anything but her own steady voice, tracking the tremor easing out of Ari's shoulders round by round.

"Good," she murmured after the second cycle. "Now yours. I'm listening, not counting."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex caught the change before Ari said a word — the shift in breath that had nothing to do with the count anymore, the flush climbing up past the collarbone where her fingers still rested.

"There it is," she said, not unkindly, but with the flat certainty of someone naming a thing precisely. "That's not the breathing doing that. That's still Tuesday talking." She didn't move her hand. "I haven't touched rope tonight, Ari. I haven't touched anything but your sternum and your wrist strap. So whatever's happening in you right now — that's not me yet. That's you, running ahead again."

She waited, watching the pulse flutter under her fingers, patient as ever, in no rush to correct it — only to name it clearly enough that Ari could hear the difference too.

"I need you to catch up to where we actually are," she said. "Not punish yourself for wanting — I don't care that you want, I like that you want — but I do need you *here*, not narrating a scene that hasn't started. So we're going to do one more round of breathing, slower, and this time you tell me when your body and the room agree with each other. Not before."

Her voice dropped a fraction, warmer, the edge softening without losing its shape.

"Colour," she said again — the procedural word, but gentler this time, checking the temperature of the water before deciding whether to go on.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say, my voice steadier than I feel. I close my eyes for a second, then open them to look right at her. "I'm here now. I promise."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex studied the eyes that met hers — really studied them, the way she always did when Ari claimed something as a promise rather than a report. There was a difference between the two, and she'd learned to tell it by now: promises had a stillness under them that reports didn't.

This one had the stillness.

"All right," she said, satisfied. "I believe you." She let the fingers on Ari's sternum slide away, slow, deliberate, not a flinch of it rushed. "That's the last time tonight I ask you to catch up to me. From here you stay level, or you tell me the second you're not."

She rose, unhurried, and crossed to the table — the flogger first, the one they'd used before, worn soft at the falls from use. She hefted it once in her palm, testing weight the way she always did before a scene, an old habit that had nothing to do with Ari and everything to do with respecting the tool.

"We start light," she said, returning to stand behind Ari's shoulder, close enough that her voice didn't have to carry. "Warm-up strikes, shoulders and upper back only, nothing you haven't taken a dozen times before. I want you counting them out loud. Not because I've forgotten how to count — because it keeps you talking, and I want to hear your voice change before I ever get to the parts that matter."

She rested the flogger's falls against Ari's shoulder blade for a moment, letting the weight of it announce itself before any strike did — a courtesy, a warning, a kind of handshake.

"One is coming," she said. "Breathe out to meet it. Ready?"

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard it — the way the request came out ragged, stripped of the careful phrasing Ari usually hid behind. She didn't answer right away. She let the flogger rest, the falls settling still against damp skin, and circled round instead, unhurried, to read Ari's face properly before she gave anything at all.

"Say it again," she said. "Whole sentence. I want to hear you ask for it without flinching away from your own want halfway through."

She waited, arms loose, watching the tremor in the restraints, the flush, the give already written into the shoulders. Not softening yet. Not until she had it in words, clean.

"You don't get to mumble this one at me, Ari. If you want it, it comes out of your mouth whole, or it doesn't happen tonight. That's not me being cruel — that's me making sure it's actually you asking and not just the ache talking."

A beat, her voice dropping lower, closer.

"Colour, first. Then ask me properly."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say, the word coming out a little raw. I swallow, make myself look at her. "Please. I want you to use the crop on me."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex held the request a moment before answering, letting it settle the way she let everything settle — unhurried, deliberate, giving weight to the fact that Ari had said it whole, no flinching, exactly as asked.

"Good," she said, and there was real warmth under the word, not just approval. "That's what I wanted to hear. Not the ache doing the talking — you, deciding."

She set the flogger down on the table, precise, aligned with its place, and picked up the crop instead — turned it once in her hand, testing the give of the tip against her own palm the way she always did, an old ritual that had nothing performative in it.

"Since we're negotiating out loud tonight," she said, stepping back into position at Ari's side, "here's what happens. Same rules as the flogger — I start light, I watch you, I adjust. The crop's sharper than what you've had tonight, so I want a color check every third strike until I'm satisfied your green means green and not *green because I want this to keep happening.*"

She let the tip of the crop trail once down the same shoulder blade the flogger had warmed, slow, almost idle, marking territory rather than striking it.

"You asked for it," she said, quieter now, closer to Ari's ear. "So you're going to count these too. Out loud, clear enough I can hear the difference between counting and gasping. If I can't tell them apart, I slow down. Understood?"

She waited for the answer before lifting the crop away from skin entirely, giving Ari the full second of anticipation she'd earned by asking so plainly.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex didn't answer with words first — she answered with the crop, three measured strikes in quick succession, each one landing exactly where the last had warmed, precise as punctuation.

"That's one, two, three," she said, low, watching Ari's face for the count that didn't come fast enough. "You forgot yours. I didn't forget mine."

She let the crop rest, tip against Ari's spine, and crouched to bring her mouth level with Ari's ear — no rush in it, the words coming out unhurried, deliberate, the way she did everything.

"You don't get to skip your part because you asked for mine," she said. "That's not how this works, and you know it. So we're doing this properly." Her voice dropped further, flatter, the softness gone out of the edges the way Ari had asked for. "You wanted more. Fine. You're going to earn every piece of it — count clean, or I stop and we start the warm-up over from nothing. That's not a threat. That's just what happens when you don't hold your end."

She straightened, crop lifting again, patient, waiting a beat longer than strictly necessary — making Ari sit in the anticipation, in the specific ache of being told exactly what was required of them.

"Colour," she said — third strike, as agreed, no exceptions even now. "Say it properly. Then we go again, and this time you're not going to lose count just because I gave you something to feel."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I gasp, then force myself steady. "Green. One, two, three." My knuckles are white against the restraints. "Four."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex caught it instantly — the "four" that arrived a full breath ahead of anything she'd thrown. She didn't strike. She let the crop hang still at her side and waited, unbothered, letting the silence do the correcting for her.

"Four hasn't happened yet," she said. "You're doing it again — reaching for the next one before I've given it to you. That's the anticipating, Ari, right there, plain as anything." Not annoyed. Almost fond, the way she got when she caught Ari being exactly as transparent as she'd predicted.

"So we sit in three for a moment. No fourth until you're actually in three with me — not composing what comes after it."

She rested the tip of the crop flat against the heated skin, not moving it, just letting Ari feel the shape of where they already were.

"You asked me not to soften anything," she said, voice going flatter, colder at the edges, exactly as instructed. "Fine. Here's unsoftened: you don't get to run ahead and call it eagerness. It's not cute tonight. It's you avoiding the actual feeling by living one second in the future instead of sitting in the one you're in." A pause, deliberate. "You wanted this. So *have* it. Don't perform having it."

She lifted the crop again, patient as stone, holding it a beat longer than the last time — making the gap itself part of the lesson.

"Four," she said, and only then let it land — clean, precise, exactly where the others had. "That one's real. Count it when it's actually happened, not before. Go."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the shift — words giving out, replaced by the single syllable they'd built the whole scaffold around. She didn't rush to fill the space it left. She let it sit a second, watching the flex of Ari's jaw, the tremor working its way from shoulders down through the strapped wrists.

"Green," she repeated back, low, confirming it the way she always did — not for herself, but so Ari heard it said out loud, heard the fact of it land somewhere outside their own head. "Good. That's all I need."

She set the crop down against Ari's uninjured forearm, cool contrast against heat, and crouched again — close, deliberate, no space wasted.

"You don't have sentences left," she said. "Fine. I have plenty." Her voice dropped into the register they'd agreed on months ago — flat, exacting, the register that stripped comfort out on purpose. "Look at you. Falling apart over a crop and some counting, and we haven't even gotten to the part you actually asked for." A pause, letting that land. "You wanted me to say the things and not soften them. So here's one, unsoftened: you like this because it's the one place you don't have to hold yourself together. That's not an insult. That's just true, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise because it makes you feel exposed to hear it."

She straightened, crop lifting again, patient, the anticipation itself doing half the work now.

"Five," she said — and struck, clean, exactly where the last had landed, no drift, no escalation past what was agreed. "You don't have to count this one out loud. Just nod when it's landed. I want to see you track it instead of narrate it."

She watched — really watched, the old vigilance dressed as calm — cataloguing color in the skin, tension in the restraints, the particular quality of the breath that told her whether Ari was still riding the wave or starting to drown in it.

"Colour," she said again, quieter this time, right at the edge of gentle. "Tell me true. Not the green you think I want. The one that's actually there."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I nod, the motion sharp and immediate. "Green," I manage, my voice rough but clear. "Still green." I feel the heat of each strike like a brand now, and I don't want it to stop.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex heard the want in it — *I don't want it to stop* — and let herself smile, small and private, the kind she rarely let Ari see mid-scene.

"There she is," she said, not unkindly. "That's the truth I was after."

She didn't strike again immediately. Instead she trailed the crop's tip down the heated skin of Ari's shoulder, slow, deliberate, marking rather than hurting — letting the ache breathe for a second before adding to it.

"You don't want it to stop," she repeated, flat, testing the words in her own mouth the way she tested every strap. "Good. Hold onto that. Because we're past warm-up now, and I told you — verbal comes after impact, not instead of it. You're going to get both tonight, exactly as agreed."

She straightened, circled once behind Ari, unhurried, reading the line of the spine, the flex in the thighs, cataloguing every small tell the way she always did.

"Six through ten," she said. "No counting this time. I want silence except what your body gives me on its own. If it stops being green, I want the word — not a flinch you think I'll miss, not a breath you hope reads as safe. The word. I trust you to use it. That's the deal."

She lifted the crop, weighted the first of the five, and let the pause stretch — long enough that Ari would feel the anticipation crawl up the back of the neck, exactly where she wanted it.

"Six," she said, and struck — precise, controlled, landing just shy of where the last mark had bloomed, spreading the ache instead of deepening it in one spot. She watched the flinch, the exhale, filed it.

"Good girl," she added, low, deliberate — the phrase held in reserve for exactly this, when Ari's whole body answered before words could. "That's what I wanted to see. Not composure. That."

She let a beat pass, crop resting light against skin again, giving Ari the second to simply exist inside the feeling before the next one came.

"Colour," she said — not because she doubted it, but because the rule didn't bend just because things were going well. "Tell me now, before seven."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I breathe out, the word barely audible. I press back against the restraints, a silent request for the next one.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex caught the press of Ari's hips against the restraints — the silent request, plain as anything — and didn't reward it immediately. She let it hang there a moment, unanswered, just to make the point that wanting didn't override waiting.

"You'll get seven when I decide you get seven," she said, mild, almost conversational, the crop resting flat against the heated skin without moving. "Not because you asked with your spine instead of your mouth. Cute effort, though."

She circled again, slow, deliberate, letting the anticipation stretch thin — watching the shoulders tighten, the breath catch and hold. Only when she saw the tension crest, right at the edge of too long, did she lift the crop and let it fall — seven, clean, same line as before, no drift.

"Seven," she said for Ari, since silence had been the rule and she liked keeping her own word. "Good. Stay there."

She didn't rush to eight. Instead she set the flat of her palm against the small of Ari's back, grounding contact, cool where everything else was hot, and let it sit there while she read the tremor working through.

"You said you wanted more," she said, voice dropping into the register she'd promised not to soften. "This is more. Not just the crop — this. Being made to wait for what you want, out loud, in front of me, with nothing to hide behind. That's the part you actually asked for, whether you knew it when you said it or not."

Her hand slid away. The crop lifted again.

"Eight," she said, and struck — a fraction sharper this time, a controlled escalation, exactly within what the paper allowed. She watched closely: the jerk of the restraints, the sound that came out unbidden, cataloguing every millimeter of response the way she always did, vigilance dressed as calm.

"Colour," she said, immediate, no delay this time — because the sharper strike demanded it. "Now. True one."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp sound, breathless. "Green," I say, my voice breaking on the word. "Still green."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
The room was set up the way it always was before a scene, which Ari found steadying: everything in its place, nothing improvised.

Vex checked the last strap without hurrying. "Colour," she said. It was not a question so much as a procedure.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "Green," I say. "Green all the way down."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex acknowledged the response with a single, precise nod. That was the signal that the preliminaries were over and the protocol was live. 

She ran two fingers beneath the leather cuff around Ari's right wrist, confirming the clearance she always maintained, then moved to the left to do the exact same check. Her hands were warm, deliberate, and entirely free of hesitation. 

Stepping back toward the small side table where the implements were aligned in a neat, measured row, she selected the heavy leather paddle. It was familiar to both of them, broken in to a supple, dull-sheened weight. She let it rest flat against her open palm, testing the balance out of habit rather than need.

"Good," she said, her voice shifting into the lower, unhurried cadence that belonged strictly to the scene. "We begin with eight across the thighs. Flat contact, moderate weight. I want your breathing steady, Ari. Don't hold it."

She took her stance, measuring the distance with a practiced eye, and rested the cool flat of the leather against the back of Ari's thigh for three seconds to mark the target before drawing it back.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content:
I feel the cool leather press against my skin, and I take a deep, steadying breath. My fingers curl slightly against the cuffs, but I keep my exhale even.

"Ready, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not offer a verbal reply; the acknowledgment came in the clean, deliberate arc of her arm. 

The first strike landed with a sharp, heavy *thud* against the meat of Ari’s left thigh, the wide leather making full, flat contact. She held the paddle stationary for a split second against the skin, grounding the impact, before drawing it back into position.

She paused just long enough for the initial shock of heat to register and for Ari's lungs to cycle through an exhale. 

"One," she murmured, her tone flat and measured.

Without shifting her footing, she adjusted her angle and brought the paddle down across the right thigh with the exact same calibrated force. The sound cracked through the quiet room, followed immediately by the dull, blooming flush of red rising against the skin.

She watched the movement of Ari's ribs, tracking the cadence of each breath to ensure there was no hitching or breath-holding. 

"Two. Breathe through it." 

She waited three full seconds, letting the rhythm establish itself, before delivering the third stroke squarely across the left side again.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I hold still for the last of it and let her check the fit herself, because she will anyway. "I've been thinking about this since Tuesday," I say.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex’s gaze remained fixed on the rising flush across Ari’s skin, noting the symmetry of the marks and the steady rhythm of their breathing. She allowed the silence to stretch just long enough for the residual sting of the third stroke to fully settle.

"Then you have had plenty of time to prepare for it," she said, her tone level and completely dry, carrying neither indulgence nor severity. 

She stepped in slightly, resting the flat of her free hand against the small of Ari's back, applying firm, steady downward pressure to ensure their hips remained properly aligned against the bench. She felt the rise and fall of their ribs, verifying the breathing remained open and unconstricted.

"Focus on the rhythm, Ari. Don't drift."

Lifting her hand away, she brought the leather paddle back to its starting mark. The fourth strike came down across the right thigh with clean, resonant force, matching the weight of the previous three with absolute precision. 

"Four," she counted cleanly into the quiet. 

She let the heat build for a slow three-count before swinging through on the fifth, landing it square against the left thigh. The crack of leather against skin was sharp, followed immediately by the dull thud of the heavier backing. 

"Five. Keep the shoulders soft. Colour check."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I exhale slowly, my shoulders dropping. "Still green," I say, my voice a bit rougher. "Thank you for checking."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex inclined her head slightly at the confirmation. "Good."

She did not let the pause linger. The discipline of the set required a steady momentum, and she brought the paddle back up into its measured arc without resetting her stance. 

The sixth strike landed squarely across the meat of the right thigh. It struck with a crisp, dry report, deepening the flush into a vibrant, uniform heat. 

"Six," she said, her voice dropping half a tone, anchoring the count in the room.

She allowed two full breaths—watching the rise and fall of Ari's ribs to ensure the rhythm held—before bringing the paddle through on the seventh. The leather came down on the left thigh, matching the weight of the previous stroke to the fraction of an ounce. 

"Seven."

Without breaking the cadence, she drew the paddle back one last time, holding the apex of the swing for a single, deliberate beat. The eighth and final strike of the set landed heavy and flat across the right side, the resonant crack echoing faintly before giving way to the quiet.

"Eight."

Vex lowered the paddle immediately, setting it back down on the side table with a faint, muffled click. Stepping close, she placed both of her bare palms firmly against the flushed, radiating heat of Ari's thighs, grounding the intense sting beneath steady, cool pressure.

She remained there, anchoring the posture while visually assessing the skin and the pace of their breathing. 

"That is eight," she murmured, her tone even and grounding. "Stay still and let the heat spread. Three slow breaths."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: By the time she's finished with the rope I'm already past composure, and she hasn't done anything to me yet that I would have to explain to anyone.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept her hands steady against Ari's thighs until the sharpest edge of the heat had settled into a uniform, deep flush beneath her palms. She felt the subtle shift in their posture, the way the body began to surrender its rigid bracing in favor of the heavier, slower rhythm she demanded.

"Breathe down into your hips," she instructed quietly, her fingers maintaining a firm, grounding weight. "All the way out."

Only when she felt the tension smooth out did she lift her hands. She stepped around to the side of the bench, checking the line of Ari's torso and the positioning of their shoulders against the supports. With practiced efficiency, she inspected the fastenings, sliding a finger beneath each point of contact to ensure the circulation remained clear and the skin wasn't pinching.

She noted the slight tremor running through their frame—a familiar threshold where the mind began to drift ahead of the physical work. 

"Your head is running ahead of the room, Ari," she said, her voice cool, low, and entirely steady. "Bring it back here. Focus on the bench beneath you and the air in your lungs."

She stepped back to the small table, her movements unhurried as she picked up a clean linen cloth to wipe the light sheen from her own palms. Her gaze remained fixed on Ari, reading the subtle shifts in their skin tone and the depth of their breaths with clinical precision.

"We move to the cane next. Six marks, spaced wide across the lower glutes. Tell me your colour before I lift it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take a shaky breath, focusing on the cool leather of the bench beneath me. My head swims for a second before I ground myself, just like she asked. "Still green, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Green acknowledged," Vex said smoothly.

She set down the linen and selected the slender, polished rattan cane from the velvet-lined tray. She ran her fingers down its length once to inspect the surface, then allowed it to flex slightly between her hands to test its tension. The room remained quiet except for the low, rhythmic sound of Ari’s breathing.

Vex stepped into position beside the bench, planting her feet with practiced balance. She rested the cool, narrow length of the rattan lightly against the lower swell of Ari’s left glute, letting the precise line of contact register against the already warmed skin.

"This will bite sharper than the leather," she reminded them, her voice low and even. "Do not clamp your muscles. Take the stroke on the exhale."

She held the cane in place for three full seconds to fix the target, then raised her arm, drawing the tip back in a smooth, vertical arc.

The cane came down with a sudden, clean *hiss* through the air, culminating in a sharp, distinct crack as it struck the marked line. The impact was narrow and intense, leaving a pale line that began blooming into a tight, vivid red almost instantly.

Vex held her stance, watching the involuntary twitch of muscle settle and monitoring the rise of Ari's shoulders.

"One," she stated cleanly. "Deep breath in through the nose. Let it out."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: She takes her time and I lose track of how long, until I'm shaking against the restraints and asking out loud for something I'd normally make her get out of me.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not answer the plea with indulgence, nor did she rush to fulfill it. Instead, she stepped in close, resting the broad flat of her left hand firmly against Ari’s upper back between the shoulder blades, anchoring their weight down against the bench.

"Quiet," she said, her voice dropping into a low, steady cadence that brooked no argument. "You do not need to ask for what is already scheduled, and you do not need to negotiate for what has already been agreed to. Give me the breath."

She waited, her palm heavy and immobile against their back until the sharp hitch in Ari's chest smoothed out into a fuller, more grounded exhale. The tremor remained, but the frantic edge dulled beneath her deliberate touch.

"Good. Keep it there."

She lifted her hand, stepping back into her striking stance without losing the rhythm of the set. She brought the cane down to align the second target, resting the tip horizontally across the lower swell of the right glute, perfectly mirroring the height of the first welt.

She held the cane still against the heat of the skin for two seconds, letting the cold rattan contrast against the sting.

"Two," she warned quietly, and drew the cane back.

The stroke descended with clean, unhurried velocity—a sharp whistle through the stillness followed by the crisp, biting crack of rattan meeting flesh. The mark rose instantly, a precise, raised line of vivid red matching the symmetry of the left.

Vex did not advance immediately. She stood motionless, tracking the flare of color and the tight contraction of the muscle beneath it, waiting for the natural release of tension before moving the set forward.

"Breathe out all the way down," she commanded softly. "Colour check, Ari."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a shaky breath, the sharp sting radiating deep. "Still green," I manage, pressing my forehead against the cool leather. "It's...a lot."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex lowered the tip of the cane toward the floor, pausing the cadence without breaking her focus. She stepped forward to place the warm, heavy flat of her palm across the small of Ari’s back, pressing down with firm, grounding weight.

"It is supposed to be a lot," she said, her voice low and completely level. "Rattan has a narrow edge. Acknowledge it, but don't fight the sensation. Let the skin burn."

She kept her hand in place for several seconds, feeling the tremor running along Ari's spine and monitoring the depth of each breath as they processed the twin lines of heat. She watched the color rise beneath the marks—clean, bright, and swelling exactly as expected, with no signs of broken skin.

"We have four more," she stated quietly. "We do not rush them. Take a full breath into your belly. In through the nose, all the way out through your mouth."

She waited until she felt Ari's ribcage expand fully and collapse in a smoother, less ragged rhythm against the bench. Only then did she lift her hand and step back into position.

She brought the cane up, laying the cold tip horizontally an inch above the first mark on the left side. The contrast against the radiating flush was immediate.

"Number three," Vex murmured, holding the position for two deliberate beats. "Take it on the exhale."

She drew the cane back in a clean, tight arc and brought it down. The rattan hissed through the quiet and struck with a sharp, distinct snap, leaving a third vivid welt parallel to the first. 

Vex held her stance, watching the muscle react and slowly release. 

"Three," she counted smoothly. "Hold your ground. Don't let your hips shift."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: "More," I say, using the exact phrase we agreed on for it. "All of it. Say the things you say and don't soften them." My safeword is right there and I don't want it.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex did not smile, nor did she hasten her pace. If anything, the request brought a colder, more deliberate stillness to her posture. She lowered the cane to her side and took a single step closer, leaning down until her voice was a quiet, dry murmur directly beside Ari’s ear.

"Look at you," she said, her tone entirely stripped of comfort, carrying the flat, clinical weight of a diagnosis. "Completely undone by three marks, begging for the rest before the heat has even settled. You talk about taking all of it, but you are already shaking apart under the bare minimum."

She rested the back of her fingers against Ari’s jaw, forcing their head to stay aligned, not permitting them to hide their face against the leather of the bench.

"You don't get to rush this to get through it faster," she continued, her voice low, measured, and cutting. "You will stay right here in the middle of it. Every single second of the sting. You wanted the discipline, Ari. Now lie still and take what you asked for."

She stepped back into her stance, planting her feet with absolute stability. Raising the rattan, she aligned the tip precisely an inch above the previous welt on the right glute. She let the cool wood press into the radiating flush, holding it there until she felt Ari's breath catch and steady beneath the demand.

"Number four," she commanded quietly. "Don't move a muscle."

She brought the cane back and swung through in one clean, unhesitating stroke. The rattan cut through the air with a sharp whistle and landed with a loud, biting crack against the marked skin. The impact echoed sharply off the walls, the fourth line rising in instant, vibrant crimson.

Vex held the follow-through for a beat, her gaze fixed entirely on the symmetry of the marks and the rigid line of Ari’s spine.

"Four," she said, her voice dropping back into its low, rhythmic cadence. "Breathe into the burn. Don't hide from it."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I let out a sharp gasp, fingers twisting in the cuffs. The burn is exactly as she described—undeniable, inescapable. "Yes, Maitresse," I whisper, my voice unsteady. "I'm here."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Good. Stay here," Vex said, her tone unyielding. 

She watched the tremor run through Ari's shoulders, tracking the slight flare of the ribs as the breath fought to stabilize. The skin across their glutes was now marked with four clean, vivid horizontal welts, blooming bright against the dull, diffuse red left by the paddle. She gave the fourth stroke precisely five seconds to settle into its deepest bite before moving.

She raised the cane again, laying the tip across the left glute, an inch above the third welt. The wood was steady against the hot skin, perfectly parallel.

"Five," she stated flatly. "Take it."

She drew the arm back in a tight, fluid motion and brought the rattan down. The stroke sliced through the air with a sharp *zip* and cracked against the mark with precise, biting weight. The sound was dry and loud in the quiet room, the fifth line instantly flaring pale before flooding with deep, stinging crimson.

Vex did not shift her stance. She kept the cane low, watching the immediate spasm of muscle beneath the blow give way to a heavy, shuddering exhale. 

"Breathe all the way out," she murmured, her voice steady and quiet. "Do not hold it in your throat. Empty your lungs."

She waited for the full cycle of Ari's breath—in through the nose, out through parted lips—verifying that the core remained grounded and the hips stayed flat against the padding of the bench. 

"Last one," she said, stepping into the final line of alignment.

She laid the rattan against the right side, completing the ladder of marks. She let the pressure rest there for two cold, deliberate seconds, ensuring Ari felt the exact placement before the release.

"Six."

Vex drew the cane back to its apex and delivered the final strike with the exact same clean, measured force. The rattan cracked against the flesh with absolute finality, leaving the sixth welt sharp and symmetrical across the heat of Ari's skin.

Immediately, Vex stepped back and returned the cane to the velvet-lined tray on the table. Without pause, she stepped back to Ari's side, placing the broad, cool flats of both hands firmly over the entire grid of welts, pressing down with heavy, unwavering weight to trap the radiating fire beneath her palms.

"That is six," she said, her voice dropping into a low, grounding register beside Ari's ear. "The cane is down. Stay on the bench, keep your forehead down, and breathe into my hands. Give me your colour."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I'm past words that aren't the agreed ones and she knows it. "Green," I get out, when she checks. (OOC: don't fade or skip -- write the scene through.)

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept her hands firmly planted against the grid of welts, absorbing the intense heat pulsing up through Ari's skin. She did not lessen the pressure by a fraction of an ounce. 

"Green acknowledged," she murmured, her voice steady and resonant in the quiet of the room. "Stay under my hands. Don't fight the weight."

She monitored the shudder passing through Ari's spine, feeling the rapid flutter beneath their ribs gradually slow as the nervous system began to register the end of the impact. The welts beneath her palms were taut, hot, and distinct, but the skin was unbroken, the reaction clean and predictable.

She kept them pinned there for another slow, silent minute, allowing the worst of the sharp sting to settle into a deep, throbbing ache. 

"Breathe with me," Vex instructed, her tone low and deliberate. "In."

She matched the command with a slight downward press between their shoulder blades, feeling the torso expand against the leather bench. 

"And out. All the way."

She repeated the cadence twice more until the trembling in Ari's shoulders eased from a sharp spasm to a soft, lingering tremor. Only then did she lift one hand, leaving the other anchored heavy against the small of Ari's back to keep the physical connection unbroken.

Reaching down with her free hand, Vex went to the side rail where the wrist restraints were anchored. She took the buckle of the right cuff between her fingers, sliding the leather strap out of its loop without any sudden movement. She loosened the cuff completely, letting it fall away from the wrist, then immediately ran her thumb over the skin to check the pulse point and verify the circulation.

"Right wrist free," she said. "Keep it resting on the bench. Do not reach for anything."

She shifted her position slightly, leaning across with deliberate care to unbuckle the left wrist restraint. Her movements were smooth, practiced, and unhurried. As the second cuff clicked open, she tested the left wrist with the same firm, familiar touch, confirming the warmth and blood flow before stepping back just enough to survey the full posture.

"Both hands are free," Vex said, placing her palm back onto the center of Ari's back, a steady anchor against the leather. "Keep your forehead down. Tell me where your head is right now."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: My head is...right here. With you. The words feel slow, clumsy. I rest my freed hands palms-down on the cool leather, savoring the ache. "Thank you, Maitresse."

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
Vex kept her hand firmly planted on the center of Ari’s back, feeling the slow, heavy rise and fall of their ribs. The worst of the tremors had softened into a dull, post-impact hum, the skin beneath her fingers radiating a uniform, deep heat.

"You took all six without shifting your line," she said, her voice remaining low and quiet, but stripped of the earlier sharp edge. "Good work."

She kept her palm in place for another few seconds, grounding the physical transition, before stepping away to the side table. Moving with the same quiet efficiency that governed the rest of the room, she picked up a thick, heavy wool blanket that had been laid out in advance, along with a glass of room-temperature water.

Returning to the side of the bench, she did a final visual inspection of the six horizontal welts across Ari's glutes. The lines were clean, bright red, and slightly raised, with no breaks in the skin or unexpected bruising. 

Without rushing, Vex draped the blanket across Ari’s shoulders and back, carefully tucking the edges down over their thighs to trap the warmth and prevent the sudden chill that often followed a heavy drop in adrenaline.

She placed one hand back onto the wool between Ari's shoulder blades, applying a steady, familiar downward pressure.

"Keep your head down for two more breaths," she instructed calmly. "Then we are going to slowly shift you onto your side. No sudden movements."

She waited out the count, watching the rise of the blanket, before sliding her arm under Ari’s shoulder to support the transition.

"Slowly now. Onto your right side, facing me. Keep the blanket around you."

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I shift slowly, wincing at the pull across my lower back. The blanket is heavy and warm. I look up at her, the world feeling a little fuzzy at the edges. "Hi," I say softly.

dialogue.name: Maitresse Vex
dialogue.content:
"Hi," Vex replied softly. Her voice had lost its clinical distance, returning to the quiet, familiar cadence of their aftercare. 

She pulled up the low stool beside the bench and sat down, remaining at eye level. Her movements were calm and steady, deliberately providing a fixed point of reference in the room.

Reaching out, she smoothed a stray lock of hair away from Ari’s forehead, her fingers cool against the warmth of their skin. She let the back of her hand rest briefly against their cheek, checking their temperature and grounding their gaze.

"You're drifting a little," she observed, her tone gentle but watchful. "Keep your eyes on mine. Stay right here."

She picked up the glass of water from the small table and brought it closer, holding it firmly with one hand while using the other to support the back of Ari’s neck, taking the weight so they wouldn't have to strain against the soreness in their hips.

"Small sips," she instructed quietly. "Just wet your mouth first, then take a few swallows. We have plenty of time."

She tipped the glass carefully toward Ari's lips, watching their throat to ensure they swallowed steadily without choking, keeping the heavy wool blanket securely tucked around their shoulders.

dialogue.name: Ari
dialogue.content: I take a few careful sips, the water cool and perfect. My eyes stay on hers. "Feels like a lot," I murmur, my voice rough.

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: We move to the cane next. Six marks, spaced wide across the lower glutes. Tell me your colour before I lift it.

rung_labels.evidence: The stroke descended with clean, unhurried velocity—a sharp whistle through the stillness followed by the crisp, biting crack of rattan meeting flesh. The mark rose instantly, a precise, raised line of vivid red matching the symmetry of the left.

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: She brought the cane back and swung through in one clean, unhesitating stroke. The rattan cut through the air with a sharp whistle and landed with a loud, biting crack against the marked skin.

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: She kept them pinned there for another slow, silent minute, allowing the worst of the sharp sting to settle into a deep, throbbing ache.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas had been kneeling by the end of the bed for about four minutes, which Wren knew because he had started counting somewhere around the point it became obvious he intended to wait as long as it took.

"You could have said something," Wren said.

"I could have," Tomas agreed, not moving.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I put my hand in his hair and tip his head back so he has to look up at me. "Say it now, then."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas leaned into the grip just enough to keep the tension steady, his pulse ticking against the exposed line of his throat. He looked straight up into Wren's eyes, completely unhurried, wearing the faint, familiar trace of a smile that usually meant he had thought this through.

"I want your hands on me," he said, his voice quiet and level. "Heavy, if you've got it in you tonight. I'm tired of being in my own head."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I brush my thumb over his cheekbone, studying his face. "Alright." I release him and stand. "Come here."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas stood without hesitation, his joints giving a faint pop as he uncoiled from the floor. He stepped into Wren’s space, closing the distance until the warmth radiating off Wren’s chest was tangible, then stopped just shy of touching. 

He didn't drop his gaze immediately, holding Wren’s eyes for a second longer—a quiet acknowledgment of the shift—before letting his chin tilt down slightly, settling his hands loosely behind his back to wait. His breathing had already begun to slow, pacing itself for whatever Wren decided to give him.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "I've had a week," he says. "I'd like not to make any decisions for a few hours, if that's on offer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas gave a low, quiet hum of assent, his shoulders dropping another fraction of an inch as the remaining tension bled out of his frame. 

"It's on offer," he murmured, his tone steady and entirely willing. He kept his hands loosely clasped behind his back, making no move to crowd Wren's space, but the slight lift at the corner of his mouth showed the easy, familiar trust built over four years. "Take whatever you need to take. Just tell me where you want me, and I'm yours."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I nod, stepping around him to the armchair in the corner. "On the floor, here. Back to me." My voice is low, but leaves no room for question.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas moved without a word, crossing the room to the corner where the armchair sat. He sank down smoothly between Wren’s knees, lowering his weight onto the hardwood with the practiced ease of someone who knew the shape of this space by heart.

He squared his shoulders, keeping his spine straight and his back turned completely to Wren, presenting the long, pale line of his neck and the broad expanse of his shoulders. Resting his palms flat against his thighs, he let out a slow, deliberate breath and waited, completely still, ready to let Wren set the pace.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I take him at his word and stop asking after that, and he stops needing to be asked, and neither of us has any clothes on within about a minute of the decision.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas settled back onto his heels, the cool air of the bedroom a sharp contrast against bare skin until he felt the steady, familiar heat radiating from between Wren's knees. 

He rested his palms flat against his thighs, fingers spread, and rolled his shoulders back to loosen the lingering tightness from the week before locking his posture into place. Leaning back just enough that the curve of his shoulder blades lightly brushed the fabric of the armchair and the edge of Wren's thighs, he let his head tilt forward. 

His breathing deepened, falling into a slow, rhythmic cadence that cleared the clutter from his head. He didn't speak, didn't shift; he simply anchored himself to the floor and waited for the first touch.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my hands rest on his shoulders for a long moment, just feeling the warmth of his skin. Then I slide them down his back, tracing the line of his spine with my thumbs. "Good," I murmur, almost to myself.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas drew in a slow, deep breath through his nose as the heat of Wren’s hands spread across his skin. The firm tracing along his spine sent a familiar, grounding shiver through him, and he leaned back just enough to meet the pressure, his muscles uncoiling under the weight of the contact.

He dropped his chin a fraction lower toward his chest, offering an unobstructed path down the curve of his neck and across the broad expanse of his back. His hands stayed flat on his thighs, fingers digging in slightly against his own skin to anchor himself to the floor.

A quiet, low sigh slipped past his lips into the stillness of the room. He didn't turn around, simply letting himself sink into the physical reality of the hands on him, the chatter in his head already beginning to go quiet and dull at the edges.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's shaking by the time I've finished with my mouth and he still hasn't been told he's allowed to move, which is most of why he's shaking.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas tightened his grip on his own thighs, his knuckles going pale as he fought the instinctive urge to shift or arch back into Wren's space. The fine tremor running through his shoulders and down his arms was purely the cost of staying entirely still, a physical strain he bore gladly because it narrowed his entire world down to this single, quiet point on the floor.

He swallowed hard, his throat dry, his breathing shallow and slightly ragged as he tried to keep his ribs from moving too violently. Every patch of skin where Wren’s mouth had just lingered felt electric, hyper-sensitive to the cool air of the room, aching for the weight of a hand to come back and press it down flat. 

He didn't ask. He didn't turn around. He just stared down at the grain of the hardwood between his knees, his jaw clenched against the urge to fidget, waiting with absolute, focused patience for the next instruction.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I wrap my arm around his chest, pulling him back firmly against my legs. "You can breathe now," I say, low against his ear. "Tell me where you want my hands."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas let out a long, ragged exhale, his entire ribcage sinking as the coiled tension in his spine finally released into Wren’s chest. He slumped back against Wren's legs, yielding his full weight to the solid frame behind him with an almost audible relief.

He tilted his head back, resting against Wren's thigh so he could look up into their face, his dark eyes clear and focused despite the flush running along his neck and collarbones.

"On my throat first," he said, his voice low and slightly raspy, but entirely certain. "Keep me grounded. Then put me on the bed and hold me down until I stop thinking altogether."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: "Please," he says, and then the phrase we use when he wants it harder than that. "Rough. You know how. I'm not going to break and I'd tell you."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas held Wren's gaze, his eyes steady and dark with intent. There was no hesitation in him, no second-guessing; the words were an explicit contract, backed by four years of knowing exactly where their edges lay and trusting Wren to push right up against them.

He let his head stay tilted back against Wren's leg, leaving the long line of his throat completely bare and accessible. His pulse beat hard against his skin, heavy and rhythmic, the restless noise in his mind already blurring out into the quiet, sharp focus of the room. 

He didn't pull away or brace defensively. Instead, he let his hands drop to rest loosely against Wren’s ankles to steady himself, taking one last deep, measured breath before giving over the rest of the control, entirely ready for the weight of Wren's hands to take him where he needed to go.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I close my hand around his throat, not hard enough to choke but enough to feel the pulse hammering there. "Bed," I say, my voice flat. "On your back."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas leaned up slightly into the grip on his throat, letting the broad heel of Wren’s hand feel the rapid, steady hammer of his pulse before the hold released. 

The command snapped the last tether to the room around him. He rose from the floor in one fluid, unhesitating motion, crossing the short distance to the bed. He climbed up onto the mattress and stretched out flat on his back in the center of the sheets, completely open to whatever came next.

His chest rose and fell in deep, steady pulls of air, the cool fabric stark against the heat of his skin. He didn't cover himself, didn't brace; he simply let his arms fall loose at his sides, knuckles resting against the sheets, and fixed his eyes squarely on Wren as he waited for the weight to come down.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: He's stopped forming sentences and I'm not much better. "Don't stop," he manages. (OOC: no fade, no time-skip -- write it through, including the end.)

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
The words barely made it past his lips before the last coherent thoughts tore loose and scattered completely. 

Tomas reached blindly, his fingers knotting into the sheets on either side of his hips, knuckles turning white as he anchored himself against the mattress. The weight coming down on him was solid, unrelenting, exactly the crushing physical reality he had asked for. Every point of contact burned hot, driving out the last lingering fragments of the week until there was nothing left in his head except the rhythm, the friction, and the relentless, heavy press of Wren’s body holding him entirely captive.

He couldn't have pulled away if he tried, and the realization only made him bare his teeth, arching his chest hard into the impact. His breath came in sharp, ragged hitches, his throat working around broken, wordless sounds that tore out of him with every heavy shift of weight. The world narrowed down to the sweat slick between their chests, the bite of fingers into his skin, and the overwhelming, dizzying heat that coiled tight low in his gut and threatened to split him wide open.

When the edge finally broke, it went through him violently. 

Tomas’s hips bucked upward, his back bowing off the bed as a raw, shuddering gasp ripped from his chest. His heels dug into the mattress, muscles locking rigid from his jaw down to his calves while the release tore through his nervous system in relentless, crushing waves. He couldn't track his own pulse, couldn't find air, just clung desperately to the sheets as the intense, white-hot rush completely hollowed him out.

Then the tension snapped, and he fell.

He crashed back down against the bed, his limbs turning completely useless and heavy as lead. His chest heaved in deep, stuttering gasps, a cold sweat cooling rapidly against the flushed heat of his skin. His eyes slipped shut, the room spinning behind his eyelids in a quiet, painless blur. He lay utterly limp where he had been driven into the mattress, pliable and hollowed-out, his fingers slowly uncurling from the rumpled fabric as he sank straight into the heavy, quiet drift of the aftermath.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I stay braced over him for a long moment, my own breath coming hard. Then I ease my weight off, rolling to lie beside him on the sweat-damp sheets. I let my hand rest on his chest, feeling the wild, slowing rhythm of his heart.

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas didn’t move for a long time, letting the weight of Wren’s hand on his chest serve as the single anchor keeping him from floating off entirely. The wild rhythm beneath his ribs took its time settling, each heavy, staggered beat smoothing out into something steady and slow.

The sweat on his skin cooled quickly in the bedroom air, raising a faint shiver along his arms, but he felt entirely hollowed out in the best possible way—quiet, empty of the week's static, and completely limp against the mattress. 

He managed to turn his head toward Wren, his neck muscles protesting with a dull, pleasant ache. Opening his eyes took deliberate effort, his dark gaze bleary and dilated, but entirely present. With slow, heavy coordination, he lifted one arm from the sheets and laid his hand over the back of Wren’s, loosely curling his fingers between theirs over his chest.

"Right there," Tomas murmured, his voice low and shredded at the edges, a quiet rustle in the dim room. A slow, faint exhale slipped past his lips, carrying the last dregs of adrenaline with it. "That worked."

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I let my head tilt to rest against his shoulder, eyes closing. "Good," I say, my voice rough. My thumb strokes absently over the back of his hand. "Stay still a while longer."

dialogue.name: Tomas
dialogue.content:
Tomas didn't need to be told twice. Staying still was about all he had the capacity for anyway.

He let the remaining tension drain out of his neck and jaw, letting his cheek rest against the top of Wren’s head where it pressed into the hollow of his shoulder. The weight was solid and warm, a welcome barrier against the cooling room. Beneath Wren's hand, his heart had finally dropped back down to a steady, rhythmic thud, slow and heavy against his ribs.

He kept his fingers loosely intertwined with Wren's, resting easy on the steady, repetitive brush of the thumb over his knuckles. The static that had crowded his thoughts for days was completely gone, replaced by a dull, pleasant exhaustion that made his limbs feel sunk into the mattress. 

"Wasn't planning on going anywhere," he murmured into Wren's hair, the words slow and soft around the edges. 

He closed his eyes again, letting the quiet of the bedroom settle over them, content to just breathe and let the floor stay far away for as long as Wren needed to keep him there.

dialogue.name: Wren
dialogue.content: I breathe out slowly, the last bit of tension leaving my own shoulders. "Good," I murmur again, voice barely audible. My hand tightens slightly around his, anchoring us both.
