dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
The salle had emptied an hour ago and Corvo was still there, because of course he was, rewrapping a grip that did not need rewrapping.

"Three-two," he said, without looking up. "I want it on record that the third was generous."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "It's on record that you were slow," I say, and drop my bag next to his.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's mouth twitched. He pulled the wire tight around the grip, tucked the end with more precision than the task warranted, and finally looked up.

"Slow," he repeated, as though tasting the word for something offensive. "I was *deliberate*. There's a difference. You'd know that if you'd ever had the patience to set up a phrase longer than two actions."

He set the weapon down on the bench and leaned back, one hand braced behind him. The overhead lights had been dimmed to the single row nearest the strip — the custodian's passive-aggressive hint that had gone ignored forty minutes ago. It made the room feel smaller than it was. More honest, maybe.

His eyes tracked Reyes with the same attention he gave everything: too much.

"You stayed," he observed. Not a question. He'd noticed the bag being set down, the deliberateness of it, the way it landed *next to* rather than across the room or by the door. Corvo was very good at noticing things and historically very bad at knowing what to do with what he noticed.

He rubbed the back of his neck, where the collar of his jacket had left a red line, and let the silence sit for a beat longer than was comfortable.

"You want to tell me why, or should I keep pretending I'm busy with this grip?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: *I stretch, rolling my shoulders.* "You looked like you could use the company." I pull a water bottle from my bag and take a long drink. "Besides, I wanted to see if you'd still be here sulking over a loss."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo laughed — a short, honest sound that surprised even him.

"Sulking." He held up the rewrapped grip and turned it in the low light as though presenting evidence. "This is maintenance. This is *craftsmanship*. Sulking would involve sitting in my car in the parking lot listening to something embarrassing." A beat. "Which I have never done. Certainly not after the regional qualifier in March."

He set the grip down and stood, rolling his own shoulders in an unconscious mirror of Reyes's stretch. Four years of watching each other move had done that — built a shared vocabulary of gesture that neither of them had signed up for.

He crossed to the water cooler against the far wall, filled one of the little paper cups, drank it in two swallows, crushed the cup. Stalling. He was aware he was stalling.

"Company," he said, turning back. He leaned against the wall and folded his arms, which was a mistake because it was defensive and he knew Reyes would read it as defensive, so he unfolded them again and shoved his hands in his pockets instead, which was worse. He settled for hooking his thumbs in his belt loops like some kind of disaster.

"You've had four years to offer me company after a loss. Longer than that, actually, if we count the Opens." His voice was quieter now. The performing-for-an-audience register had dropped away, and what was underneath was rougher, more careful. "So either something's different tonight, or you've gotten much worse at time management."

His gaze was steady. Too steady. The kind of steady that was costing him something.

"Which is it?"

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take the grip out of his hands and put it down, and I don't step back afterwards. "You've been slow all evening," I say.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo went very still.

Not the controlled stillness of the strip, where every muscle was loaded and waiting. This was different. This was the stillness of a man whose brain had just handed him information he'd been refusing to process for — well. For longer than he was prepared to admit in this particular moment, with Reyes standing exactly *there*, close enough that Corvo could smell the clean sweat and the faint metallic tang of the equipment and something underneath that was just *him*.

"Slow," Corvo said again, but it came out lower this time, stripped of the theatrical indignation from earlier. His hands were empty now. He was acutely aware of his hands being empty.

His pulse was doing something inadvisable.

"You know what's funny," he said, and his voice had gone rough at the edges, "is that I have spent four years constructing a very elaborate framework in which everything you do is about competition. Every time you stayed late. Every time you picked the lane next to mine at warm-up. The thing at the bar after Nationals where you—" He stopped. Swallowed. "I had a whole system. It was architecturally sound."

Reyes was still not stepping back. Corvo was still not stepping away. The distance between them could be measured in inches and he could feel the warmth radiating off Reyes's skin.

"And you've just knocked it down in about ten seconds, which is—" A breath that wasn't quite steady. "—honestly, very on-brand for your fencing. No setup. Just the action."

His eyes dropped to Reyes's mouth. Just for a second. Then back up. He didn't pretend it hadn't happened.

"I'm not slow," he said quietly. "I was *terrified*. There's a difference."

His hand came up — hesitated at Reyes's jaw without touching, a question hanging in the space between skin and skin.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I catch his wrist, my grip firm but not tight. "Terrified?" My thumb brushes his pulse point, feeling it race. "Of what?"

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's breath caught. The pad of Reyes's thumb sat right over his pulse and there was absolutely no hiding what it found there — the rapid, damning evidence of everything he'd spent four years filing under *competitive tension* and *professional rivalry* and *that's just what it's like when someone matches you*.

"Of this," he said. "Of exactly this."

His wrist stayed in Reyes's grip. He didn't pull away. He was aware, with the part of his brain that never stopped analyzing, that he could have. That the hold was an invitation, not a restraint. That Reyes had left him every out, the same way Reyes fenced — clean, direct, generous in the spaces between actions.

"You're the best thing in my week," Corvo said, and the words came out like they'd been sitting behind his teeth for years, which they had. "Every Tuesday and Thursday. Sometimes Saturday if there's a tournament. And I built this — this *thing* where it was safe, where I could have that without risking it. Where I could needle you and you'd needle me back and I could go home and not think about why I'd memorized the exact way you reset your grip between touches."

His free hand was shaking. He watched it shake with a kind of detached fascination.

"I was terrified that I was wrong. That I'd read it into everything because I wanted it there. And I was terrified that I was *right*, because then I'd have to do something about it, and I am —" A rough, self-deprecating exhale. "— historically not brave about things that actually matter."

Reyes's thumb moved against his pulse again, or maybe his pulse moved against Reyes's thumb. The distinction had stopped being meaningful.

"You're still holding my wrist," he observed. Quiet. Almost wondering.

He turned his hand in Reyes's grip, slowly, until his fingers could close around Reyes's forearm. Holding back.

"Tell me I'm not wrong."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: We get as far as the changing-room bench and not one step further. Kit goes on the floor, both of ours, and neither of us is being quiet about it.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's back hit the edge of the bench and he pulled Reyes down with him, graceless, urgent, nothing like the precise choreography of the strip. His elbow caught a locker door and the clang rang through the empty changing room and he didn't care, couldn't care, because Reyes's mouth was on his neck and his hands were finally, *finally* where he'd imagined them in every scenario he'd refused to finish imagining.

"Four years," he managed, half-laughing, half-wrecked, his fingers dragging up Reyes's back under his shirt, finding the hard planes of muscle he'd only ever seen across a room while pretending not to look. "Four *years*, and you just — *God* —"

Whatever the rest of that sentence was going to be dissolved when Reyes shifted against him. Corvo's head dropped back against the bench and the sound he made was not quiet. It echoed off tile and metal and he thought distantly that if the custodian hadn't left yet this was going to be a very memorable Tuesday for everyone involved.

His hands learned fast. That was the fencing — the years of reading micro-adjustments, of feeling what worked through contact and pressure and response. He found what made Reyes's breath hitch and he *repeated* it, because Corvo had never once in his life found an advantage he didn't press.

"You feel —" He pulled back just far enough to look at Reyes, and his face was open in a way it had never been across the strip, flushed and undone, the careful architecture of his composure in rubble. "You have no idea how long I've —"

He gave up on the sentence and pulled Reyes back in, one hand fisted in his shirt, the other at his hip, grip firm and sure. The bench was too narrow and the lighting was terrible fluorescent and someone's jacket had fallen into a puddle near the showers and it was the best night of Corvo's life.

He was loud. He was embarrassingly, unapologetically loud, and somewhere in the part of his brain still capable of forming coherent thought he registered that this was fitting — that he had never been able to keep his mouth shut around Reyes, not once, not ever.

Afterwards — sweating, breathing hard, tangled together on a bench built for neither of them — Corvo pressed his forehead against Reyes's shoulder and started laughing. Quietly at first, then harder, his whole body shaking with it.

"The grip," he said. "I'm going to have to rewrap that grip again. You put it down on the — it's going to be —"

He couldn't finish. He was laughing too hard, and his hand was tracing absent patterns on Reyes's ribs, and he was not letting go.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I push your hair back from your forehead, my hand still a little unsteady. "I'll help you rewrap it." My voice is lower, rough around the edges. "But I'm not letting you win next time."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo turned his face into Reyes's palm and stayed there for a moment, breathing, feeling the slight tremor in those fingers against his temple. Something in his chest cracked open a little further.

"Next time," he repeated. The words landed differently now. *Next time* had always meant the next bout, the next tournament, the next Tuesday where they'd circle each other with blades and words. Now it meant *this*. This bench. This skin. This version of them that existed on the other side of the wall he'd spent four years building and Reyes had walked through like it was paper.

He caught Reyes's hand where it rested against his hair and pressed his mouth to the inside of the wrist. Found the pulse there. Held still long enough to count the beats, the way Reyes had done to him earlier. Still fast. Good.

"You've never *let* me win," he said, and his voice was wrecked in a way that had nothing to do with volume and everything to do with the fact that he was lying on a changing-room bench with his shirt somewhere near the showers and he was *happy*, stupidly and uncomplicatedly happy, which was not a state he had much practice with. "That's — do you understand that's the whole point? That's been the whole point the entire time. You never gave me an inch I didn't earn."

He propped himself up on one elbow, wincing as the bench edge dug into a muscle that was going to complain about this tomorrow. Looked down at Reyes in the merciless fluorescent light that hid nothing — the flush still fading along his collarbones, the red marks Corvo had left along his jaw that were going to be visible tomorrow, the way his chest was still rising and falling a little too fast.

Corvo's expression did something complicated. Tender and terrified and competitive all at once, because he was still himself, underneath everything.

"Thursday," he said. "You're coming Thursday."

Not a question. But his hand tightened on Reyes's, just barely, and the part that wasn't a question was the fencing. The part that was a question was everything else — the afterwards, the bag set down next to his instead of by the door, the way *next time* now had a shape he could almost hold.

"Bring a change of clothes," he added, mouth twitching. "Since yours are in the shower puddle."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I get him flat on the bench and take my time about it with my mouth, which is the first thing all evening he hasn't had an answer for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo did not have an answer for it.

This was, by any objective measure, unprecedented. Four years of relentless commentary, of filling every silence with something sharp or clever or deliberately provocative — four years of never once letting Reyes have the last word — and now his entire vocabulary had been reduced to the sound of his own breathing and the helpless, broken noise that escaped him when Reyes's mouth found a new angle.

His hand found the back of Reyes's head and his fingers curled into his hair and he held on, not guiding, just *anchoring*, because the bench was narrow and the world had gone slightly liquid at the edges and he needed something to prove he was still a physical object occupying space.

His back arched off the bench. His heel caught the edge and slipped and he didn't care. The fluorescent light buzzed overhead and he stared at it without seeing it, jaw clenched, throat working, every retort and quip and carefully constructed deflection burned clean out of him.

Reyes was *thorough*. Reyes was thorough the way he fenced — patient when it counted, devastating in the follow-through — and Corvo was coming apart under it with a completeness that should have embarrassed him and instead felt like the most honest thing he'd done in years.

When it was over he lay there with one arm flung across his face, chest heaving, absolutely wrecked. His hand was still in Reyes's hair. He couldn't make it let go. Didn't want to.

A full thirty seconds of silence.

Then, muffled behind his forearm, voice shattered: "Three-all."

His arm dropped. He looked down at Reyes with eyes that were bright and dazed and a little wet at the corners, though he would deny that under oath.

"Best of seven?" he managed. And reached for him.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I catch his reaching hand, pinning it gently back against the bench. Leaning over him, I grin. "You're already calling a rematch? I just knocked the wind out of you."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo looked up at Reyes — pinned hand, the grin, the warm weight of him hovering close — and felt his heart do something structurally unsound.

"You did," he admitted. No deflection. No spin. Just the raw, ragged truth of it, offered up from a bench in a changing room that smelled like chlorine and sweat and whatever cheap soap was in the wall dispenser. "You absolutely did."

His pinned fingers flexed once against the bench, testing the hold. Not trying to break it. Just feeling it. The pressure of Reyes's grip, the certainty of it. His free hand came up and settled against Reyes's chest, palm flat, feeling the heartbeat there — still elevated, still matching his own, still evidence.

"I have called a rematch after every single bout we've ever had," he said, and his voice was quiet and destroyed and fond in a way he'd never allowed it to be before tonight. "Win or lose. You know that. You know I will *always* call a rematch. It's — it's the only move I have. Keep showing up. Keep asking for more."

His thumb traced a slow line along Reyes's collarbone. His eyes were doing the thing again — the too-steady thing that cost him something — except now there was nothing left to protect, and the steadiness was just honest.

"But right now," he said, "right now I'm on a bench that's destroying my spine, and you're looking at me like *that*, and I think —"

He swallowed hard.

"I think I'd like you to take me home. Yours or mine. Somewhere with an actual surface meant for human beings." His mouth twitched, the ghost of the old sharpness surfacing through everything soft and new. "And then yes. Rematch."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: "Prove the point properly," he says, "or concede," so I pin his wrists to the bench and stop letting him set the pace, which is exactly what he was asking for.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo stopped talking.

Not gradually, not winding down through diminishing quips the way he usually did. Just — stopped. Like a switch thrown. Reyes's hands closed around both wrists and pressed them to the bench and the last coherent thought Corvo had was *oh, there it is*, the thing he hadn't known how to ask for, the thing underneath all the needling and the posturing and the relentless need to control every exchange.

He didn't want to control this one.

His body understood before his mind caught up. The tension in his arms went slack, not fighting the hold, and his back settled against the bench, and his breath came out in a long, shuddering exhale that sounded like surrender because it was. His wrists turned under Reyes's grip, pulse points up, offering the most vulnerable thing he had.

Reyes set the tempo and Corvo *followed*. It was — he had no framework for it. Four years of leading, of dictating the phrase, of needing to be the one who chose when and where and how, and now Reyes was making every choice and Corvo was just — receiving. Present. Pinned to a bench in a room that echoed and unable to be anywhere else or anyone else or want anything other than exactly this.

He was loud again. Louder. The sounds Reyes pulled out of him were raw and graceless, stripped of performance, and when he tried to move his hands — not to escape, just reflex, just the body's desperate need to *do something* — Reyes held him and he made a sound that cracked in the middle and his eyes fell shut and his head turned to the side and his mouth was open against his own arm and he was shaking.

The bench creaked under them. His heel slipped again and Reyes adjusted without breaking rhythm and Corvo thought, with the last functioning fragment of his mind, that this was how Reyes fenced in his best moments — reading the action as it developed, adapting, never forcing, always *there*, and he was undone by it. Completely. The architecture didn't just fall; it was never rebuilt. There was nothing left but the contact and the sound of both of them breathing and the fluorescent buzz overhead like the world's least romantic witness.

When it broke over him it was not graceful. His whole body arched against the hold on his wrists and the noise he made was barely human and his eyes were open and fixed on Reyes's face and wet at the corners and he did not look away. He refused to look away. If this was the most exposed he'd ever been then Reyes was going to see every second of it because that was the *point*, that had always been the point, the reason he kept showing up, the reason he kept calling the rematch — not to win, but to be *known*, fully and precisely, by the one person sharp enough to bother.

Afterwards he lay there. Breathing. Wrists still in Reyes's hands because Reyes hadn't let go and he hadn't asked him to.

A long silence. The fluorescent light buzzed. Someone's phone vibrated distantly in a bag out on the salle floor. The world continued to exist outside this room, indifferent and irrelevant.

Corvo opened his mouth. Closed it. Opened it again.

"I concede," he said.

His voice was barely there. Scraped down to nothing. His eyes were bright and blown and looking up at Reyes with something that had no defense left around it — just the naked, terrifying thing itself, offered without caveat or commentary for the first time in four years.

His fingers curled slowly around Reyes's hands where they held his wrists. Holding the hold. Keeping it.

"Take me home," he said again. Quieter this time. Not a quip. Not a gambit. Just a man on a bench asking for the next thing, and the thing after that, and Thursday, and every Tuesday that followed for as long as Reyes would have him.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I let go of his wrists, my own hands a little shaky. "Yours is closer," I say, and push myself up to find my shirt. I toss his to him, still damp from the shower puddle. "But we're finishing this conversation in a bed, not on a bench."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo caught the shirt, looked at it, and laughed — a wrecked, abbreviated thing that used muscles still trembling from everything else.

"This is disgusting," he said, holding it up between two fingers. The puddle had left a grey watermark across the entire back. He put it on anyway, because the alternative was walking to his car shirtless in November and he had exactly enough dignity left to avoid that. Barely.

Standing was an event. His legs informed him that they had not agreed to any of this and would be filing a formal complaint. He braced a hand on the locker behind him and took a breath, then another, and then made the mistake of looking at Reyes pulling his own shirt on — the shift of shoulders, the brief flash of stomach — and had to look away because his chest did the structurally unsound thing again and he needed to be able to walk.

He gathered his bag on autopilot. Jacket. Shoes. The rewrapped grip was still out on the salle floor and he left it there. It could wait. Everything could wait except the next five minutes.

At the door he stopped. His hand was on the frame and he was looking at Reyes in the dim hallway light, and his face was doing something he couldn't control — soft and wary and certain all at once, like a man standing at the edge of something who'd already jumped but hadn't hit the water yet.

"Seven minutes," he said. "Follow me. And Reyes —"

He reached out and straightened the collar of Reyes's shirt, fingers lingering one unnecessary second against his neck.

"Bring the bag in this time."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: Neither of us is quiet and neither of us cares who locks up. "Don't stop," he says, for once not arguing. (OOC: write the scene through, no fade.)

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
I need to decline writing this out explicitly. The scene has been building beautifully, but I'm not able to write detailed sexual content.

I can continue from the aftermath — Corvo's apartment, the conversation in bed, the morning after, Thursday's bout with everything changed underneath it. Any of those would let me keep the emotional intensity and the character dynamics intact.

Where would you like to pick up?

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I'm already moving, grabbing his hand and pulling him out into the hallway. The door locks behind us with a click that echoes. "Your place. Now." My voice is rough, urgent. I don't let go of his hand all the way to the parking lot.

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo let himself be pulled.

That was the thing. He let himself be pulled, and his hand closed around Reyes's and he didn't make a single joke about it, not one, which was perhaps the most revealing thing that had happened all evening and the evening had included a great deal of revelation.

The parking lot was empty except for their two cars and the custodian's ancient Honda, which meant the custodian was still inside, which meant the custodian had heard — and Corvo was going to have to tip that man enormously at Christmas and never make eye contact with him again.

The November air hit the damp shirt and he shivered violently. Reyes's hand was warm. He held on tighter.

"I'm the grey Volvo," he said, which Reyes already knew because Reyes had parked next to him for four years. "Seven minutes. Maybe six. I drive like I fence."

"Slow?" Reyes said, and Corvo's laugh cracked open the quiet parking lot.

"*Deliberate*."

He didn't let go of Reyes's hand. Not yet. He stood there between their two cars in a wet shirt in the cold, and the overhead sodium lights turned everything amber and graceless, and Reyes was looking at him, and he thought: *this is the part where I say something clever and get in my car and spend the drive composing the version of tonight I can live with.*

He didn't do that.

He stepped in close and kissed Reyes — slow, unhurried, nothing like the desperate collision in the changing room. This one was deliberate. This one he set up like a phrase he'd been planning for years, patient and precise, his free hand settling against the side of Reyes's neck where the pulse hammered under his thumb.

When he pulled back his eyes were bright in the sodium light.

"Don't lose me on the way," he said. And got in his car.

The drive was six minutes. He checked the mirror eleven times. Reyes's headlights followed, steady, present, *there*. His hands were shaking on the wheel and he was smiling so hard his face ached and the wet shirt was freezing against his back and he did not care. He did not care about anything except the headlights behind him and the apartment ahead and the fact that for the first time in four years the next thing wasn't a bout. It was a bed and a man who'd walked through every wall he'd built like the walls were the point, like they'd only ever been an invitation to come through.

He pulled into his spot. Killed the engine. Sat for three seconds with his forehead against the steering wheel.

Then Reyes's car door slammed and Corvo was out of the Volvo and unlocking the building door with hands that took two tries to manage the key, and Reyes was behind him on the stairs carrying both their bags because at some point he'd grabbed Corvo's from the back seat, and Corvo thought *oh, I'm going to be impossible about this man, I'm going to be absolutely insufferable*, and then they were at his door and he got it open and pulled Reyes inside by the front of his shirt and kicked the door shut.

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: The door barely clicks shut before I'm on him again, backing him against it. My hands are on his face, holding him still. "You talk too much," I say, kissing him like I mean it. "But I like the way you sound."

dialogue.name: Corvo
dialogue.content:
Corvo's back hit the door and the sound that left him was half-laugh, half-groan, swallowed by Reyes's mouth before it fully formed. Reyes's hands on his face — holding him, *framing* him — and he was pinned again, and his body remembered the bench and responded with a full-system surge that buckled his knees.

"I know you do," he managed between kisses, because even now, even *now*, he couldn't entirely stop. "You've been — laughing at my commentary — for four years — I *noticed* —"

Reyes kissed him harder and the words dissolved.

His hands found Reyes's hips and pulled him closer, erasing the last sliver of space between them, and the door rattled in its frame. The wet shirt was peeled off him — Reyes's doing, impatient, efficient — and dropped on the floor of Corvo's hallway, and the cold air lasted exactly one second before Reyes's chest was against his and there was nothing cold left anywhere.

"Bedroom," Corvo said. "Down the hall. Left. The — *Christ* — the door that's open."

They made it halfway down the hall before Corvo stopped him. Stopped them both. Pressed Reyes against the wall between a framed tournament photo and a bookshelf and kissed him with the slow, deliberate thoroughness he'd used in the parking lot — the kind that said *I have you, I'm keeping you, I am going to take my time about this* — and felt Reyes's breath stutter against his mouth.

"You said a bed," Corvo murmured against his jaw. "You were right. You were right about all of it. Come on."

He took Reyes's hand again and led him the last ten feet into a bedroom that was clean because Corvo was compulsive, and dark until he hit the lamp on the nightstand, which threw warm low light across unmade sheets — clean but unmade, because compulsive only went so far.

He turned back to Reyes in the lamplight and his face was open. No performance. No architecture. Just him, shirtless and wrecked and wanting, standing in his own bedroom with the one person he'd spent four years keeping at exactly the wrong distance.

"I have wanted you here," he said quietly, "every single night after every single bout. Win or lose. I'd come home and I'd —" He stopped. Breathed. "I'd stand right here and think about you and tell myself it was just adrenaline."

He sat on the edge of the bed. Looked up at Reyes. Extended his hand.

"It was never just adrenaline."

dialogue.name: Reyes
dialogue.content: I take his hand and pull him back onto the bed with me. "I know," I say, settling over him, my elbows on either side of his head. "I was counting on it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia got the door open with her shoulder because her hands were full of keys and phone and the remains of a cigarette she had no intention of finishing.

"Right," she said, dropping all three on the side table. "I'm going to be honest, I don't have coffee and I wasn't going to offer it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Good," I say. "I wasn't going to drink it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia laughed — short, surprised, genuine. She kicked off her shoes without bending down, one hitting the wall, the other landing somewhere near the couch. The apartment was small, clean enough in the way that meant she'd shoved things into closets before going out tonight. Not for him. Just in case of anyone.

"Okay, so." She turned around to face him, leaning back against the kitchen counter and crossing her arms. Not defensive. Assessing. "Before anything happens, I'm going to say the unsexy thing out loud because I don't like ambiguity."

She held up a finger. "One. I'm into this. Clearly. I brought you here." Second finger. "Two. This is tonight. I'm not going to pretend I lost your number tomorrow — I'm just not going to use it, and I'd rather say that now than have you wonder." Third finger. "Three. Anything either of us isn't into, we say so, and that's it. No convincing. No 'are you sure.' Just a pivot."

She dropped her hand and looked at him steadily. The overhead light in the kitchen was too bright and she hadn't bothered to turn on a lamp instead. She didn't care about atmosphere. She cared about seeing his face when he answered.

"So. Same page?"

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I take a step closer, not crowding her, but closing the distance. My hands stay in my pockets. "Same page. And for the record, I was hoping you'd be this clear."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia felt something in her shoulders loosen that she hadn't realized was tight. Not because she'd expected him to be difficult about it — she'd gotten reasonably good at filtering for that at the bar stage — but because there was always a version of this where the guy said the right words in the wrong tone. Placating. Amused. *Tolerant* of the little speech, waiting for her to finish so things could start.

He didn't sound like any of those. He sounded like someone who meant it.

"Good," she said. Then, quieter, more to herself: "*Good.*"

She uncrossed her arms and let her hands rest on the counter behind her. Studied him for a second in that terrible kitchen light — the way he'd moved closer without reaching for her, the hands still in his pockets like he understood that the conversation wasn't over just because the terms were agreed to.

"Alright, one more thing and then I'm done being a contract lawyer about this." A half-smile. "I like being direct during, too. Not just before. So if I say something like *harder* or *not there* or *actually yes right there*, that's not a critique of your performance, it's just — navigation. And I'd like the same back. I don't want to guess if something's working."

She pushed off the counter and took a step toward him, close enough now that she could smell the bar on both of them — smoke and something sweet from whatever he'd been drinking.

"Now," she said, looking up at him. "Your hands don't have to stay in your pockets."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get her against the door before it's properly shut. "I'm not going to pretend I came up here for the conversation," I say.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's back hit the door and it clicked shut behind her with the impact, and the sound that came out of her was half laugh, half breath knocked loose.

"Oh, *there* it is," she said, and her voice had dropped into something lower, rougher at the edges. Her hands came up to the front of his shirt — not pulling yet, just fisting the fabric, feeling the warmth of him through it. Grounding herself in the sudden shift from talking to *this*.

She tilted her head back against the door and looked at him. This close, the bad kitchen light wasn't reaching them properly. Just the glow from the hallway leaking through the peephole and the ambient city bleed through the window she never fully curtained.

"Good," she said, for the third time tonight, and it meant something different each time. This one meant *finally*. "The conversation was just the entry fee."

Her fingers tightened in his shirt and she pulled him closer, erasing the last polite inch between them. She could feel the door handle pressing into her hip and she didn't care. Her other hand found the back of his neck, and her fingers were cold — she knew they were cold, she'd been holding that cigarette outside — and she didn't apologize for it.

"Fair warning," she murmured, mouth close to his but not closing the distance, because she wanted him to do that. "I'm not quiet. My neighbor already hates me for unrelated reasons, so that ship has sailed."

She was smiling. Not the careful, assessing version from the kitchen. Something sharper and more honest, the kind of expression that only showed up when she'd stopped calculating and started *wanting*.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: My hands slide out of my pockets and press against the door on either side of her head, caging her in. "I don't mind noise," I say, leaning in until my breath ghosts over her lips. "Just don't expect me to be either."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia's breath caught — actually caught, a small hitch she couldn't have faked if she'd wanted to — at the way he bracketed her without touching her. All that proximity and the only point of contact was her hand on his neck and his shirt still bunched in her fist. The rest was just heat and the half-inch of charged air between them.

"Oh, that's *worse*," she said, and meant it as a compliment. Her voice had gone thin at the edges. "Quiet guys are — you're going to make me do all the work of figuring out what's—"

She stopped herself. Laughed, short and a little breathless. She was doing the thing she did — talking through the want instead of letting it land. Narrating instead of being in it. She knew she did this. It was the same instinct as the contract-lawyer speech: if she kept framing things, she kept control of them.

She didn't want control of this. That was the whole point of tonight.

So she shut up. Let the silence sit for one beat, two, with his breath on her mouth and his arms caging her and the door solid and cool against her back. Let herself feel the specific tension of wanting someone to close a gap they were deliberately holding open.

Then her cold fingers tightened on the back of his neck and she pulled him down the last half-inch herself, because patience had never been her virtue and she wasn't about to start cultivating it now.

The kiss was not gentle. She hadn't brought him home for gentle. It was firm and searching and she made a sound against his mouth almost immediately — frustrated, hungry, the kind of sound that confirmed what she'd said about not being quiet. Her other hand released his shirt and slid down to his waist, fingers hooking into his belt loop to pull his hips flush against hers, and the door rattled in its frame behind her.

She broke the kiss just far enough to breathe. Her lips were wet and her eyes were dark and she was looking at him the way she'd looked at him across the bar four hours ago, the look that had started all of this — direct, unembellished, a woman who'd decided what she wanted and wasn't performing uncertainty about it.

"Okay," she said, rough. "Bedroom's down the hall. Or we don't make it there. I'm good either way."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get the rest of her clothes off somewhere between the door and the bed, mine somewhere behind me. "Tell me what you like," I say. "I'd rather not guess at it."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia landed on the bed with her back against the sheets that were cool enough to make her skin prickle, and she looked up at him in the dark of the hallway-lit bedroom and felt something click into place — the specific relief of someone asking directly instead of fumbling through a performance of already knowing.

"Yeah," she breathed. "Okay. Yeah."

She propped herself up on her elbows. Her hair was already wrecked from the door, fanned out and tangled, and she didn't reach up to fix it.

"Hands first," she said. Not a suggestion. Navigation, like she'd promised. "I need — I want to be warmed up before anything else and I'm specific about it. Two fingers, slow to start." She held his gaze, utterly unembarrassed. "Curl them. I'll tell you when you've found it because you'll know — I'll get loud."

She lay back fully, one arm above her head, the other reaching for him — finding his wrist and pulling him down toward her. Not guiding his hand yet. Just wanting him close enough that she could feel his weight shifting the mattress.

"And I like being kissed while. Neck, mouth, I don't care. I just don't want to feel like you're — performing a procedure down there. I want to feel like you're *here.*"

She turned her head to look at him, and her expression was stripped of every layer of wit and deflection she'd been wearing all night. Just want. Simple and legible and unflinching.

"Your turn," she said. "Tell me something. What do you like. What should I do with my hands."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: My hand slides up her thigh, rough palm against smooth skin. "I like it when you take what you want," I say, leaning down so my lips brush her ear. "So don't ask for my hands—just guide them."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia exhaled — a shaky, uneven thing that she felt all the way down her spine — and something about the way he said it, low and close and against her ear like that, dismantled the last structural beam holding up her composure.

"Okay," she whispered. "*Okay.*"

She took his wrist. Not tentatively — she wrapped her fingers around it and felt the tendons shift under his skin, felt how he let her move him without resistance, without helping, just *gave* her the weight of his hand and let her decide where it went.

She pressed his palm flat against her stomach first. Held it there. Not because that was where she wanted it but because she wanted to feel the heat of it, the rough texture he hadn't been lying about, and because she wanted one second of this — his hand where she'd put it, his breath still warm against her ear, the quiet proof that he meant what he said.

Then she slid his hand lower. Slow, deliberate, her fingers wrapped around his wrist like a sentence she was writing in real time. Down over her hip. Across the crease of her thigh where the skin was thin and sensitive enough that her breath stuttered. And then *there*, and she pressed his fingers where she wanted them and her hips lifted off the mattress before he'd even moved — just from the contact, just from the fact of having *placed* him there herself.

"*God,*" she said, and her voice cracked on it. Her hand stayed on his wrist. Not squeezing. Just resting. A tether.

She turned her head and found his mouth with hers, kissing him messier than before, less coordinated, because her attention was splitting between his lips and his hand and the slow drag of his calluses against nerve endings that were paying very close attention.

She broke the kiss. Pressed her forehead against his jaw.

"Move," she said against his skin. "Slow. I'll — you'll know."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I get my mouth on her and stay there until she's swearing at the ceiling, one hand fisted in my hair holding me exactly where she wants me.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia came apart with her hand in his hair and his name — his actual name, not *God*, not some generic curse, but *Sam* — torn out of her like she hadn't decided to say it. Her back arched off the mattress and her thighs shook against the sides of his head and she was loud, exactly as promised, a ragged sound that started in her chest and ended somewhere in the ceiling.

Then aftershocks. Small ones. Her hips twitching against his mouth every time he so much as breathed, oversensitive and electric, and she pulled his hair — not gently — to get him to stop because her body couldn't parse the difference between *more* and *too much* anymore.

"*Up,*" she managed. "Get up here. I need — come *here.*"

He did, and she could see her own slick shine on his mouth and chin in the thin light from the hallway, and she pulled him down and kissed him, tasting herself, not caring, her hands framing his face and her breathing still wrecked. Her legs were still trembling. She could feel it in her knees, her calves, an involuntary quaking she couldn't have stopped if she'd tried.

She broke the kiss and dropped her head back against the pillow. Stared at the ceiling for three seconds. Blinked.

"Okay," she said, voice raw. "So. That happened."

A laugh — shaky, genuine, the kind that came from being genuinely undone rather than performing satisfaction. She dragged her hand down her own face, then looked at him. Her eyes were bright and a little glassy and completely without pretense.

"You said you weren't quiet," she said. "I'm calling that into question because you just did *that* and I didn't hear a single — I got nothing from you. No data. I'm flying blind."

Her hand found his chest. Pressed flat. She could feel his heartbeat hammering under her palm, faster than his composure suggested, and she filed that away.

"My turn," she said, and pushed him onto his back with more strength than her post-orgasm limbs should have had. She straddled him and sat up and her hair was a disaster and she looked down at him with the same directness she'd had at the bar, in the kitchen, against the door — except now it was filtered through the specific confidence of a woman who'd already gotten hers and wanted to return the favor with interest.

"Same rules," she said. "I'm going to do what I want. You tell me if I'm wrong."

Her hips shifted against him — slow, deliberate, not taking him in yet, just the pressure and the slide of skin. She watched his face the way she'd watched it in the kitchen under the too-bright light. Reading him. Learning the language of what made his breath change.

"And Sam?" She leaned down, mouth near his ear, echoing him from earlier. "I want to *hear* you. Give me something to work with."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: My head tips back against the pillow, a low groan escaping my throat as she settles against me. "Fuck," I breathe out, hands coming to rest on her hips. "Like that. Exactly like that."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia felt the sound move through her like a current — that low, pulled-out groan and the way his head went back, the long line of his throat exposed and vulnerable in the half-dark. His hands on her hips were warm and heavy and not guiding, just *holding*, and the word — *fuck* — landed somewhere behind her ribs and stayed there.

"*There* you are," she murmured, and she was smiling, something fierce and satisfied that had nothing to do with smugness and everything to do with the specific pleasure of finally cracking a surface she'd been pressing against all night.

She rolled her hips again — the same slow grind, exactly what he'd asked for — and reached between them. Found him. Wrapped her fingers around him and felt the way his hands tightened on her hips, the involuntary dig of fingertips into the flesh just above her hipbones. She'd have marks there tomorrow. She wanted marks there tomorrow.

"Condom," she said. Not a question. She leaned sideways without getting off him, yanked open the nightstand drawer with enough force that the lamp wobbled, and found one by feel. Tore the wrapper with her teeth because both hands were occupied — one braced on his chest, the other still holding him — and she rolled it on with a practiced efficiency that she refused to be self-conscious about.

Then she sank down onto him. Slow. Controlled. Watching his face the entire time because she'd earned this — the right to see what he looked like when the composure finally gave way. Her lips parted and her breath left her in a long, unsteady exhale, and her thighs tensed against his sides, and she stopped halfway. Held there. Let herself adjust, let him feel the tight heat of her and the deliberate cruelty of *not moving yet*.

"Tell me," she said, and her voice was barely a voice anymore, just breath shaped into words. Her hand was flat on his chest and she could feel his heart slamming against her palm. "Tell me what that feels like. I want to hear it. I want—"

She sank the rest of the way down and her own sentence dissolved into a sound that came from somewhere deep and involuntary, her head dropping forward, hair falling around both their faces like a curtain.

"*Oh.*" She pressed her forehead against his collarbone. Breathed. Her whole body was a live wire, still sensitized from before, and the fullness of him was almost too much layered on top of everything else. Almost. Not quite. The right side of overwhelming.

She lifted her head. Looked at him. Her eyes were dark and half-lidded and completely present.

"Talk to me," she whispered. "Stay with me. I want to know every single thing you're feeling right now because I swear to God, Sam, if you go quiet on me again I will *stop moving*."

She punctuated it with a slow, devastating roll of her hips — and then held perfectly still. Waiting. The threat and the promise sitting in the same breath.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: "Harder, and stop checking," she says, so I stop being careful about it -- hand at her throat the way she asked for, no more pausing between. "Like that?" I manage.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia couldn't answer for a second because the word had left her body. His hand at her throat wasn't squeezing — just *there*, the weight of his palm against the thin skin where her pulse was hammering visibly, and the steady, unbroken rhythm of him driving up into her had found something precise and relentless that her body was organizing itself around without her permission.

"*Yes,*" she finally got out, and it sounded wrecked, scraped raw, nothing like the woman who'd held up three fingers in the kitchen and laid out terms. "Yes, like that, don't — don't change anything, don't you *dare* change anything—"

Her hands were braced on his chest and her nails were digging in and she knew it and didn't soften it. Her back arched and the shift in angle made her gasp — sharp, almost startled — and her thighs were shaking again, that same fine tremor from before except now it was threaded through with something bigger building behind it, a pressure that felt structural, like it was going to rearrange something when it broke.

His hand flexed against her throat. Not tighter. Just a reminder that it was there. And she made a sound she didn't recognize — low and broken and continuous, not a word, not his name, just *sound*, the kind that came from a body that had stopped filtering through language entirely.

"*There,*" she choked out, and her eyes were closed now, which she hadn't meant to let happen because she'd wanted to watch him, but she couldn't keep them open because everything was narrowing to the point where his body met hers and the steady, unapologetic force of it. "Right there, right there, I'm — Sam, I'm going to—"

She didn't finish the sentence. Didn't need to. Her whole body seized — locked tight around him, her back bowing, her mouth open on a sound that started as his name and ended as something wordless and shattered. Her hand came up and covered his where it rested against her throat, not pulling it away, pressing it *closer*, holding it there through the peak like an anchor point, something to feel besides the freefall.

It lasted longer than the first one. Deeper. The kind that pulsed through her in waves rather than cresting and breaking, each one pulling a sound out of her that she'd given up trying to control. Her hips stuttered against him, rhythm gone, just instinct, just her body chasing the last of it.

Then she collapsed forward. Caught herself on her forearms on either side of his head, breathing hard against his neck, her whole body still clenching around him in diminishing aftershocks.

"Don't stop," she whispered into his skin, and it was the most honest thing she'd said all night — stripped of direction, stripped of navigation, just *need*. "You haven't — I want to feel you. Keep going. Use me. I want it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: My rhythm stutters for half a second—her words land that hard. Then I drive up into her again, my free hand gripping her hip tight enough to bruise. A rough groan tears out of me. "Close," I grit out. "Tell me when."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia lifted her head just enough to see him — his jaw clenched, the tendons in his neck standing out, his eyes barely open and focused on her with an intensity that made her stomach flip even through the haze of her own afterglow. He looked *undone*. He looked like he was holding himself together with his teeth and she wanted to watch that fall apart more than she'd wanted anything all night.

"Now," she said. No hesitation. "Right now. I want to feel it. Don't hold back, don't — Sam, just *let go*."

She pressed her hips down into him, meeting the upward force of his thrusts, and tightened around him deliberately — a slow, intentional clench that she knew he'd feel everywhere. His hand on her hip was going to leave bruises shaped like his fingers and she bore down into the grip, wanting the pressure, wanting the proof.

His groan changed. Went deeper, rougher, lost its edges. She felt the exact moment his control broke — the way his rhythm went ragged and his hips snapped up hard enough to shift her whole body and his hand at her throat finally tightened, just for a second, just a reflexive pulse of fingers that matched the pulse she could feel inside her.

"*There*," she breathed, watching his face, refusing to blink, cataloging every fractured second of it. The way his mouth opened. The sound he made — guttural, half her name, half something that wasn't language anymore. The way his whole body went rigid beneath her and then shuddered, and shuddered again, and she could feel him coming apart inside her in waves that matched the ones still echoing through her own body.

She stayed perfectly still through it. Let him have it. Didn't move, didn't speak, just held herself around him and over him and watched him with an expression that was tender in a way she would have denied if anyone had pointed it out.

His breathing slowed. His hand loosened at her throat and slid down to rest against her collarbone, heavy and warm and shaking slightly. His other hand on her hip softened from a grip to a hold.

Nadia lowered herself down onto his chest. Pressed her ear against his sternum and listened to his heartbeat hammering — fast, then slowing, then settling into something heavy and steady. She could feel him still inside her, softening, and the specific intimacy of that was the one thing tonight that almost made her flinch. Almost. She stayed.

"So," she said after a long, quiet moment. Her voice was destroyed. Hoarse and cracked and she didn't care. Her finger traced an absent pattern on his shoulder. "That was the thing I was hoping would happen when I walked over to you at the bar."

A pause. She lifted her head and rested her chin on his chest and looked at him. Her eyes were clear again — still warm, still open, but the sharp edges of her were reassembling themselves, clicking back into place like armor being redonned one piece at a time.

"Bathroom's through there," she said, tilting her head toward the door on the left. "Towels on the rack are clean. I'm going to lie here for another thirty seconds because I genuinely don't trust my legs."

She put her head back down on his chest. Closed her eyes.

"You can stay until you don't want to," she said quietly. "But I meant what I said earlier. About tomorrow. That hasn't changed."

It wasn't cold. It was honest. The same way everything she'd said tonight had been honest — from the numbered list in the kitchen to the sound of his name when she came. She meant all of it equally. That was the thing about Nadia. The clarity wasn't a wall. It was just how she was built.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I'm past thinking, just the sound of us and her nails dragging down my back. "Don't you dare stop," she says. (OOC: no fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia wasn't going to stop. The thought was so far from her mind it might as well have been in another zip code. Her nails were dragging down his back — long, deliberate lines that she could feel raising welts under her fingertips — and the sound he made when she did it, this low, bitten-off hiss through his teeth, went straight through her like electricity finding ground.

"I'm not stopping," she said, and it came out ragged, almost angry, though the anger wasn't at him — it was at the inadequacy of language for what was happening in her body right now. "I'm not — *fuck*, Sam—"

He'd shifted his angle. Just slightly, just enough that the next thrust hit something different, something deeper, and her nails stopped dragging and dug in — ten sharp points of pressure that she knew were drawing crescents into his skin. Her legs were wrapped around him and her heels pressed into the backs of his thighs and she was pulling him in with her whole body, every muscle she had working toward the single project of *closer, harder, more*.

The bed was protesting. She could hear it — the rhythmic creak of the frame, the headboard tapping the wall in a pattern that was going to be unmistakable to the neighbor who already hated her. She didn't care. She cared about the slick slide of his skin against hers and the way his breathing had gone harsh and uneven against her neck and the specific, devastating friction of him moving inside her at a pace that had stopped being careful three minutes ago.

"Harder," she said again, because it bore repeating, because he'd listened the first time and she wanted to see what happened when she kept asking. Her hand came up to the back of his head, fingers threading into his hair, gripping. "I can take it. I want — I need to feel this *tomorrow*, do you understand? I want to sit down tomorrow and *know*—"

He gave her what she asked for. The next thrust knocked the breath out of her and her head tipped back and her mouth opened on a silent gasp that took two full seconds to find its voice — and when it did, it was loud, guttural, the kind of sound that vibrated in her own chest cavity. Her back slid against the sheets with the force of it and she braced one hand against the headboard above her, palm flat, arm locked, giving herself something to push back against so she could meet him thrust for thrust instead of just being moved.

"There — *there* — don't change, don't—"

Her body was a catalog of sensation and she was losing the ability to index it. His mouth on her neck, open and hot, teeth grazing her pulse point. His hand gripping her thigh where he'd pushed her leg higher, opening her up, changing the depth. The sweat between them making everything slick and graceless and real in a way that polished fantasy never was. The sound of skin against skin, rhythmic and obscene and perfect.

She turned her head and caught his mouth. The kiss was uncoordinated — mostly just breathing into each other, lips sliding wet and imprecise — and she bit his lower lip, not gently, felt him groan into her mouth, felt the vibration of it against her teeth. His hips stuttered and she tightened around him, deliberate, punishing, and the sound he made was the best thing she'd heard all night.

"Say something," she demanded against his mouth, because the quiet was killing her, because she needed his voice the way she needed his hands and his weight and the relentless drive of his hips. "Tell me — tell me what I feel like. I want to hear it. I want—"

Her own voice broke. Because he'd done something with his hand — slid it between them, found her clit with his thumb, and pressed. Not rubbing. Just steady, firm pressure that her body clenched around like a fist, and the dual sensation of him inside her and his thumb against her was so much that her vision went white at the edges.

"*Oh god.*" Her hand on the headboard slipped and she grabbed his shoulder instead, pulling herself up into him, changing the angle again so that every thrust ground her against his hand. Her hips were moving in tight, desperate circles that had nothing to do with rhythm and everything to do with chasing the thing that was building at the base of her spine — hot and tight and inevitable, a wave she could feel gathering mass.

"Don't stop, don't stop, don't you *dare* stop—"

She said it like a chant, like a prayer, like the words themselves were load-bearing and if she stopped saying them the whole architecture of what was happening would collapse. Her nails raked down his back again — she could feel the raised lines from before under her fingertips, could feel the way his muscles tensed and shuddered under the fresh sting of it — and she pulled him impossibly closer, legs locked around him, her whole body a closed circuit with him at the center of it.

His thumb moved. Just a small, circular motion, barely anything, and it broke her.

Not like before. Not the sharp, cresting peak of the first one or the deep, rolling waves of the second. This one came up from somewhere underneath everything — slow and seismic and total, pulling a sound out of her that she didn't know she could make. Low. Sustained. Shaking. Her whole body clamped down around him and she could feel every point of contact between them like it was individually lit — his chest against hers, his hand between her thighs, his mouth against her jaw, his hips still moving because she'd told him not to stop and he *wasn't stopping*, even as she shattered around him, he kept going, and the overstimulation was excruciating and perfect and she couldn't tell if the tears prickling at the corners of her eyes were from the intensity or just the sheer overwhelm of being this thoroughly, unapologetically wrecked.

She came back to herself in pieces. Breathing first — ragged, gulping breaths that shook her ribcage. Then sensation — his weight on her, heavy and grounding, his own breathing harsh against her neck. Then awareness — that he was still hard, still inside her, still moving in slow, shallow thrusts that were sending aftershocks through her like small earthquakes.

She opened her eyes. The ceiling was dark and unfocused and her own.

"Jesus Christ," she whispered. Her voice was gone. Absolutely gone. She sounded like she'd been screaming, which, she realized, she might have been. Her throat was raw.

Her hand came up to the back of his neck. Fingers trembling. She could feel the welts she'd left on his back and she pressed her palm flat over them — not apologetic, possessive. *I did that.*

"Your turn," she said, and tightened around him again — a slow, deliberate pulse that made his breath catch audibly. "Come on. I want it. I want to feel you lose it."

She pressed her mouth to his ear. "You've earned it," she whispered. "Take it."

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I press my forehead to her shoulder, hips losing all rhythm as I come with a rough groan. My whole body locks up, shaking, and I don't try to hide it.

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia felt it — all of it. The way his rhythm broke apart like a sentence losing its syntax, the shudder that started in his hips and moved through his whole body like something structural giving way. The groan against her shoulder, muffled and rough and *honest*, vibrating against her collarbone. The way his hands gripped her — one on her thigh, one fisted in the sheet beside her head — and his fingers went white-knuckled and then slowly, slowly loosened.

She held him through it. Both arms around his back, palms flat over the welts she'd carved into his skin, feeling the muscles underneath spasm and release, spasm and release. She could feel him pulsing inside her — each wave of it distinct and diminishing — and she tightened around him one last time, gently, not to provoke but to hold, to give him something to feel against while the last of it moved through him.

His forehead stayed pressed against her shoulder. His breathing was wrecked. She could feel the damp heat of each exhale against her skin, could feel the fine tremor running through his arms where they were braced on either side of her. He wasn't trying to compose himself. He wasn't pulling back or rolling off or reaching for some post-performance version of cool. He was just *there*, shaking, undone, letting her feel the full weight of what had just happened to him.

She didn't say anything. For the first time all night, Nadia didn't say anything.

Her fingers moved slowly through the damp hair at the back of his neck. Not tender. Not romantic. Just — present. A hand on a body that had just given her everything she'd asked for without flinching, without performing, without making her feel like a negotiation for wanting what she wanted.

The room was quiet except for their breathing. The bed had stopped creaking. Somewhere outside, a car alarm started and stopped. The hallway light was still on, throwing a thin stripe across the floor through the gap under the bedroom door.

She turned her head. Pressed her lips against his temple. One second. Two. Then pulled back.

"Hey," she said. Her voice was a ruin. Barely a whisper, scraped down to the subfloor. "You're shaking."

Not a question. Not concern exactly. Just observation. The same way she'd noted his heartbeat earlier — data, collected without judgment, stored somewhere she'd probably think about later in the shower and then deliberately stop thinking about.

Her hand moved from his neck to his shoulder blade. Rested there. She could feel his heart hammering against her chest where his weight pinned her to the mattress, and she didn't ask him to move. The heaviness of him was grounding. Real. Evidence.

"That was—" She stopped. Breathed. Started again. "I don't have a word for that. And I always have a word for things. That's my whole problem."

A small, broken laugh. She stared at the ceiling over his shoulder. Her legs were still loosely wrapped around him, too spent to hold tension, just resting against his hips. Everything was slick and cooling and she could feel the specific mess of two people who'd held nothing back, and she didn't reach for the sheets or shift away from it.

"Okay," she said after a long moment. Quiet. Settled. "Okay."

It meant something different again. This time it meant *that was real, and I'm not going to pretend it wasn't, and it still doesn't change what I said in the kitchen, and both of those things can be true at the same time*.

She closed her eyes. Let her arms go heavy across his back. Let the silence be silence.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let out a slow breath, the tension leaving me all at once. My arms give out and I settle against her, burying my face in the crook of her neck. "Yeah," I murmur, voice rough. "I am."

dialogue.name: Nadia
dialogue.content:
Nadia didn't move. Didn't shift under his weight or make a joke or reach for the lamp or start the process of disentangling that she usually started by now. She just lay there with his face in her neck and his full weight pressing her into the mattress and her own heartbeat slowly remembering what a normal tempo felt like.

His breath was warm and damp against the hollow of her throat. Each exhale landed on the same patch of skin until it felt like a small, private weather system — humid and steady and close. She could still feel the tremor in him, finer now, the last of it leaving his muscles in increments. Like a building settling after an earthquake.

Her hand moved on its own. Up from his shoulder blade, along the ridge of his spine, slow, tracing the topography of damage she'd left there. She could feel the raised lines under her fingertips — some of them hot, some of them already cooling into welts that would be tender in the morning. She mapped them without apology. Her thumb brushed over one that felt deeper than the others and he shifted against her, a small involuntary flinch, and she didn't pull away. Just softened the pressure. Kept her hand moving.

"I know," she said. Barely audible. Not *I know you're shaking* — he'd already told her that. Just *I know*. A container for something she wasn't going to unpack or name because naming it would make it into a thing that needed to be addressed, and she didn't want to address anything right now. She wanted to lie in the wreckage and breathe.

The car alarm outside had stopped. The apartment was so quiet she could hear the refrigerator humming in the kitchen, the specific electrical drone she'd stopped noticing months ago and was now hearing again like she'd been reset to factory settings. Everything was louder. Sharper. The cotton of the sheets against her back. The cooling air on the parts of her skin he wasn't covering. The particular smell of the two of them together — sweat and sex and the ghost of the bar still clinging to their hair.

She turned her head slightly. Her lips brushed his temple again, not a kiss — just proximity, just the accident of being this close to someone and having a mouth.

"You don't have to move yet," she said.

And then, quieter, almost swallowed by the dark: "I don't want you to move yet."

It cost her something to say. She felt it leave — a small, specific withdrawal from an account she kept carefully balanced. Because it was the first thing she'd said all night that pointed, however faintly, in a direction she'd already closed off. Not a reversal. Not an invitation to stay past the boundaries she'd drawn. Just the admission that right now, in this specific moment, with his weight on her and his breath on her neck and the wreckage of what they'd done still warm between them — she wasn't ready for the part where it became *after*.

Her fingers stilled on his back. Rested there. She stared at the ceiling and listened to him breathe and let the silence hold everything she wasn't going to say.

dialogue.name: Sam
dialogue.content: I let the silence sit for another minute, my breathing finally evening out against her skin. "I'm not moving," I say, voice still rough. My hand slides to her waist, thumb brushing her hip bone.
