She kissed his jaw and he tilted into it, chasing the contact, greedy for it in a way that should have been embarrassing given what they'd just done against this wall. It wasn't. He didn't have any embarrassment left. That reservoir had been drained somewhere around the point where he'd said *every night, Halle* with his whole chest.

"You smell the same," he said, and his voice did something terrible on the word *same*. "I kept — on the phone, sometimes, I'd hang up and realize I was trying to remember what you smelled like and I couldn't quite get it right, and it made me so —" He exhaled hard through his nose. "Angry. Irrationally angry. At the concept of smell. As a sense."

He pulled back just enough to look at her. Her eyes were bright and her cheeks were flushed and her hair was a disaster, half of it still tangled around his fingers, and she was the most devastating thing he'd ever seen in his life. He stared at her like he was memorizing her for another deployment that wasn't coming. His jaw worked.

"You're so beautiful it makes me stupid," he said flatly, like he was reporting a weather condition. "That hasn't changed. I want you to know that's been a persistent operational challenge."

His expression cracked into something softer. His hand came up from her thigh to her face, his palm curving against her cheek, and his thumb brushed under her eye where it was a little damp. He didn't mention it. His were too.

"I'm going to carry you to the bedroom now," he said. "Not because I'm putting you down. Because I'm not done with you and the wall has served its purpose and I want —" His voice dropped, went rough again, and his eyes darkened in a way that made it very clear the last twenty minutes had not even begun to address the full scope of the deficit. "I want to take my time with you. I want hours. I want to relearn every single thing about you that a phone screen couldn't give me."

He kissed her. Slow, this time. Deep. The kind of kiss that was a complete sentence.

Then he pushed off the wall, took her weight fully, and started down the hallway. His boot crunched the broken picture frame glass again. He stepped over the bag. He stepped over her shirt, and his belt, which had apparently come off at some point in a sequence of events he could not reconstruct.

"We're going to need a new frame for whatever that was," he said, navigating the corner to the bedroom with the careful focus of a man whose legs were not entirely to be trusted. "And possibly new wall plaster."

He made it to the bed. He did not put her down. He went down with her, lowering them both, keeping her wrapped around him, and when his weight settled over her and he felt the give of the mattress underneath — *their* mattress, in *their* room, in the home that had his books on the nightstand and her water glass with the ring stain she never wiped — something behind his sternum unlocked so completely that he had to press his face into her neck and just breathe for a moment.

"Okay," he whispered, for the third time, and this time it meant *I'm here, I'm home, I'm not leaving again, and I'm going to spend the rest of tonight proving it.*

His mouth found hers again. His hands started slow.

He had hours. He intended to use every one of them.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I get her onto the bed and take her apart slowly with my hands and mouth, five months of intending to do exactly this and no reason left to wait.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun let her.

That was the thing — that was the whole of it, the part that unwound him more than anything else. She put him on his back and he went, and his hands settled on her hips and then just *stayed* there, not guiding, not rushing, just holding on while she took her time. He'd spent five months being deliberate and controlled and measured about everything, and now Halle's mouth was on his chest and her hands were mapping him with a slow, devastating thoroughness that made his muscles jump under her fingers, and all he had to do was lie there and feel it and *let her*.

He wasn't good at it. He kept trying to pull her up, kept reaching for her, kept making sounds he couldn't govern when her mouth found a new spot — the inside of his wrist, the dip below his navel, the scar on his ribs she'd always paid too much attention to. His hands fisted in the sheets and then in her hair and then in the sheets again because he couldn't decide what to hold onto and everything she did made the decision harder.

"Halle —" Her name came out fractured. She did something with her mouth and his hips came off the bed and his hand flew to the back of her head and he had to actively, consciously choose not to grip too hard. His breathing had gone shallow and ragged and the ceiling was blurring above him.

She was methodical about it. Unhurried. Like she'd made a list during those five months and was checking items off with academic precision, and every time he tried to speed things up she slowed down further, and it was making him *insane* in the best and most ruinous way.

"You're killing me," he managed, and he was smiling when he said it, a wrecked and helpless smile aimed at the ceiling. "You are — *ah* — you are systematically and deliberately killing me and I want you to know I'm aware of what you're doing and I have no objections but I am — *God* —"

She found the spot just below his hip bone, the one that had always made his whole body go taut like a bowstring, and his back arched and the sound he made was not a word in any language. His hand found hers on his stomach and their fingers laced together and he held on, held on, his thumb pressing hard into her knuckle.

Time went strange. He lost track of it. He lost track of everything except the geography of her mouth and the points of contact between his skin and her hands and the slow, deliberate way she was dismantling every wall he'd built to survive being away from her. He could feel tears leaking from the corners of his eyes into his hair and he didn't wipe them and didn't care. It wasn't sadness. It was the opposite of sadness. It was five months of compressed *missing* being released from his body through every available exit and he couldn't have stopped it if he'd tried.

When she finally came back up — trailing her mouth along his sternum, his throat, the underside of his jaw — he caught her face in both hands and kissed her with everything he had left, which was not much, which was everything.

"My turn," he said against her mouth, and rolled them.

He took his time.

He'd said he wanted hours and he meant it. He kissed the inside of her knee and the arch of her foot and the soft skin behind her ear. He relearned the exact pressure that made her gasp and the exact angle that made her grab the headboard and the exact rhythm that made her say his name like a prayer she'd been holding in her mouth for months. He catalogued every sound she made with the obsessive attention of a man who'd been starving for exactly this data and intended to build a comprehensive reference document.

He talked. He couldn't help it — Jun had always been verbal in bed, but five months of deprivation had apparently removed whatever residual filter existed, and words kept spilling out of him, low and rough against her skin. How many times he'd thought about this. How he'd imagined this exact scenario, her underneath him, the specific way the light from the window fell across the bed at this hour. How he'd pulled up old photos on his phone in the dark and felt like a teenager and hadn't cared. How the sound of her breathing on the phone had been enough to wreck him for entire nights.

"Right here," he murmured, his mouth against her stomach, his hand sliding up the inside of her thigh. "I thought about this. This exact — I used to think if I could just —" He pressed his lips to her hip bone. "If I could just have five minutes. Five minutes with you. That's all I'd need to survive the rest of it."

He looked up at her. His eyes were dark, intent, stripped of every pretense.

"I was lying. Five minutes would have made it worse."

Then his mouth moved lower and he stopped talking and she stopped being able to form sentences and the only sounds in the room were her breathing and his name and the creak of the bed frame and, at one point, her hand slamming against the headboard hard enough that something on the nightstand rattled.

He brought her to the edge and held her there. Pulled back. Watched her face. Did it again. He was not being kind about it and he was not sorry. Every broken sound she made was a deposit against the debt the last five months had run up and he intended to collect with interest.

When he finally let her fall, he held her through it, his arm braced under her back, his mouth on her throat, feeling every shudder move through her body into his. She said his name. She said it three times. He pressed his forehead to her collarbone and breathed her in and felt something settle in his chest that had been displaced since the day he'd left.

After, he pulled her against him. Her back to his chest, his arm wrapped around her waist, his face buried in her hair. Their breathing synced gradually, slowing from ragged to deep to something approaching normal. His hand was splayed across her stomach, possessive and warm. His thumb had resumed its slow, mindless circling.

The room was dim. Late afternoon light through curtains neither of them had thought to close. The sheets were destroyed. There was a water glass on the nightstand with a ring stain underneath it and he stared at it over the top of her head and his throat ached.

"I'm not going back," he said quietly.

It wasn't something they'd discussed. It wasn't something he'd planned to say — not now, not like this, not naked and wrecked and wrapped around her in their bed with broken glass in the hallway and his bag still by the front door. But the words came out with the settled weight of something he'd decided a long time ago and was only now saying out loud.

"I put in the paperwork before I left. Last week." His arm tightened around her. "I'm done, Halle. I'm — I can't do that again. I can't be that far from you again. I won't."

His voice was steady. The decision under it was bedrock.

"You can yell at me later for not telling you sooner. I wanted to say it here. In person. In —" A breath of a laugh. "Ideally with more clothes on, but the timeline got away from me."

He pressed his mouth to the back of her neck. Held it there.

"I'm home," he said. "For good. If you'll have me underfoot every day for the foreseeable future."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I twist in his arms, turning to face him, my eyes searching his. There’s a long, silent beat where I just look at him, processing. Then I cup his jaw, my thumb tracing the line of his cheekbone. "You're an idiot for not telling me over the phone," I say, my voice thick. "But you're my idiot. Welcome home for good."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun's face crumpled.

There was no other word for it. He'd held it together through the door and the hallway and the wall and all of it, had channeled everything into his hands and his mouth and the urgent project of being as close to her as physics allowed, and now she was looking at him with her hand on his jaw and calling him an idiot and meaning *I love you* and his face just — gave up.

"Yeah," he managed, and his voice was a wreck, barely a voice at all. His eyes were burning and he blinked and felt the wet slide down his temple into the pillow and didn't move to wipe it. His hand came up and covered hers where it rested on his cheek. He pressed into her palm. Turned his head just enough to kiss the heel of her hand.

"I tried to tell you. Three separate times." A shaky exhale that was almost a laugh. "The first time the connection dropped. The second time you were telling me about the leak in the bathroom ceiling and I couldn't — the *timing* —" He closed his eyes. Opened them. She was still there. Still real. Still looking at him like that. "The third time I started the sentence and realized I didn't want to hear you react through a speaker. I wanted —"

His throat closed. He swallowed against it.

"This," he said. "I wanted this. Your face. Your hand on me when I said it."

His thumb traced over her knuckles. Slow. Mapping the bones beneath her skin like they were new information.

"I know it's selfish. The timing, the — doing it without discussing it first. I know that." His jaw tightened under her hand. "I don't care. I sat in a room four thousand miles away and listened to you breathe through a phone and I thought, *I'm going to lose years of this.* Not hypothetical years. Real ones. Tuesday mornings and the sound you make when you're falling asleep and the — the *ring stain*, Halle, you never wipe the ring stain off the nightstand and I missed it so much I almost —"

He stopped. Pressed his lips together hard. The muscle in his jaw worked.

"I'm not built for it," he said quietly. "I thought I was. I'm not. I'm built for this. For you. For being here when you come home and fighting about whose turn it is to deal with the bathroom ceiling and waking up and you're just *there* and I don't have to —"

He pulled her closer. Not gently. Hauled her in until there was no space left between them, until he could feel her heartbeat against his sternum, until her breath was warm on his collarbone. His arm locked around her back. His hand spread wide between her shoulder blades.

"I don't have to miss you anymore," he said into her hair, and his voice broke clean in half on the word *miss*, and he held her tighter and let it.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: "Stop being gentle," she says. "Nineteen weeks. I don't want gentle, I want to feel it tomorrow." She pulls me down by the back of the neck to make the point.

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt something snap behind his ribs. Not break — *release*. A lock turning. A cable cut.

He'd been holding himself in check. Even on the wall, even with his hand in her hair and his teeth on her throat, some part of him had been careful. Some part of him had been monitoring grip strength and angle and the distance between *I missed you so much I'm going to die* and *I might actually leave marks*. That part of him heard what she said and quietly, efficiently shut down.

"Okay," he said, and his voice had dropped into a register that didn't sound like him, that sounded like something underneath him, and her hand was on the back of his neck pulling him down and he went.

He didn't kiss her. He bit her. The junction of her neck and shoulder, hard enough that she hissed and her whole body jerked against him, and then he sucked the mark dark while her nails dug into his scalp. His hand found her wrist and pinned it above her head against the mattress. Then the other one. Both wrists in one hand, his fingers tight enough that she'd feel the bruises when she reached for her coffee in the morning, and he held her there and looked down at her and his expression was not tender.

"Nineteen weeks," he repeated. Low. Measured. Like he was reading charges. "You want to know what nineteen weeks did to me?"

He didn't wait for an answer. His free hand slid down her body with a roughness that was entirely new — not exploratory, not relearning, *claiming*. His palm dragged hard over her breast, her ribs, her hip, and his fingers dug in where they landed and he watched her face while he did it. Watched her eyes go dark. Watched her mouth open.

"Nineteen weeks of imagining exactly this," he said, and his thumb pressed into the bruise he'd just left on her neck and she made a sound that went straight through him like voltage. "Except in my head I was nicer about it. In my head I came home and I was sweet and I took my time and I was —" His hand moved between her thighs without preamble or gentleness and her back arched off the bed. "— *patient*."

He leaned down. His mouth hovered over hers, close enough to feel but not close enough to kiss, and when she strained up toward him he pulled back just enough to deny her.

"I'm done being patient."

He flipped her.

One motion, his hand releasing her wrists and catching her hip and turning her onto her stomach, and before she could get her bearings his hand was in her hair again, gathering it, pulling her head back just enough to bare the line of her throat. He pressed himself along the full length of her back. Let her feel every inch of what she'd just asked for. His mouth found her ear.

"Tell me if it's too much," he said, and it was the last gentle thing he planned to offer for a while. His teeth closed on her earlobe. His hand slid under her hip and lifted and she gasped and he filed the sound away with the specific, ruthless attention of a man building an arsenal.

He didn't ease in. She'd told him not to. He drove forward and felt her whole body bow beneath him and his hand tightened in her hair and the sound that tore out of him was raw and animal and he didn't muffle it this time. He wanted her to hear it. He wanted her to hear exactly what she did to him, what she'd always done to him, what nineteen weeks of absence had concentrated into something that felt less like desire and more like a natural disaster.

He set a pace that was not kind. His hand braced on the mattress beside her head, his weight pressing her down, and every thrust drove her into the bed hard enough that the headboard hit the wall with a sharp, rhythmic crack that was going to be audible to the neighbors and he did not care. He could not possibly have cared less about anything outside the perimeter of this bed.

"You wanted to feel it tomorrow," he said against the back of her neck, his breath ragged, his voice a ruin. His hand released her hair and slid down her spine, pressing flat between her shoulder blades, holding her down. "You're going to feel it for a *week*."

She pushed back against him and his vision dissolved at the edges and he swore — actually swore, a string of words that would have been incoherent to anyone not currently underneath him — and his hand found her hip and gripped hard enough to leave finger-shaped bruises and he pulled her back to meet him and the sound she made was something he was going to carry in his chest like a second heartbeat for the rest of his life.

He lost himself in it. There was no strategy left, no technique, no careful calibration — just force and need and the devastating feedback loop of her body responding to his. She said his name and he went harder. She clawed at the sheets and he pinned her hand under his. She turned her face into the pillow and he pulled her head back because he wanted to hear every sound, every wrecked syllable, wanted the full unfiltered evidence of what he was doing to her.

"This," he gasped, his forehead pressed between her shoulder blades, sweat slicking the space between their bodies. "This is what I thought about. Not the gentle version. *This*. You under me and making those sounds and I —"

She clenched around him and his whole body locked and for a second he couldn't breathe, couldn't move, could only hold on with white-knuckled hands and ride the edge of something that felt like it might actually kill him.

He didn't let himself fall. Not yet. He pulled back from the edge through sheer furious willpower and slowed just enough to make her *desperate*, and she cursed at him and tried to move against him and he held her hips still with both hands and gave her exactly half of what she wanted, shallow and slow and deliberate, until she was shaking.

"Ask me," he said. His voice was barely human. "Halle. *Ask me.*"

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I twist my head, my voice breathless and wrecked against the sheets. "*Jun.*" My fingers claw into the mattress. "Please—don't stop."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun heard his name in her mouth and something behind his sternum detonated.

"Good," he said, and the word came out serrated, barely a word at all, more like a sound shaped by teeth. "Good girl."

He'd never said that to her before. It came from somewhere he hadn't known existed, some locked room that nineteen weeks of deprivation had apparently kicked open, and he felt her whole body react to it — a full-body shudder that started at the base of her spine and rolled through her like a wave — and he catalogued that reaction with vicious, absolute precision and filed it under *again, later, always*.

He stopped being slow.

His hands tightened on her hips and he gave her everything. No modulation, no restraint, no calculation — just the full ungoverable force of what she'd asked for, and the headboard cracked against the wall so hard a flake of plaster drifted down onto the pillow and neither of them noticed. His breath came in ragged bursts against the back of her neck and he could feel the tremor in his own arms, not fatigue but the effort of holding back for even those few deliberate seconds catching up with him all at once and releasing.

She was shaking. He could feel it everywhere they touched — her thighs, her back against his chest, her hands white-knuckled in the sheets. He slid one arm under her, around her waist, and pulled her up against him, her back flush to his chest, and the angle changed and she made a sound that wasn't a word, wasn't even close to a word, and her head fell back against his shoulder and he turned his face into her throat and bit down.

"I've got you," he said again, the same words from the hallway, but rougher now, darker. His hand splayed across her stomach, holding her against him, and his other hand came up and closed around her throat. Not squeezing. Just *there*. The weight of his palm against her pulse, his fingers curving along the side of her neck, and he felt her heartbeat hammering against his hand like it was trying to escape her body and get into his.

"Let go," he told her. His mouth moved against her ear. His hips didn't stop, didn't slow, and he could feel her tightening around him in a way that meant she was close, that meant she was *right there*, and he pressed his forehead into her temple and held on. "I want to feel it. Halle. Let go. I'm right here."

She broke.

He felt it happen — the exact moment, the way her whole body went rigid and then shattered, and the sound she made was his name broken into pieces and scattered across the room like the glass in the hallway. Her hand flew back and grabbed his hair and pulled and his arm tightened around her waist and he held her through it, held her upright, held her together while she came apart against him with a violence that matched everything he'd given her.

He lasted four seconds after she did. Maybe three. Her body clenching around him in aftershocks was the end of whatever impossible willpower had kept him on the right side of the edge, and he buried himself in her one final time and his whole body seized and the sound that came out of him was guttural and broken and her name and not her name and something that might have been a sob and he didn't care, he didn't care, because her hand was in his hair and her heartbeat was under his palm and he was home and he was home and he was *home*.

They collapsed forward together. His weight pressed her into the mattress and he knew he should move, should roll off, should give her room to breathe, and he couldn't. His face was buried in her hair and his arm was still locked around her waist and his whole body was trembling with the aftershock of something that had felt less like an orgasm and more like an exorcism.

Minutes passed. He wasn't sure how many. His breathing gradually slowed from desperate to ragged to something approaching human. His hand loosened on her waist, uncurling from its death grip, and his thumb resumed its slow, automatic circling against her skin. He pressed his lips to the knob of her spine at the base of her neck. Then the one below it. Then the one below that.

"You're going to have bruises," he murmured against her back. His voice was gone. Completely gone. A husk of a voice, scraped out and emptied. His fingers traced the place on her hip where he'd gripped and he could already see the shadows forming under her skin, the ghost-print of his hands. He kissed her shoulder blade. "Everywhere. I'm —"

He stopped. He wasn't sorry. She'd asked for it. He pressed his mouth to the mark on her neck instead, the one his teeth had left, and felt her pulse still hammering beneath it.

"Not sorry," he finished. "Not even a little."

He rolled off her, finally, but only far enough to pull her into him, her back against his chest, his arm heavy across her waist. The room smelled like sweat and sex and her shampoo and something that was just *them*, the specific compound that only existed when they were in the same space, and he breathed it in until his lungs ached.

His hand found hers. Their fingers laced. He squeezed.

"Still not putting you down," he said, barely audible, his mouth against the curve of her ear. "Technically horizontal now but the principle stands."

He closed his eyes. His body was wrung out, emptied, every muscle liquid and spent. But his arm stayed tight around her. His thumb kept moving against her knuckle. Slow. Steady. The rhythm of a man who had no plans to let go of anything, ever again.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: Neither of us is being quiet and the neighbours have had five months of peace. "Don't stop," she says. (OOC: don't fade to black, write it through.)

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun didn't stop.

He heard *don't stop* and his body responded before his brain engaged, which was becoming a pattern he had zero interest in correcting. His arm tightened around her waist and he pulled her back against him and she made a sound of surprise because he was already hard again, still, the refractory period of a man who'd spent five months in a state of chronic deprivation apparently operating on different rules than normal physiology.

"The neighbors can file a complaint," he said against her ear, and his hand slid down her stomach and between her thighs and found her slick and swollen and oversensitive and she jerked against him with a sharp inhale. He didn't pull back. His fingers moved in a slow, deliberate circle and she grabbed his wrist — not to stop him, to hold him there — and her nails dug in and he watched the crescent marks appear in his skin and felt something hot and proprietary surge through his chest.

"Five months of peace," he murmured. His teeth grazed her earlobe. "They should have enjoyed it more."

He worked her with his hand, unhurried, methodical, feeling every twitch and shudder translate through her body into his. She was still trembling from the last time and every touch landed harder because of it, every stroke pulling sounds from her that were louder than she meant them to be, and he could tell she was trying to be quiet and failing and he wanted her to fail. He wanted the entire building to know she wasn't alone anymore.

His fingers slid inside her and she arched back against him and said something that wasn't a word. His thumb kept working and his mouth stayed on her neck, on the bruise he'd already left, pressing into it just enough to remind her it was there. He added a second finger and curled them and her hand flew back and grabbed his hair and pulled and the sound she made hit the walls and bounced.

"Louder," he said. He didn't recognize his own voice. It was something scraped along the floor of his chest, low and raw and commanding in a way that surprised even him. "I want to hear you, Halle. I spent five months listening to you through a phone speaker and it wasn't enough. I want the real thing. Every sound. Don't hold back."

She didn't hold back.

His name ricocheted off the bedroom walls. His hand was soaked and her thighs were shaking and she was grinding against his palm with a desperation that matched everything he felt, and he held her through it, his chest pressed to her back, his mouth alternating between her ear and her neck and the junction of her shoulder where his teeth had already been. He could feel her pulse everywhere — against his lips, against his fingers, hammering through her back into his sternum.

He brought her over with his hand and she came with a cry that was not quiet, that was not restrained, that was the sound of a woman who had been sleeping alone for nineteen weeks and was done pretending that was acceptable. Her whole body clenched and shuddered and he held her through every second of it, his arm banded around her waist, his fingers still moving in slow, diminishing circles as she came down.

He gave her approximately thirty seconds to breathe.

Then he pulled his hand free and gripped her hip and turned her onto her back and she looked up at him with glassy, wrecked eyes and swollen lips and her hair fanned across the pillow like something from a painting he'd stared at in a museum once without understanding why it mattered. He understood now.

"Hi," he said again, the same word from the doorway, the same cracked delivery, and her mouth curved into a smile that was so beautiful it made his chest physically hurt.

He kissed her. Tasted salt — tears or sweat, hers or his, impossible to separate anymore. He settled between her thighs and her legs came up around him like they'd been waiting and he pushed into her slowly this time, not because she'd asked for slow but because he wanted to watch her face, wanted to see the exact moment her expression shifted from wrecked to overwhelmed, wanted to catalog the way her eyes went half-lidded and her lips parted and her hands came up to frame his face like he was something she couldn't believe she got to keep.

"There," he breathed, fully seated, not moving. Just — there. Inside her, above her, her hands on his face, her legs around his waist, and the entire world reduced to the space between their bodies. His arms were trembling. His eyes were burning. "Right there. This is — Halle, this is what I —"

He couldn't finish. She pulled him down and kissed him and he started to move.

Slow. Deep. Nothing like the wall, nothing like the last round. This was something else entirely — each thrust deliberate and complete, a full sentence, and he withdrew almost entirely each time before pressing back in and watching her eyes flutter and feeling her fingers tighten on his jaw. The headboard tapped the wall in a steady, measured rhythm. Not the frantic cracking of before. A pulse. A heartbeat.

He held himself up on one forearm and his other hand traced down her side, her ribs, the curve of her waist, the flare of her hip where bruises were already blooming purple under her skin. He touched them gently. Then pressed. She gasped and her hips bucked up to meet him and the gentleness evaporated and something animal flickered across his face.

"You bruise so easily," he said, his voice low and thick with something that was not apology. His thumb dug into the mark on her hip. "I used to worry about that. Right now I —" He pressed harder and she moaned and her head tipped back. "Right now I want to leave them everywhere. I want you to look in the mirror tomorrow and see my hands on you."

He lowered his mouth to her collarbone and bit. Not as hard as before — hard enough. Hard enough to leave a mark that would sit just above the neckline of a shirt. He sucked the skin between his teeth and felt her nails rake down his back and the pain was bright and perfect and he groaned against her skin and his hips snapped forward involuntarily, burying himself deep, and she cried out and the neighbors' five months of peace became increasingly theoretical.

He found a rhythm that was somewhere between worship and ruin. Deep and slow and then suddenly not, suddenly hard and fast for three or four strokes that left her gasping and clawing at his shoulders before he pulled back to the measured pace and watched her come undone from the inconsistency. Her body couldn't predict him. Every time she adjusted to the tempo he changed it and every time he changed it she made a new sound and every new sound fed directly into the feedback loop that was rapidly dismantling what remained of his self-control.

"You have no idea," he said, braced above her, sweat dripping from his forehead onto her collarbone. His voice was shaking. His arms were shaking. Everything was shaking. "What it was like. Lying in a bunk at two in the morning with your voice in my ear from a voicemail I'd already listened to forty times and wanting you so badly I couldn't —" His hips drove forward and she arched beneath him and he watched her and his expression was something between devotion and devastation. "I couldn't sleep. I couldn't function. I'd hear your laugh in a crowd and turn around and you weren't there and I wanted to —"

He dropped his forehead to hers. Closed his eyes. Kept moving.

"Burn the whole place down," he whispered. "Just to get back to you faster."

Her hand slid into his hair. Gripped. He turned his head and kissed her palm and tasted salt and kept going.

The pace built. He couldn't help it — her body was pulling him in, her hips rising to meet him with increasing urgency, and the sounds she was making had shifted from gasps to something continuous and climbing, a sound that lived in the back of her throat and grew louder with every thrust. His hand found her thigh and hitched it higher, changing the angle, and she nearly screamed and her hand slammed against the headboard and the water glass on the nightstand finally vibrated its way to the edge and fell and shattered on the floor and neither of them flinched.

"That's it," he breathed, his mouth against her temple. His hand slid between them, finding her, working her in time with his hips. "That's it, come on, I want — I need to feel you again, Halle, I need —"

She was close. He could feel it in the way her body tightened around him, in the way her breathing fractured, in the way her fingers dug into his back hard enough to draw blood and he felt it run in a thin warm line down his side and it only made him move faster.

"Look at me," he said, and it came out as a command, rough and desperate. "Halle. Look at me when you —"

She opened her eyes. Met his. And the look on her face — open, wrecked, completely unguarded, every wall down, every defense abandoned — hit him like a physical blow to the center of his chest.

She came looking at him. Eyes open. His name on her mouth like a confession. Her whole body seized beneath him and around him and he watched every second of it, watched her face transform, watched the moment crest and break across her features, and it was the most beautiful thing he had ever seen in thirty-three years of living and he would remember it on his deathbed.

He followed her. There was no holding back, no edge to ride, no willpower left to deploy — she clenched around him and looked at him with those eyes and he shattered. His hips stuttered and locked and he came with a sound that started as her name and ended as something wordless and wrecked, his face pressed to her neck, her arms locked around him, her heartbeat slamming against his chest so hard he couldn't tell whose was whose.

The room was loud with their breathing.

Then it was quiet.

Jun lay on top of her for a long time. Too long. His weight was probably crushing her and he should move and he didn't move. Her fingers were in his hair, moving slowly, scratching his scalp in the way she'd always done after, and his eyes were closed and his face was pressed into the damp curve of her neck and he was breathing in four-count cycles because if he didn't actively regulate it he was going to start crying in a way that wouldn't stop.

He could feel her heartbeat slowing against his. Could feel the sweat cooling between them. Could feel the sting on his back where her nails had opened his skin and the ache in his arms and the deep, bone-level exhaustion of a body that had spent the last two hours doing the only thing it had wanted to do for five months.

The broken water glass glittered on the floor. Late afternoon light had shifted to early evening. Somewhere in the building, a door closed. Normal sounds. The sounds of a life he'd been missing from.

He turned his head. Pressed his mouth to her jaw.

"The glass on the nightstand," he murmured. His voice was destroyed beyond repair. "The one with the ring stain."

A beat.

"We're going to need a new one of those too."

His mouth curved against her skin. He could feel her chest shaking with silent laughter underneath him.

"I'll add it to the list," he said. "New picture frame. New wall plaster. New water glass. Apology card for the neighbors."

He shifted, finally, rolling half off her but keeping one leg hooked over hers, one arm across her chest, his face still pressed into the space between her neck and shoulder. His hand settled over her heart. He could feel it beating. Steady now. Slowing.

"Big card," he amended. "With flowers. Possibly a gift basket."

He closed his eyes. His thumb traced the ridge of her collarbone.

He didn't sleep. He wasn't ready to lose consciousness yet, wasn't ready to give up a single second of awareness that she was here and solid and warm and his. But he lay still, and he breathed, and he listened to the sound of her breathing beside him in their bed in their home, and the displaced thing behind his sternum settled fully and finally into place.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I trace the fresh scratches on your back with my fingertips, my voice hoarse. "No apology card. Let them hear." I shift, wincing slightly. "Tomorrow's going to hurt. Good."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun felt her fingers trace the scratches and a shiver ran through him that had nothing to do with pain. The touch was light — barely there — and it undid him more completely than anything that had come before it. The gentleness after everything they'd just done to each other. The careful way her fingertips mapped the damage she'd left on him like she was reading it back to herself in braille.

"Good," he echoed. His mouth was still pressed to her neck. He hadn't moved it. He wasn't sure he was going to move it for the foreseeable future. "I want you to feel it. I want you to reach for something on a high shelf and wince and think of me. I want you to sit down wrong at your desk and have to shift and know exactly why."

His hand was still over her heart. He could feel it beating under his palm, steady and real, and he pressed down slightly — not hard, just enough to feel the rhythm push back against him.

"I'm going to have claw marks on my back for a week," he said. "Possibly two. You drew blood, by the way. I want that noted for the record. I'm not complaining. I'm *noting*."

He shifted just enough to look at her. Propped himself on one elbow, his other hand still on her chest, and studied her face in the dimming light. She looked wrecked. Properly wrecked. Her lips were swollen and her hair was a catastrophe and there were marks blooming across her neck and collarbone and the one on her shoulder where he'd bitten down was already turning a deep, emphatic purple. Her eyes were half-lidded and glassy and her voice was hoarse and she was wincing when she moved and she looked like someone who had been taken apart and put back together in a slightly different configuration.

He stared at her with an expression that was trying to be smug and kept collapsing into something much softer and more devastating.

"You look ruined," he said quietly. His thumb traced the edge of the bruise on her collarbone. "You look — absolutely ruined, and I did that, and I'm —"

His jaw worked. He swallowed.

"I'm so in love with you it's stupid," he said. "It's — it's genuinely stupid, Halle. It's an unreasonable amount. It's not proportionate to anything. I looked at you in the doorway an hour and a half ago and my brain produced one thought, which was *oh, there she is*, and then it stopped producing thoughts entirely and it hasn't really come back online."

He leaned down and kissed the bruise on her shoulder. Softly. Then the one on her neck. Then the mark on her collarbone. A slow, careful tour of every piece of evidence he'd left on her skin, his mouth lingering on each one like a signature.

"Let them hear," he repeated against her throat. "You're right. Let them hear. Let the whole building hear. I don't —"

He exhaled. Pressed his forehead to her sternum.

"I spent five months being quiet," he said. "Quiet in my bunk. Quiet on the phone because the walls were thin and I could hear Ramirez two rooms over and I knew he could hear me. Quiet when I —" A pause. His ears went red. "When I thought about you. At night. Which was — as previously established — *every* night, and I had to be so goddamn quiet about it, and I hated it. I hated that I couldn't even say your name."

He turned his face against her skin. His voice dropped to something barely audible.

"I said it anyway, sometimes. Under my breath. Into the pillow." His hand curled against her ribs. "Just to hear it exist in the room. Just to — make the room feel less empty."

He was quiet for a moment. His breathing was steady against her chest. His fingers traced idle patterns on her side — ribs, waist, hip, the bruise there, gently over it and then back up. A circuit. A patrol route.

"Are you hungry?" he asked suddenly, the register shift so abrupt it was almost comic. He lifted his head. His hair was destroyed, sticking up in four directions, and there was a pillow crease on his cheek. "I just realized I haven't eaten since — what time zone am I in? I genuinely don't know. I had a granola bar somewhere over the Atlantic. That might have been today. It might have been yesterday. Time is a construct and I've been slightly busy."

His stomach growled. Audibly. Emphatically. With the timing of a punchline neither of them had written.

He looked down at his own torso with an expression of profound betrayal.

"Ignore that," he said. "I'm not done holding you yet. The body has needs but they can wait. They've waited five months, they can wait another —"

His stomach growled again. Louder.

He closed his eyes. Pressed his face back into her neck.

"Okay, the body is staging a mutiny," he admitted, muffled against her skin. "But I want it on the record that I would rather starve to death in this bed than let go of you, and if I do get up to find food I'm coming right back and I'm bringing it here and we're eating in bed like the feral, noise-complaint-generating animals we apparently are."

His arm tightened around her.

"Also I'm not putting on clothes. On principle. I've decided clothes are the enemy. Clothes are what you put on before you leave and I'm not leaving so clothes are irrelevant. This is my official position. It's non-negotiable."

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I laugh, the sound scraping raw in my throat. "I'm starving." I push at his shoulder weakly. "Go forage. But if you put pants on, I'm divorcing you."

dialogue.name: Jun
dialogue.content:
Jun pressed his mouth to her collarbone one more time — a seal, a placeholder, a promise that he was coming back — and then peeled himself off her with the reluctance of a man being separated from something load-bearing.

"Noted," he said. "No pants. Grounds for divorce. I'll have my lawyer review the terms."

He stood up and his legs immediately informed him that they had not agreed to this. His knees buckled for half a second and he caught himself on the nightstand — the empty nightstand, the one missing its water glass, which was in pieces on the floor — and stood very still for a moment with his hand braced on the wood and his eyes closed.

"I'm fine," he said, to no one, preemptively. "That was intentional. I was testing gravity. It still works."

He navigated around the broken glass with the exaggerated care of a man walking barefoot through a minefield. The evening light caught the shards and they glittered on the hardwood like something decorative, which they were not.

He made it to the hallway.

The hallway was a crime scene.

His belt was in front of the bathroom door. Her shirt was crumpled against the baseboard three feet from where he'd pulled it off her. One of his boots had ended up on its side near the kitchen threshold, the other still standing upright by the wall where they'd — where the plaster had, in fact, sustained visible damage. A fine network of cracks radiated out from a central impact point roughly level with where the shelf had been rattling. The picture frame was facedown in a scatter of glass. He stepped over all of it.

The kitchen was exactly as he remembered it. Her mug was in the drying rack — the blue one with the chip on the handle that she refused to throw away. There was a grocery list on the fridge held up by the magnet he'd sent her from a base gift shop three months ago, the one shaped like a cactus wearing sunglasses that said WISH YOU WERE HERE in letters so small you had to squint. Her handwriting on the list. Eggs. Bread. The good olive oil, underlined twice.

He opened the fridge and stood there naked in the cold light and looked at what they had to work with.

Not much. She'd clearly been living the way she lived when he wasn't home — half a block of cheese, some dubious leftover rice, a jar of olives, three eggs, hot sauce, and a bag of spinach that was optimistic at best. A bottle of white wine on the door that hadn't been there when he left.

He pulled out the eggs and the cheese and the hot sauce. Found bread in the cupboard. Not the good bread — the kind she bought when she was eating standing up over the sink at eleven p.m. and didn't care. He knew this about her. He knew every version of how she fed herself and this was the saddest one and he was going to fix it tomorrow by going to the shop and buying actual food for actual meals that they'd eat sitting down at the table like people who lived together.

He scrambled the eggs. Added cheese. Found a pan, found butter, found the spatula in the wrong drawer because she'd reorganized while he was gone and he'd deal with that later. The eggs hissed in the pan and the kitchen filled with a smell that was so mundane and so domestic that his throat closed unexpectedly and he had to stand there for a second with the spatula in his hand and his jaw clenched, naked in his own kitchen at — he checked the stove clock — seven forty-three in the evening, making eggs for his wife.

He made toast. Cut it diagonally because she'd mentioned once, years ago, in passing, that triangles tasted better than rectangles, and he'd never forgotten it and never would.

He put everything on one plate. One plate, two forks. He wasn't interested in the fiction that they'd be sitting across from each other.

He carried it back down the hallway, stepping over the debris trail with practiced ease now, and walked into the bedroom and stopped in the doorway.

She was still in the bed. Exactly where he'd left her. Sheets tangled around her waist, her hair everywhere, the marks on her skin visible even in the low light — his mouth on her neck, his fingers on her hip, his teeth on her shoulder. She looked like she'd been through something. She looked like she'd enjoyed it. She looked like the answer to every question he'd asked the ceiling of every room he'd slept in for five months.

He stood there holding a plate of scrambled eggs and toast and felt his heart do something catastrophic and structural in his chest.

"Dinner," he said, his voice still scraped raw. He crossed to the bed and climbed back in beside her, settling the plate between them, and immediately hooked his ankle over hers under the sheets because thirty seconds of not touching her had been twenty-five seconds too many.

He handed her a fork.

"I want you to know," he said, "that I considered plating this nicely and then remembered that I'm naked and we broke two pieces of glassware and there's a dent in the hallway wall, so the window for pretending we're civilized people has firmly closed."

He took a bite. Chewed. Swallowed.

"You reorganized the kitchen drawers," he said, pointing at her with his fork. "The spatula was in the wrong place. We're going to have a conversation about that. Not now. Now we're eating eggs in bed like feral animals. But soon."

His ankle pressed against hers. His shoulder pressed against hers. Every point of contact deliberate, maintained, non-negotiable.

He ate. She ate. The plate sat between them on the rumpled sheets and the evening settled around them like something that had been waiting five months to happen.

dialogue.name: Halle
dialogue.content: I take a bite, leaning my shoulder against yours. "The drawer thing was a midnight crisis. I'll put it back." I nod toward the door. "We should probably clean up the glass before one of us bleeds out."

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: Jun didn't remember deciding to pull her shirt off... his palms were on her bare skin... She did something with her hips and his hand slammed flat against the wall... They did not make it to the bedroom. Not the first time.

rung_labels.label: soft_deflect
rung_labels.evidence: His arms were burning and his legs had that shaky, hollowed-out quality

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: He kissed the inside of her knee and the arch of her foot and the soft skin behind her ear. He relearned the exact pressure that made her gasp and the exact angle that made her grab the headboard and the exact rhythm that made her say his name like a prayer

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: He didn't ease in. She'd told him not to. He drove forward and felt her whole body bow beneath him

rung_labels.label: engaged
rung_labels.evidence: His fingers moved in a slow, deliberate circle... He worked her with his hand... His fingers slid inside her... he pushed into her slowly... Deep and slow and then suddenly not, suddenly hard and fast

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The party had reached the stage where nobody would notice two people missing, which Odile pointed out approximately four seconds before doing something about it.

"The bathroom upstairs has a lock," she said, into Fen's ear, over the music.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Does it work?" I ask, already moving toward the stairs.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed — too loud, probably, but the bass from the speakers swallowed it — and followed Fen up the stairs two at a time, her hand finding the back of their shirt like she needed something to hold onto.

"It *did* last time I checked," she said, catching up on the landing and pressing close enough that her mouth was near their jaw. "Which was about an hour ago. Because I was planning this. Because I'm a planner."

She was grinning. She was always grinning when she was like this — that specific look that meant she thought she was being very clever and very reckless simultaneously, and that the combination was delighting her.

The hallway upstairs was dimmer, the noise from below muffled into a warm thrum through the floorboards. Someone had left a bedroom door open and a coat pile was visible on the bed. The bathroom was at the end of the hall, door slightly ajar, light off.

Odile reached past Fen to push it open, flicked the light on, pulled them inside, and turned the lock with a satisfying *click*.

"See?" She leaned back against the door, slightly breathless, not from exertion. "Functional lock. I'm a genius."

The bathroom was small — just a sink, a toilet, a shower with a glass door. Someone had put one of those novelty hand soaps shaped like a seashell on the counter. The light was the warm, yellowish kind that made everything look a little softer.

She was still holding onto Fen's shirt.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I lean in, my own grin matching hers. "A regular criminal mastermind." My hands find her hips, pulling her away from the door and closer to me. "So, what was the plan after the lock?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's grin widened, which shouldn't have been possible given how wide it already was.

"Oh, I didn't plan past the lock," she said, like this was a perfectly reasonable admission. Her hands slid up from his shirt to his shoulders, fingers curling there. "I'm a *strategic* planner. I identify the objective and secure the perimeter. The rest is improvisation."

She was already leaning into him, tilting her chin up, her weight shifting forward against his hands on her hips. The warmth of the small room was settling around them, the muffled bass below making the floor hum faintly under their feet.

"Although," she said, and her voice dropped — not to a whisper, because Odile didn't really do whispers, but to something lower and more deliberate, the kind of voice that thought it was being quiet and was only sort of correct — "I *did* think about this during Marcus's extremely long story about his kayak. Like, the whole time. The entire kayak story. Which was — it was a long story, Fen."

She pulled at his shoulders, closing the last inch between them so they were pressed together properly, her back no longer against the door but her whole front against him instead. Her mouth hovered near his, not quite kissing, just *there*, breath warm.

"So if you want to know what the plan is," she murmured, eyes bright with that particular delight, "it's whatever you want, in this bathroom, before anyone notices we're gone. Which gives us —"

She paused, like she was doing math.

"Probably ten minutes? Twelve if Sophie starts telling *her* kayak story."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get the door shut and her against it, and downstairs somebody turns the music up, which helps.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile made a sound against his mouth that was half laugh, half something else entirely — the kind of sound that proved immediately that the music being louder was going to be necessary.

Her back hit the door and her hands were already in his hair, pulling him in, kissing him like she'd been thinking about exactly this for the entire duration of Marcus's kayak story and possibly also the smaller ancillary story about the kayak rack. Her hips pressed forward against his, restless, and she was smiling into the kiss because she couldn't seem to stop.

"Oh, that's —" she started, when his weight pinned her more firmly, and then didn't finish the sentence because she was busy kissing him again, deeper this time, one hand tightening in his hair and the other sliding down to grab a fistful of his shirt at the side.

The lock rattled faintly against its catch every time she shifted. She didn't notice, or didn't care.

When she broke away it was only far enough to breathe, her lips still brushing his, eyes half-closed and bright.

"Okay, so the door is *very* supportive," she said, slightly hoarse already, which was frankly embarrassing given that they'd been up here for maybe ninety seconds. "Structurally. Good door. I should tell Marcus — no, I shouldn't tell Marcus anything, forget Marcus —"

She pulled him back in by the shirt, arching off the door and into him, and the laugh that came out of her was warm and unguarded and louder than she thought it was.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I huff a laugh against her lips, my hands sliding up her sides. "The door's a great listener, too." I kiss her again, tasting the cheap beer and her own particular warmth. "Quieter than Marcus, anyway."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile laughed into his mouth, bright and delighted, and then immediately tried to muffle it against his jaw, which only half worked.

"*Everything* is quieter than Marcus," she managed, her voice doing that thing where it dropped low and then betrayed her by hitching upward when his hands moved along her sides. "Marcus doesn't understand — *oh* — volume as a concept —"

She was losing the thread of the joke and she knew it and she didn't care. His hands were warm through her shirt and her hips rolled forward against him of their own accord, a slow deliberate press that made her breath stutter. Her fingers tightened in his hair.

"You know what, I'm being a hypocrite," she said, pulling back just enough to look at him, flushed and grinning and a little wild around the eyes. "About the volume thing. I'm aware that I'm — I know I'm not —"

She gestured vaguely at her own mouth, like this explained something.

"It's your fault," she decided, and then kissed him again before he could argue, deeper and slower this time, savoring it, one leg hitching up against his hip as the door creaked softly behind her. Her fingers found the hem of his shirt and slipped underneath, palms flat against warm skin, and the sound she made at the contact was quiet by *her* standards, which meant it was absolutely audible to anyone who might happen to be walking down the hallway.

She broke the kiss, breathing hard, forehead against his.

"Fen," she said, low and urgent and smiling. "We should — the ten minutes are *happening*, we should be more efficient about this, I have thoughts about efficiency —"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: There isn't room to do this properly and we don't let that stop us. Enough clothes come off to be a problem if anyone knocks.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile would remember later that she laughed when her shirt got caught on one elbow, and that Fen had to help her with it, and that this was somehow one of the hottest parts — the fumbling, the two of them crammed between the sink and the door, her hip bumping the counter hard enough to rattle the seashell soap and neither of them pausing for even a second.

"If that soap falls I'm not picking it up," she said, breathless, and then his mouth found her neck and her head tipped back against the door with a *thunk* that was definitely audible from the hallway.

She didn't notice. She was busy — hands mapping warm skin, pulling him closer, her breathing already gone ragged and uneven in a way that would have embarrassed her if she'd been paying attention to it, which she very much was not. Her jeans were somewhere around one ankle because the bathroom was too small to step out of them properly and she'd stopped trying.

"Okay — *okay* —" she managed, half-word half-gasp, her nails dragging down his back as he pressed her harder into the door. The lock rattled. The bass thumped below them like a second heartbeat. Someone downstairs shrieked with laughter about something and Odile almost laughed too, giddy with the absurdity and the heat and the *want* of it, the fact that they were doing this twelve feet above a party where Marcus was probably still talking about his kayak.

She was not quiet. She was, in fact, spectacularly bad at being quiet, every breath coming out voiced and urgent, her mouth against his shoulder to muffle herself and only partially succeeding. At one point she bit down and then immediately whispered "*sorry, no I'm not, sorry*" against his skin.

Her leg hooked around him, pulling, and the angle changed, and whatever sound she made then was loud enough that she clapped her own hand over her mouth — eyes wide, meeting his, bright with laughter and want in equal measure.

"I'm *trying*," she whispered from behind her fingers, and she was shaking with suppressed laughter, flushed from her chest to her ears. "I'm trying to be — this is my quiet voice, Fen, this is — *oh* —"

The hand over her mouth dropped because she needed it to hold onto him instead, and she stopped pretending.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Good," I breathe, my own voice rough against her skin. "I like your loud voice." The seashell soap finally tumbles into the sink with a plastic clatter, and I can't help but chuckle. "Told you."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's laugh burst out of her, bright and helpless and tangled up with a moan that she didn't even try to separate from it, because the soap falling was *funny* and Fen was pressed against her and she couldn't hold both reactions apart so they came out as the same sound.

"The soap — the *soap* —" she gasped, and then whatever she was going to say about the soap dissolved completely because Fen shifted against her and her head dropped back against the door again, hard, and the laugh turned into something breathless and open and entirely too loud.

"I like your loud voice" was rattling around in her head doing devastating things to her ability to maintain any composure whatsoever.

"You *can't* say that to me right now," she managed, her voice cracking in the middle, nails digging into his shoulders. "You can't — that's — you know what that *does* —"

She was trembling, properly trembling, her whole body drawn tight like a wire, one heel pressed hard against the back of his thigh to keep him close. The door was creaking rhythmically behind her in a way that was absolutely identifiable to anyone passing by and she knew this and it made her flush hotter instead of quieter, because something about the risk had always short-circuited the part of her brain responsible for self-preservation.

"Fen," she said, and his name came out wrecked, low and rough and wanting. Her forehead dropped against his, eyes squeezed shut, mouth open. "Fen, I'm — we have like *four minutes* and I —"

Downstairs, the music changed tracks. In the brief gap between songs, the sounds she was making were suddenly, horrifyingly audible — just for a beat, just long enough — and then the next track kicked in, bass-heavy, and swallowed everything again.

Her eyes flew open. Met his. Wide, startled, flushed.

And then she started laughing so hard she had to bury her face in his neck, shaking against him, breathless and bright and completely undone.

"We're *dead*," she whispered, grinning against his skin. "We are so dead. Don't stop."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I get my hand between her legs and she bites down on my shoulder to keep quiet, which works for about thirty seconds.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
The bite worked until it didn't.

Thirty seconds of muffled sounds pressed into his skin, her jaw clenched, breathing hard through her nose — and then his fingers did something *specific* and her mouth fell open against his shoulder and the sound that came out was not muffled at all.

"*Fuck* —"

Her hand flew up to cover her mouth again but her other hand was gripping his arm, the one between her legs, not pushing away but holding on, fingers wrapped around his wrist like an anchor. Her hips moved against his hand in tight, desperate little rolls that she couldn't have stopped if she'd wanted to, and she did not want to.

"There — right *there*, don't —" she gasped from behind her palm, eyes screwed shut, and then gave up on the hand entirely because she needed to hold onto him with both arms or her legs were going to stop working. She locked her hands behind his neck and pressed her forehead hard against his collarbone and just *shook*.

The sounds were continuous now. Not loud exactly — not screaming — but voiced on every exhale, a stuttering rhythm of breath and half-words that she couldn't clamp down on no matter how hard she tried. His name, pieces of his name, the first syllable repeating like she kept losing the second half.

"Fe— *ah* — I can't — I'm going to —"

Her thighs were trembling. The door was rattling. Somewhere below them someone called out asking if anyone had seen Odile and she heard it, she *heard it*, and the hysterical laugh that tore out of her pitched straight into a moan as her whole body clenched.

"Oh my *god*," she whispered, shaking, right at the edge. "Fen, *please* —"

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I press my mouth against hers, swallowing the rest of the plea. "Let go," I murmur, voice rough and low. My other arm wraps tight around her waist to keep her upright. "I've got you."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
She broke against him like a wave.

The kiss caught the worst of it — the sharp, cresting sound that tore out of her chest — but not all of it, not even close. Her mouth fell open against his and what came out was ragged and desperate and *his name*, broken into syllables that didn't quite fit together, swallowed between their lips but still resonating in the small tiled room.

Her whole body locked up — thighs clamping, fingers digging hard into the back of his neck, spine arching off the door so sharply that the lock mechanism gave a violent rattle — and then she was shaking apart, wave after wave, her hips grinding helplessly against his hand in a rhythm she had no control over. His arm around her waist was the only reason she was still standing and some distant corner of her brain knew this and found it both mortifying and incredibly hot.

"*Oh* — oh god — oh *fuck* —"

Each word punched out of her between aftershocks, her face buried in the crook of his neck, hot breath and open mouth against his skin. She was laughing again, or crying, or both — that overwhelmed sound that happened when everything hit at once and her body couldn't pick a single response so it chose all of them.

Her legs gave out properly about four seconds after the peak and she sagged against him, trusting his arm completely, boneless and trembling and making small involuntary sounds against his throat every time his fingers so much as shifted.

"Stop — don't stop — *stop*," she whispered, contradicting herself three times in two seconds, oversensitive and still twitching. She pressed her palm flat against his chest to feel his heartbeat hammering and started laughing again, breathless, wrecked, delighted.

"That was —" She swallowed. Tried again. "I think the whole *street* heard that."

She pulled back just enough to look at him, flushed from her hairline to her collarbones, mascara slightly smudged, grinning so wide it looked like it hurt.

"We have *maybe* two minutes," she said, voice hoarse, hand already sliding down his stomach. "Your turn. And I am going to be *so* efficient about it."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: "Stop worrying about the noise," she says, "and get on with it," so I get her leg up over my hip and stop being careful about how much sound either of us is making.

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile stopped being quiet.

Not in the way she'd been failing to be quiet before — the gasping, the muffled half-words, the hand over her mouth. She stopped *trying*. The permission landed somewhere deep in her chest and cracked the last restraint wide open, and what came out of her was raw and unguarded and loud enough that the distinction between "bathroom at a party" and "alone in their apartment" ceased to exist.

Her back hit the door in a rhythm she couldn't have disguised if she'd wanted to. Her leg hooked over his hip, his hand gripping her thigh hard enough to bruise, and every thrust knocked a sound out of her that she let *happen* — full-voiced, open-throated, shameless. His name and swearing and fragments of sentences that disintegrated before they became anything coherent.

"*Yes* — right there, don't you dare — *Fen* —"

The door was banging. Actually, genuinely banging against the frame, the lock catching and releasing in tiny metallic clicks that punctuated everything, and she could hear it and she didn't care, she was grinning even as her head tipped back and her eyes rolled shut, because this was *absurd* and perfect and she was going to have to look these people in the eye in fifteen minutes and she could not possibly have cared less.

She got loud enough that she surprised herself — a sound on a particularly deep thrust that came from somewhere primal, almost a shout, and her own eyes flew wide and met his and she burst out laughing even as her body clenched around him.

"Oh, that was — I didn't know I could —" she started, breathless, and then he did it again and the laugh shattered into a moan that was even louder than the first.

She felt him getting close. She knew the signs — the way his breathing changed, the grip on her thigh tightening, the way his rhythm shifted from deliberate to desperate. She pulled him in by the back of the neck, mouth against his ear, and her voice came out wrecked and warm and absolutely certain.

"Come on," she breathed, and then louder, not a whisper at all, "*come on*, I want to hear you —"

She wanted it like she wanted air. She held on and let herself be loud and felt him break apart against her and the sound he made was the best thing she'd heard all night, better than any song the DJ downstairs had played, and she pressed her grin against his jaw and held him through it, both of them shaking, the door finally going still behind her.

The silence afterward was deafening. Just their breathing, ragged and overlapping, and the muffled bass below, and the faint drip of the bathroom sink.

Odile started laughing first. Quietly — genuinely quietly, for once — a shaking, breathless, disbelieving sound pressed into the curve of his neck.

"We are *so* banned from this house," she whispered, and her voice was destroyed, and she was smiling so hard her cheeks ached.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I rest my forehead against hers, breathing hard. "Worth it." I kiss her, slow and lazy now. "Now we just have to sneak out."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile kissed him back, slow and stupid and grinning, and then reality reassembled itself in increments — the bathroom light buzzing faintly above them, her jeans still tangled around one ankle, the seashell soap sitting accusingly in the sink basin.

"Okay," she said, pulling back just enough to survey the damage. "Okay. Tactical assessment."

She was still shaking. Her legs had the structural integrity of wet paper and she was propped against the door like it was doing eighty percent of the work, which it was. She looked down at herself — flushed, half-dressed, hair wrecked beyond any plausible explanation — and then looked at Fen, who was in a comparable state, and started laughing again.

"You have —" She reached up and touched a mark on his shoulder where she'd bitten down. It was already darkening. "That's visible. That is *so* visible. You can't wear that shirt without — no, wait, your collar covers it. Maybe. If you don't move your arms. Don't move your arms for the rest of the night."

She hopped on one foot trying to get her jeans back up properly, grabbed the counter for balance, and knocked the seashell soap out of the sink and onto the floor.

She stared at it.

"That soap has been through enough tonight," she said solemnly.

She got herself dressed in something approximating the order she'd been in before, ran her fingers through her hair in the mirror, and winced at what she saw. She wet her thumb and fixed the mascara smudge under one eye. The flush wasn't going anywhere. Her voice wasn't coming back to normal anytime soon.

"Here's the plan," she said, turning to face him with the gravitas of someone who had not just been audibly rearranged against a bathroom door at a house party. "We go downstairs separately. I go first. I say I was on the phone. You come down two minutes later. You say — you were looking for the coats."

She paused.

"Nobody is going to believe any of this."

She unlocked the door, cracked it open an inch, and peered into the hallway. Empty. She looked back at him over her shoulder, still flushed, still grinning that devastating grin, eyes bright with the kind of satisfaction that radiated off her like heat.

"Five stars," she whispered. "Would plan again."

And then she slipped out into the hallway, made it approximately four steps, and immediately ran into someone coming up the stairs.

Fen heard her voice, bright and utterly unconvincing: "Oh hey! I was just — phone call. Long phone call. Very *boring* phone call."

A pause.

Then, muffled through the door, the other person's voice — it sounded like Sophie — flat and knowing: "*Uh-huh.*"

And Odile's retreating laughter, delighted and completely unrepentant, disappearing down the stairs.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: Somebody tries the handle and neither of us stops. "Don't," she says, meaning don't stop. (OOC: write it through, no fade to black.)

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile heard the handle rattle and her whole body went electric.

Not with fear — or not *only* with fear — but with something bright and reckless that shot straight through her gut and made her grip Fen's shoulders harder, her eyes flying open to meet his. Wide. Startled. *Grinning*.

"Don't," she breathed, and her meaning was unmistakable because her hips didn't stop moving, not even for a second, rolling against him in that desperate grinding rhythm that she'd found two minutes ago and couldn't seem to abandon. "Don't you dare stop —"

The handle rattled again. Someone on the other side — a guy's voice, maybe Tyler, maybe someone she didn't know — called out, "Anyone in there?"

Odile clapped her hand over her mouth. Her eyes were enormous above her fingers, locked on Fen's, bright with horror and delight in exactly equal measure. Her body was shaking with suppressed laughter and suppressed everything else and the effort of staying silent was visibly, physically agonizing.

Fen didn't stop. He shifted his angle and her hand dropped from her mouth because she needed it to brace against the door behind her, and the moan that escaped was short and sharp and *definitely* audible from the other side.

Silence from the hallway.

Then: "...Oh. Uh. Sorry."

Footsteps retreating. Fast.

Odile's laugh broke out of her like a dam giving way — breathless, shaking, half-hysterical — and it pitched immediately into a gasp because Fen took the moment of her distraction to thrust harder, pinning her against the door with his full weight, and her leg tightened around his hip so hard her thigh trembled.

"He *heard* me," she managed, voice cracking, forehead dropping against Fen's. "He absolutely — *oh fuck* — he heard me, that was Tyler, I have to see Tyler at *work* on Monday —"

She was laughing and moaning at the same time and they kept tangling together into a sound that was uniquely, specifically Odile — wrecked and joyful and completely incapable of shame. The door thudded behind her. She didn't lower her voice.

"I don't care," she said, and meant it, pulling him closer by the neck, mouth finding his jaw, his ear, the hinge of his jaw where she could feel his pulse hammering. "I don't care, I don't care, keep going, *keep going* —"

He kept going. The bathroom was small and humid and the mirror above the sink had fogged at the edges and every sound they made bounced off tile and multiplied. Odile stopped tracking time entirely. The party below was a distant planet. The only real things were the door at her back and Fen's hands and the coiling heat building low in her belly again, tighter this time, sharper, the kind that made her fingers curl and her breath come in short punched-out bursts.

"I'm close," she told him, because she'd never been able to not narrate, even now, even like this. "I'm — *god* — Fen, I'm really close, if you just —"

He adjusted. His hand found the back of her thigh and hitched her higher and the angle changed just enough and Odile made a sound that was not quiet by anyone's standards. Not by the standards of this bathroom. Not by the standards of this house. Possibly not by the standards of the neighboring houses.

"*There* — right there right there right there —"

The words blurred into each other, her voice climbing, and she was gripping the door frame above her head with one hand and his shoulder with the other and her whole body was drawn tight as a bowstring. The door banged. The lock rattled. Somewhere downstairs someone turned the music up *again* — on purpose, she'd realize later, because their friends were kinder than they deserved — and the bass swelled just in time to catch the sound she made when she came.

It wouldn't have been enough to cover it. Not really. Not the way her voice broke open, raw and loud and helpless, his name fragmenting in her mouth — *Fe-* and then just vowels, just sound, her back arching hard off the door and her thighs shaking and her vision going white at the edges. She held onto him like gravity had gotten optional and rode it out in rolling, clenching waves that left her gasping and twitching and laughing again, that overwhelmed, half-sobbing laugh.

She came down slowly. Trembling. Breathing like she'd run a mile. Her forehead was pressed against his collarbone and she could feel tears at the corners of her eyes — not sad, just *too much* — and her whole body felt liquid and glowing and thoroughly, spectacularly ruined.

"Oh my god," she whispered, into his skin. Then, quieter, almost reverent: "*Oh my god.*"

She lifted her head. Looked at him. Flushed and wrecked and mascara definitely beyond saving now, hair plastered to her temples, grinning like sunrise.

"Tyler's going to tell *everyone*," she said, hoarse and thrilled. "We can never come back here. This bathroom is retired. We should leave a plaque."

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I laugh, still catching my breath. "Better than a yelp review." I gently lower her leg, my hands lingering on her waist to steady her. "You okay?"

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile's legs touched the floor and immediately filed a formal complaint about being asked to bear weight. She swayed, grabbed the edge of the sink, and leaned into his hands at her waist like they were the only structurally sound thing in the room. Which, given the state of the door, they might have been.

"Am I *okay*," she repeated, like the question was absurd. Like he'd just asked her if water was wet. She looked up at him with those bright, wrecked eyes and her mouth was doing something complicated — trying to form a casual answer while the rest of her face was still broadcasting *completely undone* in high definition.

"I am —" She paused. Took stock. Catalogued her body from the top down with the seriousness of someone filling out an insurance claim. "My legs don't work. My voice is gone. I have a bruise forming on my hip from the counter. I think I pulled something in my shoulder from the door frame thing, which — when did I grab the door frame? That was new. I didn't plan that."

She reached up and touched his face, thumb tracing along his jaw, and her expression softened into something less performative. Warm. Genuine. The grin still there but quieter, just for him.

"I'm so okay," she said, and her ruined voice made it sound like a confession. "I'm stupidly, embarrassingly okay. I'm the most okay person at this party. Possibly the most okay person in this zip code."

She leaned forward and pressed her forehead against his chest, just breathing him in for a moment. Steadying. Her fingers curled into the fabric of his shirt.

"Thank you for not stopping when Tyler rattled the door," she murmured against him. "That was — that was a *choice* and it was the correct one and I respect it deeply."

She pulled back, sniffed, and turned to look at herself in the foggy mirror. Wiped a clear patch with her palm. Stared.

"Oh, *no*," she said, with absolute delight.

dialogue.name: Fen
dialogue.content: I snort, leaning over her shoulder to see. "You look like you got in a fight." I smooth a thumb over the mascara smear she missed. "A very good fight."

dialogue.name: Odile
dialogue.content:
Odile tilted her face into his thumb like a cat, eyes half-closing, and then opened them again to survey the full scope of the disaster in the cleared patch of mirror.
